# Changelog

Unreleased changes live in `changelog.d/` (one file per batch); `scripts/changelog_assemble.py` folds them into the next version section at release.

## 0.11.0 — 2026-11-12 — thinking roles with judgment owned by the role, the test diet with a quarantine, project knowledge from onboarding, gate A reading answered questions from the register, the mutation probe proved by its own marker

- Test harness: three slow test files (`test_story_run_s7_live.py`, `test_no_move_seam.py`, `test_story_run_refusals.py`) get a 600 s per-file ceiling in the selftest table, so a loaded shared CI runner no longer kills them at the default 300 s (FR-31); the ceiling only keeps a green file green, and the contract test pins all three rows.

- The docstring and two comments of `probe_by_code.py` now say what the probe does: only the exact `qa-probe-<token>` read in a failed row's text proves (`proved_by: marker`), a failure with text and no token goes to the code critic as `cause: judgment`, and `cause: tooling` stays for a row with no text, an unknown pass body, a launcher that may not rebuild and an unbound row; no behaviour changed.

- `question_register.py --raise --from-handoff` now reads a relative path against the story folder (the form the driver passes, `work/handoffs/<dispatch>.yaml`), not against the process working directory; an absolute path is unchanged, a blank value is refused.

- QA Factory is licensed under Apache License 2.0; the full text is in `LICENSE`, and every plugin manifest names `Apache-2.0` with the author `Xartaxana`.
- The marketplace is `qafactory`: install with `claude plugin marketplace add Xartaxana/QAFactory` and `claude plugin install qa-factory@qafactory`. An installation from an earlier marketplace is removed first: `claude plugin list` shows its id, `claude plugin uninstall <that id>` removes it (UPGRADE.md).

- The brief-pack byte budget no longer depends on where the plugin is installed: the measure counts the plugin root as a fixed token, so the same story is trimmed the same way on every machine; the brief text still carries the real paths. The plan critic's pointer to its rubric section (`On the plan`) is now a door that survives trimming, and a few words of the plan critic's fixed text are tightened to make room.

- A saved last-block S6 result finished on the recovery road with a refused case (`story_run.py`, `completion_for`) now awaits the
  consumer's acceptance like the live road, where before the stage could neither close nor dispatch the consumer.

- The package no longer carries an agent CLI of its own: `references/external-agent-calls.json` ships an empty `forms` list and `cost_capture.py` has no built-in form. A project that calls an external agent from a session adds a row under `cost.external_agent_forms` in `qa-factory/config.json` (same shape as before); until it does, such a call is a shell command like any other and the price lists no form it counted. A recorded call key with no form marker is now reported as a form with no row, never lost.
- The default sign-in recipe for a UI stand no longer names a browser storage key or a session cookie: `login.ui.landed.session_cookie` is empty, so a login is proved by the sign-in field being gone. A project that wants the stronger proof names its cookie (and any storage keys to preset) under `manual_capture.login.ui` in its config.
- The names inside the package's examples, fixtures and tests are neutral (Test Project 1, TP1-<number> keys, example hosts, Test User N): a data change only, no behaviour of a role or a gate changes.

A story whose sides hold no real part of this team now always carries the implicit `product` side, whatever earlier stories recorded and with or without `--no-trace`; a story's own answer about another team's side no longer drops it. A reference-only story (every side real) no longer gets the implicit `product` side.

- The probe walk now writes its live receipt once per walk (the note "already holds this proof" appears only when the receipt file existed before the walk), and a repeat whose per-check records cannot be read, or disagree with the receipt, runs the probe again instead of answering `already_probed`.

- Briefs that reach the words rung of the trim ladder keep the person's waivers (`brief_pack.py`): a waiver of this stage (or
  of `*`) now keeps its own line at words level 1, in the order of level 2, instead of a count line, at EVERY stage and role;
  its whole text stays in `<ID>-decisions.md`. A level-1 brief therefore carries one line per waiver, and may pop more input-file
  lines than before: the person's words outrank the file list.
- The level-1 brief names the decisions side file once, in `## Not in the brief`, not twice (`brief_pack.py`): about 95 bytes
  less in every level-1 brief; briefs that never reach the words rung are byte-identical; a brief kept at level 2 by the rule
  below and still over pops its input files in the new priority.
- The words rung is taken only when it makes the brief strictly smaller (`brief_pack.py`): a rung that costs the person's words
  and saves nothing is skipped, and the last resort pops input files from the form that is kept. `over_ceiling` keeps its
  closed vocabulary: `words at level 1` still means the words at their shortest kept form.
- The last resort pops input-file lines in a fixed priority (`brief_pack.py`): the "critic findings: none yet" line, the source
  material, the other named inputs, the case files (the "... and N more" line first, then the last case first), the window's
  test file last; the doors never. The order the lines are RENDERED in does not change; `<ID>-files.md` lists them in it.
- A brief that stays over its budget after every cut says so (`brief_pack.py`): the first line of `## Not in the brief` names
  the budget and the reasons, outside the budget (`budget_bytes` is the same with and without it), and the line printed by
  `brief_pack.py` carries the same reasons for the conductor. Under `--output` or `--dry-run` the line adds that no side
  file was written in this run. `budget_bytes` no longer counts the by-range note of a brief over 30 KB either: it is measured
  before that note, like the over line.

- Place answers (`place_answers.py`): a `bug` answer for a place whose recorded draft was absorbed into a merged draft may now name the
  merged draft, so the analyst has a door and the place is no longer shown as a gap while the merged draft carries it; a draft that
  neither belongs to the place nor absorbed the place's draft is refused with the same texts as before

- Fix round of the arm-B fix batch (t-1945 review): the stage critics of S2, S3 and S4 owe at least one `findings` row when the verdict sends the window back (`rows_owed_when`, findings not questions); an untouched template row, nested or not, is not a filled row (`handoff.only_template`, one reader for the skeleton and the check), and the refusal names the stage's own row keys. `untyped` joins the repair-debt reasons of the ledger (a debt file written before the word still loads). A manual case is walked unprepared only for a malformed evidence rule of its OWN obligations, not another case's. One author token, one reader of the rows-owed and relaxed-section blocks, and the charters of the code critic, runner and case critic are back inside their size ratchets.
- Round 3: the code critic charter keeps its two pinned clauses (the files the precheck lists as not checked by code are read in full; S7 runs its control experiment on a Then-stricter-than-requirement red anyway) and cuts only repeated prose instead.
- Round 4: the code critic charter says the could_not_judge road in the pinned words again (the conductor records the window as unresolved with the reason) and its process ratchet is set to the measured value; the K-B5 control form is emptied of its optional findings list like the real form; the two K-R7-7 send-back cases carry a typed finding in the critic's form.

- The stage critic's form skeleton (S2-S4) arrives with the author's form already named in `inputs_read[0]` (the driver knows the author's last accepted dispatch; the critic may change the row), and with its optional `questions` and `findings` lists empty (`[]`, the sample rows kept as comments), so an untouched sample row is neither refused as unfilled nor raised as a question.
- A rework dispatch relaunched with no handover form or launch card on disk now gets both from the one dispatch-files writer; a form already on disk is never rewritten.
- The refusal of `stage_done.py --acceptance` for a critic form that does not name the reviewed dispatch now names the concrete `inputs_read` row to write (or says that no accepted author dispatch exists yet) and no longer mentions a hash.
- `question_register.py --raise --from-handoff` skips a `questions[]` row whose `question` is still the contract's placeholder.

- S5 code critic without typed findings (F4): a review that sends a window back (`concerns`, `review`) now owes at least one `findings` row. The contract `s5-critic-to-automator.yaml` carries a `rows_owed_when` block, `handoff.rows_owed` reads it, and `handoff_check.py` refuses an empty `findings` once, naming the field and the closed cause list. A send-back that still reaches the driver with no typed finding closes with the route code `untyped` (never a `test_defect` round on an assumed cause): at S5 it asks the existing closed question `s5.nobody_review` (review again / debt / stop, no conductor call), at S7 it stops the round. The `qa-code-critic` charter now names the key path `findings[N].cause`, the row fields, the closed cause list and the values-file way.

- Conductor moves are now data columns: each row of `moves` in `conductor-actions.json` gains `args` (`"rework"` for the one move whose option carries the closed `args` list, `null` for every other) and `offerable` (with `not_offered` when false). An option that carries `args` on a move whose column is `null` keeps its place and loses the key (the dropped tokens are noted as `args_dropped` in `state/conductor.jsonl`) instead of making the whole answer unusable. `resume_with_words`, `story_fact` and `revoke_exclusion` are never offerable; their refusal quotes the row's own reason. A column value outside the vocabulary is `DataUnreadable` naming the row.
- When the conductor asked or stopped with a question and its options are refused, the person now reads the conductor's own text instead of only the generic fallback: after the lead, `What the conductor found:` and the text (cut at 1200 characters), then one line for each word it quotes that the shown answers do not carry (`` `restart` is not offered here: ... ``), then the priced fallback options. Gate fallbacks carry the same block and still never offer `go on`.
- The conductor charter shows the option schema without `args` and says only the `rework` option adds it; the moves section of the prompt prints, per open move, whether its option carries `args` and lists the moves that are never options.

- a person's `go on` over an exhausted stage review (the stage critic's verdict unreadable, or a reject on the last round) now has a reader (`stage_review_exhausted` in `story_run.py`): a word recorded AFTER the critic's dispatch started closes the stage as a driver accept (`by: person`) and files one finding; a word recorded earlier, an unreadable time, a revoked word or another stage's word passes nothing, and the conductor is asked as before.

- A manual-agent obligation whose `evidence_policy` is not one word of `api | cli | no_write | static | ui` (a record, a list, a blank, an unknown word) is refused at the S3 exit with the row id and the five words; the strategist is told the five words in its plan contract. At S6 a preparation failure that is the factory's own (a malformed policy in an old approved plan, a crash of the request writer after the scope checks) no longer drops the case or ends in a bare `TypeError`: the case goes to the manual agent marked `unprepared`, the agent walks it with the recorder, and the record carries observations and a finding but no pass or fail. The walk reaches coverage (`not_run`, with the reason), the ledger (`unprepared_walks`), the failure analyst and "Left with you" (`unprepared_walk`) under its own name. Refusals the story owns (an unconfirmed expectation, a gate A drift, an unpinned case, the approved scope) are unchanged.

- The sensitivity probe now reads a Playwright locator, page or response assertion that carries the author's own message. Such a report prints `Error: <message>` on one line and the library's `expect(locator).not.toBeDisabled() failed` unprefixed on the next, and the detector rows T1 and T2 demanded the `Error: ` prefix there, so every UI test with a message ended `incomplete` (cause `data_row`) instead of `intended_failure`. Each of the two rows gained one alternative for the unprefixed library line, anchored on its closing ` failed` (a data change in `references/detectors.json`; the reader is unchanged); the prefixed forms still fire, and the mutated statement itself, a quotation of the form inside a message or a log line, an unrelated `Error:` line and an empty report still do not.

- Integration of the manual-lane doors: every copy of the probe-gap door now names the case key (`probe gap: <case key>`) from one constant, and a named `--attempt` on an old env_blocked row with no sign-in evidence says what the gate does (capture into a new attempt) instead of the halt wording.

- The S5 probe-gap door now names the key the window reads. The door printed `probe gap: <instance id>`, but an instance id is a phrase with spaces and the window reads only a one-token word, so the person's word was refused and the story stopped. Every door text (the window note, the controller's two refusals, the phase file, the state-exits row, the conductor's moves) now says `probe gap: <case key>`, and the controller's refusal lists the case keys the window needs. When the review of an S5 window ends at the seam with green tests whose probe the tool could not read, the question to the person now says so in plain words and names the cases; on `go on` the driver records one `probe gap: <case key>` word for each of them, from the keys it carried with the question (a new helper `window_record.probe_gap_cases` joins the ids; the readers `contract.probe_gap_words` and `probe_gap_block` are unchanged). A probe nobody ran, a stand that was down and a red test keep their own doors and take no such word.

- A login by code the factory does not know (an access kind other than `local_login`, nothing sent) no longer ends the manual lane. The `env_blocked.json` row now carries owner `factory` and cause `login_unknown`, its sentence says the login was not tried and the block goes on (a screen case signs in through `fill-account` steps in a new attempt, a seed is done through the screens), and neither `fill-account` steps, `--attempt` nor `manual_evidence.py build` tell the runner to halt. A truly refused account stays locked: a row with no cause locks the screen route only when the last row of its `steps.jsonl` is a failed `ui` step, and the causes `build` and `device` lock as before; a row an old run left with no steps and no cause no longer locks.

- An unprepared manual case now always has an outcome that the runner's own tool writes: `manual_evidence.py unprepared --task-root <root> --case <case> [--observations-file <file>] [--not-walked "<why>"]` records the case with its observations and no pass or fail. Whether the case was walked is derived from the recorder's `steps.jsonl` files, never from the runner's word: a walked case carries its newest attempt (so the recorder's surprise lines travel with it), a case with no recorder step needs `--not-walked` and says why in "Left with you". The runner's prompt line names the command, `write-block` refuses a record with a missing dispatch, time or revision with a door instead of a `KeyError`, the S6 exit refusal names the command, and `unprepared_walk` is a row state in the vocabulary.

- A halt the person already saw at an exit-gate question and answered `go on` to is no longer asked a second time. When the question said the role also stopped, `go on` now hands the person's words to that role once, in its own session (the question is priced as one more working session of the role), and the old halt is not asked again; a new halt after that resume is still asked.

- Walker, second fix round: a verdict the case record would refuse is now refused while the walk session lives in the places it was still accepted - an item with no capture at all (the server takes one `look` itself first; with the sign-in window open it is refused with the door), an observation that cites a surprise line that does not exist, a "before" picture taken after the item's first action or after the "after" picture (the server also takes no "before" over an attempt that was acted on; sign in in a call of its own); an observation with no `quote` is refused at the verdict (code never writes a citation the role did not make, so the earlier fallback to the first words of the capture is removed); the S6 completion on the recovery roads (a cut, a launch that never happened, a person's resume) waits for a case of its own lane that was re-queued; the saved-result road finishes the walk's after-step too, and a saved result no longer reopens a walk session for no role; the form values count the cases that were walked, carry a refused case's own reason and are applied again when a late verdict changes a record.

- Walker road after the verdict (fix round of the live walker): `walk_session.py final` now takes the `completion` proof and the server takes the `pre_action` picture itself before an item's first click or fill, so a pass or fail walked by the charter builds a valid case record; a verdict the case record would refuse (no limitation on an `inconclusive`, a Then-level limitation dropped, an observation with no quote, a missing before-picture) is refused while the session lives, with the door, through the same rule functions as the record check; the form values of a walk fill every field code owns; a walker's halt or cut no longer ends the lane's unwalked items (a record for a missing verdict is marked and is no verdict; `run_role` reopens the session and runs the after-step for any dispatch that has a walk record); a two-account lane opens with `--actor2`; the teardown check reads the case's `## Teardown` section.

- `manual_capture.py`: a browser `read <selector> [mode] expect=<text>` compares the value read with the role's own planned text (whitespace collapsed) and records `expect: matched|differs` on the step row; a `ui` call only records it. A `status` surprise line now also carries the answer's number (`status`), `_run_steps` takes an optional `stop` call-back (none = as before), `_store_requests_seen` takes an optional `since` mark, and `lane_key` names a case's account set. New data object `walk_session` in `manual-capture-steps.json` (batch limits, stop rules). Groundwork for the kept-session walker; the server itself lands in the next node.

- `stand_lease.py`: the stand lease record of an environment now holds `holders: [{job, pid, started, mode, acquired_at}]`. `hold(..., mode="exclusive"|"walk", max_shared=1)`: an `exclusive` holder (a suite, a capture) shares the stand with nobody; up to `max_shared` `walk` holders of distinct jobs (manual walkers) share it with each other and with nothing else. Each holder releases only its own row (job + pid + birth); a holder whose process is gone is dropped at the next acquire and named in the notes; `--release` frees every holder, each named with the person's reason; `--status` lists every holder with its state. `run_suite.hold_stand` passes `mode` and `max_shared` (default exclusive, the suites' call unchanged); a case-lane walk of `walk_session.py` holds the stand in `walk` mode; `probe_debt.stand_state`, the walk's `stand_busy` answer and the onboarding's live-lock listing read the new shape and name every holder. Lease records written by an older package version are not read.

- New capture step `fill-new-account <selector> user|secret [template]`: the agent makes a new account through the app's own sign-up form on a stand whose config row records `safe_to_break`. `user` generates the pair, records it and types the name (the template defaults to the data row `generated_user_template`, `{generated_username}`; `{generated_username}@example.test` fits a form that validates an email; a template without the placeholder is refused); `secret` types the same pair's password and is refused without a `user` step before it. The step, the log and the answer carry `created:<name> [generated]`, never a value, and a generated value that matches a `secret_content_patterns` entry is replaced, or the step is refused when three pairs in a row match. The step opens the same sign-in window as `fill-account`. A sign-up the app refuses (a step fails while the page is still on the form) records the account `unconfirmed`, and `--as created:<name>` refuses it.
- `CreatedAccounts.add` now writes the two created-users files under an OS lock: two walkers adding at once keep both rows, and a created password is never lost.

- `walk_session.py verdict` now checks the walker's verdict against the item's own attempt and stores the item's result record (`work/walks/<W>/<item>.json`, with `timing.jsonl`): a Then without a result, a pass or fail without a quote found in a capture of this item's attempt, and a pass with no final snapshot after the last action are refused with their door; a walker that ends without a verdict leaves every Then inconclusive, saying where its last call stopped. `manual_evidence.py` gains `record_from_walk` (the case record reduced from the result record: a pure fold of the walker's own per-Then words; an unprepared case goes to `write_unprepared`; a refusal is returned, not raised). New `walk_timing.py --task <KEY> [--summary] [--json]` reports wall time, recorder calls, stops, tool calls, tokens and cost per item, grouped by place; a figure it cannot measure says why.

- New `app_card.py build --task-root <T>` writes `work/app-card.md`, the app card of a story: stand addresses, entry routes (project profile and `work/flow-requests.json` with `path:line`), the sign-in route and whether gate A proved it, account roles and key NAMES, the users the story created (names only), test data, page objects of the repo map and the walkers' notes (`work/app-card-notes.jsonl`). Every section is lines or `not known: <why>`; the first line says the card is no oracle; no credential value is ever printed; the card is at most 8 000 bytes (the entry routes are cut and the tail line names how many); it is rebuilt only when the hash of its inputs changes.

- A manual runner dispatch that has a walk session (`state/walks/<dispatch>.json`) now gets a thin walk brief: the walk line (accounts, signed in or `fill-account`), the app card path, every item with its Given, steps, Thens verbatim and teardown, the `walk_session.py` commands and the rule that the application's sources are not read; it carries no manifest line, no `env_probe`, no `finalize_task`, no file list and no repository map. The story's first lane still gets the exploration lines, later lanes do not. A manual dispatch without a walk session keeps today's brief and gains one line naming the path of `references/manual-evidence.md`. An item whose case holds no Then is named in the brief instead of being rendered as an empty list.

- the manual runner is now taught the walk: a new `references/walk-charter.md` (about 3 KB) says how many steps one `walk_session.py step` call should carry (every step of a manual case in one call, one step or two or three obvious ones where the page decides the next), what stops a call, and what to do at a stop; the runner's injected text swaps the 12 KB `manual-evidence.md` for it (the grammar stays on the fallback road and for the analyst, by path), and the runner's own charter drops the repo-script lines it no longer needs. The runner's role-load rows go down (15,566 total, 14,407 process).

- The driver walks the manual half of S6 in lanes: up to 3 cases that share one account set (`controller.walk_lanes`, one function for the driver, the `story_step.py start` door and the progress line; guest cases form one lane, a case whose request cannot be read walks alone). Before a lane the driver makes sure a run report exists, builds the app card and opens a walk session for the lane's account; after the walker ends it closes the session, builds the case records from the walker's result records, runs `finalize_task.py`, writes the form's values and a timing end line. `run_role` takes a new keyword `after=` that runs once the role is over (also when it crashed or returned nothing) and before `bind`, `handoff` and `finish`; `resume_role` reopens a dead walk session before the resume words. A record the build refuses is walked once more in the next lane and then closed `left_unchecked`. A lane whose session cannot open runs on the recorder as before.

- Walker slice 1 is integrated: the session server (`walk_session.py`), the walk charter of the runner and the app card (`app_card.py`) are on one branch, and the audit knows `app_card` as a command-line script.
- The explore charter no longer points at the runner's removed "error guessing from the code facts" text; it points at the runner's hypothesis rule.

- Mutation probe judgment: a `probe gap:` word (the test's own id, its case, `tooling:<language>` or the class) no longer names a test whose probe is still waiting for the code critic's judgment, in the window and in the acceptance alike; only `probe not proved: <case key>` names a test the critic could not judge.
- `probe_by_code.py --judge` now refuses a dispatch that is not the code critic's open S5 dispatch for the probe's case (an author's dispatch, an S6 one, a critic of another window, an unreadable controller row); a dispatch resumed through `parent_retry` still works.
- A probe of another line than the obligation's check no longer publishes an obligation binding as `proven` (the case stamp fell through to it); the test row keeps its receipt, and the window keeps the off-target door, which now names the true road: `story_step.py finish ... --unresolved <why> --reason "<words>"` by the role, and says that no word of the person closes it and that delivery then requires a current sensitivity proof.
- The two S5 refusals about owed green tests name the door the probe record calls for: the critic's `--judge` for a test not yet judged, the person's `probe not proved:` word (with its case keys) for a test the critic could not judge, and the `probe gap:` word only for the tests it serves.
- A case that holds both a test the critic could not judge and a test the tool could not read now gets the "not proved" question first, showing the first kind only; the other kind is asked at the next refusal. The question shows the check as the plain inverted statement, never the factory's own marker expression.
- Removed the readers of a producer that no longer exists (a gap "named by the factory"), moved the readers of `cannot_judge` facts and the "not proved" word into `proof_level.py`, split `judge_record`'s refusals into helpers, and named `probe not proved:` in the S5 phase text and the state-exits table.

- Test pins follow the reviewed probe nodes: the gate-registry comparison count is 142 (`probe_by_code._judge_detector_rows`, row `probe_verdict`), and the written probe record's key set carries `target`.
- No behaviour of the package changes in this fragment.

- Mutation probe: the receipt's `target` and `proved_by` now reach the window's probe block, so a probe of another line than the obligation's check raises the `semantic_sensitivity` gap from a real receipt; the `--at` door is shown only for that cause.
- Mutation probe: a probe whose target could not be compared with the obligation's assertion is now said in the window verdict notes instead of passing silently.

- The mutation probe of a test that is not Python now proves "the broken check fired" by a fact the factory controls: the inverted statement carries a message holding `qa-probe-<token>`, joined at run time from two pieces so no source line or code frame holds it contiguous, and a failed run whose failure text holds that exact token was thrown by that check (`proved_by: marker`), whatever the library's wording and whatever site the frame names. How a message attaches to an assertion form is data (`assertions[].message`, `assertion_probes.<language>.marker_expr` in `references/detectors.json`; xUnit `True`/`False`, NUnit `That`/`AreEqual`/`AreNotEqual`, JUnit 5 and 4, AssertJ `as`, Playwright `expect`); a form that takes no message, or a file whose library cannot be told, keeps the plain inversion and the wording table (`proved_by: fires_as`) as before. The token of another run, a token only in an echoed source line or a system-out, a passed row and an error row are never a proof.

- Mutation probe: a run that failed at the mutated line with a text neither the factory's marker nor a library row reads is now `incomplete` with `cause: judgment` and `judgment_facts` (the statement, the frame, the whole message, the failure text), never a gap asked of a person; the place of a failure alone proves nothing.
- Mutation probe: `probe_by_code.py --judge <instance> --verdict fires|other_failure|cannot_judge --quote "<a line of the text>"` lets the code critic close such a record: `fires` writes a live receipt (`proved_by: critic`, the quote kept), `other_failure` is a `wrong_location`, `cannot_judge` keeps the record open with the reason; a judgment of other bytes, a quote absent from the stored text or a second judgment is refused with the door.
- A `cause: judgment` record is never "could not run", so no person's probe-gap word covers it; the window names the critic's `--judge` door, the delivery says "not proved" with the owed judgment, and at the S6 close it is one digest line (nobody judges there).
- Delivery: the factory finding for such a test is `PROBE_NOT_JUDGED` (was `PROBE_DETECTOR_ROW_MISSING`).

- The code critic's charter, form and vocabulary now carry the judgment of a mutation probe that failed at its mutated line on a text the tool cannot read (`cause: judgment`, `probe_by_code.py --judge`) in place of the old data-row road; the charter also teaches reading a failed probe's log (fired, did not fire, cannot tell) and aiming the probe at the check the Then names. Two repeated passages of the critic's form were cut to stay inside the size ratchets, and the code critic's ratchets were lowered to the measured values.

- The live probe now records which statement it mutated (`target`: line, end line, the manifest's `assertion_id`, and whether the mutated statement holds that line). A receipt of a probe that broke another line than the obligation's check no longer counts as proof: the window names `semantic_sensitivity` with both doors (probe the Then's line, or return the item `unverified`), delivery does not count the receipt, and a re-probe replaces a stored off-target record. A receipt with no `target`, or with an `assertion_id` that is not of the form `<file>:<line>`, counts as before.

- When the code critic answers `cannot_judge` on a mutation probe, the person gets their own question at the S5 seam, with the facts: the test, the line and statement of the broken check, the first lines the test printed, and the reviewer's reason. `go on` records one `probe not proved: <case key>` word per case (a new block name, no class: one word never widens); `rework` sends the tests back with the person's words. A `probe gap:` word (instance, case, `tooling:` or class) never names such a test, and a `probe not proved` word older than the judgment is not read. When both kinds are owed in one window, this question comes first and the probe-gap question at the next refusal. A red item, an unjudged record or a never-run probe is never listed.

- A person's `stage acceptance` word now passes the acceptance of a stage judged by its consumer only when it was written after the author's dispatch was accepted, at every place the driver consults it (the close sites of the run and triage stages, the wait for the doc scribe, the settle of a rejected acceptance), not only in the new per-turn step. A word whose time cannot be read passes nothing. A word given as the answer to a question this turn needs no age. A dry run says that a word would pass and records nothing. When recording the pass is refused, the retry repeats the whole pass, so the finding about it is still filed.
- The text a person reads when the driver stops on the same step, or on repeated refusals, now names the earlier open stages by their place and the role in plain words, with no dispatch id and no raw controller reason; the ids and the reasons go to the conductor's text and the details file. A stuck mark left by a process that died while the conductor was asked no longer attaches a later, unrelated answer to the old step.

- A stage that awaits its consumer's acceptance (S6 by the failure analyst, S7 by the doc scribe) can now be closed from wherever the driver stands. The read-only `story_step.py where` asked the controller what comes next without the pipeline, so it could not see a standing acceptance record and kept naming the consumer's stage while `next` named the author's stage; the driver never re-entered the stage that closes and stopped on the same step four times. `where` now reads the pipeline exactly as `next` does. A person's `stage acceptance` word for such a stage is also recorded at the top of every driver turn (a new step after the code close, before `where`), through the one writer, only when it was written after the author's dispatch was accepted, and the pass is filed as a finding (once per stage and author dispatch, with the person's words cut at 500 characters).

- A stage the driver closes by itself is no longer a dead end when an EARLIER stage is still open. The close used to be refused with the controller's "required prior logical stage incomplete", filed as a defect of the factory, and put to the person as a question with `retry` and `stop` only and the line that no word of theirs passes it. Now the driver reads which stage is behind from the controller's one reading of the state and acts. If the earlier stage waits for nobody, the driver goes back to it on its own (one silent retry per controller revision; the same refusal again at the same revision is asked). If the earlier stage waits for its consumer role's acceptance (the failure analyst for the run stage, the doc scribe for the triage stage), the question names that stage and role in plain words and offers `go on`: the person's word is recorded as the acceptance through the same path every such word takes (a driver accept and a finding), and the close runs again. Any other refusal, and a controller state that cannot be read, keep the old question.
- The close of a stage that its consumer role accepts (the run stage, the triage stage) now says who accepted it. The words come from the acceptance record: when a person's word passed the acceptance, the close digest and the question say a person's word accepted it; when the consumer role accepted, the words are the old ones. Before, the close always said the failure analyst or the doc scribe accepted, even when the person's word had.

- The driver's stuck stop no longer says only "I cannot tell from here what is holding it" when an earlier stage is open. When the same step comes back four times in a row, the lead now lists, from the controller state and the pipeline, every earlier stage that is not completed: its status, whether its consumer role's acceptance is awaited or already stands (and for which dispatch), and the controller's reason. A state that cannot be read leaves the old lead, never an invented fact. The count is the named constant `STUCK_REPEATS`.
- A stuck stop the person already answered is not put to them again with the same words. The answer is recorded under the step it was about (`stuck_asked` in `driver-state.json`), and when the same step comes back the text sent to the conductor says what the person answered and when, and that the same question would not move it.

- Fix round on the analyst's settle session: a settle or control walk record is no longer read as a case walk when a dispatch is resumed or continued (`walk_reopen`), and an opening record keeps its lane; the person's own `bug` answer may leave `expectation.id` empty, its quote is then read against the dispatch's reason; `walk_session.py close` under a held stand shuts the session down without the end probe instead of waiting; a settle lane takes a new plain id and writes a timing line named for its lane; a failed open names its cause (`stand_busy`) in the answer and the record, and the driver classes by it; a place whose id the lane cannot carry no longer loses the session for the others; the session line passes `--parent-pid` and the step flags, and the analyst's Commands card gets the step, look, final and status rows with the true `--items`; a `place-gap-` line is withdrawn once its place is settled; the analyst's charter keeps the two-readings question line and its tools line is split into its own bullets.

- Places of S7, fix round on the critic's verdict: a `bug` answer withdraws the person's question line only when the draft's walk receipt stands now (otherwise the line stays and the close turns it into a named gap); the close also withdraws the line of a place settled as a bug after the write, and writes the gap of a place whose chain was withdrawn under `place-gap-<id>`, so a suspicion always keeps a register line. A first `bug` answer no longer leaves a stale "not settled" gap. The investigation's projection puts no question on a place the analyst settled. `close-unsettled` no longer loses a person's question (an `open` place that also has a draft keeps the investigation road; a line of another owner is named, not rewritten; a corrected line keeps its question; a `conflict` stays a conflict on the second close). A draft with no `confirmation` word is a place, a corrupt answer record of a `new-` place is listed as unreadable, a made-up `--dispatch` is refused when the story state reads, a walk of a draft with a triage row and no readable run report no longer lifts it. The brief names the keys of the answer file and the required flags of the capture command; the gap reasons are chosen by name and the scribe line cap is a data row.

- The walk session has two lanes for the failure analyst (`walk_session.py open --place case|settle|control`, default `case` = unchanged). A `settle` session opens its attempts under the same root as `manual_capture.py ui|http --case settle-<place id>` (`work/evidence/manual/settle-<id>/aN/`); a `control` session under `evidence/control-<id>/aN/`, the folder a triage row's `control.evidence` is checked in. Both take the stand lease per request (waiting at most `request_lease_wait_s`, 60 s, then exit 3 `stand_busy` naming the holder) instead of for the session's life, so the analyst's own test runs are never blocked by its session, and are not ended by `idle_s` (they end with their dispatch, their parent or `max_s`). An item id with a slash, a drive, `..` or `__` is refused naming `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`; an unknown `--place` is refused listing the three.

- New `place_answers.py list|write|close-unsettled`: the suspicious unconfirmed places of S7 (a register row whose `code_says` contradicts, an investigation target nobody resolved, a bug draft whose step is `unconfirmed`, the analyst's own `new-<slug>`) are joined by one reader; the failure analyst answers each (`bug`, `not_a_bug`, `requirement_silent`, `impossible`) with a quote from a capture the recorder wrote for that place and the source of its expectation (`requirement`, `question`, `person`, `none`; never `none` for a bug). Code checks keys and cross-references only; the answer is written as `evidence/place-answer-<id>.json` and carried to the findings register; a place nobody settled becomes a named `coverage_gap` at the close. `investigation.unresolved_targets` resolves a target the analyst settled (new key `settled`). `manual_capture.py ui|http` are offered to the failure analyst for `--case settle-<place id>`. Judgment census: `blocking_per_role.qa-failure-analyst` 131 -> 132 (`place_answers.py::_refuse`).

- `bug_records.py`, `contract.py`, `vocabulary.yaml`: a bug draft's `reproduction` takes a third kind, `walk` - the record the analyst's `place_answers.py write` keeps for a place. The step reads `reproduced_by_factory` only when that record stands now (the answer is `bug`, names this draft and its place, its capture is in the recorder's index and unchanged); a doubtful record leaves the draft `unconfirmed`. A walk lifts a code-reading draft, a manual check or an observation (which have no run of their own); a draft that rests on a test result keeps the "red now" fact, and a triage-road draft keeps its APP_BUG row. Entries of the other kinds are judged exactly as before. The report says "the analyst walked it on the stand"; the code-reading refusal now says a walk may be its receipt.

- `bug_records.py`: a code-reading draft whose requirement the register row does not mark `code_says: contradicts: <its fact id>` is now accepted when a walk receipt of the same draft stands and its record names that requirement as the expectation (source `requirement`). A receipt of another draft or place, a void receipt, another requirement, a `person`, `question` or `none` source, a hand-written record or an unreadable file still leaves the draft refused. The `contradicts` road is unchanged.

- S7 driver, first half of the places road: the failure analyst's brief now lists the places to settle (each with its sources, state and the expectation the record names, the four answers and the four sources, the capture case `settle-<place id>`, the `place_answers.py` commands; more than 40 places are cut with a pointer), and every S7 code closer (`s7.no_failures`, `s7.pretriaged`, `s7.after_repairs`) records the places nobody settled as named `coverage_gap` lines BEFORE the read-only investigation is asked, so a place is never both a settle gap and an investigation gap. The S8 scribe gets one line of settled places (with the source of each expectation) and unsettled ones. The investigation brief says the places were the triage's to settle. A failure of this code is one printed line and S7 goes on.

- Every S7 triage dispatch of the failure analyst (a first one, a scribe-reject rework, a seam rework, a resume) now gets the places to settle and a walk session from one site in the driver: `run_role` appends the place lines before the dispatch's extra lines and opens `walk_session.py open --place settle` only when the role will actually run; the session is closed in a `finally`, so a role that crashes or is refused leaves none behind. A session that cannot open (the stand held or down, the walker absent) is recorded, the brief says "no walk session: <why>" and names the road that needs none (`manual_capture.py ui|http --case settle-<place>`, or `impossible` with that why), and the gap reason of the close follows it. A resumed dispatch whose session is not alive gets it reopened before the words go in. An investigation dispatch gets neither. The analyst may reopen a session that ended with `walk_session.py open --place settle` (a card in the role commands); `walk_session.py verdict` on a settle or control walk is refused with the door `place_answers.py write`. Gate B no longer marks a code-reading draft "by reading the code" once the factory has reproduced it: it shows the reproduction words.

- The failure analyst's charter now tells it to find out the truth on the page: in a triage every suspicious place nobody confirmed is walked on the stand before it is left, and the answer is a bug (with the requirement it breaks), not a bug (with the words seen) or a place the requirements are silent on (a question for the person, never a bug); an expectation the factory derived itself is no requirement. Its tools line names `place_answers.py list|write` and the `settle-<place>` walk commands, and its key page lists the keys of an answer (`work/place-answers/`). The S7 skill phase carries the same road, including the close step `place_answers.py close-unsettled` before the investigation section. A bug draft's `reproduction` kind `walk` is named in the run contract, the S7 hand-off form and the state-exits map. To pay for it the analyst's loaded text drops the filing-header section of the bug contract and a few lines that repeated other loaded text; its role-load ratchets go down (17,753 -> 17,751 total, 16,145 -> 15,999 process).

- Role-command cards for the walker and the analyst: `walk_session.py item|step|look|final|verdict|done|status` (the commands of the walking `qa-runner`; `open` and `close` stay the driver's) and `place_answers.py write` are registered in `references/role-commands.json`, so a refusal of these commands carries what to write and how to prove it, and `walk_session.py --help` repeats the cards. `test_role_commands.py` feeds each card's own example to its command over a real loopback walk server (scripted recorder, no browser) and the analyst's answer over a temp story.

- The driver reads a script's answer as the last line of its output that is a JSON object, through one reader. A warning a controller prints to stderr (for example the note about a project folder copied elsewhere) no longer hides the answer: before, the scope of S6 came back unread and the stage closed as "nothing to execute" although the manual half held cases. A controller call with no readable answer is now refused with the text that came back, and S6 refuses an answer without a scope instead of closing over it.
- The same reader (now `hooklib.read_answer`, shared by the driver and story_step) is used for the handoff_check form answer, so a stderr warning no longer makes the form read as unparsable; the pretty-printed probe_by_code answer is read by `hooklib.read_document`, which a warning holding a brace no longer breaks.

- A walk with two accounts starts: the kept walk server runs ONE Playwright driver for all its browsers (a second `sync_playwright().start()` in the same thread was refused), each actor keeps its own persistent profile, and the driver stops with the last browser. A walk brief finds the case of a pinned story (`state/case-versions/<case>/cv_<hash>.md`): its Given, steps, Thens and Teardown are shown instead of "Case file: not found".

- `probe_by_code.py` reads ONE target for a test of any language, in this order: `--at`, then `--oracle`, then the manifest row's `assertion_id` (`<file>:<line>`), then the first check. `--at` is no longer refused on a Python test, and it takes `<line>` or `<file>:<line>` (the spelling of `assertion_id`); a check is found by its line in the whole file, so a check in a helper or a page-object method needs no declaration. A probe whose id stands on the second check of a test no longer breaks the first one.
- A target line that holds no check of a form the factory reads is refused before a byte is written, naming the nearest check below it, the helper the line calls, and the two doors (`--at <line>`, correcting the row's `assertion_id`). A target file that is absent or outside the test tree is refused for every language (an absent `--oracle` file no longer falls back to the test). The probe record's `target` gains `source`, and the plan's `mutation_detail` gains `target_source` and `target_outside_body`.

- A repeated probe of the same test bytes is answered by the bytes AND the target: a probe of another line (the retarget a `no_failure` note prints, `--at <the Then's line>`) runs instead of being refused as a repeat, with a note naming the line the earlier probe had. The same bytes and the same target are still refused as before; a record written before `target` existed runs when a line is asked for.
- A probe of another line no longer overwrites a proved record of the obligation's check: it is kept beside it (`work/probes/<instance>--L<line>.json`), the standing record stays as it was, and no receipt is published from the beside record.

- `probe_by_code.py`: a test's spec now names its reader (`reader: "ast"` for Python, `"table"` for the other languages), and the places that asked whether a spec had a `language` read that key instead. A Python probe plans the same detail keys as the table's plan (`language: "python"`, `message_marker`, `message_form`, `statement_inverted` and the rest), and the factory's own marker `qa-probe-<token>` now travels as the inverted assert's message, an expression joined at run time (`'-'.join(['qa-probe', '<token>'])`), so a traceback that echoes the source line never holds the contiguous token. `references/detectors.json` gains `assertion_probes_ast` (Python's marker expression and frame grammar, read only through `assertion_detectors.ast_entry`) and an optional `frames_deepest` (`first` / `last`; unknown when absent) on the table entries, read through `assertion_detectors.frames_deepest`.

- `probe_by_code.py`: Python's check vocabulary is now data. `references/detectors.json` `assertion_probes_ast.python.forms` holds one row per kind of check (`PY-assert`, `PY-assert_that`, `PY-unittest`, `PY-unittest-none`, `PY-pw-expect`): a closed AST shape (`assert`, `call`, `method`, `chain`) plus the row's own names, receivers, rename map, wrap text and message slot, validated by `assertion_detectors.ast_entry` (a broken row is a typed data gap naming the field and the row). The code no longer spells `assert_that` or any method name (`ASSERT_THAT`, `PY_FORMS` removed; `_is_assert_that` -> `_form_of`, `first_assert` -> `_first_check`, `_assert_that_replacement` -> `_call_replacement`). A Python probe now reads `self.assertEqual`-style unittest checks (inverted by the row's rename map, the marker as `msg=`) and Playwright-for-Python `expect(...).to_*` chains (`to_` and `not_to_` swapped, the marker as the head's `message=`, an `await` kept); a check of a row with no inversion (`self.assertRaises`, `self.fail`, ...) that comes first is refused naming the row and the doors, never skipped for a later one. The `--at` door and the write check read the same rows, so an id on `self.assertEqual` opens. A `with self.assertRaises(...)` / `with pytest.raises(...)` block is a check too (shape `with`, rows `PY-with-unittest`, `PY-with-pytest`, spanning the with header only), refused as not invertible by code when it comes first. When call statements that no row reads stand before the check a plan takes, `target_note` names their lines and the row set. `assertAlmostEqual` keeps its positional `places`. Existing `assert` and `assert_that` probes plan byte-identical statements.

- `probe_by_code.py`: the probe's report rows are bound by ONE rule keyed by the contract's shape. A contract with a `file` is read by `red_sandbox.selection_rows` as before; a contract with no `file` (a pytest contract) or no contract is read by `red_sandbox.matching_rows` against the requested node, and every matching row is judged (a plugin-parametrised `test_x[chromium]` row is the node's, `func[webkit]` never matches `func[firefox]`, none is picked silently). A report with no row of the node says what it held. The frame reader is asked for every reader the factory knows (`reporters.READERS`, so `reporter: pytest` is read) with the pytest command read from the request's argv once. A raw row that holds a failure or an error problem is judged `failed` / `error` even when a `<skipped>` child outranks it in the row's own status. `judge_detector` is renamed `judge_probe_row` and `_judge_detector_rows` `_judge_rows`; the behaviour of the row judge is unchanged.

- `probe_by_code.py`: ONE row judge for every language (t-2064 N3b). A Python test now carries `language`, `entry` and `tail` in its spec and its run goes through the same road as any other language (`_judge_rows` over the runner's rows); Python's own judge (`verdict_of`, `_judge_row`) is removed. `judge_probe_row` is a short sequence of steps: a failed row whose failure text holds the probe's own marker is `intended_failure`, `proved_by: marker` - the only proof the code writes; a pass is never proved (a pass of a check chosen by `--at` or the manifest's id that does not lie in the located body of the test is `incomplete`, never `no_failure`); a failed row with text and no marker is `incomplete`, `cause: judgment`, with the place (`location_hit`) and the stack frames among the facts for the code critic. The place of a failure and the library's wording (`fires_as`) no longer prove anything and `wrong_location` is no longer written by the probe (the alternative probe keeps its own judge); an old record's `proved_by: fires_as` still reads. A null `fires_as` never crashes.

- `probe_by_code.py`: every read failure of a mutation probe now reaches the code critic (t-2045 N4, B7). A failed row, or an `error` row (an exception outside an assertion, a setup or fixture failure), with a failure message or text and no token of the factory's own is `incomplete` with `cause: judgment` whether or not its place was read - an unreadable place is a fact the critic reads, no longer a gap of the tool; a row with no message and no text stays `cause: tooling`. `judgment_facts` carries EVERY unsettled row (`rows: [{test_id, status, message, failure_text}]`, at most 12, then `rows_cut`), so each parameter of a parametrised test is shown, not the first; the flat keys stay for the readers that predate it. A failure text beyond the cap keeps its head and its tail around one mark, so a runner's last (raising) line survives. `--judge` accepts a quote from any stored row and refuses `fires` when the stored text is empty or rows were cut (door `cannot_judge`; the person's `probe not proved` word then follows, as before). A Python body with no check of a known form, and a check whose row cannot be inverted (`invert: null`), are now refusals of the tool: they leave the record `refused: tool` with the language (`python` from the AST reader's entry) and `cause: tooling`, so they reach the seam. `detectors.json` is read once per process.
- `references/detectors.json`, `probe_by_code.py` (t-2162): the residual a `no_failure` row prints for an entry that is not compiled is now the optional string key `passed_residual` of the entry (the TypeScript entry carries the compiled-output wrapper text, the Python entry prints none); the five guards of `_inverted` refuse as a tooling refusal, so each leaves a record with its language and `cause: tooling`.

- `probe_by_code.py`: ONE hop out of a test body that holds no check now works for every language, through data. A test whose body asserts nothing is followed into the helper it calls by name (calls read in source order from the code with strings and comments hidden), in the test's own file and then in the files it imports from the test tree; the first declaration holding a check is the oracle, and the probe's note names it as before. TypeScript and Java read their imports from the new optional `import_forms` rows of `references/detectors.json` (`{pattern, resolve: relative | dotted, suffixes}`; a Java static member or nested class resolves to its class file); C# has none, so only the same file is searched and the note says so. `helper_declaration` for TypeScript now also reads an arrow const with a block body and a class (page-object) method, and never reads a call, a keyword block or an anonymous arrow as a declaration. A file outside the test tree is never hopped into and never mutated; an import that names no file is skipped with a note; a name declared twice in one file with a check in one of them is a refusal that names the lines; a check two hops away is a refusal whose door is `--at <file>:<line>`; a fixture handed in by `test.extend` is not followed, and the refusal for a body with nothing to hop into now names the same door. Python keeps its conftest chain and fixture parameters.
- `probe_by_code.py` gains `declared_once(data, suffix, function)` and `enclosing_declaration(data, reader_entry, line)` (pure readers of the same data), and `probe_debt.py` replays a probe that mutated a helper in any language by `declared_once` instead of requiring a hand-named helper outside Python; a language with no entry gives a reason naming the data gap.

- `probe_by_code.py --mutation expected` is removed: it replaced the expected literal of a comparison with another one, which proved nothing the inversion does not, and only Python could run it. The flag is still accepted by the parser and is refused for every language with one sentence and the door `--mutation invert`. A stored record whose mutation was `expected` still reads, and `probe_debt.py` replays it as `invert`; any other unknown stored mutation is refused as before.

- Probe by code: the critic's `fires` judgment of a check the tool could not judge is pinned the same way for C#, TypeScript and Java (a fast test on the walk's per-check record and the re-folded aggregate on disk). No behaviour change: the slow case had read the aggregate from before the judgment.

- the probe walk honours a person's word on a repeat (t-2064 fix W): a call repeated on the same bytes and the same model is still answered `already_probed` with nothing launched, but when the person has recorded the word for that repeat after the standing record, the walk re-runs the checks it holds as proved (one run through the same attempt as a first run), the aggregate carries the word in its notes, and the next call is answered again because the re-run's own record is newer than the word. Under `--at` the word re-runs only the selected check. A re-run that does not prove is written as any later attempt on a proved check is.

- `references/detectors.json`, `scripts/assertion_detectors.py` (t-2064 P1): the data a red probe on every check reads. Every language entry now STATES whether it has a soft form: `soft_assert_patterns` is `[]` on csharp, java and the Python AST entry (this framework's plain forms do not continue after a failure), and the readers treat an absent key as the same `[]` plus a note that the row does not say (`soft_stated`). Forms carry `actual_arg` (the argument that holds the value the check reads, or `compare_left` for Python `assert`) only where the argument order was verified in the library's documentation and on a sample run; a form in doubt has no key (JUnit `assertEquals` and the like: the head also matches JUnit 4, whose message comes first). The TypeScript entry gains `probe_no_retry` (rows chosen by what the test file imports, `--retries=0` for `@playwright/test`; no project config is touched) and `interruption_texts` (the runner's own "Test timeout of Nms exceeded" line, which only demotes a marker). New readers `actual_arg_of`, `soft_stated`, `no_retry_flags` and `interruption_texts`; a regex that fails reads as `[]` with a note, never an exception. Nothing reads the rows yet except these readers.

- The probe's list of a test's checks now reads soft SCOPES: a bracketed region whose checks do not stop one another (NUnit `Assert.Multiple`, JUnit `assertAll`, AssertJ `assertSoftly` and `AutoCloseableSoftAssertions`). A scope is a row `soft_scopes` of the language's entry in `references/detectors.json` (`opens`: a regex ending on the opening bracket; `head`, optional: which checks inside are the scope's soft ones); every check inside is listed with its own key and `soft: true`, the scope's own opening is not a check, and the plan puts them in one run. The scope's end stops the test where it closes, so the plan never reads a check past it in the same run, and a stopping check inside a scope runs alone. A scope whose closing cannot be found, or that holds no check the factory reads, is no scope and a note names the line. A soft scope that ends at a CALL, not at a bracket (AssertJ `SoftAssertions softly = new SoftAssertions(); ... softly.assertAll();`, TestNG `SoftAssert sa = new SoftAssert(); ... sa.assertAll();`), is a row with a new optional field `closes`: the scope opens at the declaration `opens` matches (which then needs no trailing bracket; the loader refuses a row with neither) and ends at the first later `closes` match in the same body; `{name}` of a named group of `opens` (the variable) is put into `closes` and `head`. A variable with no closing call in its body (returned, passed on, closed in a conditional, a lambda or an after-each) opens no scope: its checks read as stopping and a note names the line.

- `probe_by_code.py --plan --task T --instance I --test N [--json]` prints the checks of one test and the runs that would probe them (`{checks, plan, notes}`); it reads, and writes, runs and locks nothing. `checks_of` lists every check of a known form in the test's body, the checks a `then_bindings` row names outside it, and, when the body holds none, the checks of the one helper the hop finds; `run_plan` groups the non-stopping checks into one run and gives a stopping check its own run (or lets it close a group as its last member).

- `scripts/probe_by_code.py` (t-2064 P3): a model of a check on every reader, and the factory's own marker on the check as written. `load_models` reads the critic's file `work/probe-models/<dispatch>.json` (`{"models": [...]}`, exactly one kind per entry: `actual`, `find` with `replace`, `invert`, `not_here`, `product`; at most 65536 bytes, the guards the alternative probe's `load_model` shares); a missing file or an empty `models` is one refusal that names every check with its line and only the doors that open for it. `plan_model` places the edit and never judges it: `actual` replaces the argument that holds the value the check reads (the matcher, the expected value, `.not` and the message are never edited), `find` replaces code that stands exactly once between the start of the body holding the check and its statement, `_edit_shape` refuses a half-bracket or unbalanced edit and a change of the line breaks, edits apply bottom-up, two entries that edit the same bytes are refused naming both, and a file keeps its BOM, its line ends and its line count. After the value edit each check gets ONE marker (`marker_token` now takes the check's key): the table readers through `_with_marker`, which skips its echo guard when nothing was inverted (`fires_as` None; it used to raise `TypeError`), Python through the new `_assert_with_marker` and `_assert_that_with_marker`; a form that takes no message, or a guard that fails, plans the edit with no marker and a note, so the row goes to the role and never to `intended_failure`. Nothing calls `plan_model` from the probe yet. - probe_by_code: the probe can now walk the plan of one test's checks (`_walk_plan`, not yet on the live road; `_probe` is wired to it in the next step). For each plan row it keeps the author's file under a verified byte copy, writes the critic's model with one marker per check, runs the file once, puts the author's bytes back and verifies them, judges the run check by check, reruns a check alone (once, with a token of its own) when the joint run did not show it, and writes one per-check record after every row. A restore that is not verified ends the walk with the copy kept; the walk stops when a run fails on the span of an earlier check; the `--timeout` is shared by the whole walk and what is left is named, never dropped; the runner's no-retry flags go through `build_request`, and a run with them that gives no rows is made once more without them. `_check_proved` skips a check already proved with the same model entry on the same bytes.
  Mutation checked: in `_walk_plan` the restore guard `if got["restore_failed"]:` was made unreachable; `test_failed_restore_ends_walk` (`assert len(world.runs) == 1 and result["ended"] == "restore_failed"`) then fails because the next row runs on the unrestored file (see the report for the byte copy, the hash before and after).

- The probe walk reuses a recorded result only when it was made under the same no-retry flags as the walk that asks: a result recorded without the flags is not served to a walk that runs with them (and the reverse), a record with no flag field is run again, and a run made again without the flags records the empty list. Edge tests of the walk pin checks in helper files, a second check on one line, an alone rerun that stops, fails to restore or runs out of time, a helper or an argument that throws, a `find` whose target breaks, a run of one and a cut last token; each was shown red by removing the line it guards.

- probe_by_code: a walk over the plan now has ONE writer of the instance's probe record (`_aggregate_record`, not yet on the live road; `_probe` is wired to it in a later step). After every row and at the end it folds the per-check outcomes into `work/probes/<instance>.json`: the checks with their model entries as written, the plan runs, what is left (`plan_remaining`) and `plan_unfinished` when the call's time ran out, and every key the receipt, the window block and the replay readers read. The verdict is `intended_failure` only when every owed check is proved and at least one is; otherwise it is the worst surviving verdict, or `incomplete` with the cause of the check that decided it (a tooling row makes the whole record tooling, an unfinished plan is never a pass). A plan with no check writes nothing and says why.
  Mutation checked: in `_aggregate_verdict` the survivor loop `for kind in _SURVIVOR_ORDER:` was emptied, so a record with one survivor read as `intended_failure`; `test_one_survivor_of_each_kind` (`assert record["verdict"] == kind`) and `test_survivor_order_picks_the_one_that_says_most` then fail (see the report for the byte copy, the hash before and after).

- probe_by_code: a walk now ends with the live receipt, made from the aggregate alone and only when the plan is complete (every owed check proved, at least one proved; `not_here` rows neither prove nor block). - probe_by_code: `--at` and `--oracle` no longer run a single-probe road of their own: they select rows of the plan and go through the same road as a plain call. `--at <line>`, `--at <file>:<line>` or `--at <line>#2` runs that one check (the first on a line with two, `#2` the second); `--oracle [<file>::]<function>` runs the checks of that function and names no row otherwise. The selected row needs a model (the same refusal and door as a plain call; `--mutation invert` beside `--at` opens nothing), always gets its per-check record, and the aggregate is rebuilt over the whole plan: the other rows keep what their records prove, the rest read `not_reached`, and a receipt appears only when the whole plan is complete, so a selection never publishes one check of several.
