New fast file `scripts/tests/test_probe_product_publish.py`.
- product probe repeat (fix round H): `proof_level.already_probed(..., kind="product", check_key=...)` has a fourth item: a repeated PRODUCT probe over the same test bytes, the same product bytes it broke and the same check (the key the receipt's `checks[]` names; no key asked: the bytes guard alone) is answered `already_probed` from the `one_check` receipt in `work/sensitivity-receipts/` (accepted only through `product_receipt_holds`), with no second run and nothing published. Only `red_sandbox.py --probe` passes `kind="product"` (and the key when its request names exactly one expected location); the walk and every other caller keep today's answers, and a `whole_unlisted`, old or unreadable receipt never answers.
- delivery owner of an owed model (fix round G, R2): `check_delivery._owes_factory_judgment` is False for the plain-call state (`proof_level.probe_plain_call_owed`: models owed, rows not selected), so delivery reads `review_unverified` (the critic's), not `review_unverified_factory`. An aggregate written before fix round D has no `judgment_owed` list and reads as before; the same plain call rebuilds it with the list, and no release is expected between (a story keeps its plugin generation).
- walked aggregate judgment (fix round D, B2): `probe_by_code._judgment_fold` is the one producer of the aggregate's `judgment`, `judgment_facts` and `judgment_owed`: after the code critic says `cannot_judge` on every check that owes a judgment, the aggregate reads `cannot_judge` with the facts (the person's `probe not proved:` door opens); a record no check of which owes `--judge` (rows an `--at` call did not select, a check with no model yet) is routed by the window's note and refusal door to the plain call (`proof_level.probe_plain_call_owed`), not to a `--judge` that refuses.
- probe readers (fix round F): an old LIVE receipt (`probe_by_code.py`, no `checks`) gets the same info line an old product receipt gets, through the one carrier `_probe_scope_notes` (EP-I); an aggregate that exists but cannot be read or parsed, is not an object, or has `checks` that is not a list, or a per-check record that exists and cannot be read, reads `model_changed` with a note naming the file (an unknown is never a pass; an absent aggregate is read as before); the window reads a check key's file and ordinal through `probe_by_code._parse_at_row` and its record through `_read_check_record` (no key grammar of its own).

- what the roles read about the probe (t-2064 P7): the code critic's brief card (`brief_pack.py`), its ahead card (`references/ahead-cards.json`) and the S5 phase text carry the calls of the probe road: one `probe_by_code.py` call per instance with no `--at` walks every check of the test; each check needs an entry in the critic's model file `work/probe-models/<dispatch id>.json` and a check with none is refused before any byte; `--at` selects one row and needs its entry; a plan of more than 3 rows runs in the background and `plan_unfinished` is answered by the same call; `red_sandbox.py --probe` proves only the one check it names and the critic names it with a `product` entry. The card no longer offers `--mutation invert|expected`. The code critic's charter carries the experience and points at the card for the calls: every check is probed; for each, how the broken product would answer, and that value is written (a value the healthy product can also give proves nothing; no idea: invert and say why); only our marker proves without the critic; a real check not on the plan's list is `unverified`; `no_failure` is a test defect unless the instance never reaches the check, which the critic says with why in its findings (`unverified`); a Then whose check passes under its model goes back `unverified`; the rubric names an independent stopping check and a soft check whose next read is junk as `mechanical`. The driver's S5 critic brief says the same in one sentence. The automator's charter tells it to write independent checks of a step in the framework's non-stopping form where it has one. Role load did not grow (the critic's rows went down by 3 and 6 tokens).

- Project knowledge, phase 0 (PK0-1): a new answer registry `scripts/project_knowledge.py` keeps what a person told the factory once about the product - which roles it has, which account a role uses on a stand - in `qa-factory/records/project-knowledge.json` (carried across a reinstall and collected with the other project records), with the person's own words, the scope the answer holds in, who recorded it and when. One writer (`record`, under a lock, refused for a story that leaves no trace) and one pure reader (`state`, config first for an account; an unreadable registry, a revoked row, twins or a malformed note read as unknown and the person is asked). The conductor gets `project_knowledge.py account|role|revoke|show`; `account` writes the stand's account through the existing decision writer first and its record second. Nothing asks differently yet: the stages that read the registry follow in the next nodes.

- The S3 brief of the test strategist now lists the product's roles from the project's record of earlier answers and the stand's accounts: each role with whether it has an account on the chosen stand and who said so (the person with the story, the project's settings, or a role's notice the person has not yet confirmed), at most 15 roles then a count, and the roles the person removed on one line. An empty roster, no chosen stand and an unreadable record each say so; a failure adds no lines and never blocks the brief. No other stage or role gets these lines.
- The strategist's charter gains one craft paragraph on roles as a coverage axis, and names the optional `product_roles` handoff section for a role the requirements name and the list lacks.

- Project knowledge, phase 0 (PK0-3): the S3 form of the test strategist gets an OPTIONAL `product_roles` section - every role the plan checks, also one the roster in its brief lacks (a role still only noticed is named again, so the person is asked again), with the sign-in and where the requirements name it. A form without the section, an empty list and the untouched placeholder row all mean "nothing noticed" and the form check owes nothing new. At gate A, after the person's answers are applied and before the gate is rehearsed, the driver records every named role the project does not know (and the person has not turned down) as `noticed_unconfirmed` - never as known, nothing for a story that leaves no trace, and a failure to record is one stderr line, never a stopped gate. A role is confirmed by the person at the gate in the next nodes.

- Project knowledge, phase 0 (PK0-4): gate A asks about an account ONCE per stand and role instead of once per case. When cases of a story sign in as a role the project holds no account for, the gate shows one card for that stand and role (`RA-<stand>-<role>`) listing the cases it holds, with the person's answers and the three price lines per answer: the names of the two variables in the env file (kept for the stand from now on), `accept` (this story only), or "not a role of this product" in their own words; a role whose entries in the stand are ambiguous (twins) gets a card whose door is `myself` or `accept`. A case the person already answered in this story (the question or its own card) is left off the card; the sign-in probe adds a note, not a second card, for an account a card already asks about. A role the strategist noticed and this story's plan names gets a confirm card that does not hold the gate (silence keeps it unconfirmed, and it is asked again next story). An account the person gave in an earlier story is not asked again and is said in one line. No new answer words; the card id is lossless for an ASCII name and a short hash otherwise (a stand name holding a hyphen or a space is always hashed), so two roles or two stands never share one. The card's `the test:` and `missing:` lines are written whole, the machine marker of the "acting on your earlier answers" line never appears in the text a person reads, and a very long stand or role name still leaves the question inside the finding's first 200 characters.

- Project knowledge, phase 0 (PK0-5): the stand's default login is asked only when the story needs it, by ONE rule that gate A and S6 both read (`gate_preflight.default_login_needed`). It is needed when a case declares the default account, the plan automates something, a manual case names no account, an executed case seeds data, or an executed manual case names a role whose account is not recorded on the chosen stand (the runner would create it as the default); it is also needed whenever the plan, a case or the registry cannot be read. A role the person said is not a role of this product (its cases are carried as not run) no longer asks for it. When it is not asked, gate A says so in one line instead of listing missing login keys, and S6 does not read the default account. S6 also reads a role's account on the chosen stand only, and refuses with the reason when no stand is chosen (the reserved `env:` / `created:` / `default` accounts need no stand and are not refused for it).

- The conductor texts now name the project's answer registry: the role, twins and confirm cards are answered through `project_knowledge.py account` and `role` (a story that leaves no trace refuses them), `references/environments.md` records accounts the same way, `design/architecture.md` AR-3 says a project's facts live in the config or in `records/project-knowledge.json`, and `design/state-exits.md` has a row for every stored state of that registry (known, noticed_unconfirmed, not_needed, revoked) with its way out.

- The pre-tool guard now closes `project_knowledge.py account`, `role` and `revoke` to every role (`show` stays open) and refuses a role's write to `qa-factory/records/project-knowledge.json`, so a role cannot turn its own inference into a recorded project fact.

- Project knowledge, phase 0 (PK0-9): a role the person said is "not a role of this product" is not asked about again. In a later story gate A shows no account card and no finding for that role: its cases are carried as not run through the existing "decided once" road, and the packet's "Decided once" block says so in one line (the role, the story and the date of the answer, each case named with its title, and the person's own words). The sign-in probe never signs in as such a role, even when the project's settings hold an account for it. At gate B the same cases are not carded again: the carry is marked as the project record's own, a changed commit or image does not reopen it, and it is reopened the moment the answer is taken back or the role is named again by a later answer. `<name>: ask again` takes the record back (the entry in the record of earlier answers, then this story's own records that rest on it). An unreadable record, a taken-back or superseded answer, or a carry that names no record is asked as before; the environment-record road is unchanged.

- The report facts now carry counters for a story that has a sides record (`report_facts.py --json`, key `sides_measure`; nothing is added to the report text, and a story with no sides record has no such key): the share of provisional rows settled without touching the marked line (with the count per row status), the cost of the dispatches that ran after code arrived (`phase2_cost`) against the cost of the dispatches made before the first of them (`phase1_cost`; the conductor's own spend is carried apart as `conductor_cost`, and the three share one shape), the plan rows that stand on a substituted or unknown side, the sides that are not real, whether the sides are unknown, and the hold. Each counter is read through the reader that owns its fact (the journal's money as the dashboard reads it, with its per-call-root rule); an input that is absent, unreadable or has no journal record makes the counter `unmeasured: <why>`, never 0, and a story with no phase-2 dispatch prints phase 2 as `absent: <why>`. The architecture map names the side-ledger and awaiting-state tests as detectors of AR-28 and AR-25, and the side readers as carriers of AR-13.

- Sides of the product, read from one place. `references/side-realities.json` holds the reality words (`real`, `absent`, `substituted`) and the default side, and `contract.side_realities` is its one reader; `contract.story_sides` returns every side of a story (`reality`, `deliverable`, `settles_by`, `reference`, `source`) from `pipeline.sides`, or the default when the story records none or its file cannot be read (then one line on stderr says why); `contract.parks_after_s5` is true only for an absent side the story delivers; `contract.awaiting` reads the hold of a story waiting for code, with its `cause` and `held_from` (a record written before them reads `s5_absent_side` and `S6`). `stage_done.py --set sides.<name>.<attribute>=<value>` and `--set sides_unknown=` write the record: a reality outside the data file is refused naming the allowed words, a side name outside any list (for example `kiosk`) is accepted, and a stage transition keeps both fields. Nothing writes `pipeline.sides` yet, so every story behaves as before.

- The project remembers what a person said about its sides. The answer registry takes three more keys, `product.sides` (whether this team's stories deliver a side, and who makes it real when they do not), `environments.sides` (how a stand holds a side) and `environments.reference_for` (the stand that still runs the old version of a side); side names are compared exactly, so `UI` and `ui` are two sides, and a value outside the shape or a reality word outside `references/side-realities.json` is refused. `project_knowledge.py side` records them on the person's words (closed to roles by the guard, `show` stays open), `project_knowledge.subjects` lists the subjects of a key, and `contract.story_sides` reads the registry after `pipeline.sides` and before the default (each side carries `source: registry` and the `registry_key` it came from). At the start of a story the driver reads these rows, records a person's answer to "whose is this side" once per project so the next story is not asked, refuses a launch side name that differs from a recorded one only by letter case, and writes `pipeline.sides_unknown` when the registry cannot be read or holds a malformed side row; an experiment that leaves no trace keeps the answer in the story only, with one line saying so (the line is also a warning of the story's record). The rows of the stand the story selected are read even when `--env` was not given, a side known only from that stand's row is asked "whose is it", a project that has `product.sides` rows has no implied `product` side, a side name holding a dot or an equals sign is refused (it is a key of the story's record), and a relaunch reads the registry again and clears `sides_unknown` once it reads cleanly.

- A story can say that its code is not built yet, and that a side of the product is not real. The no-change questions (`s0.no_change` for a local story, `s1.no_diff` when the scout finds no change) offer a new answer, `not built yet`: the tests are written now from the requirements, what cannot be known yet gets a named placeholder, and the story stops after them and tells you what is missing. The driver records it as `pipeline.sides.product` with `reality: absent`, `deliverable: true`, `source: person`. The answer `ungrounded` no longer promises a "not met" bug at gate B (no code made one); it now reads "go on with the requirements only, on the code the stand runs now; a test that goes red is judged like any red". New launch flags `--side <name>=<reality>` and `--reference <side>=<stand>` (repeatable, kept on a restart like `--mr`): a reality outside `references/side-realities.json` is refused at the command line naming the allowed words and the corrected flag; a side name the project has not recorded is accepted, and when it is not real the driver asks once, in the closed question `sides.deliverable`, whether this story delivers it (`ours`) or another team does (`another team's`). A single-side story is never asked, and a launch whose sides are all real writes no `pipeline.sides` at all, so such a story behaves as before. The scout's charter and `phases/s1.md` carry the same answer. The sides are written into `pipeline.json` in the same write that records S0 (a refused value stops before S0 is recorded and S0 replays); when the launch names a side other than `product`, the record also carries `product: real` (`source: default`); `--side product=absent` is the same as `not built yet` and asks nothing; a curly apostrophe in `another team's` is read as the straight one. The skill's and the README's flag lists name `--side` and `--reference`.

- A registry of what a test assumes, in the automation manifest. `provisional[]` rows (`id` `P-<n>`, `kind`, `what`, `assumed_from`, `home {file, line_hint}`, `dependents`, `settles_on`, `status`, `evidence`) are sent through `manifest_put.py --fragment` and merged by `id`; a field a fragment omits survives. `home_hash` is built by the tool from the line that carries the marker `qa-provisional: P-n` in the row's `home.file`, wherever that line is (`line_hint` is only a hint, so an edit above the line changes nothing); a hash a role sends is dropped, the baseline is kept once the row settles (the tool also stamps `evidence.home_hash_after`), and a marker that cannot be found leaves the row with no hash and is printed. `retracted_provisional: ["P-n"]` keeps the row as history with `status: retracted`; an id that names no row is refused, and a malformed `provisional` (not a list, a row that is no object, an id that is not `P-<n>` or repeats) is refused before the commit. `tests[].provisional` (`[P-n]`) merges with the other fields of the test row. `contract.manifest_provisional` is the one reader: an absent field reads `[]`, and a malformed row is skipped and named in the return value, never raised. The kinds (`placeholder_locator`, `assumed_contract`, `side_substitute`, `reference_value`) are rows of `references/provisional-kinds.json`. `manifest_from_tests.py` writes `sides: {}` on a new test row only when the story has a side that is not `real`; a story with every side real gets the same manifest as before. The `automation-manifest.json` contract and its role slices describe the fields, `design/state-exits.md` has the ways out, and `references/null-outcomes.json` declares the empty outcome. Nothing requires or checks the registry yet, so every story behaves as before.

- The S5 exit now checks the sides of a story and excuses a test that cannot run yet. New family `sides` of `s5_precheck.py` (`check_sides`, called right after the manifest check): C1 a test of a story with a side that is not real declares `sides` (`{}` is legal); C2 the side names in `tests[].sides`, `then_bindings[].about` and `provisional[].settles_on` are sides of the story, compared exactly; C3 a `provisional[]` row has a known kind, a home file that holds its `qa-provisional: P-n` marker (found by the marker, so a line that moved is not an edit), and dependents that are bound Thens; C4 every marker in a test file has a row; C5 a `pending_implementation` row names only instances whose test declares an `absent` side that the story's sides also call `absent`; C6 an open row on a side that is now real, a settled row that does not cite a run block stamped real with a matching hash, and a pending row left standing after every instance ran on real sides are findings. The family is not passable by a person's word; only `sides-undeclared` and `provisional-open-on-real` are, by tag. A first-look placeholder (`placeholder_locator`, `assumed_from: first_look:<R-n>`) on a real side is an accounting row and is not an open-on-real finding. One reader, `acceptance.pending_instances`, excuses an instance from its run mapping (`s5_precheck`), its probe (`window_record`) and its `run_witness` (`check_witness`: a manifest whose every test is pending owes the collect row instead). `run_suite.py --collect-only --tests <ids> -- <test command>` takes one collect and prints the `runs[]` row `kind: collect` (`partial: true` when a file failed to import); it launches nothing and is never a run witness. A story with no `pipeline.sides` and no provisional rows is checked exactly as before. A pending row that names instances is no longer refused as `both-lists` (a green test of a named instance is `pending-but-green`); the window of a pending instance carries the outcome `pending_implementation` (no fingerprint, no evidence, no probe owed) and `validate_window` re-derives the claim, so a record that only says it is a gap; one reader, `acceptance.run_witness_excused`, excuses `run_witness` for an all-handed or all-pending manifest in `check_witness`, the phase JSON check and the handoff derivation; the pending road accepts only a whole (not partial) collect that covers every pending test file; `stage_guard` lets `run_suite.py --collect-only` through while a dispatch is active; `check_sides` takes the window's scope, so a window is not refused over another window's test; the settled-row checks read only the hash the tool stamped and no longer ask a role for it; the marker file is looked up under the root the writer hashes against; after an arrival a standing pending row gives one finding, not two.

- The delivery check now keeps a green that met only a substituted or unknown side apart from a real proof. A covered Then (or a walked manual case) whose run is stamped with a side that is not `real`, whose test does not declare that side `real`, whose stamp carries `sides_unknown`, or whose stamp cannot be read at all, reads `not_verified:on_substitute` or `not_verified:sides_unknown` instead of `passed_green`; a red on a substitute stays a failure, a real green beside a substituted one proves the Then, and a row with no stamp and no non-real declaration reads exactly as before. The run row of a test is found by the one join every other reader uses, so a row the runner spelled differently from the manifest is read too, and a Then whose own test has no green row reads the case's green rows instead of being skipped. A Then that an open first-look placeholder locator stands behind (named in the row's dependents, or proven only by tests that name an open row) reads `not_verified:placeholder_open` until a run settles the row; it sits right after `failed:*` and before the flaky, skipped and hand-off words. All three read as the third verdict `after_checks`, one "Left with you" item per case with its tests and how to run them again, in words of their own in the summary, and the Then table no longer prints `pass` for such a Then. A story held for code (awaiting or stopped) now reads as ONE record `awaiting_implementation` (`delivery_ready: no`, owner product, no bug candidate and no gate B reason; a red a recorded verdict already stands behind keeps its own record) with words by the hold's cause: "waiting for a fix", or "stopped after the first look: the feature does not work yet"; the dashboard card shows the same words with the age of the hold.

- Every execution block now records which sides of the product it ran against. On a story that has a `pipeline.sides` record, a side that is not real, or `pipeline.sides_unknown`, a run block and a manual block carry `sides_met` (side to reality, copied by code at the moment of the run) and, when the sides could not be read, `sides_unknown`; a story with no `pipeline.sides` record, no non-real side and no `sides_unknown` has blocks byte for byte as before. A `pipeline.json` that is present but unreadable (a BOM is read), or a `pipeline.sides` that is not a side record, stamps `sides_unknown` and no `sides_met`, never the default all-real. A reparse copies the stamp of the block it supersedes, an imported run block keeps the stamp it was given at import (the import re-check no longer compares it), and `finalize_task.py` carries it onto every `results[]` and `current_manual_checks[]` row. A walked manual case may carry a record-level `about: [<side>]`, given in the walk verdict or with `manual_evidence.py build --about <side>`; the record check refuses a name that is not a side of the story and names the sides it knows. The qa-runner charter gains one line asking for `about` when the story has a side that is not real.

- A story can now be held for code. The controller keeps one state, `awaiting`, with two causes: `s5_absent_side` (a side the story delivers does not exist yet; held from S6) and `first_look_stop` (the person stopped after the first look; held from S3). While it stands no stage from `held_from` is dispatched, prepared or relaunched (`next` answers `awaiting_implementation`, or the terminal `awaiting_stopped`), a rework of such a stage is refused with its doors, and the stage guard refuses the role's start (a person's recorded word passes it and is journaled as `gate_override`). A rework of the stages before `held_from` runs inside the hold. New controller operations: `await`, `arrive`, `stop_waiting --words-file`, and `first_look_continue --words-file F --source-head H --register-hash R` (the caller's keys are stored as given; it clears a `first_look_stop` hold only, and is refused on `s5_absent_side`, on a stopped story, on empty words, without `H` or with a bad `R`). New purposes `bind`, `reference_walk`, `first_look` and the repair cause `source_arrived` (before `ticket_changed`). `arrive` with nothing held only records the arrival; a stopped story starts no dispatch except the rework the person's words reopen it with (checked where the dispatch commits), and a second `stop_waiting` with the same words after such a reopening is a new decision, not a replay. `stage_guard.py stories` and the archive's open items print the cause and the date; a stopped story is no open item.

- The driver now parks a story that waits for code and takes it up again when the code arrives. After S5, when a side the story delivers does not exist yet, the driver writes `interim-report.md` (assembled by code from the sides, the tests per case, what ran and what each run recorded about the sides, and the open placeholders), records the wait (with its cause and the stage it holds from, and the newest accepted S5 dispatch) and stops with exit 0, also under `--until gate_B`. A relaunch with no flag prints the report again and dispatches nothing; a stopped story prints its stopped line and exits 0. A relaunch with `--mr`, `--branch` or `--commit`, or `--side <name>=real` for a recorded side that is not real yet, records the arrival (`implementation_source`, the sides with `source: arrival`, the controller event `arrive`) after the changed-ticket question is asked and before any rework, also on the run that carries the answer to it; the word survives a question asked in the same process, and a replay after a crash records the same sides. The arrival then owes its own rework, one stage per turn after a changed ticket's: the scout (S1) and the requirements tester (S2) go back over their accepted work and the automator runs the bind round (S5), by cause `source_arrived`. A `--side` word for a name the story never recorded is said and changes nothing. The answers of the new questions have executors: `arrival.not_waiting` (`re-ground`, `ignore`, `stop`) and the `not built yet` answer of `s1.no_diff`, which records the product side as absent like its `s0.no_change` twin. `continue_command` repeats `--side` and `--reference`, and the packet's restart line leaves out the `--side <name>=absent` of a side the story waits for. New priced questions `arrival.not_waiting` and `awaiting.stop`.

- The S5 briefs of the automator and the code critic now name the story's sides, and the automator's brief says what it may assume and must declare. A story that has sides to tell (a sides record, a side that is not real, or an unknown record - the one rule the execution blocks are stamped by) gets side lines in the brief head, read by code from the one sides reader; a record that cannot be read (not an object, or marked unknown) is one line saying no side counts as real, never the all-real default. A side that came from the project knowledge registry and whose row names its `registry_key` is marked `[knowledge:<registry_key>]` so the later measurement can count it reached; a side with no key gets no marker. The header says an absent side cannot be run and a substituted side runs only against its substitute. The automator's brief also names `tests[].sides` (an absent side is written and collected, not run, and listed `pending_implementation`), `then_bindings[].about`, `provisional[]` and `tests[].provisional` when the story has sides to tell or provisional rows exist; the kinds and the reality words are read from their data files, the kinds through the one reader `contract.provisional_kinds`, which the S5 exit check now uses too. The brief of an all-real story is byte-identical to before. The bind round (purpose `bind`, the S5 round after the code arrived) carries its own procedure in the brief and lists only what its dispatch must act on: for the cases of its scope, the open rows whose side is real now and the kept-by-decision rows whose side became real (back to open), a count of open rows still waiting for a side that is not real, and the pending rows split into the instances to run and the ones an absent side still excuses, each with the area-qualified key to retract the row by (`retracted_unresolved`); an empty list is said, and a failure to list is said. The `s5.md` and `s2.md` commands now carry the `--cases` and `--reason` the controller requires. The automator charter gains the third grounding route and the sides and `about` declaration; the code critic charter gains judging `about` and `sides` by the boundary and a mock for a side; the requirements tester charter gains the reconciliation of late-arrived code with the register (`code_says`, `affected`). Role load: qa-automator 19,754 to 19,859, qa-code-critic 18,909 to 19,101, qa-requirements-tester 12,496 to 12,590 tokens.

- The old version of a feature as data: `reference_snapshot.py put|show` keeps `work/reference-snapshot.yaml` (`reference_env`, `walked_at`, `items[]` with `id`, `area`, `user_path`, `observed`, `evidence` paths, `old_test`, `locators_portable`, and `gaps[]`). `put` takes the walk by code (the newest S1 dispatch whose purpose is `reference_walk`) and cites every capture through `walk_session.capture_cited` with the reference stand, so a capture of a first-look walk or of another stand is refused; an item with no capture and no old test is refused, `items: []` needs a gap line, and an existing snapshot is replaced only with `--replace`. Every refusal names a door and writes nothing. A `precedent` Then may now cite `reference:<item>` (second form of `contract.PRECEDENT_REF_RE`); `contract.then_oracle_errors` takes `snapshot_items`, `parity` and `basis` and refuses the form unless the item is in the snapshot and the case basis is `requirement:R-n` of a register row whose new `parity` column says `yes` (`contract.parity_ids` is the one reader, read by header only); `validate_artifacts.check_then_oracles` passes them from the story's own snapshot and register. A claim's `before_ref` still refuses `reference:<item>` (it keeps the `base:` form only). Nothing writes a snapshot or sets `parity` yet, so every story behaves as before. `references/artifact-contract-reference.md` states the shape.

- Reference stands (S-c), the walk and the stand rules: when a side of a story carries a `reference` (the launch flag or the project's record), S1 has one more dispatch after the scout - the runner walks the old version in a `survey` walk session on the reference stand and writes `work/reference-snapshot.yaml` with `reference_snapshot.py put` (a card in `role-commands.json`; `--replace` when S1 is made again over an existing snapshot - a `rework S1` does not open the reference window again, that road is queued); `stages.json` S1 names it as an optional dispatch (purpose `reference_walk`, not a stage role) and S2 reads the snapshot. A story with no reference runs S1 exactly as before. A reference stand's build is never asked: the implicit stand pick skips it, and the runtime probe of a named reference stand compares nothing (`not_applicable`, `no_changed_file`); the story's own stand is still asked.
- The reference is never the stand under test (C8): a run request aimed at it is refused at the entry of `run_suite.py --request` (`run_refused`, exit 2) and by `validate_request`, with a door naming the story's own stand. `reference_snapshot.py` now refuses a usage error with its card, like the other role commands.

- One bug with many manifestations, fix round: a `person` basis of a merge now names its dispatch (`{dispatch, quote}`) and stands only when that dispatch is an S7 rework recorded as the person's words, asked for the cases of the merged draft, and the quote (12 or more non-space characters) is in that dispatch's words (`place_answers.person_words_of` is the one reader, shared with the `person` source of a place answer). The cause facts have one reader, `bug_records.cause_view`, and the bug text, the gate B packet and the report print from it with one phrase for how the cause was confirmed (the run count is a word; a run with no start state is no distinct start state; a basis that no longer stands is never printed as confirmed). The `## Manifestations` lines of the bug text carry each manifestation's case. The gate B door block says "has one cause" only of a confirmed cause; the linked pair also gets its keep-apart option in a mixed packet; a "possibly the same cause" link shows on both rows. An absorbed code-reading manifestation is not asked for `seen` and `start_state` and is marked as found by reading the code; the superseding check reads `manifestations[].requirement`; `bug_neighbours.py` no longer raises inside its own reader.

- A bug draft may now carry the shared cause of several failures and every way it shows (the data shape of "one bug, many manifestations"; nothing refuses on it yet, no role is asked to write it yet). `contract.py` gains the closed words `MECHANISM_STATUSES` (`confirmed`, `unverified`, `unknown`), `MECHANISM_BASIS_KINDS` (`code_line`, `run`, `person`) and the placeholder `BUG_MECHANISM_CUTOFF` (`None`: no draft is owed a `mechanism`). `bug_records.py` gains the readers `draft_cases` (one reader for `case`, `cases` and `manifestations[].case`), `manifestation_refs` and `manifestation_summary`, `draft_requirements` now adds `manifestations[].requirement`, and two problem lists: `mechanism_problems` (shape; a code line stands through the one code-line verifier, a run through the recorder's index; `confirmed` needs a standing entry; a status spelled other than exactly `confirmed`, `unverified` or `unknown` is refused) and `manifestation_problems` (shape; each entry names an APP_BUG triage row or a probe that stands, or is a code-reading draft absorbed with `from_draft`; a red test or the reason there is none; the first entry is the draft's own row). A draft with neither key yields no problem. `place_answers.capture_stands` is the capture check lifted out of the answer check so a mechanism's run and a manifestation's probe are judged by the same reader. The analyst's key page (`bug-drafts/*.json`) lists the new keys with their empty outcomes and marks `siblings` as legacy (nothing reads it; `possibly_same_cause` replaces it).

- One bug with many manifestations now reaches the S7 claim, the gate B rehearsal and the bug text (`bug_records.py`, `handoff_check.py`, `gate_preflight.py`): an APP_BUG row that a draft's `manifestations[].triage_row` names is covered by that draft (never a row with `blocking_check`; `pair_drafts` stays pure and gains `manifestation_no_row` and `manifestation_not_app_bug`), and the blocker's cases are read through `draft_cases`. A draft that merges 2+ manifestations under a cause the factory cannot re-read (no `mechanism`, a status other than `confirmed`, a basis that does not stand: `merged_unconfirmed`) is refused at the S7 claim and is a finding with the person's door at the rehearsal; a manifestation that names no row or a non-APP_BUG row is refused the same way, and the same-place refusal names the `manifestations` door. The rehearsal asks the critic's roll-call about every case of a merged draft, and asks a new triage draft for `mechanism` only once `BUG_MECHANISM_CUTOFF` is a day (nothing is asked while it is `None`). `mechanism.statement` is now required when the status is `confirmed` or `unverified`, and the first manifestation is the draft's own row when the two name the same instance (a bare instance and its full key are one row). The bug text of a draft with 2+ manifestations adds `## Cause` and `## Manifestations` (all of them, no cap); a draft with one manifestation or none gets the same text, byte for byte.

- A bug that shows in several ways is now one bug in the trace, the dashboard board and the report (node N3a of "one bug, many manifestations"; no role is asked to write the new draft keys yet, so an ordinary draft reads exactly as before). The trace's bug record reads a draft's cases through `bug_records.draft_cases` (so `case` no longer hides `cases`, and a case that only a manifestation names finds its bug through `bug_for`), takes the requirements of every manifestation, and carries the lines of the ways it shows, the cause (status, statement, how it was confirmed, claims nobody verified) and the drafts it may share a cause with. The dashboard's bug row lists every case of a merged draft. In the report, under a bug that shows in two or more ways, one line says the cause and how it was confirmed (by the line of the application code, by trying it from n starting states, or both), one line per way it shows, none cut, and a "Not verified:" line for every claim nobody verified; a cause that is only a hypothesis, or one whose evidence can no longer be re-read, is never printed as confirmed; a bug the analyst suspects shares a cause with another is told "Possibly the same cause as <row number> (not verified)". A bug with one way and no link prints the same bytes as before. A new test, `test_draft_readers.py`, fails when any script other than `bug_records.py` reads a draft's `case`/`cases` by hand again (with a planted-line control inside it).

- Gate B now shows a bug that was drafted from several ways it shows (t-2187 N3b): the head says how many ways it shows ("one cause" only when the cause is confirmed), a cause line says how it was confirmed in words, a claim no evidence confirms is printed as "Not verified", a cause that is unknown is printed as "Cause not established: <why>" and never as a cause, a stated cause that is not verified is printed as "Possible cause, not verified: <statement>" followed by the reason, the ways are listed a), b), ... (six at most, then how many more; the bug's readable text holds them all), and a draft linked as possibly sharing a cause says so by the other bug's number. One question follows the list ("One bug or several"): for a bug with several ways it offers `file`, `split` (these are different bugs) and `not a bug`; for bugs linked as possibly the same cause (a link counts from either side, a chain is one group, a link to a bug not shown in the packet counts for nothing) it offers `merge`, and when no bug has several ways the block says the factory suspects one cause but could not confirm it and offers `merge` or `file` (file them as separate bugs); each option has its three price lines; no code reads `split` or `merge`, the conductor does. A case a bug names only in one of its ways is no longer reported as "no draft speaks for it" and is an item of the packet. A bug with one way, no stated cause and no link renders exactly as before.

- One cause, one bug report: the bug reporter's charter now says defects with one confirmed cause are one report listing every manifestation, each with its own steps and failing test, and a suspected shared cause is a link between separate reports. `artifact_producer.py validate` reads the source draft of a bug through the one draft reader; when that draft has two or more manifestations the bug file must list every case in `cases`, carry `## Cause` and `## Manifestations`, and name in the latter each manifestation's case and its red test command or the reason there is none. A draft that cannot be read is one refusal that names the door; with no task root the check is not run and the validator says so instead of passing it. A draft with one manifestation, or none, files exactly as before. The bug-file section of the key page names the two new sections.

- The failure analyst, the manual-agent runner, the explore charter and the doc scribe carry the experience of one bug with many manifestations: lay the red rows side by side before drafting, name the mechanism, vary the start state (empty or filled, selected or erased, previous value, stock) to discriminate the cause, say how far the cause is confirmed, merge only on a confirmed cause, and the scribe returns a merge the cause does not explain. The analyst's tools line points to the neighbourhood command `bug_neighbours.py` in place of the one-draft-per-location clause.

- New `bug_neighbours.py --task-root <task root>` prints the neighbourhood table of an S7 triage: the failures, observations, triage rows and drafts that share a requirement, a case, a test file, a code line (the same normaliser `same_location` uses) or an equal seen text, with the shared value. It is a hint for the failure analyst and the scribe, never a verdict: it reads only, writes no file, and says nothing about whether two units are one cause. A source it cannot read is named as unreadable instead of reading as an empty table. The S7 triage brief carries the table cut to `brief_neighbours_max` groups (`references/place-answers.json`) with the command for the rest, and the failure analyst's and the scribe's command cards list the command.

- A `bug` place answer whose draft was absorbed into a merged draft (a manifestation of a live draft names it in `from_draft`) is now settled through that merged draft, when the merged draft's own step holds or the manifestation's evidence is the answer's own capture; it is no longer a gap at the close. A place whose draft is simply gone, or named by two merged drafts, stays a gap as before.

- One bug with many manifestations: the phase text and the cutoff land. `phases/s7.md` tells the analyst to draft one bug per mechanism (`mechanism`, `manifestations`) and names `bug_neighbours.py --task-root <task root>` on the skill road; `phases/s8.md` sends the gate B words `split` and `merge` to `rework --stage S7` with the person's words and has a `split` of drafts that share a `defect_location` write `distinct_defect`. Every triage draft created on or after 2026-11-10 is now asked for `mechanism` at the gate B rehearsal (`contract.BUG_MECHANISM_CUTOFF`, read only by the new `contract.mechanism_owed`, the same day rule as `red_test_owed`); older drafts and code-reading drafts are not asked. A `person` basis entry of a mechanism now stands when its quote is found in the words the factory recorded for a rework of S7 (`bug_records.recorded_person_words`); with no quote, no record or no match it does not stand. The bug text of a merged bug closes its `## Manifestations` with "After the fix, re-check every manifestation; one that still fails is a separate bug."; the rehearsal reads a draft's primary case through `draft_cases`.

- The hold after S5 for an absent side now asks whose the side is. Once the hold is recorded and the interim report printed, the driver raises the closed question `awaiting.absent_side` over the first absent side this story delivers (`not ours` / `relaunch`, with prices), in plain words: what the factory waits for and what each answer does. `not ours` records the side as another team's and substituted for this story (`deliverable false`, `reality substituted`, by the person), keeps the person's words in the project's record of sides (the same writer as the answer at the start of a story, by the driver; an experiment with `--no-trace` and an unreadable registry keep the answer in the story only and say so in one line, which also lands in the story's warnings for the report and gate A), and lifts the hold with the controller's own `arrive` naming that side, so the run goes on with the side substituted; a second story of the project is not asked, and a later word that the side is ours overwrites the row (history kept). `relaunch` leaves the hold standing and is kept for that hold only. Another word goes to the conductor. The question is asked on every entry into the hold, not only the first: with several absent sides each is asked on its own, a `relaunch` on one goes on to ask the next in the same run, an answer never changes another side, and a later bare relaunch of a hold whose sides all said `relaunch` asks again with a lead that names the earlier answer and its date; a crash or a lost question file asks again too. The refusal of `first_look_continue` on such a hold and the doors `next` lists name this answer; the interim report no longer says nothing is asked of the person and names the answer.

- A run aimed at a reference stand (the stand that runs the OLD version of a side) is no longer refused: it goes, and it is recorded as a sample. Its run block carries a `reference_run` mark (the stand, the side, "not the story's code") and is written to `work/reference-runs`, never to `work/run-blocks`, so the reducer, the ledger, the proof stamp and the delivery verdict never read it as the story's evidence; the report names it ("a run on the reference stand - a sample, not the story's result") and counts it apart. A reparse of a sample stays a sample. A run block with no mark (older runs) reads as the story's own stand, as before. The record that names the story's own stand ALSO as the reference of a side is still refused at validation and at `run_suite.py --request` entry (a data contradiction, with the record as the door). Read through `stand_identity.reference_run_mark` and `stand_identity.reference_runs`.
- Every test the report shows now says whether its result came from real code or from a mock. `ledger.real_or_mock` writes the words on each ledger test row (`real_or_mock`): `real code`; `on a mock: <side> — kept by the person's decision (date not recorded)` for a test with a `kept_by_decision` row (the row carries no date field, so none is guessed); `on a mock: <side> — the side was substituted` for a test proven while its side was substituted (each mocked side is listed); `real or mock: not established` for an unreadable stamp, `sides_unknown` or an unreadable `provisional` field (an unknown is never `real code`). The `## Proven` lines carry it, a green stays green, and the check that holds the report against the ledger (`check_report_left_with_you`) names a test line with no mark, and a ledger that names a mock the report never mentions. A ledger written before the field existed is not checked. The scribe's `Left with you` form names the field for each test an item lists. Role load: qa-doc-scribe 17,944 to 17,959 tokens (process 16,954 to 16,969).

- `rework S1` of a story whose side carries a reference stand now re-enters the S1 reference window: the scout's rework leaves S1 open, the runner walks the old version again and its snapshot is put with `--replace`. This holds on every road that reworks or finishes the S1 scout: the code road, the relaunch road of the person's rework, the ticket-changed rework (it reworks the scout, not the window's runner), and a plain relaunch, a resume or a saved result of the scout (S1 stays open and the next entry runs the window). A resumed role of a survey walk (the reference window, the first look) gets its walk session back on the stand its record names, and the session is closed when the role ends; a walk that never started is not reopened. The runner's reference-window brief names the snapshot contract (`references/artifact-contract-reference.md`). The manifest's merge request (a bare number, `!n`, or a link in any form, leading zeros dropped) is read by ONE reader, `vcs_evidence.mr_iid`, for the MR receipt of the base slice and for the head asked of the remote by the first look. `project_knowledge.py side --deliverable` says when a `--stand` beside it was not used (the answer is the project's); a later word about whose a side is overwrites the value, the earlier row stays as history. Pinned: a side re-read after a relaunch with no recorded answer keeps the default `ours`.

- Walk session: a new `survey` place (`walk_session.py open --place survey`) is the first look at a story or a reference stand. Its attempts go under `work/evidence/manual/survey-<item>/aN/`, the stand lease is held for the session's life and no request takes a lease of its own, it has no case verdict (the refusal names `first_look.py put` / `reference_snapshot.py put`), and the close writes the timing. `open` and `serve` take `--env <name>`: the `environments[]` row of that exact name (case counts; an unknown name is refused naming the stands there are) and only that stand's hosts are reachable; without `--env` every existing place walks the first row exactly as before. The walk record now names `place`, `stand`, `profiles` and `attempts`, and the new `capture_cited` returns "" only when a quote is words of a capture file of THIS survey walk's attempt of the item on the named stand, else the reason with its door.

- Walk session: `http <METHOD> <path|url> [--body-file <file>]` is a step of `walk_session.py step`, beside the screen steps. It sends one request on the walk's stand as the request's actor (a path is joined to the stand's `base_url`; a full URL must be on the walk's hosts, checked by the walk before any step runs and again at the send), and keeps the evidence the screen steps keep: one JSON document of request and answer in the item's attempt (the one body cut and the one base64 rule, headers redacted, the actor's account hidden, a secret in the answer saves nothing and leaves no excerpt), a quote check by `capture_cited`, and `surprise:` lines for a 3xx (a redirect is never followed), 4xx or 5xx answer, a redirect to a foreign host and an unreadable JSON body; the default stop rule reads the 5xx number. The single request of `manual_capture.py http` and the walk step now share ONE executor, `http_call`. A survey walk of a project with no profile that fits a UI capture has no browser: its record says `profiles: {http: <id>}`, each named actor signs in once by the HTTP request the project records (the actor's own stored account, not only `default`; an actor with no known HTTP sign-in leaves the walk open and its steps end `failed` with `http_sign_in_unknown`), and a screen word is refused whole; a project with neither a UI nor an HTTP profile refuses `open` (exit 2, cause `no_reachable_surface`). Walks with a screen and walks that make no HTTP step run as before.
- Walk `http` step, fix round: an `http` step is sent on the walk's OWN stand only (a walk with no `--env` no longer lets the first stand's Bearer token reach another stand's host); the request secret scan skips the headers code itself sets (`redact_headers`), so a JWT Bearer login through `manual_capture.py http` is accepted as before; `step --final` on a walk with no screen is refused with the walk's door; a malformed redirect `Location` is a `surprise:` line, not a crash; `http` joins `steps.type.keeps_run`; a survey walk whose only fitting profile is HTTP (a single `api` profile) has no browser.

- First look: a new `first_look.py` keeps the record of the first look at the new version on the stand (`work/first-look.yaml`) and the attempt that walks it (`state/first-look-attempt.json`). The walker sends one YAML row per requirement of the register with `first_look.py put` (a status, `blocked_by` for a `missing` or `unreachable` row, where it lives on the stand, and the capture that shows it, tied to this walk's attempt of that requirement through `walk_session.capture_cited`); code writes the walk, the stand, the stand build (`confirmed` only on a `deployed` word of the person at the one implementation head), the code heads map, the register hash and `sides_met` itself and ignores the walker's values for them; a first look that was not walked is `put --null <reason>` with empty rows and one gap line. `current_keys` is the one producer of the heads text and register hash that `first_look_continue` stores, `read` is the one reader (stale on other code or another register), `share` is the reachable share without `access` and `nature` rows against the floor `first_look.reachable_floor_percent` (default 30), `due` is the pure question whether a walk is owed (no code yet, empty or unreadable register, no stand, an attempt on the same heads, one retry of a walk that could not be opened) and `continued` compares the person's `continue` with the current keys. The closed words are `references/first-look-statuses.json`; the form is `references/artifact-contract-first-look.md`. Nothing in the existing stages calls it yet. `role-commands.json`: the `walk_session.py open` card names the survey place for `qa-runner`. `role-commands.json` also carries the `first_look.py put` (rows file only; the null record is the driver's) and `first_look.py show` cards for `qa-runner`. `put` refuses a `blocked_by` on a `confirms` or `contradicts` row, refuses when the code or the register changed since the walk was opened (the driver opens a new attempt), and `put --null` never replaces a walked record that is still current. The words the code checks (`blocked_by_required_for`, `share_excludes`, `no_capture_needed`, `attempt_settled`) are data in `first-look-statuses.json`; the attempt is written through `event_store.atomic_json`; `work/first-look.yaml` and `state/first-look-attempt.json` are in the collect sets.

- The first look has its place in the flow. S3 may carry one optional `qa-runner` dispatch of purpose `first_look` before the strategist's first window (no new stage, the stage numbers do not change), and `work/first-look.yaml` is an input of S3 to S7 and of the case critic's and code critic's briefs; a missing, unreadable or `null` record reads "no first look" and a record walked on other code reads STALE. The runner's brief for that dispatch names the open survey walk and its stand, the screen and HTTP test profiles, each requirement with the path of its text, the walk commands with the `http <METHOD> <path> [--body-file <file>]` step, `first_look.py put`, the contract and the form's words, the sides of the story that are not real, and the accounts the factory already has by role (names only, never a key or a value); the brief of any other dispatch is unchanged. That brief carries no case-walk tail: its goal and DoD are the first look's, its final-message path is `work/first-look.yaml`, and its ahead card says `first_look.py put` checks the record. The runner signs in only as the actors the walk was opened with. The qa-runner charter gains a `First look` craft paragraph.

- The first look reaches the roles that read it. The head of the S3 briefs (strategist and the plan's reviewer), the S4 briefs (case designer; case critic), the S5 briefs (automator; code critic), S6 (runner) and S7 (failure analyst) gains lines from `work/first-look.yaml` through one function, `brief_pack.first_look_lines`: counts by status, the red rows with their reason, the sides that are not real and an unestablished stand build at S3; the paths walked at S4; the locators, routes and data seen, ahead of the automator's own discovery, at S5; the record path and the rule on a diverging step or a rediscovered selector for the two critics; "the width was walked, do not repeat the survey; your cases are still walked step by step" at S6; the red rows with the question "is there an executed check, if not a bug candidate" at S7. At most 12 lines per brief, then `+N more: work/first-look.yaml`; a line about one requirement carries `[first-look:R-n]`; no record, a `null` record, an unreadable one and a stale one are each one line; no line carries a seen value as an expected one (data values and samples are prefixed `seen:`). The case critic's S4 brief also carries the product's roles (`[knowledge:product.roles]`). The app card gains a `First look` section after `Entry routes` (at most 20 requirements, 8 lines each, 200 characters a line; it collapses to a pointer before the routes are cut), and its hash covers the record. The strategist, case designer and case critic charters and `explore-charter.md` gain a short craft paragraph each; the `precedent` form in `artifact-contract.md` (and its case designer slice) names `reference:<item>`. Role-load ratchets raised to the measured load (J-15): `ratchet_tokens` qa-test-strategist 16,854 to 16,925, qa-case-designer 13,269 to 13,331, qa-case-critic 18,271 to 18,308; `process_ratchet_tokens` qa-case-designer 12,072 to 12,094 (qa-case-critic stays at its measured 15,941, below the merged 15,942). The closed first-look words the briefs use (`red_statuses`, `bug_candidate_blocked_by`, `stand_build_confirmed`) live in `references/first-look-statuses.json`, and `first_look.state` is the one classification of the record's state for the card and the briefs.

- The driver walks the first look before the plan. At the start of S3 (before `s3_prepare` and window 1) `Driver.first_look_step` asks `first_look.due`: when no look is due it writes the null record with its reason (a specific reason already written for these heads is kept) and the plan is made as before; when one is due it opens the survey walk for the register's requirements on the story's stand, registers the optional `qa-runner` dispatch of purpose `first_look` named by the S3 row of `optional_dispatches` in `stages.json`, and runs it. The controller no longer refuses that dispatch for lacking an `execution_kind` (one predicate, `controller.runner_kind_required`, for `prepare` and `apply`; every other runner dispatch is refused as before). `story_step.py start` admits a `(role, purpose)` row of `optional_dispatches` without making it a role of the stage, and its `finish` never completes the stage with it; `stage_guard` places the dispatch on its stage and the exit gate judges it by its own output (`work/first-look.yaml`), not by S6's or S3's plan files. Walk actors: the accounts the factory has first (the stand's default login, then the project's roster in its own order), `guest` in a slot left over; an account that exists but was not opened is named to the runner, which records `unreachable` / `access` naming it (`first_look.walk_actors`, one reader for the driver and the runner's brief). A walk that cannot be opened ends the attempt `open_failed` (retried once on the same code; `no_reachable_surface` is not retried), writes the null reason and asks nothing. A dispatch that was not accepted keeps its attempt (a record `put` wrote stays `written`), the plan goes on at once and nothing is asked over it. When the share of requirements the stand showed in an ACCEPTED record is under the floor (`first_look.reachable_floor_percent`, default 30) the closed question `first_look.dead` (`continue` / `stop`, with prices) is asked, once per walk: any answer marks the walk asked (`first_look.mark_asked`); `continue` goes to `controller.py --operation first_look_continue` with the keys of `first_look.py show --json`, `stop` holds the story with cause `first_look_stop` from S3; the machine's `take_answer` now routes the answer to its executor. `first_look.py show --json` also prints `due` and `share`. The exit gate's window-1 test looks only at strategist dispatches that count (`exit_gate.s3_strategist_records`). The S3 phase card carries the same commands for the conductor.

- A story the person stopped after the first look (`first_look_stop`) now has its own report, its own question and its own arrival. The hold prints the first look's report (`interim_packet.first_look_packet`: what the stand showed, the requirements it did not reach with the evidence the walker cited, the code the look was about, the day the story stopped, the restart command) instead of the S5 packet; a story stopped by the person's words prints a line naming the first look. A relaunch with no flag compares, per repository, the head the first look recorded with the head the same source has now (`git ls-remote` in the repository's checkout: `refs/merge-requests/<number>/head` for a merge request, whether the manifest writes a bare number, `!42` or a link, then the entry's own branch when that gives nothing; a commit alone does not move): one repository moved, or the manifest names an implementation the record does not, and the code arrives; otherwise the closed question `first_look.same_code` (`wait` / `source` / `continue`, with prices) is asked, with one line for every repository whose head could not be established (never read as "moved"); after a `wait` the next question names the day of that answer. `continue` is the same `first_look_continue` operation as for `first_look.dead`. A flag on the hold (`--mr`, `--branch`, `--commit`, or `--side <s>=real` for a side not yet real) records the arrival and owes the reading of the story again against the new code (S1, S2) and then the flow from S3: no bind round and no affected-rows rework, since S5 never ran.

- A red test of an element the first look saw missing is now accounted, never excused, on a real side. The S5 exit check accepts one provisional row on a real side: a `placeholder_locator` with `assumed_from: first_look:<R-n>`, and only while the first-look record (read through its one reader, fresh) holds that requirement `missing` or `unreachable` with `blocked_by: product`; a record that is absent, unreadable, stale or null, a row of another requirement, a `confirms` row and a `blocked_by` of `access` or `nature` each refuse it. `references/provisional-kinds.json` gains `on_real` per kind (`first_look_only` for the placeholder locator, `never` for the rest; a kind without it reads `never`), so a substitute, an assumed contract or a copied reference value on a real side stays refused. For every test linked to an open row (it names the row in `tests[].provisional`, or it is bound to a Then of the row's `dependents`) the exit now requires the declaration (also from a test that does not touch the placeholder: a needless declaration costs only a re-pass line, a missing one a green on a placeholder), refuses a `blocked_by_env` row, a hand-off to the person, and a missing, skipped, xfail, deselected or collect-only run, and refuses a `tests[].provisional` id that is no row of `provisional[]`. The ledger no longer reads a hand-off, an environment block or a `disposition: skip` / `unverifiable` decision in place of `not_verified:placeholder_open`: a Then behind an open placeholder reads `placeholder_open` there too, while a red stays `failed:*`; the predicate of an open row is now public (`ledger.open_placeholder_rows`) and read by both. The grounding rule does not change. The contract text of the automation sides section, the automator charter (the first look comes before its own discovery; an element the first look saw missing is a failing test, never a skip) and the code critic charter (a selector or route found again where the first look saw it is a finding; the declaration is accounting, not a claim of reliance) say so. Role load: qa-automator 19,859 to 20,149, qa-code-critic 19,101 to 19,373 tokens (process 18,466 to 18,607 and 17,430 to 17,571).

- Counters of the first look and of what the factory knew (`report_facts.py`, facts keys `first_look_measure` and `knowledge_use`): the price of the first-look dispatch by the story's own journal, the reachable share, whether the dead-share question was asked and what the person answered, the attempt's outcome, the `placeholder_open` plan rows at delivery, and the number of stand needs and gaps the first-look record named. ONE function, `report_facts.knowledge_use(task_root)`, counts the USE of each fact the story KNEW, that is a registry fact recorded before the story began (a fact the story itself taught is not one it ignored; a row or a story with no time reads `unmeasured`): whether a brief named the element with its `[knowledge:...]` marker on the same line (an account pair has no brief carrier, so its reach reads `unmeasured`) and whether it was used (a role in the strategist's `product_roles`; an account pair is used when none of the cards gate A SHOWED, from `state/driver-state.json`, is the pair's; a side taken from the registry); for a first-look row whether a brief carried its `[first-look:R-n]` marker, whether a seen locator or API route stands in an S5 test home, and whether an S4 case cites `first_look:R-n` (the count of S5 probes on seen elements reads `unmeasured`: no S5 probe record keeps a selector). A counter whose carrier is absent or unreadable reads `unmeasured: <why>`, never 0, including counter-metric (2) beside a registry that cannot be read. The keys are present only for a story with a first look or a registry fact it knew before it began. The retro now prints the question count with its counter-metrics and one table of reached / used / not used, with the finding lines "the first-look record was not read" and "a known fact did not reach a decision"; a count of zero questions is printed only with its counter-metrics. Counters never refuse and never judge how well a fact was used.

- Gate A for a story with a reference (S-c): the packet gets one block about the old version, in words - the behaviour claims that differ from it or are not known to, the requirements that ask to match it with nothing seen of it, what was seen and neither a test case uses nor a difference shows (named, up to 8, then the count), the gaps of the walk, and one count line (`N of M behaviours ... are carried over as they are`); it says that what was seen of the old version is a sample and not evidence for the story, and that the approval confirms which requirements ask to match it (or that it confirms none). Every behaviour seen is also written, by its words and marked carried over / differs / used by no test case, to `work/reference-behaviours.md` beside the gate A message, and the count line and "The long documents" point to it. A story that matches on every behaviour gets one line with the count and no heading; a snapshot that is absent or cannot be read gets one plain sentence and the rest of the brief as it is for a story with no reference; a requirements list that cannot be read is said, never read as "no difference". A story with no reference gets exactly the packet it got before. A behaviour claim may now cite `before_ref: reference:<item>` (an item of the story's reference snapshot; the requirements tester's charter says when); the S2 register check and the S3 claim projector accept it only for an item the story's snapshot holds, and refuse it (as before) when there is no snapshot. The charter sentence raises the requirements tester's start load ratchet 12616 -> 12649 (process 11266 -> 11299).

- Driver and checks: a ticket rework of S3 now goes to the plan's author even when a first look was accepted after it; `s3_window` and `s3_author_done` read the strategist's records through the one reader; the owner words of an open question (`po_ba`, `dev_arch`, `qa`) are one list in `handoffs/vocabulary.yaml`, and the S2 readiness check and the S3 `new_questions` check both refuse an unlisted word with the same sentence.

- Test harness: `selftest.py` reads an optional `scripts/tests/test-layers.json` (keep / quarantine rows, one reader `test_layers()`), filters quarantined files out of every shard, `--fast` and the plain run before sharding, reports files in neither section when `enforce_listing` is on (they still run), and gains `--quarantined` / `--watch-out PATH` for a measurement run of the quarantine with a JSON watch record. With no such file the runner behaves as before.

- Test harness: `scripts/tests/test-layers.json` now exists with the keep list (one row per test file the canon keeps, with its layer, reason and the modules and data files it covers) and the files held by unmigrated role-text pins; nothing is quarantined and listing is not enforced, so the canon runs exactly the same files. The fixture-to-owner map moved out of `selftest.py` into the `fixture_owners` section of that file, and `selftest.py --quarantined` no longer hides a failing check flag given in the same call.

- Test harness: `scripts/tests/scenario_walk.py`, the scenario walker. A recorded synthetic story is walked stage by stage through the package's own doors (exit gate, joint check, `story_step start`, the gate brief and the gate decision road, the delivery assessment), each on a copy of one shared world; a facet with no carrier is a NOTE line, a red line names story, stage and facet, and `--witness-for <path>` names the scenario tests and keep rows that judge a changed path. Its own table is `test_scenario_walk.py`, over the hand-assembled fixture `fixtures/synthetic-scenario/`.

The walk covers the exit gate of stages S1..S4, the S2 hand-over and the recorded gate A question and words; a facet that today's code refuses where the recorded run was accepted stays red and names its story, stage and facet.

- Test fixture: the story `cart-1` (`scripts/tests/fixtures/stories/cart-1/`), a scrubbed recorded run of the synthetic MyBooks task CART-1 captured by `tools/story_capture.py`, and its scenario test `scripts/tests/test_scenario_cart_1.py` (`scenario_walk.run("cart-1")`). The walk covers the exit gate of stages S1..S9, the recorded gate A and gate B words, and the delivery word; a stage that today's code refuses where the recorded run was accepted stays red and names its story, stage and facet.

- Test quarantine, pin-held files: a test file listed in `pin_holds` of `scripts/tests/test-layers.json` no longer blocks the first quarantine-enter; it is not moved, stays in the canon as a listed file (`selftest.py` with `enforce_listing` runs it and prints no `unlisted:` line), and the enter summary and commit message print `held by pins: <n>`. Each keep row covers the helper modules of `scripts/tests/` it imports and the fixture its owner row names, so the changed-path witness finds the detector behind a helper; the `named_by` lines count line breaks the way an editor does; a quarantine row with a non-numeric `seconds` is refused by name.

- Test side only: the scenario walker (`scripts/tests/scenario_walk.py`) reads one vocabulary for a gate decision and a question kind (`GATE_ACTIONS`, `QUESTION_KINDS`), compares the `handed` facet with the required inputs of the recorded handoff form (a template path or a folder is a NOTE, not a failure), starts the next stage with the start arguments the recorded dispatch carries, cuts the world before the next stage's first dispatch by itself, takes `cut_before_seq` per facet, and copies worlds without the slow permission calls. Story `cart-1` is re-recorded through the capture tool and walks the `handed` facets of S2..S8.
