- Requirements register template: names the `norms_list: true` marker of the one norms-list question again (the sentence was lost); role rules register: four rows (the designer card's `sufficiency_review` and `reuse_decision` vocabulary, the critic card's `Over the plan case budget:` line, the template marker).

- Role rules: the mandatory rules of the role texts are one register, `design/role-rules.json`, read by one script (`scripts/role_rules.py --check`) and checked by one test (`test_role_rules.py`) and by `selftest.py --limits`; a rule is a row of a few of its own words (the anchor) that must stand exactly once in each file a role reads it in, so a rule cut from a role text to fit a size cap turns red with the row and the door named; twelve text-pin test files (`test_blocked_by_env_texts.py`, `test_case_role_twins.py`, `test_case_roles_twin_rules.py`, `test_critic_lines_hf2.py`, `test_detection_role_texts.py`, `test_gate_continuation_texts.py`, `test_mixed_then_texts.py`, `test_recommended_rule.py`, `test_red_then_texts.py`, `test_s7_control_experiment_texts.py`, `test_scout_conflict_rule.py`, `test_time_fork_rule.py`) are replaced by it (test-diet TD-5).

- A second `type` on the same field with no step between no longer puts the focus back: it goes on with the typing, as a person does. When the page took the focus away, the keys go where the focus is and the step is not ok (`focus lost before the call: keys went to <what has focus>`, plus a `surprise:` line); a field gone from the page is a failed step with nothing typed. A `click` or any other step between two `type` calls starts the typing afresh. The walk charter says a string typed in a row is ONE `type` call and a recorded focus loss is a finding.

- Failure analyst places: one `bug` answer of a place now lifts every draft of that place (a second draft of the same place no longer stays unconfirmed with "the walk was of another place"); a bug draft with no `confirmation` word now reads "unconfirmed" in the gate B packet, the report, delivery and the board; a `bug` answer no longer settles a place while another draft of that place stands unconfirmed, and the refusal names that draft's own reasons and only the doors that exist (add a `walk` entry citing the record when it has none, merge it into the answer's draft when it is the same bug, or leave it and the close names the place as a gap); the place-answer reader and the walk-receipt check share one JSON reader, and `places` is split into one helper per source.

- A failure rule lifted with `restore_request` is out of what the closing `capture post_action` checks: its result (`requests failed: N`) is written at the lifting, and only a rule still on can refuse the capture. A rule lifted with no match says `surprise: fail_request <glob> matched no request` in the `restore_request` answer and in the first `look` or `read` after it. At the boundary between two items of a walk session every rule the previous item left is lifted and forgotten, its result goes into that item's evidence, and the next item never sees it. A `fail_request` pattern with a single leading `*` (no `**`, no scheme) gets a hint that `*` does not cross `/` (write `**/api/x`); it is a hint, never a refusal. A `press` or `paste` right after a `type` on the same field goes on without a new focus, with the same fact as `type` when the page took the focus away.

- New step `end-session` (browser surface, in a `ui` call and in a walk session): it deletes every cookie of the current actor's browser context and leaves the page open, as for a person whose session ran out, so the next request of the page goes without the session cookie. The answer says how many cookies were deleted; an actor with none (a guest, one not signed in, a second `end-session` in a row) gets `0 cookies` said aloud, not a failure. No cookie name or value is stored. A device has no such step and its steps file naming it is refused with the device's own list. A step that takes no argument now refuses an extra one with the door `write <step> alone on its line`.

- Walk lanes with an account key (`story_run.py`, `walk_timing.py`): an `env:<login key>` account is looked up in the stand's records
  (`credentials_by_role`) by its login key, the way `--as` reads them; exactly one role with the key opens the walk session. A lane whose
  accounts cannot open a walker session - no pair, two roles with the key, a role the stand does not list, no two-key note, an account no
  machine can check, more accounts than a walk holds, a request that cannot be read - is no longer walked on the old road and no longer stops
  the run with a question: each of its cases is recorded `not walked: <reason>` in the story's words, one finding is filed per lane, and the
  next lane walks. Only a failed session open takes the old road. `walk_timing.py` leaves the items the driver marked `walk_old_road` out of
  every figure and names them, with or without a timed walk.

- A code-only close of a stage (`controller.py --operation code_only`) no longer waits for a dispatch whose session is over: one the liveness reader finds abandoned or never started does not hold the close, and one that returned but was never accepted does not hold it either. Every dispatch of the closing and earlier stages that stopped and was never accepted is set aside by the receipt (`superseded`, `passed_over_by`), so the story goes on to the next stage; the receipt, the stage entry and one finding per dispatch name it ("returned, never accepted", "abandoned", "stopped, never accepted"), and the report's "Left with you" carries a line for each. A dispatch that is alive or whose state cannot be read (including a reader that fails) still refuses, and the refusal names the dispatch, its role and stage, and the door (wait for it, or release it with the person's word). The driver's question for a close held only by an earlier stage is offered even when a dead dispatch is still marked running.

- `manifest_put.py` refuses a `tests[]` row whose `assertion_id` (`<file>:<line>`) names a line that holds no check, before the commit (`assertion_line_problems`): the refusal names the line, the nearest check below it as the door (`<file>:<m>`) or says that none follows. In live runs 7 of 41 ids stood one line above their check (a blank line), so a probe aimed there proved nothing. A check counts when it starts on the line or its statement spans it, by the one reader the probe uses (`probe_by_code.check_on_line`, imported only when an id is being written or changed). Only a row that writes or changes its id is looked at; a language with no reader, an unreadable or unparsable file, a path outside the project and an id of another form are one printed note, never a refusal and never a silent pass.

- `selftest.py` now marks a test file red with `ran nothing: add a script entry` when it exits 0, defines `test_*` functions (read from the parsed source) and its output shows no executed check (no tally with a non-zero total, no pytest summary with a passed or failed test); fourteen pytest-style test files that the selftest could not see got the one-line pytest entry (`-p no:cacheprovider`) and now run their checks.

- Conductor: the card now names a command that exists for writing one field of a handover form, `handoff_check.py --file <form> --set <field>="<word>"` (it named `handoff.py fill`, a library with no command line, which exited 0 and changed nothing); and `handoff_check.py --set` of a word the field already reads now says `nothing changed: <field> already reads <word>` instead of a silent success.

- The S1 and S2 handoff forms, the S2 phase file and the S2 brief now say the implementation diff file is absent for source `current-code` as well as `ungrounded`, matching the S1 exit.

- The S1 exit now refuses `stage_done.py --set implementation_source=current-code` while `work/impl-diff*.txt` holds a line, so the scout hears about a stub diff file on its own exit instead of the conductor hearing it from the S3 entry. The refusal says what is wrong, what is expected and the two doors (delete the file, or record `diff`); nothing is written. The scout charter and the S1 phase state the requirement before the work: with `current-code` no diff file is written. A blank or absent file passes, and a story whose source is not `current-code` is unchanged.

- Plan contract: the strategist's slice now says every plan row carries `schema_version: 2` (the example row carries it), and the refusal of a row that is not on schema version 2 names the exact key and the number 2, and says so when the row holds a look-alike key such as `coverage_schema_version`; the refusal of a plan was 20 rows long on a key the role had never been told.

- Gate A: a question the person already answered in the question register is no longer listed as "cannot be answered as it stands"; the shape check now asks the register (the one reader of a question's status, through `question_register.matches`, shared with the gate brief's open-question list) as well as the question's own `answer`. The register's answer belongs to the FIRST row of an id: a later, different row with the same id is still checked as it stands. In the gate brief's open-question list the same rule holds: a question that follows an answered (or conductor-owned) row with the same id used to vanish from the list and is now listed. A register it cannot read is a note, with the question checked as it stands (FR-59).

- A walker can now say whether an account works with the step `account <handle> confirmed|unconfirmed "<what you saw>"`: a created user the sign-up did not visibly confirm becomes usable on the walker's word, and a doubted given account is recorded for this story only (`state/account-doubts.json`, written under the shared file lock). The report no longer lists an unconfirmed sign-up as a user the story created: it counts them (`K sign-up(s) not confirmed`) and names the accounts the checks could not confirm.

- project's way of getting more test accounts and walker data (`config.json` `manual.accounts_way`, `manual.data_way`; `config_contract.walk_supply`): the

  answer); one reader returns them shape-checked, never raises, drops a secret-looking value without printing it, and reads
  anything but one of the three data-change sentences as `existing_only` and not known; record kinds that differ only in case or
  surrounding spaces are merged into one (their `existing` lists joined, the first request kept); three question prices
  (`s6.walk_supply`, `s6.walk_account`, `s6.data_change`) and three conductor rows (merge on write) carry the way to record them

- walker claims (`walk_session.py claim`, `walk_pool`): a walker says, before it changes a record other walkers could also use, which one; a claim held by another live walk waits up to `claim_wait_s` and then refuses naming the holder walk, the item and the door; the verdict of an item frees its claims only when the case names a teardown and the verdict itself says `"teardown": "done"` (any other word, or no teardown section, leaves them `dirty`), a row assigned to a walk that has not opened yet is held like a live holder's, and a walk that ends leaves every claim it still held `dirty`; a list of claims that cannot be read refuses and never grants; an `--all` claim is granted over records changed earlier and says which, in a `note` line, instead of refusing (t-2174 TR3-10 C)
- `walk_pool.py` (new): the accounts of a lane and the records it may change, as readers that return `(result, notes)` and print nothing: `lane_handles` (the body of the driver's `walk_actors`), `pool_of` (the base account plus the extra accounts the person named, only those whose key names exist in the env files, not doubted, not a second spelling of one key pair, with an `ok` sign-in probe row, capped by `limit_by_role`, obtain lanes counted in the cap), `assign_lanes` (round robin per account, `guest#<lane>` per guest lane, `obtain:<role>#<lane>` past the pool when the person said a user may sign up and the stand may be changed), `short_parts`, and `assign_entities` (a free record of an exclusive kind per lane, all of an item's records or none, written `in_use` before the dispatch; a lane-private `create:` record only when the person's data-change answer allows it) (t-2174 TR3-10 C)
- the walker's charter grows by the one claim sentence: `qa-runner` ratchet 15578 -> 15641 tokens and process ratchet 14370 -> 14433 (raise named: +63 tokens, spec t-2174 Part C item 8, accepted by the Lead 10.11.2026)

- gate A also signs in as the project's extra accounts (`manual.accounts_way.more_accounts`) of every role a manual case names, one browser
  sign-in each, so the walkers' account pool keeps only extras the stand let in; an extra that fails (keys not set, refused by the stand,
  no browser, a recipe that does not fit) is one note naming the role and its position - never the handle - and is dropped from the pool,
  with no question to the person and no stop of the gate; the base account's own question is unchanged, and with no extra accounts
  configured nothing changes (t-2284 TR3-10 D8)

- the factory now asks about the accounts and records parallel manual walkers need, instead of staying silent: one question, asked once per
  project, about how walkers get more test accounts and which records they may share (`the app makes them` / `one at a time` / `I will add
  accounts`); one question, asked once per project, about whether it may make and remove records on the stand; and one question per missing
  role when a manual check needs an account the project's settings do not have (`added` with the names of the two environment-file
  variables / `by hand` / `go on`). Each is a closed question with its prices, set aside while the other checks go on, and recorded in the

- A plan row can now say what its walk changes: an optional `walk_data` (a list of `{kind, exclusive: true|false, changes}`) and an optional `walk_global` (a reason, when the walk touches what every check sees). The plan check refuses only the shape, on every row that carries a field (a non-list, a blank `kind`, an `exclusive` that is not a true/false, a `changes` that is not text, a blank `walk_global`), and names the row, the field and the right shape with an example; it never judges whether what the strategist wrote is right. A row that says nothing, or `walk_data: []`, is no constraint, so plans written before this change are unchanged. The fields travel whole into the case's `request.json`, through both the prepared and the unprepared (walked-as-is) door; the S3 brief tells the strategist they exist, once, even when the flow-request measurement fails; and the strategist charter gains one sentence of tester experience. Nothing reads the fields for assignment yet: the lanes that use them arrive with the rest of the accounts-and-data work. The strategist's role-start load ratchet rises 16718 -> 16747 tokens (its process ratchet 15287 -> 15286); no other role's load moves. Judgment census 162 -> 163 for the strategist (`blocking_per_role.qa-test-strategist`): the new `_validate_walk_fields` shape check, a coordinator decision queued to the Lead.

- `probe_debt.py --settle` no longer repeats work it already did on the same inputs. A rebind that was kept (refused, or a dry run that would not write the instance) is remembered with the shas it was made on, the record's modification time, the author dispatch and the `generated_from` files, and is not dry-run again until one of them changes. When every item is stamped the same as at the last settle and was left for a reason a repeat could only repeat, the settle starts no subprocess, re-addresses its debt file to the new dispatch and `story_step.py start` says `probe_debt --settle: nothing changed since <dispatch>, not run`. A changed sha on either side, a rewritten record or an unreadable debt file always runs the settle.

- Onboarding interview: one new plain-words question asks whether the project's build or test runner compiles the whole test folder every time (so a half-written test file in one window could break another's run). A yes records `dispatch.parallel_windows: 1`; no answer keeps the default of 3 and records nothing.

- A session that works for one dispatch is now told apart from its siblings: the S5 exit checks (the precheck, the branch accounting, the exit gate's digest and scope readers) read "which dispatch is this" through one reader (`dispatch_identity`), from the dispatch id the driver puts in the child's environment or the gate names to its detectors. With two automators running and no dispatch named, the S5 precheck reports it could not tell whose handoff it judges instead of judging every case of the manifest. With one running dispatch nothing changes.

- The guards that run inside a session now tell parallel windows apart through the same one reader. A typed test-run request passes when it names the running dispatch of its own window (with two windows running and no dispatch named in the session, the request's own dispatch id picks the window; a session that is named and carries a sibling's id is refused as before). The owner guard no longer opens for a session that is not the owner because a sibling of the owner is running, and a session's role is read from its own dispatch rather than the first one running. The hook that records a role's return, and the environment projection refresh, wait for a sibling's commit instead of dropping the return (the return waits up to 31.2 seconds - three tries, computed, not measured - and the projection refresh up to 10 seconds); a failure after the wait is still swallowed but leaves one line in the hook's log. With one running dispatch, or no name, nothing changes.

- S5 windows no longer share the files a critic reads (spec t-1937, TR3-15). The probe debt is one file per critic dispatch (`work/probe-debt/<dispatch>.json`, `probe_debt.debt_rel`); what carries from one settle to the next is a separate story-wide memory (`work/probe-debt-memory.json`, the last settle's doc whole; an unreadable memory means the settle runs, a memory that could not be written is reported and removed). The advice the exit gate files for an S5 automator is `work/advice-S5-<dispatch>.json` (atomic; no identity or another stage keeps `advice-<stage>.json`) and the critic's brief names the file of ITS window's latest accepted automator (`brief_pack.advice_of`). The judge's file is `work/judge-code-<dispatch>.json`. The notes are `work/s5-notes/<dispatch>.md`, one per dispatch (registry rows per role); the brief and the receipt's `read_first` list the old `work/s5-notes.md` and every per-dispatch file. `sizing.py` publishes `work/sizing.json` by replace. A story from before reads the old files as a fallback and never writes them.
- `probe_debt.py --settle` never touches a running window: an item whose case belongs to, or whose test file is in the file set of, another S5 dispatch that is `running` or `returned_unaccepted` is left with reason `running_window` and no subprocess is started for it (an unreadable controller record leaves every item outside the settling dispatch's own scope). A kept rebind remembered across settles now has its own reason, `rebind_same_bytes` (`same_bytes` stays the probe's).

- First-write ownership of a test file by an S5 window (`window_files.py`, `guard_pre_tool.py` `window_file_check`): the first window to Write, Edit or NotebookEdit a test file claims it in `state/window-files/` (`O_CREAT|O_EXCL`, one winner); a later write by another window is refused with the door of a new file in the same directory (where a test lives stays the role's choice). A claim holds until `window_files.release` (no takeover): an open window and a grown round keep their files, a window sharing a case with the owner is the owner. Support files are not claimed; a session with no dispatch name, a critic and a plan dispatch are not checked; with `dispatch.parallel_windows` 1 nothing is claimed and the write goes the old road. An unreadable claim is an unknown owner and refuses with the same door; an unreadable story controller is retried, then the write passes with one notice to the person (a journal signal). A second refusal in a row names the story's state (windows meeting on files) and stops nothing. The conductor frees a claim with `python window_files.py --task <task root> --release "<window>"`. Writes through Bash are not seen (the launch gate is the net).
- `agents/qa-automator.md` and `agents/qa-code-critic.md` tell the roles about file ownership before the work: the automator that a claimed file takes a new file, the critic that a test in a new file beside another window's file was forced, not chosen.

- The driver keeps `boundary` and `last_dispatch` per thread (`story_run.py`, same names, no call site edited), and gains the chain record that a
  window's thread will run under: `Driver.as_chain(record)` / `Driver.adopt_chain(record)`, `ChainRecord`, a `chain` field on `Refusal`, and
  `ChainStream` (a `[W<n>] ` prefix for a chain thread's console lines, nothing for the main thread; not installed yet). The S5 review's close
  check now reads the critic dispatch once and hands it to both readers. On the serial road every value and every printed byte is unchanged.

- The S5 window scheduler now has an end-to-end test file (spec t-1937, TR3-6 and TR3-18): `test_story_run_s5_parallel.py` runs a real driver over real `claude` stub processes at the default of three windows (three authors at once, a crash, a question, a limit, a halt and Ctrl-C each in one window, the close happening once whatever the order, windows that share files running as serial, the single-window story equal to `parallel_windows: 1`). The test stub gained per-call start and end marks, a capped barrier and a capped hold, so overlap is proved by the order of marks and never by a clock; no package behaviour changed.

- The driver times the steps between one role's result and the next launch (`story_run.py` `Driver.timed`, `story_step.py` `start`): one line per step in
  `state/driver-timings.jsonl`, and `python driver_timing.py --task <KEY> [--json] [--check-hop-s N]` prints each hop's wall, its steps, the
  unattributed remainder and the per-step totals (a story with no such file prints "no timings recorded", never 0 s). The console says
  `note: <step> took N s` only over 20 s. The journal row of a role or conductor call now carries `wall_ms` next to `duration_ms`, with one
  note when the CLI's own count trails the wall clock by more than 120 s. While a role's process is waited for, one line
  `[progress] <dispatch> has written nothing for N min (last at HH:MM)` appears once per silence episode; the driver never stops a role for it.

- New config key `dispatch.parallel_windows` (whole number, 1 or more, default 3): how many S5 automation windows may run their role sessions at once. Windows run in parallel by default; a project may set 1 (or 2) to run them serially or fewer at a time. A config without the key reads 3; a value that is not a whole number of 1 or more reads 3 with one `note:` line and never stops a run. The template carries the key; the scheduler that reads it lands separately.

- The controller can now let a second S5 window start beside a running one, so parallel windows have a place to run. Only the driver's scheduler asks for it (`story_step.py start --parallel-window`, `controller.py --operation rework --parallel-window`), and only for S5 automator or code-critic windows whose cases do not overlap and whose number stays within `dispatch.parallel_windows`; every other second start keeps the old refusal word for word. A stopped window resumes beside its running siblings, and the S5 stage stays `running` while any window works. `story_step.py finish --not-complete --open-windows <cases>` tells the controller which other windows are still open, so the window that finishes first is no longer refused as "no role to close the stage"; a bad window name is refused naming the real ones. Completing S5 while another window still runs is refused, with the person's word `close beside a running window` as the way past.

- The S5 code critic now writes its findings to `work/test-code/critic-findings-<dispatch>.md`, one file per critic dispatch, so two windows reviewed side by side never share one. The registry row `work/test-code/critic-findings-*.md` is matched by the write guard with a `*` pattern (a key without `*` keeps its exact match, and the old `critic-findings.md` row stays); the form's `findings_file` deriver, the author's repair round and the author's brief each read the file of their own critic, fall back to the old `critic-findings.md` only for a story that has it, and never take "the newest file on disk". The S4 findings file is unchanged.

- S5 windows that share no file now run side by side (spec t-1937, TR3-6; the default `dispatch.parallel_windows: 3` starts to act). The driver runs each open window as a chain on its own thread; one driver lock is held by a chain except while its role's `claude` runs, so bookkeeping stays one step at a time and only the role sessions overlap. A session waits while another window's running session holds a file of its window (claims plus the manifest's test files), and never refuses once that session ended. The person's question, a refusal or a stop of one window starts a drain: running sessions finish and book, nothing new is registered, and ONE exception is raised after all chains ended (the model-service `limit` is not a stop: the run goes on one window at a time). A window that closed frees its test files, and the entry sweep frees those of closed windows. `dispatch.parallel_windows: 1`, one open window and an owed round take the old one-window body unchanged. The exit gate's state lock waits 10 s instead of 1 s and says so when it used the wait, the driver state is written by replace, and the S5 notes line names the per-dispatch notes folder as well as the old file.

- The driver's generic chain scheduler moved out of `story_run.py` into a new module `driver_chains.py` (`DriverChains`, the base class of `Driver`; `ChainKind`, `ChainRecord`, `ChainStream`, `Drained`, `once_on`, `ThreadSlot`): no behaviour change. `run_chains` takes two optional keywords, `kind=` (what a chain is called and what its session holds) and `seam=` (the stage's own failure ranking); the S5 console lines, the launch gate and the seam read the same words and files as before, and the module itself names no stage. This is the base the walker lanes of S6 will run on.

- The S5 launch gate's file set for a window now also holds the files a replay of the recorded probe of its manifest rows mutates (the test file of the record's `test_node` and the oracle file), read from the probe record through `probe_debt.record_files`; two windows that share only an oracle file are no longer launched together. An unreadable or absent record leaves the set as it was.

- The manual half of S6 can now run several walkers side by side: the driver puts each lane of manual cases on the same scheduler the S5 windows use, up to `manual.walkers` at a time (default 3; `1` keeps the one-lane-per-entry road exactly as before). A lane does not start while a running lane holds one of its cases or one of its accounts, so two walkers never sign in as the same account and never walk the same case; lanes that share an account run in turn. Lanes that meet a stopped or running dispatch, or whose account cannot be read, run first one at a time and the rest follow side by side. S6 closes only by the finish that leaves no open lane, whatever the order the lanes finish in; an unreadable state counts as open. A lane that crashes lets the others finish and book, and one question or failure is raised after the drain. Known limits: two walkers on different accounts may still touch one entity (isolation comes with the accounts and data way). Guest cases do not wait for each other: each guest lane gets its own guest handle (`guest#<lane>`), so guest lanes run side by side whenever the records they use do not overlap.

- The controller can now let a second S6 manual walk start beside a running one, so parallel walkers have a place to run. Only the driver asks for it, and only for manual runner dispatches whose cases do not overlap, whose accounts differ (two walkers never sign in as the same account; a guest is an account too) and whose number stays within the new `manual.walkers` key (default 3, `1` runs one walker at a time as before; a value that is not a whole number of 1 or more reads 3 with one note line). A dispatch that carries no account is an unknown account and nothing is started beside it. Every other second start keeps the old refusal word for word. A stopped walk resumes beside its running siblings, and the S6 stage stays `running` while any walk works. Onboarding asks once how many manual walk-throughs may run side by side.

- The brief of a stage critic or a consumer analyst (`brief_pack.py`) now carries a `Reviewed dispatch:` line with the path of the row of the author's dispatch it reviews (the value `stage_done.py --acceptance` needs in `inputs_read`), read through the same readers `stage_done` compares with; with no such dispatch yet the line says so and who acts. The refusal of a form without the path names the value to write and who acts, and the S7 form template (`handoffs/s7-analyst-to-scribe.yaml`) points to the brief line: a role no longer learns the requirement only from the refusal after its work.

- When a run with parallel windows starts to drain (a window failed, or the boundary limit was reached), a window that was waiting for a sibling's running session no longer starts its own session after the drain began: it stops there with its window left open for the next entry, instead of holding the person's question behind a whole extra session. The window whose own launch reached the boundary limit still launches, and a window with nothing in its way is not affected. With one window nothing changes.

- With parallel windows, S5 no longer leaves test-file claims behind when it completes: once the stage is completed and no S5 dispatch is running, stopped or returned without acceptance, every claim of the stage is freed, whichever finish closed it, so a later rework's automator is not refused over an earlier window's file. A window whose last round came back unaccepted now counts as open, and the serial body of the stage reads the same close rule as the parallel one when more than one window is allowed, so the stage no longer closes over that round. The brief of a window on the serial body now carries the file-ownership line whenever the guard enforces it. With one window nothing changes.

- Collect: a story the person stopped with Ctrl-C is no longer read as a dead driver for the calls that stop cut off. The driver writes one `stopped_by_person` row to `driver-runs.jsonl` (when the process began, and the calls it launched and saw no end for), and the stall rule K3 passes exactly those calls by, naming them as "stopped by the person"; a driver that died on its own, a call of an earlier process, a call launched after the row and a row with no call list are still a stall. The driver's own journals are now appended through the package's one appender, so a torn last line is repaired before the next row; on Windows a new row ends in a bare line feed, not a carriage return and line feed (readers take both).

- The S7 and S8 handover forms arrive with the path of the reviewed dispatch already filled (`inputs_read[0]`): the runner's dispatch for the analyst's form, the analyst's dispatch for the scribe's form, from the same reader the brief's "Reviewed dispatch" line uses (`brief_pack.reviewed_dispatch_id`). The role may change the row; with nothing awaiting review the placeholder stays and the stage check still refuses a form that names no path. A form already on disk is never rewritten.

- `stand_lease.py --release` with the stand's lease record held by another process no longer ends in a traceback: it changes nothing and says the record is held for over the wait, to wait a moment and repeat the same command, and by whom (exit 3, the code of `stand_busy`). Tests now pin that taking, releasing and a person's release refuse and write nothing under a busy lock, and that a broken lock surfaces.

- S5: a window whose last round is an accepted author round that no critic has reviewed (a resumed `test_defect` round, or a driver restart between the author's round and the critic's look) is now read as open and goes to the code critic, instead of ending the stage at the "every window is accepted ... recover" refusal; a mechanical author round completes the window as before, and the single-window road is unchanged.

- One file lock for the package (TR4-2 part A): `event_store.take_file_lock` / `hold_file_lock` take one byte of one file with a non-blocking try polled until a monotonic deadline, the same on Windows and POSIX. A lock that stays held raises `LockBusy` (a `TimeoutError` naming the lock file, the seconds, the recorded holder or that none is recorded, and the door); a lock that cannot be tried at all raises `LockBroken` with its stage (`open`, `platform`, `lock`); `EventStore.lock` re-raises a failed open or a missing platform module as `LockBroken` and keeps a failed lock call (stage `lock`) as the same `StateConflict` as a busy lock. A holder is recorded after byte 0 only for locks under `qa-factory/state/`; a lock file in a project's tree stays the single byte `0`. `EventStore.lock` and the created-users lock of `manual_capture` run on it (their refusal texts are unchanged; the second adds the holder words); `file_lock_state` and `lock_holder` read a lock without writing it. A new ratchet test lists the files that still carry a private copy.

- Four more private file-lock copies now call the package's one lock (TR4-2 part B): the case version store and the story case links (`case_versions.py`), the answers file (`question_register.py`), the probe copy locks (`probe_by_code.py`, the lock call stays an injectable seam and a held lock is still "held", any other failure "broken") and the live-writer probe of the onboarding apply (`onboard_apply.py`). Busy refusals keep their old head and add the holder words ("no holder recorded - released when that process ends: wait and repeat" where the lock file sits in a project's tree, which stays the single byte `0`); a lock that cannot be tried at all now says so in the lock's own sentence instead of reading as another writer. The onboarding probe no longer creates a lock file that vanished after the scan: it answers "unknown".

- The lease registry, the environment claims, the stand lease, the stand health record and the estimation ledger now lock through the package's one file lock: the same 10 s wait on every platform (it used to be about 10 s on Windows and unbounded elsewhere), and a lock held longer is refused with a sentence naming the lock file and the recorded holder instead of a bare OS error or a hang.

- The exit gate's state lock and the project-decisions lock are now OS file locks (the package's one file-lock helper): a hook or writer killed while holding one no longer leaves the gate or the registry busy for the rest of the run, and a lock file is never deleted. A refusal names the lock and, where recorded, the holder. The project-decisions lock moved to the file `qa-factory/state/project-decisions.lock`; an older leftover `.project-decisions.lock` folder is listed and never blocks.

- The driver writes the "not checked" record of a case (`refused` in its request.json) through one helper instead of three copies; the records written are unchanged, and a test counts the writers so a new copy fails.

- the "checkpoint active work" refusals of the controller (`controller.py`: revising the plan, reopening gate A, invalidation; `execution_request.py`: the S6 close context) read "what holds, and is it alive" through one helper built on the liveness reader the code close already uses: a dispatch whose session is provably over no longer blocks and is recorded as a stop by the next operation (`state_repair`), a live or unreadable one is refused by dispatch id, role and stage with the doors (wait, checkpoint it, release it with the person's word) (TR4-7)

- Manual walk: a typing chain no longer carries from one actor to another, and two spellings of one field (`#qty`, `input#qty`) continue it when the browser backend says they resolve to one element (`same_field`; a doubt means a new field).

- exploration charter for `qa-runner` at S6 (`references/explore-charter.md`, `scripts/brief_pack.py`): the first manual window of a story
  prints the charter's path, the cells of the perturbation table and the axis oracles in its brief; the role keeps a `tried` table
  beside the case and records a violated oracle as an `observations[]` entry, which reaches S7 as `<case>#obs<n>`. A flow with no
  request list is "not measured: <reason>", never "no bugs"; the charter carries no rule of any one project.
- perturbation axes `keyboard_input` and `reload_mid_operation` (`references/perturbations.json`, `scripts/user_path_failures.py`):
  one reader, `perturbation_axis`; `failure_axis` is its `request_failure` view and S3 reads it as before.
- `requests-seen.txt` (`scripts/manual_capture.py`, `references/manual-capture-steps.json`): each `ui` call stores the requests its page
  sent to a stand host (no query, repeats counted, capped, secret-looking lines counted not kept); a device writes no file and says so.
- every `manual_capture.py` `ui`, `http` and `app` call holds the stand's lease while it runs and answers `stand_busy` (exit 3, nothing
  opened) when another run holds the stand; a lease that cannot be used is a stderr note, not a block.

- `qa-automator` and `qa-code-critic` are charters of the form of `references/charter-form.md` (`agents/`): the tester's craft of S5 (where bugs hide, techniques for choosing the level, reusing and
  proving a test) replaces the numbered procedure; what code holds is told by its refusals. Each role gets a generated key page
  (`references/slices/<role>/handoff-keys.md`) and the header lines of its brief (`references/brief-form.json`); the critic's form gains `not_looked`, one row for each place it did not read.

- `s5_precheck.py`: the checks that judged test code (a sleep or an environment read in a test, a before/after comparison on an unasserted base, tests that differ only in data, a copy of
  an existing helper) now print an `ADVICE` block for the code critic and never refuse the author; the cross-reference checks (an unconfirmed expectation asserted as proved, a test changed after a red run)
  still block. The route word of an unresolved row is chosen by the role and checked against the closed list; the judge that translated free words into a route word is gone.

- `qa-runner` and `qa-failure-analyst` are charters of the form of `references/charter-form.md` (`agents/`): the tester's craft of S6 and S7 (where bugs hide, techniques) replaces the numbered procedure; what code holds is told by its refusals. Each role gets a generated key page (`references/slices/<role>/handoff-keys.md`); the runner's craft moved here from `references/explore-charter.md`, which keeps the perturbation matrix and the form of `tried.md`.

- charters for `qa-bug-reporter` and `qa-doc-scribe` (S8) and `qa-retro-analyst` (S9) in the form of `references/charter-form.md`: the tester's craft
  (where bugs hide at the stage, techniques) in place of the procedure the code already holds; each role gets a generated key page
  (`references/slices/<role>/handoff-keys.md`) and the header lines of its brief (`references/brief-form.json`). The reporter attaches the failing
  test to the bug and names the damage to a person; the scribe states what is proved within which boundaries and leaves nothing out of "Left with you";
  the retro reads only `work/retro-numbers.json`.

- bug drafts and bug records carry `red_test` (path and command) or `red_test_none: <why>`; `violates` takes the six closed kinds and `code` is refused as an oracle; the severity scale is a suggestion the analyst
  may overrule, no longer a check of code (`validate_artifacts.py`, `contract.py`, `bug_records.py`). The report check refuses factory ids by shape and no longer reads phrases.
  The word lists of the S5, S8 and S9 handoff forms stay closed on route fields and take `new: <word> -- <why>` on the rest (`handoff_check.py`).

- stages S6 and S7 are accepted by the role that consumes their output (`stages.json` `acceptance_by`): the failure analyst accepts or returns the run with a quote of the artifact, the scribe does the
  same for the analyst's work, and the next stage opens for that role only when the acceptance record exists (`stage_done.py`, `stage_guard.py`, `story_run.py`); a return repeats the author within `repair_cycles`.

- the end of the S7 repair road is "awaiting acceptance", not a closed stage (`acceptance_awaits` marker in `pipeline.json`, read by `awaits_acceptance` in `story_run.py`): the scribe is let in to accept the analyst's work,
  and a bare attempt to close S7 with neither a wait nor an acceptance record is refused with the name of the record it needs.

- `explore-charter.md`, `qa-runner.md`, `qa-failure-analyst.md`, `artifact-contract-run.md`: the roles are told the recorder's new words before the work: `look [<sel>]` (the page tree goes into the evidence when the runner looks for itself), `watch`, `fill --whole` (`fill` now keys a field as a person does), and the `surprise: <id> step <n> (<word>) <kind>: <fact>` lines. The runner puts every surprise into a cell's `seen` and into an observation with `"surprise": "<id>"`; the analyst judges `<case>#sur-<id>` and `<case>#sur-overflow` like `<case>#obs<n>` (`NO_DEFECT` quotes the line); no role ratchet rises.
- `perturbations.json`: the `multi_digit` kind uses `fill`, which now clears the field and keys the value one character at a time.

- `manual_capture.surprise.ignore` is retired: the recorder writes and shows every `surprise:` line, and no project rule hides one. The template key and the `[ignored by rule n]` suffix are gone, `surprises_ignored` is no longer in the `ui` summary or the record, and a project config that still carries the key loses it at the next migration (`config-keys.json` `removed` row, with the reason).
- The retro analyst's S9 brief gains one line, `prior_retro_lines`: the last accepted S9 retro form of the project's most recently active other story, its path and how many rows its `tried` table holds (a form that cannot be read is named; no earlier story, no line). `qa-retro-analyst.md` gains one craft bullet, "Start where the last retro looked". qa-collect already packs the form (collect-sets B16), now pinned.
- `qa-code-critic.md` and `qa-failure-analyst.md`: the form keys and file names move from the Techniques bullets into new Tools bullets; the experience stays in Techniques. The process rows of the two roles in `role-load.json` rise by the moved tokens.

## 0.10.9 — 2026-11-04 — gate A answers applied and decided items not re-asked, verdict reasons by owner, manual checks driven by the agent with recorded evidence, Playwright TypeScript identity, role start load measured in tokens

- a role whose agent file lists no Bash is no longer told to run `handoff_check.py` (`story_run.py` `exit_ask` and `handoff_ladder`): the
  resume over the exit gate's refusal and the mechanical third turn tell `qa-test-strategist`, `qa-case-designer`, `qa-case-critic` (and
  any role with no readable agent file) to fix the lines of `work/handoffs/<dispatch>.yaml` with its Edit tool, and say the exit check
  runs by itself when it hands off; a role with Bash gets the same text as before (F14)
- the conductor can install a project's dependencies (`references/conductor-actions.json`, action `install_dependencies`): it runs the
  install command the `s5_dependencies` gate note names, once, and counts it done only when `dependency_drift.py` then prints `in_sync`;
  with no command in the note, or a failed install, it writes nothing and offers the person three ways on; it never runs a command the
  note did not name (C3-18)
- the TypeScript probe fixture is the real LOCAL-1 Playwright report (10 rows, a `Retry #1` block, an absolute frame) and the real probe
  record of TC_010 instead of a reconstruction (`playwright-red-probe.junit.xml`, `playwright-red-probe.record.json`): the probe key reads
  the failed row by its case, at the mutated line 109, and the verdict stays `intended_failure` whether or not the retry block is cut (RN1-8)

- `scripts/selftest.py --shard I/N` runs the I-th of N weight-balanced parts of the test files (weights from `scripts/slow_tests.json`), so the release run can be split across CI jobs; `--slow-tests --from` refuses a joined output with a missing, repeated or mixed-total shard (exit 2)

- Typed JSON comparison and one ASCII fallback (`scripts/onboard_apply.py`, `scripts/console_io.py`, `scripts/judge_run.py`, `scripts/stand_health.py`,
  `scripts/stage_done.py`): `compare_trees` no longer calls two config files the same when they differ only as `true`, `1` and `1.0` or as `"1"` and `1`
  (it compares canonical dumps, and a side that is not JSON or is nested too deep is "differing"). The three copies of the console ASCII fallback are
  now `console_io.plain` / `console_io.ascii_only`; their output is unchanged.

- The stage journal line is written after the story lock is released (`scripts/stage_done.py`, `scripts/event_store.py`): `stage_done` no longer takes the shared
  journal's lock inside the story's history lock (nested locks), and no longer re-reads the journal for the event id (`log_append.write` is the one dedupe). A journal line
  that cannot be written after the commit is one stderr line and the event stays committed; running the same `stage_done` command again writes it, never twice.
  `event_store.replace_file` is the one retrying replace (Windows access-denied and sharing-violation retried), used by the atomic writers. A failing
  migration check now prints its stderr and the `left` list instead of a bare assertion.

- The gate registry now lists `run_suite.selection_line` (the console line that counts the selected tests a run report does not hold) as an exempt measure site, so the A26 audit no longer reports its `selected` / `matched` / `report_rows` token set as an unregistered verdict (D3-B1).

- manual checks, critic fixes (topic D4): after the agent signs in through the form (`fill-account` steps), the next `ui --session` or
  `http --session` call of that actor is accepted from the proven profile instead of being refused; a `NO_DEFECT` reason must quote
  with real quotation marks (an apostrophe is none) and the quoted words must stand in the observation's recorded evidence, and the row
  may name observations only; one attempt-aware rule decides which row answers an observation (`contract.observation_duplicates`,
  used by the triage validator and the refresh); `manual_evidence.py rejudge` uses `--observations-file` and every command that does not
  read it refuses it; the excerpt of a step is kept in `observe/<line>-excerpt.txt` and `steps.jsonl` is never rewritten; `NO_DEFECT`
  is in the verdict lists the roles read; the two bans a byte cut dropped are back in the analyst and runner texts; the per-actor sign-in
  probe of gate A is its own function with one door text; one text for the "body cut at" limitation; the `--session` help and the runner
  text say `http` needs the same `--profile`; the deferred-question refusal names no door it cannot serve

- S5 critic fixes (t-1746): the run block no longer marks a row `selection_short` (nothing read it, and it named a false cause on an ambiguous or inconclusive row), and the console selection line is not printed for an inconclusive run (its rows already say the runtime or input changed).
- The S5 exit's second detector (`s5_precheck`) now judges the same window as the branch accounting one: the running automator dispatch, else the ONE `returned_unaccepted` one (a repair round of a stopped window), and no longer every case of the manifest; both read the live dispatches through one reader, and an unreadable dispatch state is named as such instead of "none returned unaccepted" (t-1746, RN1-26, AR-13, AR-19).
- `manifest_put.py`: a re-sent `deviations` row for the same `test` replaces the stored one in place (the unit key is data, `ACCUMULATE_UNITS`), so a corrected reason no longer stands beside the old one; `retract_idle_lines` reads the retract names through `_retract_names` (t-1746, critic Q3, Q4).

- Small-work batch of the gates and delivery topics: a plan row whose `if_answered` is present but is no object is a shape finding and is skipped when a late answer is laid over the plan (it was named for rework by mistake); the gate-decision review precondition asks `Controller.review_is_stale` instead of its own copy of the rule; one shared predicate (`task_price.unread_agent_calls`) tells an agent that ran with its usage unread from an idle one, used by the price and by the retro's spend.

- The triage word `NO_DEFECT` (an observation of a manual check judged not a bug) is now in the re-run cause table and the judged-form vocabulary, and `validate_artifacts.py` refuses it on anything but an observation target (`<case>#obs<n>`) or without a quoted reason, and refuses two triage rows for one observation (RN1-10).

- Case designer (`agents/qa-case-designer.md`): the Then of a field that sends or redraws carries the field's own requirement as its `then_oracles` ref, and a case asserts only its own requirements (the case critic's matching rules for the response shape and for a repeated requirement are left to the merge report's open question)
- A red because the response carries no field the Then reads now carries `field_absent {then, field, read_from, shape_ref}` (automator, artifact contract, code critic, failure analyst): the analyst judges it by its `shape_ref`, a case's own requirement with the data held nowhere is one `APP_BUG` instead of a case defect

- Dashboard (`scripts/factory_dashboard.py`, `scripts/dashboard_cost_groups.py`): a driver-run story's By task row now shows its time
  (the sessions' machine time from their cost files, counted once per session; a session whose time cannot be told, including a
  rebuilt cost file, is named untimed in the cell and in the "All stories and activities" total instead of being summed as part of
  the whole), and a priced task names the sessions that only tag it in their cost file as unbound - not in its price - with the
  rows where their money is counted; no dollar moves (CD1-27)

- CI repairs on the closeout branch: the strategist's plan-contract slice names `branch_accounting.py` again (stage-joints told leg), `references/metrics/cost.md` C06 carries the catalogue's retro-relation sentence, the case critic charter no longer spells an inline run of `critic_rollcall.py` (role/Bash parity), `ActorSession.state` reads through `hooklib.read_json`, and `contract.run_results` keeps a link that spells its area as a key, so a red run row that names only `area/TC-n` in `covers` is never hidden from `case_set_aside`.

- Collector (`references/collect-sets.json`, `scripts/collect_pack.py`): the set table now covers the story folder an investigation
  reads - handoffs, review receipts, critic windows, digests, briefs, driver packets, triage, test-code critic findings, the
  requirements register, the critics' judge inputs, the raw ticket text, the delivery summary, the report and its history, and the
  driver's state - every story file the package writes resolves to a row - and names the product's code (implementation diffs,
  base slices, MR receipts at any depth under the sources folder, the context bundle and its lines view) as an explicit skip; project-level files the table did not name (turn dispatches,
  stand probes, decision transactions, coverage map, words) are covered too. The table is compiled and matched by two module
  functions (`compile_entries`, `match_entry`), and a binding test holds the story scope to the package's two artifact registries (CL3-3)

- Collector (`collect_pack.py`): a story row's `plugin_version` is read through `story_version.plugin_version_of` - `run_mode.plugin_version` first, the old top-level key as fallback, null when neither exists - so a history written by the running factory no longer shows an empty version (CL3-5)

- Collector (`collect_stall.py`, `collect_pack.py`, `references/collect-loops.json`): qa-collect packs the transcripts of a story that looped - a role dispatched again and again, a cap of rounds hit, a limit passed by your word, a repair or exit limit put to you - not only of a stalled one; a story whose looping cannot be established is packed too, and the manifest names the loop signals per story (`looped`, `loop_signals`)

- The S5 window's rework cap is no longer spent by the factory's own refusals: a conductor round over a refusal that is not about the window's tests (for example a missing receipt) counts against a cap of its own (2 rounds), so a later round over the window's own findings still finds its 2 rounds, and the person is no longer told a window was "sent back for rework" when nothing was reworked. Each round in `window_rounds` now records its `cause` (`window` or `refusal`); a record without one counts as `window`.

- S5 window (`acceptance.py`, `window_record.py`): an instance handed to the person is believed only as far as the story's
  manifest says (`acceptance.handed_instances`, the one reader for the record's builder and its validator); it owes no run
  evidence, so a window of handed tests closes by its derived `unresolved` pair, and a claim the manifest does not hold is
  refused as `handed_unconfirmed:<instance>` (at accept the refusal is the bare gap line; the door is named on the `window_record.py` road) (B-375)
- S5 window probe (`reporters.py`, `window_record.py`): the probe block keeps the lines of the failure the reason was compared
  against (`reason_detail`, bounded) and `window_record.py` prints a `note:` when the reason matched on the failure's first
  line only (B-380)

- Every role's brief now carries a `## Your final message` section: the digest form of that dispatch with the header, one row per id of its scope and the stage's artifact path already written; the role fills in only the verdict, each state and each reason (F11). Advice only - the handoff check is unchanged

- Stage joints (F6-51): `references/stage-joints.json` is the census of every check the factory makes of a role (the exit-gate
  families, the blocking detectors of `stages.json`, the S5 window gap kinds), with what produces the demanded thing and the
  file the role receives that tells it. `selftest.py --contracts` now also runs `test_stage_joints.py`, which walks code to
  registry, registry to code and demand to instruction, and refuses a check with no row, a stale row and a token no told file
  names; a leg that does not exist today is a declared gap under a shrink-only ratchet. `test_stage_joints_12586.py` feeds
  recorded run-12586 artifacts (automation manifest, test plan, triage) to the checks that judge them.
- Retro: a line "Gate blocks by class" counts the run's exit-gate refusals by the first finding they name, and an observation
  says so when one class repeats three times (a repeated refusal is a defect of the factory's code or of what the role is
  told). A run with no journal now prints `unknown` for rejects, gate blocks and compacts instead of `0`. The dashboard
  card reads the same class reader (the first finding only; a block with no text is `(no finding text)`).

- The retro is always the full one. `stage_done.py --set retro_mode=numbers|skip` is refused: the refusal says the retro always runs in full and names the door for the person's words (`waiver.py --remark --stage S9`, which the gate B packet and the MR's open items carry). The conductor prompt, `conductor.md`, the gate B phase (`s8.md`), the S9 phase and the retro analyst no longer offer a short retro; a story an older version recorded with `numbers` or `skip` still runs that mode (GW1-3, B-271)
- The gate B phase no longer tells the conductor to show the person a waiver command: a rehearsal `fix` is told in words and the conductor records the person's word itself (GW1-3, B-272)

- Whole-identifier check (`contract.names_whole`): the right edge now refuses a variant that continues the word with any
  non-space character after `. : / \ [ @`, so a person's word about `a.py::test_x` no longer passes `a.py::test_x[-1]`,
  `a.py::test_x[(1, 2)]`, `PC-1` no longer passes `PC-1@TC_002`, and `tests\a` no longer passes `tests\a\b.py`; the
  asking-again direction is unchanged, and `R-3.`, `(R-3)`, `R-3, R-4` still name `R-3` (GW1-52)

The session start no longer asks for re-onboarding after a plugin update when the project's configuration is current; unknown provider-API, host-hook and base-slice probes are no longer shown at gate A - they are listed as not established.

- Sizing (`scripts/sizing.py`, `scripts/contract.py`, `scripts/brief_pack.py`, `scripts/validate_artifacts.py`): the register row now carries the requirement text
  (`contract.register_rows` gains `requirement`, found by the header that starts with `Requirement`; a register with no such
  column is refused naming it, and the S2 register check turns that into an ordinary refusal that names the expected header), and
  `sizing.parse_register` reads through it. Before, the key was empty on every real register, so the area bump and the copy-only /
  logging-only reducers never fired. A P1 area bumps a requirement only through a PATH it names (`a/b`, `name.ext` with a known code
  suffix; prose such as "Node.js" or "e.g" is no path), matched against the row's `observable` cell, never against the requirement's
  words; a surface kind word of the area (`ui`, `api`...) can only narrow a path match and never matches alone; an area that names no
  path bumps nothing and the reasoning says so. `work/sizing.json` records the areas' state (`areas`), and the S4 brief of the case
  designer and the case critic gets a `## P1 areas` section: the requirements placed in each area, each area code could not place
  (left to the designer's judgment), and "no requirement falls in a P1 area" only when code checked at least one area and the
  register was read; otherwise it says what is unknown (OH3-34)

- The scout no longer halts on a requirement/code conflict that the ticket's comments, description or linked issues already settle: it records the source and the one-line quote that states the decision, and S2 carries it as settled. An unresolved conflict halts as before.

- the task packet the dispatch hook hands a role holds `known_paths` once (the state's resolved paths with the dispatch record's resolved
  paths laid over them) and shows the running dispatch as a whitelisted projection (`id`, `stage`, `role`, `kind`, `scope` and the keys a
  role reads) instead of the whole record, which carried `known_paths` a second time, the request binding and the controller's
  bookkeeping (`inject_context.task_packet`); a dispatch with no readable record is shown as kind `first` (RC1-14 part 2, step 1)
- a dispatch has a kind (`inject_context.dispatch_kind`: `repair` when its record names the work it reworks and a cause, `rework` with the
  work only, otherwise `first`; a field that is empty or not text, or a record that cannot be read, is `first`), and `inject-map.json`
  `kinds` names sections of a role's own slice that a kind is not handed; the first row drops two sections the automator's repair never
  uses (`### Importing a developer or CI result`, `### Profiles, leases and build commands` of the
  execution-lifecycle slice), every rule a repair uses stays; a row naming a heading or entry that is not there is reported by
  `inject_context.map_problems` and fails its test (step 3)
- `role_load.py` measures the text the hook hands a dispatch of each kind (`--kind first|repair|rework`; with `--story`, the kind of the
  measured dispatch), through the hook's own `entries_for` and `delivered_text`; audit A22 judges the kinds the map has rows for
- a dispatch refused because a rules file is over the injection budget now leaves a line in `state/dispatch-denials.jsonl` like every other
  refusal of the hook, so `recover` can close the receipt that says running for an agent that never started (TP1-15045 class)

- Role start load, compression step 2 (RC1-14, part 2): rules the code already checks leave the role's prose as one line `Code checks: <what>; the refusal names what is wrong and the way through` - quiet runs through the runner and the whole-read limit and the digest shape (`references/common-rules.md`), the defect hypothesis and impact class (`references/automation-candidacy.md`; the form comment above `impact_class` in `handoffs/s3-strategist-to-designer.yaml` carries the closed list), the `then_bindings` check (`references/artifact-contract-automation.md`); the slices are regenerated. A rule whose code check the refusal does not name stays as prose.

- Role brief (`scripts/brief_pack.py`): the person's words for the role are the first section after the head and are never cut to fit the 6 KB ceiling - at the last level every gate word, warning, halt and answer keeps one line and the waivers collapse to a count line, and a brief whose words alone exceed the ceiling goes out over it and says so (`over_ceiling` in the result); the repository map is the first thing to give, and every removed thing is named in a `## Not in the brief` section with the file to read (trimmed input files go to `<ID>-files.md`); the digest template `## Your final message` is the last section and sits outside the budget, so it can no longer push the person's words out (a brief with no template ends with one line pointing at the digest shape in the rules); a brief over 30 000 B says on its first line to read it by range; the digests heading is never left empty

- the driver no longer starts a role with no rule layer: when the injection layer cannot be built (a rules file over the injection budget, a
  missing or empty `inject-map.json`, a role the map does not name, any other error) `Driver.system_file` raises a refusal to the conductor
  (`injection_over_budget` with the hook's own text, `injection_unbuilt` with the door `inject_context.py --dry-run --role <role>`), writes the
  same `state/dispatch-denials.jsonl` line the hook writes so `recover` can close the receipt, and runs no role; this differs from the hook, which
  fails open on an error other than the budget (RC1-14 part 2, step 5)
- the driver builds a role's task packet with the hook's `inject_context.task_packet` and the dispatch kind of its record: `known_paths` once,
  the dispatch as a whitelisted projection with its `kind`, and a repair is not handed the sections its kind drops

- Role start load (`scripts/role_load.py`, `references/role-load.json`, audit A22): one measure of what a role reads before its first useful action - charter, the project's `CLAUDE.md`, injection, packet, launch card, brief with its side files, handoff form - printed layer by layer and as a sum in bytes and tokens (`role_load.py --role <role> | --all [--story <task>] [--json]`), with a control against the first request in the cost file (`cost_capture.first_request_lookup`). Audit A22 now judges that sum in tokens: the threshold (25,000) is provisional until the owner confirms it and prints an info line, a per-role shrink-only ratchet is red, and the two byte ratchets over the common layer stay. The byte caps of A22 (42,000 B per role) and the whole check A25 (58,000 B per role) are retired; `retro_numbers.rules_weight` reads the same measure; the retro names a role it could not measure beside the rules' cost and prints an unreadable `role-load.json` as an unknown with its reason; a ratchet row may sit at most `ratchet_slack_tokens` (1,000) above the measure; a first-request layer that could not be read makes the control `not_measured`, never 0 (RC1-14, part 1)

- Delivery reasons (`references/delivery-reason-owners.json`, `scripts/check_delivery.py`): a test the stand holds (a `blocked_by_env` row nobody has decided) is now reported as "blocked on the stand: <case> ..." and is the environment's, not the product's, so the report no longer lists it under what blocks delivery on the product side; a malformed unresolved row is reported as "manifest record: ..." and is the factory's (RD1-4)
- Stage guard (`scripts/stage_guard.py`): a refused delivery command names the delivery verdict and every way it opens (`yes`, `after_checks`, a `deliver_with_risks` journal line), and says the verdict was never computed when there is no ledger, instead of "delivery_ready is not yes" (RD1-4)
- Doc scribe (`agents/qa-doc-scribe.md`): the witness reads the word `check_delivery.py` printed, not its exit code, which is 1 on `after_checks` too (RD1-4)
- Gate A card (`scripts/stand_gaps.py`): the raw end of a program's output no longer rides on the card's `missing:` line; it is kept on the gap as `output_tail` for the conductor (RD1-4)

- Fixed (`run_suite.py`, `launch-causes.json`, `execution_request.py`): a test killed by the project's own pytest timeout is recorded as a
  `timeout` block of the run summary (named test, the limit and where it was read from) and never read as a stand failure. A hard kill with no
  report is `execution_status: timeout` (it was `broken_run`); one timed-out test among results keeps the run `failed`/`broken_run` and adds the
  block; `reason_code: project_timeout` marks the instance. The runner's timeout lines are data in the pytest row of `collect_forms`
  (`timeout_kill_line`, `timeout_failure_message`, `timeout_header_line`), and `pytest_timeout_setting` is the one reader of the project's
  per-test limit (argv, `addopts`, ini `timeout`; pytest 9 config names are reported as unreadable, never as "none") (RH2-9)
- `s5_precheck.py`: a `blocked_by_env` row stands only on a run that shows the stand (`execution_status: env_blocked`, a STAND SIGNAL on a run no
  timeout killed, or a connection-refusal exception named by a `run_evidence` row of `stand-answers.json`); a project-timeout run is never such
  evidence. A row with no recorded run is refused for a story started on 0.10.9 or later and is a note for an older one (RH2-9)
- The judge no longer asks "is this the environment?" about a run the project's timeout killed, so the run is never rewritten to `env_blocked` and
  the diagnosis never says "check the stand" (`judge_run.py`); the automator's brief carries a `Per-test timeout:` line at S5 and S7 and
  `qa-automator.md` says what a `timeout` outcome means (RH2-9)

- Doctor context probe on Claude Code 2.1.309: the launch id of the host's `Agent` answer (`agentId`; the older `agent_id` and
  `id` still read) is now a data row (`launch_id_keys` in `references/host-report-forms.json`) read by ONE function
  (`host_adapter.launch_id_of`), used by `host_dispatch.record` (Codex) and `agent_autobind` (the Claude PostToolUse
  `Agent|Task` hook, which now also binds the probe's proof to that id before its story filters); the probe is then judged
  `delivered`, and an answer with no launch id leaves it `unverified` with the reason "host response carries no launch id"
  (RN1-1). The install smoke now drives that path with an `Agent` launch and asserts the binding
- Exit gate and subagent journal: the child of the doctor's context probe is recognised by ONE predicate
  (`host_probe.is_probe_child`: the binding, or the probe's own mark tied to the same session, an `emitted` proof and the
  bound agent) and is no longer judged as a stage role nor journaled as an `unknown-task` stop (RN1-1)

- The S3 exit no longer accepts a manual row that rests on `rung_basis` kind `not_measured`: a `manual-*` row (and an `if_answered` patch that sets one) names a probe (`measured`), the environment's reason (`impossible`), a person's word or a judgement, and a P0 row adds a `reason`; the accepted kinds and the priority are data in `branch-accounting.json` (RN1-13)

- S3 strategist: nothing code knows is left to the role, and no formal rework round follows the exit (release-next/1 RN1-2):
  the `coverage_contract_revision` mark is written by code when S3 closes (the S3 exit judges the plan as if it were stamped; a
  row that names another revision is refused with the expected value); the S3 form drops `scope[].coverage_contract_revision`;
  every question-branch problem of the plan rows (`unresolved_ref`, `missing_refs`, `bad_branch`, `invalid_variant`,
  `stale_reason`, `settled_question`, `dependent_pair`, `missing_branch`) is refused at the S3 exit, in the strategist's own context, a
  register of zero questions or one that cannot be read never passes, and a finding printed twice is one line
- New door for a question the register does not hold: a plan row writes `new:<n>` in `question_refs` and an entry in its
  `new_questions`; code raises it as the next Q-n when S3 closes (one question per row and entry, a different later entry on the same
  row is a new question), renames it in `test-plan.json` and `test-plan.md`
- An S3 rework form arrives with the ids of the plan rows it was sent for (`handoff_init.py --rows`, recorded under `derived:`)
- A question raised at S4 with `"replaces": "Q<m>"` in its `raise_questions` entry re-points the plan row and moves the row's
  branch to the new question by the MEANING of the readings (now / before), never by letter; any doubt leaves the branch to the
  strategist's rework and says why

- Onboarding: a UI served on the API's own address (Next.js, Rails, Django) is no longer recorded as an API-only stand. Discovery now
  names the API's own address key and the keys on its origin (`frontend_same_origin`), and the interview proposes
  `environment.frontend.url_key = <base_url_key>` when the project's UI tests open that address (RN1-3)
- `env_probe`: when a project records no UI address but has a browser test profile and a harness-command login recorded `ok`, the stand's own
  address is read as its UI (source `base_url (ui login probe)`); an undeclared http key on another origin, an unreadable recorded address,
  an HTTP login, several stands or an unreadable table of test surfaces each keep the question to the person (RN1-3)
- The harness-command login ceiling is twice the duration recorded at onboarding (`environment.access.login_probe.seconds`), kept between 60
  and 300 s, and 300 s when none is recorded; a login that does not finish is reported as "did not finish in time", not as "refused" (RN1-3)

- Gate A: the message the person reads is now a file the code writes, `work/gate-a-message.md` (`gate_brief.py --gate A` on the skill
  path), and the conductor prints it whole, its own words after it; a Stop hook (`gate_shown.py`) refuses, once per message, a turn
  that ends without the file's cards, `Answer:` lines and approval line. The skill, phase and eval texts no longer ask for "paths to
  the full artifacts" (RN1-4)

- User-path failures (scripts/user_path_failures.py): a story with no diff (current code) now reads the files the S1 context bundle names (facts[].path, in the project or its configured checkouts) through the same patterns; "not measured: no code" is printed only when there is no diff, no register place and no file in the bundle; unreadable bundle files are named; a label is always relative to the root it was found under (RN1-5, regression of G2-14)

- The case critic now has the twin of the designer's rule 5a: it does not strike a Then "value kept whole, field still in focus" on a field whose value goes to the server or redraws the page, and its absence is a finding; a presence test binds both texts.

- Mutation probe, non-pytest reports (`probe_by_code.fires_on`, RN1-8): the runner's failure body is compared line by line (leading
  whitespace cut; one shared reader `assertion_detectors.fires_in`, also used by the echo guard), so a Playwright JUnit report - a
  `[chromium] > file:line > title` header, the assertion's own `Error: <msg>`, then the indented `expect(received).not.toBe(expected)`
  line - is read as `intended_failure` when it fails at the mutated line (the live LOCAL-1 run killed every probed test and still ended
  `incomplete`). The report's `message` attribute is still matched whole. The detector rows are unchanged; a failure away from the
  mutated line is still `wrong_location`
- Mutation probe, `incomplete` where the run failed at the mutated statement but its wording is not in the detector row (E15): the record
  now says `cause: data_row` (the factory's data to correct) instead of `cause: tooling`, so no `probe gap: tooling:<language>` question
  goes to the person; with several report rows `data_row` holds only when every incomplete row says it; a real tool refusal or an
  unreadable site is still `cause: tooling`
- `qa-code-critic`: one rule - on `incomplete` with `cause: data_row`, the critic reads the probe-run log and, when the inverted assertion
  form is there, writes `critic_verdict: unverified` plus `sensitivity_proof_missing_reason` quoting the log line (a word the contract accepts)

- The conductor settles a problem itself before it asks a person (FR-48, AR-17): new `references/person-owned.json` lists what only a
  person can know or decide (access, requirement intent, money, risk, outbound, team agreement, subjective, gate word), and
  `scripts/person_owned.py` is its one reader (class check, the refusal sentence both roads use, `--check`, and `--share` for the
  detector: classified and unclassified questions and words, `needless` always `unknown`). This part ships the rule text and the reader; the
  driver, waiver and text changes follow in the same release

- A question to a person now names its class (FR-48, AR-17): the conductor's `ask_person` / `stop` answer carries `why_person` (a class of
  `references/person-owned.json`) and `checked` (what it read); the driver refuses one without them once, then falls to its priced fallback
  with one `defect_found`. `driver-questions.jsonl` rows gain `source`, `why_person`, `checked` and `class_check`. On the interactive road
  `waiver.py --why-person <id>` records the class beside a person's word (an unknown class exits 2 before anything is written; a word
  without the flag is recorded as before, with one line saying it is counted unclassified)

- A probe gap the factory owns is named by the factory, never by the person (RN1-9, E15): a green test whose probe record of these bytes
  is `incomplete` with `cause: data_row` (the failure's wording is missing from the detector row) is a probe gap named `factory:data_row`
  in the S5 window, accepted as unresolved without a word of the person, and it is no longer covered by the person's class word
  `probe gap accepted`. The person's own word about the test is still read first. The factory's sentence is never quoted as the person's
  words (`named by the factory: ...`) and is not written to `state/passed-by-person.jsonl`
- Delivery: that test is left with the person under the new kind `review_unverified_factory` (after_checks, owner factory), and the
  ledger carries one `PROBE_DETECTOR_ROW_MISSING` factory finding per such test (the factory's data to correct). A test file that is
  gone, a record of other bytes or any other cause keeps the plain `review_unverified`

- The conductor settles a problem itself before it asks a person: `conductor.md` opens "How you decide" with the rule (read what the code left, ask only a class of `references/person-owned.json`) and its answer line carries `why_person` and `checked`; 22 phase lines that told the orchestrator to ask a person about a recorded state now read the evidence first and name the class (`person-owned: <class>`); a probe record with `cause: data_row` is the factory's gap, not a question (RN1-9)
- The halts table moved from `SKILL.md` to `references/halts.md` with a "read first" column and the class of what is left for the person; the first cells are unchanged (RN1-9)

- Fixed: a ticket's screenshots over 30,000 bytes could not be opened by a role (the read guard refused them whole, and a
  picture cannot be read in parts), so they became gaps the person was asked about. A picture is now recognised by its first
  bytes and judged by its own limit, `read.max_image_bytes` (default 5,242,880 bytes, the size up to which the ticket adapter
  downloads an image); text files keep the 30,000-byte whole-read limit. A picture over its limit is refused with a door that
  records it as unread with cause `too_large`. The default-gap line ("measured size N bytes, over the M bytes a role can open")
  now names the limit that applies to the file's kind, so a readable picture is no longer reported as unreachable. The real
  attachments of TP1-10937 (8 to 210 KB pictures, 6 KB markdown) are pinned as downloaded and readable.

- Gate A rehearsal: a story whose test plan has rows but whose case folder holds no case file is no longer passed as "every case is pinned"; the rehearsal raises one factory-owned finding saying the factory writes the cases before the gate. An empty plan, a plan of skipped rows or no plan file stays silent, and an unreadable plan is reported as an unavailable step (SC5-15)

- S5 exit (`s5_precheck.py`): new gate `open-oracle-asserted` (registry row `s5_open_oracle_asserted`). A Then whose expected value the one resolver (`traceability.then_oracle_states`) reads `open` or `invalid` - or has no readable `then_oracles` entry - may not be bound to an asserting instance unless the same Then also carries an `expectation_unconfirmed` row. The finding names the Then, the instance and the assertion line, and one door: bind the Then `expectation_unconfirmed` and assert only the established part (the question is in the register), or return the case to S4 (it names no question the register holds). A person settles it only by answering the question; no recorded word and no judge passes it. A case with no `then_oracles` line gets one note instead of a finding.
- S5 exit: the four-phrase prose search for an open oracle (`OPEN_ORACLE_RES`, `open_oracle_lines`, `check_oracle`) is removed - it matched none of its phrases on the case that motivated it, and its door named a file the automator cannot write. The execution lifecycle names the gate for the automator.

- Tests: `test_story_step.py` split by command into `test_story_step_{start,finish,decide,config,gate}.py` with shared helpers in
  `story_step_common.py`, and the two gate A answers `test_story_run_gate_repair.py` reads now live inside the package
  (`scripts/tests/fixtures/bench-13797-answers/`); no user-visible change (TQ1-10, t-663)

- Tests are written the way the project does (TQ1-11): the briefs of the S3 strategist, the automator and the code critic name the approach recorded at onboarding by path and state - the code rules document, the state of each `test_data` key (recorded / unknown / not recorded), the strategy documents - and copy none of it; one reader of `test_data` (`config_contract.test_data_states`, "TBD" and "?" read as unknown); strategist rule 4c (data and accounts the project's way before a stand need goes to gate A); automator rule 6 (a deviation is an `approach:` comment in the test language's own comment syntax plus a `for_the_reviewer` line); rubric dimension 4; the code judge's `code_owns_its_data` reads `project.test_data` and no longer passes an account supplied by a fixture it cannot see
