- Broad status forms (`references/detectors.json` `broad_status`, `broad_status_context`, `broad_status_doors`,
  `scripts/validate_artifacts.py`): `is_in(`, `any_of(`, `>= 4xx`, `< 5xx`, `range(4xx, `, `greater_than(4xx|5xx)` are
  refused on write when a status word is within 3 lines; a line passes only through a door: `# oracle_unknown: Q<n>` (code
  left open, same-credentials control in the test), `# broad_status: range per R-<n>|Q<n>` (a requirement or the person's answer
  states the range) or `# broad_status: not a status (<why>)`; `retry_markers`, `skip_markers` and `plan_antipatterns` are read
  through `assertion_detectors.shape_patterns` too, and a key that cannot be read means a built-in floor and a note, never no
  check (TQ1-2)
- Actor control (`code-review-rubric.md` dimension 2, `judgments.d/code.json` `code_narrow_negative`, `qa-case-designer.md`
  rule 6, `qa-case-critic.md` dimension 8, `test-code-patterns.md`): a permission refusal also shows the same credentials
  doing an allowed call and asserts the reason code a source names; an open code is a 4xx range plus that call, the exact-code
  Then bound `expectation_unconfirmed`; a dead token no longer passes a 4xx check (TQ1-2)

- The S3 exit now refuses a plan row whose `fit: extend <test>` / `param <test>` (or a `reuse` link's candidate id or `test_ref` path) names a test the project's working tree does not have (no such file, a folder, a path outside the tree), naming the path and the doors: the name as it is in the tree, `fit: new` with the new optional row field `fit_absent: "<test>"`, or a person's word. A working tree that cannot be found is a warning, never a refusal. The S4 designer and case critic briefs and the S5 automator brief now give the resolved path of every test a row builds on, say "NOT in the working tree ... write as new" or "not verified" for one that is absent, and carry a `fit_absent` row as "its page objects and helpers are part of this case" - so no role searches the disk for a test the plan named.

- A test that bounds a stamp the server writes (an async write, a background job after the response, two clocks) by the test's own times now names its tolerance from the requirements and a "cannot tell" outcome: the case designer writes it, the case critic flags its absence, the test-code patterns give the window `[t_before - tolerance, t_after + tolerance]` with a `pytest.skip("cannot tell: ...")` inside the tolerance, and the code review rubric fails a zero-width bound on an async write (TQ1-24). The case critic also carries again its two rules that the 0.10.9 merge had dropped: the Then's field exists in the response shape (`oracle_field_absent`) and one behaviour belongs to one case

- The code critic's red probe can model a case's declared alternative reading (`probe_by_code.py --mutation alternative --alternative <case>:ALT-n --model <file>`): a Then that passes under reading B is reported, and `probe_by_code.py --task <TICKET> --alternatives` lists what is owed, stale or proven (TQ1-25)

The S4 case critic now answers every pair of cases that share a requirement under `## Merge candidates` (merge or keep, with a P16/P19 reason). A merge changes no case: both cases are approved with the concern `parametrise into one test: <ids>`, which reaches the S5 automator like any case-critic concern. The critic also states the lower level an e2e or manual row could take, and explains a case count over the S3 plan's case budget (`plan_case_budget`, not written until its producer lands; absent it is only a note). The S4 exit refuses a round that leaves a pair unanswered or approves a merged case without that concern.

- User-path failures (S2) also read the files the notes of `context-bundle.json` name, resolve repo-prefixed places (`<repo>/src/...`, register quotes included) and bundle facts through the project's configured checkouts, find a request whose answer is never looked at (`discarded_response`), and add the files of the checkouts that call an address the set already calls (at most 8); "Not measured: no code" is said only when nothing at all could be read.
- S3 gets the requests of the flow from code: `work/flow-requests.json` (`requests[]` with `method`, `url_template`, `source`, `path`, `line`, `also_at`; call shapes in `references/request-call-patterns.json`, placeholders named after the template variable) and `Flow requests:` lines in the brief. The strategist plans a row that fails each request with 500 and timeout (`requests`, with the R of its flow in `requirements`) or says why in `request_homes`; the S3 exit refuses what is left (failure kinds and the oracle live in `references/perturbations.json`).

- Exploration core (`scripts/exploration.py`, `scripts/explore_step.py`): `explore_step.py frame` turns a feature phrase into
  `qa-factory/explorations/<slug>/`, probes the tracker and the repositories, and asks one priced question before anything runs
  (`references/exploration.json`, question key `explore.frame`)

- Exploration identity in the guards (`scripts/stage_guard.py`, `scripts/exit_gate.py`, `scripts/subagent_journal.py`, `scripts/host_dispatch.py`,
  `scripts/exploration.py`): a dispatch or a stop of an exploration role (`qa-scout` E1/E2, `qa-requirements-tester` E3) is recognised by ONE
  predicate, `stage_guard.exploration_named` - a whole `Exploration: <slug>` line of the dispatch, an `explore:<slug>` id, or (a stop) the
  opening prompt of the child's own transcript - and is no longer taken for the only story of the project. The label is read before every
  story step; `QA_FACTORY_TASK=explore:<slug>` only at the place of the person's word, never over a story the event names; a label with a
  story id or a `Ticket:` line, two names, a name that is no slug and a name with no exploration folder are refused with the door
  (`explore_step.py brief` / `frame`), and a role with no exploration step is refused with the roles the table names. An exploration stop
  is never judged by a story's S1/S2 checks, and its journal line carries `task: explore:<slug>`. An unreadable
  `references/exploration.json` leaves every story dispatch fully checked and writes one signal. `explore_step.py` joins the receipt
  scripts of `references/session-identity.json`; `import exploration` no longer loads the controller.

- Manual capture (`scripts/manual_capture.py`): `ui` and `http` take `--session <actor>` - one persistent browser profile per actor
  under the attempt (`sessions/<actor>/`), the calls of a case join one open attempt, `ui` reopens the page the last call ended on and
  `http` sends through the profile's cookies instead of the factory's Bearer login, so a project whose sign-in is not a request the
  factory knows no longer ends a manual case as a user block. A session runs the project's `login.ui` recipe (`sign_in`, proven by
  the landing check) only for a sign-in the gate A probe recorded in `state/sign-in-probe.json` for the same recipe; otherwise the
  call is refused before anything opens, and a proved sign-in that later fails to land is an environment block (cause `stand`), not
  the user's. A sign-in field of the recipe may be `{"test_id": ...}`. New `session close` deletes the profiles (their cookies are a
  credential). Each observed step's excerpt is also kept in `steps.jsonl` as `observe_text` (RN1-10)

- A manual check records what the runner doubted at any step, not only its Then verdicts (`manual_evidence.py`,
  `contract.py`, `qa-runner.md`, `qa-failure-analyst.md`): the record carries `observations[]`, each entry a step, what was
  expected, what was seen, a capture of the attempt and a quote that must stand in that capture's text (or, for a picture, in the
  excerpt the capture tool wrote for the step); a made-up quote is refused by field name, and a quote beyond a capture stored
  cut says so. `[]` is the declared empty outcome; records made before the rule read as `[]`. `contract.triage_targets` names each
  entry `<case>#obs<n>` (also for a green check), and `build` refuses an attempt that still holds a live browser profile
  (RN1-10).

- Gate A (`scripts/gate_preflight.py`): a new rehearsal step proves, for every account a `manual-agent` case signs in as (a `stand_account` precondition), that the stand lets it in - one real browser sign-in per account through the same `sign_in` a manual capture uses, in a throwaway context - and writes `state/sign-in-probe.json` (`ok`, `failed` or `not_proved`, with the recipe fingerprint) for the S6 `--session` call to read. An account the stand refuses is a question to the person with three answers; a recipe that does not fit the login page, or none recorded, is the factory's to fix; an account whose keys are not where the runner reads them is that account's finding only, and the other accounts are still probed. Nothing is written, and no browser opened, when no manual case names an account (RN1-10). Onboarding phase 1 records the project's sign-in recipe from its own page object or login test

- Run report identity (`scripts/red_sandbox.py`, `scripts/run_suite.py`, `scripts/finalize_task.py`): a selected test whose
  `report_test_id` is the runner's bare title, or a title with the path of the project's own tree, now binds its report row when the
  row's name equals the title, the row's classname is the contract's file (or its tail on a path-segment boundary) and the id's own
  file part, if any, is one file with the classname; a prefix title, another file, a neighbour directory, another tag or another
  case never binds, and one title in two classnames stays `not_run`, ambiguous. The run block counts selected against matched
  (`report_scope.selection_count`), marks an unmatched row that has no other code `selection_short`, and the console says a short
  selection once, naming no runner and the place to look; exit code and status do not change. The manifest join in the finalizer
  reads every spelling of an instance (`instance_id_aliases`): a block row spelled the 0.7.7 way no longer becomes a phantom
  `INSTANCE_MANIFEST_JOIN_FAILED`, an id that answers two different manifest rows is still the finding (RN1-21)

- `manifest_put.py`: a fragment no longer erases what it did not send (RN1-22, found on LOCAL-1 run 3, where a hand fragment carrying a
  copied `tests[]` row shrank `then_bindings` from 29 rows to 3 and replaced the earlier windows' `deviations` and `plan_remarks`). The
  writer's `then_bindings` array now replaces only the rows of what the writer wrote about (the instances of its `tests[]`, the cases of its
  own `then_bindings` and `unresolved[]` rows) and every other row stays; a Then of a unit a hand fragment names but does not send stays too
  and `run` prints a `kept ...` line with the door; top-level lists no family names (`deviations`, `plan_remarks`) accumulate (an `id` row
  replaces the stored row with that `id`, in place; an equal row is not added twice). The one sign that replaces whole is the new top-level
  `retract`, a list of key names: `"retract": ["then_bindings"]` also takes out the Thens of a unit the fragment names and does not send. `run`
  refuses a `retract` that is no list, holds a non-string, or names `tests`, `unresolved` or `obligation_bindings` (it names the door each has:
  `retracted_instances`, `retracted_unresolved`, `retracted_obligations`) and says when a retract names a key the fragment does not send; `merge`
  ignores an invalid one, so an old journal replays without raising and keeps the rows it used to drop (RN1-22)

- Driver (`scripts/story_run.py`): a question about only SOME manual cases no longer holds the work that does not depend on them. The
  stand-sign-in question and the dry-gate question name the cases they hold (`Person.holds`); when the S6 scope has a case outside them
  the question is set aside (`Driver.defer_question`: the same text and the same `driver-questions.jsonl` row as a live question, kept in
  `state/deferred-questions/<n>.md` and `state["deferred"]`), S6 closes over the other cases with the held ones left unchecked (their
  request says they wait for the answer to question n), S7 runs, and the questions are asked one by one, as they were, before gate B
  (`Driver.deferred_step`, exit 3, head line `question: k of N, waiting since S6`). The answer is read by the original question's own
  executors; a `retry` sends exactly the held cases back to S6. A gate, the conductor's stop, a question with no cases and a scope with
  nothing else to go on with are asked at once, as before. `--until` and `--max-boundaries` print the open list. The skill road carries
  the rule in `phases/s6.md` (its code follows the driver shell, SC5-3) (RN1-24)

- The S5 exit gate now judges the window that handed off even when its dispatch is `returned_unaccepted` (a stop with no bind receipt): the running automator dispatch is read first, and only when there is none the ONE returned one; a returned window no longer reads as "every case of the manifest". Two returned windows, none, or a window with no readable scope is `UNREADABLE:` with exit 3 (the conductor's seam), never a pass and never a judgment of the whole manifest

- Test scaffold (`scripts/tests/fixtures/manual-evidence/scaffold.py`): the fake world fixes the factory's User-Agent
  version, so the web pin of `test_surfaces.py` no longer goes red on every release (t-1668)

- An `excluded:` home of the requirements register is either `Q<n>(<letter>): <why>` (a blocking question whose answer leaves the part out) or the person's own words QUOTED from `state/words`; any other reason that says the person decided is refused at the S2 exit, and gate A lists every cut made by quoted words under "Left out by your words" with a door to say which part to keep
- A bug found by reading the code is a draft with `evidence: "code-reading"`: an oracle (a question the person settled, or a requirement whose register `code_says` is `contradicts`) joined with an S1 code fact, checked at the S7 claim and the gate B rehearsal, shown at gate B marked "by reading the code, not proven by a run" with three answers (file, not needed, prove by a run)
- A requirement whose expected result is unambiguous and which the S1 code contradicts is recorded in the register's `code_says` column and planned as one expected-red check, not asked as a question; the S2 exit refuses such a question

- The scout's definition of "done" is now the person's path through each function (where they start it, see its result, change or undo it, and what each place calls), not one observable per sentence; a tool that did not read a source is a question for the scout, not a verdict, and the S1 brief no longer forbids the search the scout's own procedure asks for.
- New `ticket_adapter.py query --path <API path> --output <inventory> [--save <file>]`: one GET of the configured tracker API at a path the role chooses (a filter's search, a project's issues), the answer kept whole under work/, one summary line on stdout. `peek` and `collect` given a link where a ticket key belongs are refused before any request, naming the key inside it and the two doors (`peek <KEY>`, `query`). The scout's card lists `query` and `record-source`.
- A derived requirement that states a product norm is a requirement: the norm is its oracle and the code its observable; a value only the code states is a fork with its own question; the norms are put to the person in one confirmation question. The register's `code_says` column takes `unknown: <why>`, and a bare `unknown` is refused where an S1 fact stands on the row's own line.

- The files the S1 scout named are no longer the whole flow: the files of the configured checkouts that call an address the flow already calls (the cart page that shows and edits what the add-to-cart page wrote) join the set the S2 failure scan and the S3 request list read, at most 8, the rest and any file that could not be read named in a reason. A request line of the S3 brief names the other files that make the same request (`also in CartPage.tsx`) instead of counting its sites.
- The S3 brief names the functions of the register's `## Functions` that the plan walks as a person does, and the strategist charter says what a walk row is (start, see the result, change, undo, with real input, every oddity recorded); the compound-requirement paragraph left the charter (`coverage-design.md` holds it).
- The question-branch check of the plan now runs at the S3 exit, where the strategist still holds the plan, and refuses what the remark after the stage used to report; `missing_branch` keeps its own refusal and `no_row_for_question` stays a warning. `ticket_adapter.py get`, `children` and `freshness` refuse a link given as a ticket key, as `peek` and `collect` do.

- Rules a role is judged by now stand in its card before the first attempt: the strategist card carries the letter-branch rule (`oracle_unknown: false`, `coverage_obligations` with `sufficiency_review` and `observation_contract`); the case designer card carries "one case per plan row, an `unverifiable` row too", the readiness id of a question and the `now` / `before` key rule (moved out of the charter); the case designer and case critic hold ONE basis rule (`vocabularies.md`, the six kinds of `grammar.ORACLE_RE`; the plan row's `oracle` column is another field)
- A role's words after the path line of its digest are kept whole in `state/findings/<dispatch>-digest-notes.md` (`role_digest.file_notes`) instead of being dropped; the gate A rehearsal's uncommitted-change count of the test repository leaves out the factory's own `qa-factory/` folder

- A letter answer on a before/now card is now applied. On a story with no diff the card no longer offers "a regression - say what it was" (it says the expected value is the text the case writes for that answer), and an answer on the "before" letter settles the question when every case Then of that question carries a real text for it: the register records which cases it read, and the resolver gives each Then its own case's text. An empty or `unknown` Then text never stands as an expected value.
- The note for an answer that was not applied says why: `before_value_missing` when the row is unchanged but the "before" value is missing, `changed_since_answer` only when the row changed. A plan row that rests on an answered question (in `question_refs`) and has no prepared change is no longer left silent: the test planner is named for it with a line that says so.

- Gate A does not ask again what the person already decided in their own words (t-1697 D1-B, RN1-14): a `## Reading forks` Decision written as
  `"<their words>" (<file>.txt)` (at least 3 words, found in `state/words`) closes the contradiction card of that requirement and is listed under
  "Already decided by you"; a contradiction with the code that the register already records as `code_says: contradicts` is no card; the S2 exit
  refuses a question about a requirement decided that way unless it says `asks_beyond_words: <what the words leave open>`.
- A gate item about a subject keeps its id between rehearsals (`case_environment-TS-10`, `vcs-test-repo`), so a recorded word cannot land on another
  item; the case-environment item offers a third answer, `<id>: product gap`.
- The norms-list question can be marked `norms_list: true`; gate A now checks it with the register's norm rows (a marked question naming a non-norm
  row is refused), and the validator refuses a behaviour claim that points to a question about other requirements while another question is about it.

- Bug drafts (`scripts/bug_records.py`, `references/bug-status-words.json`): the reader of the open bug tickets of a story's own sources (`open_source_bugs`: type in `bug_types`, status not in `closed_statuses`, with the `file:line` places and the requirements the register attributes to the ticket) and the matching rule a draft is compared with (`matching_open_bug`: same place, or a shared requirement; a bug with neither is never matched). A missing or unreadable word list lists nothing and says why; an unreadable ticket is skipped and counted. Nothing is wired into gate B yet (RN1-18, first part)

- A gate A finding about a declared gap in a plan row that names a requirement offers a third answer, `<its id>: product gap` (the product has no such function): the word is recorded by one writer, `scripts/product_gaps.py` (record and revoke, both listed for the conductor), the requirement is reported as not implemented (delivery not ready), it is no longer listed under "Skipped by the plan" or "Not proven", and the same row is not asked again; a row that names no requirement, or an unreadable word list, offers no such word
- Bug drafts carry `defect_location` and `requirements`; two drafts that name one defect place are refused at the S7 claim unless merged or marked `distinct_defect`; the analyst runs `bug_records.py open-bugs` and marks `extends_open_bug`, which gate B shows as "Extends the open bug" only when the scan of the story's sources holds that exact key, otherwise the old "your call" line

- Gate A refuses a design review whose case designer was accepted after its case critic (the critic has not reviewed the cases as they stand); the existing repair runs the critic again before the person sees the gate, and the packet says so when it is shown. The order of accepted work is read in one place, `Controller.accept_order`; a case re-pinned by code after the critic is the known limit

- Delivery report: the "Because ..." of a `no` now names the product's bug first. The candidates are read in owner groups (confirmed
  bugs, bug drafts that name a requirement, product gaps, reds the product owns, unproven requirements, tests the critic could not
  verify, reds of the environment or a review, reds of the factory); a `CASE_DEFECT` red no longer outranks a product bug that
  stands after it. Only the order of the sentence changes, never the verdict word (RN1-16, t-1698)
- Delivery owners: a reason that names only cases whose current triage verdict is `CASE_DEFECT` (for example `traceability: ...
  unresolved (contradicts_requirement) with no decision attached`) is the factory's, not the product's; a coverage obligation with
  no cause at all (`gap` empty or `none`, no `execution_state`, no `oracle_open`) is the factory's `coverage:` reason and names
  what is missing. An absent state beside a real gap text still reads `coverage red:` (RN1-23, t-1698)
- Delivery verdict: new kind `product_gap` (`no`, owner product) and reason family `product gap:`, read from the typed carrier
  `work/product-gaps.json`; an absent file changes nothing, an unreadable one adds the factory finding `PRODUCT_GAPS_UNREADABLE`
  (RN1-15, t-1698)

- A case is joined by identity (`contract.case_matches`) at every place that still compared keys exactly: the traceability chain (`unresolved[]` links, run results, impossible rows, the cases a person took by hand), the ledger's `unresolved[]` lookup and the delivery completeness check, so a manifest row `TC-002` and a case `web/TC-002` are one case and a case with its test or its decision is no longer reported as "neither in tests[] nor in unresolved[]"; two different areas, `TC-1` and `TC-10`, and two blank keys stay unmatched. When several `unresolved[]` rows name one case, the row reached first by the ledger's branch order answers, never the last one
- A run-report `current_results` list no longer loses a row when two rows share a computed identity (rows with only a `test_id`): the later row is kept under `<key>|<test_id>` or `<key>#<n>`; `Story._case_failed` also reads a `partial` row the run observed red (`case_stamp.is_red_row`); the dashboard no longer shows a manifest `green` as `passed` for a row whose run result is not terminal (a run-observed red reads `failed`, anything else its own word or `not recorded`)

- Case lookup by identity, the remaining places: a case is now found by the same identity match everywhere (`<area>/TC-NNN` and
  its bare `TC-NNN` are one case; two areas never match) in the delivery owner check (a world gap such as an impossible row no
  longer lets the case be treated as the factory's), the stand-gap carry (a second gap of the same case under another spelling
  blocks the carry), the traceability chain (the assert-stricter set and the manual-human evidence package) and the ledger
  (hand-off with a red run, impossible rows, run results, and no bare duplicate of a case a plan row already has). Nothing new is
  raised: an empty case or key matches nothing (t-1698 D2-B2)

- Run results: the bare case id (`TC-4`) of an area row (`api/TC-4`) is now added to the results only when exactly one area
  carries that id; with two or more areas there is no bare alias, so the red of one area is no longer read as the result of
  another. The ledger's whole-case "expectation unconfirmed" sentence and its manual-human hand-off lookup now match a case by
  identity (a bare row meets its area case; two different areas stay two cases) (D2-B3, t-1698)

- Cost capture (`scripts/cost_capture.py`, `references/host-report-forms.json`): the time a question stood open to the person (the
  host's question tool, named in the data row `claude.person_question_tools`, from the call to its answer) is now part of
  `human_wait_s`, uncapped and counted once next to the capped turn gaps; the cost file also lists `human_waits[]`, says
  `question_waits` measured or unmeasured and counts `open_questions` (RN1-25); an incremental scan whose checkpoint says part of an
  agent file was read but whose ledger holds no request for it now reads the file again from the start instead of pricing it at
  zero with its tools intact (CD1-13)
- Task price (`scripts/task_price.py`): an agent of the task that ran (it has tool calls) but whose usage was never read is
  named in the new key `not_estimated_agents`, the status becomes `incomplete` (`differs` still wins) and the finding says the price
  is at least the figure shown, instead of printing it as exact; the price figures keep their types (CD1-13)

- Retro numbers (`scripts/retro_numbers.py`, `references/metrics/catalogue.json`, `references/metrics/cost.md`): the stage table now
  prints a wall time and a machine time (the stage's wall time minus the waits for a person inside it, question waits included) and
  the wait line names a capture that did not measure question waits, so an older cost file never reads as "no wait"; a repair round
  is a dispatch whose scope an earlier dispatch of the same stage and role already had (the controller's dispatch records, matched by
  case identity), a new window is not one, an empty scope is named and not counted, and a story with no dispatch records keeps the
  per-role count, labelled; the dispatch count of a role and a stage is the number of dispatch records, not of agent files; a role's
  cost is called "not estimated: its usage was not recorded" only when no cost record of the story (a file with tokens, a driver row
  with a cost) carries usage for it (RN1-25)

## 0.10.8 — 2026-11-01 — the requirements fence at S3 and candidate defects reach the plan, Playwright TypeScript and mobile surfaces, branch accounting of every ticket sentence, manual checks on stands without docker, honest prices and reports

- the retro forecasts a story's price from the precedents of its own size and unit (`retro_numbers.py`, CD1-5): one line, "M stories on
  the function count so far: low..high, median, n precedents, at the rates of each run", or "too few (2 of 3)" below three; a record of the
  old unit (the register's rows) never prices a story counted in functions, an incomplete record is a floor and no price, a null price is
  never read as zero (a recorded zero is no price either), the median is printed only on three or more single prices and the line says
  how many it had, and what was left out is counted in the line
- the estimate facts and the ledger carry the unit of the size letter (`forecast.size_unit`, `function_count`, `computed_budget`,
  `defect_capped`, `size_mismatch`), read from `work/sizing.json`; `size_unit` and `size_final` are read by the forecast and the drift
  signals, `function_count` is kept as a record and nothing reads it back from the ledger yet; `sizing.nearest_precedents` finds a record
  the factory wrote for the first time
- the dashboard drift line and the "legacy estimate" signals of `metric_signals.py` take their cohort by size and unit, so a change of unit is
  never read as drift; the precedents table marks a record counted in rows with " (rows)"

- The approved scope is read by every reader the same way. The driver's list of pinned cases (`Driver.pinned_cases`) is the
  controller's own reading, so a link with no version is no longer sent to the case critic or to a dispatch as if it were
  pinned. A manual runner block is written in the same keys as the dispatch scope it sits in (a bare number two areas hold
  is every one of its keys), so the block is no longer refused as "not in the dispatch scope" after the scope was respelled;
  the block's limit of 5 counts those keys, and a replay of a committed block after the index moved keeps its door. A
  hand-written `revise_plan` key reused for another request is refused with the scope the key was committed with (or the
  fields that differ) and a door: a key of its own and the current `expected_revision`. The scope refusals name
  `case_versions.py --all` as the move that records the pinned cases, and the hand-written `revise_plan` where `--all`
  leaves a scope set by hand alone. Under an orchestrator lease a hand-written `revise_plan` is still refused ("stale or
  missing orchestrator lease") unless it carries the lease's `owner_session_id`; with it the request passes, and the field is
  read once and is not written into the plan. The driver's own `revise_plan` takes the owner from the current lease and
  supplies it itself. This covers `revise_plan` only: after a driver rollover the other driver calls that need the lease
  (`dispatch`, `invalidate`, `accept`) carry no owner and are still refused. A `revise_plan` the code wrote (`case_versions.py --all`, the driver) no longer marks plan rows as the person's
  override and no longer writes a `human_answer`, and it never overwrites the words a person left on a row. `case_versions.py
  --all` answers `review_scope` (the case ids the case critic is dispatched over) and the driver's critic scope is the same
  function. The unused `contract.scope_member_keys` is removed.

- The controller reads the story's name in one place, `Controller._ticket()`: the journal row of a gate-A override, the gate
  decision id, the `ticket` of `pipeline.json`, the resume and finish doors and the doors of the CLI all name the folder
  even when the story root is given as `.` or `..` (before, a root `.` gave an empty name and the veto of a live worker
  was lifted silently). The vetoes that compare a name with a host receipt (the checkpoint veto, the liveness repair and the
  launch offer of a desktop story) now ask for every spelling of the story's folder a receipt may carry (another case on a
  case-blind disk, a link), so a live worker is never lost to a spelling. Lists of case ids in the scope refusals are cut
  at one limit with the number named (the areas, the broken pins and the spellings the index keys differently were cut
  without it); `detector_verdict.named` gains an optional `tail`.

- The stage guard no longer reads a plain command as a delivery because of a variable and a substitution (CX2-27). On run 12586 a
  function that wrote the person's answers (`run(){ python ... --answer $1 ... --words-file $W/s2-$(echo $1|tr Q q).txt ...; }`) was
  refused as `gh pr create` from the `hub pull-request` row: a bare `$var` counted as the program and a word with a substitution filled
  the next slot of the form. A bare `$var` now counts as the program only when a form word stands after it in the segment (`$gh pr
  create`, `$gh $(echo pr) create` and `$gh $(echo pr create)` are still deliveries), and substitutions standing alone under a head that
  is no command of its own - a mention command (`echo $(a) $(b)`), a bare `$var` (`$a $(f) $(g)`) or a loop head (`vcs.list_heads`:
  `for`, `foreach`) - are arguments. A written form word still refuses wherever it stands, and a word with a substitution that writes
  the whole rest of the form (`gh $(echo pr create)`) is now read as that form. Before gate B a refused delivery shape no longer names
  the doors of gate B (`deliver with known gaps`, `check_delivery`), which cannot open yet: it says the guard read those words as a
  delivery, that gate B comes after S8 and what state S8 is in, and how to write the command without them (split it, or put the text in
  a file with the Write tool). The verdict is unchanged: only the sentence. Known and named: a form held wholly in opaque text
  (`a=gh; $a $(cat words.txt)`, `$a $(f) $(g)`) passes, as any script file does.

- a manual-agent case the person took by hand at a refused stand (`refused.by: person_checks` in its `request.json`) and that has no run result now gives its requirement an outcome in the traceability chain: the gap word `unresolved:handed_to_person`, kind `handed`, so the requirement is one line of "Left with you" (one per case) and the verdict is the third one instead of `no` for a broken chain; the plan obligation of such a case (a schema-2 `test-plan.json` row whose cases are all taken by hand) is no `coverage:` reason either, unless its run is red; a run result of the case (red or green), a manifest `unresolved[]` row, a lane other than manual-agent, a `left_unchecked` record (the `go on` word) and any `refused` that is not exactly the record keep the gap they had (a manifest `tests[]` row with no result for the case reads the hand-off), and a requirement that also has a broken case stays `no`
- the stand-login question no longer says that `by hand` makes the delivery verdict `no`: it says the checks are left with the person and the report lists them, and that the story is ready after those checks only if nothing else holds it (`go on` is unchanged: `no`)

- What a person decides at gate A or B in the form the packet offers (`Q<n>: <letter>`, each on a line of its own) is now recorded and
  applied by one executor, `controller.py --operation gate-decision`, for the conductor and the driver alike. Before, only the driver
  applied gate A answers, and a `Q1: a` line at gate B was lost on both roads. Gate A lays the answers over the plan BEFORE the decision
  is built, so the decision binds the patched plan; gate B records the answers and never touches the plan. A call that does not record
  (a refusal, a preview, an exception) leaves the plan, its markdown and the register file as they were and moves no manifest event
  (`accept as blocked` is written only by a call that records); a refused call still records the person's words, and the next call
  patches the plan from them, so a retry with no tokens (`approve as is`) no longer loses the answers. The driver hands what only it
  holds by file (`--answers-file`, `--shown-file`, `--remedies-file`, `--answers-by`, `--no-answers`) and keeps the accepted stand gaps
  of a refused call for the retry. The answer carries `questions`: what was `recorded`, what was `already` settled, what was `unread`
  (with the reason and the way out), what was `named_not_recorded`, the plan lines, the rework the answers owe with its door, and
  at gate B the rows that still branch on an answered question (`plan_not_changed`); an unreadable register reads `unknown`, never
  an empty list. The skill phases `s4.md` and `s8.md` say to quote it. A refused call tells no plan move it rolled back (those stand as
  `lines_if_recorded`); the side writes of a decision land in the story's own project even when the shell sits in another; after a
  recorded `approve as is` over an owed rework the rework is not started, its door stays in the answer (`questions.rework_left`) and
  the report's "Left with you" names it.

- Fixed: The cost capture no longer reports a role as a usage gap because the journal and the transcript spell its name differently. The journal's `subagent_stop` line names a role by its bare name (`qa-scout`), the transcript's sidecar by the host's namespaced one (`qa-factory:qa-scout`); the two are now compared as one role (`role_name`), and the dispatches of a role in the journal are counted against its transcript files, so a lost one of several dispatches is still named. `incomplete_agents` keeps its shape: the names, once each, in first-seen order. A line of the journal that is not JSON is skipped alone instead of ending the read; a journal that exists but cannot be opened is one stderr line. A dispatch id that repeats (a retry after a refusal) counts once: a gap can be missed there, never invented.

- Changed: A role named as a usage gap now shows on the By task row it belongs to, not on every row of its session. A new cost-file field, `incomplete_where`, lists the gaps the journal saw with no transcript behind them (`agent`, `activities`, `missing`; always present, `[]` when none); a gap whose transcript exists is found through the transcript's own rows. One helper (`gap_places`) reads the place for files of this release and of older ones. When a story's rows are split between its price and the rest of the ledger, a gap that has no rows of its own is put on one row for the whole file, never on two.

- Changed: A session that has ended is final without anyone asking: when a cost file says the usage is provisional and its transcript has been quiet for 30 minutes (key `cost.usage_final_after_idle_min`, never below 5 minutes) with every turn answered, the next dashboard render recomputes it once and the file says `complete`. A turn left open for 24 hours (key `cost.usage_final_after_open_h`) means the session died: its usage is final too, and the cost file says how (`usage_final.rule: timed_out`) and the row reads "ended mid-turn". A session that is still being written, or stopped mid-turn inside those 24 hours, stays provisional and is shown as information ("still being written", "stopped mid-turn; final after 24 h"), no longer as a cost-capture finding; "Stale cost files" no longer lists a session that is still being written, and the reconciliation note points at the findings block only when the page has one. `cost_capture.py --recapture --session <id>` writes `complete` only for a session that has ended.
- One stamp for the version of what a capture derives from a transcript: `READER_STAMP` is now `capture-0.10.7`; it is part of the capture key, of every scan checkpoint and of the cost file (`capture_logic`). A cost file written by another logic is recomputed once on the first render (whatever its size), unless it is another project's session or is being written right now (reported as `kept`, shown as recorded). A file whose transcript is gone is left as recorded: an older logic alone is never an alarm.
- Two new optional config keys, `cost.usage_final_after_idle_min` (default 30) and `cost.usage_final_after_open_h` (default 24). A value that is not a finite non-negative number gives the default and one line on stderr.

- Changed: The turn that starts an activity is now the activity's price. The person's message and the orchestrator's first requests come before the `--action start` event; they used to be nobody's (Unclassified) although that turn is what the story, doctor or onboarding was started for. An activity's first segment now begins at the last turn opener (the person's message, or a background task's notification) before its start, never earlier than the end of another activity's recorded segment, so a nested start (a doctor inside an onboarding) moves nothing and a turn that started no activity stays where it was. Only the first segment moves; the sum over rows is unchanged. A project with no readable host forms, a Codex session and a role dispatched inside a parent's activity are left as they were.
- The time the person waits is counted from the person's own messages only. A tool result, a host meta line, a compaction summary and a background task's notification are no longer read as the person coming back (a tool result carries the promptId of its turn, so every tool call used to count as an answer). Which rows are not the person's is data: the new row `claude.not_a_person_turn` in `references/host-report-forms.json` (`flags`, `notification_prefixes`), read through `host_adapter.report_forms`. A slash command's `<command-message>` row is the person's (the command was typed); its `isMeta` row is not. With the row unreadable the old reading stands, no turn is moved, and one line on stderr says so.
- A folder under `qa-factory/state/` is never a task. A Write into `state/onboarding/` used to open a task called `onboarding` and price the rest of an onboarding session to it; only `qa-factory/artifacts/<task>/` names a task now. A project written by a version before 0.3.0 (task folders under `state/`) is no longer split into tasks by its Writes: its rows fall to "(no task)".
- Existing cost files keep the old split until they are captured again; the scan checkpoint records which rule it was made with and is rebuilt once when the rule changes.

- Changed: A story whose only record is the chat (no driver journal names a session of it) is no longer shown as a problem. The price answer carries `single_source`; the "By task" cell reads "single source (chat): nothing to cross-check against" in a grey information class, the price note and the retro's price paragraph use the same words, and the word "not cross-checked" stays for the cases where a second record was expected (a session still being written, a CLI charge that is unknown). A real gap beside it (a role without usage) still turns the cell red and is named; an information line such as "1 session still being written" never turns it red.
- A session whose transcript was written less than 30 minutes ago (the project's idle limit, `cost.usage_final_after_idle_min`) is "still being written" in the price too, unless the driver's journal holds a recorded charge for it, which proves the process ended; inside 5 minutes it is always still being written.

- An agent that takes several dispatches keeps every binding, and the turn budget says what it counts (DC1-11). On run 14857 four
  dispatches were sent as messages to one agent; its host receipt is one file per agent and `story_step.py bind` overwrote the dispatch id,
  so three of the four were forgotten, and the turn budget told each of them "this dispatch has made N tool calls". `bind` now also writes
  `bound_dispatches` (task, dispatch, time, in the order of first binding) into the receipt, read through the one function
  `host_dispatch.bound_dispatches`; the scalar `dispatch_id` stays the last binding, so nothing that reads it changes its answer.
  The notice names the agent ("this agent has made N tool calls ... whichever dispatch they belonged to") and, from two bound dispatches
  up, says "across M dispatches (latest D)". A host that sends no agent id gets "this role has made N tool calls in this session". The
  count stays the agent's: the context that is billed is the agent's, and the dispatch boundary is visible to code only at `bind`. The
  number of dispatches can be too low, never too high, and an unreadable receipt gives the plain form.

- The pre-tool guard's refusal of a resume to an id this story never ran now names the door when a live dispatch of the
  story can take the id, instead of only sending the conductor to a fresh dispatch: the ready `story_step.py bind` line
  for a running dispatch (or one that returned without acceptance, on a stage not yet accepted), and the ready
  `story_step.py resume --agent-id` line for a dispatch stopped for a person that no agent holds. A strategist that
  stopped with an empty form can be sent back to fill it, once its id is bound. The door is never named where it would
  not open: a retired agent, a name another story's receipt holds (on either host, a Codex spawn receipt with no dispatch
  id included), a name whose receipt of this story names a retired dispatch, a dispatch the controller would refuse to
  resume (a closed story among them), or a story with no such dispatch keeps the old text. When no name in the
  empty-record refusal is open (each is a retired agent, a vetoed receipt, or held by another story), the refusal now says
  a new dispatch is the answer instead of offering the bind. The refusal stays a refusal in every case.

- The gate A card "I cannot tell which running container serves the tests" keeps its promise. Each container the card lists
  (up to five, plain names) is now a closed answer: the person writes `<check id>: <container name>`, and the driver first runs the
  read-only content check of that container; only when the check says `matched` does it run the existing probe-registration
  command, once. Any other verdict, a timeout or an unreadable answer registers nothing, is told in words and leaves the gate open
  with the other names still answerable. Nothing is recorded as passed by the answer. A name that is not on the card, or only looks
  like one, is still the conductor's, and the card names the containers it cannot take. The two sibling cards that said "name it"
  (the stand refused, or docker lists no container) now say to name the container in words, and the conductor has a row for it.

- A first typed run with no runtime probe is refused with the command that writes it (EP1-24, `execution_request.py`): the S5 refusal now
  ends with one ready command, `runtime_probe.py --suggest --write --profile <profile>`, with the container filled in when exactly one is
  running (when the story's files are on record, only the containers that hold them count); with several it names up to five (`(+N more)`
  beyond) and leaves the choice to the role, with none or with docker silent it gives the command without a container. The
  `--template request` door stays. A profile that has no entry while others do is named as such, an entry with no `argv` is named as
  unusable, and a profile that already has an entry is never told to rewrite it; a profile with no recorded checkout, or a freshness
  read, gets no write door (the first says why). The containers are asked only on this refusal, never when a probe is registered.
- `runtime_probe.py --suggest --write` no longer ends in a traceback after the entry is written (EP1-24): the one check that follows is
  bounded to 30 s (`VERIFY_TIMEOUT_S`; the stored entry keeps `timeout_s: 120`), a check that does not finish or prints a `{` that is not
  JSON is said on stderr with the entry already written, the exit is 0, and `probe check took N s` records the time. The cause of the
  earlier 180 s was not established by measurement.
- A road with no driver gets the stand probe's command (EP1-24, `stage_done.py`): the refusal that closing the stage in front of a gate appends
  ` [command: ...]` to a `s5_runtime_probe` finding that carries a typed `argv`, resolved to this machine; an argv that still holds a
  `{token}` is never shown, a finding without `argv` or of another check (the reporter's helper line is not a command for a role) reads
  as before, and the person's word is matched on the finding's text, never on the command. `p4-generate.md` says that a project
  onboarded without the entry gets it at gate A.

- `manual_capture.py app`: the hands of a manual-agent capture on a device stand (a project whose `environments[]` row names a `surface` driven through a driver server). The steps are a closed list of their own (`app_steps` in `references/manual-capture-steps.json`: `launch`, `click`, `fill`, `fill-account`, `drag`, `wait`, `read`, `back`, `source`, `log`, `capture`); a selector is `<strategy>=<value>` with a strategy the surface's row lists, and a browser step (`goto`, `type`, `fail_request`) is refused with "no such step on this surface". The session opens through `device_stand` (a device that is not ready, a server that is not ready or a session that does not start is exit 3 with `cause: device`, never a login message), is deleted in `finally`, and every stored file says the network of the device is not confined to the stand. `source` stores the screen's element tree as a state file (hidden from the session's accounts, scanned for secrets); `log` stores the device log tail. The sign-in screen is told by `manual_capture.login.app.sign_in_selector`; without it the window never closes and `capture` is refused with that key as the door. Written against a fake driver only: no real driver or device has run it.
- `manual_capture.py` blocked-call sentences (`build`, `login`, `stand` and the new `device`) are data (`refusals.blocked_*` in `references/build-identity-methods.json`); the web texts are unchanged byte for byte.

- The build probe now reads the build a device holds (EP1-41e). On a device stand it asks `device_stand.py` for the device and the installed app (id, version, code) and for the hash of the installed file(s) (`pm path`, then `sha256sum` of each path, both named in the `artifact` block of the Android row of `references/surfaces.json`); the identity the person's word binds to is the digest of that whole value. A reinstall of the same version with another file, a new version or a new code therefore voids the word, and the question the person reads says so. When the file cannot be hashed the version line is kept, the record carries a `limitation`, and the question promises only what is seen ("a different version on the device voids it"). A build that cannot be read at all (no device, the app not installed, a failing tool, no version) is an `unknown` with its reason and no question; a version is never taken for a revision, so `matched` stays with a `command` row of the stand. A new question variant, `device_build` (data in `references/build-identity-methods.json`), is asked on a device stand instead of the no-container one, and `definition_sha` of a stand that names a `surface` now also covers its app id and driver address (a stand with no `surface` hashes as before).

- A new command, `scripts/device_stand.py`, tells the stand of a device surface (EP1-41b): is a device connected, does the driver server answer its status, and with `--deep` does one minimal session open and close. It reads `references/surfaces.json` through `surfaces.py`, so no platform, tool or driver name is in its code. A tool that is missing, a tool that failed and a tool that printed nothing it should have are each told apart from "no device"; an empty or unrecognised device list is the factory's to say, never "no device"; two ready devices with none named are never resolved to the first; a status that is not exactly `ready: true`, a page, a redirect or a cut answer is never "ready"; a session that fails to start while the server is ready is its own outcome. Each problem is told with its owner and a door, and the first one comes in the form of an environment block (`cause: device`). It asks a person nothing. Fake tests only: no device or driver server has been run.

- "This command is pytest" has one reading, and it no longer takes another runner's argument for the program (EP1-1). Two functions answered the
  question (`node_ids.is_pytest`, `execution_request.is_pytest_command`) and a `pytest` word anywhere in a command counted: `npx playwright test
  tests/pytest` was read as pytest and got `--junitxml` injected. Now there is one predicate; it strips quotes and `.exe`/`.cmd`/`.bat`, and a
  `pytest` token with another runner started to its left (any prefix of the command is a known test form) is that runner's argument. The
  other name delegates, so its importers keep working. A new `launch_check.runner_identity` is the one reader of "which runner is this command"
  (form id, collect row, the optional `selection` of a `run_forms` row, a problem of the table, or the words for a project's own script the
  factory does not read inside). `references/launch-causes.json` gains the optional `selection` of the `playwright-test` form (data, not code),
  measured on a real Playwright 1.64.1 JUnit report: the class name is the path from the test root, with `\` on Windows, and the name is the
  titles joined by a single angle quote (U+203A) without the project.

- A path is "under the tests of a profile" by one reading everywhere (EP1-12). The mutation probe's "is this an oracle place" check, the
  profile selector and the gate's reporter rehearsal each normalised the test root their own way: the probe cut a leading slash (so an
  absolute path counted as a project path) and let `tests/../src/app.py` pass the root compare, and the rehearsal read "this folder is not
  below the collect's root" as "the whole collect", offering a test outside the profile's folder to prove its report. Now the probe spells
  every path and root with the selector's one spelling and compares with the selector's one `path_under`; an empty, absolute or
  climbing (`..`) path is never a test place, and a protected path under a test root still wins. The rehearsal asks the collect only
  when the profile's folder lies below it, otherwise it takes the first test file of that folder. An unnamed manifest row beside a row
  that names a profile is refused, with the doors, when the path of its file lies under another profile's test root (it was run under
  the named profile before); a row under no root runs as before.

- A Playwright project gets a readable JUnit report without a hand-written run (EP1-22). Playwright names its report file by a
  variable, and a command could set none, so the onboarding cure for it was "explain only" and every run ended in a hand-made S6. A
  command in `profiles[].commands.one_test` may now carry an optional `env`: variable names, each exactly `{report_path}`; the
  factory sets them for that one command only, with the run's own report file (nothing else is allowed in a value, so no secret and no
  path of one machine reaches the shared config). `{report_path}` stands in exactly one place, in a word of `argv` or in one value of
  `env`; S5's contract, the probe and `report_adapt` count both. The Playwright cure is one row of `references/report-cures.json`
  (`add_argv` and `add_env`), proposed as one change the person says yes to, and the question names the variable in words. A command
  given by a person that starts with `NAME=value` is refused in words (the factory runs no shell); one without a placeholder takes
  its cure row's variable. A receipt, a kept report and an "accept always" given for the same words under another `env` are no longer
  the same command; for a command with no `env` every key and digest is what it was.
  A command's `env` is part of what "already done" means: a proposal that only sets the variable is pending until it is on disk, so
  the person's yes writes it.
  The reporter probe now judges the report FILE the command was given and nothing beside it: a missing, empty or folder-shaped report
  is "no report file" (the reason names the files left beside it), a neighbour file is never a proof, and the helper is not handed a
  reader that "fits" a file S5 never reads. A project proven earlier by a neighbour file keeps its receipt; S5 names the problem.

- A stand whose application does not run in a container no longer ends manual checking in a dead end (EP1-28). The profile of a
  `manual_capture.py ui` or `http` capture is now the project's own (`profiles[].capabilities` against `capture_surfaces` in
  `references/manual-capture-steps.json`, the plan's profile for the case when several fit, or `--profile <id>`), not the literals
  `e2e-ui` and `api`; an ambiguous or missing profile is a refusal (exit 2) before any attempt, browser or request exists. A stand with
  no `execution.runtime_probes` entry gets the default probe in memory (the factory's `runtime_probe.py` over the application's
  checkout, no container; never written to the config): `stand_probe_spec` returns the reason when there is none (no checkout, two
  repositories, two stands), and that reason is the capture's line with the door `runtime_probe.py --suggest --write --no-container`.
  Two repositories of one profile are told apart by `implementation_repos[].role` against `application_roles` in
  `references/build-identity-methods.json`; any other input stays a refusal, and an application repository with no `local_path` is
  named instead of the tests' checkout being taken. On the manual half of S6 a stand with no container reaches the build question as
  the `no_container` variant ("is that commit there?": `deployed`, `retry`, `command`, `stop`), with the containers docker runs named
  (five, then a count). A checkout that is not a git repository answers with `reason_code: no_expected_revision` and a refusal that
  offers no "capture again". When the build question of the stage was about another profile than the capture chose, the refusal says
  so and names the person's word or the conductor as the door; the code never picks `--profile` itself. The dead advice to "add
  --container for a stand that is not a docker one" is replaced by `--no-container` in `runtime_probe.py --suggest` and in the S5
  refusal. The browser door and the harness interpreter no longer name `e2e-ui` or `poetry`. Two conductor actions are added for the
  person's words "it does not run in a container" and "I do not know which build it runs".

- A manual check can now type into a field the way a user does (EP1-29). `manual_capture.py ui` gains three step words:
  `type <selector> <text> [<delay_ms>]` focuses the field ONCE, keys the text one character at a time (200 ms apart by default, up
  to 200 characters, delay 1 to 2000 ms) and logs the field's value and whether it still has focus after each character, then once more
  after 1500 ms (`settled`: a page redraws after the server answers, later than any one keystroke); `press <selector> <key>` presses one
  key of a closed list (or one printable character) and logs `focused_before`, read before the focus is set; `paste <selector> <text>`
  inserts the text at once (an `input` event, not a `paste` event, so an `onPaste` handler is not exercised). A lost focus or a lost
  value is told in the step line and the log, never judged by code: the step stays `ok`, so the screenshot of the defect can still be
  taken. An empty text, a delay or a text beyond its limit and a key outside the list are refused at parsing, with the door (`press
  Control+A` then `press Backspace` to clear a field, `fill` for a longer text). The limits and the probe wait are data in
  `references/manual-capture-steps.json`. The case designer and the code critic are told that a field whose value goes to the server
  or redraws the page is checked by behavior, not by one `fill`.

- A manual check can now make a dependency of the page fail (EP1-30). `manual_capture.py ui` gains two step words:
  `fail_request <url_glob> <status|timeout>` answers every browser request of the page that matches the glob with a status from 400
  to 599 (an empty JSON body) or drops it as timed out (never held, so the step does not hang); `restore_request <url_glob>` stops it.
  A glob with a host must name a configured stand host (the route would otherwise answer in a foreign host's name): it is refused
  with the list of stand hosts; a glob with no host is fine, and a request to a host that is not a stand still goes to the context
  guard and is aborted. The record of each failure lives the whole session: its log (`METHOD url`, no query, at most 50 lines with
  `... and N more`, a line that matches a secret pattern counted, not kept) is a supporting capture written at `restore_request`,
  when the pattern is repeated, and at the end of the session. A `capture post_action` is REFUSED (no screen, exit 1, the door named)
  while any failure of the session, active or restored, caught no request: a screen of a page that never met the failure proves
  nothing; the request of a server-rendered page is not seen by a browser route, and the refusal says the check then needs another
  level. A failure that caught nothing is also a limitation of the attempt and a name in the summary's `failures_without_hits`.
  The `capture post_action` step line carries `hits_at_capture` (the count per pattern at that screen); code does not judge whether
  the hit came from the case's action, the runner compares the count with the one before the action. The sign-in by code runs before
  the steps and does not see the route: a refused login is tested by a session with `fill-account`. The bounds (400 and 599, 50
  lines) are data in `references/manual-capture-steps.json`.

- a manual capture and the investigation probe sign in by code from what the project RECORDED (`manual_capture.http_login_source`, EP1-31): its own `manual_capture.login.http` first; else `environment.access` of kind `local_login` at the address it records (a key name is read from the project's env files, the token is found under `access_token`, `token`, `id_token`, ... also inside `data` / `result`); else the factory's default recipe, only for a project that records no access kind at all. `harness_command`, `bearer_env`, `oidc_password` or an unknown kind with no recipe refuse BEFORE any request ("login by code: ... nothing was sent", with the key to record), so an account is never sent to an address or in a form the project did not record; `environment.access.kind: none` means no login by code, said on stderr
- a failed default sign-in no longer reads as a rejected account when the stand answers 404 at the factory's own guessed address: the message names the address, says the recipe was never confirmed, and names the key to record; every sign-in failure now names where the recipe came from
- the factory's default sign-in FORM is waited for 5 seconds (`login.ui_fit_wait_s`), not the 30 second element limit; a project's own `manual_capture.login.ui` keeps the full wait
- onboarding (phase 4) writes `manual_capture.login.http` after one closed question when the project signs in by a harness command, and copies the whole `login.ui` recipe with the project's `landed.url_not` when its sign-in page is elsewhere
- `stand_access.token_value` is the one walk of a login answer for a session token; `_token_in` is its yes/no

- A manual check can now tell a missing attribute from an empty one, and read an element's state (EP1-32). `read <selector>
  attr=<name>` used to turn "the element has no such attribute" into an empty string, the same as an attribute that is present and
  empty; it now stores the marker `<absent>` for a missing attribute and keeps an empty string for an empty one. `read <selector>
  state=<name>` stores `true` or `false` for one of `disabled`, `enabled`, `checked`, `visible`, `editable`; a state outside the list
  is refused at parsing with the list, and a state the page cannot answer (for example `checked` on a field that is not a checkbox)
  is a failed step, never `false`. The marker and the states are data in `references/manual-capture-steps.json`
  (`read_absent_marker`, `read_states`). The runner is told that "disabled" or "enabled" is proved by `read ... state=...` or by a
  click without effect, and is otherwise `inconclusive`.

- a test command that starts with a Windows `.cmd` wrapper (`npx`, `npm`, `poetry`) is launched the way the shell would: its head is resolved on the environment's PATH and PATHEXT, and an argument that cmd.exe would read as something else (`&`, `|`, `<`, `>`, `^`, `%`, `!`, a quote, a line break) is REFUSED with a sentence that names the token and the door (correct the argv, or start the runner directly), instead of being silently corrupted or run as a second command; the refusal is a broken run at S5, a `launch_failed` collect, an unreadable probe, and "no report" at the reporter rehearsal (`project_env.checked_launch`, `CmdUnsafe`)
- the probes that run a command once (the runtime probe, its rehearsal, the reporter rehearsal, `--suggest` verification) kill the whole process tree at their time limit and return inside the limit plus a short grace, however a `.cmd` wrapper's child holds the pipe (`node_ids.run_captured`, `run_bounded(merge_stderr=False)`); a bare `npx` no longer raises "file not found" in them
- "the program is not found" now says what was checked (looked up on PATH with PATHEXT) and the door (install it, or correct argv[0] of the profile) instead of "not on this machine"; the question to the person is unchanged

- The probe "the test can fail" reads a Playwright TypeScript test (EP1-36). A title with a template substitution (`adds ${n}`) is refused only by a language whose entry has no `title_template`, or when fewer than three literal characters remain; otherwise it is a pattern and the declaration is found by the same matcher a report row is tied by (`test_source.matches`). Tags (`title_tag`) are taken out of both sides of every title comparison. Several candidates are still the old refusal with `--at <line>`. A run whose report holds several rows of one test (a template, a loop, several projects) judges each: the mutation is `intended_failure` only if every row failed as intended, and the surviving row is named; no row at all, rows of different files or an unbound row leave `not_executed` with the reason instead of failing on an empty list. A row with no hand-written `selector_args` and `report_test_id` is built by the code that builds them for a typed run; a profile whose command is the project's own script is refused by name (the probe is not run on it and onboarding offers the direct form), never passed.
- `profile_contract.selectors_verified(profile, root)` is the one answer to "is this profile's selector contract verified", asked by the probe's shape check and by the typed run's request: a hand-written `selectors.verified` wins in both directions; with none, the command must be one a run form selects a test with and the onboarding's rehearsal record must name this very command. The record proves that the command was rehearsed, not that the selector selects; a report row is bound by id, so a wrong True never gives a pass.
- A probe that could not judge because of the tool says so: the record carries `language` and `cause: tooling` for an `incomplete` verdict and for a report row that could not be bound (a stand that wrote no report writes no cause). One person's word `probe gap: tooling:<language>` then accepts that class once, for every instance whose own record says the same and is of the current bytes; a word about the instance or its case is read first, another language is a new question, and a record that judged the test, a record of other bytes and a red test take no such word. The delivery is unchanged: "Left with you", `not probed`.
- A refusal of the TOOL (a language with no row, a broken table, a file the lexer cannot read, no declaration or no assertion form of the entry, a command the probe cannot select on) now also leaves the record `refused: tool` beside the same one-line JSON and exit 2, when the manifest proves the test is the instance's. A wrong call (a missing file, another instance's file, a name that is not the row's) leaves none; an `intended_failure` stands.

- A test file in any language is read by the data of its language, and a language with no row is no longer a stop (EP1-37). One reader, `scripts/test_source.py`, lists the tests of a file whose suffix has an `assertion_probes` entry in `references/detectors.json` (title with its tags, group titles, a loop or a table as a pattern, the line of the test call) and says plainly what it could not read; the entry's new optional fields (`title_tag`, `title_template`, `title_placeholders`, `group_declaration`, `each_declaration`, `loop_heads`) are validated like the rest. `manifest_from_tests.py` writes the rows of such a file (no Then bindings: the language has no marker), and for a file whose language has no row it prints a note that names the file, the suffix and the door (`manifest_put.py --fragment`, with the row form) and exits 0 without calling `manifest_put`; its cases stay unbound and `s5_precheck.py` names them. A part of a file with a row that could not be read is one refusal that lists the lines. `--collect` with such a file is refused as pytest-only.
- A run of a runner whose data states a `selection` (Playwright's `file:line`) builds its selector and its report identity by code from the file as it is now, with the file name escaped; a value the role wrote wins. The report row is matched by one matcher (`red_sandbox.selection_rows`: the classname the runner writes relative to its test directory, with `\` on Windows, a name joined by the runner's separator, a pattern for a loop), and every matched row is judged: one green row never closes a red one, and an id that is not in the report is `not_run` with the code `id_not_in_report`, counted on its own in the run summary and named on the console. The per-test identity (`instance_content_sha`, `instance_code_sha`) of such a test is the file less the other tests, so an edit of a neighbour changes nothing and an edit of anything above the test does; its scope is `file_skeleton`.
- Onboarding says, once and in words, when a profile's test command is the project's own script (the factory reads no script, so per-test selection and the probe stay "not probed" on it) and offers the direct command (`direct_form`). The report names the unmeasured expectation changes of a reader the factory could not apply as a gap of its tool, not of the product.

- The S5 exit finds a case file where the project keeps it, and no longer reads a soft failure as a stopped test (EP1-38). When the
  strict name search (`<case>.md`, unchanged and still first) finds nothing, `find_case_file` asks the story's case index, so a
  project that keeps cases under its own `cases_root` with names like `TC-001-add-to-cart.md` is no longer told "no case file with
  numbered Then clauses was found"; a bare id that two areas hold resolves to nothing rather than to the other area's file, and
  the refusal now names the files and folders it looked under. For a test that is red by its own `contradicts_requirement` row,
  `red-own-behind` (a Then bound `covered` behind the red assert) is lifted ONLY when the red lines are made of soft assertions
  only (`soft_assert_patterns` of the language's `detectors.json` entry, read on the code with comments and strings blanked), the
  newest run block's own raw report is readable, and EVERY failure frame of the test in it lies inside the red lines - a throw, a
  later hard assert or a call into a helper keeps the finding. Any unknown (no report, a changed sha, a language with no entry, a
  mixed or unpinned span) keeps it as before. `manifest_put.py` refuses a hand-typed `tests[].obligation_hash` that is not the
  hash of the row's `obligation_refs` (the patch's, else the stored row's); leave it out, the code builds it.

- `manifest_put.py` no longer erases the `tests[]` rows of a case when an `unresolved[]` row speaks about particular Thens (EP1-39). A
  `contradicts_requirement` row that names only `thens` (no `instance_ids`, no `partitions`) used to read as "the whole case is
  unresolved" and took every test row of the case out of the manifest; now the rows that ran (a status other than `pending_run`,
  `blocked_by_env` or `not_run`; no status counts as ran) stay, and so does the row. A stored Then row is taken by a test only when the
  fragment says `status: green` for the case and no row of the case is red, so a green instance beside a red one proves one Then, not
  the case. When a row does move tests out (a case with no run, or a row that names no Thens), `manifest_put` prints one line per
  test row, `moved out of tests[]: <instance> (case <case> is now wholly unresolved ...; name the instances: instance_ids: [...])`.
  A `tests[]` patch that turns a stored `critic_verdict: unverified` into `approved` with no `critic_note` is refused before the commit:
  a receipt that lacks a probe is a tooling gap, not an approval. `contract.then_remainder_rows` no longer lets such a Then row hide
  the `blocked_by_check` rows of its case.

- A mobile application stand can now be described, checked and asked about (EP1-41c). An `environments[]` row may name a `surface`
  (a row of `references/surfaces.json`) with `driver`, `device` and `app`; `config_contract.py` refuses a `surface` the table lacks,
  an Appium address that is not http(s) or holds a user or a password, a serial key that is a value and not a name. The
  readiness environment check no longer reads a stand with no address as "in-process, nothing to probe": a device stand is asked
  of the device check (read-only, no session), only a verdict `ok` is ok, and a probe that cannot run, a missing application id or
  an unreadable table is `unknown` or `not_configured`, never `ok`. `env_probe.py --env <device stand>` answers the same way
  (exit 0 only for a live device stand), before any address is looked for. In a project that has both an API stand and a device
  stand, the build question of the native profile is about the DEVICE stand (`surfaces.stand_of_profile`), the web profile's about
  the API stand, and a profile with no stand of its own is a line and no question. `runtime_probe.py --suggest` of a device stand
  writes the entry with no container and does not ask docker; a device row no longer makes "two stands" for a web profile.
  Onboarding asks one closed batch for the mobile stand and writes the probe entry after the row. A web or API config is read
  exactly as before (the table is not read). No device or Appium server has been run: code and fake tests only.

- A story on a device stand (a project whose `environments[]` row names a `surface` driven through a driver server) is no longer asked about things its road does not need. The stage-5 gates key a plan row to the test profile that holds the capability of the surface whose `fits_levels` names the row's level (after the capability and id fits, before the single-profile fallback; two such profiles key nothing; a web or API project never reads the table). The brief of a manual runner block hands the `manual_capture.py app` line and `references/manual-evidence-app.md` only when the project has a device stand; `agents/qa-runner.md` names `app` in one short parenthesis, and `role-commands.json` has its row. Onboarding tells the planning roles that a case run on a device carries the device profile's `execution_profile_id`.

- A project that tests a desktop application, a command-line tool or a mobile application is no longer met with silence (EP1-41a).
  `references/surfaces.json` is the factory's closed table of test surfaces (how each is driven, who holds the hands, how a
  stand is told), and `scripts/surfaces.py` is its one reader. `readiness.py --json` gains a `surfaces` key only when there is
  something to say: a desktop or command-line project (alone) is told that agent checks on it are not supported and those cases
  go to a person; a native-application test profile with no described device stand is told the same; a table that cannot be read
  is `unknown`, never a crash and never silence. A web or API project never reads the table and its output is unchanged byte for
  byte (a pinned fixture of the `ui` and `http` captures, the `_blocked` refusals, the readiness environment and the data
  blocks). The table names no test language and no runner: tests in any language run by the project's command, and phase 1 of the
  onboarding now says the language it found. qa-doctor prints the `surfaces` words. No device or Appium server has been run:
  code and fake tests only.

- Changed: The S3 acceptance now runs the grounding check on every acceptance of the stage, not only the closing one. A window-1 (labelling) dispatch can no longer close S3 (it is accepted with `--not-complete --unresolved plan_pending`; a person's word does not pass this refusal), and its role findings are refused with the table's own check. At the exit the plan's errors and the grounding findings are one refusal: a missing table on a diff story, a table on a story with no diff, the table's check (R1 to R5, R8), the claims of the planner that are not in the register, and the new R7 - a risk `K-n` or an area `B-n` that matters must reach a plan row (`risk_source_refs`: `grounding:K-n` / `blast:B-n`) or a `not_planned` entry with `ref`, a plan reference must point at something the table holds, and the regression command of an area that matters must be named in the plan's `## Recommended regression` section by `blast:B-n`. The exit detector hands the role only the findings that are the role's. A check that could not run is a refusal with a name, never a pass; a person's word passes everything but the window-1 closing refusal. The S3 handover form gains the table as an input, the code-filled `grounding` and `blast_radius` sections, `not_planned[].ref`, and five claims checked by the same functions as the gate.

- `grounding_table.py --share --task T` (`share()`): measures the refactoring share of the S3 grounding table (counted lines of the
  production hunks whose rows carry a label the policy counts, against all changed production lines) and writes it as the ONE key
  `refactoring_share` through the table writer. The road (`none`, `notify`, `stop`) is `100*W > percent*T` in integers, strictly, with the
  thresholds and label words read only from `references/grounding-policy.json`; a share that cannot be measured (no policy, a table
  that is not whole, a production hunk with no mark, no changed production line) is `unknown` or `n/a` with a reason, never `none` and never `stop`.
  Nothing is written for a story without a diff or for a table the reader refuses.

- the tables a role writes are read by ONE cell reader, `grammar.split_cells` (G2-10): it cuts a row only on an unescaped bar, takes exactly one
  bar off each end (a cell that ends in `\|` right before the closing bar keeps it) and unescapes, so a `|` the role writes as `\|` no longer
  shifts the columns of a requirement register, a test plan, the behaviour-claims header or a branch table header; the writers use
  `grammar.escape_cell` (`project_decisions._cells` and `_escape` now delegate to the pair; the test-plan rewrite of an answered row writes
  every cell through it and leaves every other line byte for byte)
- a `## Register` or `## Plan` row with more cells than its header is refused with its R or TS id, the counts and the door `write | inside a cell
  as \|`, instead of reading a cell from another column; a register or plan `created` before 2026-10-31 keeps the old reading and gets one
  `--verbose` line, an unreadable `created` is read as new (`CELL_COUNT_CUTOFF`). The register template, the S2 and S3 phases and the
  requirements-tester and test-strategist charters tell the role to write a bar inside a cell as `\|`

- code and somebody else's test are no source of a requirement (`contract.unconfirmed_requirements`, G2-12, P20): a `derived` row with no `ac_ref`
  (`-` and `n/a` count as empty), a silent contradiction matrix and a `current-code:` observable, or a `derived_from` that starts with `test:`, is
  unconfirmed until the person answers reading `a` of its behaviour-claim question; the case, plan, coverage, manual-evidence and traceability
  readers all use it, so a Then resting on such a row reads `unknown` and never a pass. The function errs only toward "not confirmed" (no
  question list, `named`, reading `b`, a row edited since the answer, upper case and backticks all leave the row unconfirmed); `source: ac`,
