  `story` or `discussion` with a `current-code:` observable, a non-empty `ac_ref`, a `contradicts:` cell and `derived_from: invariant:` are not
  listed. A register `created` before 2026-10-31 keeps its old reading (`UNCONFIRMED_SOURCE_CUTOFF`); an unreadable date reads as new
- `derived_from` accepts `test:<ref>`; the register template, the S2 charter, the S2 phase and the refusal name `test:`, `norm:`, `bug:BUG-NNN`
  and `bug:candidate-defect`; the refusal of a claim row says its `now_ref` may be a diff line or a current-code place

- The S2 brief of the requirements tester now lists the places of the story's diff (and, on a repeat S2, the `current-code:` places of the register) that swallow a failure a user would meet: a `catch` that only logs, a `fetch` whose answer is read without its status. The shapes are data (`references/user-path-failure-patterns.json`); the tester judges which place lies on a user's path and writes a `derived` row for it. A language with no pattern, an unreadable table or a first S2 with no register is said as `not measured`, never as "no match". The full list is `work/user-path-failures.json`.

- A register row marked `derived_from: bug:candidate-defect` now reaches the plan and the roles: the S3 exit refuses a candidate that no row plans a test for, the strategist and the automator briefs carry one "Suspect places" line, and a misspelt `bug:` mark is refused by the S2 form check. The mark is data in `handoffs/vocabulary.yaml` (`derived_from_marks`).

- requirement coverage and the stop before window 2 of S3 (`grounding_table.py`, `story_run.py`): the code counts how many requirements of the
  register the change implements (`implemented` and `partial` over every requirement not implementation-only, not met elsewhere
  with a place named, and not shown untouched by the base slice); under the policy's percent, or when the merge request asks nothing of
  the story, the driver asks the person before the plan is written (`go on` / `stop`, free words go to the conductor). A word is for
  the exact state it was given for: a digest of the diff bytes and of the uncovered requirements, so a changed diff or table asks again.
  A measure the code cannot make is a refusal to the conductor, never a pass. The refactoring stop follows only after coverage passed
- `grounding_table.py --share` writes `requirement_coverage` beside `refactoring_share`; the S3 exit judges both over the current bytes
  (R6: a stop with no person's word for its present digest; R3: a saved road that differs from the fresh one)
- questions the strategist writes on a grounding row or a requirement line reach the question register as `Q-n` (`claim_projector.py`),
  one per row, once; the window-2 lines name what the code counted and the regression commands of the blast radius to carry into the plan

- a bug candidate no executed check stands behind is no longer silence at delivery (FR-22, `check_delivery.grounding_records`): a risk `K-n` of
  the grounding table (a story with a diff) and a register row marked `bug:candidate-defect` (any source) become a `bug_candidate` record
  when no plan row names it, when the rows that name it only `skip`, `manual-human` or `unverifiable`, or when its testing row is missing
  from the ledger ("could not be linked"); the kind is the third verdict (`after_checks`), reading code confirms no bug and moves nothing
  by itself, and the item is a line in "Left with you" whose `how` says gate B can send it to the failure analyst at S7 as a bug report
- a green row whose `oracle_unknown` nobody answered, and that no other green row backs, is an `unconfirmed_expectation` item for its
  candidate (the value it expects was never confirmed); a red candidate, and a candidate whose testing row did not run, add nothing (their own
  kinds say it); a grounding table or a register that exists and cannot be read is ONE `factory:` reason, never "no candidates"
- `planning_contract.row_tests_it(row)` is the one definition of "a row that tests it" (`automate` or `manual-agent`);
  `candidates_without_row` calls it, its behaviour is unchanged
- the conductor's rework row (`conductor-actions.json`) and the S3 charter and phase file say the road: a `K-n` row takes its Then from the
  requirement, and a candidate left unplanned reaches the person

- a requirement of the story that the change does not implement now blocks delivery whatever the person said (FR-21): a requirement the
  grounding table calls `not_implemented` becomes a `pending_implementation` record (`check_delivery.grounding_records`), so the verdict is
  `no` (owner product) and the item is never listed under "Left with you"; an `outside_diff` requirement with no place named is the same
  record only while the person's word for the current coverage stop stands; `partial` and `unknown` give none; a coverage that cannot be
  read at delivery is one factory record, not silence. The text family `grounding:` is registered in `delivery-reason-owners.json`
- gate A tells the person what the change touches: the share of refactoring (a line from the notify mark, the stop mark noted) and the
  requirements the change leaves out, named with the register's words and marked when a question below is about them; it asks nothing, a
  measure the table saved as unknown is said as a gap of the factory, and the lines are part of the head, so the line cap never cuts them
- the report's Size block ends with what the table saved: the refactoring share and its road (`n/a` printed), the requirement coverage with
  the requirements left out, changed blocks that are part refactoring, files outside the measure, orphaned records, areas measured on a cut
  list of callers or by name search only, and, for a story with no diff, the source of its null outcome; a table that cannot be read is one
  `Unknown` line. Below the notify mark this is a line of the report, never a gate

- Gate A packet: one list of the forms an answer can take. The "How to answer" section is built from a single list (`gate_brief.answer_forms`) in which every form names the reader that takes it, and it now stands whenever there is something to answer: an open item or a stand gap too, not only a question. The blocked-case line moved there from "After your approval"; its text is unchanged. Each question card ends with its own `Answer:` line carrying the question's real id. The three different "a helper reads the rest" sentences are one: anything else goes to the assistant running the story, who turns it into one of the forms or asks back, and only the forms are read by code.

- A case can say which integration it goes through. A new precondition `{"integration": "<name>"}` names one integration the project
  records (`environment.integrations`) by the name the S4 brief lists; it is met when the project's keys for it are set where the
  runner reads them (any set of its alternatives), else gate A shows a card naming the case, its partitions and the keys of the
  nearest set. An integration a case declares no longer makes a collective line or a story-level question of its own: the case's card
  asks. A name the project does not record is a finding of the factory (the case designer rewrites the line), never a question to the
  person; a recorded row with no keys, or one marked not needed on the stand, is a question that names the case.
- The S4 brief of the case designer and the case critic lists the integrations of the selected stand (name and who needs it, no key)
  and the stand's account roles, so a case declares them by name. The case critic raises a concern for a Given that goes through a
  listed service without that precondition.
- "Accept always" is offered for a declared integration and is remembered per stand by its name.

A person's answer about a probe gap now holds for every test of the story whose probe the factory's tool could not read, so the question is asked once and
not once per window (GW1-43). The data row `probe gap: <...>` of `references/block-names.json` carries a `class`; the word is stored with it, and the
window and the acceptance read it after the equality of the test's own word (`contract.probe_gap_class_word`, one reader) for a green test whose probe
record says the tool refused it or stopped half way (`proof_level.probe_record_state` and `probe_could_not_run`). A probe nobody ran, a record of
other bytes, a stand that was down and a probe that judged the test still need their own word; a taken-back word for one test keeps that test asked
while the class stands. The window prints the decision and its date next to each test it was applied to. The repeat of gate A for the test
repository state now carries a door (`test repository state: <HEAD>`), so one answer holds while S5 writes tests into the same tree. The S5 phase text
tells the role to say in the question that the answer covers the class.

- An unknown `pipeline.stop_after` is now named instead of silently ignored. A value that is not `gate_A`, `gate_B` or
  null (`"gate_a"`, `true`, `"GATE_A"`, ...) still stops nothing, but the readiness `config_schema` note says so ("it
  stops nothing and every story runs to the end"), and `readiness.py --require config_schema` prints a short `WARN` line
  even while the capability is `ok`, so story start puts it into `pipeline.warnings` and gate A shows it. The status is
  unchanged: the line is a note, not a refusal. The list of stop values is one constant (`hooklib.STOP_VALUES`) that the
  controller imports.
- A project configuration with a leading BOM, an empty file, a file that is not UTF-8 or a JSON document that is not an
  object is read through the package's one JSON reader: a BOM config is the project's config, and an unreadable one reads
  as an empty config (no-op), never as a list. `hooklib.artifact_root` reads the BOM too and still raises on a broken file.

- A late word on an integration at gate A now reaches gate B: if you accepted a case and then wrote a different word for one of the
  integration gaps the case is tied to (`INT-...`), gate B shows the card again with what changed, instead of keeping the old
  accept. An integration the project records after your answer, and that the case is tied to, is a new stand gap for the case.
- When the factory cannot read which integrations a case is tied to (the plan, a case, or the project config cannot be read), gate
  B asks the case again and says so, instead of treating the earlier answer as still covering it.
- New `gate_preflight.integration_ids_of_case(task_root, case)`: the integration gap ids a case has at this moment (the one reader of
  the relation between the project's integrations and the story's cases, shared with the gate A cards).

- Gate A no longer shows a wall of integration lines. The cards of one integration (one per case that needs it) are ONE line in
  "After your approval": the integration, the cases it costs (six, then how many were left) and a pointer to the cards below; the
  cards, their words and their ids stay one per gap, so one answer still closes one gap. The five-line limit counts these lines, so an
  integration is never hidden behind "+N more", and integrations are listed before other rows.
- The one line for integrations the factory could not match to any case now says what is known: no case of this story declares a need
  for them, and the project does not say who needs them in a form the factory can match; a test that does need one stops in S5 and is
  reported as not run.
- A card about access to an integration says what is missing in plain words, without an `env:` or `service:` prefix.
- New `gate_preflight.unmatched_integrations(task_root)`: the integrations that line names, and whether that is known, for a reader of
  a later stage (it writes nothing and opens no socket).

- Gate A asks about a case's account or the address of the stand's UI only when the project does not already hold it. A role
  is read by one reader: `default_user`, `Default-User` and `default user` are the same role of a stand (an exact key wins, two
  keys of one spelling are never guessed between), and the gate, the capture sign-in and the screen-login check now agree on
  it. `{"stand_account": "default"}` is the stand's default account (met when its two variables are set). A new precondition
  `{"stand_frontend": "<why the case needs the stand's UI>"}` is met when the project records an address of the stand's UI.
- A question about an account, or about the address of the UI, now says where the answer goes (the env file the runner reads)
  and offers three ways out: put the values in the file and give the names, "it is not needed", or `<case>: accept as blocked`.
  A `none` precondition that names an account says that the case designer rewrites it to a `stand_account` once the account is
  recorded.
- A feature flag read without a login is never taken as on: a bare `200` or a missing field is "not verifiable", not a pass.
- The question about the UI's address offers only the way the recording tool accepts: the variable's name at most one stand, the
  address itself at several. Recording an account under another spelling of a role the stand already holds updates that role instead
  of adding a twin, and one name for both the login and the password is refused.

- Changed: A question to a person no longer calls an option recommended unless the writer first named who carries it out: the function or field of the factory that reads what the option changes. With no reader found, the option is not recommended, and if it stays, the text says it is unchecked and why; an option that changes a config key looks for that key's reader first, and with none there is no option. The rule is one line in `references/human-questions.md` after the price-and-consequences item, and the conductor's step for a decision only a person makes points at it. The code is unchanged: it prints no recommendation and cannot read the conductor's free text.

A person's recorded word now names a line by a whole identifier, and a taken-back word acts nowhere (GW1-1). The word `R-3` no longer passes a
line about `BR-3`, `R-30` or `R-3.1`, `PC-1` no longer passes `PC-10`, and a word about one test no longer passes its `[1]` variant: one
predicate (`contract.names_whole`) replaces the substring match in the gate's reader, in the dispatch an answer is routed to and in the
"block NOT lifted" check. A revoked word, `*` included, is read by no one (`contract.live_stage_overrides`): not by the story budget, the report,
the traceability appendix, the gate packet, the brief a role is handed, the "keep it local" readers or the stand-gap answers; revoking the latest
answer of a stand gap no longer brings an older answer of another stage back to life. A block that still holds a placeholder (`<case>`,
`RP-<profile>`) is refused with the real-value form and a door. A door the gate packet prints for a long open item now ends at a word
boundary, so it passes its own check. A requirement id is read only when it stands alone (`BR-1` is no `R-1`; `FR-21` is no `R-21`).

A person's earlier words now follow a story that moves to a new key (GW1-40). `waiver.py --carry-from <old key> [--carry-from-root <folder>] --task <new key>`, run by
the conductor after S0 of the new key made its folder, copies what the person said under the old key into the new history: the live words of S0-S2 and the words
of a class (a `class` record, the kinds of gap in `work/gap-classes.json`), each marked `carried_from`, with the old `at` and the source's `class`. A word of the new
story on the same block wins (`kept yours`), a word the person took back is never carried and never comes back, a repeat adds nothing (`already carried`), and
every word left behind is a line `not carried: <stage> · <block>` to tell the person. The old folder is not moved and not rekeyed, the form of `pipeline.json` is
unchanged, and a source that cannot be read is a refusal naming the door (`--carry-from-root` for a folder moved by hand), never "nothing to carry". The pre-tool
guard closes the form to every role: copying a person's words is theirs to start. The conductor has a row for it (`words_carry`). If the person has already been asked
at S1, that question is asked once more and the conductor says so.

- The exit gate names the story it is judging to every detector it starts. Before, a detector run by `finish` or by the driver
  guessed the story (the newest pipeline whose stage was running), so a refusal on story A could be lifted by a clean story B that
  was touched later. Now `exit_gate.all_errors` passes the folder of the named story in `QA_FACTORY_DETECTOR_STORY`, and
  `sizing.py`, `planning_contract.py`, `critic_rollcall.py`, `s5_precheck.py` and the S2 gate `branch_accounting.py` read it through one helper
  (`planning_contract.detector_story`). A task that names no story folder (a phantom, a wrong case, a path or a blank) is the
  third state of the gate (`unreadable`), never a guess; a bare call and a hook with no story keep the guess as before. The
  adviser `sizing.py` now runs after the verdict, so a refused stop no longer leaves a `work/sizing.json` behind; an adviser that
  exits non-zero with output leaves a signal to the person, never a block and never nothing.

Gate A names two documents to approve, not four (GW1-11). The gate A message now opens with a line built by code from one list
(`gate_brief.GATE_A_DOCUMENTS`): approve `understanding.md` and `test-plan.md`; the brief is a summary. The pinned cases are part of the
plan, so `case-appendix.md` and `requirements-register.md` are no longer listed among the documents; the files are still written.

The plan disputing itself no longer reaches a person as a choice (GW1-29). An `automate` row at e2e-ui whose `impact`, `likelihood` and `verification_depth` do not say highest risk stays a warning at the S3 exit (exit 0, the strategist's judgement), and now a branch of `if_answered` that makes a row such a row is warned about too. Gate A shows these rows as one line headed "e2e rows without a highest-risk field (n), for your information", with no options.

A gate answer that starts with `approve` and then answers the packet's items in their own forms is no longer sent whole to the conductor because some of those lines could not be read (GW1-33). The driver now asks the controller to record the approval anyway; the controller still refuses it while an item of the packet is open, and then the answer goes the old road, kept whole for the conductor. The lines nobody could read are told to the person as "not understood" (twenty at most, then a count) and are kept whole in the answer's journal row; they are never recorded as accepted. A `bug` answer beside `approve` still goes to the conductor.

- a free answer to a question of the register is read before the gate A decision seals the plan (`question_register.question_lines_unread`,
  `Driver.record_by_code`, GW1-34): a line that names an open question and is no token (`Q3: not confirmed, keep open`, `Q1: a (note)`, an empty
  `Q1:`) sends the approval to the conductor, with a note naming the line and the doors (`question_register.py --answer` / `--defer`), instead of
  being recorded without it; the code never guesses the letter. A question already settled or kept open until the report, a line in a code
  block or a quote, and the replaced earlier answer are not counted; `approve as is`, a dry run and gate B are not held; a register that cannot be
  read is an unknown and goes the conductor's road too

- The S3 exit now fences the register: every id of `## Register` must reach a row of `work/test-plan.json` and the `R` column of `test-plan.md`; a `not_planned` entry no longer stands in for a row. An unreadable register is `UNREADABLE`, never a pass, and never printed beside a known refusal. A requirement that waits for a gate A question must hold a row whose branch changes with the answer; the S4 rehearsal asks for the case an answer would need (`row_owes_case`), and a branch that makes a row `automate` carries its `level`. Gate A cards say "waits for your answer" for such a row.
- A case that stayed on a `skip` or `unverifiable` row and never ran is set aside in the delivery trace instead of reading as a broken chain (a case that ran is never set aside). A row excluded while its gate A question is still open (or could not be read) is no decision: the trace reads it `wait`, the delivery verdict is `after_checks` and Left with you names the question; once the question is answered `b` or `not needed` the row reads as before. A branch patch that drops an obligation id a case quotes is refused at the S4 rehearsal, and a gate A card says out loud when no answer changes a row or a case.

- a line of the gate A words that starts with a question id and is no answer (`Q1: a (see the ticket)`) is told as what it is
  (`question_register.near_answer`, `gate_brief.question_note`, `report_facts` "Decided at gate A", GW1-42): the card and the report say the
  factory did not read that line as an answer and show it, instead of "no answer is recorded", and tell the person to write `Q1: a` alone on a
  line; the conductor's note names the letter the line seems to carry (only a letter of the question's readings) so the closed question to the
  person is "confirm Q1 - a?". The letter is a hint: the code records no choice and the strict reader of an answer is unchanged. A question
  named only in prose, or by an older history with no words, keeps its old text

- Fixed: A live check measured on a test's earlier spelling is proved again after the test changed, instead of being left as "not proved". When a test became parametrized after its probe (`test_x`, then `test_x[p]`), or a sibling parameter's receipt reached the row through the obligation binding, the receipt was refused for the instance mismatch and the row read `missing`, so no re-probe was offered. A row whose only problem is that mismatch (same test function, same file, a known proof level, no other issue) and whose receipt is for other bytes now reads `stale`, and `probe_by_code.py` is replayed from the probe record the receipt itself names, under the row's own instance. The old receipt is never counted: the level comes from the new receipt of that probe. The same widening applies to the two doors that admit a critic's re-probe outside its dispatch's scope (`execution_request._admitted_outside`, `probe_debt._outside_scope_door`): a row with no probe of its own but a receipt of another spelling of the same test now passes them; the error stays toward "not admitted".
- S6 with a manual half proves the stale live checks again before the first manual block. Until now the re-probe ran only when S6 had no manual half, so after a fixture was edited by a later window the live checks of earlier tests stayed `not_verified:missing_sensitivity_proof` in every story that had manual cases. `Driver.s6_reprove_before_manual` runs after the automation runner is accepted, once per byte state (the mark `s6_reproved` holds, per instance, the test file's hash and the per-test content sha, which moves with a conftest or helper the test reaches, so an edited fixture is proved again), in the close context of S6, and closes nothing: the manual block closes S6 as before. A run the row recorded no identity for (`unknown`) lets the proofs go only in the life of S6 in which the automation runner was accepted (the mark `s6_manual_runner`, dropped after this step); in a later life it is one digest line, as on the path with no manual half. A test whose run is stale, a story with no confirmed stand and a failed probe are one digest line each. A test edited between this move and the end of the manual half has a stale receipt again and the ledger shows it, as it does today.
- The code file of an automator window names the shared fixtures it could invalidate. Under `## If you change a shared fixture` it lists, per existing fixture the window uses, the instances of earlier windows that hold a receipt and reach that fixture (up to 20 each, then `(+N more)`), as a heads-up and not a ban: the factory proves them again at S6. The section has a byte budget of 6000: each fixture gets an even share, names are cut from the end of its list and the cut is `(+N more)`, fixtures that cannot show one name are one last line, and the file stays under the 28 000 byte cap with the excerpts kept. What could not be read (a conftest that does not parse, a manifest that is not an object) is one line under "Not found, not checked". A shared fixture that is only reached through a conftest fixture it asks for, or an autouse one the window does not name in `uses`, is not listed.
- Not known: how many of the six unproved tests of TP2-12586 are the manual-half case and how many are the instance mismatch. The artifacts of that run were not read for this change; the live reading of one receipt's `instance_id` against its row is queued. The road without a driver (a story run by `story_step` alone) is a separate change: this one does not close the finding by itself.

- A person's decision to deliver with known gaps, said at gate B, now reaches the delivery guard. `controller.py --operation
  gate-decision --gate B` records it on the decision (`gates.B.deliver_with_risks.reason`, which had readers and no writer) and
  writes the journal line `deliver_with_risks` the guard reads, after the decision is recorded and never over an unrecorded one.
  The reason comes from `--risks-file <file>` (whole, by file) or from a line of the person's words that is the whole line
  `deliver with known gaps: <reason>` (the word is data, `risk_word` in `question-vocabulary.json`; a quoted line, a fenced line,
  a line with other words around it and a line of the replaced earlier answer are not read; two different reasons record nothing as
  a risk and the answer says so). A reason is never invented: a line with no reason, a blank file, `--risks-file` at gate A, and a
  risk next to `--mr do_not_open` or `not_offered` are refused with the way out. The answer carries `risks`
  (`recorded`, `journal`, and a `line` with the door when the journal line was not written), and the packets of both roads print
  the one form: `approve` on the first line, then `deliver with known gaps: <your reason>` on a line of its own. The guard's refusal
  of a delivery command over a recorded gate B no longer asks the person to say it at gate B again: it names the recorded reason,
  or says that gate B records no such decision, gives `log_append.py --event deliver_with_risks --task <T> --reason-file <file>`
  as the door (new `--reason-file`, read by the one words reader), and says that the guard judges a whole command before any of
  it runs. The journal line lands in the story's own project (the nearest `qa-factory/config.json` above the story), not in
  whichever project the shell sits in; with no such project the answer names the door as before. A blank or missing `--risks-file`
  and `--reason-file` is refused naming that flag, not `--words-file`.

- `inspect --media-url` refusal (`source_inventory.py`, `s1.md`): a merge or pull request link that is not an item of the source is no longer refused as "must identify exactly one external media item". The refusal now says the link is a development link and not a material; it names a collected receipt only when that receipt was read for the same request, names any other receipt by its status or its project, gives the path to read a GitLab merge request into, and says plainly that a pull request cannot be read by the factory; any other unknown address lists the source's media URLs (at most five) with the `collect` door; an unknown `source_id` lists the known ones (or names `collect` when there are none); `inspect --attachment-id` gets the same treatment (HF8-5)

- A filed bug keeps its case: the report joins a bug to its cases and requirements from the bug file and from the draft it was filed
  from (a requirement only from the draft's own requirement fields, never from its prose), and a filed bug that names no case is told so
  instead of "bug not filed". The report's appendix is now rendered by `report_facts.py --write` like any other code-owned block;
  `--check` says one line, "block `appendix` differs from a fresh render", and the S9 exit rebuilds it itself instead of sending the
  story back to the scribe after the merge request is out. When S9 refuses the report on a run with no driver, the refusal is recorded
  where `waiver.py --block "report check"` reads it, so a person's word is recorded against it instead of answering "unknown".

- The bug reporter now has a hand-off form (`s8-bug-reporter-to-scribe`): what it filed (draft, bug, case, requirements), what it did
  not file and why, and the quarantined tests; with no draft chosen it hands one `gate_b` row. A bug filed from a draft names its
  case and requirements in its frontmatter (or `cases: []` with a reason); older bugs are read as before. The report now says, per
  bug, where its file lies and whether the tracker has it (sent, not sent and why, proposed, or unknown) - derived by the code from the
  project's channel, the run's record, the person's words at gate B and the tracker books, never from the role. A draft the person did
  not choose at gate B says so, with their words.

- A bug the analyst reproduced is no longer reported as "nobody has reproduced it". A bug draft may carry `reproduction`
  (a rerun on fresh data, or the analyst's own script, each with a receipt file under `evidence/`); the code checks the
  receipt and shows the bug as `reproduced by the factory` - counted apart in the report, the traceability appendix, the
  gate B packet, the delivery fragment and the board, never as confirmed by a person, and changing no verdict. A receipt the
  code cannot read leaves the bug `unconfirmed`, says why in closed words, and raises a finding before gate B; a role's bare
  `reproduced_by_factory` and a misspelt `confirmation` read `unconfirmed`, and an unreadable bug file is counted as unreadable.
- The report derives a bug's severity from its `impact` when the bug file states none (was "severity not recorded"), and a
  requirement whose red is another case's defect says so, with the blocker's bug, instead of "no reason recorded; bug not filed".

- The address of a stand's UI is now found before the interview and recorded in the project. Onboarding discovery lists the names an
  env file holds an http(s) address under (`frontend_candidates`, names only, up to 5 with a count of the rest, none from an
  `.env.example`, the API's own address left out), the interview asks once which of them is the UI, and the answer is written as
  `environment.frontend.url_key`. A gate can record the same fact with `project_decisions.py stand-frontend --key <NAME> [--api-path P]
  --words-file F` (one stand) or `--stand <name> --url <address> --words-file F` (several stands, where the block key is not read):
  every check runs before anything is written, each refusal names its door, an address with a login is refused, the person's words
  are kept in the decision registry, and repeating the same record changes nothing. The enumeration of candidate names is one
  function (`env_probe.http_address_keys`) shared with the `frontend: not configured` hint, whose text is unchanged.
  `stand-frontend --key` looks the variable up in the env files the gate reads (`env_files`, else `env_file`); with no file named
  in the config it records the key and says `names not checked`.

- The handover form and every refusal of its values file now name the indexed way to write a row of a list, on the
  field of the form's own contract (`"scope[0].id": <value>`, the next row `"scope[1].id"`): the head line of a new
  form and of a rework form, the three refusals of a line or an object that is not `path: value`, the `no rows`
  refusal, and the pre-tool guard's refusal of a values or form write. A role that tried `scope.0.id` or a list of
  objects is told the form the writer takes instead of giving up under `blocked`. The skeleton no longer offers
  `execution[0].preconditions[0]`, a line the writer itself refuses, for a list of values inside a row, and leaves out
  the fields code fills. What a values text means to the parser, and what the writer accepts, did not change.

- **Fixed: the card for "no test to run the reporter step with" now says why (HF8-14).** One text served every cause ("I found no existing test under `tests`"), and it was untrue when test files were there and the choice was refused because two profiles share one folder, or when the gate's list of tests held tests that lie in another folder. The gate now tells the causes apart (a shared folder, a list with nothing under the profile's folder, no list and no file with a test name), says in a person's words whether the list could not be asked for, did not run, or ran and found none, prints only numbers and folders it read, and keeps the one door (`gate_rehearsal.reporter_probe_test`) with the price of going on, whatever the cause. The onboarding probe reads the same cause. A word recorded on the old text no longer matches: the question is asked again.

- The guard no longer lets the conductor send a message to a CLOSED author. An agent whose work is all accepted, on a stage
  whose `rework_mode` is `resume` (S5), with no rework of its role waiting for a binding, is closed work: the controller takes it
  back, a message does not. A resume to it is refused, on both hosts (a Codex receipt does not vouch for it either), and the
  refusal names the door: `story_step.py finish --needs-author` while the S5 code critic runs, otherwise `controller.py
  --operation rework`, whose card then goes to this agent. The author a rework restarted (its record running with the same agent
  id) is open again, and so is every case the guard cannot establish (a record without a status or a role, an unreadable stage
  table): an unknown never refuses. Other stages and every other refusal keep their text.

- An S5 critic that cannot judge a window because its author's code is defective now has a move while it still runs:
  `story_step.py finish --task <T> --dispatch-id <critic> --needs-author <cases> --reason "<words>" [--cause <repair cause>]`.
  It accepts nothing and spends none of the critic's rounds: the critic's record is checkpointed `incomplete`, the author is
  sent back over those cases (a resumed author is bound to its new dispatch), and the author's own `finish` names the critic's
  retry packet (`controller.py --operation recover`). Before anything is written the author's rework is rehearsed with the
  very check `dispatch` applies, so a refusal (the repair ceiling, an author not accepted, a closed story) leaves the critic
  running instead of stranded. Until now `rework`, `finish --not-complete` and `checkpoint` were all refused while the critic
  ran, and the conductor sent the closed author a message outside the controller. The refusal of a second dispatch now names
  the running dispatch and, for an S5 critic, this move; `finish` without `--digest` and without `--needs-author` is refused
  with the command form instead of an argument error.

- A role that already handed its report back, was resumed by a message, and answered in plain text is sent back once with the door: the
  exit gate says "Your last turn ended in text" and names the host's handback call (read from `references/host-report-forms.json`, not typed
  in code), so the conductor gets a return it can take. Only the first stop of a Claude role is judged; the host's own re-entry and the one-block
  fuse release it, an unreadable transcript is no refusal, and `story_step finish` and the driver never see this check.
- The conductor is woken about a role that has already returned. A new Stop hook (`conductor_stop.py`) asks the host's own record once when
  the conductor's session ends a turn; when a dispatch of that session, still `running` in the controller and bound by `story_step`, has every
  receipt returned (the transcript ends with the handback and its acknowledgement and the stop hooks let it go), the end of the turn is refused
  once with `story_step.py finish --task T --dispatch-id D --digest -` (or `--needs-author`). It stays silent for a role that is still working,
  for anything it cannot read, for another session's receipt and in the driver's mode, and never blocks twice for the same return.

- A person is shown words and screenshots, never the factory's own records. The gate B packet names the readable delivery summary
  (or says it is not written yet) instead of its JSON, and each bug by a readable text the code writes once per draft
  (`work/bug-text/`, outside the draft folder); the packet no longer names the draft folder. The test report no longer names
  text or JSON captures, the factory's log or its record files: a manual check says in words whether its screenshots were provided, and
  the runner's words stand when nothing was captured as a picture, and a re-judged verdict says it was read again from captures already taken.
- The delivery summary (the merge request description) says what a row's state means in words from `report-risk-words.json`
  (`delivery_state_words`); a state or a limit the data has no words for is said as "the factory cannot say", the code is never
  printed. `human-questions.md` and `human-text.json` (`technical_file_named`, checked on a report) forbid naming JSON, YAML,
  JSONL and text files, the ledger and the manifest to a person.

- A stand integration with two ways in (a cloud set and a server set of one service) is satisfied by any one complete set, and onboarding now writes those sets (HF8-11). Gate A already read `credential_alternatives` but nothing wrote it, so on run 14857 a project whose env file held the whole Server set of Jira was still asked for the Cloud keys. Phase 1 records `credential_alternatives` (and `read_at`, the places the code reads the keys) from `project_inventory.py --access --json` (`integration_proposals`) and judges the split itself: a set that is whole alone and other call sites are evidence, a name suffix is not, and in doubt no alternatives are written. `config_contract` checks the form of the new fields (the union of the alternatives is `keys`, `read_at` is `path:line` and never absolute). A row with no `required_by` is legal when it carries `read_at`. At gate A an integration whose `required_by` is only the project's own words (prose, or an id of another story), and that the project does not call `required`, is no longer one question per integration: it is ONE line of the "After your approval" block ("Stand access not set for ... The factory could not match these to this story's cases ...") with the whole fact in the rehearsal text. An id of this story, of one of its rows or of a project profile, an unreadable plan or case, and a `required` row all keep the question. A key a case names through `check.env` is no longer asked twice when it sits inside an alternative.

- A manual verdict now stands on the text the runner captured, and a verdict found wrong can be judged again without
  running the check again (run TP1-12586: TC-007 was recorded failed against the page text in its own capture, and
  the only way back was a full repeat with data that could not be seeded twice). `manual_evidence.py prepare` lists the
  case's Thens in `request.json` (`thens`); `build` takes `--then-quote "<n>=<words>"` per Then (a pass needs every Then,
  a fail the one it failed on, an inconclusive none; `--then-seen` for a Then only the picture shows, `--then-unreached`
  for a Then a failed check never got to). Code checks that each quote is in a text capture of the same attempt, at most
  300 characters; it never reads what the quote means. A request made before this rule asks for no quote. The new
  command `manual_evidence.py rejudge --of-attempt a<n> --reason "<why>"` writes a new record `a<n>-r<k>` from the
  captures of a written attempt (evidence, probes and steps copied as they were, `record.json` untouched, the record
  says the check was not run again) through the same validation as a built record; `--completion <path>` names the
  post_action capture that proves a completion the first verdict did not claim. `build --with-attempt a<n>` joins the
  open attempt of another stand profile (a ui check and an api read) to one record, each profile with its own probes
  and steps; the rule of one profile per attempt is unchanged. The runner's charter, `phases/s6.md`, the runner's card
  and `references/manual-evidence.md` say the new forms.

- A project that keeps its bugs in the repository (`external_writes.bugs: markdown`) is no longer warned about a tracker it never asked for: S0 records no `warnings[]` line for a capability whose `remedy.kind` is `not_a_defect`, and the first message skips `tracker_write` when it is not applicable. The probe text now states the value (`external_writes.bugs = <value or "not set">`) and no longer claims whose choice it is. Gate B still names where the bugs go.

- The report counts what the run checked by hand. A case the plan gives to the agent by hand (`manual-agent`) and that has a valid
  passed record now reads `pass` at the level `manual-agent` in the appendix and proves its requirement, whatever the plan's level
  column says; the plan's own reason ("not deterministic on the stand") no longer stands beside a check that was made. A case planned
  for a person (`manual-human`) reads `wait` instead of `not run`. A failed manual check reads `blocked`: not proven, and not
  "your turn to check".
- "Left with you" says every gap in one form: `- **<ref>** (<requirements>) — To check: <what>. Needed: <what is wanted of you>`. The
  findings still open after gate B, and the integrations the factory could not tie to a case (or the fact that this could not be
  established), are lines of that form. A line is found by its whole reference: `R-3` is not read inside `BR-3`.
- "Open questions" counts what "Left with you" asks beside the question register (`— 0 · 4 asked under "Left with you"`).
- "Where to look" lists each section of a file once.
- The marker of the case appendix ends the plan's regression section, so it no longer stands inside the report's regression block.
- A regression command that names a script of the package by the path of the developer's machine now names it as
  `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/<file>`; any other absolute path stays as written and is reported on stderr.
- The verdict splits the requirements "not proven" from those open only in the factory's own records: `N not proven (M of them open only
  in the factory's own records)`. The count `N` and the verdict word do not change. The ledger's reasons carry the ids they name (`refs`).

- Added: A manual runner's verdict that contradicts the text its own attempt captured is no longer left as a plain red. The failure analyst has a new triage verdict, `RUNNER_MISREAD_EVIDENCE`, for a manual check: its row carries `contradiction` (`then`, `runner_said`, `evidence` - a text capture of that attempt - and a `quote` that stands in it); one reader, `triage_contradiction_problems`, checks the form and where the quote stands and never whether it decides the Then, and the validator and the delivery check both refuse a row that fails it, so the red stands. S7 stays open and sends the check back to the qa-runner, which judges the same captures again (`manual_evidence.py rejudge`, nothing is captured again); the round is capped at `repair_cycles` per case and attempt, counted across the analyst's lives, and past the cap no question is asked: the red stands, the delivery is `no` and the owner is the factory. No bug is filed for it and no test is repaired. The state-exits table, the analyst's card and the S7 phase name the way out.

- S4 no longer needs the conductor to record the approved case scope: `case_versions.py --all` now records the pinned
  cases through the controller's `revise_plan` itself (the driver and the CLI share one request builder,
  `case_versions.scope_request`), so the case critic starts right after the pin. The answer gains `scope`
  (`recorded`, `unchanged`, `not_recorded`) and, when something needs saying, `scope_note`, `scope_behind`,
  `gate_a_stale` and `cases_changed`; the exit code is unchanged. A scope a person narrowed by hand is left as it is
  and named. The critic's start before any gate A decision now refuses with "the review scope does not hold yet" and
  the `--all` door instead of a gate A decision that never existed. `phases/s4.md` drops the separate scope step.

- The accounts of a stand now live in the project's config. Onboarding discovery lists the user/password name pairs an env file
  holds (`account_pairs`, names only, up to 8 with a count of the rest), the interview asks once which role each account is on
  the stand, and the answer is written as `environments[].credentials_by_role["<role>"] = "<USER_KEY> / <SECRET_KEY>"`. A gate can
  record the same fact with `project_decisions.py stand-account --stand <name> --role "<role>" --user-key U --secret-key S
  --words-file F [--replace]`: every check runs before anything is written, each refusal names its door, the person's words are
  kept in the decision registry, and repeating the same record changes nothing. `config_contract.py --check-environment` now
  checks that the names a role's note holds are in the env file.
- A fact recorded through `project_decisions.py resolve` (an account, and any other answered decision that writes a config
  pointer) is no longer taken back when the story that heard it ends: the decision receipt carries the time of the write and
  the config before it, and the end-of-story revert keeps that write and names it ("written by project decision").

- The audit reads the deferred-decisions table of a project's backlog through one reader (`project_decisions.deferred_table`): a variant
  heading ("Deferred Decisions (gates)") and a mixed-case column (`Asked`, `ASKED`) are read, where two audit walks of its own
  each guessed. A deferral marker is one pattern in any case: `[deferred: x]`, `[Deferred:x]` and `[DEFERRED: x]` are the same marker for the
  audit, and `project_decisions.py resolve` removes it in every spelling. New reds a project can see: (1) A13 reports a lower-case marker
  that has no open row (a paired one stays green); (2) `resolve` now refuses while a marker in ANY spelling is still live in a file the
  caller did not name, with the same refusal text ("name every marker file in this resolution") - it does not list the files, the caller
  names them; (3) the required-facts audit reads only `DD-n` rows, so a deferral written in a row with another id no longer counts and
  its topic is reported as having no deferral. `sizing.py` says whether a missing size input is absent,
  could not be read (the exception's name), or is not what it should be: a `config.json` that is absent, unreadable, a list or empty, and a
  `requirements-register.md` that exists and could not be read are four different lines, never "no register"; the weights stay the defaults.
  The `deferred` line of the risk-areas report says the row SHOULD be in `qa-factory/factory-backlog.md` (it did not read the backlog), and
  `sizing.compute` is split into private steps with the same output. The unused `read_strategy_p1_areas` is removed.

- Sizing reads the impact scale through `grammar.impact_scale`, the same reader the validators use (before, `sizing.py` kept its
  own copy and a project with no map weighed every requirement at 1.0). A project with a complete map gets the same weights as
  before. A project with no map, an empty one or a malformed entry now gets the package's own classes (a `data-loss` row 1.6, a
  `cosmetic` row 0.6) and a reasoning line that says so: the whole-map line ends "the package's default classes apply", and an
  entry that is not a `{priority, severity}` map, one that lacks either key, or a priority with no weight gets a note on every row it
  touches (before, a map without a severity and a priority with no weight were silent). A map that holds some classes and not
  others says so on a row whose package weight is not the P2 one, and an empty or null priority is named, not read as P2.
  `grammar` gains `impact_scale_problems`
  (which entries the scale dropped and why), `impact_scale_state` and `impact_scale_phrase` (the whole-map situation).

- The command guards no longer refuse a backslash that sits inside quotes before `|`, `;` or `&` (OH3-32). On run 12586 four commands of
  two S5 windows were refused as "a backslash before `|`" because a plain `grep -i "probe\|fingerprint"` held a regex alternation in
  quotes, and the refusal advised putting the text in quotes, which it already was. The shared ban (`hooklib.shell_opaque_found`) now
  asks the one command reader whether the backslash was read inside a quoted run in BOTH the bash and the PowerShell reading, and only
  then treats it as text; every hit is judged in turn, so a quoted one frees none behind it. A backslash before `(`, `)`, `'`, `"` or
  a line end, every other member of the ban, a backslash outside quotes, an unclosed quote, a backtick region, and any command that
  holds `<<` or a here-string opener stay refused. A refusal for a backslash that is already inside quotes now carries its own door
  (a character class in a regex, forward slashes in a Windows path, single quotes for a double quote). The read guard for a role without
  Bash (`host_adapter`) gets the same freedom with no edit: `rg "a\|b" f` is one plain read again.

- The stage guard no longer refuses a command for the words its heredoc or here-string only STORES (OH3-22). On run 12586 seven commands
  of two S5 windows were refused as a delivery because a plain `cat > answers.txt <<'EOF'` held `gh pr create` or `glab mr create` in the
  person's own words, or a `python story_run.py answer --words-file - <<'EOF'` body did. A body now comes out of the guard's reading only
  when the shell surely stores it: the operator's line is plain (no backslash continuation, backtick, pipe, `$'`, open quote), the
  operator is code, the body is closed, the receiver is a text receiver (`cat`, `tee`, an `echo`-like command, or a launch of a `.py`
  file), no pipe target of the command and no `>(` reads it as a command, and an unquoted delimiter's body expands nothing. Everything
  else stays executable and is refused as before: `python - <<'EOF'`, `bash <<EOF`, `ssh host <<EOF`, `cat <<'E' | sh`, a CRLF or
  unterminated heredoc, a here-string next to `iex` or `eval`. The same reading serves the commit, stash and typed-runner rules.
  The new table rows are `vcs.text_receivers`, `vcs.script_runners` and `vcs.script_plain_flags` in `adapter-forms.json`; a damaged
  table takes nothing out. A word with a substitution (`log(a):` in PowerShell) no longer fills a form slot its literal text cannot be
  part of, which ends the false refusal of `def log(a): foo(b), create_mr()`.

- Onboarding no longer asks the person about the keys the code reads and the env file lacks (OH3-8). Topic 2 of the interview keeps one question, the access scheme; the key groups come from the call sites (`integration_proposals`: all keys of a prefix, which the file holds, where the code reads them, and the folders of the call sites that are tests) and phase 1 records them as `integrations[]` rows without `owner`. A helper under a tests folder is no area. The `qa-story` texts about a missing integration say access to the service and what will not run, not keys and files: the variable names and the file are in the first move only (at most six names, then how many are left), the third move is the conductor, and "who gives the access" is printed only when the project recorded an owner. The environment note and `environments.md` name the new row fields.

- onboarding gate on the shape of `profiles[]` (`onboard_apply.py`, `profile_contract.py`, `references/profile-shape.json`): the
  proposal is checked by `validate_config` before anything is sealed, recorded or written, and a NEW problem in
  `profiles`, `implementation_repos` or `managed_dependencies` (a profile whose `commands` is a list was written to
  `config.json` in silence and every reader of `commands` then fell over) refuses with every line, the expected shape, the
  sample file and the door (`profiles: []` with the deferral recorded at phase 4); a problem the project's configuration
  already holds over the same row is shown in the summary and left, so a reinstall is never locked; an empty `profiles`
  and the profiles a proposal drops are said in the summary; `validate_config` and `validate_profile` no longer raise on a
  value of a hostile type (a list where a word was expected, a number where an array was); the plan carries a new key,
  `profile_problems` (OH3-26)

- one reader of `profiles[].commands` (`profile_contract.py`: `profile_commands`, `profile_command`, `command_argv`, `one_test_argv`): a
  `commands` that is a list, a string or a number, a command that is not an object and an `argv` that is a string or holds a
  non-word are NAMED (with `references/profile-shape.json`) and never read as "no command" or letter by letter. `readiness.py`
  no longer ends in an AttributeError on a profile whose `commands` is a list: `execution_profile` and `profiles[...]` give the
  cause, and a healthy profile is not hidden by a broken one nor the other way round; `run_suite.py --mine` refuses a profile in a
  foreign shape with the problem (a good earlier typed run is still copied); `command_proposal` and the onboarding probe no longer
  write over a list of commands; the gate rehearsal, the dependency check, the manual capture, the probe-by-code checks, the
  report adapter, the environment record and the project environment ask the same reader instead of parsing the shape their own
  way (OH3-27); the launch check answers `not_checked` with the reader's problem on a foreign shape of `commands`, and a
  `one_test` whose words are all blank counts as no command

- Onboarding now tells the shape of a test profile before the work, not only at the seal: phases 3 and 4 name `references/profile-shape.json` (`commands` is an object keyed by command name, never a list) and say that a helper building `proposal.json` must be handed that file. The `profiles_note` of a new `config.json` says the same (`commands` keyed by command name, `selectors`), and an older project's note is refreshed by the migration. Phase 4 no longer promises a "manual or preparatory profile": a missing framework is `profiles: []` with its deferral.

- The onboarding no longer closes its notes over a config the first reader cannot use. `onboarding_notes.py close` now runs
  `readiness.py` (without writing, and without touching the tracker) and reads the one-test command of every profile of the
  live `qa-factory/config.json` before it moves the run to `done/`. It refuses when `readiness.py` could not finish, when a
  profile has no command that runs one test (a profile with only `run` counts) or sets an `env` that S5 would refuse (not an
  object, a name that is not a plain variable name, a value other than `{report_path}`), when `profiles` is empty, `null` or
  not a list, or when the config is missing or not a JSON object. Each refusal line carries its own door, printed as a
  command that runs as written (values quoted for the shell): repair the profile and close
  again, or record the gap in `factory-backlog.md` (`project_decisions.py add` on that profile's own `field_refs` after a
  person was asked, `add-finding` with `launch-<profile-id>`, `no-test-framework` or `first-reader-crash` when nobody was).
  Only an open record about the same subject lifts a problem. A close that is repeated, or that ends a run already marked
  done, is not checked again. Phase 4 says so in step 9 and on the "no test framework" short path.

- A test profile the onboarding writes no longer reads `unsupported` because of an unfilled capability matrix. The sample
  profile (`references/profile-shape.json`) now names the capability `web`, which the template's `supported_capabilities`
  knows (it named `e2e-ui`, a test level, so the sample itself read as unsupported), and shows the top-level
  `adapter_capabilities` key beside it. The onboarding phase 4 tells the role to write, for each adapter, the capabilities
  that profile's discovered tests really exercise, to name them in the summary, to ask the person when it cannot show one
  (`it can / it cannot / not sure`; `not sure` leaves it out and the profile reads `unknown`), and never to infer one from
  the framework's name. The summary lists every profile whose tool nothing in the configuration says can do what the
  profile needs ("The test profile `web-tests` will read as not ready: ..."), without refusing. The readiness check no
  longer raises on a configuration of a foreign shape (a capability list that is not a list or holds a non-word, an
  `adapter_capabilities` that is not an object, an adapter id or an execution profile id that is a list): it names the gap
  as `unknown`.

- The onboarding proposal now gets the settings it lacks. A configuration the role wrote without a setting of the current
  version (for example the secret-file patterns the guards read) was installed as written, so the setting stayed absent
  until a later migration; the install now adds every missing setting with the value a fresh install writes, before the
  proposal is sealed, so the summary lists them ("N setting(s) this version added") and the person's "yes" covers exactly
  what is written. A setting that is a fact about the project itself (the application and test roots, the protected paths,
  the code repositories, the test commands, the stands, the adapters, the pre-commit commands, the definition of done) is
  never invented: the summary names those it did not fill in, and the readiness report names them as before. A value the
  project already holds (including an empty one or `null`) is never changed, and a proposal that changes one test command
  is not filled. `config-keys.json` carries the flag as `project_fact`.

- The evidence of a story no longer goes into the delivery commit. The manual-evidence copies a story exports (`evidence/`
  under the story folder: masked screenshots named by hash, the index, the runtime provenance) are generated files, like the
  raw runs under `work/evidence/` that were already ignored: the project's `.gitignore` block now names them too
  (`qa-factory/artifacts/*/evidence/`, derived from `references/install-paths.json`), the delivery manifest lists none of
  them (it still checks the index and the copies, so a corrupted manual record does not turn green, and its refusals now name
  the command that rebuilds), and a reinstall keeps the files on the tester's machine, never retiring them.
  A project that is not onboarded again gets the new block from the doctor's check (`project_gitignore.py --write`), and a
  delivery manifest built earlier (it listed the copies) is rebuilt by `delivery_manifest.py --task-root <story> --output
  <story>/state/delivery-manifest.json` (the refusal says so). Files an older install already committed (evidence copies,
  fragments, `impl-diff`) are listed in the onboarding summary as "Generated files your repository still tracks", each with
  its `git rm --cached` line, which the role runs after the person's yes; nothing is deleted from disk.

- the manual capture's sign-in reads the env files the gate reads (`manual_capture.read_login`, `_read_pair`): `environment.env_files` when it lists any, else `environment.env_file`, through `gate_preflight.configured_env_files`; a project that lists only `.env.local` no longer gets a "does not exist" for a login the gate called set. Both keys of a pair come from the files or the sign-in is refused: the process environment never replaces a file value and a pair is never built from the process environment (several files are layered, as in the gate); a folder in place of a file is `unreadable`; a later file wins over an earlier one; the refusals name every file
- the gate's card for a stand account lists every file it looked in and marks one the disk lacks with "(not found)" (`Rehearsal._looked_in`), instead of naming the first file that exists
- the brief of a manual runner block adds a line for a case whose `stand_account` role the stand holds no pair for: the role is told not to sign in as another account in its place and to say so or ask for the pair (`brief_pack._unpaired_actor_lines`); `qa-automator` names a test that uses another account than its case in the digest; S4's door for an account already recorded with another pair names `--replace`

- `config.json` key `requirements_sources` now has a producer and a reader (OH3-39). Onboarding phase 1 finds the places a project keeps
  requirements (the tracker, wiki links, `docs/`, ADR and spec folders of the code repositories), phase 3 shows them in one line
  (`found requirement sources: ... - correct?`, a question only when none were found) and phase 4 writes them; a project that
  already has a configuration gets the rows added in place and no row is removed without the person's words. The scout's brief
  at S1 lists each source with the way to read it, chosen by the new table `references/requirement-source-kinds.json` (kinds,
  statuses and routes are data: `adapter`, `grep`, `role`; a kind outside the table goes to the role) and not by a list in code:
  a tracker source in a story with no key there is "not queried", never "unreachable", an unavailable one is a gap by default,
  a credential-like locator is never printed, at most 20 sources and 200 characters of a locator are shown, and no recorded
  source is one line that says so. What the scout reads there it records with `ticket_adapter.py record-source`, so it reaches
  the context bundle from the inventory. The config check reads kinds and statuses from the table (a damaged table is an error
  naming the file) and holds `auth_type`, `secret_ref` and `username_ref` to variable names. A config without the key reads as
  `[]` as before.

- Changed: the context `qa-automator` is injected is smaller again (about 1,000 B), with no rule dropped and no cap raised. The controller-internal parts of `references/execution-lifecycle.md` (squash/merge-result provenance, scheduler and lease internals) stay in the source for the conductor but are marked out of the automator's slice; the S6 branch-accounting sentence is stated once in the contract and pointed at from the charter. Audit A22 headroom for the role is back above 3,000 B.

- The pre-tool guard no longer crashes when it scans a heredoc body for a write to the project's config: the scan named a regular
  expression (`_HEREDOC_RE`) that the one body scan in `hooklib` had renamed (`HEREDOC_RE`), so a command with a heredoc raised a
  `NameError` inside the config-write check. The guard now uses the hooklib name. Two small readers also went through the package's
  one readers: the manual-evidence JSON reader is `hooklib.read_json` (a file with a byte-order mark is read, as everywhere else),
  and the refusal that names the finish command for a critic's dispatch takes the story name from `Controller._ticket`.

- The requirements tester's command card now names `branch_accounting.py` (the sentence-by-sentence unit list and the attachment list its charter
  sends it to), so the role gets the script path and form from the card instead of an unexpanded plugin-root variable. The gate registry
  also records the site that reads a container-check verdict (`named_container_said`) under the stand-identity gate, so the audit of gate
  verdict comparisons is clean again.

- Fixed: on Windows, a native (Codex) context packet was silently lost when the project root was 56 characters or longer, because the packet name (two full 64-hex digests) plus its temp suffix reached the 260-character path limit. The packet name now uses 32 hex of each digest, so a project root of up to 119 characters writes. A packet written under the old long name is still found by its session prefix and is only ever delivered to its own session.

- Fixed: `story_step.py finish` of a repair or rework round of a stage that is already accepted is judged now (`branch_accounting.py`). The gate used to read the stage from `pipeline.json` alone, which still says `done` on such a round, so every repair round's finish was refused as unreadable and judged nothing. When the pipeline names no running stage, the gate takes the ONE stage that has a live dispatch in `state/controller.json` (`running`, or `returned_unaccepted` - a stop with no `story_step bind` receipt). With two stages live, no state or an unreadable one, it still says it cannot tell the stage (exit 3) and never judges one stage's finish with another stage's check. A call that names no story is unchanged.
- Changed: the rework commands the factory prints for a person or a role end with `--brief` like the rest: the gate B owed-rework door (`controller.py`), the closed-story rework door of a critic that needs its author (`story_step.py`) and the plan-review rework door in `phases/s5.md`. Without the flag the whole result of a rework (over 1500 bytes) filled the conductor's context; with it the answer is a summary ending in `full result: <path>` and the whole result is in that file. A code that parses a door's answer reads that file when the answer is a summary.

- Changed: the context three roles are injected is smaller, with no rule dropped and no cap raised. `references/artifact-contract-run.md` is now sliced by section: the runner gets only `run-report.json`, the doc scribe everything but `bug-drafts/*.json`, the failure analyst all four (and the FLAKY repair rule, moved to it from the code critic's `code-review-rubric.md`, where only the analyst's verdict used it). `code-review-rubric.md` states the "already checked by code" lists once and points at the charter for the rest. The injection map names the three new slices; audits A22 (injection weight, 3,000 B headroom) and A25 (dispatch budget) are green again.

- Attachment download (`source_inventory.py`, `references/jira-fields.json` `attachment_policy`): a file Jira sends with no media type
  (`null`, a `plan.md` or a screenshot) is judged as `empty_mime_as` (`application/octet-stream`) instead of being left out as an unknown
  type. The never-list of suffixes is still checked first, so a null-typed `.exe`, `.sh` or `.zip` is not downloaded, an unknown suffix
  is downloaded under the document limit, and a project policy that names no `empty_mime_as` keeps the old safe answer. A PDF (by media
  type or by name) is now stored as `blobs/<digest>.pdf` (`blob_suffixes`) so the `Read` tool opens it as a document; every other
  file keeps `blobs/<digest>`. A story already collected keeps its old receipts and paths as they are.

- Branch accounting at the S2 exit (`branch_accounting.py`, `references/branch-accounting.json`, G2-11): the register now carries
  `## Branches` (one row per qualifier, partition, variant or refusal of a requirement) and `## Source obligations` (a home for
  every sentence of the story's own text and of the linked tickets the person's review kept), and the S2 exit refuses a unit with
  no home, a branch with no row, `Branches: none` with no reason. Units are cut by structure only; the role decides what is an
  obligation. `--units` / `--unhomed --task <TICKET>` list them, 200 to a page. A register written before the cutoff date (2026-10-30, `cutoff` in
  `references/branch-accounting.json`) with
  no such section reads as legacy and is not refused; an unknown input (no snapshot, no inventory, a ticket that was not read)
  is named in a note and never read as reconciled. A kept ticket is in scope: `not_obligation` judges a sentence, never a
  ticket, and a ticket whose units all oblige nothing is named to the person at gate A with its reason. Two never-empty rows (NE30, NE31) and the gate row `branch_accounting`.
- Attachments at the S2 exit (`branch_accounting.py --attachments --task <TICKET>`, `## Attachments` in the register, NE32): the tester opens each
  file of the story and of the kept linked tickets after the contradiction matrix (the printed call is the one for the file's form) and
  writes one row per file: `agrees`, `contradicts` (a requirement, a matrix cell in an `attachments` column, the id of the `open_questions`
  record that carries the file and the requirement as two readings, `from: attachment:<name>`, and a `## Reading forks` row),
  `not_an_expectation` or `not_opened` (with a reason). The exit refuses a file with no row; code never opens a byte of a file and
  never judges it. A file too large to download, a ticket with no file and a register that predates the branch accounting owe
  no row. `## Images` is the old name of the section, and a register that still has it gets a note. `attachment` is now a reading origin.
- Branch accounting at the S3 and S4 exits (`branch_accounting.py`, TQ1-17): the plan homes every register branch (`BN-n`) and every branch read in an existing test (`candidate_branches`, `BN-T<n>`) in a row's `branches` or in `branch_homes` with a reason (a `skip` or `unverifiable` row excludes the branches it names by its own reason); every `existing_test_candidates` entry of the bundle is walked (`candidates_walked`); a `manual-agent` or `manual-human` row carries `rung_basis` (`rung_basis` is also a patch key of `if_answered`). A case carries its branches on one `branches` line (`id`, `then`, `partition`; the Then and the partition are read by the contract's own readers), and the case critic's exit refuses a branch of a plan row that no case carries and no `## Branch homes` row of the newest findings round homes (`TC-n` or `excluded` with a reason). A case outside the critic's scope is a note; an unknown scope is the whole plan. A register that predates the accounting is asked for none of it. The code-review rubric and `test-code-patterns.md` say that an "as before" oracle needs a base distinguishable from a refusal (not a 4xx).
- Branch accounting at the S5 exit and the verdict (TQ1-20): `branch_accounting.py` is also the qa-automator exit gate (each branch a case carries, by Then and partition, is covered in the manifest or held in a remainder or an `unresolved` row), and `check_delivery.assess` reads `branch_accounting.delivery_records`: a branch nobody proved, a part of the ticket text with no home, an attachment whose contradiction nobody settled, a file nobody looked at (the tester did not open it and plan gate A did not show it, or the record of what gate A showed is missing or unreadable) are debts (`after_checks`), a reading that fails is `branches_unreadable` (`no`). A partition is covered only through the test the Then's binding names (the one that declares it, or declares none); a row of `unresolved` that names the binding's instance holds the pair too. A branch homed on a reused case is always a debt, and its words say that which Then proves it is not recorded. The report gains two blocks, `### Branches left with you` (a branch, a part of the ticket or a file left with the person, one line each in the form of the other left-with-you lines) and `## Branches not proven` (only the branches the person's own recorded answer left out).
- The big-read guard and large `.pdf` files (S6, V2): a read of a `.pdf` over the size limit is bounded only by `pages` (a range no wider than `read.max_pdf_pages` in the project config, default 20); `limit` and `offset` on a large `.pdf` are now refused, with a door that names `pages 1-<N>`, because the tool bounds a PDF by pages and not by lines. Off `.pdf`, `pages` is ignored by the tool and `limit` still bounds the read as before. The listing prints the call through the same reader, so what the gate lists is exactly what the guard lets through.

- Attachments at gate A (`gate_brief.py`, `branch_accounting.attachments_view`): the plan gate now says that the text of the story and
  of the tickets kept for it was turned into requirements sentence by sentence and their attachments were not, lists the attachments
  by ticket (each as opened, or not opened with a plain cause: too large to download, this kind of file is not downloaded, could not be
  read, not opened yet), and asks once whether any of them holds a requirement to add. The answer is the gate's approval word (nothing
  to add) or the person's own words, which the conductor turns into a rework of the requirements stage. A kept ticket from whose
  text no requirement was taken is named in its own block with its reason. An attachment list that cannot be read is said as `not known`, never as none; a
  gate shown again says which attachments are new since the last time (`state["shown_attachments"]["A"]`). The words and the limit
  (15 names) are data: `attachment_words` and `attachments_shown` in `references/branch-accounting.json`,
  `attachment_question_words` in `references/question-vocabulary.json`. One reader of the inventory's list now serves the units
  and the attachments (`inventory_sources`, `scope_class`).

- Attachments shown at gate A on the skill path (`gate_brief.py`): a conductor session that quotes `gate_brief.py --gate A` now leaves
  the same record of the attachments the packet named (`state["shown_attachments"]`: `A` the whole list, `A_named` the names the packet
  printed) that the driver keeps, through one function (`keep_shown_attachments`). The record counts as "shown" only once the person has
  decided gate A, and only for the files the packet named (a 16th file behind `(+1 more)` stays a debt, and so does every file when
  the packet said `not known`). A later print after the decision changes nothing, and a print before it rewrites the record, so a second print before the decision does not repeat the `new since you last saw this list` line (known limit, queued); a story folder that does not exist is never created
  by a typo in `--task`. A ticket whose list of attachments is not known, with gate A not decided, is one `attachments-unseen` debt
  naming it (a decided gate A that said `not known` is no debt). The report names what the packet named, never the whole list.

- Screenshots of the manual checks are the tester's to confirm the manual cases; they never enter the repository, the report or the
  merge request. Every delivered text now says only whether they were provided, in one set of words: each case line of "Checked by
  hand", each exploratory finding that has a picture, and each manual line of the checks ledger end with `screenshots: provided`,
  `screenshots: not provided (none were taken for this check)` (an API check has none by design) or `screenshots: not provided (no
  copy on this machine)` (a refused export, a partial copy, a clean checkout), with no link and no path; the verdict is never changed
  by it. A picture counts as taken by the file it names, so one whose record is damaged is never reported as "none were taken", and
  every record of a case is read, not only the first.
- The paths go to the person at gate B: the gate B packet, on the driver road and on the skill road, has its own section
  `Screenshots of the manual checks` with the absolute path of each copy per case (and per exploratory finding), whole and never
  cut. The report says `provided` only for a picture that section lists; with no picture the section is absent. The paths are
  never written into a delivered file or the ledger; `report_facts.py --task <TICKET> --screenshots` prints the same list again
  on request. The traceability table's basis for a manual pass is the runner's words, not a picture path.

- shared rules (`references/common-rules.md`): the shared layer again says a role never re-reads its own draft, in 30 B, restoring the rule the 0.10.8 A25 cut dropped; no cap or pin raised

- `delivery_summary.py`, `proof_level.py`, `verification-levels.json`, `stage_done.py`, `story_run.py`, the doc scribe charter (RD1-20): the numbers of the report agree. A RED test with no proof level is counted under its own words (`red_words`: "probe not applicable: red") instead of "not probed", so 17 green and one red read "not probed: 17" and the red apart; a red test with a reached level stays on its level. `stage_S8` writes the delivery summary again right after the report rebuild (one printed line if that fails; S9 writes it once more), and the S9 exit rewrites the summary once when its recorded "Left with you" differs from the report's section (`delivery_summary.left_with_you_stale`; whitespace is not a difference; no summary or an unreadable one is silent or one `report:` line), so the MR description never carries an older list than the report. The report check itself does not compare the two. The scribe charter says a number in its prose is taken from a code-owned block and never counted by the scribe.

- `check_delivery.py`, `coverage_contract.py`, `ledger.py`, `delivery_summary.py`, `report_facts.py`, `delivery-reason-owners.json`, `delivery-verdict-kinds.json` (RD1-21): the reasons of the family `coverage` are split by typed fields instead of all being the product's. An obligation with a red run or an open oracle (the new field `oracle_open` of the obligation record, `execution_state: failed`) reads `coverage red: ...` and stays the product's; evidence the factory's tools or coverage left missing on a green or not-run obligation with a closed oracle reads `coverage: ...` and is the factory's. A field that is absent reads red. The kind `coverage_gap` now carries the factory as its owner; the verdict is unchanged (`no`). The sentence "Nothing here says the product is not ready" is no longer printed over such an unproven behaviour, in the ledger, the delivery check and the delivery summary: the factory heading opens with "N behaviour(s) no test proves because of the factory's tools or coverage; they stay unproven", and the report's verdict block says it apart from the factory's bookkeeping. The count of requirements "open only in the factory's own records" does not grow with the change of owner. A delivery reason whose owner no rule established stays with the product, now says `owner not established:` in the summary and the verdict block, and its record carries `owner_established: false`.

- A test the code critic rejected is no longer a `pass` in the report's appendix because its run was green: the row reads `blocked` ('rejected by the code critic; the green run does not count until the critic reviews the changed test') until a later review approves it. The ledger agrees: a fixed flaky test whose verdict is `rejected` reads `review_rejected`, not `passed_green`. A rejected row with no remark points to the critic's findings file when one names its case as a whole word ('the critic's remarks are in work/test-code/critic-findings.md'); otherwise it still says the remarks were not recorded.

- The S7 repair of a test the critic had rejected now ends in a critic review of that one test (reason `S7 repair review: <test>`). The test is `repaired` only when the critic approves. A critic that sends it back gets one more author round within the repair cap, and at the cap the person gets the usual repair-limit question. A test the critic had not rejected is repaired as before, with no review.

- Changed: Regression names only tests that already exist. The S3 exit refuses an item whose file is not on the project's main branch (read locally from `origin/HEAD`, the declared default branch, `origin/main` or `origin/master`, with `git ls-tree`; no fetch, no network) - a test written in the run is no regression (14857).
