When the main branch cannot be named the check stays silent and the report says so instead of printing the paths as checked. The S1 and S3 briefs carry one line saying the diff's test files already on the main branch are existing coverage, and the report's regression block lists the tests of this story on their own line and notes a path that was not checked or a story test named as regression. The regression list itself is carried unchanged.

- Changed: The plan's `## Recommended regression` has one form that works on another machine: one `Command:` line per test runner, written as the project runs its own tests, every file named once, and one item per test path. The strategist no longer writes `run_suite.py` commands (they need the plugin, which the reader of the report does not have). The S3 exit checks the section with the new `regression_scope.py`: a path named twice (or under another item's folder), an item that is in no `Command:` line or in two, two equal `Command:` lines, a command that runs the factory's own scripts, an absolute path, and a section that is absent or blank are each refused with what is wrong, what is expected and the person's-word door (`waiver.py`); the check reads the section through the same reader as the report, never parses the runner's syntax, and a check that cannot run is a warning, not a refusal.

- Changed: Every regression item names what the person's stand needs to run it (`stand: <what it needs | no stand requirements>`, for example a scheduler that starts the data sources' cron), so the list can be run on another stand. An item with no `stand:` is refused at the S3 exit. The empty outcome is declared in words: `No regression: <reason>` alone (with a reason, and not beside a list); silence is no longer an answer. The area's `regression` field of `work/grounding.yaml` now holds the tests or set that defend it, or `gap:<reason>`, never a command.

- The stage guard and the adapter-forms reader now share one reader of a command's head (the first word that is no `NAME=value`
  assignment) and one reader of the program that head names. A dotted, dashed or digit-leading word (`a.b=1`, `-x=1`, `1x=1`) is no
  assignment in the shell, so it is the head: `a.b=1 cat <<E` and `a.b=1 python x.py` no longer read as a text receiver or a script run
  (their bodies and quoted arguments are read as commands, as before the wide reading). A head word whose first path component holds
  `=` (`a.b=/x/python`, `-x=/bin/cat`) names no program, so a launcher, receiver or mention command is never read from its basename;
  `./a=b/python` stays a program. The commit-shape reader joins the same head reader. The list-heads reader goes through the same
  table-words function as its siblings.

- Fixed: Gate A no longer carries as "not verified" what the story has since proved. A real role dispatch whose transcript opens with the task packet (`# Resolved task packet` among the first 20 rows, before the child's first move) now leaves a small receipt (`qa-factory/state/host-receipts/context-delivery-<session>.json`, written at the child's stop by `host_probe.check_role_context`; a diagnostic probe child leaves none), so `host_hooks` is `ok` in `readiness.py` when the live allow/deny guard is verified and such a dispatch was seen, with no manual `qa_factory_context_probe` dispatch. This never opens the Codex spawn gate: `story_ready`, `injection` and `live_parity` are unchanged, and on Codex the receipt does not make `host_hooks` `ok` and the diagnostic door stays. `gate_brief.py` drops an S0 `vcs_api:` or `host_hooks:` warning line (machine prefix only) when its capability was proved after that story's S0 finished (`pipeline.stages.S0.finished`); evidence older than S0, a missing or offset-less time, an unreadable reader or an unexpected folder layout leave every line in place, and the lines it dropped are listed under `proved_warnings` in `gate_brief.py --json`. `host_capabilities.py` also skips a receipt file that is JSON but not an object instead of raising.

- Fixed: A merge request read through the provider's API now counts as proof that `vcs_api` works. `vcs_evidence.py` keeps one small receipt per host (`qa-factory/state/host-receipts/vcs-api-<host>.json`: `ok` after a read, `denied` after the host itself refused, no token and no MR content), and `readiness.py` reports `vcs_api: ok` from a fresh receipt (7 days, the same `adapters.vcs` route, `glab` on PATH) instead of "not verified" when it ran without `--probe-vcs`. An unknown never becomes `ok`: a live probe that asked and got no answer keeps its remedy, a live refusal outranks an older read and is written as a `denied` receipt, a refusal on any host forbids `ok` without a live answer, and a read on another host is named in the note, not used to hide a refusal.

- Fixed: When the GitLab host refuses the API probe with 401 or 403, the doctor's `vcs_api` row now says whose token it is and what is wrong with it, instead of one generic list of steps. `vcs_evidence.py` asks `glab auth status` once, only after a refusal the host itself gave (a healthy probe, a network failure, a 404 or a missing `glab` never start it), and tells five cases apart: a token variable (`GITLAB_TOKEN`, `GITLAB_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `OAUTH_TOKEN`) that `glab` prefers to a saved token, a token saved for another host only, a token for this host that the host rejected, no token at all, and a 403 where the token was accepted but lacks rights. Each case names the host, the scopes a new token needs and the one door that works (for the variable: take it out of the environment `glab` runs in, then `glab auth login`). The wording of `glab`'s output lives in `references/glab-auth.json`; an output that is not understood keeps the old steps, and no token value is ever read, printed or stored. The note of a confirmed refusal now says it in words ("the host answered 401: the call was not authenticated") instead of the internal code.

- Fixed: Before a project is onboarded, `host_probe.py` no longer creates `qa-factory/` (a probe store and its lock) in the root of the repository the project sits in, and the doctor no longer reports "hooks inactive" because of it. With no `qa-factory/config.json` in the folder or above it, `--prepare` and `--check` now refuse with exit 3 and write nothing, with or without `--root`: the refusal says the project is not onboarded yet, that the host hooks are unknown (owner: factory) rather than broken, and that the next step is `/qa-factory:qa-onboarding`. When a pre-tool hook of the host recorded a `host_probe.py` call in the same folder moments ago, the refusal says so. `--hook`, a project with the marker (from any subfolder) and the refusal for a `--root` that is not a project behave as before; the doctor's skill and its evals name the new exit.

- Fixed: The refusal of the context-diagnostic dispatch (`qa_factory_context_probe`) now names the condition that failed instead of only the door. After the unchanged first sentence it lists every unmet condition of the host probe in the order they were recorded (the same ` Unmet: id (reason); ...` text `host_probe.py --check` prints), and says plainly when the probe on record is a verified one that belongs to another host session ("run the pair in this session"), when the dispatch carries no session id (owner: factory), when the probe could not be read, or when the reason is not established. Session ids are never printed, the text collapses white space and is cut at 2000 characters (the whole list stays under `missing` in `host_probe.py --check`), and it never changes the decision or raises. The `host_hooks` note of `host_capabilities.py` for an incomplete probe ends with the same unmet list and no longer points at "the transcript call format", which a role must not read; the `--require host_hooks` WARN line carries it as one line. `host_probe.unmet_text` is the one builder of that text (it was the private `_unmet_text`).

- Fixed: The live allow/deny probe no longer loses a fact when two hooks of one host message run at the same time: every write of `qa-factory/state/host-probe.json` (`--prepare`, the guard and execution receipts, the context-probe challenge, its binding and its verdict) and of a guard-parse receipt now happens under a short writer lock, after the slow work (the package walk, the child transcript) and with the stored nonce checked again, so a store that `--prepare` replaced meanwhile takes no fact of the old pair. A lock that stays busy for 5 seconds costs the fact, never the guard's decision (DENY still exits 2); `--prepare` then says "the probe store is busy, run --prepare again" instead of a traceback.
- A guard that raises is recorded by the telemetry wrapper as exit 1 (the exception still leaves unchanged), so `--check` names `allow_guard_not_allowed` instead of an absent receipt; an unreadable or foreign-shaped probe store is "nothing observed" on the guard's path, never an exit-1 crash.
- `host_probe.py --check` names a new unmet condition, `other_session_hooks`, when the pair left no fact of its own but the hooks of another session ran after `--prepare`: run `--prepare` and the pair again in one session. The status and the other conditions are unchanged.

- `run_suite.py --mine` no longer asks pytest for the same list of test ids twice. The list a real collect gave is kept on
  the request (`collect_memo`: a key and the ids), and the next `--mine` of the same story plays it back through the same
  spelling step when the key has not moved - so the ordinary window, "edit the body of the test, run it", saves the
  collect (60-100 s of a call). The memory is used only when the key proves that a collect would answer the same; anything
  the key cannot read gives no key, and the collect runs as before (a run that is not sped up is acceptable, a parameter
  that silently does not run is not). The key covers: the argv, the run directory, the `PYTEST_*` environment, the skeleton
  of every test file (the syntax tree with the body of each `test*` function emptied unless it is a fixture or is
  referenced: decorators, signatures, helpers and the module level count), the bytes of the conftest chain, of the pytest
  configuration and dependency files, of the project modules the tests import (with the `__init__.py` of every package on
  the way and of the test directories), and the stand's identity. No key, so a real collect: a new test, a changed
  `parametrize`, any conftest edit, a red probe, a stand that was not observed (or a run budget that could not be read), a
  file that does not parse, values or `ids=` that are not a literal (a call, a name, a comprehension, `pytest.param`), a
  fixture whose `params=` is not a literal, `parametrize` under another name, `pytest_plugins`, a collection hook
  (`pytest_generate_tests`, `pytest_collection_modifyitems`, ...), `sys.path` changes and dynamic imports in the closure,
  `pythonpath` in the configuration, and `-p`, `-c`, `--config-file`, `--pyargs` in the argv. `--again`, `--cwd` and
  `--sandbox-root` never read the memory, but the collect they make is written, so the next plain call plays back the
  newest list, never an older one. A remembered list that turns out stale (pytest answers `not found`, or the run never
  ran a test) is not played back again: the next launch collects and writes a new one. A story with no earlier job, or an
  old record with no `collect_memo`, behaves as before. Named gaps: a project that sets `pythonpath` or has a collection
  hook never gets the memory; a test module that reads a file or the environment (other than `PYTEST_*`) outside `params=`
  and `ids=` to decide which tests it defines, a plugin installed with no edit of a dependency file, and a plugin named
  by an installed entry point are not seen by the key - `--again` collects afresh. `collect_memo` is not part of the
  request digest, so a repeat of the same request stays a repeat.

- `run_suite.py` now measures where the time of one call goes. The run summary carries `phases_s` with `build_s`,
  `stand_probe_s`, `collect_s`, `before_launch_s`, `pytest_s` and `after_s` (seconds, one decimal; `build_s` is the build
  without its collect and probe, so the six add up); a phase that did not happen is `null`, never `0` (a `--request` call
  builds nothing: its build phases are `null`). `after_s` ends where the summary is written: the dashboard refreshes and
  the run block that follow are not in it. One `PHASES: ...` line goes to stderr (also when a `--mine` call is answered
  `reused`/`already_run` or refused, without `pytest_s`); stdout stays one JSON document. Measuring never stops a run.
  Nothing reads the field yet: it is terminal until the retro reads it (SC2-37); old summaries have no field and are
  not rewritten.

- Changed: `manifest_from_tests.py` finds the module that holds a `parametrize` list by itself: it follows the test file's own `from <module> import <name>` (relative or absolute, `as` names, up to 3 re-export hops) to a module inside the project, reads that module for its names only (its tests and markers are not scanned) and lists it in `generated_from`. `--file <module>` stays for what the import does not lead to (third-party or dynamic imports, `import *`, `d.LIST`); two modules the import can mean, a longer chain, a circle and a module that does not parse are refused with that door.
- All marker problems of the given files are one refusal, one line per problem (20 lines, then `... and N more (--json lists all)`); a single problem keeps its old text. `--json` keeps `refusal` as a string and adds `problems`, the whole list.
- The window's code file carries a `## Marker form` section (the keys of `qa` and `qa_unresolved`, the shapes, an example with `then` and `partition`, "`consolidates` is not a marker key: the script writes it"), rendered from the marker carrier; the `qa-automator` tool line and role file say the same, so the form is no longer learned from refusals.

- Changed: `sizing.py`: a story's size is counted in FUNCTIONS, not in how thoroughly the register describes them. The tester names what a person can do or rely on separately in a new `## Functions` table of `requirements-register.md` (one row per function, the `R-n` ids it holds); `size` is the size of `2 x N` for the N functions named, by the unchanged size table, and `work/sizing.json` says `size_unit: functions`, `function_count`, `functions[]`, `functions_unlisted` and `functions_unknown_ids`, and `cited_files` (the distinct files the non-derived rows cite, printed beside N and deciding nothing). Code errs only upward: a verifiable row no function holds is one more function and is named; a row added by the grounding step after S2 is named, not counted. The weight of the requirements, the test ceiling (`cap`), `overage` and `recommended_budget` keep their numbers and meaning. A register with no `## Functions` table, or an empty one, is sized exactly as before and says so (`size_unit: requirements`). A defect ticket with named functions is sized by them; the defect cap still limits what is planned, and records `computed_budget_uncapped`.
- The gate line and the report say the same words: `size M (4 functions: a, b, c, d)`, `the test ceiling is 28, over it by 15`, and, for a defect ticket, `a defect ticket: 1 regression case is planned (uncapped, the requirements weigh 32)`; at most six names are shown, then `and k more`; one function named for more than five requirements is said aloud. Above XL the advice no longer says to split the ticket: the person's word tests it as one story, or names the functions to leave out and the plan is narrowed to the rest.
- The register template, the tester charter (steps 2 and 5), the strategist charter (step 4), `automation-candidacy.md`, the S3 form's `budget.cap` comment and the understanding template name the new unit; the test ceiling is `cap` in `work/sizing.json`, no longer a number looked up by size, so a size counted in functions never changes what S3 plans.

- Changed: The S5 smell check reaches the fixtures a test uses, not only the ones in its own file: the arguments of the test, `usefixtures` (function, class, module `pytestmark`), autouse fixtures, `@pytest.fixture(name=...)`, and the fixtures those fixtures ask for, through the `conftest.py` chain (5 folders up; a climb that stopped short of the project root says so in a note, and a `conftest.py` that does not parse is named). A `sleep` in such a fixture is a `smell` finding when the window changed that fixture (new or changed since the story's S0, measured by the same reader the novelty switch uses); one in an unchanged project fixture is not the window's. When the change cannot be established (no S0 base, no answer) the result is a hint and a note, not a finding and not silence. The finding names the fixture's file, carries the fixture's own code for the judge, and its fix says "if it is not your change, say so in your digest": the gate stays closed until the wait is replaced or the person's word on that finding (its own tag) is recorded. The check now also reaches an own-file fixture the test does not ask for by argument (autouse, `usefixtures`, a fixture of a fixture); it is a finding with the same door. The project is the nearest folder with `qa-factory/config.json`, whatever the artifact root, and the conftest climb stops at it.
- A bare `sleep` is now found by the code's syntax tree, not a regular expression: any argument (`time.sleep(DELAY)`, `asyncio.sleep(2)`), in a finalizer after `yield` too, and never in a comment or a docstring. A fixture that polls with a ceiling (a `for` that leaves under an `if`, or a `while` on a comparison or with two ways out) is not a smell; a poll in a test body still is. Named residuals: `from time import sleep as pause`, a fixture from a `pytest_plugins` module or `request.getfixturevalue`, Playwright `wait_for_timeout`; a fixture of an edited conftest that the window did not touch can read as changed, and the fix text is the door.
- The window's code file says "wait for a condition, not seconds; fixtures in conftest are the window's code too" in its header, so the rule is no longer learned from the refusal.

- A manual check that could not be read no longer vanishes into the plan's reason. When the report cannot read the results of the
  checks made by hand, a `manual-agent` case with no readable record reads `not run` in the appendix with the basis `the manual
  results could not be read: <why>`, never `pass`.
- The "Checked by hand" block compares itself with the appendix: a case it counts as passed while the appendix reads it as anything
  else (and no live test, found bug or unresolved partition explains it) gets one line, `The table reads <case> as <result>; the
  check says pass`, and the same words on stderr. The report is not refused over it.

- The report now says why a red test was triaged the way it was. A triage row may carry `detail` (one sentence, in the task's terms)
  and the failure analyst is told to write it; the traceability appendix quotes it, else the control experiment's `observed`, else
  the older `reason`, and says "no reason recorded" only when none of them holds one. A report that falls back to that phrase beside
  a triage row that has a reason prints a `report: ...` line on stderr; nothing is refused.
- "Not planned" rows of the appendix read the plan's `## Not planned` section: the text after the line's first ` - ` or em dash is
  the reason. A requirement is matched by its whole name, so `R-1` no longer picks up the line of `R-13`, nor `R-3` that of `BR-3`.
- The default words of a left-with-you check that is stricter than the requirement now also tell the person to say, in their own
  words to the delivery gate, which of the two they want; the factory lays out what it can do and at what cost. No command is named.

- Added: The retro and the dashboard now say how many tests a story ran, how many times, and why each repeat happened ("5 tests, 31 runs in 9 launches: first run 5, after a launch that failed (environment or factory, not told apart) 9, after a red run 12, planned stage run 5"). A run is one executed test instance, the same number the retro already printed as "test executions"; a red-probe launch is counted apart and is not a run. The cause of a repeat is read from fields the factory recorded (the launch purpose, the dispatch's `repair_cause`, the status of the previous attempt of the same test, a stand signal, a triage verdict), never from the text of a reason, and the words live in the new `references/test-run-causes.json`. A repeat with no recorded cause is `unknown`, with the id of its launch, never a default. A story with neither run blocks nor execution jobs says "not recorded". A baseline capture is counted apart, not as a run, and a damaged run block or job is counted and named, not fatal. The counts are also written into the estimate ledger facts (`actual.test_runs`) as a record for comparison between runs; nothing reads them back from the ledger yet.

- `case_versions.py --verify` on a story with no case file no longer answers `verified: true, cases: 0`. It exits 1 with one JSON line
  `{"verified": false, "cases": 0, "reason": ...}` where `reason` is `no_cases`, `names_outside_form` (case files exist but their names do not
  match the project's id form; up to 10 names are listed) or `pins_without_files` (versions are pinned but the files are gone; adds `pins`),
  and a text on stderr that names the folders looked in, the id form and the next step. A story with files but no version keeps its REJECT
  list, which now opens with `no case of this story has a version yet; run --all`. `--all` and `--cases-dir` with no case file give the same
  text, exit 1 and write nothing (no pin, no scope); a bare call keeps the usage error.

- The pre-tool guard for a role's values file reads the form and parses the values once, not twice (`handoff_check.py`,
  `guard_pre_tool.py`): `values_report` returns the contract and whether the merged form already holds a filled
  `blocked.problem`, and the guard reads both from it; what the guard allows or refuses, and the refusal text, are
  unchanged (SC2-13)

- `handoff_check.py` refuses a handover form whose bytes are not UTF-8 with one plain line and exit 2 (for text and
  `--json` alike), instead of a stack trace; the form is neither read with replaced bytes nor rewritten, and the line
  names the form by its file name and the door that repairs exactly that form (`handoff_init.py --task <T> --stage <S>
  --role <role> --dispatch <form name without .yaml> --force`), short enough that the driver's 200-character clip of the
  reason keeps the door. The answer of the command is built in two small functions and the row-form hints of a values
  text in one helper; what is printed, its order and its exit codes are unchanged (SC2-14)

- The guard no longer lets a message go to an agent whose dispatch is stopped (`blocked` or `paused`) while the controller does not
  know it goes on: the refusal names `story_step.py resume --task <T> --dispatch-id <D>` (with `--agent-id` when the record holds
  no agent), and the next message passes. It is given only when the controller's own resume check would accept that request (budget
  stop, another running dispatch, a closed story or no recorded stop of its own keep today's pass), on both hosts. An agent with
  two stopped records, or any record in another status, is never refused; a failure of the check is a pass.

- A halt refusal of `story_step.py finish` and the refusal of `decide` for a role that does not close its stage now name the `resume` door beside the pause and recover road: when the dispatch record holds the agent, the text adds that after the `pause` the same agent can go on with `story_step.py resume --task <task> --dispatch-id <dispatch>` and the person's word goes to that agent as a message, so the conductor no longer has to open a new dispatch for a role that still holds its context. The old text stays as the prefix of the new one, byte for byte; a record with no agent (absent, empty, blank, not a string) and the gate refusals (`finish` on a refused or unreadable exit gate) are unchanged.

- The conductor no longer binds a launched agent by hand on Claude. A new PostToolUse hook on `Agent|Task` (`agent_autobind.py`) reads the
  agent id the host's answer carries (`tool_response.agentId`) and the dispatch the launch prompt names (the first line `story_step start`
  composed), and runs `story_step.py bind`, the one writer of the receipt. It never guesses: a string answer, no id, a prompt that is not
  exactly the card's, two dispatch ids, or a dispatch the controller does not hold as `running` for that role bind nothing and leave
  the conductor's own `bind` as the door; a `bind` that fails is one journal signal and never stops a role. Codex is unchanged.
- The dispatch id in a launch prompt is now read from the form `story_step` really writes (`Dispatch: <id>.`): the liveness check could not tie a
  foreground agent's handback to its dispatch before, so such an agent never counted as returned.
- A role's handover form is checked once when the role stops: the exit gate runs the same checker as `finish` (without `--fix`, a gate writes
  nothing) and, if the form is red, sends the role back once with the fields and problems, while it still has its context. No form, a
  `halt` or `impossible` digest, two running dispatches of the role, `handoffs.required: false`, or a check that could not run ask nothing of the
  role; `finish` and the driver are not changed by it.

- the manual runner writes a case's seed (the Given as repeatable `manual_capture.py http` calls) once, into
  `work/evidence/manual/<case>/seed-steps.md` beside the case's `request.json`, and a retry of the case reads that file instead of
  composing the seed again (SC2-38 item 4, text only: no code reads, checks or gates the file; a broken or stale file is rebuilt by
  the runner; a case with no `case_seeds` has none). Secrets stay `{generated_*}` and `--as`; a seed no `http` call expresses (a
  script, the database) is named in the file in words with its reason, with no new door and no change to the verdict. The author
  of the seed in S4 (a script written with the case) is not built: the runner writes the file

- Changed: the S6 manual runner is offered one case per window, run in turn, instead of a themed block of up to five. The door `story_step.py start` prints and the driver's manual plan both cut the manual-agent cases by the same window size (one case), so a long run of manual checks no longer rides in one marathon dispatch. A `--scope` of two to five cases is still accepted (the ceiling is unchanged, and a story in flight with an accepted block of three keeps it), and the rework of manual cases keeps its block of up to five. The runner's role file no longer promises concurrent blocks under `run.parallel`: one dispatch runs at a time.

- the brief of a manual runner block names the helpers the repo map found (`brief_pack.py`, SC2-38 item 4): a `- Helpers (repo map):` line
  right after the `Page objects` line of `## The stand` lists the function and public method names of the map's utilities, in the map's
  order, at most eight, then `(+N more: <map path>)`; names only, no value, no class (a client's methods come as bare names); a map
  with no utilities, no map, a map error, a non-Python utility or a utility with no names gets no line, and the brief of an automation
  block is unchanged; the section still fits the 6 KB brief, the extra lines are paid by the `not written yet` file lines
- the window helper section and the stand line share one formatter (`_names_by_module`), so `path: names (+N more)` has one shape; the
  bytes of the window brief do not change

- a tracker the factory holds no client for (anything but a Jira with a usable `direct_api`) is read by the scout through the route onboarding recorded in the `tracker` row of `requirements_sources` (`method`, `invoke_or_command_ref`), by six general rules and no per-tracker code (SS1-15): `ticket_adapter.py collect <KEY> --relation task` records the snapshot S0 made as the task source (the snapshot of another key is refused), `peek` and the other relations are refused with the `record-source` door, and a text read by the route is saved with `record-source`; what could not be reached is a gap in `unresolved_facts`, never a question
- `readiness.py` rates such a tracker `unknown` with `route: role` (proved by use, never `ok`) and the S1 dispatch guard lets it through; a route only the orchestrator holds (an agent, a skill, an MCP tool) is refused as before; a Jira with a broken `direct_api` and no recorded route keeps today's refusal naming the missing fields
- `references/requirement-source-kinds.json` gains `pointer_ref_prefixes` (a route ref that starts with one, such as `adapters.`, points into a config setting and is no route; a table without the key is refused and named by `config_contract.py`)
- `references/requirement-source-kinds.json` gains `not_read_routes` (the `method` words that are write channels); the route is shown to the scout, never parsed or run by code; the S0 `ticket_read` question names the recorded route in its answer block, with the same three answers

- The story runner checks the launch key of a NEW story before it reads or writes anything: a `--task` that is not a key of the project's tracker (`ADD-TO-CART` on a Jira project) is a question with four answers (`no ticket`: the command `ticket_adapter.py local-key --words-file <file>` is printed and the question held; `retry`, offered only when `adapters.ticket.key_pattern` is read; `go on`, a recorded pass; `stop`). A story that already has a `pipeline.json` or a snapshot is never asked, and `--no-trace` given at the start survives the stop.
- A local story (`LOCAL-<n>`) is read from its stored text in S0 (the text file is its ticket file), is not compared to a tracker, does not require the tracker route in the readiness check, gives no commit prefix to the git route, tells the scout it is local, and the scout dispatch guard no longer demands a proven tracker route for it. A story with a tracker key is guarded as before.

- A story with a text and no ticket gets a key the factory makes (`local_keys.py`, `ticket_adapter.py local-key --words-file <file>`, SS1-14): `LOCAL-<n>`, its text stored byte for byte as `qa-factory/local-tickets/<KEY>.md`, a number never given twice (`O_EXCL`, the story folders and `superseded/` count). The shape is data (`ticket.local` in `references/adapter-forms.json`, accepted under every tracker kind; `adapter_forms.KeyForm.story_pattern`); `local_keys.is_local` is the one reader of "is this story local?" and answers False on any doubt.
- A local story never goes to a tracker: `get` and `freshness` read its text file, `collect <KEY> --relation task` records it as the task source with no client, `peek` and any other relation are refused with the file named, `review` and `refresh` need no tracker when every source is a text the factory recorded, `external_writes.py` rejects a proposal that addresses a local key (a comment target or a create's parent).
- `ticket_adapter.py record-source --output <inventory> --ref <locator> --file <text> --relation <subject|parent|normative|referenced>` records a text a role read as a source of the inventory (it reaches the bundle and the manifest from there); empty, non-text, absolute, `..`-bearing and credential-bearing inputs are refused with the expected form.
- `ticket_adapter.py get --output` on a NEW story refuses a key the project's tracker cannot have (`adapter_forms.key_refused`, the twin of the driver's check) and names the doors: `local-key`, or `--key-form-word --words-file <file>` to go on under the name, the words kept in the snapshot's `provenance.key_form_word`.

- A LOCAL story (a key made by `ticket_adapter.py local-key`) started with no merge request, branch or commit, and whose text names no merge or pull request, is asked once, at the start and before the scout is dispatched, how to ground its tests: `current code` (offered only where the project records a code repository; recorded as the story's `implementation_source` with a line in its warnings, and told to the scout), `change` (the command with `--mr`, `--branch` or `--commit` is named and the question held), `ungrounded`, or `stop`. A real ticket with no flags is not asked: the scout's cascade looks for its change, as before.
- `reference-kinds.json` gains an optional `is_change` flag (true for `merge_request` and `pull_request`); `ticket_light.change_kinds` is its one reader, and a value that is not a bool refuses the table by name.
- On the skill path without the driver, a halt of the scout on `implementation.source: none` now names the door that records the person's choice (`stage_done.py --set implementation_source=...`, then `story_step.py resume` and the value in the message); `agents/qa-scout.md` stops only when the dispatch or the continuing message does not say `implementation_source: current-code`.

- A code review that rejects a test (row `rejected`, on a stand-blocked instance or a run one) now gets its review
  receipt: `window_record.py --review-receipt` writes and publishes it and still exits 1, so the window can finish
  and go back to its author. Closing S5 over a `rejected` row is refused exactly as before.

- `s5_precheck.py` (`check_relative_oracle`), `ledger.py`, `manifest_put.py`, `manifest_from_tests.py`, `detectors.json`,
  `delivery-verdict-kinds.json`, the case designer and case critic charters, the code critic charter, the code-review rubric and
  `test-code-patterns.md`: a test that compares a value taken BEFORE an action with the same value after it, while nothing asks the
  first to be a working answer, no longer passes S5 silently (TQ1-18, TP1-12586: a moved integration "still usable", green on a
  connection check that refused 400 both times). The check reads the test's AST: the base is the earlier of two variables assigned
  from the same call with an action between them, or a variable whose name holds a word of `baseline_names` (`before`, `baseline`,
  `original`, `prev`, `old`); a base nothing asserts (a bare truthiness test or a test against None does not count) is a finding with
  the person's word as its door and the marker key `base_checked="<file>::<function>"` as the test's own door when the base is
  asserted in a fixture (only the existence of the function is judged). Only tests the story changed are judged; a nested matcher
  (`is_(equal_to(before))`) and an attribute or an index (`after.status == before.status`) are read now. The case designer and the
  case critic hold a Then "as before" to a stated working base (a stand that cannot give one: the Then keeps the working base and
  `preconditions` names the need; the automator records `blocked_by_env` at S5). A call on the other side (`assert _u(c) == before`),
  a plain call around either value (`len`, `sorted`, `set`) and tuple unpacking are read now; a shape of the base (`isinstance`,
  `len`, `has_length`, `not base`) does not count as asking it to be a working answer.
  Beside the gate, the code critic records `base_outcome` (`{outcome: refused|working, run: <attempt id>}`, `manifest_put.py
  --fragment`) after reading the run log of such a test: a green of that run is the new ledger state
  `not_verified:oracle_on_refused_base` (kind `refused_base`, delivery `no`, owner the factory), and a new run of ANY kind leaves it
  with no command: a test re-run without a repair on its old fingerprint reads as a green (the direction chosen on purpose: the
  record is the second net, the gate is the first). Remainders: when the critic does not open the log, nothing is recorded and the
  ledger half stays empty - the gate (`check_relative_oracle`) is the real check; a record that names a run an S7 flake repair made
  is not written (the S7 round has no critic).

- `copy_detector.py` (new), `s5_precheck.py`, `brief_pack.py`, `detectors.json`, the code-review rubric: a copy of code that already exists
  is found by its shape, not by its text (TQ1-19). The old check saw only two helpers with one exact body, so a second helper
  or a second fixture under other names passed every gate. Now `s5_precheck.check_copies` reduces each function and each run of
  three statements to a name-blind form (local names, literals of one type and the function's own name do not count; a call
  to another function does) and compares the functions the story's history made new or changed (every file of the manifest and
  its `conftest.py` chain, all windows) with those files and the project modules they import. A copy of a HELPER or a FIXTURE
  is a finding with the person's word as its door (the fix names the existing code; a helper, new or changed, with a scaffold row
  may also write why in `keep`); a copy in a `test*` body is a hint the code critic reads (dimension 5); in an S7 repair round every copy is a
  hint. The limits are the `copy_detector` row of `references/detectors.json` (`min_function_statements` 2, `fragment_window`
  3, `max_files` 40); a row that cannot be read is the defaults and a note, a file over the limit is named, never silent. A copy
  whose novelty could not be established (no story base) is a hint and a note, not a finding: the guarantee that a copy of a helper
  in the diff does not pass the exit holds for a diff the gate can read. A window's code file gains the header section `Helpers
  that already exist` (the functions and public methods of the modules its test files and the files of its `uses` fixtures import,
  read by the same reader as the gate, relative imports and the conftest chain included; a test file not written yet is named, not
  read as "no helper"; at most 60 names). Code that is not Python is a note, not a check. Remainders: a repeated `try/except` or
  other run of statements INSIDE a larger helper is seen only when the run is at the same nesting level as the window (a window
  does not cross a nesting level); the share of false refusals is not measured yet (section 8 of the release).

- The code-review rubric (dimensions 2 and 3) and `test-code-patterns.md` ("Executable shape"): a relative result (old/new, before/after, side, order) asserts BOTH sides against expected values and the side; a sequence of cancelling actions (delete then undo) asserts after each action and keeps its positive control; state that can still change is read after waiting for the final state, and a guard such as `if x.count():` is not a wait (TQ1-3). The rubric no longer says tautologies are caught before the critic: no detector exists, the critic checks them (dimension 2).

- `manifest_from_tests.py`, `manifest_put.py`, `s5_precheck.py`, the automator and code-critic charters: the trail to the analogue (TQ1-7).
  A second helper written beside an existing one passed every gate, because the exit check sees only a textual duplicate.
  `manifest_from_tests.py` now writes `introduced_helpers[]` - a row per non-test function or method of the given files and
  their `conftest.py` chain that is new or changed in the story's history (`file`, `name`, `novelty`; a method is
  `Class.method`); the automator fills `purpose`, `searched`, `similar_found` and `keep` through `manifest_put.py --fragment`
  (merged by `(file, name)`; the writer's re-run keeps the role's words and drops the row of a function that is gone). The
  exit check gives a HINT (never a finding: `ok` does not move) for a row whose `searched` or `similar_found` is empty and
  for a method that shares a word with another method of its class; the code critic reads the rows and names the analogue
  or the grep that found none. A helper whose novelty could not be established is a row with `novelty: unknown` and a note
  (a false "new" is allowed, silence is not); a file that is not Python gives no rows and a note. Onboarding's
  `framework-rules.md` gains one section, the readers of the exact state of each surface. Left open: the door for a
  `keep` without a scaffold row (the copy detector, TQ1-19) is not part of this change.

## 0.10.6 — 2026-10-30 — gate B asks about exploratory findings in words with closed answers, a findings register and a read-only S7 investigation, a repair form carries the stage-wide answers of its parent

- A repair dispatch's agent is now recorded on the controller's dispatch record: `story_step.py bind` of a running
  repair dispatch on an accepted stage commits a bind-only stage transition (the stage stays accepted, no rework
  sub-state), so the resume guard no longer answers "not a dispatch this story ran" for a repair agent; the guard's
  no-agent door names `story_step.py bind`.
- A repair dispatch's handover form now carries the accepted parent's whole-stage answers (register size, candidates
  considered, budget, case counts and the like, listed per contract in `handoffs/index.yaml` `repair_carries:`), each
  recorded under `derived:` with the parent form as its source, so the repair role fills only its own rows; a parent
  that is missing, unreadable, of another contract or silent on a field carries nothing and the field is asked as
  before (`handoff_init.py --carry-from`, passed by `story_step` for a dispatch with `rework_of`).
  A row whose input file changed since the parent was accepted (`<hash>` version no longer matches) and the per-dispatch
  S6 counts are never carried (HF9-1, HF9-2; run TP1-14857).

- the findings register writer (`exploratory_findings.py`): `work/exploratory-findings.jsonl` is append-only, one JSON
  object per line, written and read only by this script (`add`, `correct`, `withdraw`, `list`, `check`). An entry is an
  observation, an unresolved question or a coverage gap, never a product bug: severity, priority, a bug word or a
  confirmed oracle is refused at any depth, and nothing in it counts as proven. Its id is the physical line number
  (unique past a damaged line), a target has one active line, and a ref whose bytes changed is named by `check` and
  never rewritten; every refusal names what it expected and the door (P2 M1 step 1)
- the readers of the findings register (P2 M1 step 3): while the register holds a line, the report carries the block
  `## Exploratory findings and unresolved questions` between "Product bugs" and "Review gaps" (observations, unresolved
  questions and coverage gaps; a corrected or withdrawn line struck through with the later line's id and reason; a line
  that cannot be read is an `Unknown` line, never "none"), the Proven block gains one line that sets formal test
  execution beside the exploratory probes ("not tests, not counted as proven"), and the gate B packet opens with the
  count and each live unresolved question or coverage gap, above "Bugs found". A story without a register renders
  byte-identically to before; `report_facts.py --write` removes the block, with a history copy, once the register holds
  no line, and `--check` names `--write` as the door. Phase S9 says the rebuild picks the register up and that a finding
  is recorded with `exploratory_findings.py add`, never by editing "Left with you"
- the questions of the findings are asked at gate B in words, with three closed answers (P2 fix round): each unresolved
  question is one line (the case, what it checks, what was seen, the behaviour before the change and now, "Is this
  intended?"), answered on a line of its own as `<case id>: intended`, `<case id>: bug` or `<case id>: open`, each word with
  the three price lines (the factory, you, the story) from the new `exploratory_question_words` block of
  `question-vocabulary.json`. `intended` confirms the finding by the person's word (a new oracle `person_confirmed`, written
  only on that word, never by a role) and answers the linked question with the reading "now"; `open` leaves the question
  with the person (`deferred_to_report`, not asked again; it stays in the report's findings as "left open with you" - the
  promise of a "Left with you" line waits for the later integration); `bug` sends the failure analysis (S7) back once, with
  the person's whole words behind a code preface naming the finding (the case, what was seen, before and now). Any other
  wording, a word of another reader on a question no stand-gap card answers, two words for one question or a finding that
  changed since it was shown goes to the conductor and is never applied; the closing sentence of the answer form says that an
  answer starting with the gate's approval word has only its form lines read. The packet no longer says "nothing to answer
  here" while it offers answers, lists a question once ("Open before the MR" skips it, also when the person left it open),
  names no register id, question id, role or machine reason. The report says "waits for your answer" for a question until
  gate B is decided and "left open with you" after it, and a line the person confirmed is "confirmed by you at gate B, for
  this finding only". The failure analyst treats the person's words about a case called a bug as the expectation for that case

- the preservation tool (`investigation.py`): names every observation a run left open (the runner's `inconclusive` and
  `manual_skipped` rows, and the cases refused for an unconfirmed expectation), projects each verbatim into the
  findings register exactly once (`project`), and turns the ones nobody investigated into `coverage_gap` lines
  (`close-gaps`, three fixed reasons), so they survive `finalize_task` and reach the report. A line a role touched or
  withdrew is never overwritten; a changed observation is one `correct`; a record the factory could not read becomes
  a gap, never silence. `unresolved` lists the targets that still wait, reads `NOT_EXECUTED` and `ENV_ISSUE` triage
  rows as context only, and prints the validity of the budget file (`budget_problems`). Nothing here compares an
  observation to an expectation or files a bug. No caller is wired yet, so a story run writes nothing (P2 M2)

- `investigation_probe.py` (new) and `references/investigation-budget.json` (new): the standalone, read-only probe of the S7
  investigation pass. `http` sends ONE GET, HEAD or OPTIONS request to a configured stand host, saves the answer under
  `work/evidence/investigation/<root>/<target>/NNN-request-response.json` and counts it in the pass's `captures.jsonl`; code
  enforces at most P probes per pass, R per target and T minutes from the first probe (12, 3 and 20 in the budget file, which
  also lists the allowed methods: the numbers and the methods are data, never code). The pass is the retry/relaunch chain of the
  investigation dispatch, so a restart continues the counts and the clock, it never refreshes them. `record` writes what the
  role saw into the findings register through the register's one writer, with the counts taken from the captures and only the
  statuses they support (`unverified`, `reproduced` with R named captures, `not_reproduced`, `environment_event`; never
  `investigated`). The login is made by code from the project's own recipe (the one non-GET call, to the stand's login path,
  never counted); a request that carries a method-override header (the family `X-HTTP-Method-Override`, `X-HTTP-Method`,
  `X-Method-Override`) is refused before anything is sent, because it would turn a GET into a write; a host outside `environments[]`, a Host header, a line break or a secret in a request, and a secret in a
  response are refused or not saved; a request that was sent but whose answer is not saved (timeout, no answer, a secret in the
  answer) still counts as a probe. Nothing here compares an answer with an expected value or writes a bug, a triage row or a
  ledger outcome. A call that cannot find the investigation module or the findings register refuses and names the missing names
  (through `_required`); before the S7 integration landed every call was refused that way, now the probe runs.
- S7 keeps unresolved exploratory observations: after the triage and any repairs (or at once when nothing failed) the factory runs
  ONE bounded read-only investigation by the failure analyst before gate B, and records every observation it could not investigate
  as a coverage gap in `work/exploratory-findings.jsonl` (driver and skill road).
- HONEST BOUNDARY of the probe: "These limits bound the sanctioned tool only. `investigation_probe.py` sends read-only methods,
  at most P probes per investigation, R per target, within T minutes, and records what it saw; it does not stop a role from
  reaching the stand through Bash or another tool, and it does not stop a role from changing the stand. A request made outside
  this tool is not counted and cannot be cited as evidence. Two calls run at the same moment can each pass the count before
  either is written, and a process killed between the request and its `captures.jsonl` line leaves a probe uncounted. Enforcing
  read-only access beyond the tool (E1/E2) is deferred by the owner; this release states the limit,
  it does not claim it solved."
- The exploratory findings block of the report is written in words for a person: no register id, no file path, no hash, no status code. It names the case, says what was seen, whether the factory looked again ("seen again in 3 of 3 tries", "not checked again", "caused by the test environment, not the product") and, for a line that waits for a person, "waits for your answer" with the question in words; only screenshot file names are listed as evidence. The Proven block's formal line counts findings and coverage gaps apart ("what the factory could not check"). The lines that code projects into the register (`investigation.py`) carry the question's words instead of its id, and a record that could not be read is named in words, never by its path; a damaged register line is reported as a count, with the reasons left to the role channel. The register declares `TERMINAL_FIELDS` (fields recorded and read by nobody downstream).

## 0.10.5 — 2026-10-29 — gate B orders and closure, the bug reporter opened by gate B, red-then chains and honest probes, the agent drives the UI

- A green result is no longer thrown away because qa-factory/config.json changed somewhere the test launch never reads (TP1-14857: a stand's `frontend_url` was added and the one green test that had not changed since its last run, TC-005, was run again; the S6 digest could not say why). `config_sha` now hashes the execution-relevant configuration of the run's profile: its profile row, `run`, `execution` (without the probe entry), the `environment` pointers, the selected stand's name and address, and `tests_root`; the rules live in references/config-projection.json. Other config files are hashed whole as before. A project config that cannot be read as a JSON object, a malformed `profiles` list or `environment` block, or a nesting the fingerprint cannot hash is refused with a named line; nothing is hashed around and no new requirement is added (a project without `environments[]` or without a row for the run's profile fingerprints as before). The fingerprint carries an explicit `policy_revision` for the first time, so every result recorded by an earlier release is run once more (reported as "config_sha changed … the first run under the new rules") and reused from then on. A factory script that starts reading a new config key in the launch path by the usual access patterns fails the factory's own tests until the key is classified in the rule file.

- S5 plan: tests of one level in one file that each prove their own case now draw a grouping hint, and the rule is one rule in three carriers (`s5_plan.py`, `s5_precheck.py`, `brief_pack.py`, `qa-automator.md`, `test-code-patterns.md`, `code-review-rubric.md`): cases with the same setup and action are ONE parameterized test, the data and the expected value (from each case's oracle) being the parameters and each parameter id naming its case; a different set of Thens is a consolidated scenario or a test kept apart. On the stand run TP1-12586 the author wrote ten tests for ten cases, seven of them in one API file; the plan check and the review now say so. The hint is advice, never a finding: `s5_plan.py --check` and the plan dispatch of `s5_precheck.py` print `hint: [plan] ...` before `OK:`/`REJECT`, the exit code, the verdict and the findings are those of the same plan without it, and a plan that cannot be read keeps its finding and gets no hint.
- Plan tests have an optional `apart_reason` (at most 300 characters): the door out of the hint, for a test kept apart because of another setup, surface or fixture. Code reads only its presence and form (an empty or blank value is no reason, a value that is not text is a finding of the plan check); the plan critic judges whether it holds, and a test left unmerged is a `remark`, never a `blocker` on its own. The reason is shown in the plan slice a window reads. A case expected red by its requirement never shares an instance with another case: it may be a parameter of a parameterized test, never part of a consolidated body.

- S5 plan check (`handoffs/vocabulary.yaml`, `fit_to_shapes`): a case whose S3 `fit` is `new` may now be planned as `parameterize` (new cases with the same setup and action may be one parameterized test); before, the plan check refused such a test as a departure from S3 and the author had to declare a `deviation` or keep one test per case. A test planned against an S3 `extend` still needs the declared deviation.
- `consolidates` means two lists, and the three places that name it now say so in one sentence (the vocabulary, `artifact-contract-automation.md` and the plan check's finding for an empty `consolidates`): in the S5 plan, the tests a consolidated test merges; in the manifest, the cases the instance proves. Neither meaning changes.

- A story is closed only after what the person decided at gate B has been carried out. Gate B now gives orders: `bugs` (the bug reporter files the drafts the person chose) and `mr` (the delivery step opens the MR), each with an executor named in one row of data (`references/stages.json`, S8 `gate_orders`, read by `hooklib.gate_orders`). While an order is due the story is `executing`, neither open nor closed: `hooklib.story_closure` is the one reading (`story_closed` is its wrapper), and `controller.py --operation next` answers `execute_gate_b` with the orders, their executors and the chosen drafts instead of `closed`. On 12586 the person chose two bug drafts, the story was counted closed on the spot, and the bug reporter was refused as a closed story. Now the reporter (and only the executor of a due order, a rework carrying a person's words, and after the orders the retro) can start; every other dispatch is refused with the orders named and a door each. The retro (S9) waits until the orders are settled.
- New operation `settle_order --order bugs|mr --outcome done|cancelled [--ref <text>] [--words-file <file>] [--reason-code no_trace|delivered_without_mr]`: an MR is `done` only with its record (`--ref`, a link or an id, at most 2000 characters); an order is `cancelled` by a person's words or by the factory's coded reason with the delivery step's own record as `--ref`; `bugs` is never `done` by a word (the accepted reporter dispatch settles it) and a release of the reporter by a person's word cancels it with those words. `gate-decision --gate B` takes `--bugs ordered|not_ordered` and `--mr open|do_not_open|not_offered`; without `--mr` the MR is ordered. The decision records `decided_seq` and `decided_at` (UTC) and each dispatch `dispatched_seq`, so "after the decision" is a comparison of event numbers, never of times. Updating: a decision recorded by 0.10.4 with chosen drafts and no orders, whose retro has not started, becomes `executing` for the reporter at the first projection; a story whose retro is running or done is read as it was. A reason code cancels only the `mr` order (the person's `bugs` order is called off by their words or a release), a `decision` request carrying the keys only the projection writes (`orders_settled`, `orders_due`, `decided_seq`, `decided_at`) is refused, and the refusal of a dispatch on a closed story names only the doors that open on that story.

- The driver carries out the gate B orders (`execute_gate_b`) before the story closes and settles them. The bug reporter runs for a `bugs` order that is due and is never sent again after a person released it; the delivery step runs for an `mr` order that is due, and the `mr` order is settled from the delivery mark by `settle_order`: `done` with the MR link or id the delivery verdict now names in its new `mr` field, `cancelled` with the person's own words after `no delivery`, or `cancelled` with the factory's coded reason (`delivered_without_mr`, `no_trace`) and the delivery step's record. A process that dies right after the delivery mark settles the order on the next run and never delivers twice. A pass that moves no order is looked at once more; the second goes to the conductor, never a third pass. The driver records its gate B decision with `--bugs ordered`.
- `no delivery` cancels only the merge request order (the owner's word, 28.10.2026): the bug reporter still runs for a `bugs` order that is due, because it writes a local file and sends nothing out.
- `gate-decision --gate B --bugs not_ordered` together with `--drafts` is refused (the decision would contradict itself); the refusal names both doors: drop `--drafts`, or record `--bugs ordered`.
- Updating: a gate B decision recorded by 0.10.4 carries no orders. Its delivery still runs when no delivery mark exists, and no order is tracked; the bug reporter is derived only from chosen drafts, so a decision with the person's words and no chosen draft no longer starts the reporter (no such story was in flight on the stands).

- The bug reporter is opened by the recorded gate B decision, not by the delivery verdict. The stage guard's rule 4 used to refuse `qa-bug-reporter` while `delivery_ready` was not `yes` (or the journal had no `deliver_with_risks`), so a story with bugs could never file them: on 12586 the person chose two bug drafts at gate B and the reporter was refused with "delivery_ready is not yes". Now the role is opened by `contract.gate_approved` on `gates.B` and the pair role -> gate comes from the one row of orders (`references/stages.json`, S8 `gate_orders`, read by `hooklib.gate_orders`); the key `delivery_gated_roles` is removed. No gate B decision (no record, an empty or damaged one, declined, deferred, edit) refuses the reporter with the command that records it. The MR command keeps its verdict rule: `yes`, `after_checks` or a `deliver_with_risks` word. The gate B packet no longer says a bug is filed through "deliver with known gaps". Updating: a story whose gate B was decided on 0.10.4 is opened for the reporter by its own `gates.B`; a verdict `yes` with no gate B decision no longer opens the reporter before the gate. A hand-damaged `gates` in `pipeline.json` is now a refusal of the dispatch, not a crash of the guard.

- The gate B road is described the way the code runs it. `phases/s8.md` records the decision with `--bugs ordered|not_ordered --mr open|do_not_open|not_offered`, names the defaults when a flag is left out, sends the bug reporter through `next` -> `execute_gate_b` (no longer "rework of a closed stage"), ends an order with `controller.py --operation settle_order` (`mr` done with its link or id, an order called off with the person's words), says that `no delivery` calls off only the MR order, and starts S9 only after `next` answers `closed`; a verdict of `no` no longer stands between the person and a filed bug. `phases/s9.md` waits for every order gate B gave. `references/controller-api.md` documents the `next` action `execute_gate_b` and the `settle_order` operation, `references/conductor.md` has the row for a person who cancels an order in words, `handoffs/gate-b-to-delivery.yaml` carries `decision.orders` and the flags, and `README.md` no longer says the reporter waits for `deliver_with_risks`.

- S5 windows no longer wait for the person's word on quality checks nothing produces (`window_record.py`, `acceptance.py`,
  `coverage_contract.py`, `controller.py`): `required_quality_checks` of a window now holds only the checks a factory script
  writes a receipt for (`references/quality-receipt-producers.json`, empty today), so the four readiness ids the conductor
  recorded at initialize no longer produce four `quality:*` gaps per window and bindings no longer owe
  `quality_receipt_refs` or `quality_not_applicable_reason` for an empty requirement (live run 12586).
- The checks left out are named, not dropped (`window_record.py`, `report_facts.py`): every new window carries
  `quality_not_run` (`[]` when empty) and the testing report prints `Quality checks the factory did not run: <id> (<reason>)`;
  ids the readiness step already checked at S0 are not printed as unrun, an unreadable readiness record is printed as unknown.

- case critic (`agents/qa-case-critic.md`, `critic_rollcall.py`): `reject` now means a failing case; a round with concerns and no failing
  case is `approve_with_concerns` whatever the number of concerns, and its digest is headed `ok`, so no repair round is spent on it
  (run 12586 round 3 said `reject` over 11 approving rows and "no case fails"). A round that says `reject` over a roll-call whose cells
  hold no `reject` is read as `partial` with the basis `round_word_rule` and the door "rewrite the `Verdict:` line" (a new round on
  top); code never rewrites the critic's word (FR-35). This holds for an earlier round and for a later one alike: a later round with
  such a word refuses the rows it lists until the critic rewrites the line. Gate A words it plainly ("the critic's Verdict line
  contradicts its cells ... the cases were not changed"), and the gate A repair for this basis goes straight to a critic round (no
  designer round: the cases were not wrong), the person at the series cap.
- carried concerns (`critic_rollcall.accepted_rounds`, `s5_plan.case_concerns` / `remarks_of`, `gate_brief.py`): the notes of the
  `approve_with_concerns` rows of the accepted rounds travel to the S5 automator as remarks `CC-n` placed by case; per case the latest
  accepted round of a findings file that lists it decides (a later round over fewer cases never drops the concerns of a case only an
  earlier round reviewed). Each remark names the findings file and the round where the full finding is, and carries the critic's own
  `fix` cell of the row when the critic wrote one (an optional `fix` column of the roll-call). The window brief prints them under
  "Remarks (plan review and case critic)", the automator answers each in `plan_remarks`, and C12 refuses a form that skips one. Gate A
  prints one line, "Concerns carried to automation: TC-..". A findings file edited after its receipt carries nothing from that round
  (stderr says why); a findings file that cannot be read at all is a remark to every window, naming the file.

- The sensitivity probe finds a test whose report id carries a plugin-added parameter (`probe_by_code.py`, `red_sandbox.py`): a test the
  author never parametrised is reported by pytest-playwright as `name[chromium]`, and the probe, asking for `name`, read 0
  rows and recorded `not_executed` (run 12586, TC-008/TC-009). A request without a parameter now matches the single
  `name[<p>]` row (the record names the matched id); with several such rows `probe_by_code.py` judges every row and the
  verdict is `intended_failure` only if every row is (a judged survivor is never hidden behind an unrun row and never leaves an old
  killed record standing), the surviving rows are named in the record; a request with a parameter matches exactly, or the row
  whose parameter is the same plus one plugin token (`[json]` for `[chromium-json]`); the run block of `run_suite.py` binds a
  predicted parameter-less report id the same way when no collect spelled it; when no row matches, the note names up to 5 ids the report held. `red_sandbox.py --probe` binds its row
  through the same matcher (one function, `red_sandbox.matching_rows`; several rows are reported as ambiguous, never picked) (HF4-12)

- gate A recorded through `controller.py --operation gate-decision` now makes the `manual-agent` rows executable
  (`controller.py`, `planning_contract.make_manual_rows_executable`): the manual-agent pass ran only on the driver road,
  so a gate A recorded by the conductor bound a plan whose manual obligations were still `new`, and
  `manual_evidence.prepare_request` refused them until gate A was reopened (run TP1-12586). The pass now runs on
  the plan before the decision hashes it, converts only what the approved row already carries (`manual-agent`
  disposition and its evidence policy), never an unresolved oracle, and the decision answer lists what it did in
  `manual_pass`; a preview (`--build-only`) writes nothing (HF4-14).

- The exit gate judges the role's OWN last word (`exit_gate.py`, `host_adapter.py`, `host_probe.py`): `handoff_digest` reads the subagent's own transcript (`agent_transcript_path`) first, then `last_assistant_message`, then the session transcript; when the child's file is named but unreadable the digest is neither judged nor filed (one stderr line), never taken from the parent. Live run 12586 blocked roles 17 times with "your final message is not the handoff form", quoting the parent's prose. The handback call and the Codex rollout row are read by one function, `host_adapter.assistant_row_texts`, shared with the context probe. A Codex child's digest is now judged by the same gate (decision F-2; not yet proved on a live Codex run). The digest's row states now include the case critic's verdict words (read from `critic_rollcall.CASE_CRITIC_VERDICTS`, the one list) and a row state spelled `<word> (<known state>)` is read, so the recorded case critic word `approved (approve_with_concerns)` passes; both critic role files name the one word for the row.

- An answer to a before/now question is tied to a case's Then text by the reading's meaning, not by letter. The two readings of a before/now question now say what they mean (`claim: now|before`), a case writes its `question_thens` texts under `now` / `before` for such a question (and for the question it asks the S4 exit to raise), and one reader (`contract.question_then_text`) turns the person's letter into the key for the gate-A card, the resolver of the Then's oracle and the late-answer applier. A case that keys a before/now question by letter is sent back to its designer before the person sees the question; a question answered by letter before the update keeps its answer. The "which reading is the behaviour now" tests of `claim_confirmed`, `before_value_needed` and the resolver's regression branch ask the question instead of assuming letters `a` / `b`. A before/now question the requirements tester wrote without `claim` is named to the tester when a case already keys its texts by meaning.

- gate A no longer asks again a contradiction whose reading fork a register question closed (`gate_brief.py`,
  `planning_contract.py`): on TP1-12586 three cards (R-3, R-5, R-1) were put to the person for forks they had closed
  at the S2 stop with `Q1 b`, `Q2 a`, `Q4 a`. The `Decision` cell of a `## Reading forks` row that a question closes
  starts with that question's id (`Q1 b adopted: ...`, read by `register_fork_questions` through the one table-cell
  reader); a card is skipped when every contradicted requirement of its plan row is closed, otherwise it is built for the
  FIRST one nobody settled. A question deferred, with the designer, changed since the answer, answered on an unreadable
  row fingerprint or with no date closes nothing, and neither does any answer when the answers file has a broken line:
  the error goes toward asking. A contract line in the register template, `artifact-contract-plan.md` and
  `qa-requirements-tester.md` says it to the role before the work.
- gate A's "Already decided by you" lists the register questions the person answered (`gate_brief.py`): the reading's
  text or the person's own words (squeezed, cut at 160 characters), where it was given, ten lines and then
  `(+K more ...)`; one line says when some answers could not be read. The section is printed when only answers fill it,
  and the brief's line cap grows by exactly its bounded size so the document links at the bottom survive.

- a question raised at the S4 exit for a case reaches the `question_refs` of the case's plan row (`question_register.py`,
  `planning_contract.py`): on TP1-12586 TC-014's Then 1 was raised as Q7 while TS-14 kept its own "no settled expected
  value" card, so the person met one fork twice. `raise_for_case` now appends the new id to the row through
  `planning_contract.append_question_ref` (one row-level write of the plan, at the end of the refs, no duplicate, nothing
  else in the row changed). A plan approved at gate A is never written; an absent or unreadable plan, a case without a
  plan row, a row the plan does not have, or a `question_refs` that is no list leaves the plan as it was (the writer's
  return line says why); the question is raised in every case.
- the S5 window brief shows an `oracle_unknown` plan row's expected value as settled once the person answered the questions in its
  `question_refs` (`s5_plan.window_slice` / `render_slice`): `expected value settled by the person (Q7): <the person's words,
  whole, then the answers file>`; a ref with no answer shows `not settled yet; unanswered: Qn`; an absent register or a
  partly unreadable answers file leaves the brief as it was.
  The approved plan is never written - the reader derives the line from the answers, through the one answered-reader.

- dead yes/no wrapper over `red_run_for` removed (`case_stamp.py`): it had no caller outside tests since the one-predicate change; readers use `red_run_for` or `instance_hold` directly, and its test pins now assert `red_run_for(...) is not None`

`contract.rollup_status` names every unknown run word of a case, once each, in the order the run recorded them (`weird, odd`), instead of the last one only; the plan row of the ledger prints each word once.

- the agent sees the screen (`manual_capture.py ui`, `manual-capture-steps.json`, `qa-runner.md`, `manual-evidence.md`): after
  each of the first 40 steps the summary's `steps[]` row also carries `screenshot` and `text` (a short excerpt of the page,
  a failed step a longer one with its own screenshot); the screen of a passed step is saved in `<attempt>/observe/` and is
  never part of the record. The runner drives the UI as a user: it reads the excerpt, changes the steps and captures again.
  The step loop is its own function (`_run_steps`) and `page_words` reads the page's dialogs and body.
- sign-in by steps: the new step word `fill-account <selector> <actor> user|secret` types an account the code resolves
  (the same forms as `--as`; the steps file holds names only). While the form is on screen no screenshot is saved and a
  `capture` is refused. A login by code that did not land with owner `factory` (the recipe did not fit the page) now has a
  door: one sign-in by steps in a new attempt; with owner `user` the block still halts, and `fill-account` after it is refused.

- case actor (`manual_capture.py`, `manual_evidence.py`, `story_run.py`, `report_facts.py`, `qa-runner.md`,
  `manual-evidence.md`, `qa-case-designer.md`): a manual capture can now sign in as the account a case needs, not only
  as the stand's one default account. `manual_capture.py ui|http --as <actor>` takes `default`, a role of the stand's
  `credentials_by_role`, `env:USER_KEY/SECRET_KEY` (an account a person put in the project's env file; the factory
  never keeps the value) or `created:<username>`. Without `--as`, a case whose request names exactly one stand account
  is captured as that account; every other shape of the case's accounts is refused with the doors named (never a
  guess, never another account). `manual_evidence.py prepare` now writes the case's `kind: account` preconditions into
  `request.json` as `actors` (read only through `request_actors`; a request without the field reads as no actors), and
  the stand-login question before the dispatch also checks the accounts the screen cases name.
- created users (`manual_capture.py http`): `{generated_username}` and `{generated_password}` in a `--body-file` are
  filled with generated values in the bytes that are sent only (the template check runs on the file as written, the
  saved request keeps the placeholders, the saved answer is redacted); on a 2xx answer the password is kept only in the
  machine-local `qa-factory/state/created-accounts/<ticket>.json` and the story folder gets the user's name; the report
  says which users the story created and that they are left in place. A failed sign-in names the actor's keys.

- The stand's `qa-factory/config.json` is given back when a story ends. A story that starts fresh keeps the bytes it found
  (`story_step.py config-snapshot`, also called by the driver at the story start); at S9 and at a planned `stop`
  (`story_step.py config-restore`) the file is restored, except what a recorded writer wrote in the story's window: an
  onboarding approval, a report adaptation, or the runtime probe's `--suggest --write` entry. The file as it was before the
  revert is kept machine-locally under `qa-factory/state/config-reverts/`, and one report line names what was reverted, what
  was kept and where that copy is. A story that started before the factory kept a copy is reported as "not reverted", never
  as "unchanged"; another story in flight, or one that ran inside the window, also stops the revert with a line saying so.


- `config_contract` writes `config.json` and its migration backup through one atomic byte writer (`_replace_bytes`); backups
  are now written with LF line ends on every platform. The runtime probe's note is the constant `SUGGEST_NOTE`.

- stand frontend address (`env_probe.py`, `manual_capture.py`, `stand_health.py`, `stand_identity.py`): one reader,
  `env_probe.frontend_of`, now answers "what is this stand's frontend" for the host allow-list of manual captures, the
  login target of `manual_capture.py ui`, the stand health targets and the stand definition hash. The entry's
  `frontend.url` wins, the flat `frontend_url` stays readable as an alias, and the block's
  `environment.frontend.url_key` serves the one-and-only `environments[]` entry. Before, a stand whose frontend address
  lived only in the env file (the run of TP1-12586) refused every UI URL as "not on a configured stand"; the refusal
  now also says where the frontend address would be set. `read_frontend` and `frontend_address` moved from
  `stand_health.py` to `env_probe.py` unchanged.
- onboarding hint (`env_probe.py`, `p4-generate.md`): when no frontend address is configured, the probe names (never
  prints the value of) the env-file keys that hold an http address nothing declares, so onboarding can judge whether
  one of them is the frontend and write `environment.frontend.url_key`.

- manual block brief (`brief_pack.py`): the brief of a manual runner block now names the commands of the manual half
  (`manual_capture.py ui|http` with `--as`, `manual_evidence.py build`) on its card and carries a section `The stand`
  right before the commands: the API address, the frontend address (read only through `env_probe.frontend_of`; an address
  with credentials in it is reported as not configured), the accounts the runner may pass to `--as` (names only), the env
  key names that may form an `--as env:USER_KEY/SECRET_KEY`, the account each manual case names (read only through
  `manual_evidence.request_actors`) and up to five page objects of the repository map. Where something is not configured or
  cannot be read, the section says so. The section is never cut to make room: the map, the digests and then files give way
  first. The brief of an automated block has no section.

- A person's word now passes the refusal of the plan-rework row bound (`controller.py`, `_s5_plan_accept_problems`,
  `_plan_rework_rows_problems`): the refusal "the rework changed the rows of ..." names the door for the person's words
  (`waiver.py ... --block "plan rows by person: <dispatch>;"` and `--words-file`), and once that word is recorded for the dispatch
  the same accept goes through. The `;` closes the dispatch id, so the word for `S5-qa-automator-5` never passes
  `S5-qa-automator-50`; an unreadable record leaves the refusal standing. A rework built with `--words-file` was never bound and
  still is not; without the word the refusal is the old text plus one sentence, ending as before with the repair marker (t-1508 R2).

- A UI step that ran out of time on an element now says why. The old text, "no element matched", was printed for every
  timeout, even when the element was on the page and a dialog mask covered it. The step now asks the page (without
  waiting): no element matched only when none did; otherwise the element is not visible, not enabled, covered by
  `tag.class` (with its text, unless the text matches `secret_content_patterns`), or "could not be established" when
  a probe failed. The failed step's screenshot path comes next, the browser's own first line last. A step that
  finished after the element limit is reported as completed late, not as "no element matched".

- S7: `red_sandbox.py --diagnostic --repo ROOT --request diag.json --task-root T [--dispatch ID]` is the failure analyst's ONE run of a red test without the asserts of the Thens that wait behind its red one, in a disposable copy of the tree. On the stand run TP1-12586 two independent Thens sat after a red assert and nobody could say whether they would hold. The variant may only REMOVE lines of the instance's own test function (`variant_shape.py`: a line added or changed, nothing removed, lines moved, or a change outside the function is refused before a copy exists), `before_sha256` must be the file's bytes now, and the test in the repository is never changed. The run is the existing probe sequence (`--purpose red_probe` in the copy, the copy removed on every path) and publishes nothing: no receipt, no `work/probes/`, no manifest row, no binding, no run block, and no ordinary job whose `cwd` a later run could copy. Its only trace is `evidence/diagnostic-<label>.json` (instance, hashes, removed lines, status `passed`/`failed`/`not_executed`, the failure line; `thens` only when unambiguous: `passed` -> `held`, `not_executed` -> `not_reached`, a red variant leaves the reading to the analyst). One run per test and bytes: a second request answers `already_run` with the path; a person's recorded word `diagnostic again: <instance>` (stage S7) passes one repeat.
- `variant_shape.variant_shape(original, variant, function)` is the one helper that judges the shape of a variant of a test file (removed, added, moved, outside the function); `contract.triage_diagnostic_problems(row, task_root)` is the one reader of a triage row's `diagnostic` block (`evidence` a `diagnostic-*.json` file under `evidence/`, `observed`, optional `thens`). `references/artifact-writers.json` names `red_sandbox.py` the writer of `evidence/diagnostic-*.json`.

- `s5_precheck.py` (`_own_red_order`): a test that is red by its OWN `contradicts_requirement` row no longer passes S5 in silence
  for the other Thens it binds `covered`. A test stops at its first failing assert, so a Then behind the red never ran:
  `red-own-behind-<instance>-<n>` when the pinned lines put Then n after the red one, `red-own-order-unknown-<instance>-<n>`
