  when the order is not established (the lines are not pinned apart: the live shape), one `red-own-thens-unnamed-<instance>`
  when the row names no `thens`. The door says what to do: move the assert above the red one if the Then does not wait for the
  defect, or record it as `blocked_by_check` with `blocking_check` if it does, or pin the Then lines on the marker. In an S7
  repair round (`S7 fix: ...`) the same words are hints, not findings. A `blocked_by_check` row for a Then that ran and failed
  is `blocked-check-ran-<n>` ("it is not behind a check").

- A triage row can now name the Thens its red stops: `blocked_thens` (`{then, blocking_check, detail}`) and a row-level
  `blocking_check` (this red is another case's defect). They are read by one function, joined to the Thens recorded behind a
  check in the manifest, and shown in "Left with you" as "check after <case> is fixed", with the diagnostic run's evidence path
  when the row has one. The red's own verdict is never lowered, and the blocked case gets no second bug draft: the blocker's draft
  lists the case in `cases`; the S7 claim refuses a duplicate draft and a blocker draft that misses the case. A Then recorded
  behind a check that ran and failed is named as a factory record instead of being shown as waiting.

- S7 `reorder` round (t-1508 R7): `scripts/s7_reorder.py start|finish` keeps the snapshot of the test file before the round and, at the end, accepts only a pure move of lines of the test's function (`variant_shape`) over a still-red `repair_verify` run; the triage row is then carried to the new attempt (`carried_attempts`, `carried_by: s7_reorder`), which `contract._attempt_fits` honours for an attempt id the failure itself has. `s5_precheck` names the three S7 round reasons once (`S7 fix`, `S7 reorder`, `S7 reorder review`); the reorder reasons stay strict (findings, not hints). The driver runs the round: a triage row with `reorder: true` is an S7 repair whatever its verdict (`s7_repair_rows`), the author is registered with reason `S7 reorder: <test>`, `finish` judges the edit, and a code critic reviews that one test (`S7 reorder review: <test>`); the author's digest is never read as repaired for such a row, a green re-run (kind `green`) stops the test, a halting or `unverified` critic stops it, and a blocking `test_defect` finding is one more round. The round is counted in the S5 window's repair cap (cause `test_defect`, the controller's count; accepted for 0.10.5), and at the cap the existing `s7.repair_limit` question asks the person. `handoffs/s7-analyst-to-automator.yaml` offers `repairs[].kind: reorder`, and its claim is now `no_app_bug_expectation_was_handed_for_repair`; an empty `scope` is no longer accepted while a triage row asks for a `reorder`. `phases/s7.md` writes the round for the conductor (registered `rework` plus `story_step.py materialize`, `s7_reorder.py start` / `finish`, the critic, and the person's word `plan before windows` with its price when the plan order refuses the registration). `red_sandbox.py --diagnostic` has its role-command card (what to write, how to prove it) and quotes it in a refusal.

- Thens behind a red (`agents/qa-failure-analyst.md`, `skills/qa-story/phases/s7.md`, `references/conductor.md`): the analyst's
  rule 2c no longer sends an independent Then back to the author (S5); a dependent Then is listed under the triage row's
  `blocked_thens` with the `blocking_check` it waits for, an independent one gets ONE diagnostic run in a copy
  (`red_sandbox.py --diagnostic`, on the analyst's card) or a `reorder` of the asserts reviewed by a code critic; the
  conductor reads the triage row first, names the price of the rerun before it, and never answers the question with
  `rework --stage S5`; a rework carrying the person's words always takes `--words-file`.
- `references/artifact-contract-run.md`: the optional `triage.json` fields `blocked_thens`, `blocking_check`, `diagnostic`,
  `reorder` and the `cases` of a bug draft are documented, with their readers.

## 0.10.4 — 2026-10-28 — run honesty: an unknown is never reported as a pass, one broken test module no longer fails collection for every profile, stand health asks the API, the canon reds of 0.10.3 fixed

- The run-record join resolves the project config once per story instead of six times per test: the resolved config rides in the run-rows index and is passed to the instance-id aliases of the join and of the dashboard's `match_run_row` (optional `cfg`, default unchanged). The join outcomes are unchanged.
- The K11 key of `test_case_id_form_sites.py` now pins the join as HF2-6a defined it: a legacy entry (no identity of its own) joins the row of its case, an identified entry never takes another instance's row.

- `host_probe.py --check` names every unmet condition (`host_probe.inspect`): the result carries `missing`, a list of
  `{id, reason}` in the order the `verified` conjunction checks them (a changed or unread fingerprint, an expired probe,
  the ALLOW and DENY guard exit codes, the executed call id, a DENY that was executed, and per receipt no receipt, no
  readable transcript, or a call the transcript does not hold); it is an empty list when verified, and a missing or
  unreadable probe file is its own condition. The first sentence of `reason` is unchanged and the unmet ids follow it.
  The `verified` predicate itself did not change; a failure the list cannot explain is named `unknown_condition`
  (FB-6, RH1-11).

- The S3 exit's "question branches not checked" lines now open with the same `S3 remarks:` head as the findings line
  (one function, `stage_done.s3_remark_line`), and `story_step.py finish` keeps every such line whatever its position in
  stage_done's output; past four of them it says `(+N more not checked)` instead of cutting silently (RH1-12).

- the S5 phase card (`skills/qa-story/phases/s5.md`): the person's own decision after a blocked plan review is recorded by
  the file form `waiver.py ... --block "<that word>" --words-file <file>`, not an inline `--decision "..."`, so a free word
  travels whole through a file (FR-8); the door scan of `test_words_doors.py` is green again.
- the code critic charter (`agents/qa-code-critic.md`): the `## Procedure` section is back, with "On the plan" and "On the
  code (a window)" as its subsections, so the agents contract audit (A19) passes over the real package; the file grew by 16 bytes.
- `scripts/story_step.py`: `_next` read `controller.state()` only in `read_only` mode; that extra read was dead work, since
  `next_action()` reads the state itself, so the read is gone.

- One test file that cannot be imported no longer drops the whole collect (`node_ids.py`, `launch_check.py`,
  `gate_preflight.py`, `run_suite.py`, `red_sandbox.py`, `references/launch-causes.json`): the runner row now carries
  the runner's own facts (the flag that makes it go on, the exit it ends with, the lines that name a broken file, the
  count and a stop) as data; `node_ids.collect_verdict` is the one reading of a collect's outcome and tells complete,
  partial, none selected, all broken, stopped and unread apart. The onboarding probe and the gate A rehearsal report
  the broken files and go on; S5 checks the ids of the files that collected and calls an id of a broken file "not
  verified", never "missing" (RH1-3).
- The project's test files that could not be collected are kept in the story (`collect_gaps.py`,
  `state/collect-gaps.json`) and named in the report under the regression list with the owner by source: the project's
  for what gate A found or a folder, the story's for a test file its own S5 request names (RH1-3).
- A filter that deselects every healthy test next to a broken module is read as "the filter selected none", never as
  "every file is broken"; a test under a class whose collection failed is "not verified", never "missing"; the node-id
  CLI, the sandbox and the manifest writer use the same runner row (RH1-3 fix round).

- The doctor and gate A now see when the libraries installed in the PROJECT's own environment differ from the project's Poetry
  lock, and name the pair of versions and the project's install command. A `uv.lock` or `pdm.lock` is `unknown` ("this lock
  format is not read yet"): their markers and forks are not Poetry's, so the factory never claims a difference or a missing
  package from them. New capability `project_dependencies` in `readiness.py` (a difference is `missing`, owner `user`, with the
  command as a human step; an environment the factory cannot read is `unknown`, owner `factory`); new gate A note
  `s5_dependencies`, and the collect card repeats the pair when the collect then fails on a missing library. Gate A checks the
  profiles the story's S5 runs and the doctor the selected ones (a profile with no `selected` key is selected), one check per
  distinct environment, each result naming the profiles it covers. A package locked at several versions differs only when the
  installed version matches none of them; a valid empty list of installed packages is `missing_only`, an empty or unreadable
  answer is `unknown`. `scripts/dependency_drift.py` is the one reader; the lock kinds and the package manager to install command
  table live in `references/project-dependencies.json` (uv installs with `uv sync --locked`). The factory prints the command and
  never runs it, and never starts the project's wrapper (`poetry run`, `uv run`) to find its environment.
- Profiles may record `commands.install` (kind `setup`: no scope, no reporter, no selectors, and no `repo_id` or
  `framework_adapter` under execution schema 1), written by the onboarding profile form from a new interview question. A `setup`
  command is printed, never run, so it never makes a profile unavailable. `gate_rehearsal.skip_dependencies: true` turns the
  gate A note off.
- `project_env.py` publishes the names the dependency check reads (`walk_dirs`, `wrapped_kind`, `manager_env`, `env_key`,
  `inside`, `rel_path`, `base_name`, `overlay`, `executable_folder`, `package_manager`, `test_commands`, `profile_from`,
  `python_target`); `--profile` reads a profile with no `selected` key as selected. `profile_contract.selected_profiles` is the
  one reading of which profiles take part.
- The report heading over the rows of test files that could not be collected now reads "Test files the run could not collect"
  (the project's and the story's); the onboarding role relays `broken_files` of an `ok` launch check to the person.

- The exit gate no longer wakes a role over a check that could not run, and no longer lets one close a stage (`exit_gate.py`,
  `subagent_journal.py`, `log_append.py`, `hooklib.py`, `report_facts.py`): the unreadable records of the S2 register checks
  are named by the file S2 owns, so a crash of them blocks S2 and no other stage; a hook that finds only unreadable checks
  records a `gate_unreadable` signal and an `unreadable` receipt and exits 0 (a mixed set blocks on the author's findings
  only); a crash on the re-entry does the same. An `unreadable` receipt reads as `incomplete` in the `subagent_stop` line,
  and the journal vocabulary knows `hook_signal`. Every hook writes a journal line through one function
  (`hooklib.append_journal_line`). The run report counts a story-less signal only inside the story's own time span and one
  exit-gate note once.

- An exit-gate check that could not run is no longer counted as clean (`detector_verdict.py`, `exit_gate.py`, `story_step.py`,
  `story_run.py`): a detector now has a third state, `unreadable` (exit 3 with a line `UNREADABLE: <reason>`; any exit
  code outside 0, 1 and 3, and exit 1 with nothing printed, read the same way). `s5_precheck.py`, `planning_contract.py`,
  `critic_rollcall.py` and `sizing.py` print it instead of exiting 0 on a crash; a timeout or a detector that did not start
  is `unreadable` too. `story_step finish` refuses with exit 2 and names the check, and the driver raises one refusal for
  the conductor instead of resuming the role over the factory's own defect. Only a person's word that names
  `<script>: unreadable` passes it; `*` and the bare word do not. `sizing.py` is declared an adviser in `stages.json`: its
  crash is a signal, never a block.
- A hook that crashes or has only advice to give no longer says it to nobody (`hooklib.py`, `stage_guard.py`,
  `guard_app_under_test.py`, `validate_artifacts.py`, `guard_pre_tool.py`): one queue (`notice`, `take_notices`) hands advice
  to the model through the host adapter, and `person_signal` writes a `hook_signal` event to the project journal. A crash of
  the stage guard before a verdict allows the call and leaves a `guard_crashed` signal; a crash after a refusal keeps the
  refusal. A validator that could not check a written file now tells the role, with the command to run by hand.
- The run report lists the factory's own signals of the run (`report_facts.py`): their number and kinds, and the journal
  where the whole list is; `none recorded` when there are none, `unknown` with the reason when the journal cannot be read.
- The dispatch hook (`inject_context.py`) no longer lets an unknown pass in silence: a rules file that is missing or cannot be read, and a task packet with no paths, are named in the role's prompt ("work from the prompt and name it under blocked") and left as an `inject` signal; an event that cannot be parsed or a crash of the hook allows the dispatch with an `inject` signal, except an existing `controller.json` that cannot be read as a receipt (not JSON, not an object, a malformed `dispatches` entry or `resolved_model`), which refuses like a missing receipt, before anything else is injected: a role never starts on a model the factory did not choose when the receipt cannot be read (a crash after the receipt was read still allows the dispatch and leaves its signal). Each distinct crash leaves its own signal. The rewritten-input answer is written by one function, `host_adapter.rewrite_output`, which also takes the advice queued on the way; an advice never rides beside `updatedInput` (measured: it does not arrive) but goes to the journal. The headless driver gives a role the same "no paths" line. A signal in a project without the factory marker goes to stderr and never creates `qa-factory/`.
- An empty S5 scope over a plan that cannot be read is refused with the person's-word door `S5 scope: unreadable`, like S6 (`controller.py`); the request builder reads the selected profiles through the one `profile_contract.selected_profiles`.

- the case is the unit of "this case is proven" (`case_stamp.py`, `check_coverage.py`, `check_delivery.py`): the stamp, the
  coverage map and gate B asked the question with three different units - the map counted a pinned case automated when ANY
  one clean instance linked the current version, so one green instance lent its pass to a held sibling; it never read
  `unresolved[]`. Now `case_stamp.case_hold` is the one answer (empty only when EVERY live instance of the case is clean; no
  live instance is `no_automation_evidence`, never a pass), the population of a case and the `unresolved[]` rows are both read
  through `contract.case_matches` (a number written without its area still names the case), the map counts a pinned case only
  when every instance links the pinned version, and gate B asks the same set as before through `case_stamp.held_case_links`
  (the delivery verdict does not change). The map's count can only go down.
- Old maps (`check_coverage.py`, `coverage-map.receipt.json`): a map written before this version may count a case the stamp
  now holds - a case with one held instance beside a clean one, an `unresolved[]` row for it, or an instance that does not
  link the pinned version. The receipt check then refuses the old map ("receipt does not bind the current case facts"); the
  door is `check_coverage.py --write`, which onboarding and the S8 scribe run. It rewrites the project's whole map, so the
  counts of other stories move too.

- The critic's `probe_by_code.py --dispatch` probe asks for the open dispatch before its first byte (`probe_by_code.py`, `_dispatch_context`):
  with no open dispatch the probe now refuses at once (exit 2, `status: refused`) instead of mutating the
  author's test and answering `not_executed` after the rollback. The refusal reads or changes nothing, keeps
  the id the role passed (including a `parent_retry` ancestor id), and names the critic's door: report the probe
  as `cause: tooling`, repeated under `tooling_findings`; the instance stays unverified. An instance already
  proved on its bytes with no open dispatch is refused too (it used to answer `already_probed`); the
  `--s6-close` path is unchanged. In a `probe_debt --settle` loop a refused item is skipped and the loop
  goes on, so nothing is mutated without a dispatch.

- S6 half membership (`controller.py`, `story_step.py`): a case the person took over is refused as handed in BOTH halves, before
  its plan-row class, so the door of that refusal never leads to the other half's refusal of the same case. One cause partition
  serves both halves, and `story_step.py start` splits `--scope` once.
- `prepare` for the automated half with a derived EMPTY half no longer falls back to the whole approved scope: it refuses, saying
  the half is empty and naming the manual block and the plan-row doors.
- The empty-scope check of `validate` for S6 no longer passes when the approved plan cannot be read: the same
  `S6 half membership: unreadable` person's-word door as the membership check.
- The gate A packet names every open rehearsal item that stops approval in ONE line (items with a line door included), with the
  count, so none hides under the "+N more" of the rehearsal summary.

- The S6 automated runner half now meets the same plan-membership check as the manual half (`controller.py`,
  `story_step.py`): an automated packet over a manual-agent case, a case the person took over, or a case in neither half is
  refused on every road (`prepare`, `validate`, `story_step.py start --execution-kind automation --scope ...`, a runner rework)
  with a door per cause, and `start` refuses before it writes anything. One function, `_half_membership_problems`, serves both
  halves; the manual half's sentences are unchanged.
- New refusal for BOTH halves on a plan that cannot be read (a missing or unparsable `work/test-plan.json`): the packet is
  refused with `S6 half membership: unreadable` as the person's-word door, instead of the manual check silently passing.
  A recorded word at S6 under that block passes it.
- The empty-`--cases` refusal of `controller.py --operation rework` at S4 and later now names a door
  (`controller.py --operation stage-scope`), and for an S6 runner says the rework is one half per call.

- The gate A decision no longer records over a question nobody answered (`controller.py`, `gate_brief.py`,
  `story_run.py`): every `person_decides` item that a fresh rehearsal still lists stops `approve`. The refusal keeps the
  person's approval, lists each item with the door that passes it (a line they write, a block a recorded word passes, or
  only `approve as is`) and carries the items as a typed `open_items` key. The raw `decision` road refuses the same way.
- New closed gate A word `approve as is` (`references/gate-approval-words.json`, `passes_open_items`): the controller
  records one waiver per open item with the person's words, never a catch-all block, and then the decision; the answer
  row says "approved as is over: <ids>". It is gate A only; `gate-decision --as-is` is the caller's declaration.
- The driver says whose refusal it is: the conductor is told the approval was heard and kept, and is given a recording
  command per item; the gate asked again over a kept approval lists the items and names `approve as is` instead of
  "the factory's to repair". The gate packet names every item that has no line door in one line.
- Fix round (critic findings): `approve as is` now passes an item that has no door at all (each gets its own
  `gate A item without a door: [<id>] <text>` block at S4, read back by the one reader, so the re-check no longer refuses
  for ever); the as-is words are stored and journalled by `waiver.record_stage_overrides` like any person answer; with
  factory problems and open items together the texts keep the factory's sentences apart and do not offer `approve as is`
  (the refusal carries `item_problems_from`); the gate A phase text passes `--as-is`; one gate decision runs the gate
  rehearsal once (twice with `--as-is`), never inside the store lock.

- `stand_health.py --probe` names the dead part of the stand (`diagnosis.part`: network, api, config, frontend, frontend_proxy,
  unknown) instead of one undivided "does not answer": a dead API is never reported as a frontend problem, and the frontend's
  route to the API is judged only by an answer shown to be the API's own. What each answer means, and the order the parts
  are walked in, are rows of the new `references/stand-answers.json`, read through `env_probe.stand_answers()`; the
  verdict words of `env_probe.liveness` are unchanged. New config keys `environment.frontend {url_key, api_path}` and
  `environments[].frontend {url, api_path}` (empty = an API-only stand); the recorded `bring_up` recipe is shown for the
  conductor and never run. A named stand (`--env`) with its own `frontend` is judged against that stand's API address, and
  a connection closed without an answer or a failed TLS handshake is named as such, never as an unreachable host.
- `login_probe.outcome` (ok|failed|skipped|not_recorded): `env_probe.py --json` emits the ready object as `login.record`
  and onboarding copies it whole; the doctor's login line says "proved" only for `outcome: ok`. A record without
  `outcome` (every config written before this release) reads "not confirmed" with the one re-check command, and the
  config migration never invents the field. `config_contract` validates both new keys.

- one "same test" comparison (`proof_level.py`, `execution_request.py`, `run_history.py`, `acceptance.py`): the question
  "does this carrier still speak for this test" was answered by four copies of the rule; it is now
  `proof_level.compare_identity` (same, different or unknown, and by which sha), asked by `same_test`, by the reuse of a
  run (`same_instance_bytes`), by the red/green pair of `run_history` and by the mechanical-round check of `acceptance`.
  An unknown is never read as the same, except by the flaky-rerun counter, whose safe side is the budget (RH1-9).
- the code sha now decides when the content sha is equal (`proof_level.py`): a change of `case-markers.json` or
  `executable_sha` re-proves every carrier of an affected test (a receipt goes stale and is asked for again at delivery,
  a run reads stale, earlier flaky reruns across the update are not counted); a release doing so says it here (RH1-9).
- `run_history.py`: a contract is taken by the bare function name only when it cannot be another test's: one match, or
  several with equal code and content shas (the parameters of one function); twin classes with different shas find none.
- `acceptance.py`: a bare alias shared by rows of two files no longer names a file for the raw-bytes comparison; the
  exact instance id wins, and an alias names a file only when one row carries it.
- the paths of a test file are compared by `proof_level.same_path` on every OS, the case counts (`acceptance.py`,
  `proof_level.py`): on Windows a manifest path typed in another case than the one on disk no longer matches the job's
  recorded file, so the round asks the critic again instead of trusting a file it may not have compared.
- `check_delivery.py`: the reader of two manifest flags that nothing in the factory wrote is removed; a stale required
  live check is refused as before, through `proof_level.reached`.

## 0.10.3 — 2026-10-27 — speed and cost: the conductor and the roles read less, the S5 plan cuts its windows, validators list every problem at once, a stopped dispatch resumes, manual runner blocks, receipts per function

- New triage verdict `ASSERT_STRICTER` ("the assert asks for more than the requirement does") and the optional triage field `control`
  (the analyst's control experiment: the same action run WITHOUT the change under test; `result` is `effect_without_change`,
  `no_effect_without_change` or `impossible`, with `action`, `without`, `observed`, an `evidence` file under the task's `evidence/` folder, `why` when
  impossible, and an optional `given_gap`). One reader of the block, `contract.triage_control_problems`, serves the validator
  (`validate_artifacts.check_triage_v0`, which now takes the task root from its caller; `artifact_producer.validate` passes its own
  and says in `not_checked` when it has none) and the delivery check. A row with the word and no well-formed experiment is refused by
  the validator and is a `triage:` reason in the delivery check, so the red stays a product failure.
  `contract.evidence_ref_issue` gained `require_hash=False` and `under` so the experiment's evidence reuses the same path rules and
  must lie in `evidence/` (the triage file or the plan, which merely exist under the root, are refused as evidence).
- Delivery: the new kind `assert_stricter` (owner `product`, verdict `after_checks`) in `delivery-verdict-kinds.json`; a
  `failed:ASSERT_STRICTER` ledger row is no longer a `no` but a line in "Left with you" that names the Then, what was observed
  without the change, the requirement, and the two ways out (remove the assert, or refine the requirement). Only the cases whose
  triage row holds the word with a well-formed experiment get the item: a green, handed or differently triaged case on the same
  plan row keeps its own state, and a `failed:ASSERT_STRICTER` row with no such case reads as a plain red (`no`).
  This narrows the P21 invariant "after an observed failure `after_checks` is out of reach without a recorded word of the person":
  `ASSERT_STRICTER` with its control experiment is the one observed failure besides an answered `ENV_ISSUE` that reaches it on the
  analyst's word alone (comment in `check_delivery.assess` and the docstring of `test_third_verdict.k_f1_...` say so).
- Traceability: a red the automator handed over with `unresolved: contradicts_requirement` used to stop the chain
  (`chain_broken`, delivery `no`) whatever the triage word was. When the case's triage row is `ASSERT_STRICTER` with a well-formed
  control experiment, the chain now ends in the failed result (`check_traceability`, the set computed by
  `check_delivery._stricter_cases`, passed by the delivery check and by the `check_traceability.py` command line alike, so the
  line the driver prints and the delivery verdict agree) and the ledger row is the person's line in "Left with you". Any other
  word, and a malformed or missing experiment, leave the gap as it was. The report's traceability table no longer says "bug not
  filed" beside this word (it says there is no bug and the decision is left with the person). The unused
  `check_delivery.traceability_reasons` and its helper `_blocked_only_by_debts` are removed; the two `null-outcomes.json` rows
  that named it as their guard (NE15, NE19) now name `traceability_records`, which holds the same "register has no R rows" reason.
- The word travels in the vocabulary (`handoffs/vocabulary.yaml`, both S7 handoffs, `references/vocabularies.md` and its slices) and in
  the failure analyst's ahead card, with the `control` block in `references/artifact-contract-run.md`.

- S7 now runs a control experiment before it calls a red on an extra or different value an `APP_BUG`. The failure analyst's charter has a
  new rule 2d: first compare the test's data with the case's Given (data weaker than the Given is a `TEST_BUG` of the data, repaired by the
  automator with the Then-lines unchanged); then run the same action without the change under test, on data that answers the Given, save the
  output under `evidence/` and write the `control` block. The effect without the change, with the requirement silent on what the assert asks,
  is `ASSERT_STRICTER`: no repair, no bug draft, no rework, no return to gate A, no rewrite of the case; the person decides in "Left with you".
  A requirement that asks what the assert checks keeps `APP_BUG`; no effect without the change leaves the old rules (2, 2b). Weak data alone is
  a `TEST_BUG` of the data, but the experiment still runs on data that answers the Given: with the effect it is `ASSERT_STRICTER` and the weakness
  goes to `given_gap`. A judge's leaning or decided verdict never replaces the experiment, `case_defect` included. An experiment the
  stand cannot run is named in `control` (`result: impossible`, `why`) and never read as a pass: `ASSERT_STRICTER` is out and the draft says the
  experiment was not run. One assert with differences on both sides of the requirement is `ASSERT_STRICTER` only when every difference is outside it.
- The old defaults are gone from the texts: rule 1 ("ambiguous cases default to `APP_BUG`") now waits for the experiment, rule 2b (`CASE_DEFECT`)
  stands after it ("the default whenever both readings are tenable" is replaced), and the phase text and the S6-to-S7 handoff no longer call a red
  with `contradicts_requirement` "an `APP_BUG` by construction" or forbid `TEST_BUG` for it. `ASSERT_STRICTER` joins the verdict lists of the
  charter and of `phases/s7.md`, and the S5 "contradicts_requirement" row in `design/state-exits.md`; `phases/s7.md` also says a judge's leaning never
  skips the experiment.
- The code critic asks one more question (item 1f, with a new rubric section "An assert stricter than the requirement"): an assert that asks
  more than its Then is a `test_defect`; a Then that asks more than the requirement is a note without a cause, only in `critic-findings.md`
  (never in the form's `findings[]`, which would cost the author a round). The report writer's "Left with you" kinds name an assert stricter
  than its requirement.
- New eval 21 (a scenario for the live run, four tests) and `scripts/tests/test_s7_control_experiment_texts.py` (the key phrases, absent/present/count,
  with negative controls). Size: the analyst's charter grows by 3.5 KB, the rubric by 0.9 KB, the critic's charter by 0.45 KB; dispatch budgets
  (audit A22/A25) stay within their caps.

- `case_stamp.py`, `check_coverage.py`, `check_delivery.py`: the stamp, the coverage map and gate B's lifecycle reasons now read one
  predicate, `case_stamp.instance_hold`. A test the manifest calls green counts as proven only with a green result row of its own in
  `run-report.json`; no row, `skipped`, `partial` or an unknown word holds the case (`not_run`), and a story with no or an unreadable
  run report stamps nothing (`run_report_unreadable` names the unreadable one). `approved_with_fixes` stamps like `approved`. A case
  the stamp cannot take is no lifecycle reason, and a dead `SUPERSEDED DUPLICATE` row neither holds nor stamps a case. When the join
  cannot be built, gate B says so in one reason instead of guessing. The run index now carries the live manifest entries, so the
  legacy join of a 0.10.x story stays alive.

- A changed answer of the person now opens the rework of the plan rows the earlier answer moved (`story_run.py`,
  `planning_contract.py`): the check that drops a rework the role already did judges only a row or case it saw still
  branching on the question when the rework was named, so a row code patched for the first answer is no longer read as
  following the new one; a new answer is compared with the last answer the plan was asked to follow, so an answer changed
  back, or changed after a rework, is reworked too, also when the first answer was given at gate A (its record now names
  the register record it applied); a rework still waiting for an answer the person has since changed is replaced, never
  sent with the old answer, and own words given twice leave one line for the question (HF3-10, H41).

- Retracting a test instance now also takes out the `then_bindings` rows bound to any spelling of the dropped row (its
  canonical id, the case-prefixed id, the bare id, the selector hash) that no remaining row wears (`manifest_put.py`), and `manifest_put` prints them; a fragment that binds a Then to an id it retracts, or that
  patches a retracted instance with no `covers` / `case_version_links` (a ghost row), is refused before the commit, and
  `s5_precheck` names such a ghost in an older projection as `ghost-<id>`: the ghost used to hide the `unlinked-` mark of
  the Thens still bound to a test that was gone (TP2-2406, seq 115 and 117).

- A stale live check is proved again in the code close of S6 with no dispatch open (`probe_by_code.py --s6-close`,
  `execution_request.s6_close_dispatch`): the context is allowed exactly when the controller would take the S6
  code-only receipt (`controller.code_close_conflicts`, one predicate), only for a red probe, and refused before
  anything is read or mutated otherwise (hotfix-12586/3 HF3-6).

- S6 proves a stale live check again in its code close even when no dispatch is open (`story_run.py` `s6_reprove`): the line
  `re-probe skipped: no open S6 dispatch` is gone, and the S6 code-only receipt names each probe record it stands on
  (hotfix-12586/3 HF3-6).

- A run result word outside the result vocabulary (`ledger.py`, `contract.py`, `delivery_summary.py`): `expected_product_failure`,
  which no runner writes and the run-report validator refuses, and any other made-up word now read as not executed in the
  ledger's test and plan rows ("the run recorded <word>"), as the trace already read it; the summary no longer counts it as
  an executed test. It never reads `failed` in one table and `not run` in the other, and never `passed_green`. A case with
  a pass and such a word on two instances is no longer folded into `partial` by `contract.rollup_status`; a failed or
  error instance beside it still wins.

- The S2 requirements tester reads the implementation diff through `diff_pass.py`, every changed line of every hunk, and its brief names the register and understanding templates; the scout collects a merge request with `vcs_evidence.py` into the driver's own path and writes any other CLI output to a file; the brief names the context bundle's line view when it is current; a project document a role is no longer injected is named in its brief (at the path the project's `strategy_documents` gives it, as the injection does) and never trimmed away; the scout's card carries `--summary` in the command forms of `peek`, `assess`, `collect` and `inspect`, and the failure analyst's and the doc scribe's cards carry `bug_snapshot.py` and `report_facts.py` (SC1-10).

- `ticket_adapter.py collect|peek|assess|inspect --summary` prints the changed record (with the `assessment_ref` the next `assess` needs) and the inventory's path, size and counts in one line; `--json` keeps its shape. The scout's S1 commands use it (SC1-10).

- `grounding_section.py --show <id> | --requirement R-n` (new): prints one part of `work/grounding.yaml` by its id with its line
  numbers, read through the table's one reader and the new `planning_contract.grounding_item_lines`; nothing is written. The lines
  are the file's own bytes, so a section read here is what an `Edit` can match; an id the table does not have is refused whole.

- The 30 KB read guard answers a whole `Read` of `work/grounding.yaml` or `work/test-plan.json` with the map of its sections (`id: lines`), so a role
  reads the one section it needs with `offset`/`limit` instead of guessing windows; the files are named by `read_by_section` in
  `references/artifact-writers.json`, and a role with a shell is also named `plan_row.py --show` / `grounding_section.py`. A map that cannot be
  checked against the file is left out: the refusal keeps its old text.
- Fix: the guard's exemptions from the whole-read limit are exact places, no longer substrings of the path. `config.json` in a path exempted every
  file so named (the project's 50 KB config among them, and any project's `tsconfig.json`) and `templates/` exempted a product's own templates
  folder; now only the plugin's `references/` (templates included), the project's `.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and readiness report, and a
  story's `pipeline.json` and `work/requirements-readiness.json` are read whole. A big project config is refused with a door: `Grep -n` and a range
  read, and `config_view.py --keys` once that script exists; a small one is never refused.
- Fix: the plugin's own `skills/` folder stays readable whole, installed or loaded with `--plugin-dir` (the phase and onboarding files that
  SKILL.md says to read in full are 30-50 KB); a `skills/` folder of a product is not exempt. The exemptions of the read guard are asked of
  the package's one containment predicate (`runtime_paths.contained`), and an artifact root that cannot be resolved leaves the size rule
  in force. The guard's two reads of `artifact-writers.json` go through `load_ref_json`; with no usable registry the write-owner check keeps
  its built-in floor, as before.

- `plan_row.py --show` takes several `--row` (each row printed with its line numbers, the file's own lines); `plan_row.py --map` and
  `grounding_section.py --map` print the map of the file's sections (`id first-last`, the key ranges first), from one new function
  (`artifact_sections.section_map_text`) that returns no map rather than a wrong one; `plan_row.py --put-row <json|file>` replaces one
  whole row after the plan check, never over bytes it did not read, with every other byte of the file as it was.
- Fix: a plan row's bytes are found by parsing, not by looking for its `"id"` text. A row whose `id` follows a nested object, and a
  row whose id an earlier row's nested object also carries, were matched to the nested object, so `--set` wrote over it.

- S1's context bundle gets a line view next to its JSON (`context_bundle.py`, `work/context-bundle.lines.md`): one line per fact, source and candidate, project-relative paths (a path that cannot be made relative points at the JSON field), every other key, down to the keys inside an item, named in a "not shown here" line, and the sha256 of the JSON bytes it describes; the JSON stays the record. `context_bundle.py` prints the view's path as `view` (null when it could not be written, the JSON is complete either way) and `--validate` reports whether the view is `current`, `stale` or `absent` and writes nothing (SC1-9).

- Roles are injected only the common rules they act on (`references/common-rules.md`, `inject-map.json`): `common-rules.md` is sliced
  per role like the other references and is no longer in the `common` list; the layer every role gets alike drops from 16.5 KB to
  10.7 KB (the A22 info line, `contract_slices.common_layer`), and every role keeps at least 3 KB of headroom under the A22 cap.

- **Every claim on a form is checked or gone** (SC1-2, B-023, FR-18; `handoff_check.py`, the handoff contracts): three claims
  got a verifier that stays silent on what it cannot measure - `size_computed_by_sizing_py_not_quoted` (the form's
  `size.computed` against `work/sizing.json`), `the_verdict_was_computed_by_rollcall_not_typed` (the form's outcome and
  `review.rollcall` against `critic_rollcall.derive` over the findings file; an approving outcome over a case without a review is
  false) and `every_instance_carries_a_fingerprint_or_says_never_run` (a row that says it ran has its receipt on disk, a
  relative file inside the story). A verifier that cannot measure - no sizing file, no roll-call rows, a template row, an
  exception - gives no verdict and never `true`. Five claims that nothing read are removed from their contracts (S1
  `every_retrieved_attachment_has_an_inspection_receipt`, S2 `every_requirement_names_its_source_and_revision`, S3
  `every_row_carries_a_coverage_contract_revision`, S6 `every_rerun_names_the_fingerprint_that_moved`, S9
  `the_numbers_were_computed_by_code_and_not_recomputed_by_the_role`); a form begun before still holds the line and is accepted
  as it is. `--fix` fills a claim code can prove: an empty claim whose verifier answers yes is written `true` and recorded in
  `derived`; one the verifier measures false stays open and says what was measured; one it cannot measure stays open with the
  reason; a role's own `false` is never overwritten, and the judge is never asked for a claim. `review.rollcall` is now filled by
  code from the roll-call table, and an empty roll-call writes no `0 of 0 reviewed`.

- The conductor reads a config key and a stage card instead of whole files (`config_view.py`, `story_step.py card`):
  `config_view.py --keys [PREFIX]` lists the children of a config node with type and size and `--get PATH` prints one
  value (a JSON pointer `/a/b` is for a key that holds a dot; Git Bash on Windows rewrites a leading `/`, so there the command
  runs with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`, and a path that arrived rewritten is refused with that door; a container
  over 6000 bytes is answered with its keys and the narrower path to ask for; an absent key is an answer
  that says what absence means, never `null`; an unreadable config is exit 4, never an empty one); `story_step.py card
  --stage S<n>` prints the `## Card` section of the stage's phase file, the values of the config keys the card names and
  the index of every other section as a ready `Read <path> offset=<a> limit=<b>`, and a stage with no card yet names its
  phase file whole. TP1-12586: the 52 KB config and 76 KB of phase files were resident in the conductor's context for
  the whole run, about 6 million token-reads (speed-cost SC1-8).
- `controller.py --brief` answers a `rework` or `checkpoint` result over 1500 bytes with a summary (`controller.py`; the full
  result is written by `event_store.atomic_json`, and `event_store.atomic_text` is its text twin that `config_view.py` uses):
  the keys the conductor acts on (`error`, `problems`, `recorded`, `dispatched`, `next_action`, `next`, `window`, `action`,
  `stage`, `dispatch_id`) whole, every other field as a count or a short value, and a last line naming
  `state/output/controller-<operation>.json`, which holds the whole result (when it cannot be written the whole answer is
  printed and a line on stderr says why). Every other operation prints whole with or without the flag, and without the flag
  the answer is byte for byte what it was. The ready `rework` / `checkpoint` commands the controller prints end with `--brief`.
  `story_step.py where` ends with `stage card: story_step.py card --stage <stage>`. TP1-12586: 33 controller calls put
  157 thousand characters into the conductor's context, `--operation rework` alone 110 thousand (speed-cost SC1-8).

- **The form lists its own allowed values** (SC1-2, RC1-9 (a), the owner's word 26.10.2026: variant (i);
  `handoff_init.py`): every `<one of vocabulary.X>` placeholder of a new form reads `<one of vocabulary.X - a|b|c>`, the words
  taken from the vocabulary through `handoff.allowed` (a row's `state` carries the words of the role that fills it, the list a
  refusal prints). A hand-written list in a contract is replaced in the form by the vocabulary's, a tail such as `, or a dash
  when ...` and the line's comment stay, and an empty or unreadable list is written `NONE READABLE`. The check still reads the
  contract's own placeholders, so no verdict moves; a form begun on 0.10.2 is checked as before. The `state` of the two critic
  contracts (S4 case critic, S5 code critic) was `<one of the above>` and now names `vocabulary.row_states` like every other
  row. A comment line at the head of the form tells the role how it is filled: `path: value` lines in one Write of
  `<dispatch>.values.yaml`, plus the stdin call for a role with a shell.
- **A form started again never meets the values file of the attempt before** (SC1-2, `handoff_init.py`): a
  `<dispatch>.values.yaml` that is waiting when `handoff_init` writes a form (a new one, or `--force`) is moved to
  `<dispatch>.values.stale.yaml` first, and nothing applies it; the form that is already there (no `--force`) keeps its file.
  When the file cannot be moved it is deleted, and when it cannot be deleted the form is still written and the output says in
  one line that the old words will meet it. The handover section of `common-rules.md` and `handoffs.md` now teach the one-call
  fill instead of `--set` field by field.

- **What a role wrote in its values file counts before it is applied** (SC1-2, B-1; `handoff_check.py`): a halt, a `blocked`
  and a critic's findings that a role wrote only in `<dispatch>.values.yaml` are read by `story_step finish`, the driver, the
  conductor's help and the repair route as if the file had already been applied. `handoff_check.form_view` is the one reader:
  the form plus its waiting file merged in memory, exactly as the next writing `handoff_check` run will record them (the later
  word of the role wins), writing nothing. A missing, empty or unparseable waiting file, a contract that cannot be read, or any
  failure on the values side gives the form as it lies on disk; an unparseable file is refused by `--fix` with its line number, so
  the form does not pass `finish` over it. The conductor is also shown the waiting file beside the form, and a cut-off role's
  outputs list it. `handoff_help.py` now reads the form as UTF-8 with BOM, a byte that is not UTF-8 no longer stops it with a trace.

- **One refusal, one command** (SC1-2, RC1-11; `handoff_check.py`): a handover form that is not ready is refused in ONE block
  with ONE ready command instead of a `--set` command under every problem. The command is a skeleton of `path: value` lines:
  the allowed values inline (`header.verdict: <concerns|halt|impossible|ok>`, a role's `state` words only), a line for every
  path to fill (a form with no rows gets every field of its first row), and a line for the door of a problem that lives on
  another path (a `blocked` row names `blocked.problem`); a placeholder left as it is writes nothing. A role with a shell sees
  the `--fix --values - <<'EOF'` command and, always beside it, the door of the values file (it works in any shell and in none);
  a role without a shell sees the file door alone, and `blocked.field` / `blocked.problem` in the same file; a role not named
  sees both. When a values text is refused, the lines of the role that were good come back in the skeleton, so it rewrites the
  file whole and loses nothing. `refusal_text` is the one builder of this text and `values_report` is the same check for a
  values text not yet written (it writes nothing, never asks the judge, and leaves out a blank field that `--fix` fills itself,
  so a role that cannot produce it is not refused for it). `--json` gains `values_skeleton` and, per problem, `kind` and `also`.

- **A handover form is filled in one call** (SC1-2, RC1-11; `handoff_check.py`): `--values <file|->` takes every field of
  the role at once, as `path: value` lines (or one flat JSON object) with the paths the refusal prints; `-` reads stdin, so a
  role with a shell needs no file at all. A path with the next row index (`scope[1].id` on a one-row form) opens that row from
  the CONTRACT's own row, and `open_questions[0].readings[1]` opens inside its parent; a hole (`scope[3]` with two rows) is one
  problem and opens nothing. An unknown path is one problem with the closest known path beside the values that were applied
  (it used to stop `--set` with exit 2 and lose the rest; `--set` of an unknown path is exit 1 now). A `<dispatch>.values.yaml`
  beside the form is applied once by the next writing run (`--fix`, `--set`, `--values`) and renamed
  `<dispatch>.values.applied.yaml`; a read-only run shows the merged form and writes nothing. The order is the waiting file,
  then `--values`, then `--set`; a line that does not parse applies nothing and is named by file and line; a placeholder
  left in a values file is not a word and is not written; `--set` keeps its raw meaning. `--json` only gains `values_applied`,
  `values_pending` and `values_notes`. The measurement behind it (12586, 0.10.2): 138 form-filling calls by five roles
  (strategist 73, scout 20, designer 18, tester 16, case critic 11), an estimated 18 percent of the cache reads of the story's
  requests; the aim is at most two calls a dispatch, proved by the repeat run SC1-13.

- `stage_done --status running` no longer re-renders the dashboard and metrics (`stage_done.py`): every dispatch paid that twice on its launch path (measured about 57 s on a story copy); the transition is written as before and the view catches up at the story's next event, with `state/dashboard-deferred.json` saying so meanwhile. The refusal for `--status done` over a stage the controller has not accepted now names `story_step.py finish` with the stage's dispatch id instead of a hand-built accept request (SC1-12).
- The package fingerprint is computed once per process while the package files are unchanged (`runtime_paths.py`), and the gate rehearsal collects through the same runner as S5, with its `-qq` and tree retries, so a project whose own `addopts` carry `-q` or `-v` gets the same node ids in both (`gate_preflight.py`, `node_ids.py`; EP1-11, C3-26) (SC1-12).

- S5 starts with one automation plan for every case (`s5_plan.py`, `work/s5-plan.json`): `--init` writes the skeleton (cases,
  the S3 row, the Then clauses), `--mode` says whether a story's S5 is `planned` or `legacy`; the form is fixed by the
  first S5 dispatch and never switches silently. The plan's words live in `handoffs/vocabulary.yaml` (`test_shapes`,
  `fit_to_shapes`, `plan_verdicts`, `plan_remark_kinds`, `plan_remark_rows`, `data_strategies`, `plan_deviation_kinds`);
  `manifest_from_tests.py` reads its shapes from there. `controller.s5_part_of` tells a plan dispatch from a window dispatch
  (`purpose: s5_plan`).

- `s5_plan.py --check` names every gap of the S5 plan at once (cases and Then clauses, shape and level against the S3 row, the
  existing test an `extend` builds on, the 300-character limits, a test across two written windows); a window gets its plan slice
  (`--window N`, `--out FILE`) and the critic's remarks, read from the one chain of plan reviews (`reviews`, `remarks_of`).

- Two new S5 handovers: the automator's plan to the code critic and the plan review back (`s5-automator-plan-to-critic`,
  `s5-critic-plan-to-automator`; an index row may name the dispatch `purpose` it serves, and `handoff.contract_of` returns it only
  for that purpose); the window form gains the optional sections `plan_remarks` and `deviations`, so a window started on the
  previous release still passes the check; the plan file `work/s5-plan.json` is a declared S5 output with the automator as its writer.

- An S5 plan dispatch never counts as a window: it does not close S5, spend a window's repair rounds, or stand in for a window's reviewer.

- S5 windows start only after the plan review; a plan review never closes S5; every refusal names its door and a person's word passes it.

`s5_precheck.py` checks a window against its plan: tests, Thens, files, shapes, counts, a row per plan remark and a declared reason for every deviation. The plan dispatch has no manifest: its detector is the plan's own check.

- The exit gate files every digest it passes under its dispatch (`work/digests/<id>.txt`) and mends four form defects itself - prose before
  the header, a missing path (the stage's artifact), a reason over 80 characters, an absolute path under the task root - keeping the role's text
  beside it; `story_step.py finish --digest -` takes the filed digest. Anything else in the form is still refused as before.

- The S5 plan dispatch is started and finished by `story_step` like any other: its skeleton, its review stamp, and the next command; a
  resumed role reads only its delta.

S5 texts follow the one-plan form: the stage page leads with the plan dispatch, its review, the narrow rework and the windows that follow the plan; the automator's charter gains the plan dispatch and "a window follows its plan" (`plan_remarks`, `deviations`); the code critic's charter and the review rubric split into "On the plan", "On the code" and "Conformance to the plan". The judge line for the failure analyst, the red-on-purpose sentence and the oracle refusal no longer promise a bug draft for a test left red on purpose: S7 decides what each one is.

- **A plan rework for cases added after the plan review now reaches the plan; a resumed card names its brief once; a refused digest leaves no earlier file** (SC1-14 fix round; `story_step.py`, `exit_gate.py`, `controller.py`, `qa-automator.md`): `story_step materialize` of the rework of the S5 plan refreshes `work/s5-plan.json` (the author's rows stay, the new cases get skeleton rows, both hashes become current), so the window gate no longer refuses for ever; a repeat `materialize` changes no byte of the plan, and a refused one writes none. A resumed role's card no longer repeats "Read the brief first" after its resumed line, and an agent id that `bind` set on the dispatch record is not read as a resume. The plan critic's card is no longer handed the code judge's output or the probe-debt note. A digest the exit gate refuses removes the digest file an earlier stop of the same dispatch left, so `finish --digest -` reads the role's last word; the digest path has one spelling (`exit_gate.digest_path`). Every ready S5 plan / window rework command the controller prints ends with `--brief`. The automator charter tells the role to tag each planned test with `qa(shape=<the planned shape>)`.

- The S5 plan no longer records a window per case: a window's slice is read from the controller's cut and says when the window is
  over its cap or grew; a plan rework after new cases keeps the author's plan and refreshes its hashes; the test report names every
  window that went over its cap.

- After the plan review, S5 windows follow the plan: the cases one test covers are one window, kept whole even over the window cap
  (`over_cap`); a window is its author's chain, it is never cut again, and a case whose test reaches it joins it (`grown`).

- A case added to S5 after the plan review whose test reaches a window already written sends that window back to its author and critic with the new case; S5 does not close before both have covered it, and a plan look must cover every row the rework moved.

- An S5 window brief carries its plan slice, the critic's remarks for its cases, and the code it will touch in a side file; the plan
  dispatch's brief names the plan (or its parts when it is over the read cap) and the plan's exit check; a resumed role reads only the
  delta.

- Question-branch checks name every finding in one round (`planning_contract.py`): a variant that breaks the plan
  contract lists all of its contract errors, not the first two, and a malformed key no longer hides the rest of its
  branch. When a variant replaces `coverage_obligations` under other ids than the row's `coverage_delta` maps, the
  finding adds the way out (keep the ids the delta maps), because `coverage_delta` is not a patch key; when a variant
  sets `oracle_unknown: true` on a row that does not carry `design_review_required: true`, the finding says that
  field is not patchable and is set on the row itself. TP1-12586 spent six S3 repair rounds on two plan rows,
  two fields at a time (speed-cost SC1-1).

- S3 remarks travel as one package and are repaired by a fresh dispatch (`stage_done.py`, `story_step.py`, `contract.py`,
  `references/stages.json`, `phases/s3.md`): the S3 exit writes every question-branch finding to one file under
  `state/findings/` (a long finding wraps, none is cut), prints one short `S3 remarks:` line with one rework command whose
  `--reason` names that file and narrows the dispatch to it, and the stage's new `rework_mode` (`fresh` for S3: a new agent;
  `resume` for S5: SendMessage with the delta) says how the card is launched, read by one function, `contract.rework_mode`;
  `finish` keeps the remarks line whatever follows it, and a handover form refusal lists every problem, not the first four.
  TP1-12586: 6 rounds, 15 messages into a 486k session, 55.1M cache-read tokens (speed-cost SC1-1).

- Telemetry maintenance (`telemetry_capture.py`): the pass over `state/telemetry/` skips a raw file whose size and
  modification time are unchanged since its aggregate was written, instead of re-reading and re-writing every
  aggregate on each cost capture (TP1-12586: 1750 per-process files, about 5 s a wave every 40 s). The pass is
  `maintain_dir`, meant for Stop only; closed per-process `hook-<pid>.jsonl` files are merged into one
  `hook-merged-<UTC date>.jsonl` per day, each line kept once (by `event_id`), under one lock that the collect pack
  shares. The Stop-time pass no longer rotates a file by size, so no `.closed` file appears and no span leaves the
  count. The pass now runs from the Stop capture and from every SubagentStop capture (also one skipped by the 30 s
  window or deferred because another capture holds the cost lock), after the dashboard refresh and with the cost lock
  free, instead of inside every capture; a dashboard refresh that fails no longer skips it. The "Recorded metric
  signals" notice is no longer printed after each Write or Edit (the signals stay in `metric-signals.json`, on the
  dashboard and at the Stop). The collect pack's telemetry sum takes the merge lock (waiting up to 30 s), counts each
  span event and each unreadable line once across all files, reads regular files only (never a symlink), and reports
  `merge_lock` (`held`, `busy`, `unavailable` when the lock could not be made at all, or `none`) and `vanished_files`.
  The pack's `B8` `files` and `bytes` now count only the span files that were read (`*.jsonl` and `*.jsonl.merging`),
  no longer the aggregates, `.closed` files or markers of the folder. The other summaries of the pack (`dir_stats`,
  `host_receipts`, `artifacts_summary`) name a file that vanished while they ran in `vanished_files`, instead of failing.

- the command reader reads a text once per shell dialect in a hook process (`hooklib.py`): `walk` (the stage guard's delivery,
  commit and runner shapes) and `command_segments` (the read guard) now share one cached read of each (text, dialect),
  up to 32 pairs; the cache changes the price of a hook call, never a verdict. The Units it hands out are tuples all the way
  down, so one reader cannot change what another sees, and a failed read is never cached, so a command the reader
  could not read is refused again on every call. `command_segments` still returns fresh lists on every call (SC1-5b)

- launcher (`hooks/run-py.cmd`, `scripts/run_py_entry.py`): on Windows the launcher remembers the base Python interpreter in
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\qa-factory\python-path.txt` instead of searching PATH (three `where` calls, about a second) on every hook call.
  The first call that finds an interpreter by search writes the file, silently and atomically; later calls start that path
  directly. The file is a hint: a missing, empty or garbage file, or a path that no longer exists, falls back to the search,
  and a cached interpreter that exists but cannot start is probed once, the file is deleted and the call repeats through the
  search. A venv interpreter is never remembered. The door: delete the file, or set `QA_FACTORY_PYTHON` (the cache is then
  neither read nor written). Nothing is added to a hook's stdout. The POSIX half is unchanged.

- **The turn-budget notice no longer throws the call away** (SC1-6; `guard_pre_tool.py`, `turn_budget.py`, `host_adapter.py`):
  the TURN BUDGET used to be a blocked call - the host discarded the call and the role repeated it, 14 times in run 12586, each
  repeat a request over a 200-480K-token context, while the refusal footer said "do NOT try the same call again" and the notice
  itself said to make it again. The guard now counts first as before but never exits on it: the call runs, and the notice travels
  beside it in the PreToolUse `additionalContext` (`host_adapter.notice_output`, the one place that knows the host's shape; no
  `permissionDecision`, so it never approves a call). Measured on `claude` 2.1.310 in a throwaway project: `additionalContext`
  of PreToolUse and PostToolUse reaches the model, a PreToolUse stderr at exit 0 and a bare PostToolUse stdout do not - so the
  scout's notice, which used to go to stderr, is told for the first time. When another rule refuses the same call, its refusal
  and its door keep their own words and the notice follows on stderr marked "(Not part of the refusal above.)". The notice now
  ends "This is a notice, not a refusal: the turn budget stops no call." - a tail that is true on both exits
  (after another rule's refusal a call WAS stopped, by that rule). The config's `turns_note` and the onboarding page no longer
  say "the same call again proceeds"; the previous text stays in the note's history, so a project holding it is settled to the
  new one without anything moving to `answers_legacy`. The `PT-turn-budget` row is gone from the refusal registry (it refuses
  nothing); `turns.soft` and `turns.repeat` keep their meaning and their reader.

- Refusals name the command that repairs them (`controller.py`, `artifact_producer.py`, `ticket_adapter.py`, `context_bundle.py`): run 12586 lost 27 scout and 19 tester results to refusals that named neither the field nor the command; an operation that reads `--input` and gets none (every APPLY operation but `checkpoint`, `reopen_story` and `leave_unlaunched`, and `baseline-inputs`) no longer prints a traceback, an accept without an `idempotency_key`, with a `dispatch_id` for `id`, with a wrong `status` or with `unresolved` and no `reason` names the field and the command that writes the request whole (the accept door names the running and the returned dispatches), a batch item without "data" names the key, a usage line is followed by a ready command with the call's own values (and the ready line of `freshness --decline` and `accept-gap --point` carries the flags the parser then requires), and a manifest record without `source_sha`, or a manifest with no `implementations` at all, is named at `context-manifest.json implementations` (SC1-7).
- An S1 accept over a source gap names the person's `ticket_adapter.py accept-gap` and a plain `story_step.py finish` as the way on, lists pending sources with the unavailable ones, and no longer advertises passing `unresolved` and `reason` by hand (SC1-7).
- The scout's, the requirements tester's, the failure analyst's and the bug reporter's brief cards carry the full command forms (`brief_pack.py`, `role-commands.json`): `peek`/`collect` need --output, the bundle is built with --manifest/--output/--root (a relative path in the manifest resolves against --root), and a producer batch is {"artifacts": [{kind, path, data}]}; the requirements tester is a role of `validate-batch` and `publish` in the registry; argument errors of `artifact_producer.py` and `context_bundle.py` now end in the role refusal with the card (`role_cli.RefusingParser`) (SC1-7).

- Every stage but S5 opens with a stage card the conductor prints instead of reading the phase file whole: each of
  `phases/s0.md`..`s9.md` (S5 follows with its rewrite) gains a `## Card` section of at most 4000 bytes (the input, the
  commands before the dispatch and the role's three `story_step.py` commands, the `config:` keys the stage reads, the
  halts, the exit and `story_step.py card --stage S<n+1>`), and the "read phases/s<n+1>.md" lines at the exits now print
  the next card. `test_stage_cards.py` holds the size, that every card command is spelled in the body of the same file,
  that a card carries no dispatch template, and that its config keys parse. The scout's dispatch template adds
  `--summary` to `peek`, `assess` and `inspect`, and the hand-written controller accept texts of S1, S2 and S8 name
  the `story_step.py finish` door a refused accept prints. TP1-12586: the phase files of S0, S1 and S4 (76 KB) sat in
  the conductor's context for the whole run, about 3.3 million token-reads (speed-cost SC1-8).

- **A role without a shell fills its form in one Write; an Edit of a form whose values file waits is refused** (SC1-2, RC1-11;
  `guard_pre_tool.py`): the one Write of `<dispatch>.values.yaml` is proved against the handover form before it lands. The
  values are merged into the form in memory and checked without the judge; a file that leaves the form not ready is refused in
  ONE block - the same text `handoff_check.py` prints - carrying the role's good lines back verbatim and the lines to fix, so the
  role rewrites the file whole and loses nothing. A green file lands; so does a file that fills `blocked.problem` (a role that
  cannot fill a field says so, and is never a dead end); a blank field that `--fix` fills itself (a findings file, a case
  version) is not asked for, and neither is anything when no form lies beside the file or the check fails - `story_step finish`
  and the driver check again. A Write over an existing form now names the values file as its first door (no `--set` per field).
  An `Edit` of a form while its values file waits is refused, because the file is applied over the form at the next check and the
  edit would be lost: the field goes into the values file, and a role with Bash may apply the file first with `--fix` and then
  Edit. `<dispatch>.values.applied.yaml` and `<dispatch>.values.stale.yaml` are code's traces: a Write of either is refused and
  names the file the role means. Only the exact suffix `.values.yaml` is the role's file. Four rows of the refusal registry
  (A24): the rewrite row and three new ones.

- Adding a test function to a file no longer changes the per-test identity of the other tests in it, and the label "the receipt holds over a comment-only change" is no longer shown when the change was another test: the receipt is shown as current outright, or "the test's code is the same as when it was proven". Any other module-level change still counts for every test of the file. A live check that went stale in a later window (TP1-14857, FB-10: four receipts of window 1 were read "for other bytes and other code" after window 2 changed the same file, and their re-probe was refused as outside the critic's scope) is now re-probed by that window's code critic: `probe_debt.py --settle` and `probe_by_code.py` admit it outside the dispatch's scope; its review is not re-checked by this.

- A `local_login` stand whose endpoint expects `email` instead of `username` no longer reads as "environment missing (HTTP 422)": when `environment.access.user_field` / `secret_field` are empty, the login probe tries the field pairs of `references/login-body-fields.json` in order (`username`/`password`, then `email`/`password`), moving on only when a 400/422 answer asks for a body field that was not sent, and reports the pair the endpoint accepted; onboarding records that pair in `environment.access` and in `login_probe`. An answer that judges the account (a wrong password or a throttle naming a field that was sent) is never retried and keeps its old report. When every pair is refused for its shape, readiness reports `environment` with `gap_id: login-field-unknown`, owner `factory`, and the one-line fix first; the onboarding phase no longer files a refused body shape as a stand problem. The manual capture's HTTP login reads the same field names through the same attempt loop instead of its own `email` default, and refuses field names the probe refuses; a project recipe with its own `body` is sent as written (TP1-14857, FB-3/FB-5).

- A dispatch stopped for a person (the S1 source review: `checkpoint --status blocked`) and continued by its own agent is running again: `story_step.py resume --task <T> --dispatch-id <ID>` replaces the `stage_done --status running` step of the S1 phase and records the resume on the same dispatch, and the driver calls it by itself before it resumes a stopped role's session, so `finish` accepts the work and `pause` can stop it again; until now the dispatch stayed `blocked`, `finish` was refused with "a stopped dispatch is not accepted where it stands", and the only way on was a retry dispatch that superseded the scout (TP1-14857, FB-4). The refusal of an accept on a stopped dispatch now names the resume first when its agent is recorded, and `next` carries `resume_command` on a `resume_checkpoint` action in that case. A second stop or return of a resumed dispatch is journaled as its own event instead of being answered with the first one.

- The runtime probe no longer calls a stand stale because of a build file the image never ships (`runtime_probe.py`,
  `references/build-identity-methods.json` `non_runtime_files`, config `execution.non_runtime_files`): files such as
  `Makefile`, `Dockerfile` or `.gitignore` are data rows; absent from the container they are recorded and not compared,
  and the stage-entry line names them; present and different they are still compared. A project adds names with `also`
  and keeps its own app files compared with `except` (TP1-14857 FB-8).
- The gate A container pick no longer drops the right container for lacking a file the image never ships, and asks no
  container question when the story's only compared files are of that kind.

- A content mismatch has a person's door (`stand_identity.py confirm --content`, the build question's `test as is`): the
  word binds to this story's commit, the exact bytes the check saw and the image, any change voids it, and the report and
  the manual evidence say the tests ran by the person's decision (FB-8).

- `story_step.py start --stage S6 --role qa-runner --execution-kind manual --scope <ids>` registers a manual runner block the way the driver does: it prepares each case with `manual_evidence.py prepare` (one shared function on both roads; a case that cannot be checked by hand is named with its reason and left out of the next block's command), and sends the block's cases to the controller as `manual_case_ids` (equal to the scope, `purpose: manual`), so the skill road no longer needs a hand-built controller request and `materialize` (TP1-14857, FB-9). The block rule (1..5 unique cases) is on the S6 card and in `start --help`; a refused block lists every problem in one answer, each with its door, and a block over five, or `start` without `--scope`, prints the ready command of the next block. The controller now refuses a manual block that names an automated case, a case handed to the person, or a case outside the plan's manual half, on every road. A rework of an S6 runner takes its half from its cases' disposition and carries the block, so it is no longer refused for a missing execution kind. The S6 card names `--execution-kind` for both halves; each dispatch but the last S6 dispatch of the stage is finished with `--not-complete`.

- The price of a story run from inside a doctor session is whole again. A story activity closed at the end of a response used to hand every later turn back to the doctor activity it was started over, so the rest of the story (TP1-14857: S5 to S9, about half its spend) was priced as the doctor's and the story card and the retro showed $13.86 instead of about $27.8. The cost capture now gives the turns after such a stop to the story, as it already did for a story started on its own, and the turn between two entries of the same story belongs to that story. A price whose session holds money after the story began that may be the story's but is bound to another activity (a doctor or onboarding activity that was never closed, or a doctor run again after the story's stop) is now "incomplete" and names that money; for a cost file captured before this release the price names `cost_capture.py --recapture --session <id>`, which re-reads it.

- The scout learns the discovery fields before the work, and one refusal lists every problem (`context_bundle.py`,
  `validate_artifacts.py`, `ahead-cards.json`, `qa-scout.md`): the v2 discovery records of the context manifest are checked from
  one carrier (`V2_REQUIRED`), every problem is listed in one refusal with its record position (`coverage_search[1].status`), the
  manifest's write hook and the S1 exit gate name the same problems in the turn that wrote them, the scout's card names the
  coverage_search and existing_test_candidates fields, and "nothing found" is the top-level `coverage_status: not_found`, no longer
  a per-area status the validator refused (t-1347).

- One refusal lists every problem at the remaining first-error sites (`execution_fingerprint.py`, `estimate_record.py`, `manual_evidence.py`): a fingerprint specification missing two keys or holding two bad files names all of them, each file by its list and position; an estimate facts file names every wrong key before anything is written; a manual block names each refused record by `records[i]` and no longer folds equal problems of different records into one line.
- A refused value is told its closed list (`record_schema.py`, `artifact_producer.py`, `planning_contract.py`, `manual_evidence.py`): "unsupported value", an invalid bug status or severity, case status or channel, verification depth and starter levels now print the values they accept; the failure analyst's card names `instance_id` and `attempt_id`, the retro analyst's card names the facts file's keys, and the runner's charter names the five keys of the fingerprint specification.

- A test holds the validator class (`tests/test_validator_class.py`): every role-facing validator in it must list two defects
  of one input in one answer, each with its record position, and every role command and role-written artifact must name where
  the role learns its fields before the work; a validator that stops at the first problem, or a field list the role is never shown,
  fails the build.

## 0.10.2 — 2026-10-26 — the TP1-12586 S5 runs without the person's words: a red test is an ordinary S5 outcome, a Then is the unit of outcome, the person's answers apply at once, one collect, S5 off the cost hot path

- The question store learns three things the next parts of the "answers apply at once" fix build on (HF2-7, part 1).
  A person can keep a question open until the report: the token `Q3: until the report` (or `question_register.py --defer Q3 ...`)
  records the new status `deferred_to_report`; it is not asked again, it is not settled, and `--reopen` puts it back.
  A different answer to a question that is already settled (a new letter, or `not needed` after a letter) is refused with the
  door that works - reopen it first - instead of silently becoming the last record while the plan keeps following the first;
  the same answer again, and an answer to a question whose row changed since, are written as before. One module now says
  what "settled", "open" and "an open blocker" mean (`settled`, `is_open`, `open_blocker`, `answer_key`), always reading an
  unknown status, a missing severity or an unreadable answers file as open; `where_words` gives each `where` value the words a
  person reads. At the S2 exit the readiness verdict is checked against the answers: `blocked` with every blocker answered,
  not needed or kept open is refused with the way out (`ready`), `ready` with a blocker still open is refused, and a question
  that has an answer but no row in `open_questions` is named. `artifact_producer.py validate` / `validate-batch` without
  `--task-root` cannot check the verdict against the answers: they say so in a new `not_checked` field (never an error) and
  `publish` always checks. A story whose answers file exists and cannot be read is counted in `skipped.unreadable_file`
  (HF2-7)

- The stop that asks the whole batch of questions learns to stop on ONE blocking question (HF2-7, part 2). `question_stop.blocking_stop`
  says whether any question is an open blocker (a question not marked `major` or `minor`, or with no usable severity, that has no
  answer that still holds) and which of them carry no severity at all; their cards say "it is not said whether the work can go on
  without this answer, so the factory treats it as blocking". The batch reads "open" from the one definition in the question store:
  a question whose answer was given on a row that has changed since, or whose "before" value is still missing, is in the batch again
  (its card says why), is counted again in the threshold, and "Your answer settled N" counts only the answers that still hold, plus
  the questions kept open until the report. The cards are built in one place (`open_cards`), and the "How to answer" block in
  another (`answer_block`): it now also offers `Q3: until the report`, and says that a whole answer of `go on` / `stop` is read as
  that word only where those words are offered. A new stop reason `blocking` has its plain words in `question-thresholds.json`
  (HF2-7)

- An answer the person gave after the plan was written is now applied by code, once, and never guessed (HF2-7, part 3; TP1-12586). `planning_contract.apply_recorded_answers` lays each recorded answer over the plan rows that branch on the question (`if_answered`), takes the question out of those rows, and names the rest for rework: a row with no branch for the answer goes back to the test planner, a case whose per-answer Then texts lack the recorded answer goes back to the case designer. It leaves the plan alone, and says why in one line, when the question text changed after the answer or its "before" value is still missing (the question is asked again), when gate A is approved (the plan is the one the person approved), and when the answer was changed after it was applied (the planner reworks what followed the first answer). Each pass is noted once in `question-answers.jsonl` (`answers_applied` with `record_at`, `before_plan`, `not_applied`), so a repeat call does nothing and an answer given before the plan exists is applied by the first pass after it. The plan is written whole or not at all, and the notes after it.
- The gate A rehearsal and the stage exit read "settled" from the one definition in the question store. A case's per-answer Then entry that holds the text for the recorded answer (an empty text counts) is resolved and no longer called "already answered"; an entry without it still is. An answer whose question changed since, or whose "before" value is missing, is no longer treated as settled by the plan check, so the question is checked as open and asked again. `Q3: until the report` typed at gate A is recorded as kept open (and said), not dropped. The gate card says where an answer was given in words ("answered when the requirements were checked") instead of the code of the place, and a question kept open until the report says so on its card (HF2-7)

- The brief of every role now carries what the person already decided about the questions (HF2-7, part 4). Until now a brief
  read only the journal's `human_answer` events, so a role that started after the person answered Q1-Q5 at a stop did not see
  the answers, and its brief still said `open halt S2 ... blocking question(s)` for a stop that had been lifted. The brief
  (`brief_pack.py`) reads the answers file through `question_register.answers_for_brief` and prints one line per question the
  person answered, marked not needed, or kept open until the report: the question's id, the reading chosen (letter and text),
  where it was decided in plain words, and the person's words whole - or, when the line would not fit, a pointer to the side
