  file `<dispatch>-decisions.md` that holds them (words over 20000 characters are cut with a pointer to the answers file).
  The same words under several questions are written once, and the journal's copy of those words is not repeated. A question
  that is asked again (its row changed after the answer, or it is open) has no line. When the answers file has a broken line,
  a line that is not an object, or cannot be read, one line says that an answer may be missing; the story's own
  `answers_applied` records never raise it. A halt is open in the brief by the same field the archive, the stage guard and the
  retro read (`resolved`): a halt the story lifted is gone from the brief, and one with no `resolved` is open.

- A person's answer to a question now takes effect at once (HF2-7, part 5). The driver records the answer lines of a halt at the
  requirements, plan or cases stage by code before any helper is called, so an answer made only of question lines never reaches the
  conductor. At the next stop, and at gate A, the recorded answers are laid over the test plan by code, and the role that wrote what
  still follows the other reading is sent back by the driver itself (`question_answer`, a new rework cause that spends none of the
  repair cap).
- One open question that blocks now stops the story at the stage's handoff whatever the number of open questions; a person's `go on`
  passes it only on the text they were shown, so a blocker whose text changed, or a new one, stops again. The stop at the cases stage
  is added. A `go on` on a stop for blockers alone no longer records a pass of the question limit.

- The texts that tell the roles and the orchestrator how a person's answers are handled now say what the driver does (HF2-7, part 5b).
  The S2 stage file no longer tells the orchestrator to write an `escalated` event and to paste the answers into the role's prompt:
  the driver records every whole-line token (`Q1: b`, `Q1: not needed`, `Q1: until the report`) by code and resumes the role with the
  person's words, and words that are not a token are recorded whole with `question_register.py --answer|--not-needed|--defer ... --words-file`.
  The S3 and S4 stage files say that a blocking question still open stops the stage after the author's handoff (S4: before the critic).
  `qa-requirements-tester` is told, before it writes, what the S2 exit checks against the answers file (an answered question stays in
  `open_questions` with its id and text, `blocked` and `ready` follow the blocker questions still open) and that `not_checked` in the
  `validate` output is neither an error nor a halt. The block `question threshold` is now a stop at S4 too, and the blocking stop has
  its own priced answers (`questions.blocking`: the plan or the cases are written on the blocking questions left open, if the person goes on)
  (HF2-7)

- `run_suite --mine` collects once and reads the stand once before the launch (`run_suite.py`, `execution_request.py`):
  one `--mine` on run 12586 spent about 20 minutes on its own plumbing for about 20 seconds of tests - the collect
  the request builder took, then a second collect of the runner's own id check whenever the first was not clean, and
  three runtime probes. The ids the builder could not respell are now matched, by the same `node_ids.match`, against
  the list of the collect it already took; a collect that is unreadable, empty of parsable ids or timed out is said as
  "node ids were not verified" and is not repeated, and the launch goes on. The ids nobody proved are proved by the
  run: pytest's `ERROR: not found` (exit 4) is answered in the ordinary summary as `blocked: node_id_mismatch`,
  `missing: [{asked, nearest: []}]` and `execution_status: not_executed` - never passed or failed, and not a result in
  the run budget. An explicit `--node-id` of an existing file without `[...]` is not collected at all; an id with
  parameters still goes through the one collect (a plugin may spell them). The stand reading the build takes is the one
  before the launch (the post-run comparison stays), so a `--mine` reads the stand twice instead of three times; a
  request file not built by `--mine` is still checked in full (EP1-17)
- The refusals that do not need a collect come before it (`execution_request.py`): a test file nobody can find, a
  story's first typed run with no `runtime_probes` entry and nothing to copy a probe from, and a stand the probe
  refuses are given before about 100 seconds of collect, not after. `_spell_as_collected` reports `verified` only for
  ids found once, in their own file, in a parsed non-empty list; file names that differ only in case are two files on a
  case-sensitive file system (EP1-17)

- A green run of a test is no longer taken for the result of the test as it is now (`proof_level.py`,
  `window_record.py`, `acceptance.py`): after the fixtures of a story were edited, run 12586 reported the old green runs as
  the tests' results. `proof_level.run_freshness` compares the per-test shas the run row recorded
  (`instance_content_sha`, `instance_code_sha`) with the identity re-measured over the bytes on disk, by the rule
  `same_test` already applies to a review, a probe and a receipt: the same test, or the same code of it after a comment, a
  docstring or a blank line, is `fresh`; a changed test, fixture in `conftest.py`, declared helper, renamed variable or
  function, a deleted test file and a helper that cannot be measured now are `stale`; a run that recorded no identity,
  or a test that no run of the story selected, is `unknown` and is said so, never read as fresh. The closure is
  what `function_sha` hashes: data files a test reads, fixtures that come from a plugin that is not a declared helper,
  and a `conftest.py` above the run's working directory are outside it, and an edit there can still read `fresh`
  (an accepted risk, named in the docstring). `probe_freshness` and `staleness` ask the same of a test's live check,
  per instance from one measurement, and carry what a re-probe by code needs (`replay`); nothing is written
- The S5 window copies the run row's two shas as the item's `run_identity` (only when both are there) and names a run of
  other code as the gap `stale_run:<instance>` beside the outcome's own gap, with the door `run_suite.py --mine <case>`.
  Code does not derive an `unresolved` pair for it and no recorded word is read for it. A run that recorded no
  identity, or a test with none, is not a gap: `window_record.py` prints `run freshness not measured: <why>`
- `acceptance._passed_on_current_bytes` asks the same predicate and keeps its own direction (a run that cannot be
  placed reads as passed in the blocked context); `validate_window` reads the closed set of `change_disposition` values
  from the row-field carrier (`window_record.REQUIRED_ROW_FIELDS`) through an import inside the function, so
  `import acceptance` still loads no `window_record` (EP1-15)

- S6 now decides the freshness of an automated result by the same predicate the ledger will use (`story_run.py`,
  EP1-15): `s6_freshness` asks `proof_level.staleness`, and a result the evidence function keeps but whose run row's own
  per-test shas say it ran other code (for example a helper module that is not a declared helper of the run) is moved to
  the tests to run; it also returns the stale live checks with what `probe_by_code.py` needs to replay each. When runs are
  stale too, the runner goes as before but is launched with `complete=False`. With the stand not confirmed (the word
  `stand not confirmed` is recorded) nothing is launched or proved: `N tests changed after their run are left for a run
  elsewhere`. With nothing stale the calls and the digest are what they were
- Known limit: the driver replays a stale live check by code (`probe_by_code.py`, before the last `finalize_task.py`) ONLY
  under an open S6 dispatch for `probe_by_code`, and no path opens one today, so in this release the replay does not run.
  Each stale live check prints one digest line, `re-probe skipped: no open S6 dispatch for probe_by_code`; no question goes
  to a person and S6 closes at the site `s6.reprobed`; the ledger keeps the stale probe as
  `not_verified:missing_sensitivity_proof`, so the check stays visible as unproved. The door is to run `probe_by_code.py`
  by hand under an S6 dispatch. A probe that cannot be replayed by code (no recorded test or mutation, or a line anchor
  that moved with the edit) and a test with no run on its current bytes are each one digest line as well

- The ledger no longer reads a green run of other code as a pass (`ledger.py`, `test_state`): after the run row is read
  (`case_stamp.run_row_for`, unchanged), `proof_level.run_freshness` compares the per-test shas the run recorded with
  the test on disk now. A green whose test, or a fixture or helper it uses, changed since the run reads
  `not_executed:changed_since_run` and the detail carries the sentence of the check; a comment, a docstring or a blank
  line is not a change (D-0017). A red keeps its `failed:*` state whatever the edit, and says the test changed after
  the run. A row that recorded no per-test shas (a non-pytest runner, an older run) keeps today's reading and the
  detail says "run freshness not measured: ..." instead of staying silent; so does a green whose test file cannot be
  found where the ledger runs (the ledger cannot tell a deleted test from a ledger read outside the run's project; the
  S6 window still reads a missing file as stale). The delivery verdict reads `not_executed:changed_since_run` through
  a new kind pair in `delivery-verdict-kinds.json`, chosen by the new need `stand_word`: when the person's word that
  passes the stand block is recorded for S5 or S6 the kind is `changed_unrun` (`after_checks`, owner `environment`) and
  "Left with you" names `run_suite.py --mine <case>`; otherwise it is `changed_unrun_ours` (`no`, owner `factory`: a
  stand was there and the factory did not run the test again) (HF2-11, 11c)

- The fields every `tests[]` row of the automation manifest owes are now one list, and the automator learns the missing ones at the S5 exit instead of from the critic or the conductor (`window_record.py`, `s5_precheck.py`): `window_record.REQUIRED_ROW_FIELDS` names `assertion_id`, `defect_location`, `change_disposition`, `change_basis_ref`, `obligation_refs` and `profile_id` with what each holds, who writes it and where it is needed, and the window record reads its item fields from that list; `window_record.row_field_gaps` answers what a row still lacks, by the readers the window and the run already use (a missing or empty value is missing, a string of spaces is a value as it is for the window; `profile_id` only for a row whose file lies under a test root two selected profiles share and which names neither, or names a profile the config does not hold; `obligation_refs` only for a case whose plan row carries an automated obligation, written by the marker `qa(obligations=[...])` and never by hand). The S5 pre-check raises ONE `manifest` finding listing every missing (row, field) pair of the dispatch's cases with the fragment door (`manifest_put.py --task <T> --fragment <file>`); no recorded word and no judge lifts it, and an unscoped run says it did not check (HF2-12, EP1-18)

- The automator is told the row fields before its first handback, and the marker writes the red rows (`manifest_from_tests.py`, `agents/qa-automator.md`, `s5_precheck.py`, `window_record.py`): after the write the script PRINTS the row form - `{"tests": [{"instance_id": "<id>", "<field>": null, ...}]}` for the rows of that run that still lack `assertion_id`, `defect_location`, `change_disposition`, `change_basis_ref` (and `profile_id` where two selected profiles share the file's test root), read back from the saved manifest (from the pure merge on `--dry-run`), with one legend line per field; a field the marker writes (`obligation_refs`) is named in the legend with the marker and has no slot; `--json` gains the key `row_form`. The form is never part of the fragment, because `manifest_put` updates a row with every key a fragment sends and a `null` would wipe a value the role wrote. `qa_unresolved` takes `instance_ids=[...]` (a slice of the case, no echo rows), `thens=[n]` (the red Then of a `contradicts_requirement` row) and `reason="blocked_by_check", then=[n], blocking_check=, detail=` on the test function or `pytest.param` that holds the Then (one `then_bindings` row per instance, never an `unresolved[]` row); the registration lines a project pastes are now built from the keyword tuples, so `partitions` and the new keys are in them. A `blocked_by_check` or `contradicts_requirement` row a role sent by hand now outlives a writer run unless the run writes the same Then of the same test, and the run says how many it kept; the Then number is read by `contract.then_number`. The charter names the fields in one sentence (net bytes below the charter's before-size), and the four phrases that said the marker cannot write these rows yet (`s5_precheck.py`, `window_record.py`) are reworded (HF2-12, EP1-18)

- The code critic and the code-review rubric name four test-code defects that run 12586 let through (HF2-13, HF2-14, HF2-15; `agents/qa-code-critic.md`, `references/code-review-rubric.md`, `references/test-code-patterns.md`): a second helper written beside an existing one that does the same job under another name, and the same fixture created twice in one window (dimension 5; the repair extends the existing one); a test that raises before its assert - an unpack of `find(...)` or an index into a `pytest.param` - so the red line names no Then, with a new patterns section "The red line names the Then" for the automator and the critic ("assert the count before unpacking"); a refusal test that does not discriminate the cause (a blanket `pytest.raises(HTTPError)` or a 4xx every move gets) and a masked value compared with a masked value (dimension 2); and the check that the test's level matches the S3 plan's `level` for its case, where a row with no `level` is "not checked", never "matches" (critic Procedure, item 1). No role file grew: the critic file is 3 bytes smaller than before (EP1-13, EP1-14, EP1-12)

- The Then number of a `then_bindings` row and the tag of the waiting `then-remainder-unrecorded-` finding now each have
  one carrier (`contract.py`: `then_number`, `THEN_REMAINDER_TAG`, `THEN_REMAINDER_WAITS`): `s5_precheck` and the code
  judge read the number through the same function, and the exit gate takes the waiting tag from the contract instead of
  spelling it again. A `then` that is a bool or a float (`true`, `4.0`) now reads as naming no Then, like a list or a
  dict, so its clause stays uncovered rather than silently bound; a digit string such as `"2"` still reads as 2.
  No finding text, exit code or JSON shape changes (HF2-2)

- One reader now says which test is red against which requirement (`acceptance.red_by_requirement`): an `unresolved[]`
  row `contradicts_requirement` makes a test red only for the case, the instance, the partition and the Then the row
  names, and every matching row of a test is returned, not the first. `acceptance.row_slice` is the one reading of what
  a row's `instance_ids` / `partitions` mean (`P-msteams` and `msteams` are one partition, `contract.partition_key`),
  `acceptance.red_by_own_row` asks whether a row is a case's own, `acceptance.story_scope` lists the instances of every
  case of a story. Anything that cannot be read (runs, report, manifest) reads as "not red". A Then that sits behind a
  red assert of its own test has a name now, `blocked_by_check`, in the contract's closed list of reasons and in
  `contract.THEN_REMAINDER_REASONS` (`then_remainders`, `then_remainder_rows` and `handed_tests` take `reasons=`; the
  default is exactly what they returned before). No finding text, exit code or JSON shape of a command changes yet
  (HF2-3)

- The S5 precheck reads a test that covers several cases and stops at one red assert by the pair (Then, test), not by the
  whole case. A `contradicts_requirement` row is compared with the tests and partitions of ITS slice: a green sibling
  of another partition is no longer `partial-green`, a green test the row's slice reaches is `contradicts-but-green`,
  and a row that names a slice with no red test behind it is `contradicts-no-instance`. `uncovered-partition-N` is
  said only where a green test covers the partition. A Then recorded behind a red check (`blocked_by_check` in
  `then_bindings`) asks nobody for a word: it must be well formed, a Then of the case, not also proved on the same
  test, and name a case or test that is red (`blocked-check-unknown-N`, `blocked-check-not-red-N`,
  `then-remainder-conflict-N`); it also needs no assertion (`no-assert-N` is skipped for it). New findings: `red-two-cases-<test>`
  (one test red for the rows of two cases: keep one row, record the rest as blocked), `red-links-unbound` (a red test
  covers a case and nothing says what became of that case's Thens on it), `blocked-check-row` (that reason belongs to a
  Then, not to a whole case). Every new door names the fragment road (`manifest_put.py --task <T> --fragment <file>`)
  and `retracted_unresolved`, never the marker. The default output for a Then left with its owner is unchanged
  (HF2-3)

- `manifest_put.py` can take an `unresolved[]` row away: `--fragment {"retracted_unresolved": ["TC-004"]}` drops the row
  of that case (a bare id finds the row of every area), keeps the key in the manifest's `retracted_unresolved` history
  and prints the slice and the `thens` of each row it dropped. Before this a row that names a slice (`instance_ids`,
  `partitions`) stayed forever after its Thens were recorded one by one, and nothing could remove it. A key that names
  no row, or one an earlier send already dropped, is refused; so is a fragment that sends and retracts the row of one
  case. A re-sent `contradicts_requirement` row now REPLACES its slice (`instance_ids` and `partitions` as one group)
  and its `thens` (a second group) instead of keeping an older value beside the new one; a patch that leaves a group
  empty keeps the old row's group. A fragment whose `unresolved[]` holds two rows of one case with different reasons
  (say `contradicts_requirement` and `blocked_by_env`) is refused before anything is written, where the later row used
  to win and the other reason was lost without a word; journals that already hold such an event fold as they did.
  The keys of a row's slice are read from `contract.UNRESOLVED_SLICE_KEYS` (`design/state-exits.md` has the two new rows)
  (HF2-3)

- One test that covers several cases and stops at one case's red assert no longer paints every case it covers red, and no
  longer lets any of them read green. The checks ledger reads each case by its OWN runs: a case whose own tests are green
  but whose Thens stand behind another case's red (a `blocked_by_check` row, or a Then covered by the test that stopped)
  reads `not_executed:blocked_by_check` with a line saying which Then waits for which check - "not proven", never a
  pass. A case with a `contradicts_requirement` row whose own run failed reads `failed:<verdict>` instead of
  `not_executed`, and a case's own row never hides its own bug. The delivery check lists the blocked Thens in "Left with
  you" (new verdict kind `blocked_by_check`: the third verdict, `after_checks`; the words are the author's `detail`, or
  `check after <case> (<title>) is fixed`), keeps a Then the person took beside a failed case, and no longer asks a test
  that is red against a requirement for a sensitivity proof. `rollup_status` is unchanged (HF2-3)

- The requirements trace (the appendix table of the report) reads a Then that stands behind another case's red as not proven,
  never as a pass. When one test covers several cases and stops at one case's red assert, a Then bound `blocked_by_check`
  reads `blocked` with the words "not checked yet: in the same test, <case> (<title>) fails first; check this again once
  that is fixed", and a Then covered by the test that stopped reads `blocked` with "not proven: the test stopped at <case>
  (<title>), Then <m>, before reaching this check; check this again once that is fixed". Both tests of the Then stay in the
  row; a Then with no test behind it is still `blocked`, never dropped; a bug found on another test of the same case still
  wins; a case's own red row reads as before. A case whose title cannot be read is named once as "the check this one depends
  on (<case>)". The red instances are read once per story through the ledger's reader (HF2-3)

- The role texts say how a test that stops at one red assert is written and judged (`agents/qa-automator.md`, `agents/qa-code-critic.md`,
  `agents/qa-case-designer.md`, `agents/qa-failure-analyst.md`, `references/code-review-rubric.md`,
  `references/artifact-contract.md` and its generated slices): the automator moves independent Thens before the red one and
  records a Then the red stops as `blocked_by_check` through `manifest_put.py --fragment`; the code critic reads an
  independent Then left behind a red as a dimension 6 finding (`cause: test_defect`); a commented-out Then is
  sanctioned (dimension 8) only with its reason in the code, its `then_bindings` row with reason `handed_to_person` or
  `blocked_by_check`, and its Left with you line, otherwise it is masking; the case designer knows a Then that only makes
  sense after another case's check stays a Then of its own case; the failure analyst triages a red that stops other
  Thens once and does not count the Thens it blocks as failures; the artifact contract names the `blocked_by_check` row
  (`blocking_check`, `detail`), `thens` on a `contradicts_requirement` row, `retracted_unresolved`, and that a re-sent
  `contradicts_requirement` row replaces its slice and its `thens` separately. A red by a product bug is not commented
  out by any of these texts (no owner's word yet); `scripts/tests/test_mixed_then_texts.py` keeps the key phrases and
  checks that the phrases awaiting the owner's word are absent. No source file grew: every added byte is paid by a cut in
  the same file (HF2-3)

- A test that fails against its requirement now closes the S5 window with its own manifest row (HF2-4 part a). When the
  `unresolved[]` row `contradicts_requirement` names a failed instance (the case, the instance or partition, the Then, all
  read by the one reader `acceptance.red_by_requirement`) and the critic approved it, `window_record.py` records the gap
  `contradicts_requirement:<instance>` instead of `product:<instance>`, no probe is asked of the red test (whether a mutated
  run fails at the intended assert depends on the order of the asserts), and the instance carries a
  `probe_not_applicable: {why: red, reason: contradicts_requirement, rows: [...]}` block with every row that names it.
  `contract.window_shape_errors` accepts the block as the third way to satisfy a new or changed instance (beside a probe
  and a named probe gap), only on an instance that ran red and never beside a `probe` or a `probe_gap`. A window whose
  gaps are all derivable is "acceptable as unresolved" - exit 0, the review receipt written, S7 triages the red; a test
  that is red for the rows of two cases is told in a note. A green test with such a row still owes its probe, a handed or
  stopped item is never red, and a failed run, a missing run, an `error` run, a row of another case, instance, partition
  or Then, or a critic word other than `approved` keep the refusal. A red test no row explains is told the one road that
  closes it - the `unresolved[]` row sent through `manifest_put.py --task <T> --fragment <file>` - instead of the critic's
  probe and a person's word, neither of which can close it; the refusal of the reader (a row about a sibling instance, a
  partition, a Then) is printed with its own fix, once per red instance (HF2-4a)

- An S5 window of red tests the requirement contradicts is now accepted by code, with no word of a person (HF2-4 part b).
  `story_step.py finish` derives the pair from the window record for the new kind `contradicts_requirement` (beside
  `blocked_by_env`, `handed_to_person` and `probe_gap`; a red nobody explained, `product:`, is still no kind and derives
  nothing), and the controller takes the window only when the completion names `contradicts_requirement`; a pair typed by
  hand without the word, or a bare `passed_green`, is refused with the command that derives the pair. The refusal of a
  failed instance that lacks its block names the manifest row road instead of the person's `probe gap:` word, which
  stays the door of an instance that ran green. The critic's receipts check no longer asks a sensitivity proof of a test
  that is red by its row at the moment of the check (the one reader `acceptance.red_by_requirement`, over the whole
  story, so a red of an earlier window is exempt too); a test that went green later, or whose row was retracted, owes its
  proof as before, and a reader that fails exempts nothing. The `s5.md` phase text and the code critic's step 3 say that a
  red test with its `contradicts_requirement` row takes no probe, `s5.md` no longer says a person's word passes the oracle
  findings of the precheck (no word does; they are the author's repair), and `design/state-exits.md` names how a story
  leaves such a window: `controller rework`, with the S7 triage deciding `APP_BUG` or `CASE_DEFECT` (HF2-4b)

- `manifest_put` merges `then_bindings` by unit and no longer replaces the whole array (`manifest_put.py`): a hand fragment (a
  role's or the conductor's) replaces the rows of each unit it names - (case, `instance_id`), a null `instance_id` being a
  unit of its own - and every row of a unit it does not name stays, so a blocked-row patch for TC-005 on one test no longer
  takes the covered rows of TC-005 on another test. The writer's fragment (`tests[]` rows carrying `generated_from`) is still
  the full array and replaces it whole, so a test that moved from TC-007 to TC-008 leaves no covered TC-007 row behind; a
  writer fragment without `tests[]` is merged as a hand fragment, never worse than a hand one. A hand fragment that sends only
  part of a unit's rows takes the others out, and `run` prints each row it took out as `<case> Then <n> on <instance|none>`
  so no row is lost silently. A journal written before the rule folds by it, with nothing reported as unprojected (the
  projection is the journal)
- A Then a person's decision deferred (`then_bindings` row, reason `deferred_by_decision:*`) beside a green test reads
  `deferred_by_decision` in the ledger (`ledger.py`), after every failure word and before the blocked and hand-off remainders:
  a red result still reads `failed`; and the requirement report puts a `pass` beside a deferred result in the deferred class
  and beside a blocked one in the waiting class instead of "proven by tests" (`report_facts.py`)
- The S5 precheck stops asking for an assertion of a Then that is recorded as not checked (`s5_precheck.py`, finding
  `no-assert-N`): a Then with no covered row whose unresolved row carries a reason of the closed list (the stand, a hand-off, a
  pending implementation, an unconfirmed value, a check ahead of it) or a decided deferral. A reason outside the list,
  `contradicts_requirement` (a red by a product bug is not commented out), and a Then that also has a covered row keep the
  finding

- A test the run recorded nothing for is no longer read as passed. The trace table (`traceability.py`) reads `pass` for an
  instance only from a green result row of its own; the manifest's `green` / `written` word is no execution. With no row
  the instance is `not run` and the basis is the ledger's own sentence (`ledger.NO_RUN_RESULT`: "no result for this test in
  run-report.json"); a row whose word is neither green nor red (`skipped`, `partial`, a word nobody knows) is `not run` and
  names the word; a case handed to a person with no row waits for the person (`wait`); a manifest `red` with no row is `not run`
  and never claims a red run that does not exist. `case_stamp.run_row_for` is the one join "what did the run record for this
  test", built from the same three steps as `red_run_for` (one shared function over a set of rows): a row of ANOTHER test never
  matches - not a `::` tail two tests share (`a.py::TestA::t` and `a.py::TestB::t`), not a sibling parameter, not a stale row
  or the row of a red probe, a diagnostic or a baseline run - and a bare function with several parameter rows reads its worst
  row whatever the order of the report. A story written before instance ids keeps its reading: an entry with no identity of its
  own that is the only live entry of its case joins the only current row of the case, and with a second entry of the case
  neither inherits it. The ledger reads the same row (`test_state` no longer lends a green sibling's result of the case to a
  test that never ran), and `mark_answered` adds the gate A suffix only for an answer that still stands
  (`question_register.settled`). The legend of `not run` says what is true now

- The report says "proven by tests" once, takes a question's status from one place, and checks its appendix (`report_facts.py`).
  The verdict's "Of N requirements: M proven by tests" is now derived from the same carrier as "K green tests count as proven":
  a requirement keeps the class `proven` only when every `pass` row of the trace that names tests has a test the Proven block
  counts, and one whose test ran green but is not counted reads "not proven" with the reason (the code critic has not approved
  it, or a live check is still owed) - or `wait` with the hand-off words when the test is one a person took (it is not the
  critic's doing, and a person still has to act). A manual record (`pass`, no tests) is unchanged. With no readable ledger the
  number is `unknown` ("proven by tests: unknown - ...") and the requirement reads `unknown`, never a count. A question is
  open unless `question_register.settled` says the person settled it: one kept until the report is listed with that mark, and
  an answer given to an earlier wording of the question is listed (and its Then keeps the "Needed" line); under the quoted gate A
  words the block says "Your words here name Q4, but no answer to it is recorded, so it stays under Open questions." for each
  id the words name with no answer recorded. `--check` compares the appendix section with the render of the trace as it stands
  now (the body under the heading, newlines trimmed): one line per row whose Result cell differs, that is absent from the
  appendix (unless the traceability check already names it) or that the trace no longer has, one line for the table when
  something else differs or two rows share a key, and one line when the trace cannot be built. The refusal names the scribe;
  it never asks for an automatic rebuild, which cannot repair the appendix. A Then whose row numbers no Then (a bool, a float, a
  list) is read by the contract's one reader and says "a Then the row does not number". A requirement whose trace row is red is
  never filed under "Skipped by the plan" by a gate A waiver: the waiver covers a test the plan skips, not one that ran and
  failed, and the requirement stands under "Not proven" with the basis of its row.

- Mutation probe and `--node-id` runs keep the profile a manifest row names (`probe_by_code.py`, `execution_request.py`):
  with two profiles over one test root the probe built its request without the profile the row had already named and
  was refused as "profiles share the test root", so no instance of that run ever got a sensitivity verdict. The probe
  now hands the builder the row's profile, and a `--node-id` run takes the profile that the manifest rows of the same
  case and file agree on (nothing else of the row travels with the id). A root two profiles share with no `profile_id`
  on the row is still refused, never run under the first profile; the probe's refusal names the manifest-row door only,
  because that tool has no `--profile` (`run_suite --mine` keeps `--profile ID`) (EP1-16)
- A profile the config does not hold is refused naming the ids it does hold (`execution_request.py`,
  `probe_by_code.py`): a `profile_id` on a row or a `--profile` that is not in `qa-factory/config.json` used to run
  under the profile that owns the file by path, or to fail as a gap of the onboarding; both readers now ask one
  predicate (`known_profile`) and say whose name it was. An explicit profile that differs from the row's runs, with a
  note saying the row's name did not decide (EP1-16)

- Cost capture no longer slows every tool call. The `--debounced` capture (PostToolUse, SubagentStop) never renders the
  dashboard any more, and its 30 s window is asked before the session lock (`_debounce_window_open`: one `stat` of the
  cost file, no lock and no parse), where it used to be asked under the lock after the whole cost file was read. The
  window errs towards "capture": a missing file, a file from the future, an unreadable file or a session with a
  pending marker is captured now. The Stop capture renders the dashboard once, with its lock free, after every outcome
  (finished, unchanged, deferred), and the Stop entry of `hooks.json` is asynchronous, so the host's turn no longer
  waits for it. A Stop writes a `started` marker before it asks for the lock (after the onboarding and ownership
  checks); a Stop the host cuts off leaves it and the Cost tab shows the session as stale ("a Stop capture started at
  ... did not finish"), and the next Stop of any session of the project records the tail of one other session, the
  oldest marker whose transcript is not live (an ordinary incremental capture, pinned valuations kept; one per Stop,
  the rest wait for the next). A SubagentStop of the Claude host no longer replaces the parent's cost file with the
  subagent file's totals: the parent is captured from its own transcript, so its requests and cost never shrink (a
  subagent file outside the parent's `subagents/` folder is named on stderr). Markers
  written before the `kind` field read as "gave up on the lock" as before. `validate_artifacts.py` no longer renders
  the dashboard on a Write/Edit under `qa-factory/`; its metric-signal notice reads the last receipt. The cost
  document and its fields are unchanged; no new setting (`QA_FACTORY_SKIP_DASHBOARD_REFRESH=1` still silences every
  render) (HF2-9)

- "Left with you" no longer prints an empty line for a case whose Thens stand behind another case's red check when the
  author moved those Thens before the red assert (`check_delivery.py`, `ledger.behind_red`, HF2-0 R1): the covered Thens
  of the case on the red test are listed in `to_check` (unioned with any blocked Thens, by Then number; the case itself
  when no Then number is readable), and the item gets the same default words as its siblings,
  `check after <case> (<title>) is fixed`, unless a record already carries its own
- The ledger detail of a Then that stands behind another check no longer says `its other Thens passed` unless the case's
  own run (its runs outside the red test) passed (`ledger.py`, HF2-0 R2): a case with no run of its own, or whose own run
  failed or errored, reads `<case> Then <n>: behind <blocker>` alone, in the mixed form too

- Integration texts of wave 1 (`skills/qa-story/SKILL.md`, `phases/s5.md`, `phases/s6.md`, `agents/qa-automator.md`, `agents/qa-code-critic.md`, `references/artifact-contract-automation.md`, `references/vocabularies.md`): the halts table says the answers to the S2 question halt are recorded by code; `s5.md` says a `node_id_mismatch` without `nearest` is corrected from the test source (the roles say the same) and names the row form `manifest_from_tests.py` prints; `s6.md` says S6 reads run freshness by `proof_level.run_freshness`, sends stale runs to the runner and proves stale live checks again by code under an open S6 dispatch (the digest says `re-probe skipped` otherwise); the paragraph on a Then another check stops (`blocked_by_check`, `thens`, `retracted_unresolved`) moved from `artifact-contract.md` to `artifact-contract-automation.md`, where the automator reads it, and `blocked_by_check` joined the reason list of `vocabularies.md`. The delivery words of a Then behind a check whose title cannot be read are `check after the check this one depends on (TC-004) is fixed` (the id once, as `traceability` prints it), and the "Left with you" item of a case whose only kind is `blocked_by_check` lists only the Thens behind the red check (`check_delivery.py`, `build_left_items`); a case with no Then row lists none. Slices regenerated. (hotfix-12586/2, integration t-130)

## 0.10.1 — 2026-10-24 — the TP1-12586 run no longer stalls: collected ids behind a banner, fingerprint records, two profiles on one root, a Then or a probe handed to the person, a finished critic, the integration gap named before gate A, no stop after a gate

- A banner a conftest or a plugin prints before pytest's collected ids no longer ends the collect with zero tests
  (`node_ids.py`, `parse_collected`): a `=` line before the first id is skipped as a banner, a `=` line after the ids
  still ends the parse (pytest's warnings and errors sections stay out of the ids) (EP1-9)
- One count verdict on a collect, shared by S5 and gate A (`node_ids.py`, `unread_count`): a collect that exits 0
  while pytest's own count line reports tests (`N tests collected`, and the deselected form `3/4 tests collected
  (1 deselected)`) but no id could be read is a refusal naming N and the head of the output at S5, and an
  `unavailable` rehearsal step at the gate (`gate_preflight.py`, the s5_toolchain collect), never a silent "no
  tests"; an empty output with exit 0 and no count line stays an empty collect (EP1-9, AR-15, AR-28)
- The gate's reader of a collect output is the same parser (`gate_preflight.py`, `first_collected_node` through
  `node_ids.parse_collected`): gate A and S5 cannot disagree on the same bytes. Narrowing: the gate now offers only
  `<file>.py::` ids, so a non-.py item of a pytest plugin (a YAML test, for example) is no longer picked for the
  rehearsal and the card asks the person instead (EP1-9, AR-13)

- A Then the person takes is a named remainder beside the case's green test (`contract.py`, `s5_precheck.py`,
  `manifest_from_tests.py`, `manifest_put.py`, `ledger.py`, `check_delivery.py`, `report_facts.py`, `traceability.py`):
  when only one Then of a case (or a named part of it) cannot be checked on the stand, the automator writes
  `qa_unresolved(case=, then=[n], reason="handed_to_person", owner=, part=, detail=<steps>)` and keeps the green test for
  the other Thens, instead of writing a test that cannot run. The S5 exit passes the remainder only with the person's
  word `then handed: <case>#<n>` (read by identifier, never by substring; `partial-green` is still refused at source and
  its refusal now names this door); the ledger reads the case `not_executed:handed_to_person`, the delivery verdict is
  `after_checks`, "Left with you" names the Then with its steps, and the requirement reads "waiting", never "proven".
  A Then both proved by a test and left, a Then of no case file, and a case whose every Then is left are refused with the
  door named. A recorded `*` never opens a Then remainder nobody named, at the exit gate either (`exit_gate.word_class`
  reads it as refused; only the `then handed:` word for that Then, judged at the source, passes it). (HF1-10, GW1-14)
  When the same case also carries a test the code critic could not verify (a probe gap), "Left with you" lists EVERY Then of
  the case with the part on the Then the person took, not only that Then. The three readers of a person's prefixed word
  (`executor unavailable:`, `then handed:`, `probe gap:`) are now one (`contract.stage_override_values`) and all skip a revoked
  record: a revoked `executor unavailable:` word no longer hands the profile over (the person is asked again). (HF1 batch fix round)

- Seven role cards in `references/role-commands.json` now say what their parsers accept (the class of EP1-8: a card describes a form
  its parser refuses): `manual_evidence.py write-block` lists the record fields and says the record is the `record.json` that
  `build` wrote; `export` names the required `--output`; `manual_capture.py ui` says the file needs at least one `goto` (not
  that it starts with one) and that every goto is on a configured stand; `artifact_producer.py publish` names `--kind`,
  `--task-root`, the `work/` and canonical-name limits and the `--expected-hash` an existing target needs; `external_writes.py
  --record` names the required `--external-id`, the `--remote-revision` a keyed proposal needs and the authorization it waits for;
  `plan_row.py` names the required `--task` and says that `1`, `yes`, `on` become the boolean true and `0`, `no`, `off` false
  before the number rule (the old "digits as numbers" was wrong for them); `context_bundle.py` lists every required field of
  `requirement_sources`, `coverage_search` and `existing_test_candidates` (HF1-12, FR-11, FR-14)
- `context_bundle.py --validate` refuses an invalid `relation`, `status` or `origin` by printing the closed list of that field,
  sorted, and the position of the record (`requirement_sources[0] has invalid relation or status: relation must be one of
  clarification, normative, ...`), as its card promised; a value that is not a string is refused the same way instead of raising
  (FR-1, AR-9)
- `test_role_commands.py` feeds every card's own example - a spec written exactly as the card says - to its command through
  `role_cli.run_guarded` and requires it to be accepted, removes one required item from each example and requires a refusal that
  names it, and requires the card to equal `--help` word for word; for `write-block` and `context_bundle` every field of a record
  is refused when missing exactly when the card names it (AR-13)

- Plan contract (`references/artifact-contract-plan.md`, `scripts/contract_slices.py`): the `grounding.yaml` section no longer says "Words: `vocabulary.grounding_labels`, `requirement_grounding_states`", a pointer to a file the strategist's pre-tool guard refuses it. The source carries a generator token and `contract_slices.py` writes the strategist's slice with the words themselves, from the one line builder `handoff.grounding_vocabulary_line` (an unreadable vocabulary or an empty list reads `NONE READABLE`, never blank). A change of the vocabulary makes `contract_slices.py --check` red until `--write`, the same ratchet the charters' digest line has (OH3-14 class).

- A probe that cannot run here, accepted by the person, closes the S5 window as a named gap (`contract.py`,
  `acceptance.py`, `controller.py`, `window_record.py`, `story_step.py`, `block-names.json`): a test that ran green and
  owes a live check, but whose probe came back `not_executed` or `incomplete` (the tool or the stand stopped it), no longer
  stalls the window at "probe is missing for a new_or_changed instance". When the person's word `probe gap: <instance id or
  case key>` names it, `window_record.py` writes a `probe_gap` block beside (never inside) `probe`, the shape check, the
  window validation and the controller accept it in one change, `story_step.py finish` derives the `unresolved` pair, and
  the critic's `unverified` carries the test to "Left with you" at S8 through the existing `review_unverified` road. A gap
  nobody named stays refused at the shape check, the window validation and the controller (a typed `unresolved` pair does
  not pass it), with the recording door named; a recorded `*` or `not receipted` never opens it; a red test, or a test whose
  probe ran and judged it, takes no word; a valid receipt outranks the word. (HF1-14, EP1-10)

- A fingerprint input given as the `{path, sha256}` record that `fingerprint_files` itself holds is read by its path
  (`execution_fingerprint.py`): `build` met `Path(record)` and died with a bare TypeError that named nothing. One reader
  (`_input_record`) and one claim check (`_check_claim`) now serve `build` and `verify_files`, so the same record gets the
  same verdict from both; a `sha256` that is present but is not a 64-hex digest (empty, a number, null) is refused by name
  instead of being skipped or reported as changed bytes, and a value that is neither a path nor a record is refused naming
  its group and index (`test_files[2]`) with an example record. `file_hash` takes a path only and refuses a record by name
  (EP1-8, HF1-2)
- The role card of `execution_fingerprint.py` in `references/role-commands.json` says each file list holds "paths or
  {path, sha256} records (helper_files optional)", and a test pins the card, the `--help` epilog and the parser to that one
  form: a spec written exactly as the card says is fingerprinted (EP1-8 (3), FR-11, FR-14)

- Two execution profiles over one test root no longer resolve to the first of them in silence
  (`execution_request.profiles_owning`, `_profile_for`; `probe_by_code._profile_of`, `_profile_cwd`;
  `gate_preflight.Rehearsal._choose_test`): with an api and a ui profile both rooted at `tests/`, every row whose
  manifest entry named no profile ran under the api command and the gate-A reporter rehearsal "proved" the ui profile
  with the first test under the shared root, an api test. ONE predicate now says which profiles own a path (one
  normalisation: `tests`, `./tests/` and, on Windows, `Tests` are one root), and the selector, the probe's run
  directory and the rehearsal all ask it. A run whose rows fall under a shared root is refused naming the profiles and
  the door (`profile_id` on the manifest row, or `--profile ID` where the tool takes one; `probe_by_code` has none and
  names only the row); rows that name two profiles get the "one `--mine` per profile" refusal; an unnamed row beside a
  named one under a shared root is refused naming that row instead of running under the named profile. The rehearsal
  picks no test by path for such a profile, says so and leaves the `gate_rehearsal.reporter_probe_test` card; the
  onboarding probe, which learns what a command writes, still takes any test under the root. The onboarding phase text
  (`p4-generate.md`) asks for one root per profile and no `-v` repeated when `addopts` already carries it, and
  `references/execution-lifecycle.md` names `profile_id` on a manifest row (EP1-10; FB-7)

- The stand login probe sends the body fields the project's login expects (`stand_access.py`,
  `config_contract.py`, `project_inventory.py`, `references/templates/config.json`,
  `references/login-error-shapes.json`, `qa-onboarding` phases 2 and 4): `environment.access` gains the optional
  `user_field` / `secret_field` (JSON field NAMES, defaults `username` / `password`) that `local_login` sends, so a
  stand whose login expects `email` is no longer read as refusing the factory after an HTTP 422. A 400 or 422 names
  the field names the stand's own answer complains about, read through the shapes of the new data row
  (`detail[].loc`, `errors[].field` and the like) and redacted to names; no receipt prints the user or the secret.
  `config_contract.access_errors` refuses a field name that is not a field-name string and two equal names (they
  would drop the user from the body while the login read `ok`), and the probe sends nothing in that case. Onboarding
  discovery (`project_inventory.py --access`) carries the two keys and says when it did not find them (OH3-10)

- The context probe reads a child's answer that comes back through the host's handback call (`host_probe.py`): Claude
  Code returns a subagent's final report through a tool call whose input holds the words, so the child's assistant rows
  carried no text and every probe child was judged `tool_used` or silent. The strings of that call are now the child's
  texts and the call is not a tool the child used; any other tool call still is (OH3-13).
- The host's return form is a data row with one reader (`references/host-report-forms.json`, `host_adapter.report_forms()`):
  the handback tool name (matched exactly) and the host's acknowledgement row live in the file, not in `host_probe.py`.
  A file that is absent, unreadable or malformed gives no forms, and the probe then takes no call for a handback and
  stays `unverified`, never `delivered`.

- S3 labelling brief (`brief_pack.py`, `handoff.py`, `phases/s3.md`): the strategist's window-1 brief now carries every word of
  `grounding_labels` and `requirement_grounding_states` in one `labels: ...; requirement states: ...` line that
  `handoff.grounding_vocabulary_line` builds from the one vocabulary reader (the driver's dispatch text is to call the same builder).
  The role is no longer sent to `handoffs/vocabulary.yaml`, which the pre-tool guard refuses it, and the conductor no longer carries the
  lists by hand; a missing vocabulary or an empty list is declared in the line, never left blank (OH3-14).

- A Claude Code worker that handed its report back is `returned`, not `alive` for ever (`dispatch_liveness.py`,
  `claude_stop`; `worker_lifecycle.active_binding` asks the same question through the one `host_verdict`): a critic's
  `story_step` receipt stays non-terminal until `story_step finish`, its transcript was fresh and then its receipt old,
  so the dispatch read `alive` and then `unknown`, and `story_step pause` after the critic's reject was refused ("host
  worker is still active") until a person said it was gone. The return is the host's own record: the transcript's LAST
  line is the host's acknowledgement of the handback call (read by structure and by the names in
  `references/host-report-forms.json`, never by the words of the reply), the call is the row before it, the
  acknowledgement is at or after the receipt's `bound_at` or the transcript's first prompt names the dispatch, the
  sidecar `.meta.json` does not say `finished: false`, and the stop hooks have let it go (a journalled stop of the same
  receipt at or after the acknowledgement; otherwise `dispatch.native_completion_grace_s` after it). A child resumed
  after a handback has rows after the acknowledgement and stays `alive`; the SubagentStop hook's line alone is never a
  return. The receipt is not written and nothing is accepted: `returned` is "the role stopped". Every doubt (no forms
  file, a cut last line, an acknowledgement that is not a success, a clock ahead, a journal that cannot be read) keeps
  today's answer and says so in the evidence (OH3-16, AR-5, AR-28)
- The report forms file (`references/host-report-forms.json`) gains `claude.finished_marker` and `codex.completion_event`,
  each with its reader, and `host_adapter.report_forms(host=...)` validates one host's rows whole: a row missing or of
  the wrong type is no forms for that host, never a default in code. The Codex completion event's name is read from it
  too (`native_stop`): with the file gone a completed rollout is no return and the evidence says why (AR-1, AR-22)
- `story_step pause` of a dispatch whose host worker has handed back passes with no person's words; when the controller
  still refuses it for a host worker, ONE line after the refusal gives that dispatch's liveness state and its door
  (wait and ask `where`; the person's `release`; a recorded cancellation) (OH3-16, FR-1, FR-2)
- A host receipt of a dispatch the controller no longer holds `running` is not an active worker (`worker_lifecycle.
  active_binding` asks `binding_is_active`, the reader the spawn guard already uses): its receipt stays `running` on a
  host whose stop hook never marks it terminal, and the checkpoint veto kept treating a dispatch the controller had
  settled as a worker still at work; every doubt (no story named, no controller, no status) keeps it active as before,
  and the spawn guard is unchanged (OH3-16)

- The story goes on to the next stage in the same window after gate A or gate B is recorded (`skills/qa-story/SKILL.md`,
  `phases/s4.md`, `phases/s8.md`): the unconditional "stop with one line ... continue with /qa-factory:qa-story" after a
  gate (since 0.7.11) and gate B's "end your window" are gone, so the person is no longer made to restart a factory that
  could have gone on (GW1-12). The window changes only when the factory's window budget says so, and the one planned
  stop left is the project's `pipeline.stop_after`; the steps a decision authorized (publication after A, delivery
  after B) still run in the window that recorded it before any stop or window change.
- The `gate-decision` answer of `controller.py` leads with what to do next and says whether the window changes
  (`controller.py`, `window_budget.py`, `story_step.py`): `next_action` is the first key and now has `pipeline.stop_after`
  applied (`stop` past the named gate), `window` is `{verdict: fits|change|unknown, line}` (`null` with a stop), and the
  whole receipt stays last under `decision`. `window_budget.window_verdict` asks the same `remaining >= need` question
  right after a gate is recorded, read-only on the recorded stage costs; a measure that cannot be taken is `unknown`,
  never `fits`. The one reader of `pipeline.stop_after` moved from `story_step.py` into `controller.py` and `story_step`
  calls it. A `turns.window` of zero or less is the default window, not the 20-turn floor.
- The between-stages turn notice no longer tells the orchestrator to close the window and stop (`turn_budget.py`): it
  defers to the WINDOW BUDGET line and goes on with the next stage when there is none.

- A stand integration the project recorded at onboarding (`environment.integrations[]`) whose keys are not where the runner reads them is
  named at gate A, in "After your approval", before the person approves (`gate_preflight.py`, `check_s5_credentials`; TP1-12586: the
  Jira integration was known since onboarding and the person learned of it in S5, and only because they had asked to be told). A
  `required_by` that equals an id of this story (a plan row, an obligation of its rows, a profile its automate cases run on, a case area)
  (the whole id as written, never a part of a longer word: `TS-1` does not tie `TS-10`, `TS-10 needs it` ties nothing)
  ties the cases it names: one stand-gap card per case and integration, in the existing card form, answered with the existing words
  (`myself`, `run`, `accept`; `change` is never offered on a secret) and read by the same recorder, gate B carry and delivery check.
  Anything else (the prose "api: Jira datasources and tools" is the 12586 shape) is never read as words: it is ONE question for the whole
  story naming the integration, the project's own words for who needs it and the missing key names inside the first 200 characters the
  brief shows, with the three ways out written under it (put the keys there yourself, accept the gap, or tell the conductor which cases
  use it). Key names only, never a value (GW1-13, AR-22, AR-23, AR-24, AR-28)
- The brief lists a missing integration first among the rows it shows, so it is not behind "+N more"; an integration whose keys are all set
  is one report line there ("whether they reach it is not proved before the automated run"), not a question (GW1-13, F-3)
- `check_s5_credentials` reads the keys where the runner reads them, through `_loaded_env_files` and `_env_names` (the reader
  `check_case_preconditions` already uses): a project that lists `environment.env_files` or loads its files in a conftest is no longer told
  a key is missing that sits in a file the runner loads; a project that names only `environment.env_file` sees no change. The login
  question says "and N more" when it names more than eight keys instead of dropping the rest. An integration with
  `credential_alternatives` is asked only when no alternative is satisfied, and then for the alternative nearest to it (GW1-13, AR-13)

- The install smoke checks the host's handback form (`scripts/install_smoke.py`): a synthetic probe child whose only
  answer comes back through the host's handback call must read as delivered, a synthetic Claude Code worker that handed
  its report back must read as `returned`, and one with a row after the handback must not. Every name (tool, acknowledgement,
  sidecar marker) is read from `references/host-report-forms.json` through `host_adapter.report_forms()`, so a missing or
  malformed forms file makes the smoke FAIL with the reason instead of passing.

## 0.10.0 — 2026-10-21 — the finish gate reads the exit gate, the conductor's roads are one driver, and the Codex rollout's fixes come home

Scope note: this release does not yet enforce by code that the S3 plan is complete against the grounding table (the
requirements vocabulary, the diff reader and the table itself ship below; the completeness gate follows in 0.10.1). The
guard of assignments on the walk and the walk analogs (CX2-23, CX2-14) also follow in 0.10.1.

- Prices as data for the closed questions of the story (conductor/1, C1-3 node A; P22): `references/question-prices.json`
  (one top-level key `questions`, one loader `no_move.load_question_prices`, one price-row resolution `no_move.price_row` shared
  with the conductor's `fallback`) holds the three price lines of every option of the halt question, the S1 source gap and
  review, the no-diff question, the question-threshold stop and the two package questions. The words of each option stay in
  `story_run.py`; `Driver.closed_question` renders them with the lines from the data, and a data file that cannot be read shows
  the question without price lines and files one `defect_found` (a question is never withheld for its prices).
- The halt question now lists its answers with their prices (your own words, or `stop`); `stop` as the whole answer holds the
  question (exit 3) without a conductor call and without filing the words for the role. When the scout's manifest says no
  change was found (`implementation.source: none`), the halt is the no-diff question with its three answers and `stop`; like
  every halt it lists what the scout reported and says when the scout stopped again.
  `handoff_check.manifest_impl_source` is the one reader of the manifest's three shapes of that field.
- The question-threshold stop lists `go on` and `stop` beside the answers by id; a whole answer `go on` is the person's pass
  (`waiver.py`, block `question threshold`) and does not resume the role; `stop` holds the question. `question_stop.batch_text`
  takes the rendered price lines and puts them above the answer block.
- `human_text.price_problems` checks every option line under "What each answer costs and does", with a token or without
  one; the S1 gap text no longer promises that `retry` runs the collection again (no executor read it).
- The nine questions S0 can ask (the ticket that could not be read, a title taken from the first line, a ticket with no
  criteria, the list of sources not to read in its three forms, two launch sources, the stand, the readiness check) list
  their answers as option lines with the three price lines under each, from the same data file. Every one of them now takes
  `stop` as a whole answer: the question is held (exit 3) with a first line that says nothing runs and nothing is spent, no
  conductor is called, and no words are kept for the next step; `stop please` is other words and is asked again as before.
  The late list-of-sources question gets `stop` as the door of its "start again from a fresh copy" option, which had none.
  A price row the data lacks leaves the option lines without prices and files one `defect_found`; the question is still asked.

- An answer the story's closed questions cannot read now goes to the conductor instead of bouncing back with "nothing moved"
  (conductor/1, C1-3 node B; P22, D-0041). It applies to the S0 stops, the `package` questions and the changed-ticket
  question, and to a refusal the run itself ends with when an answer's words are on the record. Every `--answer` is new
  words and is exactly one conductor call; a rerun with no `--answer` calls no one and shows the same priced question again.
  The question comes back with one lead, `Your answer "..." is not one of the answers this question takes, so nothing has
  moved yet.`, and its own option lines under it; a conductor `continue` or `retry` passes nothing, adopts nothing and
  stores no stale block, and a conductor that offers one of the question's own words (`read`, a stand's name, `new text`)
  back is honoured only for words the question reads itself. A stand named like an answer of the factory (`stop`, `retry`,
  `go on`, `restart`, `prepare the stand`) cannot be chosen by name: it is left out of the stand question and one finding
  names it.
- Three exits that told the person to run the same command by hand are questions now: a ticket that was said to be "not
  needed" with nothing read, a ticket with no title at all, and a lost tracker login (at S0 and at the freshness check of a
  story that is already running). Each lists its answers (`retry`, the ticket as text, `not needed` where the story can go
  without it, `stop`) with the three price lines. The freshness question's `go on` records that the look was skipped and holds
  for the freshness window, so a later run inside it does not ask again.
- A second `stop` at a held question no longer stacks the first line; the scout's "Launch flags" line keeps the flags the
  story was launched with after an answer; the question the run asks while a stage is stuck names the stage it is stuck at.

- A rework that carries a person's words sets aside what runs after it (conductor/1, C1-4a; P22; `controller.py`): `rework
  --words-file` now writes a `rerun_after` stamp on the dispatch request - the completed stages after the reworked one (up to
  S8), the accepted review of the reworked stage's closing role over the reworked cases, and the approved gate decisions after
  it - and the journal replay lowers those stages to `pending`, stales the reviews (each carries `stale_by_rework`, naming the
  rework) and the gate decisions (staled by status, no mark), and leaves a `skipped` stage alone. A reason typed by code
  (`--reason`: the driver's repairs, the conductor's refusal repairs), a rework of a closed story and the ticket-changed road
  keep today's flow with no stamp. The controller refuses a stamp it did not build, naming the field (`rerun_after.stages`,
  `.reviews`, `.decisions`, `rework_of`): an unapproved decision, gate A past S4, gate B past S8, a review that is not an
  accepted dispatch of the stage's closing role (or is the reworked role's own), a stamp on a request with no `rework_of`.
  `invalidate` and the
  stamp share one staling helper; `pipeline.json` drops `rerun_after`, `code_only`, `receipt_id` and the later-work marks of a
  stage that no longer carries them. Nothing in the driver uses the stamp yet.

- A gate is approved by its own word, and any other words go to the conductor (conductor/1, C1-4b; P22; `story_run.py`,
  `references/gate-approval-words.json`, `references/conductor-actions.json`): at gate A and gate B the driver records the
  gate decision only when the FIRST non-empty line of the answer is the approval word (`approve`, read with the one token
  normalizer: BOM, quotes, one closing full stop, case and spaces) or when the person chose `approve` from the options the
  conductor offered. The rest of an answer under the word is read as before (the cards of gate A, the stand-gap lines and bug
  numbers of gate B) and kept whole in the decision; an unreadable stand-gap line still keeps the decision from being recorded
  by code. Any other words are never recorded as an approval and never kept as one: they reach the conductor whole, which
  offers the moves open at the gate with their prices (`rework`, `approve`, `retry`, `stop`; `go on` is closed at a gate). The
  conductor never records a gate decision itself. `rework` sends a stage back to its role with the person's words and, through
  the controller's `rerun_after` stamp, makes the stages after it run again; a second such rework of a stage that is already
  waiting to run again stamps its own window too. The gate is then shown again with a line saying which words were worked on
  and which stages ran again. A stand-gap record the story refused is no longer put back to the person ("send your whole answer
  again"): it goes to the conductor once with the failed line and the refusal. Both gate packets state the approval word, read
  from the same data file the check reads; an unreadable word list approves nothing and names no word. An answer an older
  driver kept as "the person's decision" (prose) is handed to the conductor once and is not described as refused. The
  `rework_stage` move now has the token `rework` and the price `stages_again`; a new `approve_gate` move has the token `approve`.

- A person's word for "one more repair round" now passes exactly one round (conductor/1, C1-5 node A; P22). The controller's refusal of a round past the repair cap, and of a mechanical round past its cap or for a reviewer, starts with the pass of that round (`round pass <n> for <role> on <stage>:<hash>` / `mechanical pass <n> for <role> on <stage>:<hash>`, built by one function from the window's ledger key) and prints the recording command for it; the pass of the author and of the critic travel in `repair_budget.passes` of the dispatch packet. Before, the single stage-wide word `repair round` passed every later past-cap round of every window for both roles; words recorded that way earlier still pass, since the sentence after the pass still holds them. The conductor's rework move names the pass of the refused round, as the refusal prints it, for both roles. A dispatch a rework of its own stage set aside (an S5 rework staling the S5 critic) keeps counting as a paid round, so the person's word no longer resets the critic's cap; one an earlier stage's rework set aside opens a new window, and the pass key then carries that rework's id (the window's life), so a word recorded for a round of the old life never opens the same round of the new one; the reviewer's mechanical pass number counts by the same rule. The packet checkpoint and cumulative budget refusals name the limits they hit and the way on. `references/question-prices.json` gains the priced answers of the repair-limit questions (`s5.repair_limit`, `s5.nobody_review`, `s5.nobody_environment`, `s5.nobody_tooling`, `s7.repair_limit`); their sites arrive with the driver nodes.

- An S5 window whose repair limit is spent, whose repair count cannot be read, whose rejection is nobody's to repair, or whose verdict sends the tests back naming no blocking finding is no longer closed in silence (conductor/1, C1-5 node B1; P22). The driver asks the person ONE closed, priced question BEFORE the code critic's finish (in `run_role`, `resume_role` and the recovery road of a saved critic result), with no paid call: `round` (the test writer repairs, the critic reviews again; the person's word is recorded as the controller's two round passes, one per role, so it passes exactly one round), `debt` (the window closes and is written to `work/review-debts.json` through the ledger's one writer), `fixed` (the person changed the tests; the critic's pass only) and `stop`. A rejection nobody can repair asks by its cause: `s5.nobody_environment` (`fixed` after the person fixes the stand), `s5.nobody_review` (`review`: the critic looks again, spending none of the cap), `s5.nobody_tooling` (`debt` or `stop`, the factory's defect filed). The question says in words how many times the critic sent the tests back and what the limit is, so each round asks with a changed body; a count the controller cannot report offers only `debt` and `stop`; a controller that reports no passes is refused by name. The close of the last window and the recovery road (`completion_for`) follow the same rule: a critic's finish closes S5 only over a route with no seam reason, or over the recorded `debt`. The "every window is accepted but S5 is still open" refusal no longer names `waiver.py`: it points to `controller recover`. `repair_route.route` carries the seam reason of a close (`cap`, `unknown`, `mech_cap`, `nobody`, `sent_back`). The fix round after the integration review closes the roads the first cut left open: a round the controller did not count is asked as an unreadable count instead of closing the window; a tooling finding of a review that closes over a question is still told and filed as the factory's defect, once; a round the person chose is marked as run only after the stand and build checks, so a stand question cannot swallow it; a recovery that finishes a critic whose route still owes the test writer an ordinary round runs that round on the next entry instead of stopping at the "still open" refusal; the questions list each finding as "<test> - <what the critic said>" and name the round that is bought on a limit not spent; the passes the driver writes are pinned against the real controller and the real `waiver.py`. An answer `debt` to the question about an owed round consumes the round: the debt is recorded as on the first road, the window closes over it (the critic's finish is completed by the same rule as the debt of the first road), no round runs, and the next entry does not stop at the "still open" refusal; the same answer given again changes nothing.

- The S7 repair loop no longer gives up on a failing test in silence, and S7 now stays OPEN until its repairs end. While the failure analyst's triage holds tests whose fault is the test itself, the analyst's finish leaves
  S7 open on a pair the controller accepts (`repairs_pending` and a timeless reason that lists the tests), the repairs run inside
  the open stage, and when they end the driver closes S7 by code: `finalize_task`, then the `code_only` receipt, then
  `stage_done` with the analyst's digest and what happened to the repairs (`repairs: fixed=R not_fixed=D stopped=N`). A story
  already past S7 is untouched. A failure of the current run that has no row in the triage (for instance after a person's rework
  of an earlier stage) sends S7 back to the analyst and is never closed over. When the cap of a test is spent, or the count cannot
  be read, the driver asks the person ONE closed, priced question per test, count and triage run, with no paid call: `round` (the
  test writer repairs that test once more and it is run again; the person's word is recorded as the controller's round pass for
  the test writer on that window, so it passes exactly one round), `debt` (the repairs of that test stop for good in this triage
  run; the test is written to `work/review-debts.json` as an S7 window naming the test by the ledger's own reference, the one the
  report's `Runs left failing` section matches) and `stop`. A test no test of the plan answers is recorded under the run's own name
  and the question says it is not yet listed in the report. There is no `fixed` here: running a test again
  after the person's own edit is the test run's job, not a repair round. A count the controller cannot report offers only `debt`
  and `stop`, and no round is started blind; a controller that reports no passes is refused by name. A test is asked once per
  count; a rerun or a later loop turn at the same count asks nothing, and a test left in debt is not asked again when a sibling of
  the same case moves the count. Within one triage run a test is known by its own row in the analyst's triage, never by what the
  test plan lists at the moment: the repair round rewrites the plan, so the references the plan gave a test are read once, when the
  repairs of that triage run begin, and kept. A test repaired by a round is not repaired again, and the person's answer is found
  again, however the plan changed in between. An answered `round` is marked as run before the round is dispatched and taken back
  when the controller refuses to start it, so the person's round is never run twice and never lost while the stage is open. A person's
  recorded decision on the analyst's dispatch outranks the close: `close` dispatches no further round; `open_work`
  keeps the stage open while the repairs run, and when every test's repairs have ended the driver asks the person ONE closed, priced
  question that quotes the words they kept it open with - close the stage now (one receipt written by the factory's own commands,
  nothing run again) or stop. Unanswered, the question is asked again on every step and nothing is closed over it; `stop` is held and
  comes back on a rerun; the person's `close` closes the stage by code on the next step. The S7 answers live apart from the S5 windows' (`repair_limit_s7`), so no S5 reader meets them.
  An accepted analyst whose triage leaves a failure of the current run report unbound is never trusted, and a failure with no name at
  all counts as unbound: S7 is triaged again instead of being closed over it - once: when that second triage still leaves a failure without a verdict, the
  driver asks the person (naming the failure) and does not pay for a third. When the person has recorded that S7 stays open for
  more work, the driver's "same step four times" stop says the factory asks them before it closes the stage, in one line instead of
  "I cannot tell what is holding it".

- The report and the gate B packet now say which tests the code critic rejected when a window closed at its repair limit, and what the
  critic asked (conductor/1, C1-5 node C; P22): a new report block `facts:review-gaps` stands right after `facts:bugs` (a marked report
  written before it gets the block from `report_facts.py --write`), and gate B lists the same lines under "Rejected by the code critic".
  Per window one line says how many rounds were spent against the limit and what the person chose; per test the critic's own words
  (the problem, what it expected, what to fix) follow, or the plain statement that the remarks were not recorded. Both surfaces call
  ONE renderer, `report_facts.review_gap_lines`. Runs of S7 left failing at their limit stand under their own heading with the
  triage's words. The head's residual names the windows ("repair limit exhausted on N windows").
- `work/review-debts.json` (new) is the record of those windows: written only by `ledger.write_review_debt`, read only by
  `ledger.build`, which joins it to the critic's form (`repair_route.findings`, now keeping `file`, `line`, `expected` and `fix` too,
  each cut at 300 characters with an ellipsis) and puts `remarks`, `repair_limit` and `repair_windows` into `ledger.json`. A story
  without the file reads exactly as before; a rejected test no window covers is printed with "the critic's remarks were not recorded".
- `check_delivery.mark_handed` restates the rows of a case whose `request.json` says `refused.by: person_checks` as handed to the
  person (the third verdict, `after_checks`), once, beside the manifest's own handed rows.
- The review-gaps block and the gate B section now list every test an S5 window speaks for, whatever happened to it afterwards (it
  failed at S6, was triaged at S7, or was delinked: "(the test no longer exists)"), so the critic's words never drop out of the
  report. The function names and the critic's words pass the same filter the verdict's reds use: words the report may not carry (a
  `work/` path, a `ti_` / `cv_` hash) are left out of the quotation and the row says once "(a path in the critic's words was
  shortened)", so the report is never refused over its own block. A run's failure line names its source: "the run's reason: ..." is
  `results[].reason` of the run report, or "the run recorded no reason". A record entry the reader cannot read is named by its place
  in the problem line and kept as it stands on every rewrite; a file nothing of which can be read is left untouched and the writer
  says so. Gate B reads the ledger inside the guard of the delivery word, so two differing copies are said, not a crash.

- The conductor's question is no longer thrown away over the style of its quotes (conductor/1, C1-5d1; P22; `no_move.py`):
  `validate_options` reads the tokens the prose names in any quote style - backticks, single or double quotes, the typographic
  pairs - and refuses the question only when it names a token of the closed vocabulary (a move's own word or a door of the
  site) that is not among the options, with the reason naming that token ("the question names `retry`, which is not one of its
  options"); a prose that names fewer tokens than the options is shown as it is, an apostrophe inside a word ("the scout's") is
  never a quote, a quoted span that is no token (a file name) is ignored, and an empty question is still refused. Before, a
  question that quoted its tokens with apostrophes fell back to the generic question and its paid answer was lost (cmp3, S1).
  `references/conductor.md` says what the option token `retry` (move `person_does`) means: the person does the work outside the
  factory, then the factory looks again; it never resumes or reruns a role.

An exit-gate refusal that survives the resume limit is now a question to the person instead of a dead end. When a role has been sent back once over the exit gate's findings and the same set comes back (or the role has no session to resume), the driver asks one closed, priced question in the story's words: `round` (one more paid turn of the role in its own session, with the check's exact lines and the person's words), `fresh` (the dispatch is released through the controller and the role starts again with the check's lines and the files it left), `go on` (the lines that reached the question are passed one waiver row each, the sources' open work is closed through `accept-gap --point`, and the pass is filed as a factory finding) and `stop`. `go on` is not offered while a handover-form line remains, and every absent option is said. The same question serves the handoff ladder, the refusal road, a resume whose session is gone and the structured-artifact repeat; no conductor call is paid for it. Waiver rows written by `go on` are revoked by one sweep when their dispatch is accepted, released or superseded. A relaunch after a person's release now carries the person's words, and `pending_words` are spent as soon as the resumed result is saved. The conductor's `restart` move no longer says, in its description and in its precondition, that the new session does not see the words: after a release the new session gets the person's words.

- A finished story no longer restarts work on its own (conductor/1, C1-6 node A; B-331; P22). When a story is closed (gate B decided, S8 done) and a dispatch of an unfinished stage never reached an agent, `next` used to answer `relaunch` and the driver ran the role with no question. Now `next` answers `closed` with `held` (stage, role, reason; no packet), the driver asks one closed question with three priced answers (`run again` / `leave` / `stop`), and the dispatch check itself refuses a `dispatch` on a closed story unless it is the retro (S9) or carries a person's reopening (`reopened_at` plus their words, making the story open by the one reading of "closed"), so the skill path cannot start the work by hand either.
