Two new controller operations carry the person's word by `--words-file`: `reopen_story --dispatch a,b` reopens the story with their words and records the set the word covers (`next` then relaunches exactly those, one at a time; held work the word did not name stays held), and `leave_unlaunched --dispatch a,b` ends the work (`superseded`, `left_by_person`, the stage completed as `person_left`, so a later reopen never prepares it again). A finished story with nothing held says "the story is finished; nothing is pending" and promises no reopening. The `rework` refusal for a role that has a live (not accepted) dispatch on the stage now names it and both ways on (resume it, or release it by the person's words). A story closed before this change carries no `reopened_at` and is read as never reopened.

- The S6 stops ask with prices, and code carries out every answer (conductor/1, C1-6 node B; P22). The stand sign-in question (`retry` / `by hand` / `go on`), the stand-confirmation question (the stand's name / `retry` / `go on`) and the new question for a plan whose manual rows were approved at a gate A that was recorded dry (`reapprove` / `go on` / `stop`) each carry three price lines per answer (the factory, the person, the story) and are raised as questions of the seam: `retry` and `go on` are carried out by the seam's own executors (`waiver.py --words-file`), so the two site-own executors that recorded the pass with an inline `--decision` are gone. `by hand` and `go on` at the sign-in question are two records now (the request of each screen case says `refused.by: person_checks` or `left_unchecked`; a pass the conductor recorded from free words reads `left_unchecked`), so the delivery check can tell a case the person takes from a case nobody checks. A dry gate A used to print a line and go on; `reapprove` now reopens the test design review and asks gate A again (the controller's `semantic_reopen`), `go on` records the person's word for the block `gate A recorded dry`, and the question is not asked again once passed. The free-words prompts of the two stand questions hand the words to the conductor by file, not inline.

- The delivery no longer ends in a promise nobody carries out (conductor/1, C1-6 node C; P22, FR-9, FR-48). A report that does not match the answers recorded at gate B used to stop with a note that sent the person to start the report writer by hand; now it is a closed question with three price lines per answer (`no delivery` / `stop`; the mismatch lines are its lead, the gap is the factory's own and never put as a choice to own it). A delivery check that crashes, times out or prints nothing readable used to stop with "the factory will look at it", which nobody did; now it files ONE defect (owner: factory) and asks (`retry` runs the check again at once / `no delivery` / `stop`). The delivery step's own questions (`ask_person`, `stop`, an answer it did not understand) are priced and keyed by the verdict word the check printed: `go on` and `retry` are two distinct records (`delivery_choice`, read by the delivery step and spent after its call), `go on` costs one more session of the conductor and says that verdict word (never "ready to ship" on "ready once you finish the checks"; on that word its person line is the checks left with them), `no delivery` ends the delivery with nothing sent, `stop` holds the question. The second hand-over of the delivery in one run no longer tells the person to run the driver again: it says to answer `retry`. The delivery prompt names the tokens `go on` / `retry`. New price class `conductor` ("one more session of the conductor") in `conductor-actions.json`.

- Driver (conductor/1 C1-7a, the owner's principle P22): a journal row the journal refused is no longer dropped or only printed. The rows of a person's words (`human_answer`), the filings of the factory's own findings (`add-finding`) and the `--warn` line of an S0 pass are now OWED when their script exits non-zero: the driver prints one line, keeps the row in `driver-state.json` (`owed_rows`), writes it again before any brief is built (right after the answer is taken, and first in every loop turn), and a row refused a second time is a question to the person (retry / go on / stop, no paid call; the text names row ids and counts, never the person's words). The person's `go on` is recorded under the new block name `journal rows not written` (a row of `references/block-names.json`), is paired with ITS question by the row ids that question carried (never by the clock, so a word given before or beside a newer question never answers it), gives those rows up (`rows_given_up`, one `rows_given_up` line in `driver-runs.jsonl`), and a later refused row of the same script is given up with no second question. Later roles read `human_answer` rows as the person's standing instructions, so a lost row used to remove the person's words from every later brief without a word.
- Driver: `py(check=True, expect=...)` raises a refusal that says what the step was to leave behind and what the door is, carries the mark `known = False` (the mark that the known-refusals routing of the next change, C1-7b, reads so that a phrase of the step's own output never routes it; nothing reads it yet), keeps `expect` on its retry, and a script that runs past its time ceiling now raises under `check=True` instead of returning exit 124 unchecked. `py_trace(script, ..., why=...)` runs a script nothing decides on, with a mandatory reason, and journals a failure as `trace_failed` in `driver-runs.jsonl` (the story's dashboard refresh and the defect line of a package-copies pass use it).
- Driver: pasted material that could not be recorded (a failed `inspect`, or a block no open item can be named for) comes back as the person's own question naming what is recorded and what is not, and a fenced answer is never also taken as accepting the gap. A mode-switch pass that could not be recorded comes back as the person's question and keeps the mode question, so the next `go on` is the mode switch's again and never the package-copies pass.
- Audit A27: the baseline shrinks by the 24 sites above (102 to 78).

- Driver (conductor/1 C1-7b, the owner's principle P22): a factory script the driver ran and whose exit it dropped is no longer a silent pass where a later decision reads what the script was to write. These steps now raise a refusal of the factory's own when the script exits non-zero (a timeout included): the readiness file at the start of the story, the case appendix at the end of S4, the "S6 running" record before a manual block, the ledger at S8 (its retry runs the whole S8 step again) and the retro numbers before S9 is recorded complete. The refusal says which step did not complete, what it was to leave behind and the door (retry), and it is never routed by a phrase of the step's own output (`already completed`, `STORY BUDGET`, ... no longer turn it into `continue`): it reaches the conductor, so the person gets the priced choice instead of a story that goes on over an unwritten file. A retry of the readiness step goes on with the rest of S0.
- Driver: the readiness check at S0 (`readiness.py --require`) is read from its JSON record and not from its exit code: a missing capability is the person's question as before, a record with nothing missing goes on, and a crash, a usage error or an empty answer is the factory's own refusal (it used to pass silently, or be put to the person as "something required is missing"). The S8 verdict check (`check_delivery.py`) is read from its record too: a correct `no` is an answer, an unreadable record is the factory's own refusal before the report writer reads a ledger the check did not write. The traceability check's exit 1 stays a plain answer.
- Driver: five traces that nothing decides on (the question-stop `halted` record, the repair-budget defect line, the S5 tooling-finding line, the defect filer's own failure and the S9 estimate) go through `py_trace`: a failure is one printed line and a `trace_failed` row in `driver-runs.jsonl` with the reason it is safe, and it never stops the story. The person's retro-skip words are an owed journal row (C1-7a's ladder).
- Audit A27: the blind spot B3 is closed (a branch `if code: print(...)` that only prints is no longer counted as a read of the exit), and the baseline shrinks by the 11 sites above (78 to 67).

- Driver (conductor/1 C1-7c, the owner's principle P22): the last six places where the driver ran a factory script and dropped its exit now follow the same rule as the stage functions of C1-7b. The `running` stage record written before a role is resumed on the person's words and before a relaunched dispatch starts is a gate: a non-zero exit is a refusal of the factory's own that names the step, what it was to leave behind and the dispatch, the role is not started over it, and its retry writes the record and then runs the role once (the registered dispatch is never run a second time behind the refusal). The record has ONE writer (`Driver.record_running`), which writes nothing on a stage the controller has already completed (later work of an accepted stage: a rework, a repair), because the stage record refuses `running` there by design and no retry could cure it. A dispatch the driver finds registered but never launched (a conductor's `continue` over a refused record) now starts with the same record, the role lines and, for a relaunched packet, the relaunch reason (the fresh line and the person's release words). At gate B the ledger is rewritten over the person's answers and the merge-request description is rewritten at the end: a failed ledger or description is a refusal, never a delivery over a stale file, and its retry runs the whole S9 step again; the traceability check's exit 1 stays a plain answer with its reason. The `halted` stage record written right before a halt's question goes through `py_trace`: a failure is one `trace_failed` row with the reason it is safe, the person is asked about the halt all the same, and the role is not run again for it. Audit A27: the baseline shrinks by these six sites (57 to 51). Tests: the stubs of `Driver.py` in five test files now take `check` and `expect` like the real one and forward both (a forwarding pin over the counted stubs, plus a check for a stub that takes `check` and returns a non-zero exit without raising; three known stubs of one test file are queued).

- Audit A27 (conductor/1 C1-8, the owner's principle P22; `python -B scripts/audit_factory.py --no-move`) finds the driver's states without a move outside the one seam `Driver.no_move`: a `Person`, `Stop` or `InfraStop` built outside it (or a call of a function that returns one, followed through any depth of unannotated wrappers), and a factory script run (`self.py` / `self.py_stdout`) whose result is dropped or only printed. A site that must stay carries `# remains: <reason>` on its statement's first line or on the comment-only line above it; an empty reason, an orphan door, or one door over two sites is a finding. Today's 105 sites are an exact-count, shrink-only baseline in `audit_factory.NO_MOVE_BASELINE` (a cap `NO_MOVE_BASELINE_MAX` that must equal the sum), keyed by file, function, class and a discriminator, so a swap of two different sites inside one function stays red. A27 also pins that only `Driver._ask_conductor` calls `self.conductor` and that `run_claude("conductor", ...)` stands only in `Driver.conductor` and `Driver.delivery`. It reads the driver set only (`story_run.py` and `driver_*.py`), not the package's other scripts. It runs from `test_audit_rules.py` (CI `package-fast`), not from the project doctor, and prints a census with its blind spots under the header. FR-42's check line names it.

- `detector_verdict.py` (new), `exit_gate.py`: the exit gate reads the WHOLE verdict of a detector, not its last three
  lines (`detector_errors`) or four (`witness_errors`): one record per finding, in the order printed. A role refused for
  four findings is shown all four and repairs them in one turn (cmp3, S5: four rounds, one finding each). The list the
  hook prints and the receipt keeps is cut by BYTES (6000), never by lines, and past the ceiling it says how many are left
  and names the file that holds all of them, `state/findings/exit-gate-<role>.txt` under the task root (class K1).
- `detector_verdict.py`: one contract for the output of the five `stages.json` detectors and `check_witness.py` - the whole
  verdict on stdout, a header `REJECT — N`, then exactly N lines, one finding each (a label `[check id]` after the `- `,
  the repair on the same line after ` — fix: `). `parse` is the one reader of it (the exit gate, `check_delivery`'s
  witness reasons, the audit's A17); output that does not follow the contract is shown whole as one record, never cut,
  and a refusal that printed nothing is a defect with a door (the role's digest), never a pass. Also here: `render` (the
  byte ceiling and its pointer), `refusal_text` and `split_items` (the reader of the controller's combined refusal head,
  for C2-2 and the driver's routing, which follows in C2-1s).
- `s5_precheck.py`: one line per finding (`- [check id] message — fix: fix`), the header says the recorded words were judged
  at the source (`(words judged at source)`), and a finding the source refused to every word - a family no word can pass, or
  a `changed-after-red` word given before the pair's green run - has its own `WORDS_REFUSED_AT_SOURCE: <id> <cause>` line
  above the header. The footer names the person's door only for what a word can pass. A word copied from the printed
  line now matches at the source exactly when it matches the gate's record.
- `exit_gate.py`: `judge_words` replaces the single `split_overridden` call. Each record is judged by the rule of the
  producer that wrote it: a finding the producer already judged at its source, and output not in the contract's form, are
  not passed by a NAMED word (that would be the substring match of t-108 over what the producer refused); the person's
  word `*` passes them, except what the source refused with its tag (`family`, `predating`), which no word passes, `*`
  included. A defect of the detector itself carries no repair marker, so the driver does not send the role to repair it.
- `planning_contract.py`, `critic_rollcall.py`, `check_coverage.py`, `check_witness.py`: every REJECT carries its count and
  the whole verdict is on stdout (`check_coverage` and `check_witness` printed theirs to stderr, where a WARN list on the
  other stream hid it); no `[:10]` cut; the "rows to repair" repeat line of the S3 exit is gone, its summary line stays as
  a tail; the hand-made executable obligation's refusal line names every problem, not the first.
- For one release the gate keeps the pre-C2-1 summary record of each refused detector: a word a person recorded against
  that old text (its prefix, its door line, its last lines) still passes the plain records of that detector, as it passed the
  whole detector before. It blocks nothing and is shown to nobody; the next release removes it (F-13 of t-720).
- `story_run.py` (C2-1s, the driver's half of class K1): the texts a role is resumed with over an exit-gate refusal no longer
  show the first eight (the resume), eight (the mechanical third turn) or six (the `Refusal`) of N findings. Each says `N finding(s)`
  and carries every line, whole, up to the byte ceiling (the one renderer, `detector_verdict.render`); past it, the count that is
  left and the path of the file that holds the whole list, `state/findings/<dispatch>-handoff.txt`. The lines the code filled
  into the role's form (were 12) and the material it fetched (were 8) go through the same renderer (`-filled.txt`, `-collected.txt`).
  A dry run names no file it did not write. Also here: `route_known` replaces `match_known` over the whole text of a refusal that
  is a LIST - the exit gate's findings, and the controller's combined refusal (`N problems - the request is refused whole, every
  one is listed:`, C2-2) read through both of its transports (`story_step: refused - ...` and the JSON-escaped `--operation
  decision` line). Every item is routed on its own and the route is taken only when all items agree; a marker or phrase of
  one item no longer leads the rest, and a head whose items do not match its count goes to the conductor, never to a match over
  the text. A single refusal is routed byte for byte as before.

- One refusal for every independent defect (conductor/2, C2-2; class K1 "one at a time"): the controller no longer raises the
  FIRST problem of a request. `decision` and the S5 completion collect `(class, message)` problems and `Controller._raise_all`
  refuses them whole: one problem is its own sentence, unchanged; several are one text headed `N problems - the request is
  refused whole, every one is listed:` with `1) ...` lines (equal messages folded as `(xK)`, the class that of the first
  problem). The S5 completion runs in tiers: no window object, or a window of the wrong shape, stops with a sentence that says the
  other checks did not run; every other check (code-review receipts, scope map keys, empty instances, coverage, schema, author and
  critic, mechanical round, per-instance obligation refs, input hash, source revision, quality checks) is collected, a helper that
  refuses ends the tier as the last line, and `validate_window` runs only on a clean list, so it cannot fall over a field an
  earlier check refused. The code-review receipts stand FIRST in every tier (fix round t-791): a refusal for a missing or
  misshapen window record never hides a missing receipt, and a person's word that passes the record still lets the receipts
  refuse.
- The gate rehearsal names every defect of an open question in its one finding and no longer cuts the plan-contract violations
  at eight; a blocked-by-env remedy with several problems is refused with all of them in one line.
- `design/controller-blocks.md` now walks the collected `(class, message)` problems too (227 blocks), generated by
  `tools/controller-blocks-gen.py`, held to the source by `test_controller_blocks.py`.

- Scope keys of a manifest cell (conductor/3, C3-12; `contract.py`, `controller.py`): `contract.scope_keys(cell)` is the one
  rule for which keys a window may use for an `unresolved[]` cell - the exact text always, plus each bare id when the cell is a
  compound of ids only (`TC-001/TC-002/TC-003`); `speakers/TC-009` is an area key and answers to itself only. `case_ids` is
  unchanged (the ledger and `check_result_rows` still match by it). `Controller._cases_without_instances` is keyed through it,
  so the S5 completion no longer calls an area-keyed case with no instance "stray" ("it does not carry ...") when the manifest
  row is there, and `story_step.py decide --hand` works on a story with area keys. A cell the manifest holds twice is read from
  the later row only when that row is also a no-instance reason (`impossible` / `handed_to_person`); a later row with another
  reason does not override the earlier one. `decide --hand` writes a bare handed row back in the scope's area-keyed spelling.

- A stage closed by code now stays closed by code after `stage_done` (`controller.py`): the driver writes the `code_only` receipt and then runs `stage_done --status done`, and the `stage_transition` projection used to rewrite the stage entry as `{status, reason}`, erasing `code_only` and `receipt_id`. `s6_closed_by_code` (S7 entry, `check_delivery`) was therefore false for every S6 closed by code, and a story whose S6 had nothing to execute stopped at the door of S7. The second close of an already closed stage (never a reworked one) now carries over the run marks (`rerun_after`, `code_only`, `receipt_id`, `later_work_status`, `later_work_settled`) under its new status and reason; a stage that was reworked and closed again by a real run still gets the fresh entry, and a stage without marks gets the entry it always got (C3-14).

- project environment resolver (`scripts/project_env.py`): `resolve(project_root, profile, environ)` chooses the environment a
  project's tests should run in, from the project and not from the factory's own interpreter, in the order the profile's
  wrapper (`poetry run`, `uv run`, a venv python), the active virtual environment when it lies under the project root, the
  package manager the profile names (Poetry: `poetry env info -p` run in the project without the activation variables, a
  foreign environment refused), a `.venv` or `venv` folder from the commands' cwd up to the project root, and the inherited
  environment. The result names its `source`, a `where` that is never an absolute path, an overlay `env` (the environment's
  `Scripts` or `bin` folder first on PATH, `VIRTUAL_ENV` set) and the sources it refused with the reason. `launch_argv(argv,
  env)` resolves `argv[0]` on the overlay PATH, because on Windows `Popen` looks a bare name up on the parent's PATH and
  `env=` does not change that. `python -B scripts/project_env.py <project_root> [--profile <config.json>] [--json]` prints
  which environment the factory would use for a root, and exits 2 with one line for a root that does not exist. No run,
  no record and no person text changes in this part (C3-18 part 2 wires the launch sites)

- The run marks of a stage entry (`rerun_after`, `code_only`, `receipt_id`, `later_work_status`, `later_work_settled`) now follow ONE rule for every writer of the entry (`controller.py`, `_carry_run_marks`, the transition table above `STAGE_RUN_MARKS`): a late `accept` with `stage_complete` on a stage closed by code (`set_stage`, completed over completed, never a reworked one) keeps `code_only` and `receipt_id` exactly as the second `stage_done` close already did, so the S7 entry check still sees the S6 as closed by code; a `state_repair` that re-closes a stage naming the dispatch a role ran no longer carries a stale `code_only` over from the entry it replaces (a repair naming no dispatch ran nothing and keeps the receipt). A stage lowered or closed again by a real run still gets the fresh entry (C3-20).

- `detector_verdict.py` (conductor/3, C3-8/9 part A; class K1 "the first of N"): three helpers beside `render`, the one carrier of a computed list that is not a block. `joined` is the list in ONE line: every item, or the items that fit a ceiling and one trailing part `(+K more <noun>(s) - the whole list: <place>)` whose place is a file this very call wrote or a place the caller names; a ceiling without a place is refused, a lone line longer than the ceiling is cut at a character boundary and said so. `named` is the ids inside one finding (`a, b and K more (<where>)`, the body of `gate_preflight.named_ids`). `compound` builds the controller's combined refusal (`N problems - the request is refused whole, every one is listed:`), pinned equal to `Controller._raise_all`. Also: a labelled producer's stray `REJECT` with no count is a named defect (it was lost inside the unmigrated text), and the "unmigrated detector output" sentence and the "printed nothing" ending have one builder and one constant each (the exit gate's record is byte for byte as before).
- The sites that cut a list now show it whole or point at the rest: the handoff-form refusal (`role_digest.py`) names every error, not five; `stage_guard.py` refuses a dispatch with every reason of the order and gate A rules (and, on S6-S8, the manifest rule) in the controller's combined form with the head on a line of its own, so a router gives each reason its own part; `manifest_put.py` names every problem of a refused fragment up to the ceiling and then the count with the file `state/findings/manifest-put-<novelty|expectation>.txt` that holds all of them, and the existing-records list names where the rest is; `exit_gate.py`'s case identity gives every file its new name (a file past the sixth lost it); `report_facts.py` tells every reason a hand-check record is invalid, and every invalid record of a case, not the first; `readiness.py` names every stand problem; `planning_contract.py` and `critic_rollcall.py` say where the ids past the limit are.
- `onboard_apply.py`: no group of the onboarding listing is cut at 20 any more. The configuration change, the files moved, deleted or set aside and the git removals are what the person approves, so they are printed whole (a decision on a slice is not a decision); the other groups (kept, unknown, refused, locks) are printed whole too, because the proposal file (`--out`) holds none of them, so a "+N more" had no place to point at. The added settings and kept notes of the configuration bullet are named whole.

- The stage guard no longer lets S6-S8 pass in silence when the automation manifest is missing or cannot be read (conductor/4, C4-1). Dispatching a role of S6, S7 or S8 now refuses when `work/automation-manifest.json` is absent (S5 is not recorded as skipped by a policy, so the manifest of its instances is owed) or is there but is not a JSON object ("could not be read"); each refusal names the file, what was expected and the door (qa-automator writes it through `manifest_put.py`; `controller.py --operation recover` shows the controller's state). A manifest that is read with zero items passes as before, and so does an absent one when `pipeline.json` records S5 as skipped by a preparatory / no-implementation policy (no manifest is expected there). The refusal is one line of the dispatch guard's list (`dispatch_errors`), like the order and gate A reasons: a person's recorded word passes it with `waiver.py --stage S6 --block "is absent"` (or `"could not be read"`), the pass is journaled as a `gate_override`, and the refusal ends with that command - the word does not create the manifest, it says "go on without one". The same check shows in `stage_guard.py --ticket --stage` and in `controller.py --operation dispatch`; the commit of test code keeps its rule (S5 commits tests before the manifest exists) and S1-S5 are untouched. Registry row `SG-manifest-unread` (A24).
- Behaviour change for real stories: the unresolved-reason rule (an `unresolved[]` row whose reason is outside the closed list blocks S6-S8 and the commit of test code) now runs on the canonical layout. The guard used to read the flat `automation-manifest.json` only, so a story laid out as `artifact-registry.json` says (`work/automation-manifest.json`) was never checked. The manifest is now found at `work/automation-manifest.json` when that file exists (readable or not), and at the flat legacy name only when `work/` holds none; a stale flat copy is never read over an existing `work/` one. A story that carries such a row is refused with the message it always had; at the S6-S8 dispatch the person's word now passes it too (`waiver.py --stage S6 --block "unresolved cases without a reason"`), besides giving each case a reason from the closed vocabulary (or `deferred_by_decision:<gate>`) by re-dispatching qa-automator. The commit of test code has no stage, so its only door is still the reasons.

- Controller clean-up after the C4-4 review (conductor/4, C4-10): the per-reference loop of `accept`, `policy`, `code_only`,
  `reconcile_dispatch`, the Gate A carry and `prepare` is one helper (`Controller._ref_issues`, with `_found` for a loop over
  paths); every refusal keeps its text, its order, its class and its map row. The scope check of `dispatch` and the manual
  runner block (`validate_manual_runner_block`, also reached from `prepare`) refuse an unhashable scope entry instead of
  raising a TypeError. `_validate_gate_a_content_current` with no current Gate A decision names the drift checks it
  did not run, as its sibling chains do. A cancellation request whose `evidence_ref` or `authorization_ref` does not resolve is
  now refused as a malformed request (`ValueError`, like every other reference of a request) instead of `StateConflict`.

- A case file is looked up by its id with the NAME matched exactly on every platform (`s5_precheck.case_files_named`,
  used by `find_case_file`, `handoff_check._case_front_matter` and `judge_results._find_case_file`). `Path.rglob("TC-001.md")`
  matched `tc-001.md` on Windows and not on Linux, so the same story found its case file on a developer's machine and lost
  it in CI; now `tc-001.md` is no case file for `TC-001` anywhere, and neither is `TC-001.MD`. An id with glob characters
  is a literal name. `dashboard_refresh` compares the files it hashes by `os.path.normcase` of the path: the same file
  reached through two overlapping roots counts once, as before (no behaviour change; the intent is now stated).

- The conductor's priced options at gate A or B no longer name a price for `approve` when the question has no original answer on file (conductor/4, C4-14; the analog C2-7 left). `gate_option_rows` and `gate_prices` take `has_words` (default true, so every other call is unchanged byte for byte); the conductor prompt passes whether `asked.words_file` exists, so the prices are made of the same rows the fallback question shows. The tests that stand in for `record_by_code` now take any call (`*args, **kwargs`) and record it, so a signature the real method grows no longer breaks them or drops an argument.

- Record schema and case batch refusals list every problem (`record_schema.py`, `case_versions.py`): a record with two
  independent defects (a missing key and a wrong-typed field, two bad array items) and a case batch with several
  unreadable files or identity collisions used to be refused for the first one and again for the next, one repair per
  round. `record_schema.validate` and `case_versions.validate_batch` now raise one `ValueError` that names all of them,
  in the order the checks run, through the same combined refusal the controller writes; one problem is still its own
  sentence, unchanged. A value of the wrong type is still told alone at its place, and an unsupported schema keyword
  still raises on the spot (the schema's defect, not the record's). (C4-5)

- The four block names the factory's own code writes and reads in pairs (`question threshold`, `mode switch`, `stand not
  confirmed`, `stand login missing`) are now rows of `references/block-names.json` too, each with the code that reads it, so
  the table is the one place that says who reads a block name. A reader pointer may now name a method
  (`<module>:<Class>.<method>`): the class must stand at the top level of the module and the method be defined inside it;
  any other shape is refused naming the row. Behaviour of the writer is unchanged: these names were and stay accepted by form.

- `Redactor.residue_document(text, kind)` (`scripts/machine_facts.py`; collect/2, CL2-2): the post-check's reader for a WHOLE file.
  A JSON file is read by its string leaves (every value, and every key, after the writer's own parse), JSONL by line (a line that is
  not JSON is a unit of its own), anything else by line, and each unit goes through `residue` unchanged: the same finders, the same
  `{finder, category, view}` rows. The escaped text of a whole JSON file is not a unit the filter ever wrote, and read as one it
  flags `\\.env\\.` of the shipped config's pattern list as a UNC path. A JSON text the writer would not parse falls back to its
  lines (a false alarm at worst, never a silent pass); `residue` itself and its early exit are untouched.
- A pin that the passes a unit takes depend on its views, never on its length (`test_collect_redact.py`, operations counted, not
  seconds): a 64 KB unbroken run costs exactly what a 1-character unit costs. The quadratic time the collector saw on such a run
  sat inside the old credential-URL rule (a match attempt at every letter) and was removed from the rule in the previous fix round.

- Fifteen more JSON reads now go through `hooklib.read_json`, which gains a keyword-only `kind=` (a document of another
  type, say a list where an object is wanted, is the caller's default): `archive_task.read_json`, `stage_guard.read_json`,
  `gate_brief.read_json` (the 23 reads behind the gate brief), `retro_numbers.read_json`, `stage_done.read_pipeline`, `s5_precheck._load`, `story_budget.read_config` and
  `read_marker` and the pipeline read in `story_budget.check`, `window_budget.read_config`, `read_marks` and the pipeline
  read in `open_work`, `turn_budget.read_count`, `exit_gate._read_json`, `hooklib._json_or_none` and the story pipeline
  read of `guard_app_under_test`. Each keeps its own default and its own set of swallowed errors. Two visible changes,
  both for the better: a `pipeline.json`, `config.json` or counter file with a UTF-8 BOM is now read as data instead of
  reading as "nothing there" (so a BOM-marked archived or closed story is now seen as archived or closed by the stage
  guard), and a path given as a `str` is accepted. No pipeline, config or state file inspected in the project copies
  starts with a BOM, so nothing on record changes.
- `tests/test_read_json.py` pins the readers case by case (C5) and carries a census (G5) that fails when a new function is
  only "read this JSON file, else a constant" and neither calls `hooklib.read_json` nor has a reason in its `KEPT` list
  (forge/4, t-666).

- `host_probe.injection_marker` now issues a 32-hex challenge (was 48) and asks the diagnostic child to return
  `QA_CONTEXT_RECEIVED_<challenge>_END.`, a sentinel that belongs to the identifier instead of the trailing `.`: on
  13.10 the two probe children of TP2-2406 on Codex Desktop answered 41/48 and 47/48 characters of the 48-hex
  token and reproduced no `.`, so the S4 context proof never verified, while the 32-hex allow/deny nonces were copied
  into 24 of 24 native tool calls on the same host. A host or model that trims the last output character now trims the
  sentinel, not the challenge; the verifier does not require the sentinel (`_EN`, `_END`, `_END.` and the bare
  challenge all verify). The probe store of every earlier build is `stale` after this change (the fingerprint hashes
  `scripts/*.py`), so a proof written by the previous build is not accepted until `--prepare` is run again (CX1-2).
- `host_probe.check_child` records `status: mismatch` (with `returned`, at most 120 characters of `[0-9A-Za-z_]`, and
  `child_transcript`) when an assistant row carries `QA_CONTEXT_RECEIVED_` but no assistant row carries the whole stored
  challenge, instead of leaving `emitted`, which read like "no answer". The decision is taken after the whole scan (a
  mismatch row never masks a whole one), a `delivered` proof is never downgraded, and rows of the developer, user and
  system roles (the host's own instruction row carries the full challenge) are never read. A proof is still only the
  whole challenge: no prefix, no partial match, no structured answer. A stored challenge of any shape but 32 or 48
  lowercase hex (absent, empty, not text, another length) is not judged at all, and nothing the function reads can
  raise: a store or an event of any shape ends in no write. A child that made ANY tool call (a Claude `tool_use`
  block, a Codex `function_call`, `custom_tool_call` or `local_shell_call` row) never yields `delivered`: it may have
  read the challenge from the probe store or the launch packet instead of being handed it; its prefixed answer is
  recorded as `status: tool_used`. This rule is unmeasured on a live Codex Desktop probe (the 13.10 rollouts were not
  available): if real probe children call tools, every probe reads "not proven" until the rule is adjusted - never a
  false pass.
- `host_probe.inspect` adds `injection_detail` on a `mismatch` store while the guard is verified ("the probe child
  answered '...' (its first 47 of 48 characters match the challenge); re-probe under a new task name"; the number is
  the agreeing prefix, so a wrong last character reads 31 of 32, never 32 of 32; `returned` is cut again to
  `[0-9A-Za-z_]` when read back; a stale store or an unverified guard carries no detail, because the re-probe it names is
  refused without a verified guard), and a detail of its own on a `tool_used` store; `host_capabilities.inspect` puts it
  first in the note while the guard is verified and injection is not; `qa-doctor` tells the doctor that a partial
  answer is a re-probe. The acceptance of a `delivered` proof by its transcript hash no longer raises on a store
  that holds a wrong type there. Outcomes are unchanged: `injection: verified` only from `delivered` with its
  transcript hash, `story_ready` only with both proofs.
- `host_probe.probe_command` reads the command the guard checks (CX1-2, FR-17): the normalized event's `command`, else
  `cmd`; a raw event goes through `host_adapter.normalize` first, so a Codex `local_shell` call `["echo", "<token>"]` is
  now recognized as the probe's echo (it was read as the text of a Python list), and a `["bash", "-lc", ...]` call is
  the joined text, as the guard sees it. The transport record's own input is no longer read, and any event
  `normalize` refuses or cannot read is an empty command, never an exception in a hook wrapper.

- A Codex run no longer stalls on a role that finished but whose `story_step` receipt nobody closed
  (`dispatch_liveness.py`, `worker_lifecycle.py`; TP2-2406 S4, 13.10.2026: the checkpoint was refused with "host
  worker is still active" while the case designer's rollout had ended with `task_complete`): for a `story_step`-bound
  receipt the liveness reader asks the HOST's own rollout of the receipt's exact path (`native_rollouts`, `native_stop`;
  the first line through `codex_usage.first_row`, the one reader of a rollout's first line). Every candidate rollout of
  the path in this launch is asked: `returned` only when each of them ends with a clean `task_complete` that is no
  earlier than the receipt's `bound_at` and older than `dispatch.native_completion_grace_s` (default 300 s: the
  SubagentStop hooks can still send a worker back after its `task_complete`; measured at up to 164 s per hook); a
  rollout still being written, cut mid-row, aborted, dated by a clock nobody can trust (no zone, a bare number, more than
  a minute ahead), or compressed (`.jsonl.zst`, no decoder: the evidence says "rollout unreadable") is no evidence and
  leaves today's answer. Nothing is written to the receipt and no work is accepted: `returned` means "the role
  stopped"; `active_binding` frees the controller's checkpoint by the same helper, the spawn guard is unchanged.
- The progress line says "returned 15:55, its dispatch still open" for a dispatch whose session ended while its record
  still says `running` (`story_progress.py`; `design/driver.md`), instead of "recorded running ..., not proven alive"; a
  process known gone is still said first.
- A native spawn refused because the host is unverified now leaves its denial row (`worker_lifecycle.note_unlaunched_denial`,
  FB-24): the dispatch the spawn names when it is `running` of that role with no agent; otherwise exactly one such
  dispatch of the role, written without a dispatch id so the controller's single owner rule decides; a receipt of the
  role that is still active, or a named dispatch that is not an unlaunched one of the role, writes nothing.
- `dispatch.native_completion_grace_s` joins `references/templates/config.json` and `config-keys.json` (default 300).

- `env_probe.py --env NAME` probes THAT stand and nothing else (with name-only entries the env file names one stack, whichever stand is picked) (`env_probe.py`, `selected_probe_config`): the global
  `environment.health_url` was borrowed for a named stand, so a dead stand read as alive through the default stack
  (TP2-2406, FB-36). The entry's own address (`api_base_url`, `api_url`, `base_url`) and its own
  `health_url`/`health_path`/`health_expect` are what is asked; a name that is missing or ambiguous stops the probe
  before any request, with a door in the words. An entry with a name only is the live shape: the stand is at the env
  file's `base_url_key`, the probe asks that address (the block's absolute `health_url` is kept only when it sits at the env-file address, dropped otherwise) and the verdict
  line says "address_source: env file". The ONLY entry may inherit the project's address, and then the verdict line says
  "address inherited from the project" (JSON key `liveness.address_source`: `own` | `inherited` | `env file` | `block`).
  Under `--env` a liveness of `unchecked` (no address anywhere, entry or env file) is Layer 1 and the exit code is 1,
  never a pass. Every address the probe prints goes through
  `http_client.safe_url`, so no credential in an address reaches a role's context; the `keys` line names the real reason
  (the selection, or the env file) instead of always blaming the env file.
- `plan_environment` plans `create` for a verified-absent environment (`environment_preparation.py`, FB-23): an observed
  runtime that is exactly `state: absent`, carries the request's `environment_id`, `absence_verified: true`,
  `resources: []`, a time and evidence references, plus an authorization with `create: true` bound to the environment and
  the target revision and an `actions.create` of the adapter. Anything less is refused or blocked, an unknown EXISTING
  runtime still fails the identity rule, and `create: true` changes nothing for an environment that exists
  (`references/environment-preparation.md`).
- A red probe of a TS/JS project can reach its assertion (`red_sandbox.py`, FB-27): the request may add
  `sandbox_setup: [{"kind": "npm_ci", "cwd": ..., "package_sha256": ..., "lock_sha256": ...}]` and the clone gets its
  `node_modules` from the lock, inside the throwaway clone and before any mutation is written, bounded in time (the tree
  is killed at the limit), with the exit code and the tail of the output in the refusal, and an exit of 0 that did not
  create the folder is not "ready". What a kind runs is data (`references/sandbox-setup.json`); the request chooses a kind,
  a folder and the pins, never a command. The installs of one probe call may add up to `sandbox.install_timeout_s`
  (`config.json`, 540 by default). The receipt of the install is part of the sensitivity proof (`dependency_setup`,
  inside the receipt hash), and `_run_mine` reads a typed refusal printed on stderr, and only that form.
- The scheduler no longer hangs on a talkative child (`execution_scheduler.py`, FB-32): the pipes of each runner are read
  from the moment it starts, so a runner that prints more than the pipe buffer finishes by itself and its lease is
  released. A reader that fails with the child alive kills the child and closes the group `failed` with `output_error`; a
  pipe a grandchild keeps open after the exit waits a grace period and the group closes with what was read. A child that
  exits 0 and does not end its stdout with a JSON summary line is `unknown` (with `unknown_reason`), never `completed`: exit 0 is not a result.
  `node_ids.kill_tree` is public and `node_ids.run_bounded` is the one bounded launcher (the collect and the install use it).

- A role without Bash is never sent to a command its guard refuses, and on Codex Desktop it is told the tools it really
  has (`host_adapter.py` `CODEX_DESKTOP_TOOLS`, used by `inject_context.py`, `brief_pack.py` `NO_SHELL_HEAD` and the
  refusals of `role_policy`): on 14.10 (TP2-2406 S4-6/S4-7) the launch prompt, the brief and the plan refusal
  sent the case designer, the case critic and the strategist (`tools:` without Bash) to `handoff_check.py`,
  `manifest_view.py` and `plan_row.py`, the guard refused each call and the roles halted with their forms untouched;
  on 16.10 (S3-4) the Desktop child's `exec` cell held `tools.exec_command`, `tools.apply_patch` and
  `tools.mcp__codex_app__*` and no Read, Grep, Glob, Write or Edit, so the strategist sent an empty `apply_patch` and
  then asked `mcp__codex_app__open_in_codex` to read its brief. The launch prompt (`story_step.py` `_prompt`) tells such
  a role to fill its form with Edit and not to run the checker; the brief (`brief_pack.py`) gives it a no-shell card,
  names the file to read where a script slice was, and never says `--help` is a door; the plan refusal
  (`guard_pre_tool.py` `plan_write_check`) names Edit, and `references/role-commands.json` says the same for
  `plan_row.py`. One text of the Desktop tools is carried verbatim by the injection, the brief and the refusals (the
  read limits inside it are the guard's own `_READ_DOOR`, stated once); a refusal of a connector call keeps its old
  text for a role with Bash and for the orchestrator. The injection is a Codex-event block that says itself it is about
  Codex Desktop; a role file that cannot be read adds nothing and says so on stderr (a pass that is told).
- The `tools:` line of a role file has ONE reader (`host_adapter.py` `tools_line`, `role_tools`, `role_has_bash`, over
  `hooklib.parse_frontmatter`) where eight readers in five files each parsed it their own way: an empty `tools:` line
  was read as the line after it (`model: sonnet`), a `tools:` in the body of the file counted, a BOM before the
  frontmatter made a role with Bash look like one without, and an audit took `BashOutput` for Bash. The guard, the
  launch prompt, the brief, the injection, the driver's continuation note and the audits A23, A2, A2b and A19 now answer
  the same question from the same set; a file with no `tools:` line is a role without Bash for every text written to a
  role (`Driver.role_has_bash` no longer assumes Bash), and the refusal of a plan or form rewrite names Edit alone on
  Codex and both doors on Claude Code.

- The S5 brief of the automator now states the checkout the orchestrator recorded and the implementation commit, and the
  role compares commits, never branch names (`brief_pack.py`, `agents/qa-automator.md`, `references/execution-lifecycle.md`).
  On 17.10 TP2-2406 halted its automator twice at S5 (`S5-qa-automator-1` and `-2`) with "not on story branch": the
  charter said "verify the branch the orchestrator recorded" and named no place where that is written, the only branch
  name in the role's inputs was `implementation.branch` of `context-manifest.json` (`TP2-2406_session-feedback`,
  the merge request's source branch), and the checkout Gate A had approved was on another branch at the same commit
  (`TP2-2406-factory-082-codex`, `state/test-repo-base.json`). The repair brief of the second dispatch then quoted
  the first halt as its cause, so the only branch statement the next role read was the previous role's wrong claim. Now
  `brief_pack.branch_check_line` writes one `Branch check:` paragraph into the head, right after `Scope:` and before any
  repair line, for every role whose slice of `execution-lifecycle.md` carries the section "Before the first write" (read
  from `references/inject-map.json` and the section markers, not typed; today the automator): the recorded checkout
  (`recorded checkout <branch>@<12 hex>`, described and never asked for), the implementation commit of the manifest and
  whether it is HEAD (for a commit that is not HEAD the role is told that HEAD must carry its change: its own
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> HEAD` proves it at once, a squash, a rebase or a commit of another repository
  is proved by content, and the role halts only when the change is absent), and that the manifest's branch is the merge
  request's source branch, not a branch to switch to. It reads three task files (`state/test-repo-base.json`, `work/context-manifest.json`, `pipeline.json`; the
  inject map and the lifecycle source only to pick the roles) and makes no git call. What it cannot
  establish is named, never passed as a fact: no record, a record whose git was not usable, a detached HEAD, a record
  made late, a manifest with no commit, and neither record nor commit each get their own words; a reader that fails
  becomes the line "could not be built" and the brief is still built. The automator's charter (rule 1 and the heading of
  its halt) and the "Before the first write" section of `execution-lifecycle.md` (with the automator's slice) say the
  same: HEAD carries the change of the commit the line names, and only an absent change halts. The halt wording the
  orchestrator matches on is unchanged.
- Effect to know: the S5 brief grows by 0.4 to 0.9 KB. The head is never shrunk, so on a brief already near 6 KB the
  inlined head of the repository map is what gives first (the map stays one link away); the ceiling of 6 KB is not
  raised. Not changed here: the orchestrator's own source check (`source_preflight`, the S0 step) and the story skill's
  "not on story branch" line.

- The exit gate and S8 judge only the story the stopping role belongs to (`exit_gate.py`, `bug_records.py`, `host_dispatch.py`).
  On Codex Desktop a SubagentStop arrives with no task field and the agent type `default`, which maps to no stage: the gate ran
  as `unknown-task`, audited every bug of the project's shared `bugs/` folder, and BUG-1..3 of TP2-2530 and 2534 (no
  `area`, no `impact`) blocked the exit of TP2-2406 eight times. `_identity` now has a third task source, `_named_ticket`,
  after the event's own field and the stage branch: it keeps `resolve_ticket`'s answer only when something NAMED the story (an
  explicit id, exactly one existing story in the dispatch text, the one story the task name's slug names, `$QA_FACTORY_TASK`).
  The resolver's guesses (the single running story, the single open story) are not names. A stop nobody named stays
  `unknown-task` and gets the FULL bug audit, whose list opens with one header line saying that no story was named, that some
  findings may be another story's, and how the orchestrator names it (`$QA_FACTORY_TASK`, `story_step bind`); a list with no
  finding gets no header. A role with no stage (a foreign agent, `default`) reads only the bug audit (`bug_audit_errors`), not
  the story's phase json, cases and register.
- Whose bug is it: `bug_records.owner_of(bug, task_root)` answers `mine`, `other` or `unknown`. `other` needs something that
  POSITIVELY names another story that exists on disk (the front matter `task`, or a `gate<G>-<ticket>[-n]` id) and nothing that
  names this one; `unknown` is checked like `mine`. A ticket-less id, this story's earlier gate B decision when `controller.json`
  cannot be read, a `task` and an id that name different stories, a `task` that is no story here, and a story without a
  `pipeline.json` are all `unknown`; `task` is compared without regard to case. The join with the story's gate B ids is read
  once per audit, not once per bug. Before this, the first version of the rule skipped those bugs as another story's.
- `host_dispatch.enrich` accepts the binding `story_step bind` wrote for a Codex Desktop child (`bound_by: story_step`, the
  child's exact agent path, no session id), so the child's stop names its story. The record is read, never rewritten, so a
  child's stop does not mark it terminal (only `story_step finish` does); a finished (`terminal`) record names nothing for a
  later launch under the same path. Records are read through `hooklib.read_json`, so a broken, empty or non-object record is no
  binding and raises nothing, and a failing scan of the receipts' directory names no story (it used to raise out of `enrich`,
  `read_event` answered None and the gate exited 0 for every stop). A role bound this way now carries its `agent_type` and
  `task_id` on its tool calls too, and its stop runs the stage checks, not only the bug audit.
- A `diagnostic` or `flaky_diagnostic` run is never a product row and never a manifest-join ghost (`contract.product_result_rows`,
  `finalize_task.reduce`, FB-43): a row keeps its own `purpose`, else takes its block's, and only those two purposes stay out of
  the join (red-probe and baseline rows are joined as before). A manual failure carries its attempt, so a triage row of an older
  attempt does not answer it (`contract.triage_failures`, `_attempt_fits`, CD2). The stamp leaves a pin the manifest already
  bound to an immutable case version (`case_stamp.stamp`, CS2).

- A resume on Codex (`followup_task`, `send_input`, `send_message` to anyone but `/root`) is judged by its RECIPIENT's story
  (codex/1, CX1-9; TP2-2406, 16.10). The receipt `story_step.py bind` or the host wrote for the recipient's dispatch
  names the story, and it is read before the dispatch text and before the single-running-story guess, which a Codex resume no
  longer inherits: a follow-up to an accepted story with pending rework used to be checked against whichever story was running.
  A recipient no receipt names, in a project that has stories, is refused with the door `story_step.py bind ... --agent-id
  <recipient>` instead of being allowed; a project with no story is not refused, and the Claude host keeps its identity as before.
- A name that receipts of two stories hold names no story, and a receipt vouches for a recipient only when ALL receipts that
  answer to it name this story and a dispatch of it that can still be resumed. An agent of a `superseded` or released dispatch is
  not resumable on either host; the refusal says which dispatch retired it ("N agents recorded for this story, none resumable")
  instead of "no agent is recorded". A `send_input` with `interrupt` is judged by the same recipient rule as a resume (the worker-lifecycle stop guard still runs first).
- `host_dispatch.binding_names` is the one reader of the names a receipt answers to (`agent_id`, `task_path`, `task_name` and the
  last component of a path); `receipt_files` is the one scanner of the receipt directory (a broken file names nothing and never
  fails the reading of another); `resolve_binding_path` answers with the exact file or with exactly one match, never the first of
  several. `story_step.py bind` records `task_name` and `task_path` beside the keys it always wrote.
- Stopping a worker (`interrupt_agent`, `close_agent`, `send_input` with `interrupt`) matches the target or its last component
  against every name of every receipt, and judges ALL matches: a `terminal` receipt with the same name no longer lets a live worker
  be stopped without a recorded cancellation, and an unreadable receipt beside it no longer lets a stop through.

- Codex host surface (`hooks/codex.json`, `host_adapter.py`, `host_probe.py`): `shell` and `local_shell` (an argv list
  or text, every text field joined) are shell calls to the guard; a Desktop code cell (`exec`, `js`) is a shell call
  only when it holds exactly one literal `tools.exec_command`, with that command as the text the shell checks read.
  Any other cell with text, as text or as an object, is refused (the guard exits 2 and prints what is wrong, what
  was expected and the door: send one call per cell; it is a refusal of the call, not a parse failure, so it never
  counts towards the guard's escalation), and so is a cell that asks for a tty session, so a nested
  `apply_patch` or connector call is neither passed to checks that cannot see it nor let through unchecked.
  `exec_command` and `shell_command` read every command field like `shell` does (a second field cannot hide behind
  the first). A shell, `exec` or `js` call with no command text is refused with
  the fields and the door named, whether or not the event carries a Codex marker (`is_codex` now also reads the
  transport record `normalize` keeps). The doctor's probe reads that transport first, so the DENY echo inside
  `functions.exec` is still recognized and the ALLOW echo still passes (CX1-1)
- `send_message` to the parent (`/root`, or no recipient, under every one of the five recipient aliases rule 6 reads)
  is a progress note the guard does not judge as a resume (`AgentMessage`); a note to any other recipient, and
  `send_input` and `followup_task`, stay `SendMessage` under rule 6. That the host's `send_message` never wakes a
  worker is her observation (TP2-2406), not measured here, so the exemption is no wider than it (FB-13, CX1-1)
- The guard and the probe receipt of `hooks/codex.json` run only on the tools they inspect, with matchers that are the
  regex image of `tool_short_name` (a generated census test, full match and search alike); waits, plan and image calls
  no longer pay for them. The debounced cost sample keeps its empty matcher (CX1-1)
- Connector reads (`host_adapter.role_policy`): `host_tools.read_only_calls` names the exact call forms of a
  code-taking connector tool that are reads (full match only, one non-empty code field, a regex that does not compile
  classifies nothing). `host_tools` has ONE validating reader: a value of the wrong shape permits nothing and prints a
  warning that names the key. A string `host_tools.read_only` no longer permits by substring, and a list or a number
  there no longer raises (FB-38, CX1-1)

- `controller.py --task <KEY>` is now a flag of its own, and flags are no longer abbreviated (`controller.py`): argparse used to
  read `--task TP2-2406` as the abbreviation of `--task-root`, so the key became a relative root and the controller
  created a phantom story folder in the current directory (`state/events.lock`, then a projection of "S0, revision 0" on
  `recover` that looked like a success). The parser now has `prog="controller.py"`, takes the docstring as its description
  (it used to be passed as `prog`, so every argparse refusal opened with the whole docstring), turns abbreviations off, and
  takes exactly one of `--task KEY` and `--task-root PATH`; a request carrying both is refused naming both.
- One rule turns a ticket key into its story folder (`hooklib.py`, `story_root`): the key is one path component, the project
  is required, and the folder must be an existing directory whose name IS the key, found in the listing of the artifact root
  and not by asking the file system about the joined path. On NTFS `tp3-1`, `TP3-1 ` and `TP3-1.` are all "a directory", and a
  root whose name differs from its folder is refused later by the event store as a corrupt journal; a near miss is now refused
  up front, naming the real folder. A key over the file system's name limit is a refusal too, on Linux as on Windows.
- The controller never creates a story folder and writes nothing under a root that is not a story (`controller.py`): every
  problem with the call (unknown operation, bad key, missing folder) is found before the person's words are read and before
  any file is touched, and is one refusal listing all of them (one exception: `--task` outside a project exits 3 with the
  shared "no project" text, before the other problems are collected; `--task-root` needs no project). On a folder with no `state/events.jsonl` only `prepare` (it
  only reads) and `initialize` (when S0 has written the folder's `pipeline.json`) act; any other operation is refused with
  "initialize task before work" when the folder holds a `pipeline.json`, which the driver turns into `initialize`, and with a
  "not a story folder" refusal that does not use that phrase when it holds neither file, so the driver cannot loop.
  `initialize` aimed at the artifact root used to write a journal there, and aimed at the project root it left a lock
  file behind before its own refusal; both are refused now, writing nothing.
- `tools/controller-blocks-gen.py` and `design/controller-blocks.md`: the new refusals are routed (`_cli_story_root`).

The approved scope is pinned cases, compared by keys. `revise_plan` writes the keys the case index holds (`TC-001`,
or `<area>/TC-003` for a number two areas hold) and refuses what no pin names, with the story's own key refused at
`initialize` and `revise_plan` alike. A rework and a dispatch name a case in any spelling the index reads
(`TC-001` or `session-feedback/TC-001`): a member equal to an approved one passes, otherwise every key it names must be
approved, and the dispatch records the approved keys. Refusals name the door (`--operation revise_plan`,
`case_versions.py --task-root <root> --all`); the driver's `revise_plan` compares keys and keys its call by the story's
revision and content. New `references/codex-host.md` (named from `phases/s0.md`).

Gate A reads the case critic's verdict per plan row, from the critic's own receipt. A row's verdict is the word of the accepted critic that covered it, for that row's cases only, in the bytes the receipt measured (the end of `critic-findings.md`, since a new round goes on top and earlier rounds are never edited), and only in that receipt's own round: the round ends where the next-older accepted receipt of the same file begins, or at the next `# ` round heading, whichever comes first. The word is the roll-call's `verdict` column; a roll-call without that column gives each of its rows the round's own `Verdict:` word, as before. A round that rejects one case no longer refuses the rows it approved, and a scoped repair round no longer clears rows it never reviewed. Every doubt is `partial`: a cell outside the closed list, a case the roll-call does not name or does not mark reviewed, a round with no `Verdict:` line or no roll-call, two roll-calls in one round, a receipt whose bytes are no longer in the file, an unreadable ref. A later accepted round that rejects a case outside its scope still refuses that row, and one whose bytes were edited holds it at `partial`. Each refused row carries `verdict_basis` (`column`, `round_word`, `no_review`, `unreadable`, `receipt_mismatch`, `two_rollcalls`) beside the prose `verdict_source`, and the refusal is worded from the basis: only a word the critic wrote is called the critic's verdict, a round with no per-case word says so, and an edited findings file is named with its receipt and the two doors (run the critic round again, or the person's word). A receipt without a findings ref keeps the older rule. The case critic's card and `case-lifecycle.md` name the `verdict` column, the `# ` round heading and the prepend rule; the gate A brief gains one line, the critic's word per plan row as gate A reads it, with the first reason in plain words. The reporter rehearsal now proves the format the command itself declares (`commands.one_test.reporter.format`, an explicit `none` included) before the profile's older `reporter.kind`, and says so when the two differ.

- A Codex Desktop orchestrator no longer loses the call that starts a role to its exec cell (`launch_card.py`,
  `story_step.py`, `controller.py`; TP2-2406, 12.10.2026: `start` runs 34-112 s, the cell yields after about
  30 s, S2 was dispatched three times and launched once). `story_step.py start` prints `dispatched <ID> (revision N)` and
  `launch card: <path>` first, flushed, as soon as the controller has recorded the dispatch (a refused or failed
  dispatch prints neither), and writes the same Agent-call block, whole, to `work/briefs/<ID>.launch.md` as its LAST
  step: after `stage_done running`, the probe debt, the brief and the handover form. A card that cannot be written is
  one note and the block is still printed. The line `dispatched ...` is printed once and before every slow step; the block
  and its bytes are what `start` printed at the end before.
- `next` and `story_step.py where` answer `launch` (`card`, `subagent_type`, `bind`, `reason`) for a running dispatch of a
  desktop story that nothing shows was launched: no agent id on its record, no host receipt of the story and role in any
  status (one that names the dispatch, or none), no return mark, no refusal of the dispatch hook (a row naming the
  dispatch, or the Codex row that names none, attributed by role, stage and time), no unreadable receipt or denial file -
  and only while the host's liveness verdict is `unknown` (an `alive`, `returned`, `abandoned` or `never_started` verdict, or
  one that could not be taken, keeps the old `wait_existing_job`; so does a story with no `qa-factory/config.json`). While
  the card is not written yet the answer is `wait_start` (`card`, `age_s`, `rebuild`, `release`): no timeout, the age is
  reported, `where` rebuilds the card from the brief and the handover form when `start` died after them (the form is waited
  for whenever the handoff registry has a contract for the pair), and the person's word (`release`) frees a dispatch no
  `start` is writing. The driver's stories, a process with the run-mode variable set, a story without a `desktop` stamp and
  `_next_action_for_state` answer exactly as before.
- `stage_done.py` takes `--dispatch-id`; `story_step.py bind` passes it, the stage transition's payload carries it (only
  when non-empty; the transition's identity and idempotency key are unchanged), and the controller's projection puts the
  host's agent id on THAT dispatch of its record - only when it is `running` and of the transition's stage; a transition
  that names none (every store written before this change), a name the record does not know, or an empty id changes
  nothing, and the stage entry never carries it. A dispatch on an already accepted stage gets no transition, so its
  record keeps no agent id there and the host receipt alone decides `launch` or `wait_existing_job`.
- `references/codex-host.md` gains the launch-card paragraph (700 B budget; the size pin 600 -> 1300) and the «Follow
  `next`» item of the `qa-story` skill names `launch` / `wait_start` and points at it. The environment-facts census gains
  one named carrier (`work/briefs/<DISPATCH>.launch.md`, writer `new-10`, leaves at N2) and its baseline row.

- A dispatch the controller committed outside `story_step.py start` - a `controller.py --operation rework` packet - now gets
  its brief, handover form and launch card: `story_step.py materialize --task <T> --dispatch-id <ID>` writes them from the
  packet that IS committed (`story_step.py`, `launch_card.py`, `brief_pack.py`; TP2-2406 S3-3, 15.10.2026: `start --id`
  was refused because it builds a fresh request, `where` answered `wait_start` for 7000 s, and the brief held none of the plan
  rows TS-1..TS-4 and TS-8). It never calls `prepare`, `apply` or `stage_done` and touches neither the log nor the state; the
  card is written last through `_write_dispatch_files`, the one writer `start` now shares, and a second run writes nothing. The
  prompt and the brief carry the packet's identity (`Rework of <parent> (cause ...)`, the plan rows, the inherited
  `input_hash`, the purpose) for a rework only; a normal `start` prints and writes the bytes it always did. It refuses, with
  the field, the value and a door and before writing anything, an unknown or non-running dispatch, a record that differs
  from its event, a rework whose `input_hash` is not its parent's, a driver-mode story and a card on disk that differs
  (never replaced). `where` and `next` name the door only for a packet no `start` registered (`launch_card.outside_start`);
  the `rework` command's result carries it as `next`.
- The idempotency refusal of the event store (`event_store.py`) names the key, every field that differs and both values, as
  `IdempotencyKeyReused` (a `StateConflict`; the head sentence is unchanged); `start --id <committed id>` appends the
  `materialize` door once, the controller's different-scope refusal (`revise_plan`) keeps its text and is raised only when
  scope is the whole difference.
- `story_step.py finish` no longer records a role's declared halt (`header.verdict: halt|impossible` in its handover form, or
  a halting digest) as `accepted`: it refuses before any accept (exit 2, nothing recorded) and names the doors - `decide`
  where `decide` takes the dispatch, `pause --status blocked` then `recover` otherwise. A recorded `decide` decision on that
  dispatch outranks the halt (named as a note) and counts as the person's word on the form. A role that does not close its
  stage takes `decide --close` only when its form declares the halt, and `finish` then does not close the stage over the role
  after it. The driver reads the same word through one reader (`_declared_halt`), also before it resumes a role. A
  `repair_verify` rework whose evidence is byte-identical to its parent's prints `no change against <parent>` as a note.
- `references/codex-host.md` gains the paragraph on a packet committed outside `start` (400 B budget) and the `qa-story`
  skill sends a rejected artifact to `materialize` after `rework`.

- The driver runs a story over the Codex CLI (`story_run.py --host codex`, or `driver.host` in config.json): a role is
  `codex exec --json -C <project> -` with the prompt on stdin, a continuation of the SAME dispatch is
  `codex exec resume <thread id> --json -`, and the thread id is the dispatch's agent id (`bind`). The conductor, the
  handoff check, `finish`, the in-flight record, `dispatch_liveness` and the journals are the same code; the journal
  rows of a Codex call carry `host`, `usage` and the price with its label. The role's definition (the one function the
  Codex hook also reads) and the rule layer travel in a fresh prompt; a continuation gets the words alone. Verified
  against `codex exec --help` of codex-cli 0.158.0 and the event names in its binary, not against a live run
  (`parse_codex_jsonl`, `codex_cmd`, `host_prompt`; `design/driver.md`, "The Codex host").
- Why: on TP2-2406 under the Codex desktop host the orchestrator model waited for its spawned roles itself
  (501 `wait_agent`, 403 `wait` and 26 `sleep` turns, 129.9M input tokens, 46% of its input) because `spawn_agent`
  returns at once and nothing in the package owned the loop. The driver waits on the child process, so no model turn is
  spent while a role runs, on either host.
- The model: `--model`, else `default_model.codex` of `references/driver-infra.json` (the latest Terra,
  `gpt-5.6-terra`); `-m` is always passed and the journal names the model used. The Codex host with neither stops with a
  refusal naming the key and the file (exit 2). The price of a Codex call is worked out from its usage by
  `cost_capture.value_usage`, the same pricer and tariff list as every price (the long-context tier is chosen by the
  call's sum of input tokens), and labelled "estimate: default tariffs (references/model-rates.json); long-context tier by
  the turn's sum" - on the journal row (`cost_basis`), on the dashboard's story card and in the retro. A journal row
  keeps one meaning of `total_cost_usd` on both hosts, the running total of the thread; the call's own price is
  `call_cost_usd`. A model with no tariff or a call with no countable usage is "price unknown: <why>" (`call_cost_usd`
  null, the thread's total unchanged), never `$0`.
- A call's stream is read by the last terminal event: `turn.failed` is the call's error and its message is what the
  infrastructure rows read (the agent text before it is kept apart); a stream with no terminal event, a continuation
  answered in another thread (`resume_mismatch`), a stream of text with no event at all (`no_events`, the text kept in a
  journal note), an empty stream and a line that is no event are named in the driver journal and never read as a
  success (an empty stream with exit 0 claims nothing and is a note, not an error). A story keeps its host: a run of the other host over a story that holds sessions
  is refused at start, naming `--host <the host it started on>` or a new story.
- `references/driver-infra.json`: three `codex_*` rows (a login refusal, a usage limit, a broken stream), `unmeasured`,
  each with `hosts: ["codex"]`; `infra_failure.classify` takes the host and tries a row with `hosts` only for a call of
  one of them, so a role's own text on Claude never reads as a Codex login failure.
- `inject_context.role_block` is the one function of a role file's body; `codex_role_instructions` (the hook) and the
  driver's Codex prompt both call it.
- Tests: `test_story_run_codex.py` (the parser, the argv and the prompt, one dispatch's lifecycle with identity,
  continuity, money, an auth stop, a transient retry, an unknown CLI failure and an incomplete stream; S1 end to end
  through the real driver process with a `codex` stub; the Claude path unchanged; the host battery and the start
  refusals), `test_infra_failure.py` (the `hosts` key), `test_no_real_claude.py` and `harness.py` (`STORY_RUN_CODEX` is
  guarded like `STORY_RUN_CLAUDE`: no test starts the real CLI).

- A regression for the FB-14 state of TP2-2406 runs on the package's own road (`scripts/tests/test_fb14_real_state.py`,
  CX1-16): the preserved S1 inventory (a parent and a story that were read but never received an inspection receipt, a feature
  gap the person accepted) is judged by the four readers of S1 (the controller, its S1 accept, `stage_done`, the exit gate of the
  scout) before and after `ticket_adapter.py receipts` stamps the snapshots (`inspection_by: code:snapshot`). A word about one
  source (`accept-gap --source-id`) or about a whole kind of gap (`accept-gap --cause`) reaches all four readers; the three words
  the run saved as `stage_overrides` pass nothing; an empty words file, an unknown or partial source id, a word recorded for
  another stage and a snapshot of other bytes each have their case. No package behaviour changes: three cases of a word that
  `waiver.py --stage S1` passes by substring (a partial id, a lower-case id, a single id lifting the line of two sources) are
  pinned as expected-red findings for a later node.

- A folder is never created under a wrong story root: the creators and readers of part A ask the story-root drivers of
  `hooklib.py` instead of building `<artifact root>/<key>` themselves. `story_step`, `source_exclusions`, `stand_identity`
  (`_task_root`), `stand_gaps` and `gate_preflight` (`resolve_task_root`), `handoff_init` (`task_root`), `bug_records`
  (`_story_exists`, now through `is_story_folder`, keeping its own `pipeline.json` test), `sizing` and the hooks `inject_context`
  (`note_denial`) and `exit_gate` (`_findings_path`) all answer through the one rule; a story that is not there is a refusal that
  says what is wrong, what was expected and the door, and nothing is written.
- `handoff_init.py`, `sizing.py`, `stand_gaps.py` (and so `gate_preflight.py`), `source_exclusions.py` and `question_register.py`
  now match flags exactly (`hooklib.exact_options`): `--task-r` is no longer read as `--task-root`. `handoff_init.py` decides the
  story before it reads the contract and no longer falls back to the current folder when `hooklib` does not import. A story the
  flags name must exist: `sizing --task X`, `stand_gaps --task-root X` and `handoff_init --task X` on a missing story used to
  create the folder (or answer `[]`) and now exit 2 with one `{"error": ...}` line. Both flags together must name the same folder.
  An empty `--task` or `--task-root` is refused, never read as the current folder.
- Creators write only under a story that exists (S0 is the only road that makes a story folder, unchanged):
  `EventStore.commit` and `EventStore.recover` refuse a story folder that does not exist (`lock()` keeps creating its own folder,
  for the five project-level mutexes), `JobStore` creates nothing when it is constructed or read (`jobs()` of a missing folder is
  `[]`), and `write_baseline_receipt`, `retro_numbers --write-retro`, `brief_pack`, `manifest_put`, `manifest_from_tests` (a dry
  run too), `import_test_receipt`, `repo_map`, `question_register`, `probe_by_code`, `run_suite` (`--request`, `--detail`, `--task
  --label`, `evidence_dir`, `write_run_block`) and `build_mine_request` (fresh evidence) refuse a missing story as a line, not a
  traceback. `inject_context.note_denial` keeps a denial for a ticket with no story folder in the project's own list of denials
  and the exit gate saves no findings file for it.

- One rule decides "this folder is a story" (`hooklib.py`, `is_story_folder(parent, name)`): the name must be a string that is one
  clean path component (not empty, no blank at either end, not `.` or `..`, none of `/ \ : NUL`), spelled exactly as in the
  listing of `parent`, and a directory. It never raises (a listing that fails is "no") and never creates anything. A folder named
  `TP3-1 ` (a trailing blank; an ordinary name on Linux, one that NTFS holds only when it was created through the
  extended-length prefix) is no longer a story, so `story_root("TP3-1 ")` now refuses where it used to accept; the near-miss sentence ("A folder 'TP3-1' exists: the key is matched exactly.") and every other text of
  `story_root` are unchanged, and its decision now goes through the leaf.
- Three drivers ask the leaf (`hooklib.py`): `story_root_at(path, program, door)` for a path (an empty or blank path is refused,
  never read as the current folder; `.` is the caller's explicit word for the folder it stands in; the project is not required; the
  path comes back as given, and it must reach the folder that was judged: on Linux a path through an absent folder or through a
  link, `nowhere/../TP3-1`, is refused), `story_of(program, key, root, door, project=None)` for a script's pair of flags (neither
  flag gives a refusal that names only the flags that script has; both flags must name the same folder; two phantoms, or two
  empty values, are one refusal with both sentences and the door once; `project` is the explicit project root a script's `--root`
  names, under which the key resolves, as `story_root(..., project=)` does), and `story_cli(...)` for a script's `main` (one `{"error": ...}` line on stderr and exit 2, or, with `exit=False`
  under `role_cli.run_guarded`, the exception for the guard to print). Every refusal is a `StoryRootError`, a `ValueError` whose text
  is the finished refusal (what is wrong, what was expected, the door). Nothing calls the new functions yet: the callers follow in
  CX1-18 parts A and B.
- `hooklib.exact_options(parser)` turns abbreviations of long flags off on a parser and on every subparser it has when
  called (`exact_options(ap).parse_args(argv)`): one helper for the 34 parsers that take `--task-root`, instead of a literal in
  each constructor.

- The 31 scripts that take `--task-root` (`artifact_packet`, `artifact_producer`, `artifact_supersede`, `case_stamp`,
  `case_versions`, `delivery_manifest`, `delivery_summary`, `handoff_check`, the seven `judge_*`, `manual_capture`,
  `manual_evidence`, `migrate_artifacts`, `plan_row`, `red_sandbox`, `render_case_appendix`, `report_facts`,
  `runtime_paths`, `runtime_probe`, `s5_precheck`, `stage_status`, `story_progress`, `story_version`,
  `ticket_adapter freshness`, `tms_publication`, `traceability`) read their flags exactly: `--task-r` is no longer
  `--task-root` (the abbreviation that once turned a key into a relative path), and the subparsers of `tms_publication`
  and `manual_capture` are exact too. The story the flags name is resolved right after parsing, before an input is read
  or a byte is written: a root that names no story is refused with the one driver text (exit 2, or the script's own
  refusal channel where it has one), where it used to answer a green `OK ... 0 case(s)`, `{"verified": true}`,
  `"older": true`, a traceback, or make the folder on the spot (`delivery_summary`, `render_case_appendix`,
  `manual_capture`, `artifact_producer`). An empty or blank `--task-root` is a refusal, never the current folder.
  `report_facts.py` and `traceability.py` exit 2, not 1, for a story that does not exist (a refusal of the call, like
  every other). `controller.py --task-root` uses the same path rule (CX1-18).
- The controller's operation lists are named for what they are (`controller.py`): `ROUTED_OPERATIONS` (each has its own
  handler in `main`; some of them write) and `APPLY_OPERATIONS` (they go through `apply`/`validate`), with `OPERATIONS`
  for both; the old `READ_OPERATIONS` / `WRITE_OPERATIONS` are gone, not aliased.

- The shell tokenizer (`hooklib.command_segments`) reads more of the forms the shell reads as one word or as nothing, so its
