  cuts match the shell's there: in bash a backslash before `$` or another backslash is part of the word (no substitution
  starts there; a backslash before any other character is read as before, so a PowerShell command that a Codex host labels
  `Bash` keeps its quote parity and its subexpressions in view); in PowerShell `<# ... #>` at the start of a word is a comment
  (an unclosed one runs to the end of the input; inside a word `<#` is text) and the stop-parsing token `--%` makes the rest
  of its line literal up to an unquoted `|` or `&&`. The shared ban `hooklib.SHELL_OPAQUE_BAN` still refuses its forms whole
  in the runner guard and the read guard, so no refusal of those two guards changes; the readers that sit behind no ban (the
  direct test launch, the commit and delivery shapes) see these two cuts as the shell makes them and keep every other cut
  as before. `$( )`, `<( )`, `( )` and the backtick are cut as before. (CX1-19)

- The command guards read a command with ONE walker (codex/1, CX1-20; `hooklib.walk`): the direct-test-launch guard, the
  delivery and commit shapes of the stage guard, the typed-runner rule and the read guard no longer cut a command at the
  parentheses of `$( )`, `<( )`, a backtick pair or a PowerShell `( )` / `{ }` group, nor search for substitutions
  themselves. Every body the shell would run, at any depth, is judged on its own, in BOTH shell dialects whatever the tool
  label says. A word with an unquoted substitution may be the program (`$(echo gh) pr create`, `git $(true) commit`,
  `` `echo gh` pr create ``), and a name built by a substitution, quotes or a backslash (`py$(true)test`,
  `run_sui""te.py`) is read as the name it makes. A runner launch whose arguments hold a substitution or a group is refused
  with the way out (write the path and flags literally, `run_suite.py --request FILE`); a reader that runs a program
  (`find -exec`, `-execdir`, `-ok`, `-okdir`, `rg --pre`, awk `system(`, sed `e`) is no longer a mention of the runner -
  one table, `launch-causes.json` `reader_runs`. Relief: `echo $(rg -n x run_suite.py)` and a `git log --grep "run_suite"`
  pass. Named widenings: a bash command whose quote parity PowerShell reads differently (`git commit -m "a\" ; dotnet
  test"`) is blocked under either tool label (the refusal says it read the command as PowerShell and how to write it for
  bash), and `$f = { pytest -q }` counts as a launch. The hook's fast gate admits a command with a `$(` or a backtick,
  and the stage check reads the command as the role wrote it. A bash backtick pair ends at its first unescaped partner
  whatever is open inside it (`` echo `$(a` b `pytest -q` c `` runs `pytest`), a `#` right after a backslash-escaped
  `;`, `|`, `&`, line end or TAB is no comment, and a reader's flag (`-exec`, `--pre`) launches only under its own
  program (`echo -exec pytest` runs nothing). A refusal of a delivery names the command the role wrote (`gh ...`), not a
  form a substitution happens to fit. Named widening: a shell command over 64 KB is refused before any guard reads it
  (the refusal says to split it or write the long text to a file), because reading 400 KB of nested openers took minutes.

- The two command guards read a command with one tokenizer (`hooklib.command_segments`, which now takes `spans=True` for
  the raw slice behind each segment): a role without Bash can read its plan with `rg -n '"id":"TS-(1|2|3)"' <plan>`
  (`host_adapter._is_one_plain_read`; the quoted `|` and parentheses are text, an unquoted one is an operator, and `rg --pre`
  is refused), and the runner guard (`stage_guard.rule_typed_runner`) no longer reads `rg -n 'a|b' run_suite.py` as a
  launch of the runner (FB-25) and lets a non-executing flag free only its own command, not a neighbour's (FB-40)
  (TP2-2406 S3-3). The runner guard reads every command in both shell dialects, so a refusal in either one is the
  answer; its private regex splitter is gone.
- Forms the shell reads differently from that tokenizer are refused whole by both guards through one constant,
  `hooklib.SHELL_OPAQUE_BAN`: a backslash before `; & | ( ) ' "` or a line end, `<#`, `--%`, the typographic quotes
  U+2018..U+201E, a lone CR, and the forms that hide a launch or a second command inside what the tokenizer reads as
  a comment - a backslash-escaped blank before `#`, `)#` and a VT or FF before `#`. The refusal names the sequence, says the shell reads it differently from the guard, and
  names the way to write the command without it. The runner guard also treats a command cut at a parenthesis as a launch
  whatever its words are (`python -X $(true)cat run_suite.py --task X` hid the launch behind a reader-headed piece), so
  `python (Join-Path $S run_suite.py) --request r.json` is refused: expand the path first. (CX1-5)

- The exit filter of the coming collect archive and the one generator of path spellings (`scripts/machine_facts.py`,
  `references/collect-redaction.json`; collect/1, CL1-1; D-0052): `path_variants`, `short83` and the replacement-table builder
  `machine_table` moved out of the test-side census (`state_census.py` imports them, its baseline gains and loses no row), and
  the redactor is built on them. It redacts a unit whole when a secret detector hits it, keeps JSON valid JSON (parse, walk,
  dump; the key order kept, colliding keys suffixed ` #2`), cuts JSONL and text on `\n` only, and checks its own output through
  the escaped, percent-encoded and double-encoded views of every unit before letting it out. What it will not search for (a name
  below 3 characters, a machine name below 6, a secret value below 8, an absent identity source) is a named gap row carrying
  the kind and the length, never the value. Nothing in the package calls it yet; the collector arrives with the next node.

- `scripts/collect_pack.py`: the collector of the COLLECT skill (library; the command line comes in CL1-4). Sets A-H go into one zip in parts of at most 25 MB, manifest first, every byte through `machine_facts`, post-check on the written archive.
- The window is `state/collect/mark.json` (a prefix of bytes for append-only files); sets, ceilings and the never-list live in `references/collect-sets.json`; `references/install-paths.json` gets the row `state/collect/**`.

- `skills/qa-collect/SKILL.md`: the `/qa-factory:qa-collect` skill. One message with two questions (problems since the install or since the factory last packed the records, what to do better), the person's words kept word for word in new timestamped files `qa-factory/state/words/collect-problems-<stamp>.txt` and `collect-suggestions-<stamp>.txt` (never overwritten, never deleted; `<stamp>` is `yyyymmddThhmmss`), ONE packing command, the command's summary shown as printed. No agent packs anything; `allowed-tools` is Bash and Write.
- `scripts/collect_pack.py` is a command now: `--root --problems-file --suggestions-file [--not-asked] [--extra SET=path] [--since install] [--activity-not-recorded] [--answers-not-split] [--json]`; exit 0 packed, 1 a refusal in the FR-1 form, 2 a usage error. An answers file the reader refuses is named by the option the command carries. A person who has nothing to add is `blank`, a run with nobody to ask (`--not-asked`) is `not_asked`; the archive is written either way. A set whose data the config keeps outside `qa-factory/` is printed in the summary as `<SET>: not found at the standard place ... pass --extra <SET>=<path inside the project>`; a re-run with `--extra` packs that place whole (an extra place is never "unchanged since the last packing") and the mark moves only after a successful run. `--answers-not-split` (one text for both questions, kept whole as the problems answer) and `--activity-not-recorded` (the start step printed `ACTIVITY NOT RECORDED`) each become one gap line of the manifest.
- Set H: every story gets the stall verdict of `collect_stall` (K1..K7, windowed by the last packing); the transcripts of a stalled story - its sessions' main transcripts and the subagent transcripts of those sessions only - go into their own file `<archive>-transcripts.zip`, listed in the manifest (`kind: transcripts`), so the person can delete just that file. A missing transcript is a gap with its session id. A project that is not onboarded gets no verdict and no transcripts (set H says `gap`, as B-G do).
- Config key `collect.stall_quiet_hours` (default 24, `references/templates/config.json`); a config written before the key existed gets the same default. A value the rule cannot use (not a number of hours, negative, or a config that cannot be read) gets the default too, with one gap line of H (`config: stall_quiet_hours unreadable, default 24 used`) instead of an unknown verdict for every story.
- Activity type `collect`: `activity_capture.FACTORY_TYPES` is the one set (`TYPES` is the same object); `dashboard_cost_groups` labels a group by it and the dashboard's own `FIXED_LABELS` knows the label. The skill's spend is tagged as Collect; counted in its price with CD1-11 (a session that ran only the skill is still recorded as unclassified by `cost_capture` until then).
- Changed: `scripts/audit_factory.py`: `collect_pack` is a CLI script (audit A1); `collect_stall` is live through its import.
- `references/collect-sets.json`: the note of the virtual set H row no longer says "wired by CL1-4" (the packer draws set H from the stall rule).

- A person's request to change the factory leaves a finding, never a plugin edit (`references/conductor.md`,
  `references/common-rules.md`, `scripts/project_decisions.py`): the conductor and the orchestrator (the `qa-story` skill)
  record the request as a factory finding
  with `project_decisions.py add-finding --words-file <file> --idempotency-key change-request:<T>`; the writer completes the
  key with a 12-hex digest of the person's words (whitespace collapsed), so the same words are one finding and other words
  are another one, even when the wording of the same request differs (a new row, by design). The words travel whole in a
  file and sit on one line in the row. The rule holds where a role or conductor session exists: an answer the code recorded
  without showing it to a session leaves no finding. Roles only learn the invariant (`common-rules.md`: never a plugin edit).
- `project_decisions.py add-finding` takes `--words-file` (exactly one of `--witness` / `--words-file`; an empty, missing or
  non-UTF-8 file is refused in one line and writes nothing); a `change-request:` key with an inline `--witness` is refused
  in one line, with the door `--words-file <file>`, and writes nothing. Three latent defects closed for every caller: a retry
  of a multi-line witness (any line break: LF, CRLF, a lone CR) is the same finding (the retry is compared with the row as the
  table reads it back), a `|` in a witness
  no longer shifts the columns (`_cells` splits on an unescaped pipe only), and a key that is a prefix of another key no longer
  answers for it (the lookup is anchored at the end of the cell). A repeat of a key with other content is refused with the
  recorded row named (`FB-<n>`) and "nothing to do"; a busy registry lock is a one-line refusal that says to run the command again.
- The audit's reader of the Deferred decisions table (`audit_factory.py`) reads a row through the writer's own `_cells`: a `|`
  escaped in a cell no longer shifts the `asked` column.
- `conductor.md` and `common-rules.md` shrink by 8 and 16 bytes: repeated sentences were cut to pay for the new ones.

- One recipe of the package fingerprint and a release file (`scripts/release_fingerprint.py`; collect/1, CL1-8; D-0052): the two
  copies of the recipe, in `install_smoke.package_fingerprint` and `runtime_paths.resolve_runtime`, became one function both call, so
  every stored fingerprint keeps its value. The release step runs `release_fingerprint.py --write` in the release copy (per-file
  digests of the LF-normalised bytes, the version, the recipe id; it refuses an untracked or ignored recipe file in a git clone) and
  `--check` last before the commit. `compare()` answers `package_modified` for the coming collector: `yes` only for a byte difference
  of a named file on a release file of the same version, `no` for equality, `unknown` with a `why` for every doubt (no release file,
  unreadable, invalid, another recipe or version, an unreadable package file); editor and cache leftovers are listed apart and never
  accuse. This tree carries no release file, so every install reads `unknown / no_release_file` until the release that writes one.

- One recipe of "which package bytes make the factory" (`host_probe.py`, `audit_factory.py` A14, `factory_manifest.py`; collect/2,
  CL2-1; AR-15): the host probe's fingerprint is now `release_fingerprint.package_fingerprint()` plus the project's
  `qa-factory/config.json`, so a probe is bound to every file a dispatch is bound to (references, agents and skills too), not
  only the top-level scripts and hook manifests. The value of a stored probe changes once after the upgrade: `--check` reads
  `stale` and one `--prepare` makes a fresh probe. A package or config file that cannot be read gives
  `unknown:<why>:<nonce>`, which equals no stored value: `host_probe.py --check` then says `unverified` with a
  `fingerprint_detail` (the added key) naming the file kind and the door, never `stale` and never `verified`. `observe` (every tool
  event while a probe store exists) now runs its session and command checks before it hashes the package; what it returns is
  unchanged.
- Audit A14 reads `release_fingerprint.compare()` (`package_modified`), not the stamp: `no` is the only "no violations"; `yes`
  prints `package_modified: yes` with the changed, added and removed files (at most 10 names each, then `(+k more)`) as INFO,
  because a person's own edit of an installed copy is not a fault of the factory; `unknown` prints its `why` and the unreadable
  files as INFO and is never a pass (a fresh install with no release file stays green, saying `unknown (no_release_file)`).
- `factory_manifest.py`: `DEFINITION_GLOBS` is deleted; `collect_definition()` is `release_fingerprint.file_digests()`, so the
  stamp pins the same map as the release file. A stamp records `recipe`; `--check` on a stamp of another recipe (every stamp made
  before this change) prints one "another recipe" line and judges no file, and on a tree it cannot read prints one `UNKNOWN`
  line (exit 1). `--stamp` on a tree it cannot read refuses (exit 2) naming the files and writes nothing.

- One seam for "the factory has no move" (conductor/1, C1-1; P22): `Driver.no_move` is the only place the driver calls the
  conductor and reads its verdict. A refusal no table row knows, a person's words that match none of the offered answers, a
  cap, a stuck loop and a stand preparation that only a person can settle all end in a closed question with at least two
  options, each followed by `the factory:`, `you:` and `the story:` lines, or in a move the conductor took. The conductor's
  `options` are authoritative (duplicate tokens, a token outside the open moves, a prose that names other tokens, or none at all
  fall back to the standing `retry` / `go on` / `stop` with their prices, and the defect is journalled once); the moves it may
  take are filtered by the story's state first (`no_move.py`). A token the person answers is read against the options of
  the question that offered it, runs its own move, and is never filed as words for a role; the person's original words stay in
  one file, kept whole. A refusal raised while taking an answer now ends in a question instead of a traceback. Gate A, gate B
  and the S1 review keep their behaviour until their own executors land.
- `human_text.py` checks the price lines of every offered token (`price_lines` in `references/human-text.json`).

- The conductor's powers as data (`references/conductor-actions.json`, P22): `moves` (nine rows, each with its command, precondition,
  the cost to the factory and to the person, and what it does to delivery), `price_classes` (words, never a number) and `fallback`
  (the three standing answers `retry` / `go on` / `stop`); the test-location sequence, the `factory_fixable` command pointer and
  the exclusion door moved there from `references/conductor.md`, which keeps one-line pointers and its bans. The ban on calling a
  role is lifted for the controller's own doors (`rework`, `release`, `story_step.py start`), and `conductor.md` now says the
  conductor is called when the factory has no move and answers with options. A `rework` move is a data row whose precondition
  stays false until the later stages can re-run (conductor/1, C1-4): nothing is promised that the factory does not keep.
- `references/human-questions.md` gains a sixth element: every option of a closed question carries `the factory:`, `you:` and
  `the story:` lines, a cost nobody measured is said as a class, and one possible move is a report, not a question. A worked
  example (the stand question) is the target text; `tests/test_human_questions.py` holds the element, the example and the
  size.
- The conductor prompts in `story_run.py` (`MOVES_RULE`, the token sentence, the gate exclusion, `DELIVERY_RULE`): where a
  person's words match none of the offered answers the conductor takes a move from `moves` or asks with options; at gate A and
  gate B no options are offered (a token there would be recorded as an approval); the delivery prompt no longer forbids the
  conductor to ask when a repair is still undone, and says `no attempt recorded` on a first call. A dispatch the conductor
  registered now runs with the controller record's own `reason`, the person's words whole, not with its `purpose`
  (`dispatch_action`, FR-8).
- `controller.py --operation rework --words-file <file>` reads the person's words through `person_words.read` (a multi-line
  reason is stored whole; `--reason` together with `--words-file` is refused with exit 2 and no event); inline `--reason` is
  unchanged. `tests/test_conductor_doors.py` (K8-K14), `tests/test_human_questions.py` and `tests/test_controller_rework.py`
  hold all of it.

- One door for the person's decision about a dispatch (conductor/2, C2-3 core; classes K2 and K9): `story_step.py decide --task <T>
  --dispatch-id <D> --words-file <file> (--hand <cases> | --open [<ids>] | --close)` records the decision once, by code. `--hand`
  (S5) writes the manifest `unresolved[]` rows of the cases the person runs themselves through `manifest_put.py` (a row with the
  profile's command or the steps of the case in `detail`, the person's words only by `words_ref`; a `handed_to_person` row keeps its
  command, a `blocked_by_env` row or any other reason is refused by name) and rebuilds the window; `--open` / `--close` write only
  `state/decisions/<D>.json`, which `finish` reads (the stage stays open on the named work, or closes as it is). The words are copied
  into `state/words/` by `person_words.write_words` (the one writer of that folder, with the pure `words_file_path`). `finish`
  derives the completion pair for a handed case that lists no instance (also in a window of green instances), appends such cases to
  a pair the driver derived (the caller's reason first, the stand block second, the append last, cut from the tail with `…`), and
  `--unresolved` with `--not-complete` is refused on S5 only. The door is closed to every role (`guard_pre_tool`).
- The S1 inspection receipt is a fact of the code: the writer of the snapshot stamps `inspection_status: read` (`inspection_by:
  code:snapshot`) when the snapshot lies on disk with its hash, and `ticket_adapter.py receipts --output <inventory>` stamps a story
  that was running before; a receipt a role wrote (`assess`) is never overwritten. The controller judges the S1 close over one
  summary (`source_inputs`): the branch that read a person's word for a second, differing summary is removed.
- One record passes a missing-branch finding at both stages: the S4 rehearsal reads an S3 word that quotes the finding, so it is no
  longer recorded twice.

- A role is resumed only for judgement (conductor/2, C2-4; K9). What code can write, code writes before a paid session:
  `handoff_check.py --shorten` (with `--fix`, the driver's flag - a role's own `--fix` never cuts) cuts the tail of a form field
  over its contract limit and marks the cut with the path of the whole text (`[cut: work/handoffs/<dispatch>.yaml]`; the role's
  own words stay whole in a `shortened:` section of the form, one row per field). It cuts only when length is the form's sole
  problem (a length problem now carries `limit` in the JSON), and not when the mark leaves fewer than 8 characters of the role's
  words. The driver cuts at the first entry of `handoff` and between the first and the third resume, so a third resume is never
  spent on a count; the sentence "A reason over its limit is shortened, not explained" leaves the third resume's text.
- Before every resume of a refused `finish` the driver runs the doors of code (`Driver.close_by_doors`): the form
  (`--fix --shorten`), the code critic's review receipt (`window_record.py --review-receipt`, only when the findings file exists)
  and the scout's source receipts (`ticket_adapter.py receipts`); a door counts as having written when its target file's sha256
  changed, the refused call is made again once, and a refusal it closes prints `closed by code (...) - no resume` and writes no
  resume record. Once per (dispatch, finding set) per process, and never from inside its own retry.
- The S4 case critic's finish says `OpenWork` (`--not-complete --unresolved cases_in_repair --reason ...`, timeless, at most 300
  characters) when its verdict sends cases back, a round is left and a findings file exists - the three conditions of the repair
  round that follows - instead of a silent `stage_complete: false` the controller refuses (one wasted critic resume); with no
  findings file the old `false` stays. The recovery road (`completion_for`) applies the same rule (`Driver.s4_critic_completion`),
  and S7 and S4 share one reason cut (`open_work_reason`). The reason names the cases the critic rejected (no number when they
  cannot be read). A critic accepted with `cases_in_repair` whose round nobody registered (its finish went through the recovery
  road, or a refused finish that came back as `continue`) gets its designer round at the next S4 entry, derived from the
  dispatch records - never a new critic over the same cases. Where no assembly of the final message follows (after the first
  resume), the form is not cut while the exit gate still has a line for the role.

- `waiver.py --stage S --block` is held against the refusal that stands (`waiver.block_standing`, t-722 C2-5, class K4). The
  carrier is the driver's record of the standing refusal (`state/standing-refusal.json`: `stage`, `lines`, and `doors`, the block
  names the refusal printed in its own door line): only when that record holds lines or doors for the stage is a block in none
  of them refused (exit 2, nothing written), with those lines as the closed options and the words kept without a pass
  (`--remark`) as the other door. The dispatch guard is an advisor: the guard alone refuses nothing (at gate A it always holds
  `gate A is not approved`). The driver writes the record (`Driver.no_move`, one writer, from the lines of the refusal it is handling;
  erased when the conductor moves, the step goes through, the question is answered or none is open at start): while no refusal is
  recorded for the stage, every block the guard does not hold is recorded and the output says `not verified`, naming the guard lines
  that still stand. A block taken
  verbatim from a door the factory printed (for example `no accepted controller stage`) is recorded on the refusal's own door,
  also `not verified`: the record does not re-run the check. `block lifted` is printed only for what the guard re-run checked,
  never for a block held against the record or a door, and never after a revocation (`pass taken back:` instead). The factory's own block
  constants live in one place (`OWN_FORM_BLOCKS`; `story_step.MODE_SWITCH` and the driver's calls take their names from there). The
  conductor's note for a `go on` without a block of its own lists the lines the record holds for the stage (at most 20, the rest
  counted with the record's path), or says that none is recorded.
- `skills/qa-story/SKILL.md` and `references/conductor.md` teach the orchestrator and the conductor to take `--block` from a line
  of the refusal and to read `block lifted` / `not verified` / the refusal's list of standing lines.
- Upgrade note: the lines of a refusal are now normalised once (a trailing span is cut only when it is a door, a code span holding
  `--` or `.py`; the exit gate's handoff lines are split like every other refusal's), so the `refusal_resumes` keys and the bought-round
  keys of a story already in flight change once on upgrade: one extra resume, and a round the person bought but the driver has not yet spent is asked for again.

- The person's token answer carries the person's original words (conductor/2, C2-6; class K5): `rework` offered by the conductor now
  carries `"args"` (stage, role, cases or rows, cause) checked against a closed list the prompt prints once; a bad `args` goes back
  to the conductor once with the list, never to the person. When the person chooses it the driver records the choice (`seam_rework`)
  and, on its next step and before `where`, runs `controller.py --operation rework --words-file` over the ORIGINAL answer's file
  (whole, no `[:1500]`; a role told of words longer than 1500 gets the file's path). `restart` releases the dispatch by code through
  `waiver.run_release` (the one caller of the controller's `release`; the exit-limit `fresh` goes through it too), and `go on` with a
  known block passes `waiver.py` the original file. Every other chosen move goes to the conductor with the original words and what the
  option says. Words that are named but not on file hold the question for every one of these moves. An answer to a call for the
  person's choice may be ONE `rework` option with `args`: that is a decision, run without asking the person again.

- The fallback question carries the words of the site that raised it (conductor/2, C2-7; class K6): at gate A / gate B the question the
  factory asks when no conductor answer is usable now offers `approve` (recorded by code with the answer already on file), `rework`
  (the answer goes to the conductor with the person's original words, which names the stage; the person is not asked again), `retry`
  and `stop`, from the same table and prices the conductor's own gate options use, the stages named in words; an option that is not
  open is said in one line of the lead, and a fact that cannot be read removes its move without being told as a reason. The floor of a
  gate offers `approve` only with the answer on file and the gate open. A word that is not one of the options of a gate question the
  seam raised is now read as a new answer of the gate (the approval word, the stand-card lines of the answer with the earlier answer's
  keys kept, anything else whole to the conductor, the earlier answer appended): the `approve` that went round `retry` / `stop` three
  times in the cmp3 run is recorded once. The question after six refused moves says, in the story's words, which stage has not finished.
  `go_on_as_is` in `conductor-actions.json` says its block is one of the refusal's lines, whole. Stories in flight: a gate question
  already open with only `retry` / `stop` takes `approve` from the next answer on; nothing else changes for them. A second answer at a gate
  keeps both answers whole in the decision and in the words file the next question names, while the card lines (`Q5: a`) are read from the
  new answer alone, also when the person then chooses `approve` (a correction after `Q5: b` applies `a`, no conflict); a words file the
  question names that is gone holds the answer and tells the person, nothing is recorded; a story that has no stage at the limit says
  only that the reasons are the factory's own, with no claim about a stage.

- A stage the factory closes by code with no role (the receipt of S6 or S7, the retro's record at S9) now gets a move when its own
  record is refused (t-745 C2-8, class K3). `Driver.record_close` is the one record (`stage_done` and its tail) and `close_receipt` the
  one receipt of those closes; a refusal at either is marked, and `handle_refusal` puts it to the person (`code_close`, three priced
  questions in `question-prices.json`: `code_close.stage`, `code_close.closed_story`, `code_close.factory_file`) with no conductor call.
  The tokens have ONE executor (`_answer_code_close`): `retry`, `stop`, and at the retro `go on` (the pass is written by `waiver.py`,
  the finding is filed) and `full retro` (`stage_done --set retro_mode=full`). No role is offered where none works. A step left
  `running` is settled by `controller.py --operation recover`, once, before the question. The record of S6/S7 that was refused is
  written again only over the receipt it was deferred for (`code_close_step`), twice at most, then the person is asked.
- The known line `s0_receipt` (the retro's `no accepted controller stage`) now answers with the move of S0 only on the boundary of S0; at
  S9 it used to end the run in the generic question (measured t-763).
- Upgrade note: a story in flight with a receipt written and its record refused before this build has no deferred record; the same
  refusal, when it comes again, is asked as above.

- The factory no longer asks about what it has itself established it cannot reach, and no longer asks again per instance (conductor/2,
  C2-9; P5 / D-0043). A gap whose cause the factory's own probe established is a gap in the report and not a question: `host_unreachable`
  that the collector's receipt carries (`inspect --probe-ref`; `close_vcs_gaps` now writes that verdict by code from the receipt's
  `vcs_evidence` code, and collects again at every scout handover, so a restored VPN simply brings the merge request in), `no_tool` on an
  address that is not a merge request, `too_large` with a measured size at or above the read limit of the guard (`big_read_cap`, one
  reader). `forbidden_by_policy` is never a default (no record of a standing decision exists to check it against): it is asked. Every doubt is a question (a missing carrier, an unknown code, an unreadable table). The causes and
  the code table are data: `references/source-causes.json` (one reader, `source_inventory.cause_table`).
- One answer about a KIND of gap covers every later instance in the story: `accept-gap --cause <cause>[,..] --words-file F` writes
  `work/gap-classes.json` (never the inventory, so the sources hash of Gate A does not move); `--revoke GC-n` takes it back until S1 is
  closed, after that the door is a rework of S1. The S1 gap question offers the tokens `not needed` and, when a cause is asked,
  `skip all like these`; code reads tokens and a fence, no phrase list. The question lists only the points still asked, with a line for
  the ones recorded without asking, and is cut at 6000 bytes (a body of exactly 6000 is printed whole; the lists of names and each source line are bounded too, and a `(+K more)` line says what was left out) with the whole list in the details file.
- The S1 pair, the Gate A package (a section "Not reachable by the factory - recorded without asking you", with the door to try again)
  and the source preflight read the words of a kind through one helper and say whose answer it was and when. `environment_record.py`
  shares its file helpers (`load_rows`, `write_rows`, `next_id`, `revoke_row`) with the new record.

- phase texts and the S5 eval teach the block form C2-5 made true (`skills/qa-story/phases/s1.md`, `phases/s5.md`,
  `evals/evals.json`): a person's word is recorded with `waiver.py --block "<a refusal line, whole or in part>"
  --words-file <file>`, and what the command prints is read - `block lifted` (the guard checked it), `not verified` (the
  step that refused reads the word when it runs again) or a refusal listing the lines standing (record again with one of
  them, or keep the words with `--remark`); the S5 remedy/fixture refusal names the parts of its own lines
  ("the row says the stand is missing something", "which the approved case never mentions") instead of the free words
  `remedy` and `fixture` (t-722 class K4, axis 5; C3-10).

- The controller's remaining chains of independent checks refuse every problem at once (conductor/3, C3-11; K1; `controller.py`): a request with several defects used to be refused one at a time, so the person paid a round per defect. Now `Controller._raise_all` takes the chains of `initialize` (the three request fields), `revise_plan`, `semantic_reopen`, `orchestrator_telemetry`, `policy`, `code_only`, `invalidate` (cause and scope, the dispatches named, the four facts of a Gate A carry), `mutation` (intent, progress, receipts), the `dispatch` id and case-review pair, `known_paths` with the host's agent id, `gate-decision`, `rework`, `checkpoint`, `release`, the `rerun_after` stamp, `prepare` outputs, `gate_inputs` and the Gate A content check (the sources and the plan). One failing item is refused with exactly the text it had; several are one numbered list in the chain's order, in the class of the first. Chains whose later checks read what an earlier one establishes, whose refusals name contradicting doors, or whose evidence loops would need a new route in the block map keep refusing one at a time; two checks that read a number or a list of what an earlier one refused are skipped, and a value a later check cannot hash is now a refusal of its own instead of a `TypeError`.

- `story_run.py` (`package_check`): the receipts of the other plugin copies are read in the one code-point order of
  `hooklib.sorted_paths`, so the copy that wins `seen.setdefault` is the same on every platform (the C4-7 order class; this site
  was left for the node that was still writing the file). `test_story_run_words.py`: the pin on the inline words option now counts
  the carrier (`words_args`) apart from the file read `person_words.read(None, <file>, "--words")` in `original_words`, which
  hands nothing over inline.

- The leftovers of the one-order rule for a Path walk (conductor/4, C4-12; after C4-7's `hooklib.sorted_paths`). Gate A's case appendix now lists the cases in code-point order, the same order as the `case_index` refusal (it used a lower-cased key, so `a-x.md` came before `TC-002.md`; now `TC-002.md` comes first on every platform). The controller reads the durable `environment-jobs` records and the Gate A `baseline-receipts` in that order too (`sorted_paths`, not the platform's `Path` order). The self-test runner orders the files it walks by `Path.as_posix()` through one local helper (it does not import `hooklib`: it runs it in a subprocess), so its lists and the first ten names it prints on a hygiene failure are the same on Windows and Linux. The audit's run-block list no longer wraps the helper's list in `list()`.

- the block writer accepts the block names a code reader acts on (`scripts/waiver.py`, new `references/block-names.json`):
  `waiver.py --stage <S> --block "keep it local"` (read by `external_writes.local_only_decision`),
  `--block "executor unavailable: <profile>"` (`contract.handed_profiles`) and `--block "story budget"`
  (`story_budget.override`) are names, not lines of a refusal, and were refused (`unmatched`) when the driver's record of
  the stage held any other line, or recorded as unverified when it held none; they are now recorded at the stages their
  reader reads, whatever the record holds. The names are data (one row per name: the exact text or a prefix with one
  `<placeholder>`, the `module:function` of its reader, the stages); the value after a prefix is ONE token
  (`executor unavailable: e2e ui` is words, not a profile, and is held against the record). A table that cannot be
  read or holds a bad row (a reader that is no function of `scripts/`) changes nothing for a block the table could not
  change (a carrier, a stand gap, the guard's): those are recorded as before; where the block would otherwise be refused
  or unverified, the writer refuses it and names the file, never passes it.
  A text that is not a name (`keep local`) is held against the record as before (t-722 class K4, C2-5s; C4-3).

- The per-reference evidence loops of the controller refuse every reference that does not resolve at once (conductor/4, C4-4; K1; `controller.py`): `reconcile_dispatch` (the successor's evidence), `request_cancel` (the evidence and authorization paths), `accept` (the evidence references, with the reason of an unresolved handoff beside them), `policy`, `code_only` and the evidence of a Gate A applicability carry used to stop at the FIRST reference whose path is not a file or whose sha256 no longer matches, so a request with three bad references cost three rounds. Now each reference is one item of `Controller._raise_all`: one bad reference is refused with exactly the sentence it had, several are one numbered list in the order of the references. A stop of another class (the call's own fault before the story's references, or the reverse) keeps its place. `accept` with a status other than `accepted` now says its evidence references were not checked when it carries any. The block map `design/controller-blocks.md` walks the new collected pairs and the `prepare` row has its specific explanation back; the generator `tools/controller-blocks-gen.py` gained the two routes and a test of its own.

- Three more refusals outside the controller tell every problem at once (conductor/4, C4-5; K1, the siblings of C3-11): `session_handoff.validate_takeover` (a stale `expected_revision`, work still running, an unsupported capability or unverified acknowledgement, a foreign owner and a lease that does not advance), `worker_lifecycle.cancellation` (cause and evidence, the unreported source blocker, the missing budget authorization, the tool still running) and `contract.case_index` (every file whose front-matter id differs from its name or whose identity another file holds, over the whole story) used to raise the first failure and hide the rest, one round per defect. They now refuse in `detector_verdict.compound`'s combined form (the same text `Controller._raise_all` writes, one problem is its own sentence unchanged), in chain order, as the `ValueError` they always raised. `validate_takeover` also names what did not run when the request is not an object, and a value the later checks used to crash on (an acknowledgement or lease that is not an object, a generation that is not a number, a capability that is not hashable) is now a refusal of that check, not an `AttributeError`/`TypeError` that would hide the problems found before it. The census of the other chains (`worker_lifecycle.guard`, `gate_preflight.run`, `stand_gaps.collect`, the other raises of `contract.py`) found no further chain of one class.

- The story-runner tests no longer leave the process standing in a deleted directory (`tests/harness.py`, `tests/story_run_common.py`): `driver_for` records the caller's cwd and `harness.cleanup(root)` goes back to it BEFORE it deletes the project a Driver chdir'd into (Linux deletes a cwd, Windows refuses, so the class only ever turned the NEXT test red on Linux); `harness.guard_cwd` runs after every scenario of `run_scenarios` and at `finish`, and names the test that left a dead cwd (`test_harness_cwd_guard.py` pins it, with a negative control). Test-only: nothing in the shipped scripts changed (C4-6)

- `hooklib.sorted_paths` (`hooklib.py`): the one order of a Path walk. `sorted(<Path>)` compares the path parts with the
  platform's rules (case-folded on Windows, case-sensitive on Linux) and an unsorted `glob` is the order of the directory
  on disk, so the lines of a refusal, a report or a check list built from a walk came out in a different order on a
  developer's machine and in CI (the `case_index` red of 16.10, t-887, was one site of this class). The helper orders by
  `Path.as_posix()`: code point of the whole path, the same everywhere (`B/` before `a/`, `TC-0001` before `TC-001`,
  `a.md` before `a/x.md`); an item that is not a `Path` is a `TypeError`, not ordered by another rule. 124 walks whose
  order reaches text, a file or a fingerprint in 61 scripts moved onto it (`contract.case_glob` loses its inline key,
  `session_handoff.can_takeover` and `exit_gate.collect_errors` now list their jobs, writes and errors in that order);
  the package fingerprints of `install_smoke.py`, `runtime_paths.py` and `host_probe.py` now hash the files in that
  order, so each is the same on every platform and its value changes once (of the 400 files hashed by the first two, 6
  stand elsewhere in the order on Linux and 103 on Windows, e.g. `README.md` before `adapter-forms.json`): a fresh smoke report and a fresh host
  probe are recorded against the new value.

- The block `executor unavailable: <profile>` (and `stand gap: <id>`) is now read by one helper, `contract.prefix_value`, instead of three parsers that read the value differently (conductor/4 C4-9). The writer (`waiver.py`, the block-name check) and the person's phrase already took exactly one token after the prefix; the reader, `contract.handed_profiles`, took any remainder, so a record such as `executor unavailable: e2e ui` or `executor unavailable: : x` made it hold a profile no stand has. It now holds a profile only for a value the writer would have accepted (one token, quotes and backticks cut, no leading colon); a line with words, or with no value, is absent. The writer still refuses such a block, so the reader meets one only in a hand-edited record. The waiver script's private copy of the rule is removed.

- Rate table (`references/model-rates.json`): checked row by row against the Anthropic price page on 2026-10-16. `claude-sonnet-5-5`
  cache read is $0.10 per million tokens (was $0.20, so a story's cache reads on that model were priced at twice the true
  figure); a `claude-haiku-5-5` row is added with the prompt <= 100000 tokens tariff (the long-prompt band is named in its
  `note`, not modelled); `claude-opus-5-5` and `claude-fable-5-1` already matched the page and carry the new check date. A
  test now compares every page-listed row with the file (FR-28) and pins hand-computed request costs for the 5.x models.
  `catalogue_revision` is now `provider-docs-2026-10-16-r1`: it is part of the cost capture key. Stored cost files are not
  re-captured in bulk: a request already captured keeps the price it was captured with, and readers (task price, dashboard,
  retro numbers) re-price it from the current rate table at read time under the current revision.
- Story price (`task_price.py`): a request whose model the rate table does not list stays an unknown (never $0) and the session's
  reason now names the model: `rate unknown for <model>` (FR-41).

- Story price (`cost_capture.py`): a request served by a model fallback is now priced by the provider's own per-message records
  (`usage.iterations`, two or more usable entries), each entry by its own model, and the request is their sum. Before, the
  last transcript line of the request was priced by that line's `model` label, and a fallback request whose lines all said
  opus-4-8 but whose records held a fable-5 message and an opus-4-8 message was priced as one opus message (two real requests
  measured: 0.154843 instead of 0.427694, and 0.06271675 instead of 0.21261). Such a request is stored as one row per model:
  the row of the model the last line names keeps the request id, every other part is `<id>|<model>` (`#<position>` for a
  repeated model), so a model's tokens and money land under that model in `by_model`, `by_task`, `by_activity` and the reader
  that re-prices a stored file at read time. Each part row counts as one request, so a fallback request adds one to the request
  count per extra part (the two measured requests: +1 each). A request without such records is read as before; a one-entry or
  null `iterations` (every single-model request carries one) changes nothing; a malformed `iterations` is ignored and counted.
  An entry's 1-hour cache split is clamped into its cache write; a missing split is priced as a 5-minute write and counted
  (never an invented proportion). A line whose top-level counts are all zero never replaces an earlier line of the same request
  that has counts (the real shape of 9 measured requests: zeros on top, the numbers only in a one-entry `iterations`).
- Cost document: a new field `usage_reader` = `{"bad_iterations": n, "split_missing": n}`, written only when a count is non-zero
  (`bad_iterations` = lines whose `usage.iterations` was malformed and ignored; `split_missing` = requests with a fallback part
  that had no 1-hour split). Scan checkpoints carry `reader: "iterations-1"`: a checkpoint of the earlier reader is rebuilt once
  at the session's next capture (a live session rescans its transcript files once; a finished session's file is not read again).
  Stored cost files are not re-captured in bulk: a request already captured keeps the one-model price it was captured with until
  an explicit `cost_capture.py --recapture`.

- A manifest fragment the merge cannot take is refused before it is committed, and a journal that already holds one still
  moves. On 19.10 TP2-2406 committed seven `manifest_patch` events from `S5-qa-automator-4` (journal seq 110-115
  and 117) and `work/automation-manifest.json` stayed at revision 5: seq 115 renamed a test (the new spelling sent, the
  old one in `retracted_instances`), the new row had already replaced the old one by alias, so `_retract_instances` found
  no row for the old id and raised "names no row this manifest holds" - inside the projection, AFTER the event was
  appended. The event was durable and the projection was not, so every later `manifest_put` replayed seq 115 and raised
  again; the S5 exit gate refused for a `run_witness` the manifest could never receive, and the controller's
  `recover` rebuilt only the controller's projection and removed the one `projection-stale.json` both shared, so the
  only trace of the stale manifest was gone. Now (1) a retraction whose id the manifest held before this merge and no
  row answers to after it is satisfied, not a wrong id: the old id is recorded in `retracted_instances` once, nothing is
  dropped, and an id the manifest never held, or one an earlier revision already dropped, is refused as before; (2)
  `manifest_put.run` folds the journal in memory (the same `fold` the projection uses) and runs the merge BEFORE the
  commit, so every refusal of the merge - any exception, not only `ValueError` - is a refusal with the merge's words,
  the repair marker and the door, exit 3, and no event is appended - on the legacy-seed road too: when the journal has no
  manifest event yet, the fragment is checked against the SEED's fold before the seed is committed, so a refused fragment
  leaves the journal, `work/automation-manifest.json` and a root-level legacy file exactly as they were; (3) `fold` skips an event whose merge raises and
  names it in the manifest's new `unprojected_events: [{sequence, idempotency_key, error}]` (replaced on every fold,
  omitted when empty; `revision` counts merged events only), so a journal written before this change moves on and the gap
  is on the manifest for the role and the gate to read; (4) `manifest_put.py --task <T> --recover` replays the journal
  into the manifest (`manifest: revision <n>, <k> events merged[, <m> unprojected: seq a (error)]`; `manifest: already
  current - revision <n>, ...` and no write when the file already holds what the journal adds up to; `manifest: nothing
  to project` for a journal with no manifest event; an absent or stale file is rebuilt, and so is one that equals the
  fold in value only - `revision: true` or `1.0` for `1`, or the keys in another order), writes only the projection, is
  idempotent, and is refused together with `--fragment`; a commit
  whose projection fails now prints "event committed; projection stale - the fragment is in the journal, do not send it
  again; replay with manifest_put.py --task <T> --recover" and exits 4 instead of 3 - but when the stale projection is
  the seed of a legacy `automation-manifest.json` (the fragment itself is not yet committed) it says so, exits 3 and
  names the way on, and `--recover` names the busy-writer door only for a held lock (a migration conflict names both
  files and the orchestrator); (5) the manifest has its own marker,
  `state/manifest-projection-stale.json` (`EventStore(stale_marker=...)`, default `projection-stale.json` unchanged for
  every other caller), which the controller's recover does not touch; the audit's control-plane list and stale check
  and the dashboard's stale flag read it beside the others (and the audit now reads the environment jobs' marker too, as
  the dashboard does); (6) an `unprojected_events` entry is a terminal record of an event that cannot merge: `run` and
  `--recover` print ONE sentence for it (the whole `--fragment` command, then `manifest_view.py`), true before and after the
  corrected content is sent, and `design/state-exits.md` has a row for it and for the three stale markers; (7) the callers
  that run `manifest_put.py` as a child (`story_step.py decide --hand`, the gate-answer applier, `migrate_artifacts.py`,
  `window_record.py --review-receipt`, `probe_by_code.py` publish) read its exit code through `manifest_put.outcome`: exit 4
  (committed, projection stale) names `manifest_put.py --task <T> --recover` and is no longer reported as refused.
- Effect to know: a manifest without `unprojected_events` reads exactly as before. A story already stopped this way needs
  one `manifest_put.py --task <T> --recover`. A role that re-sends a spelling it retracted earlier (2406's seq 117 did)
  gets that row back as a row of its own - no covers, no version pin, bound to nothing - as before; retracting the id again drops it. Not changed
  here: `controller.py --operation recover` still rebuilds the controller's projection only, and `story_run`'s
  `committed_event` row still matches the new refusal text and answers "recover" (the controller's), which is not the
  manifest's door; both are queued.

- An area-qualified case id (`feedback-api/TC-003`) is now matched to its manifest row by ONE reader, `contract.entries_for_case(entries, case, cfg)`, in `run_suite.py --mine`, in `execution_request.manifest_rows` and in `s5_precheck`. The dispatch scope keeps the area of a case, while `contract.manifest_test_links` answers in bare ids on purpose, so a row with `covers: ["feedback-api/TC-003"]` was never found: `--mine feedback-api/TC-003` was refused with a message about execution profiles, and the S5 precheck reported `OB-3` unbound although its binding named the instance exactly. A qualified ask is now compared with the area-aware keys of the row, a bare ask with its links; the matcher has no ambiguity rule and never raises.
- `--mine` (the strict path of `execution_request._entries_of_case`) refuses instead of guessing, and every refusal names what the factory could not establish and a door the role can use: a qualified ask whose number the manifest holds only under other areas (the asked id, the areas held, `manifest_put.py` or hand the case back in the digest); an area-less (0.7.x) row for a qualified ask when the story's case store holds the number under several areas (one bare row is never credited to two areas); a bare ask on a number held under more than one area, in the manifest OR in the story's case store (every qualified spelling and the one to type). A qualified ask whose own area the store holds but whose row is not in the manifest yet is told "the manifest names no test for it" - never that the scope and the manifest disagree on the area, which would send the role to relabel another area's correct row. A case with no row and no file is refused with that sentence before the execution profile is chosen, so several profiles no longer turn it into "cannot tell which execution profile". An area-less row for a number the store holds under one area still runs, with a note in the run's notes; a caller that names no case store (probes, the sandbox, the scope walk) gets no area-less row for a qualified ask, as before. The asked spelling and the row's `case_version_links` pins travel into the request unchanged. A person's word that passes the scope block does not pass these refusals: it would forge coverage.
- `s5_precheck.instances_of_case`, `bindings_of_case`, `check_manifest` and the instance-id shape check read through the same predicate, so a qualified scope case finds its rows, its `then_bindings` and its duplicate and shape findings. A bare `unresolved[]` row of the number is found by a qualified scope case while the number is held under one area, and is a finding naming every spelling when it is held under two. A `then_refs` entry for `feedback-api/TC-003` is checked against that area's own case file and Then numbers, not the first file of that number. A backslash-spelled qualified ask (`feedback-api\TC-003`) reads as the slash key. Effect to know: a bare scope, a bare manifest and a bare ask read exactly as before; outside `--mine` a bare ask over a number two areas hold still returns both rows. Not changed here: other readers of `manifest_test_links` that compare a qualified id are not swept.

- The SubagentStop hook no longer tells the controller that a story_step-bound dispatch came back. On 20.10 `S5-qa-automator-7`
  and `-8` on TP2-2406 (Codex Desktop) were checkpointed blocked with "run_suite refused: no active S5-qa-automator-7
  dispatch": the native child's per-turn stop fires while the role is still working on the same thread, `subagent_journal.py`
  called `Controller.record_return` for it (controller events 131 and 135, `returned`, recorded_by `subagent_stop`, empty digest),
  and the dispatch was `returned_unaccepted` 97 s before the role's `run_suite` call, so `execution_request.find_active_dispatch`
  correctly found no running dispatch. A dispatch bound by `story_step bind` is returned by `story_step finish` alone (it accepts
  or checkpoints through the controller and marks the receipt terminal; `host_dispatch.record` already never marks such a receipt
  terminal on a stop). The hook now looks for that receipt before the return is told: the receipt `event["host_binding"]` names
  decides only when it is a story_step receipt (on the live host a receipt the host hook wrote at spawn, keyed by the child's
  thread id, and the story_step one coexist for one dispatch, and the hook finds the first); every other answer falls through to
  the receipt (read through `host_dispatch.receipt_files`, the one scanner of the receipt directory) with `bound_by: story_step` whose `task_id` and `dispatch_id` are the
  stop's own (task AND dispatch id, never the role: a previous window's receipt, or another story's receipt for the same
  dispatch id, does not shadow). When one exists - running or already terminal - `record_return` is not called; every other
  stop (a receipt written by the host hook alone, no receipt at all) reaches the controller exactly as before. The skip holds
  on every host, Claude Code included: the contract is the binding, and `story_step bind` writes `bound_by: story_step` there too.
  A stop of a story_step-bound dispatch is never a return on any host; the one terminal is `story_step finish`, and a worker
  that never finishes shows ALIVE, then UNKNOWN, then the person's release.
- Effect to know: the `subagent_stop` line of the project journal is written in every case, as before, with new fields:
  `return_owner` (`story_step` when a story_step receipt owns the dispatch, `subagent_stop` otherwise; omitted when the stop
  names no dispatch of the story, since then nobody is told: the host's own thread or agent id, which the exit gate falls
  back to when the event sends no `dispatch_id`, is no dispatch) and, when a story_step receipt owns the dispatch,
  `dispatch_receipt` (the file name of the receipt in `state/host-dispatches/`; both fields are trail, no code reads them). A
  Claude Code stop that carries only its agent id and no receipt now reaches the fallbacks that read the dispatch id from the
  subagent transcript's prompt or the event's own prompt, so the hook still tells the controller about such a dispatch. For a story_step-bound dispatch `dispatch_liveness` never decides by the journal's `subagent_stop` line: a role that
  ends without `story_step finish` is RETURNED by `native_stop` when its rollout ends with `task_complete`, otherwise UNKNOWN after
  the age threshold, with the release door. An unreadable receipt counts as no receipt; the hook never raises and never blocks a
  stop. An unknown dispatch id is never guessed from a receipt.
  `Controller.record_return` is unchanged and stays idempotent (a dispatch that is not `running` returns False and commits
  nothing). A late native stop after `story_step finish` carries no dispatch of the story (`enrich` names no story from a
  terminal receipt), so it reaches the controller under the thread id and returns nothing. Not rewritten: `returned` events that an earlier build already wrote into a story's history.

- test fixtures that model a project carry the project marker through one helper (`scripts/tests/harness.py`): `mark_project(root)`
  writes `qa-factory/config.json` from the shipped template into an existing folder, and `temp_project` builds on it; the
  fixtures of the controller, rework, resume, release and gate tests that built a story without the marker now use them
  (hand-written `{}` copies remain elsewhere: `test_scout_reliability` keeps one on purpose, its subject being the config's
  content, and `test_story_closed` keeps one in `closed_story`, to be folded in a follow-up node). Since the
  one project walk (`runtime_paths.nearest_project`) finds a project by that file alone, a story folder built without it
  silently took the "no project" road of every branch the controller guards with `_project_root()` (the host-binding veto,
  liveness, the RUN gate) and stayed green while the branch was never reached; `test_runtime_paths.py` pins that the helpers
  make a project by the marker alone (the marker removed from a `temp_project` root leaves `nearest_project` None); the
  "unknown" road a consumer takes on that None stays pinned by `test_controller_rework` and `test_controller_paths`.
  Test-only, no package code changed.

- The slow-test list is a data file (`scripts/slow_tests.json`, read by `selftest.py`): `--fast` skips exactly the files it
  names, and the hand-edited `SLOW_TESTS` tuple is gone. The file carries the thresholds (10 s to belong, under 5 s to
  leave), the measured seconds per file, `measured_on`, `source` and `max_drift`. Absent or malformed, `selftest.py`
  refuses at start (exit 2, one line naming the file) instead of running a fast tier that quietly runs everything (F6-18)
- `selftest.py --slow-tests [--from <selftest.txt>] [--update]` (new): prints the list against a measurement as
  `+ file <s>` (over the threshold, not listed), `- file <s>` (listed, under the other threshold, or gone from disk),
  `= n unchanged` and `slow tests: k change(s) (limit N)`; exit 1 when k is above `max_drift`, exit 2 when nothing was
  measured. `--update` rewrites the data file from the measurement. The two INFO staleness lines of a full run are gone:
  the diff replaces them. The nightly `package-full` job runs it on `ci-out/selftest.txt` and turns red when the list has
  drifted by more than `max_drift` files (F6-18)

- One search for the project root (`runtime_paths.nearest_project`): the nearest folder at or above a start that holds
  `qa-factory/config.json` as a file, or None - never a folder without the marker and never the working directory. Seven
  private walks in `controller`, `judge`, `bug_records`, `dashboard_refresh`, `runtime_paths` (`resolve_runtime`,
  `project_for_task`) and `critic_rollcall`, and the twin in `hooklib._nearest_project`, now delegate to it and keep their
  names; `tests/test_runtime_paths.py` finds every walk for the marker by its syntax tree and fails on a new one
  (B-309 item d).
- Two changes a user can see (B-309 item d). `check_coverage.py` run from a folder that is not a project (its default
  root, or a `--root`, has no `qa-factory/config.json`) now stops with exit 2 and names the folder and the door instead of
  printing "OK: no local cases" and exiting 0. The controller's dispatch gate, for a story that sits under no
  `qa-factory/config.json` and whose packet depends on the project (a `{project_root}` token or an absolute
  `project_root`), asks the same finder `prepare` uses, and refuses with its text and its `--project` door when no project
  holds the story; before, `{project_root}` silently became the story's own folder.
- The controller reads host receipts and transcripts only from a real project: with none found (it used to be the story's
  own folder) liveness closes nothing, `next` says `unknown` and names the missing `qa-factory/config.json`, and a denial
  recorded in the story's own folder no longer closes a dispatch as never started (B-309 item d).

- One JSON reader for the package (`hooklib.read_json`): ten private `_read_json` copies in `stand_gaps`, `gate_preflight`,
  `sizing`, `stage_status`, `tracker_write`, `exit_gate`, `execution_request`, `judge_results`, `runtime_probe` and
  `story_run` now delegate to it, each keeping its own error direction (`None`, `{}` or the caller's default). One visible
  change: a JSON file with a UTF-8 BOM now parses in those readers instead of reading as the default (B-309 item e).
- One `GATE_STAGE` table (`stand_gaps.py`; `gate_preflight` imports it) and one `_replace_table` in `project_decisions.py`
  for both the table and the findings block (B-309 item e).
- The refusal texts of the bug-report transport (`external_writes.process_bug_proposal`, `_run_command_transport`) are
  pinned by `tests/test_external_writes_bug_refusals.py` (15 texts; a new text without a test is caught) (B-309 item zh).
- Dead re-exports of `factory_dashboard` (`driver_role`, `driver_charged`, `WHY_NO_TOTAL`) removed; the lint baseline
  shrinks from 13 to 10 (B-309 item z). Two bare calls that looked dead (`story_run.stage_S4`'s `self.stages()`,
  `hooklib.needs_guard`'s `resolve_app_root`) are proved live by `tests/test_bare_calls_live.py` (B-309 item i).

- `story_step finish` re-runs the stage's exit gate before it accepts (gates-and-words/1, GW1-8; P22, FR-4, FR-59, AR-28): for every
  role whose stage declares `detectors` in `references/stages.json` (S2 tester, S3 strategist, S4 case critic, S5 automator, S8
  scribe; read from that data through `exit_gate.detector_gates()`, no role is named in code) `finish` calls the driver's own
  function `exit_gate.all_errors(role, task, "")` after the halt gate and the form check, and before anything is recorded. A
  handoff the gate still refuses is exit 3 with nothing recorded: the findings whole through `detector_verdict.render`
  (past the byte ceiling the whole list is `state/findings/<dispatch>-finish.txt`), the author's road (`pause` then `recover`,
  or the same role resumed), the repair marker, and the person's door only where it opens - `waiver.py --stage <S> --block
  "<a part only that line holds>"` for the lines a named word can pass, the person's `*` for the lines judged at their source,
  and none for the lines the source refused to every word. A released turn (the hook's fuse) is no longer an accepted handoff:
  the S5 automator that never ran its tests could be accepted and the code critic then received a window with no author run.
- No flag lifts the read (`--ignore-handoff`, `--unresolved`, `--complete`, `--window`); the person's recorded word is judged
  by the same rule as at the hook (a revoked word, a word of another stage, an empty decision and a star over a refused finding
  pass nothing) and an informed pass is said in one note. A dispatch the person decided (`decide --open` / `--close` recorded
  for it, a halt or not) is not read again and the skip is a note naming the decision kind; a decision of another dispatch,
  or a decision file that cannot be read, lifts nothing.
  A gate that cannot be read (the reader raised or answered a shape that is not `(blocking, passed)`) is exit 2 and never an
  accept. Gate-registry row `finish_exit_gate` (unknown branch: refuse with a door).
- A row in state `blocked` needs the form's `blocked.problem` (every contract that carries a `blocked` section): `handoff_check`
  refuses it with the honest shapes - keep `blocked` and fill `blocked.problem` with what stops the row; `blocked_by_env` with a
  remedy for the stand (named only to a role that may write that word); `header.verdict: halt` with the refusal quoted in
  `blocked` for a factory command that refused the run. The `scope[].state` comment of the eight contracts that offer
  `blocked`, the vocabulary row and the S5 phase file say so before the work.

- The factory says and counts "requirement", not "AC" (grounding/1, node G1-0; P23, D-0049, D-0050). S0: a ticket with NO criteria
  section no longer stops the story with the `ticket_incomplete` question; it goes on, and the FIRST line of `pipeline.warnings` (the
  line gate A shows) names the headings that were looked for and where the requirements come from instead. The only stop left is a
  LOST READ: a criteria heading with text under it (prose, a table, a list the reader could not take) from which no criteria were read,
  under either markup and in every section the scanner finds (`ticket_light.criteria_section`, the one scanner; `acceptance_criteria`
  returns its items unchanged). That stop says the factory's reader failed, not the ticket, files a finding at once, and offers
  only "paste the ticket", `go on` (the description stays whole) and `stop` - no `retry`, the reader being deterministic. An empty
  template section goes on with a line. A pass stored before this change under the old problem word still covers the stop.
  `then_oracles` gains the word `requirement` beside `ac` (the older name, read as it was and never rewritten); a requirement read
  from the code is still never one (FR-58). The gate-A question signs the first reading of a requirement without an `ac_ref` by
  its register `source` (a comment is no longer shown as "description"), and the size estimate joins such a requirement to the
  manifest by the file path of its `observable`, saying so when it cannot. The wording of FR-21, FR-58, P20, P21, the refusal texts,
  the S1 halt token (`requirement/code conflict`) and the role texts follow. New fixture ticket `QA-2` without AC.

- One reader of a recorded diff (`diff_pass.py`, `handoff_check.py`, `exit_gate.py`, `runtime_probe.py`): `diff_pass` reads a hunk by its
  counted range, so a deleted SQL comment (`-- drop table`) or an added `++ x` is no longer taken for a file header, a path keeps its
  characters (`build/x.py` was read as `uild/x.py`), a path with a blank is read whole, a combined diff (`diff --cc`, `@@@`) is
  refused by name instead of silently lost, and lines are split on LF alone as git counts them. New `diff_pass.index(work_dir)`
  reads EVERY `work/impl-diff*.txt`, adds a pseudo-hunk for a file with no hunk (binary, rename, mode, new empty) and a `body` per
  hunk; `parse`, `--json` and the render keep their previous shape; the command exits 3 when it read with refusals.
- One rule for "is this a production file" (`test_files.file_kind`, `production_files`): the S2 handoff's rows, the S2 gate's new
  modules and the runtime probe's compare list now agree. A file is a test only UNDER a test place (a test folder, a place the
  project names, or a usual name beside a usual folder); a test-looking name alone (`scripts/test_files.py`, `src/app/test_mode.py`,
  a colocated `a.test.ts`) and code under `docs/` are production rows. The S2 gate also demands the new files it could not see
  before (a headerless diff, a path with a blank) and refuses an unreadable or combined `impl-diff*.txt` instead of skipping it
  (FR-59). The handoff's `implementation.diff.*` counts read all recorded diffs and are left to the role when a diff was refused.

- Role text says what the code does, one verdict per place (grounding/1, G1-10; text only, no new check, nothing a saved story
  reads at run time): `references/artifact-contract-grounding.md` no longer says the manifest check reads every observable's
  `source` (no code does; the S2 cell-prefix check refuses a register cell that does not start with a closed word or `none`) and
  names the `note?` field and the empty `requirement` of diff behaviour no requirement names; the scout records such behaviour as an
  observable (`derived: mr-diff`, a token with no reader, is gone) and the requirements tester reads an empty `requirement` as a
  `derived` row, and a behaviour claim when only the diff speaks to it. The scout's no-diff halt writes `implementation.source: none`
  in the manifest (the field the code reads) and the orchestrator records the pipeline value after the person's answer; the
  tester's example of a missing source is `implementation_source: ungrounded`; the `s1.md` halt heading and the S1 halt eval say the
  same. The tester card names the claims row and loses 32 bytes (1188 to 1156 of 1200). The FR-21 debt row is narrowed, not closed:
  `pending_implementation` blocks (kinds file, G1-3); what is left is `skipped`. A pin in `test_s1_s2_contract.py` holds these
  words and couples the FR-21 row to the kinds file.

- S3 runs in two windows when the story has an implementation diff (grounding/1, G1-11). Window 1 (`purpose: s3_labelling`, a new word
  of the closed set in `controller.PURPOSES`, read only through `controller.s3_window_of`) labels `work/grounding.yaml` - rows, requirement
  lines, risks `K-n`, code areas `B-n`, claims - and writes no plan; it is accepted open (`finish --not-complete --unresolved plan_pending`)
  and has no handover form. Window 2 writes the plan over the labelled table and closes S3. The driver prepares the table before window 1
  (`blast_radius.py`, then `grounding_table.py --refresh`, then `base_slice.py`; a failed index or table is a refusal to the conductor, a
  failed slice is a `pipeline.warnings` line), projects the planner's claims into the register after each window, and checks the table
  again before window 2 (a moved register or diff, or an unfilled row of the role's, sends it back to window 1; a finding of the
  driver's or the conductor's that no window cures is a refusal to the conductor before any dispatch). The claims fields the projector
  judges travel in the window-1 dispatch text itself. `phases/s3.md` and `agents/qa-test-strategist.md` carry the same steps and fields. Off the diff, S3 is one window as before.
- The exit gate judges window 1 by the grounding check (the role's findings only) instead of asking for the plan, and a dispatch that asks
  for `purpose: s3_labelling` on another stage or role, or as a rework, is refused.
- The stop and the questions of grounding rows reach the person with grounding batch 2: until then nothing is asked between the windows,
  and a plan written over a table the person's stop has not seen is not yet refused by code.
- One more paid session per S3 on a diff story (measured by the live proof, not here).
- The S2 exit text names the glob it reads (`work/impl-diff*.txt`), the `derived_from` the register check refuses next and the claims
  table an implementation-only row then needs; an unread diff names the doors that open (a re-export, a person's word) (G1-10 site 4/4b).

- The S3 planner's claim reaches the requirements register through code (grounding/1, G1-13): `scripts/claim_projector.py` reads the
  `claims[]` of `work/grounding.yaml` (through the one reader `planning_contract.read_grounding`) and, in ONE move under the answers lock,
  adds the claim's `## Register` row (always implementation-only: `source: derived`, `derived_from: aspect:behaviour-change`, no `ac_ref`,
  the `diff:` observable of `now_ref`, `delta: new`), its `ids:` entry, its `## Behaviour claims` row with `origin: S3-grounding` and the
  before/now question in `requirements-readiness.json`; the counters are recomputed from the rows, every other byte of the register is
  unchanged (CRLF and a BOM stay), a second run writes nothing, and one refused claim holds all. `claim_projector.py --task T [--check]`
  is the command line (detector form 1); `s3_claim_errors` is the read-only check the S3 gate calls. The planner never edits the register.
- `question_register.py` gains `_question_row` (the one row step of a raised question, shared by the S4 door and the claim projector,
  keyed by `{case, then}` or `{claim, origin}`) and `_write_readiness` (the one writer of the raised-question file); the register's and
  the readiness file's `artifact-writers.json` entries name their machinery. On an undated register `coverage_contract` reads a claim
  the grounding step added as waiting for the person.

- The S2 handover form no longer asks for `diff_accounting`, `inputs_read[0].production_files_accounted_for` or the claim
  `every_production_file_reaches_a_requirement_or_is_named_not_requirement_bearing`, and the S1 form no longer expects them of the tester
  (`handoffs/s2-tester-to-strategist.yaml`, `handoffs/s1-scout-to-tester.yaml`, `scripts/handoff_check.py`; grounding/1, G1-16). The account of every diff
  hunk - which requirement it implements, or why it bears none - lives in one place, the S3 grounding table (`work/grounding.yaml`), whose check refuses
  an unlabelled hunk (R1; the exit gate that calls it is grounding/1 G1-5); the per-file S2 rows refused only a blank count, a blank `file` in a filled
  section and a blank or non-boolean claim, and showed files otherwise. `handoff_check --fix` no longer opens S2 rows per production file. A form saved
  before this release, or written by an earlier version of the package, is not refused for these keys: the old keys are read, never refused and never
  derived again. The S1 count `implementation.diff.production_files` stays, as a terminal size figure. The one-line note that
  `scripts/test_files.py` prints when `references/test-path-markers.json` cannot be read now says what is expected of the file and to restore it from
  the installed package; the texts about the "production" question in that script and in the markers file no longer speak of S2 rows.

- The blast-radius index by code (grounding/1, G1-2): `scripts/blast_radius.py` writes `work/blast-radius.json` from the implementation
  diff, the context manifest, git OBJECTS of the recorded commit and the project's test roots - per changed file (an area `B-n`) the
  touched symbols (Python by `ast`, never the hunk header), the callers as file:line, the tests (a test needs a found site), the
  path kind (`additive` only with proof) and, for what code could not measure, an `unmeasured: <reason>` text with a `tests_gap`
  and `shared_path` - an unmeasured radius is never "no radius". `blast_radius.ensure` is the one writer (`--task T [--rebuild
  [--force]] [--json]`; exit 0 built / reused / no implementation diff, 2 refused, 3 no such story); area ids are kept by file key and
  never reissued. The grounding table reads the file and copies it whole.
- The S3 brief of an automated window carries one line about the index (`Blast radius index (code; built|reused): ...`), built when
  the file is missing or stale; a failure is named in the line and never stops the brief.
- `handoff_check.implementation_checkout(entry, cfg, project, diff_name)` is the one "manifest entry -> checkout" survivor, called by
  `blast_radius` and `base_slice`; a non-sha implementation commit now reaches the base slice as the table's own words.

- The data form of the S3 grounding step (grounding/1, G1-3; no step logic yet): `work/grounding.yaml` is declared as an S3 output
  (not a required one) with its writer record and registry entry, and ONE reader, `planning_contract.read_grounding`, returns the
  parsed document with each scalar's typed value and comment (an absent file, an empty one, a top-level list, a `schema_version`
  other than the whole number 1, an unknown top-level key, a byte-order mark, non-UTF-8 bytes, a control character such as CR, NUL
  or U+2028, a tab in an indentation, a line that is no YAML, an unclosed quote or bracket and a key written twice at any depth are
  each refused with a typed problem - `kind` and `who` acts on it - never a partly read table; nothing else parses the file). `vocabulary.yaml` gains `grounding_labels` (seven) and `requirement_grounding_states` (five);
  `references/grounding-policy.json` holds the refactoring-share and coverage thresholds, read by `planning_contract.grounding_policy`
  (a value that is not a whole number 0..100, or `notify` not below `stop`, gives no policy and a reason). A plan row can answer a
  table entry with `grounding:K-n`, `blast:B-n` or `refactoring:G-n` in `risk_source_refs` (`planning_contract.grounding_refs`).
- The requirements register gets a last column `delta` (`new | changed | unchanged`, written at S2, read by its header only; the
  validator refuses another word, and `unchanged` beside a `diff:` observable) and the `## Behaviour claims` table a last column
  `origin` (empty = written at S2, or `S3-grounding`). A register without either column reads exactly as before; a row without a
  `delta` counts as expected to change (`contract.delta_state` says `absent`).
- Delivery verdict: the kind `pending_implementation` now blocks (`no`, owner product): a saved story whose ledger carries
  `pending_implementation` now gets `delivery_ready: no` when gate B recomputes, and a story written ahead of its implementation
  (`unresolved[]` reason `pending_implementation`) is no longer offered the MR at gate B. A new kind `bug_candidate` is
  `after_checks` (a candidate, not a confirmed failure). The premise was measured only on the owner's stand copies (116 ledgers and
  manifests, none carries the word), not on any project.

- The grounding table is prepared, carried over and checked by code (`grounding_table.py`, grounding/1 G1-4): `--skeleton` writes
  `work/grounding.yaml` with an empty row for every hunk of the recorded implementation diff and an empty line for every requirement
  of the register that is not implementation-only; `--refresh` carries the strategist's marks to a new diff by the bytes they marked
  (`sha256` of the hunk body plus its occurrence, never a line number) and keeps whatever cannot be carried in `orphans[]` - nothing
  is dropped and an orphaned row id is never given to a new row; `--check` judges the table (R0 form, R5 stale inputs, R1 every hunk
  labelled, R2 every requirement stated, R3 words and values, R4 references and what a label owes, R8 the blast radius areas) from
  the diff recomputed on disk, prints detector form 1 and writes nothing. A story that records no diff gets a null outcome
  (`implementation_source` current-code, ungrounded or absent) in place of a table. The words of the null outcome are data
  (`references/grounding-policy.json`, `null_outcome_words`). The table has one writer (`write_yaml`; `write_key` writes one key
  through it) and one reader (`planning_contract.read_grounding`); `parse_list` reads an `"a,b"` value. A table the reader refuses
