  (empty, `{}`, a list at the top, another schema) is rewritten by `--refresh --force`: the old bytes stay beside the new table as
  `grounding.unreadable-<sha8>.yaml` and one orphan points at them. The blast radius state and the code part of every area are read
  from `work/blast-radius.json`, never from the table's own copy; an absent or unreadable index file is an R8 finding.

- **Base slice for S3 (grounding batch 1, G1-8).** `scripts/base_slice.py --task T` writes `work/base-slice/*.txt` (windows of 30 lines around the old side of every hunk of the changed production and config files and around the places of `unchanged` register rows, numbered) and the `base_slice[]` key of `work/grounding.yaml` (`repo`, `file`, `base_rev`, `path`, `state: read | absent | unknown`, `why`). The text comes only from git objects of the recorded base, never from the working tree: the `diff_refs.base_sha` of the MR receipt the driver writes (`work/sources/<SRC>/mr-<iid>.json`, found by the same locator the source-exclusion check uses) when its head is the recorded implementation commit, else the first parent of that commit. A file is `read` only when that base reproduces every hunk and, when the implementation commit is in the checkout, base plus hunks is the implementation's file (a multi-commit MR, or a change reverted inside the MR, is `unknown`, never a false "before"); a new file is `absent`; every other doubt is `unknown` with the reason by name. Nothing is fetched. `base_slice.unchanged_evidence` (the one reader, recomputed at every judgement, never read back from the strategist's table) says whether an `unchanged` row's place lies on an untouched line of a file the slice read; `base_slice.base_place_problem` checks a `before_ref: base:` place (a line inside a slice window of a file the slice read). A repository without a checkout marks `unknown` only the files of its own diff, and a place that no recorded repository holds is an `unknown` record with no repository and the reason `repo unresolved`. Stories that reached S3 before this change have no key and every `unchanged` row stays in the coverage count.

- The S7 claim `no_bug_reaches_the_gate_without_a_draft_and_a_triage_row` now counts the drafts the factory writes
  (`handoff_check.py` `_claim_bug_has_a_draft`): it read `work/bug-drafts/*.md` while the drafts are `*.json`, so it refused
  every story that had an APP_BUG row and let through a draft that rested on no row. It pairs both ways, through the one
  helper gate B already used: every draft rests on a triage row with the verdict APP_BUG, and every APP_BUG row has a
  draft; nothing on either side holds; rows that are ENV_ISSUE, FLAKY or TEST_BUG need no draft. The refusal counts both
  sides, names the drafts and rows that do not pair, one door per side, and names a `*.md` file lying in the draft folder
  as not counted. A `work/triage.json` that exists and cannot be read is "no verdict" (printed, not a pass and not a
  refusal), never "zero rows".
- One reader of the draft folder and one pairing of a draft with its triage row (`bug_records.py`: `draft_dir`,
  `draft_paths`, `legacy_md_drafts`, `triage_verdicts`, `draft_triage_key`, `draft_verdicts`, `pair_drafts`): the claim, the
  gate B packet (`gate_brief.py`), its rehearsal (`gate_preflight.py`, which no longer holds its own copy of the pairing),
  the delivery summary, the judge (`judge_results.py --bugs`), the dashboard and `story_bugs` (so the traceability table)
  read the same set: `*.json` files of `work/bug-drafts/`, then of the old `bug-drafts/`, in the order gate B numbers
  them, the suffix case folded on every OS. A census of the package by `ast` (`test_bug_records.py`) fails a reader that
  walks the folder with its own glob. The delivery summary and the judge now also see a draft kept in the old
  `bug-drafts/` home (none exists on a saved story).
- The S7 analyst-to-scribe form tells the role the path the code reads: `work/bug-drafts/<file>.json`
  (`handoffs/s7-analyst-to-scribe.yaml`).

- `story_run.py` (`no_move_defect`, the empty-`ask_person` defect): the driver's own `defect_found` row now carries `--ref` (the
  dispatch the failure belongs to, else the boundary); `log_append.py` requires it, so the seam's failures were never written
  to the journal. A rejected journal write is now said once on stderr and the run goes on (FR-23, FR-41).

- Onboarding asks for the project's main risk areas again (`skills/qa-onboarding/phases/p2-interview.md`, topic 4): the
  question comes first, with three answers (name the areas / no area stands out / later) and a how-to-answer line, and the
  impact-class question follows unchanged as topic `4-map`. A commit that dropped the question had left `sizing.py` reading a
  `**P1 areas.**` paragraph that no onboarding wrote, so a new project was sized without the team's areas.
- Phase 4 writes the answer where it has readers (`phases/p4-generate.md`): `**P1 areas.**`, `**P2 areas.**` and `**P3 areas.**`
  paragraphs in the 'Risk and impact scale' section of `test-strategy.md` in the exact form `scripts/sizing.py` reads (the P2 label
  is always written because the reader stops only there or at the end of the file), a lens per area in `aspect-profile.md`, and a
  Source line. 'No area stands out' and 'everything is critical' write one sentence and no labels; 'later' writes the single marker
  `[DEFERRED: risk areas not named]` in both files and one backlog row whose `asked` column is the risk question. A paragraph a team
  kept by hand is kept byte for byte on re-onboarding, even when the answer is 'later'.
- `scripts/tests/test_sizing.py` (`oh1_10_*`) extracts the generated form from `p4-generate.md` and reads it back through
  `sizing.parse_p1_areas`, `find_area_match` and `compute`; `test_onboarding_notes.py` pins the new interview and generator
  sentences. The strategist's input table, `references/automation-candidacy.md` input 3, the phase 3 summary, the backlog template's
  example, SKILL.md's phase row and evals 1 and 12 (edited) now say 'risk areas' instead of 'risk scale'; evals 13 and 14 are new.

- The audit's A13 check (`scripts/audit_factory.py`, `a13_deferred_decisions`) pairs a `[DEFERRED: ...]` marker with the essence
  cell of an OPEN row of the backlog's Deferred decisions table, read through `project_decisions.parse_rows`, instead of searching the
  whole backlog text. The template's own prose, a closed row or a re-wrapped sentence no longer pair a marker, so a hole whose row is
  missing is reported. Whitespace and case are normalised on both sides; the match stays the first 40 characters of the essence.
- A13 now names what it cannot pair: a marker with no essence, a table with no `status` column (it is not read as 'open'), a legacy
  heading other than `## Deferred decisions (onboarding/gates)`, and a backlog that exists but cannot be read.
- `scripts/tests/test_onboarding_markers.py` (new) pairs every concrete `[DEFERRED: ...]` marker the onboarding phases write with the
  `project_decisions.py add --essence` command that creates its row, through A13 itself; a marker no phase pairs fails the test unless
  the test's short exception table names it (two rows today: the impact-scale marker and the application-repo-paths marker).

- `scripts/sizing.py` (`strategy_area_state`) tells the states of the strategy file apart instead of printing one "no readable 'P1 areas.'
  paragraph" line for all of them: no `test-strategy.md`, a file that cannot be read, the deferral marker `[DEFERRED: risk areas not
  named]` (the line says the row is in `qa-factory/factory-backlog.md`), the team's answer "No area stands out:", a `**P1 areas.**` label
  with no phrase, and a strategy that never asked topic 4. A team that said "no area stands out" or "later" was told the paragraph was
  unreadable, a claim about the file that was not true; the generic line is now kept only for the case it is true of. A file holding both the
  marker and the sentence prints the deferral and a line naming the pair as stale. The lines are reports: no weight depends on a state.
  The two literals the reader keys on are the phase 4 text of `p4-generate.md`, and `test_sizing.py` takes them from there.
- `scripts/sizing.py` (`classify_requirement`, `impact_scale_problem`): a `config.impact_scale` entry that is not a `{priority, severity}`
  map (a string, a number, a list, null) no longer stops sizing with an AttributeError; the requirement keeps the P2 default weight and the
  reasoning names the class and the type. A whole `impact_scale` that is absent, empty, or not a map now prints its own line (it said "is
  empty" for all three).

- Onboarding discovery now looks for a project document that ranks areas (`skills/qa-onboarding/phases/p1-discovery.md`, new row
  "Risk ranking"): a risk register, SLO/SLA documents, incident post-mortems or an ownership map that marks critical services is read
  and recorded in a new discovery section `risk_ranking` with its path:line; a link to a document outside the repository is recorded
  as a gap with the link and never opened; folder size, churn and test counts are never a ranking. With no such document the section
  resolves to `not_read_nothing_found` and its notes name the paths searched. Before, the risk-areas question offered "a project
  document that ranks areas" when discovery "read anything", but no discovery row ever read one.
- `risk_ranking` is a data row of `references/onboarding-notes.json` (`discovery_sections`, after `declared_conventions`), so the
  skeleton of a new run holds it `pending` until discovery resolves it; the notes of a run started before this row show it `pending`
  and stay readable.
- The risk-areas question (`phases/p2-interview.md`, topic 4) names the section it reads and says "Nothing in the repository says
  which parts of the product matter most." only when that section is `not_read_nothing_found`; while it is `pending` the question is
  put with no found-sentence. `evals/evals.json` eval 13 gains the assertion `discovery-risk-ranking-resolved`, and
  `scripts/tests/test_onboarding_notes.py` pins the row, the two texts and the rule that every section id phase 2 names is a data row.

- A deferred-decision row can name a document instead of a config key: `project_decisions.py` reads `doc:<path under qa-factory>[#<anchor>]` as a field ref
  (prefix case-insensitive, backslashes become `/`; the path must be non-empty and relative, with no `..`, drive or leading `/`, otherwise the command is
  refused naming the form). `resolve` asks for a value only for the JSON-pointer refs of a row, reads and rewrites `config.json` only when the row has one
  (a document-only row leaves it byte for byte as it was), and keeps a value given for a document ref in the receipt only; `--field-values` is optional when
  every ref is a document ref. The deferred risk-areas row of onboarding (`phases/p4-generate.md`, step 8) now names
  `doc:strategy/test-strategy.md#risk-and-impact-scale` and its resolve line gives no value, so `/risk_areas` no longer lands in `config.json`, where nothing read it.
- The impact-scale marker `[DEFERRED: impact scale not set]` now has a meaning and a row. It stands only when the targeted question about a preserved legacy
  numeric value was asked and not answered, and step 8 gains the `add` for its row (one `--field-ref /impact_scale/<class>` per preserved numeric class,
  trigger `manual`). An impact-class map left unanswered with no legacy value is no hole: the canonical map stands, the topic `4-map` is recorded as not
  answered, with no marker and no row, and the phase-3 summary says "kept the canonical map" (`phases/p2-interview.md`, `phases/p3-summary-gate.md`).
- The `add` for a kept `environment.integrations` key in `phases/p4-generate.md` (step 1) had no `--essence`, which the command requires; it has one now.
  `scripts/tests/test_project_decisions_doc_refs.py` is new; `test_onboarding_notes.py` pins the new texts, and `test_onboarding_markers.py` loses its
  exception for the impact-scale marker (the static test now pairs it with its `add`).

## 0.9.0 — 2026-10-07 — closed variety is data, a story's price is one, and the Codex run's fixes come home

Fixes taken from a legacy run of TP2-2406 under the Codex host that 0.8.1 does not already answer: the host
probe, native context, guards, sources and readiness, state and locking, the controller's continuation packets; then,
under their own headings, transport and sources, dispatch liveness, non-pytest runners and a person's decisions.

- The probe reads Codex `apply_patch` as write-family guard evidence (`host_probe.py`): the tool is resolved through the
  host adapter's `normalize`, also when it is namespaced (`functions.apply_patch`). Only an exit-0 PreToolUse receipt of
  the guard counts, so a malformed patch the guard refuses certifies nothing. A side effect of resolving through
  `normalize`: a Codex `exec_command` now counts for the bash family.
- The probe finds its echo inside a code-mode `functions.exec` wrapper through the literal-only `nested_command`; the
  exact nonce-bearing echo is still required. The context-probe instruction ends with a delimiter, so an agent that
  trims its last output character no longer breaks verification; a truncated challenge still fails.
- `host_probe.py --root X` refuses when X is not a project: with no `qa-factory/config.json` under X it exits 3, creates
  nothing and says what to pass instead. `--prepare` and the check print the resolved `root` and the probe `store`.
- A consumed probe task name no longer blocks a second probe after a fix: a context probe may carry a unique suffix
  (`qa_factory_context_probe__<suffix>`, `native_context.is_probe_task`). Nothing else is a probe, not a single
  underscore, not an empty suffix. The doctor text and the capability note name the suffixed form.
- A native launch that fails before SubagentStart no longer blocks or overwrites another task of the same host session
  (`native_context.py`): each named launch keeps its own context packet, a starting child gets only its own launch's
  packet, and a delivered packet drops its context. When the host cannot say which of several waiting launches a child
  belongs to, nothing is delivered and one line on stderr says so.
- A SendMessage that names no recipient is no longer refused as a resume of '(no id)' (`stage_guard.py`), under every
  alias (`to`, `recipient`, `agent_id`, the host's `id` / `target`). When it names several, every one must be an agent
  this story recorded, and any unrecorded one is refused by name.
- Direct tracker reads take a credential the process lacks from the project's env file (`source_inventory.py`): a
  credential that is missing or empty in the process is read from `environment.env_file`, then `environment.env_files`,
  the process value first, so the token no longer has to be exported in every shell. Values are never printed. The
  doctor's direct-Jira credential check (`readiness.py`) reads through the same resolver.
- The ssh remote-read note no longer implies missing credentials (`vcs_evidence.py`): it offers the network, key
  authorization, or unlocking an existing passphrase-protected key interactively.
- The red-sandbox restoration comparison treats the factory's generated state as volatile (`red_sandbox.py`): the state
  and records folders `runtime_paths` names, and the project's own `artifact_root` wherever it is put. What is volatile
  is named in the receipt's `volatile` list, neither copied nor compared.
- A brief Windows reader-handle race on a projection replace is retried instead of leaving "projection stale"
  (`event_store.atomic_json`): `WinError` 5 or 32, on Windows only, up to 8 attempts; any other failure is raised at once.
- `EventStore.lock`, `commit` and `recover` take `wait_seconds`, a bounded wait for an in-flight writer. The default is
  unchanged: the call fails at once, and hooks keep it. The controller, `stage_done`, `manifest_put`, `story_step`,
  `manifest_from_tests` and `migrate_coverage` commands and the driver wait up to 10 s
  (`event_store.LIFECYCLE_WAIT_SECONDS`).
- The dashboard is refreshed after the story writer lock is released, at every commit and recover
  (`Controller.refresh_derived`, the store's `after_commit` step), so a render no longer stalls dispatch or recover. A
  failed refresh after a committed event says what happened ("event committed; derived view not refreshed ...
  `--operation recover` refreshes it"), is a `DerivedViewStale` (below), says whether `state/dashboard-deferred.json`
  records it, and a successful refresh removes that file. The cost-capture refresh and the signal notice run after the cost writer lock is
  released (`cost_capture._after_capture`, called by `_capture_with_wait` and by the recapture path); a deferred or busy
  capture renders nothing.
- Every refusal raised after a durable commit is of one family, `EventCommitted` (`event_store.py`), so a caller tells
  it from a conflict where nothing was written by its type, never by the message: `ProjectionStale` (the projection
  under the lock failed) and `DerivedViewStale` (only a view derived from it, the dashboard, did not refresh). Each says
  in `stale_view` what is out of date, and in `recorded_in` which marker file records it, or that nothing on disk does;
  a failed marker write (`state/projection-stale.json`, `state/dashboard-deferred.json`) no longer escapes as a bare
  error in place of the refusal and no text claims a record that was not made. `recover` runs the store's
  after-commit step again, also when there was nothing to re-project.
- A cost file is no longer called stale for an activity file it already read (`cost_capture._stale_kind`). `generated` is
  rounded down to the second, so an activity file written in the capture's own second looked newer, and the refresh that
  now runs with the writer lock free recaptured the file and rewrote a historical import. The capture stores the sha256
  of the activity bytes it read (`activities_hash`, empty when there was no file) and the check compares content: the
  same bytes are current whatever the file time, other bytes are stale whatever it is. A cost file written before the
  field exists, and an unreadable activity file, keep the file-time rule.
- A rework request carries `case_version_links`, the current pinned CaseVersions of its cases (`controller.py`); a case
  with no pin gets nothing invented. A repair's link replaces the older link of the same case (`manifest_put.py`): a
  bare id replaces bare links, an area-qualified link also replaces bare ones and keeps another area's, so delivery
  stops re-requesting the same repair. A story already holding stale links heals at its next `manifest_put`.
- Each dispatch record keeps `request_binding`, written once at dispatch from the request as committed (the pinned
  links, `repair_cause`, `rework_of`, `reason`, `purpose`, `execution_kind`, `manual_case_ids`, `limits`, `plan_rows`).
  Retry and relaunch packets are built from it, so a resumed or relaunched repair keeps its binding, cause, lineage and
  reason. Their `known_paths` are always rebuilt portable and stamped by this package, never copied from the record, and
  `plan_rows` travel by presence (`[]` stays `[]`). A record with no binding falls back to the four fields it always
  copied.
- `relaunch_of` must name a dispatch that never started or was released, and repeat its stage, role, scope and input
  hash. A `parent_retry` that names no dispatch is a refusal, not a `KeyError`.
- The driver dispatches the controller's relaunch packet instead of a fresh `story_step start`, after the stand and
  build checks of the stand stages, and says so when the action carries no packet and a fresh dispatch is started.
- The driver's `committed_event` row (`story_run.py`) answers every refusal that says "event committed;" or "event
  already committed;" with `recover`, whatever the store words after the semicolon, and never repeats the action; when
  `recover` refuses too, the conductor is shown both texts, and a `retry` of a committed event is read as `continue`. A
  stage the controller had closed before the refusal owes its gate-entry steps, which the refused finish skipped: the
  case appendix before gate A, the report rebuild before gate B, each run once (`gate_entry_owed`).
- An accept of a returned dispatch is no longer refused as stale when only its own return receipt landed in between
  (`controller.py`): any other event in between still makes it stale.
- `story_step.py finish` owes a committed accept its tail: when the accept is committed but its view could not be
  refreshed (any `EventCommitted`), it still releases the host binding and, when the accept completes the stage, closes it. The stale view
  is reported as a note built from the exception's type and fields, not from its text, and a `stage_done` refusal after
  it is routed as that same refusal, with a fresh view: the note is the only line that differs. Any other exception
  means nothing was committed and reaches the caller as before.
- `next` relaunches a never-started dispatch of a stage even when an older dispatch of that stage was returned or
  stopped, and a never-started rework of an already accepted stage. It never proposes work on a closed story, and a
  later dispatch hides an older return only if `next` acts on it.
- `binding_receipt_ref` picks the binding of the obligation the instance itself declares (`contract.py`): the proof path
  first, then manifest order, so a stale sibling binding no longer shadows its receipt. An instance that declares
  obligations and has no matching binding gets no receipt; instances with no declared obligations keep the first-wins
  read.

### Transport and sources

- The launcher keeps every argument (`hooks/run-py.cmd`, `scripts/run_py_entry.py`): the raw tail goes to one Python
  entry that runs the script in the same interpreter. The old launcher rebuilt the list argument by argument, so
  `--set key=value` was split at the `=` and everything after an empty argument was lost. One rule resolves the script:
  an absolute path that exists is used as given, anything else resolves under `scripts/`, a bare name is never looked up
  in the current directory, and a missing absolute path exits 2 and says so.
- What cmd.exe cannot carry is written down in the launcher and pinned by `test_launcher_argv.py` (the checks of a route
  that cannot run on the host print SKIPPED): a line break, the percent-wrapped name of a defined variable, and a
  command line beyond 8191 characters. Multi-line text goes by file (below).
- `ticket_adapter.py get --output <snapshot.json>` writes exactly the bytes `--json` prints (UTF-8, LF on every
  platform), atomically and only after a successful read: the skill path's writer of `work/ticket-snapshot.json`, so no
  orchestrator transcribes a document and a failed read leaves no file. A ticket file that is not UTF-8 text is the
  person's (exit 1, owner `person`).
- Ticket `freshness` is one command with one trigger on both paths (`ticket_adapter.py freshness <TICKET> --task-root
  <root>`; the driver runs it by code on a resumed story, after the answer the run carries is recorded and before the
  next step, and before gate B is asked): a check older than 6 hours, measured from `checked_at` in `work/ticket-freshness.json` (else the
  baseline's `fetched_at`), reads the ticket again, and a story the person pasted re-reads the person's file only, never
  the tracker. A change of context (status, comments, parent, subtasks, links, attachments) replaces the baseline; a
  change of requirements keeps it and waits as `work/ticket-snapshot.next.json` until `--adopt` or
  `--decline --words-file <file>`. A waiting change is journaled once. After a replace or `--adopt`, `work/ticket-view.md`
  is rendered again from the new baseline; `work/ticket-references.json` has no renderer that works from a snapshot, so
  one line on stderr names it as stale.
- The driver asks `ticket_changed` when the requirements moved (B-364): `new text` adopts and re-runs the requirements
  and the plan (repair cause `ticket_changed`, which spends no repair cap) and asks gate A again when it was decided;
  `old text` keeps the old one with the person's words for gate B; `stop` holds the story. A lost tracker login stops
  the run, a factory fault is reported, an unreachable tracker (or a check that does not finish in 300 s) is one line
  and `ticket_unchecked` at most once per 6 hours. A check that sees a waiting text other than the declined one, or a
  check time more than 60 s ahead of the clock, is due.
- A declined ticket change is kept, shown at gate B and not asked twice (`ticket_adapter.py`, `gate_brief.py`): the
  decline is recorded as a remark with the person's words, the brief names the changed fields, and the decline holds
  until a requirement field (title, type, description, acceptance criteria) changes again, not for a label or a status
  move.
- A person's words travel by file (`person_words.py`, the one reader): `--words-file <path>` is taken by controller
  `gate-decision` and `release`, every form of `waiver.py`, `archive_task.py`, `project_decisions.py resolve` and
  `ticket_adapter.py` (`review --record`, `accept-gap`, `freshness --decline`), and the text is kept as given. A legacy
  gate B recorded a three-paragraph answer as its first paragraph: cmd.exe cuts a command line at a line break.
- The words reader refuses what it cannot take whole, and says what to pass instead: a file that is missing, unreadable,
  not UTF-8 (a UTF-16 file from a PowerShell `>`) or empty, both options at once, and inline words that arrive through
  `run-py.cmd`. Nothing is recorded. Under plain Python an inline value still works, as the driver's own list-argv
  waiver calls use it.
- The driver hands a person's words over by file (`story_run.py`): it writes `state/words/driver-<word>-<ms>.txt`,
  passes that file to the command and names it to the conductor. An answer of 40000 characters arrives byte for byte; a
  write that fails stops the driver in words, never with the text on the command line instead.
- Every door the factory prints for a person's words is built by one renderer, `person_words.door()`, and one detector
  holds the class: `test_words_doors.py` scans the string constants of the scripts and the text of skills, references,
  design, handoffs and agents for an inline words option after a recording command. A named exemption covers the
  driver's own waiver calls (list argv, no shell); upstream doors not yet converted sit in the detector's pending list,
  printed and not failed.

### Dispatch liveness

- A host receipt records when its worker was launched (`host_dispatch.py`, `story_step.py`): `bound_at` is set once,
  when the receipt is created, and no rebind, terminal mark or release refreshes it. A receipt written before it has
  none and falls back to the file's last write.
- A launch receipt is not proof its agent is still working (`dispatch_liveness.py`): a matching non-terminal receipt of
  this dispatch is `alive` while fresh (`abandoned_after_s`, 600 s by default) and `unknown` after, with `release` as the
  door. Receipt age alone never gives `abandoned` or `never_started`, and the driver's own facts keep their place ahead
  of it.
- Another story's same-named dispatch can no longer close this one or keep it alive: a host binding counts for a
  dispatch only when its `task_id` is this story's ticket. `story_step finish` releases only its own story's receipt.
- The spawn guard no longer blocks on the receipt of a settled dispatch (`worker_lifecycle.binding_is_active`): a
  dispatch the controller records as released, never started or accepted stops blocking a replacement spawn of its role;
  any doubt keeps blocking, and the refusal names the dispatch and the `release` door. `active_binding` is
  story-scoped, since dispatch ids repeat across stories.
- A recorded denial closes only its own dispatch, never a live one (`controller.py`: `_denied`, `liveness_fixes`): a
  denial naming no dispatch belongs to the latest dispatch of its role and stage started before it, and a later receipt
  or an `alive` verdict outranks any denial.

### Non-pytest runners

- One reader for the rows of a test report (`reporters.py`): `run_suite`, `red_sandbox` and `probe_by_code` read through
  it, dispatching on the typed reporter the run's summary names (`pytest`, `junit-xml`, `trx`), never on the XML root
  tag. There were four private parsers and a fifth behind `--detail`, and only one of them knew TRX.
- TRX rows no longer claim what the report does not say (`reporters.py`, `run_suite.py`): an absent outcome is `not_run`
  (it was read as `passed`), Timeout and Aborted are `error`, and only passed rows are capped, so the failures of a large
  .NET suite are no longer cut off the list. Inner results are rows, and `--detail` reads TRX.
- The selector join rule is runner-profile data (`execution_request.py`): `profiles[].selectors.join = {option,
  separator, group?}` becomes `command.selector_join` in the request, so a runner that takes the selectors of several
  tests in one option is described in config. One selected instance is never wrapped; unknown keys are refused, and a
  pytest command may not carry it.
- A red probe takes its clone through `--sandbox-root` (`run_suite.py`, `execution_request.py`, `red_sandbox.py`): the
  run directory is worked out inside the clone from the profile, so its subdirectory is kept. `--cwd` keeps its meaning
  and both together are refused; a red-probe request resolves only to a directory its caller named or one inside the
  clone, never to the author's tree. The test file is looked up in the clone only, so a probe's fingerprint can no
  longer cover the author's bytes and repeat in every clone.
- A red-probe job is never a precedent, for the command, the fingerprint list or the profile choice, and a probe's
  attempt identity includes its run directory: the next probe used to inherit the previous probe's absolute clone
  directory. An observed non-probe attempt key is unchanged.
- Red proofs bind rows by the identity the runner produced (`red_sandbox.py`): one launch per distinct case, each row
  bound by the `report_test_id` of that run's own request, exactly (a pytest run without one falls back to the pinned
  node id's tail). `--node-id` is passed for `.py::` nodes only; a case holding any other node launches whole. A
  mutated target with no row is `probe_defect`, a baseline target with no row is `not_executed`, and a baseline that
  did not pass makes the proof `incomplete`. The request's status is decided in one place (`request_status`, over
  `product_verdict`): `probe_defect` first, then a real survivor in any target, then `not_executed`, then
  `incomplete`, so no target's tooling state masks a survivor. Only `survived` blocks a repeat of the probe.
- A non-pytest JUnit failure site is not read yet, and the probe says so (`red_sandbox.py`, `reporters.py`): the answer
  is `incomplete` with a typed reason, never `survived`. A TRX failure is an assertion only when its first located stack
  frame is in the target's test file. A Jest frame used to come out as a garbage location, and Java JUnit and the .NET
  JUnit logger as none, so the probe ended `survived` with no word of why.
- `reporters.assertion_reason` is the one comparison of a pinned reason with the actual, for the producer and the
  acceptance side alike: whole texts folded (whitespace runs, the `AssertionError:` prefix). The headline fallback
  applies only to a one-line pin; a pin of several lines needs whole equality.
- Two differing mutations of one file are refused (`red_sandbox.py`): the second used to overwrite the first while both
  stayed in the receipt as proved. Identical replacements pass; the door is one probe per mutation, or one combined
  replacement.
- `probe_by_code` refuses a non-Python test with a door (`probe_by_code.py`): the refusal names `red_sandbox.py --probe`
  with its arguments, and the run directory goes to the request builder as `--cwd` on the first call instead of a retry
  matched on a refusal's wording.

### A person's decisions

- One reader of a person's answer to a stand-gap card (`contract.py`): the first word of the decision;
  the latest record of a gap id wins whatever its stage (`Z` and a naive stamp read as UTC, an unparseable `at` counts as
  the oldest, equal stamps the later record), and a revoked record opens nothing and accepts nothing. Every consumer
  reads through it. `waiver.py` prints `stand gap <id> now reads: ...` after every stand-gap record, so a record whose
  first word is none of the four is seen at once to be asked again, and refuses a stand-gap record that names no gap.
- A person can open test files inside the application tree for the automator, on their consent (`waiver.py --stage S5
  --block "protected test path: <folder/ or pattern>" --words-file <file>`; `test_path_grants.py`,
  `guard_app_under_test.py`): the automator halts and names the path, the conductor asks in words, and the record is
  made only when the person agrees, with their words as given and no prescribed first word; on a no nothing is
  recorded and the automator stays halted. It lets Write, Edit and NotebookEdit of that story's automator write test-specific
  patterns only; the markers are data (`references/test-path-markers.json`), and a pattern that is not test-specific,
  would open the whole of a protected folder, or reaches outside one is refused with what to write instead. The
  permission never opens a delete, a move, a write that empties a file, a shell, the critic, the orchestrator or another
  story, and a permission that no longer passes is ignored (the guard fails closed).
- A pattern read from app_root that reaches into a protected folder is refused for what it is (`test_path_grants.py`): a
  wildcard first folder (`**/*.spec.ts`, `*/tests/`) reaches in without naming it, and a single-segment pattern
  (`test_*.py`) names files in app_root outside the protected folder, with the folder to write in front of it.
- A file with more than one name on disk is never written under that permission (`guard_app_under_test.py`): a hard
  link in a test folder is the application file under a test name. An existing target with `st_nlink > 1` is refused
  with the way out (write the test as a new file); a target the guard cannot read at all is refused with that said.

### Pre-release 0.9: the work of the night, one line per node

- The probe keeps a byte copy of the file it mutates under `qa-factory/state/probe-copies/`, locked per path, and
  restores a file a killed probe left mutated; `--release-copy` releases a copy the author's newer edit superseded
  (B-373 a).
- `reporters.assertion_site` reads the stack-frame grammar of a runtime (`frames`, `skip_frames`, `frame_path`) for a
  non-pytest JUnit row and a TRX row; a frame that is not a project file is an unread site, never a location (B-373 b).
- `probe_by_code` probes a test in any language with an entry in `references/detectors.json` `assertion_probes` (C#,
  Java, TypeScript/JavaScript at release; a language is a data row): the mutation, the run and the reading of the
  failure are driven by the entry. A test in a language with no entry is refused as a factory data gap, naming the door
  (`red_sandbox.py --probe`), and a run the tool could not read well enough, or any factory error, gives `incomplete`,
  never a verdict on the test (B-373 c, D-0028).
- Line endings are pinned inside the package: `ai-packages/qa-factory/.gitattributes` makes every text file LF in every
  checkout except the cmd/sh hook launcher, so a Windows clone with `core.autocrlf=true` gets the same bytes as any
  other. The reinstall-equals-fresh comparison builds its fresh tree with the fixture's own line endings, and when two
  trees differ the test now names the first differing line and each side's line endings
  (`onboard_apply.difference_lines`) (B-409).
- Console encoding is now set in one place: `scripts/console_io.py` puts stdout and stderr (and stdin for hooks) on
  UTF-8 with replacement, called first by `install_smoke.py`, the launcher entry `run_py_entry.py` and every CLI that
  used to carry its own loop. A cp1251, cp866 or ascii console no longer prints `?` or dies with UnicodeEncodeError for
  the factory's own text. `install_smoke.py` children now run with `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` (B-413).
- The quiet-runs guard reads test-launch forms from `references/launch-causes.json` `run_forms` (`dotnet test`, `jest`,
  `vitest`, `mocha`, `playwright test`, `npm/yarn/pnpm/bun test`, `go test`, `cargo test`, `mvn test|verify`,
  `gradle test|check`, `rspec`, `phpunit`, and `pytest`), including behind launchers and inside shell payloads in both
  bash and PowerShell quoting; the refusal names the form and the `run_suite.py` door; a runner's name inside quoted
  text or a comment no longer trips it; `run_suite.py` and diagnostics are exempt per command segment; the qa-story
  skill says "never a runner directly" (B-404).
- Outbound HTTP goes through one helper (`scripts/http_client.py`) with the User-Agent `qa-factory/<version>`; an answer
  the tracker is not shown to have written (a firewall or protection page, an unreadable body) stops S0 once as the
  `ticket_read` question naming the check, with the token left unjudged, instead of "renew the token". The marker lists
  in `references/http-answers.json` are finalized after the VPN measurement (B-408).
- Where a project keeps its tests is the project's own word (D-0030): the new config key `test_locations` (folders or
  file patterns relative to `app_root`) is accepted as project configuration, so any role may write test files there
  while everything else under `protected_app_paths` stays closed; only the person's explicit entries open anything,
  never `run.levels`, `roots.test` or `tests_root` (they only recognise). `references/test-path-markers.json` is a
  suggestion and a fallback, not a gate: a `protected test path:` waiver for an unusual name is recorded with an
  advisory note. New `scripts/test_locations.py` (`--suggest`, `--check --candidate`) proposes and counts locations at
  onboarding and at the S5 door; the orchestrator records the person's words and the list through
  `project_decisions.py` (B-415).
- qa-onboarding keeps its own notes as the phases go: `onboarding_notes.py` writes `qa-factory/state/onboarding/`
  (progress, discovery, interview, the person's words), ignored by git from its first file. After a compaction or in a
  new session phase 0 offers to resume it, and a topic the person already answered is not asked again. The compaction
  hooks know an unfinished onboarding: precompact prints one line for the person naming where the notes are, even
  before the first config; postcompact adds a line 5 naming the status command and the phase text to re-read.
  `install-paths.json`: `qa-factory/state/onboarding/**` (new `before_install` flag: never a trace of an install) and
  `qa-factory/state/words/**` (carried) (B-411).
- One carrier for the session a command runs in (`scripts/session_identity.py`, `references/session-identity.json`):
  `activity_capture.py`, `host_probe.py --prepare` and `onboard_apply.py` now find their own session the same way, from
  the PreToolUse hook's receipt of the very call and the host's own variable (`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`,
  `CODEX_THREAD_ID`), which must agree. A disagreement, two sessions in one folder, an unsafe id or unreadable rules end
  in a refusal that says where it looked and what to do, never a guess. No role passes a session id any more, the three
  skills no longer name the variables, and the doctor's smoke report is
  `qa-factory/state/doctor-install-smoke-latest.json`. The hook writes its receipt (one file per session and script,
  with the directories the call can run in) for every call that names `activity_capture.py`, `host_probe.py` or
  `onboard_apply.py`, before `qa-factory/config.json` exists too. **New footprint outside the project:** before
  onboarding, those receipts (`~/.qa-factory/spool/qa-factory-receipts/`, pruned after 2 days) and the activity file of
  a project not yet onboarded (`~/.qa-factory/spool/qa-factory-activities/`, not pruned) live under the user's home, no
  longer under the temp folder. After onboarding the activity file moves into `qa-factory/state/activities/` as before,
  and one left in the old temp spool is carried over once (B-410).
- A stand-gap answer given at gate A (every gap of a case accepted) is carried under the case key, so the gate B card
  shows it and does not ask again; the delivery check reads the same record. Gate B asks again only when the card says
  what changed since the answer: a red run, a new build on the stand, runs that could not be read, or a later gate A
  word. Changing a gate A word takes the carried acceptance back. The gate B role text (`s8.md`) says so (B-361, the
  `s8.md` half of B-403).
- Money: the commands that count as a call to an external agent are data (`references/external-agent-calls.json`; a
  project adds rows under `cost.external_agent_forms`); the cost file's `external_reconciliation` names
  `recognized_forms` and, when a row is refused or the data is unreadable, `forms_problem` with `complete: false`, and
  the price then reads `incomplete` and says that calls of an external agent may be missing, never `agrees`; the price
  names the forms it counted calls for (`external calls counted for: ...`) on the story and spend cards.
  `judge.py status`/`ask` report `problems` for an unknown provider or mode, an unreadable config and a non-object
  `judge` block (B-407 D).
- Runner exit facts are data: `launch-causes.json` `collect_forms` rows may state `not_executed_exits` and `node_ids`;
  `run_suite` writes `exit_means_not_executed` into each summary and stand-health reads it (no fact keeps the old 2-5
  rule); a launch whose runner has no node-id checker, or when `verify_node_ids` is off or `node_ids` is missing, says
  "node ids were not verified" in `node_id_notes` (B-407 B-run).
- The ticket-key form and the delivery commands are data (`references/adapter-forms.json`, one reader
  `scripts/adapter_forms.py`): GitHub/GitLab issues (bare numeric ids, `Ticket: 123`), an unknown tracker
  (`adapters.ticket.key_pattern`) and another VCS host (`adapters.vcs.delivery_commands`, e.g. `bb pr create`) are read
  and gated. The delivery gate reads commands by their words (`glab  mr create`, `glab --repo x/y mr create`, `git push
  -o merge_request.create`, `bash -c "gh pr create"`; not `echo "glab mr create"`) and runs the commit and stash rules
  on a delivery-shaped command too; readiness gains `adapter_forms` (B-405/B-406).
- A project in a subfolder of a git repository (a monorepo) now works: an `implementation_repos[].local_path` may name a
  folder inside a repository. It is used when that repository's origin is the one `remote_identity` names, and for the
  merge-request route also the merge request's own project. When an entry cannot be used (no git, no repository, git
  cannot answer, the wrong repository), a line says why and what to change; the old "no local checkout is configured"
  is now only for the no-entry case. The onboarding preflight no longer assumes `qa-factory/` sits at the git top; the
  onboarding and doctor texts name the project folder (B-412).
- The stand-gap card says whether a gap is one case or a whole level, why it is not decided here, and whether it is
  temporary or a property of the environment. A property the person accepts always is recorded once
  (`environment_record.py`, `qa-factory/records/environment-properties.json`, keyed by the test command and the kind of
  failure for a level, by the stand and the check for a case) and is not asked again in a later story; `ask again`
  takes it back; a fault of a file or of the machine is never offered as a property. Gate B shows what the record covers and the delivery check reads it (B-414, D-0029,
  D-0030, D-0032).
- A test report the code cannot read goes code, then conductor, then person (D-0031): the unread report is kept under
  `qa-factory/state/reporter-unread/<profile>/` (at most 5 files of one run, each at most 5 MB), every reader the code has is tried, and
  `report_adapt.py` lets the conductor record a local adaptation of the profile's reporter kind (`kind`, refused when a
  kind is already recorded; `understood` for what it read, in words; `show`, `forget`); the person is asked only when
  the conductor failed too. Gate B lists what the factory adapted by itself, at most five lines, once a later proof
  confirmed it (B-416).
- Test files are recognised in one place (`scripts/test_files.py`): the project's own test locations and
  `references/test-path-markers.json`, with CamelCase test names (`FooTests.cs`, `FooSpec.scala`), `test-harness`, and
  the usual names as data. The stage guard's commit shape reads real `git commit` / `git add` segments in the tool's
  own shell dialect (Windows paths survive; text inside another command's quoted argument is no commit), and a
  project's `test_locations` counts. The S2 handoff keeps files that merely contain `test_` in their name
  (`contest_service.py`) as requirement rows; a CamelCase test name (`FooTests.cs`) or a `Tests/` folder ALONE keeps the
  row, a name and a folder that agree (`Tests/FooTests.cs`) drop it, and `docs/` is excluded in any case. It matches the
  project's word against the implementation checkout named by the story's manifest. `judge_run` stops grepping for the
  names of tests by a `startswith` pair; the usual names decide (B-407 A).
- The repository map walks every code file the markers name and recognises tests through the same leaf; a test or a
  helper in a language other than Python is listed with a note instead of being read as Python, an empty map says why
  it is empty (the roots and whether they exist, the files read and skipped, the markers problem), and the example's
  fence word comes from `references/test-path-markers.json` `fence_languages` (B-407 A-map).
- Validators and judges stop carrying private phrase lists and private rules for "is this a test file": the shapes of
  assertion lines, locators, sleeps and negative code are data in `references/detectors.json` (`assert_lines`,
  `locator`, `locator_words`, `negative_code`, `sleep`), and test code is recognised by the one leaf in every language.
  The report validator NOTES a report that names a stage `pending` or `halted` in `pipeline.json` instead of refusing it
  (the author judges what a sentence means). `s5_precheck` and `judge_code` say which test files they did not check, and
  when the markers cannot be read the extension floor decides, never "no check" (B-407 C).
- `run_suite` infers the report format of an untyped run from the cure table (`report-cures.json`: `command_formats`,
  then the row's `reporter_kind`) instead of a private substring list; a pytest command is pytest whatever the table
  says; and an inferred format that read nothing is said out loud (`parse_gap`, with the row id) (B-407 B-report).

## 0.8.1 — 2026-10-04 — a red run outranks the manifest

- The report's appendix table reads the run result before the manifest status: a test that failed or errored never
  reads `pass` in the table, even when the manifest says green.
- "Is there a red run for this test" is answered by one function (`case_stamp.red_run_for`) for the report table, the
  `Automated` stamp, the coverage count and the delivery check: the exact instance id first, then the dashboard's
  tolerant rule, parameter groups kept whole; a run row the reducer marked partial with a red raw status counts as
  red. On 18 real stories the table and the stamp disagreed on 20 of 428 manifest entries before and on none now.
- A case whose test has a red run is not stamped `Automated` and is not counted automated; the delivery check no
  longer asks for that stamp while the red run holds the case. A red run whose stand gap the person accepted stays an
  item left with the person (`after_checks`); every other red run keeps the verdict `no`.
- `node_ids.is_pytest` recognises a pytest path written with backslashes on a POSIX host.
- The package's tests no longer assume Windows (path separators, directory order, case folding, the pytest cache
  layout, a wall-clock ratio): the full selftest (318 files) and the install smoke pass on a clean Linux runner.
- No behaviour change: 182 dead names removed (unused imports and variables, f-strings without placeholders); six
  repeated pieces of logic folded into one function each (the project-root walk, the external-write transport, the
  `--task` / `--task-root` resolution, the JSONL reader, the markdown-table parser, two report renderers).

## 0.8.0 — 2026-10-04 — the loop is code, the model is the exception

On top of `experiment/qa-factory-judge` (0.7.11 + the judge + two fixes). Two full runs of
TP1-13797 on Sonnet 5 cost $109 (judge off) and about the same with the judge on: the roles
S2–S4 got 25% cheaper, the automator 43%, but the orchestrator ($37.67, 509 turns, 261k average
context, 75% of it cache reads of its own history) and the code critic ate the gain. This branch
takes the model out of the loop between the boundaries and gives every role what it used to
search for. The judge stays optional: `judge.provider: none` runs all of this by code, a fresh
conductor model and the person.

- A person's word for the build reaches the role's run (t-300 N2, t-384/t-395): every provenance reader — `run_suite
  --mine` before and after the run, the request validator, the execution fingerprint, the red probe, the manual
  capture, the evidence and coverage readers — takes a record through ONE predicate
  (`profile_contract.acceptable_provenance`): `person_confirmed` is accepted where `matched` is, never shown as
  `matched`, never `equivalence_verified`, never a baseline, and bound to its story; `unknown` and `mismatched` are
  taken by no reader, and the refusal says what the probe said and the door (texts in the `refusals` block of
  `references/build-identity-methods.json`). A word given for another build (`test deployed`) names that build as the
  source of the run; a content mismatch never offers `test deployed`; the person's run has its own runtime
  fingerprint. S5 accepts `{report_path}` inside one argv token (`trx;LogFileName={report_path}`), as the gate probe
  does.
- Gate A reuses the onboarding's proof of a test command (B-220 part 2): the proof is of the command, not of a
  stand or a build, so it is kept per profile and command and rehearsed again only when the command changed or
  stopped working — and the gate says which. The reporter card takes `myself`, `run` and `accept`; a word the card
  does not offer is left unread and the person is told the words that apply, and the conductor is handed the same
  per-card list. Giving your own command at the gate, and `change` on a reporter card, are not offered yet: the
  command is given and cured at onboarding.
- The third delivery verdict `after_checks` (t-305 N8): ready once you finish the checks left with you — decided
  from typed records through `references/delivery-verdict-kinds.json` (a kind the file does not hold is `no`), one
  list (`left_items`) and one predicate. It covers a handed test, a manual-human case, a manual check code can prove
  did not answer, a deferral the person worded, an accepted stand gap, a test the code critic could not verify, an
  unconfirmed expectation; a failure always outranks a hand-off (a hand-off restates only a row nobody ran), and a
  stand failure is lifted only by the person's recorded answer at gate B. The report's Left with you closes with two
  code blocks (what gate B's answers added; the plan's regression list); "Not proven" is split in two: "Skipped by
  the plan (approved at gate A)" and "Not proven, and what it costs". `delivery_ready` stays a bool: exactly `yes`.
  The driver recomputes the verdict after gate B, before the bug reporter and the MR, and stops in words when the
  check gives nothing it can read; the guard opens on `yes` and `after_checks`; the dashboard and the measurers read
  the word. The person's words for a build are quoted verbatim in the report (one line, cut at 120 with `…`).
- The test command is proved at onboarding (B-220 part 1, t-385/t-391): right after the profiles are written,
  `onboard_apply --apply` runs `onboarding_probe.py` over every selected profile; a command whose run leaves no
  machine-readable report and has a known one-option cure (`references/report-cures.json`) is offered in words — "I
  propose to run it as: `<command>`. Do it?" — one proposal per profile, sealed when it is asked, proved by a real run
  AND by S5's own command contract before it is shown, and applied only on the person's recorded yes through
  `config_contract.py --apply` (one approval changes one key; a headless approval of a cure is refused; a stale yes
  is refused with its door). An unknown cure is explained with the three answers. The exemption for text a person
  reads is narrowed to the backquoted command on an action line.
- The person reads no script (the pre-release technical batch, PART A t-357/t-364, PART B t-363): the gate A stand-gap
  card goes through the gate B renderer (the words `change` / `myself` / `run` / `accept` from `stand_gap_words`, the
  line `<case id>: <word>`), every gate_preflight door says "write `<id>: accept` with your reason" and the block and
  stage travel to code in the finding's `waives` field; the stage-guard, rework, re-pin, readiness, rollcall,
  toolchain, reporter and delivery texts name no script, flag or exit code; the driver reads a gate A answer the way
  it reads gate B (one waiver per gap id; `<check-id>: accept` only as the canonical word with a reason, bound to the
  packet the person saw and to the doors it showed; a `?` goes to the conductor; the same word at gate B is written
  under its own id; `<case>: accept as blocked` reaches the plan from the one line); `waiver.py --list` is the person's
  list (the stage, the block in words, their words whole, the date; `--json` for code) and the gate packets' "Already
  decided" section is the same list; the S0 config question, the stand question and the S1 review question keep
  config keys and `/qa-factory:` commands in the how-to-answer block (`human_text` rules as data in
  `references/human-text.json`, the roots from `config-keys.json`, card action slots exempt); the driver writes its
  stdout line-buffered and a `launched` row to `driver-runs.jsonl` before a role starts (two rows per call); two
  attached repositories with one name are refused naming both (and the brief prints it); a form's `artifacts.*`
  field outranks a path in the prose; the hook-written locks never stop a reinstall's "Nothing to do"; the conductor's
  action → command map is `references/conductor-actions.json`; the failure analyst's card lists `NOT_EXECUTED`.
- The driver's stand question (t-300 N1b, t-354/t-366): when the ladder of `references/build-identity-methods.json`
  cannot tell whether the stand runs the story's build, the driver asks the person ONE question per profile in words
  (the variants `how` / `mismatched` / `mismatched_sources` / `confirm` and their prefixes live in the data file's
  `question` block) and reads the closed answers itself (`deployed <sha>`, `test deployed <sha>`, `label <word>`,
  `command <...>`, `file <path>`, `retry`, `confirm`, `stop` — the forms and the value shape per form in the `answers`
  block; a form that misses its shape, or any other words, go to the conductor whole); a person's `label` row ranks
  at the label rung, below the sources; a partly recorded answer comes back as its own question naming what is
  written and what is not; S5 asks once per window, S6 once per dispatch scope; `stand_identity.py --command` keeps
  Windows backslashes and quoted parts. Not yet read by the role's own run (t-300 N2: `run_suite` and `probe_by_code`
  still accept only `matched`).
- One resolver for where the story is (t-304 N1, t-353/t-365): a path stored in state is a hint of where things were
  when written, never a fact about where they are now — `runtime_paths.project_for_task` / `contained` / `state_paths`
  / `known_paths_for_dispatch` resolve it against the project the story is in here, and the six state readers
  (contract, the dashboard refresh, the context packet, the driver's `system_file`, the controller's prepare
  fallback, the hook's dispatch record) read through them and say on stderr when a stored root was replaced; a
  recomputed map carries only the keys the stored one has, at every level; a dispatch token that climbs out of its
  root (`..`) is refused with the door, in RUN as in READ; a UNC or other-drive path never pays a network `realpath`;
  `hooklib.project_root` (it may shell to git) is tried only when the nearest folder fails. `test_resolver.py` (192
  checks; the K7 sentinel proves no reader takes a stored path directly) and the census baseline (the F3/F4 packet
  rows now `leaves_at: N2`).
- FR-59 and the gate registry (t-302 T1, t-356/t-360): every gate that judges a run, a test, a stand or a proof is a
  row of `references/gate-registry.json` (23 rows: 4 converted, 13 `debt` naming their backlog id, 6 `exempt` with the
  reason; each row says its unknown branch, its words and whether a person's word may promote it, and `vocabulary`
  says whose words the row lists); audit A26 (`scripts/gate_registry.py --check|--sites|--json`, under `selftest
  --contracts`) scans the package's AST for a comparison of a verdict word outside a registered site — a name-bound
  token set counts wherever the name is read, an `allow` entry is the whole comparison, a consumer inherits the
  `promotable` of the gate its id names. No gate changed behaviour; the debt rows are listed in
  `design/factory-rules-debt.md` under FR-59.
- Gate B and the driver's words to the person (t-342): a stand gap is answered in words on a line `<case id>: <word>` (the
  closed list is `stand_gap_words` in `references/question-vocabulary.json`) and the driver records the waiver itself, with
  no script shown to the person; free words in any language go to the conductor with the key and the option map; the retro
  is always shown in full, and the size line says what the requirements weigh and the cap of the size (the same words in the
  gate brief, the report and its template); a resume reads `resume <dispatch>: <reason>` and the reason is kept as
  `resume_reason` in `driver-runs`; the handoff form is assembled by code only when the role's own message is not a halt
  (any header of the message, not only the first).
- S7 by code (t-347): a manual check that did not answer gets a code row, verdict `NOT_EXECUTED`, `source: code`, in the
  triage (the verdict is in `contract.TRIAGE_VERDICTS`, the vocabulary, the two S7 handoff forms and the delivery owner
  table, where it lands in "Left with you"); S7 closes by code when every failure is a code row; `s7_repairs` reads the
  declared `repair_verdicts`; `failures_to_triage` reads `not_executed` after an S6 code-only receipt; the S6 null close
  calls `finalize` first; `check_witness.py` reads its triage matrix from the contract instead of a copy of its own.
- The census (t-349): the baseline is validated before a run, the snapshot is taken after stdin is read, and the run
  writes `census-notes.md`.
- Stand identity (t-336, N1a): `stand_identity.py record|confirm|forget|unconfirm` and the person-owned registry
  `records/stand-identity.json`; the ladder in `runtime_probe.py` reads sources before a label and a deployed word is
  voided by any sha read that is not the checkout HEAD; `person_confirmed` is a fifth provenance result that is never
  `matched`; a role is refused a write to the registry or to a story's stand confirmations and the person's commands.
- The red sandbox's baseline read goes through the rehearsal reader and writes no evidence (FR-45; t-345, critic t-343 F6).
- The state census (t-341): `test_state_portability.py` runs nine flows in two canary worlds and lists every machine
  fact the code stores; the baseline `fixtures/env-facts-baseline.json` names the node that removes each row and only
  shrinks (a new hit or a stale row fails the ratchet); `selftest.py --contracts` runs the null-outcome walk on its own.
- Controller packets carry no absolute path of another generation: the tokens `{project_root}`, `{plugin_root}` and
  `{python}` are resolved when a packet is used, the package fingerprint is stamped by the package that builds the packet,
  and a mismatch is refused with both ids and the prepare door; another project's legacy packet is refused by name (B-249
  half, t-329/t-335).
- The driver proves a role alive by pid: `in_flight` is written at launch, `process_alive` is None when access is denied,
  and a reused pid is told apart by its creation time (B-268).
- The conductor's door rule: with two or more doors it can take, it takes the first that keeps the story moving and says
  so in `did` (K7).
- The ticket adapter reads Jira wiki pastes (h2. sections by the detected markup, wiki comment lines), prints one error
  object under `--json`, and a missing paste file is the person's question with the path in the answer block (B-256 a/b/d-part).
- S7's null outcome is a keyed declaration: `references/null-outcomes.json` holds a registry of 12 conditions and
  `null_outcomes.py` is the detector that gives every required list, stage output and tool field one home (t-305 N0;
  `selftest.py --contracts`).
- The measurers resolve a copy by name, and `prepare_copy` prints the `Start-Process` form (B-267).
- story_progress.py: one line that says which stage, window and round the story is at, what runs and what it has
  cost so far; the driver prints it as `[progress]` at every transition and the dashboard's story card draws it.
- S7's null outcome refuses while any failure of the run report has no triage row, and one binding rule
  (`contract.bind_triage`) decides which row answers which failure for S7, gate B, the ledger, traceability and the
  dashboard; a manual check no one judged is owned by the review (`triage:manual:`).
- A capture that exits 3 with `do_not_retry` halts the manual block; the runner never signs in through steps.
- Reinstall never retires what a hook wrote; `portable_checkout` folds 8.3 spellings.
- **A reinstall ends with the same tree as a fresh install**: a project's `qa-factory/` keeps what
  is carried in `records/` (journal, ledger, coverage map, decisions, approvals) and everything
  machine-local in `state/`, ignored whole and regenerated on every install; `runtime_paths.py` is
  the one source of both, and an old-layout project is read in both worlds until re-onboarded.
  `install-paths.json` classes each path; a file it cannot class is moved, never deleted, to
  `state/retired/<date>/`. Git tracking is read-only: the listing prints the `git rm --cached` lines
  and the person runs them. A line at SessionStart says when the plugin cache, the marketplace and
  the project's manifest differ in version (B-233); it fires from this version on.
- **A ticket is read by REST in a light form; the Jira agent is never a read route** (D-06): the
  raw responses are kept whole in `work/ticket-raw/`, the role reads `work/ticket-view.md` and
  `work/ticket-references.json` (every key and link with its origin, written at S0, extended at S1).
  An unknown key prefix costs one probe per prefix, never a GET per key. A lost login is told from a
  not-found and stops the run with exit 5; exit 4 is a factory fault, exit 3 the tracker's. A
  pasted ticket goes through the same parser. New optional keys: `direct_api.custom_fields`,
  `direct_api.acceptance_headings`, `adapters.ticket.attachments`.
- **An expected value never comes from the code under test** (P20, FR-58): every Then names its
  oracle in `then_oracles`; one with no requirement behind it is `unresolved:
  expectation_unconfirmed` and shows the observed value, never a literal. Traceability reads it as
  `wait`, and the report lists it under "Left with you" as a gap, neither green nor red. Cases
  dated before `contract.ORACLE_CUTOFF` (2026-10-02) stay `legacy` and are not refused.
- **The manual-agent path shows the person before and after**: the gate A word makes manual
  obligations executable by code (`references/manual-policy-by-level.json`); S6 sends manual cases
  in blocks of at most 5 and resumes after a stop; the report has a block "Checked by hand" saying n
  of m. The runtime probe is bound to the profile checkout's revision; on a built bundle with no
  sources it records the image digest, a weaker identity that is never `matched`.
- **A probe that compares nothing is not a mismatch**: `not_applicable` with reason
  `no_changed_file` is accepted on any stand kind, and the derived-probe finding at gate A is
  `factory_fixable` (the driver registers it), no longer INFO.
- **An infrastructure failure of `claude -p` is classified, not handed on as a role's answer**
  (FR-48, B-012): on TP1-13877 five questions to a person were made of "Not logged in", a usage
  limit and a Cloudflare HTML page. `infra_failure.py` with `references/driver-infra.json` names the
  failure; the stop is exit 5 (`InfraStop`), the retries wait 5 s and 15 s, and an interrupted record
  keeps the session that had worked. The child runs in UTF-8 with the host-proxy variables removed.
  `artifact_supersede.py` is the way for a role without Bash to replace its own artifact.
- **A delivery that sends nothing has its own recorded state** (FR-23, FR-53, B-003): `--no-trace`
  sets `pipeline.no_trace`, and the null outcome of delivery is `nothing_outward`, so a comparison
  run closes delivery without asking a person. The delivery mark is written only on continue, and
  the answer `no delivery` is recorded as `declined_by_person`.
- **The stand enters S5 and S6 by code** (B-005): a failed stand probe at S0 had only produced a
  warning and `environment_pending=true`, so the stop moved on to S5 and S6; `stand_check` and the
  relaunch now carry the stand into those stages.
- **S0 keeps its promises** (FR-4, B-008, B-004): the ticket snapshot is `work/ticket-snapshot.json`,
  the file the scout's brief asks for (a story begun with the old `.md` is converted), and a
  person's `go on` at an S0 stop is read and passes that one block only, where it had been promised
  and never read.
- **The shape of a case id is data, read through one helper** (FR-13, P2, B-013): the contract knew
  only `TC-\d+` while the project writes `TP1-<ticket>_TC_<nnn>`, so `then_bindings` were found
  for none of 3 cases on TP1-13877. `case_forms.py` and `config.case_id_form` now hold the form;
  every site reads it through the helper, and roles and onboarding are told the form (`<case id>`,
  in the form the brief names). The config is revalidated by stat at most once per 2 s.
- **A proof has a level, and a level is a live receipt** (B-002, B-010): `verification-levels.json`
  and `proof_level.py`; a live receipt carries `test_code_sha`. `diff_scope.executable_sha` is
  tokenize-based and decides what is cosmetic (comments, docstrings, blanks, the factory marker)
  per D-0017. The levels flow into the ledger, `check_delivery`, `delivery_summary`, traceability
  and the dashboard; the role texts agree with them; `critic_verdict: unverified` is a word the
  digest knows, and an unverified green test is listed under "Left with you", not under Proven.
- **A test is run only as often as the run budget allows** (FR-51, D-0018..D-0020):
  `execution_request` covered/covering, `fresh_evidence`, one repeat per word, FLAKY at most 3 in S7,
  `strip_rerun_flags` in probes and FLAKY only (`references/run-budget.json`); the Gate A reporter
  rehearsal runs once per project, stand and version (`reporter-rehearsals.json`). `function_sha` is a
  per-test identity with the module skeleton, enclosing classes, bases, conftest chain, `__init__` and
  duplicate definitions, and line splitting is immune to form feeds. Probes and the review bind per
  test instance (`same_test`, `already_probed`); `red_sandbox` reuses the author's green as its
  baseline; `probe_defect` names timeouts and non-passed/failed rows. S6 decides freshness in code
  (finalize first, `code_only` with no manual half); the roles' prose says the same.
- **The cause of a repair comes from the critic's typed findings** (FR-47, B-007): `repair_route.py`
  reads it, the rounds spent are the controller's repair ledger, the S4 key does not depend on
  scope, a mechanical round is owed at the test_defect cap, and S5 and S7 have no-progress guards.
- **Every text a person reads passes the human-text rules** (FR-6, B-009): the halt, stuck and
  refused texts the driver builds are in words with the raw output in the details file, an id
  linked to its own case file on the same line counts as explained (`link_explains`), and
  `QUESTION_HEAD_RE` has one source.
- **One package generation serves a whole run** (B-014): `telemetry_hook` writes `package-<sha>.json`
  receipts, `package_check` runs after every session (host receipts too), `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` and
  `QA_FACTORY_RUN_MODE` are exported to the children, and the closed answers are `go on`, `desktop`,
  `stop` and `retry`.
- **Friction with our own code is measured on every run** (FR-55, B-011): `friction.py` and
  `friction-markers.json` put it in the S9 retro, and the experiment's `code_friction.py` imports
  from the package instead of keeping a copy.
- **The build reads every package file's bytes for an eaten escape sequence** (FR-29):
  `selftest.py --lang` fails on 0x07, 0x08, 0x0b or 0x0c anywhere in the package. The rule's own
  `Check` asked for this and nothing enforced it: tonight a `\b` written through a heredoc became a
  literal 0x08 inside a test file, and the check that test was making passed **because** its regex
  then matched nothing — the exact failure FR-29 was written from, one level up. The docstring of
  the new check ate one in the same hour, and the check caught it. Both are gone.
- **What a gate answer does not name is printed as not named** (P3, FR-41): the decision already
  keeps the person's words whole — `record_by_code` hands the entire answer file to
  `gate-decision --words` and says how many characters it recorded — and keeping the words is not
  the same as knowing what they settled. On TP1-15045 `authorization_source` came out 215
  characters long while the six readings the person had signed lived in `stage_overrides[]` and
  `state/driver-answers.jsonl`, and nothing checked that each item of the packet had a record; it
  worked only because the wordings happened to match the cards. `gate_brief.packet_items` lists the
  ids the packet puts to a person (cases, plan rows, requirements, drafts) and
  `gate_brief.attribute` reads the answer against them — by id, never by wording, so "the second
  case is fine" settles nothing. The driver prints both lists after recording and journals them:
  an item nobody named is visible instead of being read as settled.
- **The gate-B packet no longer contradicts itself about bugs** (FR-10, FR-3, P21.11): it said
  "Bugs found — none, so there is nothing to file" while the report three screens down carried
  "its bug proposal is unfiled", because it counted bugs only from the drafts S7 leaves — and the
  other road to a bug, a requirement the product does not deliver, leaves no draft at all.
  `gate_brief.undrafted_discrepancies` reads the manifest's own `contradicts_requirement` and
  `impossible` rows and subtracts the cases a draft already speaks for; both halves of the packet
  read that one function. With no drafts and a discrepancy standing, the packet says so and asks
  nothing — it is the factory's gap, the road is missing (FR-22), and the rows are printed so they
  are not lost. With drafts, the undrafted ones are named beside them instead of going missing
  behind a numbered list. And the bug-draft rehearsal check now reads the roll-call's third
  answer: a draft resting on a case whose review is **not stated** (a roll-call with no `reviewed`
  column) is the same finding as one resting on an unreviewed case, in its own words — before
  this, the gate brief printed "not stated" while the rehearsal treated silence as a review.
  `test_one_source_per_fact.py` also holds the readers: only `critic_rollcall` parses the roll-call
  table and only `check_delivery` maps a reason to an owner.
- **Every required field has a producer, or the gap is declared** (FR-11, FR-17, P21.6): the rule
  came from one instance — `not_verified:missing_sensitivity_proof` on nine instances, holding
  `delivery_ready: no` on a fully green run, because the typed receipt comes from
  `red_sandbox.py --probe` and the code critic is permitted `probe_by_code.py`. The systematic form
  is a walk: **710 required fields** across the eighteen handoff contracts, **33** of which need a
  tool to produce (a receipt, a hash, a provenance record, a count code computes). Each one is now
  answered by a deriver in `handoff_check` or a row in `references/field-producers.json`, and
  `test_field_producers.py` holds that in both directions. Writing the walk found two fields where
  the deriver existed and was wired to two of the three paths asking for it (FR-17 exactly):
  `runtime.provenance` in the automator's handover to the runner, and `rounds[].verify.witness` in
  the repair round — both were typed by hand or left empty, and both are filled by code now. The
  sensitivity receipt stays the one declared gap, with its reason: it is a decision about what this
  factory accepts as proof, not a code fix. The same walk found eight `claims.*` fields no verifier
  reads back, which is FR-18's shape and is now its own entry in the debt.
- **The id the manifest writes is the id pytest collects** (FR-16, FR-17, P21.9):
  `manifest_from_tests.py` reads instance ids out of the source with `ast`, and the source is not
  the last word on a parameter id — a project's own plugins rename it before pytest collects it
  (pytest-playwright prepends the browser). `node_ids.py` was written for exactly that mismatch
  and wired into the runner, the sandbox and the probe, but not into the writer of the ids: on
  TP1-15045 the manifest kept the author's spelling, 15 of 27 run rows never joined it, 16
  obligations read "not proven" against a fully green execution, and it surfaced at S8 — after the
  review window was accepted and the roles were released. `--collect -- <the project's pytest
  command>` resolves every id through a real collection, prints each rewrite, and refuses an id
  pytest does not collect with the nearest real ones and the repair marker. Without the flag the
  output says the ids are unverified and names the flag (FR-41), and the S5 phase file tells the
  automator to pass it. The driver's own refusals now carry the dispatch id as a field instead of
  the driver re-reading the sentence it just wrote.
- **Every state the factory records has a written-down way out** (FR-40, P21.5):
  `design/state-exits.md` walks the story's own state, the manifest's lists, the run's records and
  what a person recorded — one row per state, the command that reverses it, the test that holds the
  door open. `test_state_exits.py` enumerates the states from the source (`projection([])`,
  `manifest_put`'s merge keys, `waiver.py`), so a new field breaks the build until the walk says
  how a story leaves it. The walk found two things. **`stage_overrides[]` had no way out at all**:
  a person's word passes any block, and taking that word back meant editing `pipeline.json` by
  hand. `waiver.py --revoke --stage <S> --block <text> --decision "<why now>"` is that door; it
  appends `revoked_at` / `revoked_by` / `revoked_decision` instead of deleting, so the story still
  shows the block was passed and when it stopped being, and `split_overridden` stops honouring it.
  And **`unknown_external_writes[]` has no writer** — a missing fact, not a missing door, recorded
  so the next walk does not look for one.
- **A case's marker was being read as one instance's identity** (FR-16, found while writing the
  test above): the 0.7.x selector hash is identical for every instance of a case when the only
  legacy field a row carries is the case's own `marker` — and `manifest_put._retract_aliases` read
  that hash as a shared alias, so retracting one partition of a case **dropped its sibling row**,
  evidence and all. The hash is treated as an alias only when the fields it hashes can tell two
  instances apart (`test`, `parameters`, or a `selector` that is not the case's marker). A legacy
  manifest that identifies its instances keeps matching its own run blocks, which is what the hash
  was kept for.
- **The guard reads the artifact registry for who may write what** (FR-39, FR-17, FR-13, P21.10):
  `owner_check` kept its own eight-entry list beside `references/artifact-writers.json`, which
  names sixteen. The nine it did not know — the readiness, the machine test plan, the diff, the
  bug drafts, the retro and the two project ledgers — could be repaired from outside the role that
  owns them, which is the one thing that check exists to stop. The list is derived from the
  registry now; the in-code map stays as the floor under a broken checkout and a test holds it to
  be a subset of it. A project-level ledger carries no ticket in its path, so no one story's
  controller can answer for it: any story of this project with an open dispatch of the owning role
  does. `test_guard_write_owners.py` walks every row of the registry against the live guard (92
  checks), and putting the eight-entry map back turns eleven of them red.
- **Five detectors that read a role's wording now read a field** (FR-12, FR-13, P21.7). All five
  failed open — a dimension quietly skipped, a row quietly counted as reviewed — which is why they
  survived a run that fixed noisier things. What replaced each list of synonyms:
  - a `deferred_by_decision:*` row carries `disputes` (`nothing|derivation|case_expectation`), so
    `s5_precheck` no longer decides from the row's prose whether it is arguing with an approved
    case. A row that does not say is asked once, with the `manifest_put.py` fragment that answers
    it, and the automator's card states the field before the work (FR-38);
  - `grammar.negative_case` answers "is this a negative case" from the case's `defect_class`, a
    `negative` variant in its plan row, or a 4xx/5xx its Then fixes — a value, not a synonym. When
    none of the three says, `judge-cases.json` carries `not_judged` for that case and the critic is
    told which dimension and why, instead of the dimension going missing in silence (FR-41);
  - a roll-call's `reviewed` column is the field: with no such column the rows are `unstated`, an
    approving verdict over them is refused with the column named as the repair, and a note that
    reads like a refusal no longer overrides a cell that says `yes`. `gate_brief` stopped parsing
    that table with a second regex of its own and calls `critic_rollcall` (FR-17, FR-10); its
    line now reads "whether N rows were reviewed is not stated" where it used to say "every row
    reviewed";
  - audit A2/A2b ask `artifact-writers.json` and the role's own `## Outputs` section whether a role
    writes files, instead of running a verb list over its contract. The first thing that found was
    true: the code critic's Outputs named no file while its Procedure has it writing
