    `critic-findings.md`.
- **A refusal a role's own work closes says so in the one sentence a driver routes on**
  (P4b, `role_cli.REPAIR_MARKER`). Run 5 measured the shape: `story_step finish` refused with
  "these are the review's own receipts, not the person's to produce" — the factory naming the
  owner in plain words — and the refusal still went to the conductor and from there to the
  person, because the driver's table knew no such wording. The marker now travels with the
  refusals of `story_step` (a role outside the stage, an unknown dispatch, an untouched or
  incomplete handover form, no declared output), `window_record` (an unknown dispatch, a ticket
  with no artifacts, a receipt collision, and the whole "this window is NOT acceptable yet"
  verdict, whose every line already names the artifact its gap came from), and the node-id
  block of `node_ids` / `run_suite` / `red_sandbox`, where how a project's plugins spell a
  parameter id is our bookkeeping and the real spelling is in `nearest`. `node_ids.py` stays
  standard-library-only and fetches the constant at the moment it prints, so a half-installed
  tree loses the routing hint and not the refusal. Two things it deliberately does NOT do: a
  refusal raised by another script keeps that script's owner (no marker on "stage_done refused
  the binding"), and the person's door stays in the text — the repair is the role's, accepting
  the window without it is the person's, and `waiver.py` is still named as the orchestrator's
  (FR-4, FR-2). `test_repair_marker.py` runs those refusals for real and asserts the driver's
  own router hands each back to the role, that four boundaries that ARE a person's still reach
  them, and that no script anywhere pastes the marker's sentence as a literal.
- **Every blocking reason names its owner from a table, and an unrecognised one is a defect of the
  classifier** (FR-19, FR-20, FR-3): run 5 put 52 of 76 blocking reasons to the person as the
  product's and 43 of those were the factory's own bookkeeping. The owner was never unknown —
  `OWNER_BY_CODE` mapped `DELIVERY_MANIFEST_GAP` to `factory` — it was lost whenever a reason
  travelled as text without its typed code. Measured on all **42 reason literals**
  `check_delivery.py` can emit: **14 answered differently on the two roads** (`factory` with the
  code, `product` with the text alone), and 16 still read `product` on the runtime road, of which
  nine were ours. `references/delivery-reason-owners.json` now owns the families — by the words a
  reason starts with, longest match first, in data rather than by growing a phrase list (FR-13) —
  and both roads agree on all 42: `product` is down to **7**, every one of them a behaviour or a
  scope the person decides about. A reason no family matches is reported beside the reasons as
  `REASON_OWNER_UNCLASSIFIED`, owned by the factory, saying the owner printed is the default and
  naming the file to declare it in; it blocks nothing. The reasons list is also sorted into
  `OWNER_ORDER` now, so the task's own terms come first (FR-20): on run 5 the one true reason —
  an acceptance criterion the product does not deliver — stood behind 43 lines of our bookkeeping.
  The walk is held to the source: the test reads every reason literal out of `check_delivery.py`,
  so a new reason family fails the build until the table declares it, and dropping the
  `delivery manifest:` family puts run 5's defect back and turns the test red.
- **An unknown says `unknown`** (FR-41): `stand_lease --status` called a holder alive whenever it
  could not check the process at all — no recorded birth time means a recycled pid cannot be told
  from the original — and the driver's `wait_existing_job` refusal printed `liveness=None`, which
  reads as "nothing is wrong". The lease now answers `alive` / `gone` / `unknown` while the
  DECISION stays conservative (an unknown holder keeps the stand), and the refusal says "nobody can
  tell whether its agent is running: this host keeps no evidence either way", with the evidence it
  did find. That boundary was five of the first nine questions put to a person in run 5.
- **A failing selftest names the check that failed**, not only the file and its summary line.
  `test_stand_lease` goes red under the parallel runner and green alone; twice today the only way
  to learn which of its 41 checks broke was to reproduce the load. Up to three `FAIL` lines of the
  file now travel with the result.
- **The paths a role reaches for are given, not guessed** (FR-15, `brief_pack.file_lines`,
  `story_run.Driver.KNOWN_ARTIFACTS`): re-measured before fixing, because the plan carried 11
  misses from a partial count — run 5's transcripts hold **129 misses over 644 reads**, 20% of
  every Read a role made. The largest single cause was one file hunted at two levels
  (`test-plan.md` eight times, `work/test-plan.md` five), and the second was an earlier stage's
  artifact read before anything had written it. A declared input that is not there is now named
  in the brief — "not written yet — that is the path it will have, and nothing else is it" —
  instead of being dropped from the list, and `known_paths` carries thirteen artifacts resolved
  through the registry the writers use, with the human plan and the machine plan under separate
  keys. The packet grows by 1.6 KB; a miss costs a turn and the whole-file reads that follow it.
- **A boundary a person has answered never comes back word for word** (FR-7): one
  `resolve_return` packet reached the person three times unchanged in run 5, because nothing
  compared what was being asked with what had already been answered. `take_answer` now records the
  hash of the question's BODY — without the head that carries a timestamp, without the answer block
  that carries a path — and `ask()` reads it back: a boundary already answered returns with what
  was said, when, and a request to say what should happen if that answer is followed and the block
  is still there. The round trip is the test — ask, answer, ask the same thing again — and it
  earned its keep immediately: the first version of the hash used `re.S` in the head pattern, which
  ate the whole document, so every question hashed alike.
  - `references/human-questions.md` gains the example it had been missing: a question from the same
    run that obeys every rule, quoted whole. The file had only failures in it.
- **Every block of the controller has a named route through it**
  (`design/controller-blocks.md`, `test_controller_blocks.py`): the factory's oldest rule — a check
  stops a SILENT pass, never an informed one — was kept per check, so it held at one gate and failed
  at the next. The walk counts **188** refusals, not the 96 anyone had counted: `StateConflict` says
  the story's state is not ready, `ValueError` says the call itself is malformed, and the second
  class holds 92 more. Each now carries one of four routes — the person's recorded word (11), a
  command the message names (108), the caller fixing its own call (57), or "no word passes this,
  because …" (12) — and a test holds the table to the source in both directions.
  - Two blocks named a door that did not open: `S3 structured test plan invalid` and `S1 source
    collection pending/invalid` both advertise `waiver.py --stage … --block`, and the word so
    recorded lifted the role's exit gate while the stage stayed shut — five conductor sessions and
    $1.94 on the S3 one in run 5. Both read `stage_overrides[]` now, like S5.
  - S5's own gate raised `ValueError` — the class for a malformed call — for a block about the
    story's evidence, which is how it ended up with no route for a person's word in the first
    place; and it recorded the pass onto a projection that is thrown away, so
    `window_passed_by_person` was empty in every run that used it. An informed pass now goes to
    its own journal, `state/passed-by-person.jsonl`: which block the words passed, on which
    dispatch, and when. Not the event payload — `event_store.commit` compares a repeated
    idempotency key against the payload it stored, so a validator that adds a field turns the
    next replay of the same request into "reused with different inputs", which a probe confirmed
    before it reached a run.
- **A question is a question, and the factory's own words go beside it** (`human_text.py`,
  `references/human-text.json`, `story_run.ask`): the driver used to paste a refusal under the
  question, so detector lines, form field paths and an exit code reached the person in all twelve
  of run 5's conductor questions — while seven of those twelve obeyed the rules before the paste.
  Sixteen more conductor sessions answered `ask_person` with no question at all and the driver
  filled in "The conductor needs your word."; a person cannot answer that, so the answer came back
  as free prose and reading it cost another conductor session — $9.01 over 21 sessions, the most
  expensive family of the run. Now the refusal goes to `state/driver-question-details.md`, named in
  the answer block; when nobody wrote a question the driver writes its own from what it knows —
  where the story stands, that the reason is ours and untranslated, and the three standing answers
  — and journals the empty answer as our defect. `human_text.py` reads any such text and names the
  rules of `references/human-questions.md` it breaks (the shapes are data, the `how to answer`
  block is exempt), every question is checked before it is shown and recorded in
  `state/driver-questions.jsonl`, and a text that breaks a rule is still shown: our defect is not
  the person's problem, but it stops being invisible.
  - The construction this replaces was going to translate refusals through
    `refusal_registry.REGISTRY`. Measured first: of run 5's 76 refusals, the registry's call
    prefixes match **zero** — it covers three hook scripts, and what reaches a person comes from
    the exit gate, `story_step` and the driver itself.
- **A move for every state the other side can return** (`story_run.dispatch_action`,
  `environment_preparation.py observe`): the controller can answer eleven actions and `story_step`
  adds a twelfth, and the driver branched on six. `observe_environment_job` — the controller's
  FIRST branch, so it outranks everything — now observes the recorded stand preparation instead of
  falling through to "the driver has no move for X": a finished job is counted, a live one is
  waited on (a line printed at every look, never a second preparation started), and an orphaned one
  is settled as `blocked` and put to the person with its two doors, because whether it finished is
  genuinely unknown (FR-41). `handoff_ready` takes the lease by code — a code driver has no context
  window to roll over — and `rollover_pending` refuses with each unsettled job or proposal and the
  command that settles it. `EnvironmentJobs.observe` had no CLI, so its only caller had no door at
  all (FR-5); it has one now, one JSON object on stdout and nothing else (FR-14). The check is the
  one FR-42 asks for: the actions are enumerated from the other side's own source and every one
  must have a branch, so the next action added there fails the build until it does.
  - `KNOWN_REFUSALS` gains one row, and only one: `sequential task already has an active dispatch`
    → ask `where` again. Reading the conductor journal's `did` field refuted the other three
    candidates — the two eighteen-session families end in decisions no code may make, while all
    four sessions of this one answered "No command run, `where` already resolves it" ($0.53).
- **What the code that judges a handoff demands, said to the role before the work**
  (`references/ahead-cards.json`, `brief_pack.ahead_card`): three of the twelve roles were told
  their checker's rules up front, nine were told them afterwards, as a refused handoff. The one
  measured card is the cheapest thing in this branch — with the strategist's, S3 closed on the
  first dispatch in 51 turns and $2.53, against 176 turns and $12.83 over four attempts without it.
  All twelve have one now, each read out of the code that will judge it (`exit_gate`,
  `validate_artifacts`, `check_witness`, `source_preflight`, `critic_rollcall`, `sizing`,
  `check_coverage`, `check_delivery`, `external_writes`, `retro_numbers`) and not out of memory.
  The cards are data, not a Python dict, so the check and the sentence that announces it change
  together (FR-13, FR-38); `scripts/tests/test_ahead_cards.py` holds every closed list in a card
  to the module that owns it, refuses a card that names a door the role may not open, and proves
  the card costs the role no path from its file list.
  - `source_preflight.py` told the scout to record a person's acceptance with
    `ticket_adapter.py accept-gap` — a command `guard_pre_tool.human_word_check` closes to every
    role. The refusal now names what the role hands back, and the command as the orchestrator's
    (FR-2).
- **The rules every change to the factory must satisfy** (`design/factory-rules.md`, `FR-1` …
  `FR-44`): they used to live in commit messages, in the comments of whichever script had learned
  them, and in the heads of whoever wrote each boundary — so they held at one boundary and failed at
  the next. One checklist now, seven sections, each rule one imperative sentence plus the measured
  failure that produced it and what to check in a diff. Every one of the 44 comes from a failure
  this factory had.
  - **`design/` for documents nothing loads**, and `selftest.py --homes` to hold the boundary in both
    directions. `references/` is the definition layer: injected to roles, capped at 12 000 bytes
    per file, and inside the package fingerprint a dispatch is bound to. Eighteen documents were
    paying all three prices and earning none — three of them sat within 100 bytes of the cap, so
    the next paragraph anyone wrote would have broken the build over a limit that protects a role
    from a file no role receives; and editing a design plan changed the fingerprint that binds a
    dispatch. They now live in `design/`, out of the definition layer (FR-44).
- **The handover contracts** (`handoffs/`, `scripts/handoff*.py`, `references/judge.md`): every
  one of a story's **eighteen handovers** - ten between stages, four inside a stage, two gates,
  one that skips S5 and one that leaves the story - has a contract file that is both the form
  the sending role fills and the schema the check enforces (`handoffs/index.yaml` says which
  pair gets which; nothing resolves a contract by file name). `story_step start` writes the
  empty form from it and names it in the prompt; `finish` accepts on a green check and keeps the
  form as evidence, so a receipt cannot be left behind again.
  - **`handoff_check.py --fix` repairs by code what code can derive**: the run witness out of the
    manifest's own `runs[]`, the pinned case version out of `story-case-links.json`, the test
    files, the probes, the stand's provenance record. On TP1-13797 those refusals woke a
    200k-token role over and over - twenty-three resumed sessions at S5 ($14.15) beside nineteen
    conductor sessions ($5.97), 58% of the whole run spent on the factory arguing with itself.
  - A refusal names the field, the problem and **the values that role may write** (`used_by` /
    `restricted_to` narrow 51 states to 13-16), and every **claim** the form makes is verified
    against the artifacts: `every_instance_names_its_current_case_version: true` with ten stale
    links is refused at the handover instead of travelling to gate B as eleven delivery reasons
    owned by "product".
  - What a role cannot fill goes under `blocked` and to the CONDUCTOR (`handoff_help.py`), never
    to the person; its `candidate` field - the word the role would have written - is how a hole
    in the vocabulary is found instead of being invented four times in one run.
  - **The form is required by default** (`handoffs.required`, and the same when the key is
    absent): a stage does not close on a handover nobody wrote. A story already running under
    an older build sets it to `false`, and `finish --ignore-handoff` passes one dispatch. The
    judge stays OFF by default (`judge.provider: none`), as it always was.
  - `handoffs/vocabulary.yaml` is the single closed list (51 row states + 22 other lists);
    `role_digest` reads it, and a test refuses any drift between it and the Python literals.
  - With a judge configured, a word outside a closed list is MAPPED onto it
    (by `form_row_state` and its two siblings, which had no call site) and the conductor's
    own routing is a four-way question
    (`conductor_resolution`), both at about $0.00002 against $0.45-$0.60 for the session they
    replace. The answer lands in the form's `judged[]` with `as_written`, and the receiving role
    may refuse it like any other claim. `judge_calibration.py` reads the journal and says which
    question to keep, re-threshold or retire (`code_smell_justified`: asked 40 times, decided 0).
- **One artifact, one writer** (`references/artifact-writers.json`): every artifact a stage
  declares names the command or role that owns it, and a test refuses a new artifact with no
  owner. The defect behind it was silent - a ticket probe wrote its receipt into
  `source-inventory.json` and erased the sources the scout had collected.
- **The driver** (`scripts/story_run.py`, `design/driver.md`): one story S0–S9 headless with
  no orchestrator model. `story_step.py where` → `start` → the role as `claude -p --agent
  qa-factory:<role>` in the project root → `bind` → the handoff form checked the way the exit
  gate checks it (one `--resume` asking for the form) → `finish`. A gate, a halt, the S1 source
  review and the S9 retro question go to `state/driver-question.md` and exit 3; the person's
  words come back as `--answer FILE`. A refusal meets a known-refusal table first, then the
  **conductor** (`references/conductor.md`): `claude -p` with a fresh context, the refusal,
  `where` and the files it names; one JSON line `{"action": "continue|retry|ask_person|stop"}`;
  at most three calls per boundary, then the person. Journals `state/driver-runs.jsonl` (every
  `claude -p`: role, session, turns, cost) and `state/conductor.jsonl` (every refusal, who
  handled it). Nothing decides here: roles and scripts do.
- **The brief pack** (`scripts/brief_pack.py`, inside `story_step.py start`): every dispatch gets
  `work/briefs/<dispatch>.md` (≤ 6 KB) — what earlier roles produced, the 3–6 files to read with
  sizes, the role's tooling card (exact commands and answer shapes), the person's standing
  instructions and gate decisions that concern it, and for S5/S6 the repo map. The prompt says
  "read the brief first". A role's Read/Grep/Glob inside the plugin is refused with the hint
  that the brief carries the commands (`--help` stays open): on TP1-13797 106 of the
  automator's 711 calls read the plugin's own scripts.
- **The repo map** (`scripts/repo_map.py`): existing tests of the area, conftest fixtures with
  signatures, utils and page objects ranked by the nouns of the cases' Given/When, one example
  test head — so the automator reads ten files, not 137. `execution.s5_window_cases` sets the
  S5 window for non-UI rows (default unchanged).
- **The manifest comes from the tests** (`scripts/manifest_from_tests.py`): the automator marks
  a test `@pytest.mark.qa(case=..., then=[...], partition=..., obligations=[...])` (and
  `@pytest.mark.qa_unresolved(case=..., reason=..., detail=...)`), the script derives instance
  ids, `covers`, partitions, obligation refs with hashes, case-version links, then-bindings and
  the run status, and calls `manifest_put` once. Mirrored on TP1-13797: 23/23 instances and
  60/60 bindings equal to the hand-written manifest — and one loss of the hand path found on the
  way (`covers` dropped on a re-send).
- **Probes by code** (`scripts/probe_by_code.py`): the critic no longer edits a test to prove
  it can fail. The script mutates the first assert (invert, or a distinct expected literal;
  hamcrest too), runs that node as a typed `red_probe`, restores the bytes (sha256-verified)
  and writes `work/probes/<instance>.json` in the window's `probe` shape. The critic reads and
  copies; `no_failure` is a dead assert, `wrong_location` is a decision.
- **What TP1-13797 broke, fixed** (`experiment/qa-factory-driver`, `test_fixes_13797`):
  an S5 window may list no instance for a case the manifest's `unresolved[]` calls
  `impossible` or `handed_to_person`, when the completion names it in `unresolved` with a
  `reason` — every other case keeps the nonempty rule (FB-10, `controller.py`); `ledger.py`,
  `check_delivery.py` and `check_traceability.py` read `test-plan.md` through
  `contract.artifact`, which now also finds a delivered document under `work/` when the story
  root has none — 19 of 19 requirements were "unreachable" beside a plan the strategist had
  written (FB-10); a consolidated test proves every case in its `covers[]`, not only its
  singular `case` (`check_delivery.completeness_reasons`); a fresh story initializes `new` /
  coverage v2 with no phantom `legacy:S1`: the S0 template's `pending` placeholder is an
  inherited job only when it names a `dispatch_id` or `agent_id`, and a closed S0 alone is
  not a legacy pipeline; S6 completes only when its derived scope — the manual-agent half
  included — is covered by accepted S6 dispatches, the missing half is named, and
  `waiver.py --stage S6 --block "derived scope"` passes it on a person's word (TC-007 was
  never dispatched); a result row that joins no manifest instance
  (`INSTANCE_MANIFEST_JOIN_FAILED`) stays a current row and a factory finding but no longer
  votes on `execution_status` — three bare-name rows kept 23 green instances at
  `not_executed` (FB-12, `finalize_task.py`); `ticket_adapter.py probe` refuses to write its
  receipt over a file that holds a `sources` array and puts it in `ticket-probe.json` beside
  it — the scout once named the source inventory as `--output` and the receipt replaced four
  sources and the person's recorded review (F8). The scout's planned stop for the source
  review reaches the person by code: the exit gate's "no person has reviewed the source
  decisions" is a `s1_review` question (the `ticket_adapter.py review` table), never a
  repair resume or a conductor call, and the answer is recorded by code with
  `review --record` + `log_append human_answer` before the scout resumes in its own session
  (driver run 3 paid $0.18 + $0.37 + $0.38 of model time for that one stop). The same for a
  source material nobody can reach: "source material unavailable and not accepted by a person"
  is the `s1_gap` question (what is gone, per source, from the inventory), the words are recorded
  with `accept-gap --source-id` by code, and a conductor-kind question that is really the S1
  exit gate is answered the same way. `story_step.py finish` carries S1's accepted source
  gaps as the completion's `unresolved` + `reason` by code (the controller refuses the close
  without them and the digest has no field for it - a conductor once read the controller to
  build that packet by hand, $0.88). `claude -p` runs with stdin closed (no 3-second wait and
  no "no stdin data" warning as a question text). A stop answered after its stage has closed
  records the words and goes on instead of spending another conductor session.
- **The implementation is a source, not a place to skim** (`exit_gate.grounding_errors`,
  `brief_pack.file_lines`): every production module the diff CREATES must back at least one
  `derived` requirement, or the S2 handoff is refused with the diff named; the brief marks
  `impl-diff.txt` "read EVERY hunk, whole, in slices" instead of "slice it: Grep first". The
  S2 tester of TP1-13797 (driver run 3) never opened the diff: 14 requirements against
  18-19, the new filter module's payload limit, rejected regex operator, rejected root-anchored
  predicate and deep-copy guard all missing, and the plan that followed had 12 rows against 16.
- **The stand's identity is the factory's job** (`scripts/runtime_probe.py`): a runtime probe for a
  docker stand by code - the production files the story's diff touches, sha256 inside the
  container against the local checkout at the MR's head, printed as the runtime_provenance
  record `run_suite.py --mine` needs through `execution.runtime_probes.<profile>`. The automator
  of run 1 wrote that probe by hand inside its dispatch; the automator of run 3 could not and the
  story's first typed run was refused three times (three resumes, a conductor, no run).
- **`unverified` is a word the digest knows** (`role_digest.ITEM_STATES`): the code critic's
  charter orders "rejected, unverified and blocked" recorded separately, never as green, and the
  digest vocabulary had no such state - every honest line about a probe that could not run was
  refused and the role could not hand off at all (TP1-13797 run 3: four resumes, three
  conductor sessions, then the person).

## 0.8.0, the earlier part — experiment branch `experiment/qa-factory-judge` — a judge for the judgments, a command for a boundary

An experiment on top of 0.7.11, compared against the same factory with the judge off. Where
0.7.5–0.7.11 moved a judgment into code, the code judges by form: a regex, a threshold, an
exact spelling. The first live run of the judge (TP1-15045 up to gate A) showed the
pattern — 127 of 1,668 tool calls refused by hooks on one S5, twenty pytest launches, repair
rounds spent on a stand — and one more: 54% of the orchestrator's turns before gate A typed
controller requests by hand. This branch adds two things, both off by default.

- **A System One judge** (`scripts/judge.py`, TypeSafe `jev`): registered typed questions —
  yes/no with a probability, one option of a list, a level of a rubric — over one small state
  each, thresholds applied by code, every answer journalled to `state/judgments.jsonl`.
  `judge.provider: none` (default) sends nothing and changes nothing; `mode: shadow` journals
  and writes comparison files a role ignores; `mode: on` lets a decided answer replace the
  judgment it is registered for. Every question lives in `references/judgments.json` or
  `references/judgments.d/<subject>.json` with what it replaces, who gets an undecided item
  and how it was calibrated; a question that failed calibration stays there `enabled: false`.
  An answer never lifts a safety block, passes a gate or authorises a write; an unreachable
  judge is never a halt.
- **Judged refusals.** A refusal of FORM or DIAGNOSIS asks the judge before it fires
  (`judge.judged_refusal`): a digest whose verdict is worded differently, an `unresolved[]`
  reason outside the vocabulary (mapped at `manifest_put` time, the role's words kept in
  `detail`), a node id a plugin spells otherwise (`node_ids` resolves among the nearest
  collected ids), an S5 smell or Then finding the rule does not apply to (`s5_precheck`
  downgrades it to a hint). Only in `mode: on`; every pass is journalled and both gate briefs
  end with a `## Judge` block naming what the judge let through. Safety refusals are never judged.
- **S1–S4** (calibrated on TP1-15045): source relevance and relation, scope-changing
  comments, the requirement pair matrix (one pair per request; planted conflicts 1.0, real
  pairs <= 0.02), observation channel, test level (7 of 8 equal the strategist's), four case
  rubric dimensions over every pinned case — no case reaches gate A unread (the live critic had
  left 7 of 15). `judge_diff.py` marks diff hunks unrelated to any AC (threshold 0.9).
- **S5** (`judge_code.py`): per test function — the assertion checks what the Then says, sleep
  justified, locator fragile, fixture unneeded, and the code-review rubric dimensions the model
  can read; `--cause` fills `repair_cause` from a critic finding. Calibrated: both real Then
  contradictions of the story found, $0.0017 per window, two runs identical.
- **Runs** (`judge_run.py`, inside `run_suite.py`): every run that did not simply pass gets
  `summary["diagnosis"]` {culprit, confidence, sentence}; in `mode: on` a decided environment
  block turns a `broken_run`/`failed` into `env_blocked` (measured value kept in
  `execution_status_raw`); `stand_health` groups failures whose lines are similar, not only
  identical; `--remedy` proposes {kind, where, change, restart} from the error head and the
  config lines that carry the name — values never printed.
- **S6–S9** (`judge_results.py`): triage verdict as a hint (`APP_BUG` is never decided by the
  judge), case-defect and FLAKY-mechanism hints, bug duplicate (4 of 4 real drafts, p >= 0.98)
  and priority, manual observation against its Then, retro trap owner, ticket-change severity.
- **Onboarding** (`judge_discovery.py`): the test command, env file, login site and key role
  chosen among candidates the code found; `disc_attachment_worth_opening` ships disabled —
  metadata alone does not separate an attachment worth opening from noise.
- **One command per boundary** (`story_step.py start|bind|finish|pause|where`): prepare,
  dispatch through the guard, `stage_done`, evidence hashes, accept and the next action;
  `bind` records the host's agent id where the resume guard reads it; `finish --complete`
  closes S8 before gate B; `pipeline.stop_after` takes `gate_A | gate_B | null`. Every phase
  file carries the exact commands. `judge_reply.py` reads a person's own words at a gate or a
  stand-gap card into a registered option — it pre-fills, it records nothing.
- New optional config keys `judge` and `pipeline`; no re-onboarding. `model-rates.json` carries
  `jev-1.13.0`. Tests: `test_judge`, `test_judge_form`, `test_judge_run`, `test_judge_code`,
  `test_judge_results`, `test_judge_discovery`, `test_story_step` — none reaches the network.
## 0.7.19 — 2026-09-25 — the last rows of the bootcamp plan: a stopped role resumes in one step, the scout reads the tracker itself, the reporter is proven before gate A

The same colleague's run (TP2-2553 on 0.7.9) left three costs 0.7.18 did not touch:
resuming a stopped role took five manual steps and two refused receipts; the scout could
not read the tracker because the Jira tool belonged to the orchestrator's session, so S1
took 2 h 54 min of tickets fetched by hand; and the project's Karma wrote no report the
factory could parse, which the first real run of S5 discovered instead of the gate-A
rehearsal. Two macOS installs added a guard that never fired on a backslash path. This
release closes every open row of that plan.

- **A stopped role resumes in one step.** `next` and `recover` carry the ready retry packet —
  the exact `--operation dispatch --input` request, checkpoint inherited, old dispatch
  superseded; `accept` on a stopped dispatch names the retry id or the two ways out instead of
  "only the active dispatch can finish"; every evidence-reference refusal prints the path, the
  task root and the task-relative spelling (`contract.evidence_ref_issue`). A dispatch may
  carry the host's `agent_id`; it reaches `pipeline.json` and the controller's dispatch
  record, where the resume rule now looks for it, and the refusal without one names `recover`.
- **The scout reads the tracker itself, and S0 proves the route before S1.** A tracker
  reached only through the orchestrator's session — an MCP tool, an agent, a skill — is
  `not_configured` in readiness, not `unknown`: the S1 role holds none of its caller's tools.
  The stage guard refuses a `qa-scout` dispatch until the route is `ok`, with the remedy and
  `waiver.py --stage S1 --block "tracker route"` in the refusal; a project with no
  `readiness.json` is refused nothing. The S1 dispatch text and the scout's charter name
  `ticket_adapter.py`; the config template carries `adapters.ticket.direct_api`.
- **The gate A rehearsal proves the reporter before the approval.** One existing test per
  execution profile, through the profile's own `commands.one_test`, into a throwaway report.
  A profile whose run leaves nothing the factory can read arrives as a stand-gap card
  (`RP-<profile>`, `kind: reporter`) with the flag that cures it and the same four answers as
  every other card. `gate_rehearsal.skip_reporter`, `reporter_timeout_s` (180) and
  `reporter_probe_test` ({}) tune it.
- **The selftest has a fast tier.** `selftest.py --fast` runs the static checks and every
  test file measured under ten seconds, prints each file's seconds and keeps the slow list
  honest; the full run is the release's. `form_selftest.py` no longer runs at import and
  `make_fixture_repo.py` answers a git failure with one line and exit 2; two test files call
  their modules in-process instead of spawning thirty children.
- **The pre-tool guard normalizes a backslash path on every OS.** On a macOS host a
  Windows-spelled evidence log resolved to nothing, read as 0 bytes and passed the heavy-log
  guard; the install smoke said so and a colleague sent the fix.

Compatibility: three new `gate_rehearsal` keys and `adapters.ticket.direct_api` in the
template, all read with defaults; a story in flight on 0.7.9 is refused nothing new unless
its readiness file rates the tracker route below `ok`.

## 0.7.18 — 2026-09-24 — the bookkeeping the factory did to itself on TP2-2553

A colleague ran a story on 0.7.9 and wrote down what it cost: 22 reasons in the delivery
ledger, of which not one was the product's. The plan named an obligation `TS-1-O1` and the
manifest `OB-1`, so no obligation ever joined and twelve green instances read as nine coverage
gaps. The red probe wrote four hash-bound receipts into the obligation bindings while delivery
read the test rows, so four proofs that existed were demanded again as waivers. The first run
block used a case id as an instance id, and the four ghost rows it left could not be
superseded by the corrected rerun — `not_executed` over twelve green results. The delivery
manifest hashed four records the factory rewrites after S8 by design. S5's acceptance record
had no writer, so the orchestrator learned its shape one refusal at a time; S4's critic was
accepted without `stage_complete` and nothing could close the stage but a duplicate dispatch;
and the project had no execution profile, which nothing said before S5 refused every run.
None of it is the person's; all of it is below.

- **An obligation id is the plan's.** TP2-2553 wrote `OB-1..OB-9` against a plan naming
  `TS-1-O1`, and `coverage_projection` joins by exact equality: twelve green instances read as
  nine coverage gaps, found at delivery. `manifest_put.py` now refuses a fragment naming an id
  the plan does not (a person's word passes it: `waiver.py --stage S5 --block "obligation-id"`,
  which passes the S5 check too), `s5_precheck.py` names an unbound obligation of the scope
  while the window is still open, and `migrate_artifacts.py --if-older` renames a historical
  `OB-n` to the plan's n-th id — `retracted_obligations[]` takes the old spelling out of the map.
- **The receipt is read where the probe wrote it, and a ghost yields to the rerun.** One
  fragment now carries the proof into both `tests[].sensitivity_proof.receipt_ref` and the
  obligation binding; delivery reads the binding as a fallback and calls a row proven only
  there the factory's own defect, not the person's missing proof. A result row the reducer
  could not join is superseded by a later terminal attempt of the same case, stays in
  `results[]` with what answered it, and stops deciding `execution_status`. The delivery
  manifest marks the records the factory rewrites after S8 `volatile`, is rebuilt by
  `finalize_task.py` as its last step, and a stale hash on a volatile row is no longer a
  finding (nine false coverage gaps, four waivers demanded for receipts that existed,
  `not_executed` over twelve green results, four "stale hash" reasons).
- **The S5 window record has a writer, and the last role closes its stage.** The acceptance
  record `validate_window` demanded was written by nobody, so TP2-2553 learned its
  shape one refusal at a time, spent two waivers and left the critic's last interval running
  for close to two hours. `window_record.py --task <T> --dispatch <critic-id>
  [--review-receipt]` now builds it from the manifest, the run blocks and the receipts, prints
  every structural error and every semantic gap at once with the artifact each came from, and
  publishes the immutable review receipt through `manifest_put.py`; `controller.py
  --operation accept --window <path>` takes the file, and a window short of the shape is
  refused once, with the whole list. The stage's last role closes its stage: an omitted
  `stage_complete` completes it, a bare `false` there is refused with the flag named,
  `recover` closes a stage its own receipts already closed, and the gate refusal names that
  command instead of "stage not completed" — the road that once ran through a duplicate
  `S4-qa-case-critic-2` over evidence nobody had changed.
- **A project that cannot run a test is told so before gate A.** The story ran with no
  `profiles` in `config.json`: nothing said so, and `run_suite.py --mine` refused every run
  from inside S5 while every request was typed by hand. Gate A now asks one question with
  three answers — onboard now, name the command that runs ONE test, or run them yourself —
  `readiness.py` reports `execution_profile: not_configured` with the onboarding command in
  its step, and the runner's refusal names whose gap it is.
- **The guard matches the call, not the text that quotes it.** A subagent wrote a Jira
  comment through a heredoc; the comment quoted `waiver.py --stage S9` as an example, the
  pre-tool guard matched the literal inside the heredoc body and refused the write — and the
  agent went around the guard with `perl` instead of past it. One helper,
  `guard_pre_tool.command_text_parts`, now separates what a command RUNS from what it
  carries, and every check reads the first half; the refusal says where it matched. A body
  handed to an interpreter, a `-c` string and anything the shell expands are still calls.
- **A selftest that proves the same thing once.** `test_codex_host` started 43 PowerShell
  launches to re-prove one launcher and `test_readiness` 25 children to recompute one
  document; the fixture workspace was copied at import by 91 files and used by 6, and never
  removed. One real launch per contract, in-process calls where only the data is read, lazy
  fixtures with `atexit`, no pytest plugin autoload in the children, `test_hooks_wiring` run
  once, and the files run four at a time with the transcript still in file order. Eleven
  modules no test imported now have one each.
- **Three smaller facts about the factory, named as such.** `planning_contract.py` given a
  directory instead of a plan file answers with one line naming the right call, not a
  `PermissionError` traceback, and `s3.md` no longer asks for a run the S3 write hook already
  made. A stage whose `finished` precedes its `started` is a finding, not a clamped zero:
  `stage_done` stamps `clock_anomaly` on the record it still writes, `validate_artifacts`
  names it beside the write without refusing it, and the retro prints the stage and both
  stamps in place of the duration it cannot have. The orchestrator's share of a story is
  bounded by `retro.orchestrator_share_max` (default 0.35): above it, the retro and the
  Factory tab banner carry the same sentence with the per-stage split from the story's own
  cost receipts — the factory's work, never a cost line the person is asked to repair (F09).
- **A recapture that cannot get the lock leaves the file whole.** The cost maintenance pass
  stripped `capture_key` and `scan_checkpoints` before it asked for the session's writer
  lock, and a capture's own dashboard refresh already holds that lock: the file lost its
  idempotency key for good and every later capture rewrote it in full — the historical
  import test flickered on a second boundary since 0.7.8. The strip now happens inside the
  lock, and the test asserts the key itself over a backdated transcript.

Compatibility: one new config key, `retro.orchestrator_share_max` (default 0.35, read with
the default — no re-onboarding). A manifest written by 0.7.x with `OB-n` bindings is
renamed on resume (`migrate_artifacts.py --if-older`); a delivery manifest without `volatile`
marks is read by path.

## 0.7.17 — 2026-09-24 — the install smoke's minimal PATH is the platform's own

On the 0.7.16 macOS install the smoke's last hook probe went red — "hook launcher uses
configured interpreter with a non-login minimal PATH" — while every real hook was green.
The probe set `PATH` to `%SystemRoot%\System32` on every platform, so on macOS the launcher
ran with a PATH that held nothing.

- **The minimal PATH is `System32` on Windows and `/usr/bin:/bin` on POSIX.** Nothing else
  changes; the probe still proves that the configured interpreter starts without shell
  profiles.

Compatibility: no config key changes.
## 0.7.16 — 2026-09-24 — a question carries its readings, and a red test is a draft until someone reproduces it

Four bugs were filed on TP1-15045. One was real. One was the test's own selector: a
count of `span` elements with `has_text="ADDED"` over the whole popup, where Playwright's
case-insensitive substring match also counted the legend's "Added" chip — one badge plus one
chip, two, every run. One was a contradiction nobody had raised: AC-4 says a removed node is
"shown at its former position", the implementing developer's comment on the parent ticket
says the diff re-lays every node out — the factory tested the letter of the AC with a 1 px
coordinate check. One rested on a 404 body shape borrowed from a precedent ticket the story
never states. Neither of the two red cases had a triage verdict; both sat in the critic's
"unreviewed" list; the person could reproduce neither by hand. And the one gate-A question
that would have caught the contradiction read "where must a removed node appear when the YAML
has no layout meta?" — no quote, no readings, no consequence — and went unanswered for the
length of the story. Put to the owner as "the source says X; reading a, from the AC; reading
b, from that comment; what each one costs", it was answered in a minute: the place in the
structure. The AC stays as written; the factory changes.

- **A gate question carries its readings.** Gate A on TP1-15045 asked its one question
  as one clipped line, and nobody answered it for the length of the story. An open question
  is now a record of `source_says` and at least two `readings` with `from` and `if_chosen`;
  `gate_brief.py` prints it as a card with the quotes and the lettered readings, plus "or
  your own wording"; `gate_preflight.py` returns a question nobody can answer to
  `qa-requirements-tester` before the person is shown the gate; and the register's
  contradiction matrix — now compared against the ticket's and the parent's comments, notes
  and out-of-scope, not only the AC and the code — builds both readings by itself. A plan row
  whose Then rests on an open question is not `automate` on that assertion until the answer
  is recorded. A story written by an older build is neither refused nor asked twice.
- **A red test is a draft until someone reproduces it.** Two of the four bugs of
  TP1-15045 were red tests with no triage verdict, on cases the critic had listed as
  unreviewed, whose "steps" were the assertion line. A bug draft now carries `triage_ref`
  (the `triage.json` row, verdict `APP_BUG`), `manual_steps` a person can follow in the
  product, and `confirmation` — `unconfirmed` until the person says so at gate B or a second
  run on another stand reproduces it; the gate-B rehearsal returns a draft missing any of
  them to S7 before the person is shown a list to answer, and a recorded word passes it.
  The report, the delivery fragment and the board count the two groups apart, and an
  unconfirmed bug counts toward nothing. `s5_precheck` names the selector that caused the
  first one: a count compared to a number over a `has_text`/`get_by_text` match, which is a
  case-insensitive substring over every descendant — the popup legend's "Added" chip was the
  second ADDED badge on every run. The case critic returns a Then that rests on a statement
  the sources contradict with `contradicts_source`, and an expected value borrowed from a
  precedent ticket is `oracle_unknown`, not an assertion.

Compatibility: no config key changes. `open_questions[]` in `requirements-readiness.json`
gains `source_says` and `readings` (a bare question from an older build is printed as before
and named once by the gate-A rehearsal — a recorded word passes it); a bug draft gains
`triage_ref`, `manual_steps` and `confirmation`, a bug record gains `confirmation` (a record
without it reads as confirmed — nobody re-litigates a bug the person already filed).
## 0.7.15 — 2026-09-24 — the dashboard reads its own project, and a retry names its cause

Rendering the TP1-15045 dashboard on a copy of the project took minutes: before it read
`state/cost/*.json` the build recomputed every stale cost file from its transcript, and eight
of the ten files belonged to sessions opened one and two directories above the project — the
factory's own development, transcripts of hundreds of megabytes, one of them still being
written. The same pass ran on every hook refresh in the live project. On the Factory tab the
owner read "retry dispatches: 10 · parents (10)": ten repeats out of 53 dispatches and not one
reason, while every parent's checkpoint held the answer; beside it a "Quality and outcomes"
block repeated the health cards, and `gate_block 13` counted eleven re-blocks of one finding.

- **The cost pass reads only this project's transcripts.** `recapture_stale` recomputes a
  session only when its transcript slug says it was opened in this project (a session of a
  parent or unrelated directory is left as it is and reported `skipped`), and the pass the
  dashboard build triggers skips a transcript larger than `cost.recapture_max_mb` (default
  64) or changed in the last five minutes; an explicit `cost_capture.py --recapture --session
  <id>` still recomputes anything. The hook capture no longer writes a parent-directory
  session into this project's `state/cost/` at all — files already written stay, shown apart.
  The 15045 copy renders in twelve seconds with no environment variable.
- **A retry names its cause, and the Factory tab counts each number once.** The controller
  stamps `retry_reason` from a closed list on every resumed dispatch (`turn_budget`,
  `awaiting_person`, `environment`, `factory_defect`, `checkpoint`, `subagent_silent`,
  `no_digest_at_exit`, `compaction`, `unaccepted_result`, `host_error:<code>`, `person_word`)
  and `retry_words` when a person asked for the repeat; a story written earlier is classified
  from the parent's checkpoint wording by the same rule. F05 is the split by cause — on 15045
  `10 of 53 dispatches (19 %) · turn_budget 4 · awaiting_person 2 · checkpoint 2 · environment 1
  · factory_defect 1` — and a share above 10 % or one cause three times says so in the banner,
  as a finding about the factory or an incident of the host, never as the person's work.
- **The Factory tab's "Quality and outcomes" block is gone.** F02, F03, F05, F06 and F07 each
  live in one "Factory health" card or line; `gate_block` counts the findings it named
  (`13 · unique 6 · 1 still open`), so eleven re-blocks of one finding after a waiver no longer
  read as eleven refusals.

Compatibility: `cost.recapture_max_mb` is a new optional config key; `retry_reason` and
`retry_words` are new optional keys of a dispatch record in `controller.json`, documented in
`references/artifact-contract-json.md`. A story in flight is untouched.
## 0.7.14 — 2026-09-23 — a finished story is closed, and a tail on it is a contradiction

TP2-2534 went S1–S8, gates A and B, twelve automated cases, MR !55 merged, suite
173/173 — and its `pipeline.json` still held a stage `running` with the controller answering
`await_gate A`. `recover` repaired nothing, because by its rules nothing was broken. That
tail made the stage guard's "single running story" fallback see two running stories, and
every Codex desktop dispatch of the live story was refused for two days (0.7.12, I-90).
Nothing in the factory said "this story is finished": it knew stage statuses and gate
decisions, never a closed story, and the doctor printed `last done: S8  active: S3 running`
side by side with no verdict.

- **A closed story stops competing for a dispatch.** The stage guard drops closed stories
  from its "single running story" guess and lists them as `closed (not candidates)`, while a
  dispatch that NAMES one still resolves to it — S9 on a closed story is ordinary. `--stories`
  prints `closed <date>` and, when a running stage or dispatch other than S9 outlived the
  closure, one next action: `controller.py --task-root <T> --operation recover`.
  `archive_task.py --candidates` offers a closed story the day it closes instead of after 14
  days of silence.
- **A story closes in code and reopens only by a person's word.** `stage_done` and the
  controller's projection stamp `closed_at`/`closed_by` when gate B is decided and S8 is
  done; `hooklib.story_closed` is the one reader, a story from 0.7.x closes by the same two
  facts with no migration, and a `running` stage never reopens one — only `release`/`rework`
  with the person's words do, recorded as `reopened_at`/`reopened_by_words`. `next` answers
  `closed` instead of `await_gate`, S9 `done` refuses to leave a running stage behind
  (`<Sn> is still running`; `recover` first, or `waiver.py --stage S9 --block "still
  running"`), and `recover` settles the tail as `stale_after_closure` — the 2534 reproduction
  is a test.

Compatibility: no config key changes; `closed_at`, `closed_by`, `reopened_at` and
`reopened_by_words` are new optional keys of `pipeline.json`, documented in
`references/artifact-contract-json.md`. A story in flight is untouched by any of this.
## 0.7.13 — 2026-09-23 — the person reads the outcome, not the ledger

The owner read the pilot's `test-report.md` and the dashboard and could not tell what to do.
The report opened with "24 reasons on the product side" — twenty of them the factory's own
bookkeeping after a mid-story manifest schema change — and "verified 0" beside 18 green
tests; one decision paragraph was pasted eleven times; a question the owner had answered at
gate A was "open"; a test variant that does not exist was "written and reviewed"; nothing
listed what was proven or what was left with the person; and the report, written before
gate B, kept asking for a word already given. The dashboard showed 54 "checks" mixing
executed instances with never-run plan rows, "level not recorded" on every test, pytest node
ids for names, "triaged 0/3" with three verdicts on disk, and a cost total ten times the
factory's own spend.

- **The test report is written from the decision down.** New order — the change, the verdict
  in words, `delivery_ready`, a one-line legend, *Proven*, *Product bugs*, *Left with you*,
  *Not proven and what it costs*, *Decided at gate B*, *Factory defects — nothing is wanted
  from you*, *Size* (forecast and fact on their own lines, no money), *Where to look* (only
  the four human documents) and a generated appendix. Each "Left with you" item is assembled
  from records — the case's words, whether a test exists, where to run, how, which answer —
  and the validator refuses an item without them, a `work/` path, a `cv_`/`ti_` hash, a
  decision id without its words, "look here first" or the machine-summary markers. After
  the gate, `traceability.py --close-gate-b` appends the person's words and drops what they
  closed. Reports written on the old contract are still accepted.
- **Traceability replaces the ledger for the person.** `traceability.py --write | --render |
  --check` builds `work/traceability.json` — one row per requirement × case × Then group,
  sorted by R then TC, with the test, its level and shape, and a result from a closed human
  list: `pass · bug · wait · blocked · not run · unreachable · deferred · not planned`
  (`contract.TRACE_RESULTS`). Every register R and every plan TC must be present. The machine
  ledger stays under `work/`: dead and STALE rows leave its table, a repeated decision is one
  footnote, and the factory's own bookkeeping — stale case-version links, join failures,
  "partial" born of a reducer — is owned by `factory`, never `product`. The delivery-summary
  fragment lives in `work/delivery-summary.md` and inserts idempotently.
- **The dashboard shows the story as a person reads it.** Triage joins by
  `instance_id`/`attempt_id`; the case title is the visible name with the node id on hover;
  the level comes from the run profile, the case's plan row or the longest `run.levels`
  path glob — "not recorded" only when all three are absent; superseded and STALE rows never
  enter. The traffic light counts executed instances only; a story expands into its own
  ring, pyramid, bugs, level groups, *Blocked by the stand*, one *With the person* group and
  *Not run by design*. A session belongs to the project only when its transcript's project
  directory is this project — sessions of parent directories are shown apart and never
  summed; an incomplete task cost is a named factory finding at the top of the Cost tab, not
  a grey "Unknown". The $-band estimates fill from the known subtotal marked as a floor.
  Removed: Latency telemetry, Run duration and volume, the duplicate Test health,
  Requests/tools/rework, Divergence drivers, the sample-view dumbbell, Orchestrator
  continuation, Execution jobs, Approved scope awaiting execution, the dead metrics-board
  banner and the `n=` footers.
- **Size is recorded as a history.** `pipeline.json` carries `size_initial`, `size_final` and
  `size_reason`; the retro and the estimation ledger print forecast → fact and the
  re-estimation when one happened.

Compatibility: `work/traceability.json` and the new report sections are read with defaults
by every consumer; a story in flight whose report was written on 0.7.12 validates against
the old contract; the dashboard renders without `traceability.json`.

## 0.7.12 — 2026-09-23 — where the plugin lives is a fact, not a fault; the host's name for a dispatch is an identity

Two users, one day, neither at fault. On macOS the plugin was installed from a clone that
sat inside the onboarded project (`deathstroke/QAFactory/...`): the smoke's
isolated self-tests resolved the person's real stories, five FAILs, two reinstalls, a
verdict of "defect in the package" — and the minimal-PATH launcher probe was red on every
POSIX host regardless, because a list with `shell=True` is not a command line there. On
Codex desktop a story was stopped four times at `spawn_agent` with "task identity is
missing or ambiguous" while the controller had accepted the dispatch: the spawn message is
opaque on that host, the only readable identity is `task_name=qa_automator__tp2_2556_s5_11`,
and the guard was looking for `TP2-2556`; a finished, merged story left `running`
made the "single running story" fallback fail too.

- **The plugin root may live inside the project.** The smoke's isolated self-tests run from a
  neutral directory inside the smoke's own sandbox, and a plugin root nested in an onboarded
  project is stated as one INFO line instead of being discovered as assertion mismatches. The
  minimal-PATH launcher probe passes one quoted command string: with `shell=True` a list is
  not a command line on POSIX, and the launcher was getting zero arguments on macOS.
  `INSTALL.md` says where a local clone belongs.
- **The root a selftest takes is pinned, not guessed.** `project_root()` asks
  `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` for the marker before it walks up from the cwd, exactly as its
  docstring always promised, and every `--selftest` that builds a throwaway project pins the
  cache and that variable together (`hooklib.pin_project_root`) and names the root it took in
  its first line. A plugin clone inside an onboarded project no longer hands `external_writes`,
  `guard_pre_tool`, `run_suite` and `waiver` the person's real stories, and a selftest run by
  hand no longer leaves telemetry in their state tree.
- **The stage guard reads the story from a Codex desktop `task_name`.** That host sends
  `task_name`, `fork_turns` and an encrypted `message`, so the slug is the only readable
  carrier (`qa_automator__tp2_2556_s5_11` → `TP2-2556`, matched against the
  stories that exist, never guessed). Archived stories no longer count as candidates;
  `QA_FACTORY_TASK=<TICKET>` is a person's word where the arguments carry no id, and it beats
  the "single running story" guess; an identity refusal prints the root, the task name,
  every story and which are running. An id the person did pass gets its own refusal instead
  of "pass the explicit task_id". A ticketless denial is written to
  `qa-factory/state/dispatch-denials.jsonl`. The doctor's context probe on Codex desktop is
  identified by `task_name: qa_factory_context_probe` alone, and the skill now says so.

Compatibility: no config key changes. `QA_FACTORY_TASK` is unset by default. Stories and
bindings written by 0.7.x read as before; a project onboarded on 0.7.x needs no re-onboarding.

## 0.7.11 — 2026-09-23 — the stand is a fact with a fix, not a paragraph

Two projects, one day. On TP1-15045 the automator found the exact cause of a blocked
partition (`customer-config.yaml:304-311`, `enabled: false`) and the person read
"blocked_by_env"; a workflow-validation test hung on a shared `assistant` fixture with a Jira
tool its case never asked for, and that was called a stand gap too. On a second checkout of the
same harness, onboarding copied four names out of a ~100-key inventory in code into
`secret_keys` — `AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`, `AWS_PROFILE`, `HEADLESS` — and the
first story stopped on keys nobody needed, while the orchestrator blamed the identity
provider's 302 and asked the person to "add the missing 4 keys".

- **A stand gap carries its own fix, and a fixture is not a stand.** A `blocked_by_env` row
  written by the running S5 dispatch now owes a `remedy` — what kind of thing is missing
  (flag | credential | data | service), the file and lines or the variable NAME, what to set,
  what to restart — and neither it nor the row's prose may print a credential value;
  `s5_precheck.py` and `validate_artifacts.py` refuse both, `waiver.py --stage S5 --block
  "remedy"` passes them, and a row written by 0.7.x in a story in flight stays a note. A block
  that comes from the test's own fixture, tool or integration, one the approved case never
  mentions, goes back as `test_defect`: minimal data through the API. The runner's
  `env_blocked[]` rows carry the same remedy and name the `env_probe.py` line that failed.
- **A stand gap is a card with four answers.** A precondition or an `unresolved[]` row that
  carries a `remedy` reaches gate A and gate B as a card — requirement → case, what the test
  does, what is missing, the exact file, lines and value, and four answers: apply, theirs,
  handed, accept (`stand_gaps.py`, embedded by `gate_brief.py`; the answer is recorded with
  `waiver.py --block "stand gap: <id>"`). On a recorded `apply` the app-boundary guard passes
  exactly the one file that remedy names, once per decision, and says which decision passed
  it; P-00 holds everywhere else. `handed` is the `handed_to_person` row of 0.7.9 with the
  remedy kept. A credential is named, never printed.
- **Three facts about a stand, three verdicts.** `env_probe.py` prints `liveness`, `login` and
  `keys` on their own lines: a stand that answers 302 to an identity provider is alive and
  wanting a login, not dead (no redirect is followed any more); the login is actually
  attempted by the scheme onboarding recorded in `environment.access` (`stand_access.py` — the
  harness's own login command, a local login endpoint, a password grant, a bearer token from a
  variable, or none); a missing key is printed with who needs it (`integrations[].required_by`,
  else the cases whose `preconditions` name it, else "nothing in this story"). Layer 1 is only
  a stand that does not answer, a login that was refused, or a key the login itself needs;
  with a proven login no missing key can stop a story. A config whose `secret_keys` name keys
  that are not in the env file — or `HEADLESS` and `AWS_PROFILE`, which nobody there owns — is
  readiness' finding against the onboarding that wrote it, owner factory, never four keys
  asked of a person.
- **Onboarding learns how the project reaches its stand, and writes only the keys it used.**
  Discovery reads the login call sites and the env files (`project_inventory.py --access`)
  and keeps two lists apart: the names the file holds, and the names the code reads that it
  does not. Only the first may become `secret_keys`/`user_key`/`base_url_key`; the second goes
  to `integrations[]` with `required_by`, where a missing key blocks an area and not the
  stand. The scheme itself is recorded as `environment.access` — one of five kinds, key NAMES,
  and the codes an unauthenticated request answers by design — and proved by one real login
  stored as `login_probe`, not by a sentence in `verified`. A config that fails its own probe
  is not written. A project onboarded on 0.7.x re-answers only the two access questions.

Compatibility: `environment.access`, `integrations[].required_by` and `remedy` are optional
for readers of older configs and artifacts; a config without `access` reads `login:
not_recorded — schema not recorded - onboarding gap` and is not blocked by it.

## 0.7.10 — 2026-09-22 — a red test by the requirement is the product, and a window costs two runs

Found on the second live S5 of TP1-15045 (0.7.8, then 0.7.9): 91 minutes and 165 tool
calls for four API cases, pytest launched twenty times where two launches would do, a red
probe that took two critic dispatches, role reports of 786–3,401 characters each and an
orchestrator that compacted mid-stage — and two cases parked on "the designer" because the
test asserted what the code did instead of what the approved case said.

- **After gate A the approved case is the oracle of S5.** A test written to an approved case
  that fails against the implementation is the factory's product: it is handed over red with
  `contradicts_requirement` and becomes a bug draft at S8. The automator and the critic no
  longer have a third route — `s5_precheck.py` refuses an assertion that contradicts the Then
  (null, status code or literal) and a `deferred_by_decision:*` row that argues with the case
  against what the code does; the doubt travels with the red test to S7, where the new
  `CASE_DEFECT` verdict sends the case back to the designer against the requirement register.
  An existing test written to the code is never an oracle. The person hears "N tests red on
  purpose", never "unresolved".
- **A refused run says which run it refused and why.** "No run block carries a result row"
  names the block and the mismatch — id spelling, a reporter row nothing maps, or no block at
  all — and `partial-green` names the instances claiming the green and the legacy `tests[]`
  row (no `instance_id`, one function-level selector) that `migrate_artifacts.py --if-older`
  now retires too. TP1-15045 answered those bare verdicts by running pytest twenty times.
- **One run per window, and evidence that is stale per test, not per file.** `--mine` runs
  every instance of the named cases in one pytest call; a call that picks part of a case while
  a test of the same file in the dispatch's own scope has never run is answered
  `run_the_window_first` with that one command — nothing launched, no key spent;
  `--purpose repair_verify`, `--again` and a person's word pass it. What makes a test's
  evidence stale is its own source, its class without its sibling tests, and the fixtures and
  helpers it names (`instance_content_sha`), so a one-line edit in one test no longer re-runs
  the other six of its file. `--mine --dispatch` accepts an id the open dispatch resumed
  (`parent_retry`) and says so, instead of refusing the role twice.
- **The red probe is one command.** `red_sandbox.py --probe` prepares the sandbox, runs the
  mutated and the baseline instances through `run_suite.py --mine`, verifies, publishes the
  sensitivity receipt and its manifest binding, and cleans up — the critic writes only the
  mutation file, down from roughly thirty manual commands and a second dispatch.
- **A role's last word is a form, not a report.** The final message is a header
  (`<role> <stage> <scope> · ok|concerns|halt`), exactly one line per item the dispatch was
  scoped to (`<id> · <state> · <reason ≤ 80 chars>`) and the artifact's task-relative path —
  nothing else. `role_digest.py` reads it and the exit gate refuses anything else once, with
  the form quoted and `waiver.py --block "digest"` as the way past it; the 0.7.x one-line
  digest still passes, so no story in flight is refused.

Compatibility: every new field and verdict is optional for readers of older artifacts; runs,
manifests and receipts written by 0.7.x replay and validate unchanged.

## 0.7.9 — 2026-09-22 — what the factory cannot do is said before the gate, and never dumped on the person

Found on the second live day: the first S5 of 0.7.8 on TP1-15045 (a story written by 0.7.6
and continued on 0.7.8), the TP2-2536 run (Maestro/iOS, no Xcode for the agent, S6–S9
never ran), a colleague's re-onboarding that showed 338 untracked state files, and the 2428
backlog. The owner's rule for all of it: the factory repairs its environment or asks for
help; only a person's explicit choice hands work over, and then nothing waits for them.

- **What the factory cannot execute goes to the person, by their choice.** Before gate A the
  rehearsal resolves the launcher of every execution profile S5 will need (`poetry run`,
  `npx`, a `scripts/*.sh` and the tools it names), and a missing one is one question with
  three answers — install it here, name an environment I can run it in, or you run these N
  cases yourself. Only the third hands anything over, recorded like every other word that
  passes a block (`waiver.py --stage S5 --block "executor unavailable: <profile>"`). S5 then
  writes and reviews that code and closes its window by code with `unresolved:
  handed_to_person` — no receipt, no waiting; S6 never runs it, S7 never triages it, the
  ledger reads `not_executed:handed_to_person` and never PASS, and gate B says
  `delivery_ready: no` with the files and commands under `## Run these yourself`.
  `run_suite.py` meeting the same missing launcher mid-S5 prints `executor_unavailable` and
  exits 3 rather than launching or handing over silently. Stand problems (a flag, data, an
  account, a degraded stand) stay what 0.7.8 made them: repaired, or a question — never a
  handover.
- **A proven case says so in its own frontmatter.** `case_stamp.py` reads
  `automation-manifest.json` and stamps a case `status: Automated` (`automated_by`,
  `red_probe`) once every covering instance is green, critic-approved and red-probed — never
  a role's prose. Wired into `finalize_task.py`; a case with an open partition, or one a
  person marked `Blocked`/`Archived`, is left alone. On 2536 that frontmatter was a
  documentation gap closed by a person's word.
- **A case number is unique inside its area, not inside the story.** `unresolved[]`, the
  pinned case links and the case index are keyed `<area>/TC-NNN` when two areas collide; a
  record written by 0.7.x carries no area and still matches, so nothing re-pins. Two areas
  holding TC-001..008 used to lose two approved entries on recovery (FB-2428-1).
- **A story resumed on a newer plugin migrates its own spelling once, by code.** `pipeline.json`
  carries `plugin_version` (`story_version.py`); `migrate_artifacts.py --task-root <T>
  --if-older` runs on resume, canonicalizes legacy-spelled manifest rows (`TC-012::test_x`,
  and the older ghost row whose id is the case itself) through `manifest_put`'s own writer,
  journals one line and is a no-op afterwards; `manifest_put` itself now retracts a row that
  stands beside its current spelling. TP1-15045 met seven "structural" findings at the
  S5 exit gate about rows nobody had written twice.
- **Reading the tracker goes through `direct_api` whenever it is usable, whatever `method`
  says.** A config with `method: "agent"` next to a full `direct_api` was refused "record
  direct_api" though it was recorded, and the scout could not reach the parent ticket. New
  method label `api`; `ticket_adapter.py --migrate-method` rewrites an old config, and
  onboarding runs it.
- **The collect survives `addopts = -v`.** A project's own `-v` cancelled our `-q` and pytest
  printed the verbosity-0 tree instead of ids, so every id of the first live 0.7.8 run came
  back `node_id_mismatch`; `node_ids.collect` recognises the tree and retries with one more
  `-q`.
- **Machine-local state stays out of git; telemetry rotates.** `project_gitignore.py --write`
  (run by onboarding, checked by the doctor) covers everything under `qa-factory/state/`
  except `journal.jsonl`, `coverage-map.md` and `estimation-ledger.jsonl` — the dashboard is
  regenerated by every run and is ignored too — plus the S5 work fragments. The telemetry
  hook prunes its own folder once a minute to `telemetry.keep_commands` (200) command pairs
  and `telemetry.keep_days` (7) of hook files: 7375 files and 27 MB after five days.

- **Bugs and comments can be filed through the tracker's own API.**
  `external_writes.channels.<name>.method: "api"` delivers through `adapters.ticket.direct_api`
  after the same gate-B authorization as a command or an assistant — for a project with no
  write command and no assistant, which used to get "the right exists" and a markdown
  proposal that reached no tracker. They are authored as the token's owner, named at gate B
  and in the run's own line, never the credential.
- **The S5 exit gate judges the handoff in front of it.** Its re-run of `s5_precheck` is
  scoped to the one running automator dispatch; unscoped, it spoke about every case in the
  manifest, and the automator of window TC-001/TC-002 was refused its own handoff over a
  TC-014 finding from a window closed a day earlier — and halted.

Compatibility: every new field and reason is optional, every new config key has a default,
and receipts, manifests, links and pipelines written by 0.7.x replay and validate unchanged.

## 0.7.8 — 2026-09-22 — a role that cannot see cannot repair

Found on the whole S5 of TP1-15045 under 0.7.6 (session 57cf578c): 12.5 hours, 16
dispatches, $99.80 — and 4 of 14 cases ready for the gate. Tests ran for about 130 of the 650
role-minutes; 127 of 1668 tool calls were refused by the factory's own hooks. The roles were
not slow: they repaired red tests blind, heard another role's turn count, and spent the
repair cap on the stand and on bookkeeping.

- **A run in which nothing ran names its cause, and small logs read freely.** The run summary
  carries `error_head` (the log's `ERROR` / `E   ` / `usage:` lines) whenever pytest exits 2–5
  or collects nothing; `--detail` works under an open dispatch in both spellings
  (`--task T --label L --detail TEST`, `--request FILE --detail TEST`) and launches no test.
  Raw run logs are refused by weight, not by extension: up to `guards.raw_log_free_bytes`
  (8192) they read freely — 87 of that run's 109 logs — and above it the refusal names both
  routes. The "tooling blocker" two critic dispatches were spent on was the first line of a
  1.2 KB log nobody was allowed to read.
- **Node ids are checked before anything is launched.** A probe asked for
  `[buffer-R3-vs-selected-R1]`, pytest-playwright collects
  `[chromium-buffer-R3-vs-selected-R1]`: exit 4, a burned sandbox, two cases left without
  proof. `node_ids.py` checks asked ids against a real `--collect-only`, resolves an id with
  exactly one real spelling itself and refuses only a truly missing one, with the nearest ids
  (`node_id_mismatch`, nothing launched, no idempotency key spent). `red_sandbox.py` does the
  same at prepare time without burning the destination, and its expected reason tolerates
  pytest's `AssertionError: ` prefix.
- **The turn counter is per dispatch.** It is keyed by the host's `agent_id`; a role hears
  about its own dispatch in the role's words, the orchestrator about its window. One
  session-wide counter had told a role in its first minute "930 tool calls, hand back": 43
  interruptions, and a critic that stopped at 71 calls of its own.
- **A repair round is a round about the test.** Dispatches carry `repair_cause`
  (`test_defect | mechanical | environment | tooling | reviewer_error`); only `test_defect`
  spends the cap of two, counted from receipts by retry chain, and the refusal at the cap
  lists what it counted. A mechanical fix the critic words (a sleep, a raw locator) goes to
  the author once per window and is closed by the author's own green run on the new bytes —
  `mechanical_round` on the window record keeps the review and the probe bound to the bytes
  they were made on, and the author's dispatch completes the window; no second critic,
  nobody's round. The critic reviews statically before any run, so such a fix surfaces in
  round one. A `stand_signal` stamps the next dispatch `environment`. On that
  run rounds went to manifest bookkeeping, a missing env file and the reviewer's own five
  parallel runs, and a five-line sleep fix was refused "because the cap was reached".
- **The stand is one, and the factory knows it.** With `run.parallel: false` a second
  `run_suite.py` launch waits on a project-level lease (`stand_lease.py`; a dead holder is
  taken over, a person frees a live one) instead of failing five UI runs at once.
  `stand_health.py` recognises three different tests failing with one line, or a run over 3x
  the median of comparable runs, and puts `stand_signal` with one plain sentence and a timed
  probe into the summary: repairs stop and the person hears the sentence.
- **Case preconditions are checked before gate A.** A case names what it needs from the stand
  (`preconditions`: flag, data, account, variable, service) and the gate rehearsal checks it
  there — an env check against the env files the runner really loads, an http check as one
  anonymous GET. One grouped question per case inside the gate packet; a check that cannot
  run is the factory's, never the person's. That run learned in S5 that
  `features:subWorkflow` was off and the accounts sat in an env file the conftest never loads.
- **S5 windows are small and share what they learned.** `stage-scope` cuts S5 into `windows[]`
  of 2 UI or 4 other cases (`dispatch.ui_window_cases`, `dispatch.api_window_cases`), never
  mixed; roles append to `work/s5-notes.md` what the next window must not rediscover (page
  objects and their load gates, stand rules, env files, id spelling) and receive it through
  `read_first`. Three dispatches of that run cost $8–15 each at 250–350K tokens of context.
- **`run_suite.py --mine CASE` runs my test.** It builds the typed request from the open
  dispatch and the manifest, spells node and report ids from one real collect, and answers a
  green run over identical bytes `reused` (`--again` forces one). Roles hand-wrote 106
  request files on that run and read the factory's sources to learn the shape.

Compatibility: every new field is optional and every new config key has a default; receipts,
manifests, cases and counters written by 0.7.x replay and validate unchanged.

## 0.7.7 — 2026-09-21 — a dispatch nobody is doing is proved, not guessed

Found on the first S5 of 0.7.6 (TP1-15045: one window of three in two hours, 18 test
runs, 42 guard refusals), on a colleague's diagnosis of TP2-2523 (a role that had
started and stopped held the story forever), and on the 0.6.0 pilot TP2-2534 (a
green run whose bugs never reached Jira). Three rules of the owner run through it: the
person hears one sentence or a question; a check stops a silent pass and a person's word
passes any block; the factory proves what it claims about its own state.

- **A dispatch nobody is doing is proved, not guessed.** `dispatch_liveness.py` reads the
  role's own subagent transcript, the host binding and the journalled stop: `alive` is never
  closed, `never_started`, `abandoned` and `returned` are closed by `recover` and `next` with
  the artifacts kept and the stage startable, and a host that proves nothing answers
  `unknown`. 0.7.6 closed by absence of a record — and on Claude Code, which writes no launch
  receipt, that fit every running dispatch. `next` now answers `resolve_return` or `relaunch`
  with the ready packet; the SubagentStop hook records a role's return with the controller;
  `--operation release --dispatch <id> --words "<theirs>"` (also reached by `waiver.py
  --block "wait_existing_job"`) lets a person's word free a dispatch, which on
  TP2-2523 it could not; `rework` on S1–S3 takes `--rows` instead of `--cases`.
- **The guard stopped taxing work it never had to stop.** `run_suite.py` calls that launch no
  test (`--reparse-block`, `--recover`, `--detail`, `--help`) pass while a dispatch is open, a
  command that only mentions the runner is not a run, a RunRequest may name the instances of
  any case in its scope, a request written by the same command that runs it is a note instead
  of eleven identical refusals, and a batched schedule merges a repeated instance instead of
  refusing it. A fail-closed refusal that fires twice in a row on different calls stops the
  story with a diagnosis the factory owns (audit A24 now demands a pass or an escalation of
  every fail-closed entry).
- **S5 ends at a deterministic check, not at a critic's reading.** `s5_precheck.py` (the
  automator's exit detector) counts the manifest's own invariants, the Then clauses each case
  actually proves, the reporter row each test actually has and five test-code smells, and
  hands the list back to the author as one repair round; on TP1-15045 it names a case
  green at four of eight partitions, a Then the test contradicts and an expected status
  changed from 401 to 403 after a red run. One test has one identity
  everywhere (`contract.instance_id`, see below; `instance_file_stem` for paths — a Windows
  file name takes no `::`), the manifest drops a stale copy in both directions and refuses a hand edit, a code
  review is accepted only with its findings file and `review_receipt_ref`, and the red probe
  no longer fails because the factory redrew its own dashboard underneath it, no longer runs
  without the automator's untracked new files, and no longer blames a test for a mutation
  that changed nothing.
- **A gate is rehearsed against its environment too.** Gate A's rehearsal collects the
  project's existing tests through its own run command (`ModuleNotFoundError: pydantic` cost
  a fifteen-minute window after the approval) and checks the keys and accounts the cases need
  against the environment file the runner really reads, naming the file the credentials go
  into. Gate B's rehearsal asks the tracker for the RIGHT to create an issue without creating
  one (`tracker_write.py`: `mypermissions` and `createmeta`, or the project's declaration plus
  one question the orchestrator asks and records), kept with the channel's fingerprint, read
  by the doctor and by S0 — which says in the story's first message that its bugs will not be
