  filed — and a channel that cannot deliver is the person's question with three answers, not
  a `factory_defect` with a waiver. Gate B's bug list is built by code — numbered, impact
  turned into a priority, one line of what is broken and how to see it, the path, the
  duplicate the role found — and "keep it local" is `deferred by decision` with the
  `obligations.md` rows, never `NOT_CONFIGURED`.
- **The person hears one sentence.** `stage_status.py` builds it from the receipts (a critic
  returned, an author repaired, a role halted, a window closed, the state was repaired); the
  eight critic findings addressed to the author that the person had to read are in the
  author's file, where they belong.
- **Story size is computed.** `sizing.py` weighs every verifiable requirement by the priority
  its impact class maps to — the "strategy's risk multiplier" the old formula named never
  existed in any project — applies the sibling factory's reducers, the defect-ticket cap and
  the cap table, raises only the requirements bound to the touched place on a migration or a
  surface crossing, and writes the arithmetic to `work/sizing.json`; XXL recommends splitting
  the ticket and blocks nothing. The register gains an `impact` column.
- **Story cost sticks to the story.** A gap between two segments of the same story, and the
  tail after its last one, belong to it (57cf578c: "(no task)" fell from $5.71 to $0.19); a
  marker-less role is bound by the ticket in its own prompt; stale and backfilled cost files
  recompute before the dashboard reads them; "By agent" is built from factory sessions only
  and reconciles with "By task" to the cent; the S9 retro's story spend no longer counts every
  agent twice. TP1-15045 over its three sessions reads $48.81, not $9.23.
- **Four reviews read the factory as each role would, and 63 findings came back.** Most are
  fixed here. S0–S2: S0 closes before the controller is initialized (a `code_only` receipt
  closes it after), S1–S9 accept the role's dispatch before `stage_done`, the S1 source stop
  has a flag-built `--operation checkpoint`, a role's halt is no longer refused for the
  artifact it halted before writing, readiness' `not_configured`/`unknown` is a warning and
  not a halt, `warnings[]` and `environment_pending` have a place in `pipeline.json`, the
  scout records `issue_type` so a bug is sized as a bug. Reading a tracker is
  `adapters.ticket.direct_api` only — an assistant returns no attachments and cannot reach
  a parent, so every read command refuses that route and names onboarding; writing through
  an agent is unchanged. S3–S4: the plan's `impact` (risk) and the register's `impact_class`
  (damage) are two fields, the register's contradiction matrix reaches the plan as
  `source_conflict`/`oracle_unknown` and the owner as a gate-A question with the quote,
  `planning_contract.py <file>` reads the `{"rows": […]}` shape, cases are pinned and verified
  in the project's own `cases_root` with one `--store` default, the gate-A brief links the
  plan and understanding.md again and shows the computed size (XXL included), the design
  review carries the case critic's own verdict, rows a person changed are marked
  `overridden` by code, a critic fix no code can apply is a debt for the person instead of a
  repair S4 can never close, and the critic's round cap is `done · verdict=reject`, decided
  at the gate. S5–S7: `run_suite.py --template` prints the RunRequest skeleton so no role
  guesses a field, the pre-tool guard names the typed interface when a dispatch is open, the
  red probe's `--baseline` reaches the publication branch and its bindings come from the
  manifest, a requirement the code contradicts has a named outcome (`contradicts_requirement`
  → red hand-over → APP_BUG), one test may prove several cases everywhere, an `inconclusive`
  manual check enters triage, the flaky threshold is three reruns everywhere, and the round
  number the person is shown counts repair rounds only. S8–S9: S8 closes before gate B and
  the decision takes `--drafts`, so chosen bug drafts stop reading `provenance_invalid`; the
  retro always runs `qa-retro-analyst` over the numbers code computed (`numbers`/`skip` only
  on the person's own words, and a `numbers` retro is written by `retro_numbers.py
  --write-retro` with its estimation record); "keep it local" is recognised however it was
  recorded; a write channel with no adapter refuses (exit 5); the story budget's ceiling
  stops its caller (exit 3). Gate B lists what is still open before the MR — unanswered
  questions, undecided findings, remarks (`waiver.py --remark`), unresolved rows — and "open
  the MR anyway" carries the same lines into the MR description. At a gate the factory waits
  with no deadline; an answer matching no option is re-asked once only when it changes
  scope, oracle or stand.
- **A case is coverage, not a test method.** `contract.instance_id` drops the case prefix
  (`test_validate[missing-assistant]`): the cases an instance proves are `covers` on its
  manifest entry, and the automator records the shape it chose (`shape`, `consolidates`) after
  an execution-design step — reuse, extend, parameterize, consolidate or new; minimum
  duplication with complete coverage, optimized for maintainability, diagnostic value and
  execution cost, not for the number of test methods. `s5_precheck.py` no longer counts test
  functions per case — it checks that every Then clause and partition is bound to an instance
  that covers that case, and hints when two new tests differ only in their data. Ids written
  by 0.7.7 still match their own rows.
- **Role slices from one source.** A reference is still one file per subject, but a role is
  injected only the sections marked for it: `<!-- roles: qa-x, qa-y -->` above a heading,
  `scripts/contract_slices.py --write` renders `references/slices/<role>/*.md`, and those
  files are committed because the injection hook has no time to render anything.
  `inject-map.json` points at them, A22 weighs them, A9 and `selftest.py --slices` refuse a
  stale one. The four roles that were writing fields out of contracts nobody delivered — code
  critic and failure analyst on the automation manifest, case critic on `## Gate A debts`,
  doc scribe on coverage links — now receive them. Smallest headroom under the 42,000-byte
  cap went from 287 to 1,793 bytes; the requirements tester pays 15,964 fewer. Charters keep
  the verdict and the why-clause of every rule; the shape lists a validator names in its
  refusal left them.
- The doctor now checks that the pre-tool guard still PARSES this host's events, not only
  that it fires: `host_probe.py --check` reports `guard_parse` over the guard receipts of this
  session (a shell call and a file write), and a `PT-unparsed-event` / `PT-patch-unchecked` on
  record reads `guard_defect`, `owner: factory`, with the host version. S7 tells the person
  about a repair round in one line built by code, counting the failing tests the triage
  handed back. `pipeline.json` is hand-written exactly once, at S0's creation of it:
  `stage_done.py --set key=value` (implementation_source, size, environment,
  environment_pending, parent_feature, retro_mode) and `--warn "<line>"` write everything the
  phases used to ask the orchestrator to edit in by hand — and a replayed stage transition no
  longer rolls those facts, or a waiver's overrides and remarks, back to the snapshot the
  stage closed on. The dashboard header reads the package version from its manifest (it said
  0.7.0 for seven releases).
- Doctor and onboarding: the `tracker_write` capability with three readings; the bugs channel
  of onboarding closes only on a confirmed write right; the doctor may `release` a dispatch
  on the person's word. New optional config keys: `sizing.weights`, `dispatch.*`,
  `gate_rehearsal.*`, `external_writes.probe.*`, `external_writes.bugs_project`,
  `external_writes.channels.<name>.writes`.

## 0.7.6 — 2026-09-21 — a gate is the last stop before its next stage

The first live run of 0.7.5 (TP1-15045) showed gate A, heard "approve", and then stopped
four more times, each over a fact the factory already had on disk. The owner's rule that
came out of it: every check is made before the person is addressed; after their answer the
factory runs without questions or refusals it could have computed.

- **A gate is rehearsed before it is asked.** `gate_preflight.py --gate A|B` (also
  `controller.py --operation gate-preflight`) dry-runs everything the approval unlocks: the
  decision the controller will record, the stage guard, `prepare` and the derived scope, the
  pins, the critic's unapplied exact fixes, the plan contract, the working tree and branch,
  and the gaps the plan itself declares. Each finding has an owner — the factory repairs
  `factory_fixable` before anyone is asked, `person_decides` enters the gate packet as a
  question (the dirty-tree and branch question was a separate stop after gate A),
  `factory_defect` is stated with the command that passes it — and `stage_done` will not
  close S4 or S8 while a repair the factory owes itself is open. The gate brief carries
  "After your approval".
- **One word for an approved gate, and the guard hears the person.** The controller recorded
  "approve" as `gates.A.decision = "approved"`; the stage guard passed only `"approve"`, so
  the story could not enter S5 under a green 113/113 selftest. `contract.gate_approved` is
  now the only reader of that field and knows every spelling; `stage_guard.dispatch_errors`
  runs both dispatch rules through `waiver.split_overridden`, journals `gate_override` and
  ends each refusal with the ready command, and `waiver.py` re-checks the block it recorded
  and prints `block lifted` / `block NOT lifted` instead of OK over one that still stands.
  New audit A24 (`refusal_registry.py`) holds every refusal on the dispatch path to naming
  its override and its test — the principle is checked by code, not by the author's memory.
- **Gate decisions and reworks are built by the controller, not typed.**
  `--operation gate-decision --gate A --words "<their words>"` derives scope, hashes and
  design reviews and records them in one call; `--operation rework` takes a role back over
  named cases with the inputs of its own accepted work. A critical plan row binds to its
  cases through the case front matter, so a plan whose `required_scenarios` are prose no
  longer refuses an approved gate (it cost three role dispatches). Refusals name their
  allowed values; `{"error": "'supported'"}` is gone.
- **A refused dispatch leaves no receipt.** The stage guard runs inside `--operation
  dispatch`; a denied `Agent` call leaves a line in `state/dispatch-denials.jsonl`; a running
  dispatch this host can prove was never launched is closed as `never_started` by `recover`
  and by `next`, so a story is no longer told to wait for an agent nobody started.
- **The owner guard lets a role rework its own accepted stage.** Since 0.7.5 a rework no
  longer sets a stage `running`, and on Claude Code the hook sees the parent transcript, so a
  designer could not edit its own cases. The guard now reads the open dispatch in
  `state/controller.json` and the host's agent fields, and names `--operation rework`.
- **A critic's exact fixes are applied by code**: `critic_rollcall.py --apply-fixes` replaces
  the text, re-pins the case and checks it landed — no designer dispatch; zero or several
  matches stay a gate debt. A role with no Bash is never told to run a validator.
- **Activity is recorded on Claude Code.** A Bash-invoked `activity_capture.py` had no
  session id, so a story session read `has_factory_activity: false` and most of its cost
  fell under "(no task)". It now recovers the id from the PreToolUse receipt of its own
  call (`session_env.py` also offers it through `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`), and `--backfill` rebuilds
  a past session's activity from its transcript.
- **Hooks keep to factory sessions.** The read-size limit and the turn counter act only where
  there is factory activity, a role, or an open dispatch; a session with none writes a cost
  summary instead of a per-request ledger (1.36 MB became 63 KB). The turn counter resets at
  a compact and at a closed stage and speaks of the window, never "this dispatch".
- `project_decisions.py` survives Git Bash rewriting a `--field-ref` that starts with `/`;
  the skill forbids offering the person a plugin edit or "ask the maintainers", and a window
  that only recovered or recorded goes on into its stage instead of asking for a restart.

## 0.7.5 — 2026-09-21 — the factory does not hand a person its own defects

Found on the second live run of TP1-15045 (0.7.4) and in a pilot's feedback on 0.6.0
(TP2-2530). The run reached the threshold of gate A and then told its owner there
was an "inconsistency to fix" in `pipeline.json`. There was, and it was the factory's.

- **An accepted stage is reworked, never lowered.** A `stage_transition` of `running` on a
  stage the controller had accepted rewrote its status, and `stage_done --status done` then
  refused the stage it had just lowered: the story stalled one step before gate A with no
  legal way forward or back. The transition now records `rework` on the stage,
  `stage_done --status running` refuses it and names SendMessage or `revise_plan`, and
  `controller.py --operation recover` repairs an already-broken state itself, journalled.
  The skill says it in words too: the person is asked only what a person decides. The doctor
  may run `recover` for a stuck story nobody is working on (`phases/repair.md`) — the one
  repair it performs, because it is shipped, idempotent, journalled code.
- **The S5/S6 scope is computed, not typed.** `--operation stage-scope` (and `stage_scope`
  in the prepare packet) derives it from the approved plan's dispositions. An empty S5/S6
  dispatch, and an empty approved scope at gate A, are refused while the plan names cases —
  on 0.6.0 an empty window closed S5. Both pass on a person's word. The repair cap counts
  the window's own dispatch receipts, so it holds on a host that reports no counters.
- **A window changes only at a stage boundary.** `window_budget.boundary_notice()` asks for
  a compact or a fresh session when what is left will not cover the NEXT stage, measured
  from this story's own stages, and says nothing after S4 or S8: gate A and gate B are
  asked in the window that closed the stage before them, over a brief `gate_brief.py`
  builds by code. A window had ended one step before gate A and the person got a restart
  command instead of the question. The brief also names the e2e-ui rows set to
  `automate` without a highest-risk reason — the S3 warning about them reached nobody.
- **The retro stopped being an agent doing arithmetic.** `retro_numbers.py` computes every
  figure; `qa-retro-analyst` writes prose over it under a blocking budget; the gate B
  message asks `full | numbers | skip` and `pipeline.json.retro_mode` records it (default
  `numbers`, no dispatch). A story can carry a money or token ceiling (`config.budget`)
  that warns at 50/80% and stops to ask at 100%; their word passes it like any other block.
- **The plan contract is checked while its author is still there.** `planning_contract.py`
  is S3's exit detector and applies exactly what `gate-inputs` will require — a plan without
  `coverage_contract_revision` had passed S3, survived case design and two critic rounds,
  and was refused three dispatches later. **A critic's verdict is computed from its own
  roll-call** (`critic_rollcall.py`): an unreviewed row makes it `partial`, the digest
  carries "N of M reviewed" and the ids reach gate A — seven of fifteen cases had gone
  unread under an approving verdict. A last-round concern with exact replacement text is
  applied without a new round (`approve_with_fixes`) and code checks it landed. **Pinning
  case versions is the orchestrator's step** (`case_versions.py --all`, `--verify`); case
  links are stored project-relative; `defect_class` and `reuse_decision` are validated on
  write; an `automate` row at e2e-ui level without a highest-risk reason is warned about.
- **Two roles were told to run a script they had no tool to run.** `qa-requirements-tester`
  and `qa-bug-reporter` hit `No such tool available: Bash`; both `tools:` lines are fixed
  and `role_permissions.py` (doctor, step 3) catches the class. A role reporting a tool as
  unavailable is a halt, never the orchestrator doing the role's work.
- **A stale environment block no longer outlives the run that answered it.** A later
  terminal attempt of the same instance supersedes a manifest `blocked_by_env` and the
  reducer's historical `env_blocked` rows; the record stays, marked. **`delivery_ready: no`
  says whose problem it is**: every reason carries an `owner`
  (`product | factory | environment | review`), `ledger.json` carries `blocked_by`, the
  reducer's `factory_findings` — which nothing had ever read — arrive at gate B in their
  own list, last, and a story blocked only by `["factory"]` says so in words.
- **Key-shaped text costs one lookup per prefix.** A key's prefix must be a known tracker
  project (the task, its parent and links, `/browse/` URLs, read sources,
  `adapters.ticket.project_keys`) or is probed once; the same story spent 51 Jira requests
  on `BR-1`, `FTR-01`, `TC-001`. 404 rows collapse into one review line
  (`--expand-not-found`). `collect` no longer defaults `--relation` to `task`.
  `review --late` marks a source shown at gate A without pretending it is the person's
  answer, and `review --record` refuses text that reads like the factory narrating a silence.
- **Subagent spend was parsed as zero on Claude Code**: `scan_file()` excluded every
  `isSidechain: true` row, which is every row of a `subagents/agent-*.jsonl` file. Six
  roles, 146 requests and 12.83M tokens had been reported as `tokens: 0` and the story's
  cost understated by about half. The cost file now carries `incomplete_agents` and
  `has_factory_activity`, and a task mixing a priced and an unpriced model still reports
  `priced_subtotal_usd`. A role dispatched before the story's first artifact write is
  billed to the task of the story activity it ran inside (the scout, the most expensive
  role of that run, had gone to "(no task)"). `claude-fable-5-1` and `claude-fable-5` are in
  the default rate catalogue at the current API list prices, so a session that used them
  is priced like any other; the same run now reads $10.57 for the story, not $6.13.
- **Dashboard.** The duplicate "By activity" table is gone (By task is the one source of a
  story's cost; the two disagreed by the cost of every halt). Sessions with no factory
  activity collapse into one row outside the story totals. "Token composition" is one
  third-width card with a legend and a hot-cache-share headline, with a warning rule
  (`metrics.hot_cache_min_percent`, default 90) evaluated per session and story through the
  shared banner. "Deferred decisions" has its purple border back in the empty state.
- A `PermissionError` on a telemetry file no longer fails `recover`; exit-gate detectors
  run with `-B` so nothing writes bytecode into the package.

### The doctor's probe can verify on Claude Code

- The live allow/deny probe could not verify on Claude Code, whatever the hooks did.
  `hooks/hooks.json` ran the guard directly, past `telemetry_hook.py` — the one place that
  writes a hook receipt and marks the probe; `host_probe.py` was not wired on PostToolUse at
  all; and `host_call_present` understood only the Codex transcript row. `checks` stayed
  `{}` and `host_hooks` stayed `unknown` on every Claude Code session since 0.7.3 promised
  the probe "wherever the active manifest declares the hook events". The guard on
  Write/Edit and on shell calls now goes through the wrapper (Read stays direct: one size
  check on the hottest path), the probe is wired on PostToolUse for shell calls, and a
  receipt is correlated with the `tool_use` block of a Claude Code transcript by call id,
  session and exact command. `test_claude_host_probe.py` runs the manifest's own command
  lines with Claude-shaped events and ends in `status: verified`.
- The doctor does not debug the factory. Evidence that does not arrive after one probe is
  one `unknown / owner: factory` line; reading or grepping the plugin's scripts and
  manifests is refused by the skill. A doctor that could not get its receipts had gone
  reading `host_probe.py` on the person's limit.

## 0.7.4 — 2026-09-20 — a person's word passes any block

Found on TP1-15045: S1 halted three times, the third time on gaps its owner had already
accepted in writing. The decision was journaled and changed nothing.

- An unavailable source or material blocks a *silent* pass and nothing else. Once the
  person accepts it (`ticket_adapter.py accept-gap --words "<their words>"`) it stops
  blocking everywhere `completeness()` is read — exit gate, `stage_done`, controller — and
  stays on the record as `accepted_gaps`, repeated at gate A. Empty words are refused, and
  so is accepting a gap on a source that has none.
- No block is one a person cannot pass: `waiver.py --task <T> --stage S<n> --block "<error
  text | *>" --decision "<their words>"` writes `stage_overrides[]`, which the exit gate and
  `stage_done` honour and journal (`gate_override`). The pre-tool guard refuses all three
  word-recording commands from inside a role.
- A mentioned ticket is looked at before it is collected. `ticket_adapter.py peek` reads
  title, description, AC and links; comments, attachments and the tickets it names are
  fetched only after it is assessed `relevant`, and `collect --relation referenced` refuses
  anything else. An excluded source owes no materials: its attachments no longer hold the
  gate (`completeness()` checked attachment receipts regardless of source status).
- The person sees every source with the factory's decision. The scout's first dispatch ends
  at `qa-scout S1 review`, released by the exit gate as `awaiting_human`; the orchestrator
  prints `ticket_adapter.py review` and asks it in one message with the stand question
  (S0 no longer stops for an ambiguous stand). S1 cannot close before `review --record`.
  Sources found later go into the gate A message instead of a second stop.
- Key-shaped text is no longer a source: `UTF-8`, `ISO-8601`, `LICENSE-2` are dropped on
  extraction, a token the tracker answers 404 for is left out by `peek` — only while
  another ticket of the same tracker is provably `read` in this inventory (Jira says 404 for
  "no permission" too, and a dead session says it for everything; without that proof a 404
  stays an unavailable source), and it is its own `not found (404)` line in the review, machine exports (`.html`, `.json`, `.xml`,
  `.csv`) are not mined for keys and links, and namespace/licence/CDN URLs are not
  "external media". The same story grew to 64 sources, 57 of them excluded.
- S0 runs `readiness.py --probe-vcs`: a green preflight now covers reading the MR, and an
  unauthenticated provider API is said to the person before S1 spends a dispatch on it.
- A real dispatch of a stage supersedes the imported `legacy:<stage>` placeholder, which
  stayed `incomplete` and sat in every checkpoint as a blocker after a host change.
- `stage_done.py` owns `halts[]` (append on `halted`, resolve when the stage runs again) and
  takes `started` from the dispatch clock instead of the first call it happens to see.
- The doctor's context probe is not journaled as a `subagent_stop` of `unknown-task`, and a
  review stop is journaled `awaiting_human`, not `completed`.
- `install_smoke.py --reuse-within HOURS` answers from a passed report of the same package
  fingerprint; the doctor uses 24.
- The exit gate re-checks a handoff once on Stop re-entry and never blocks there. A role
  that repaired its artifacts after a block is recorded `check_passed`; before, every
  repaired handoff was released as `incomplete` unread.

## 0.7.3 — 2026-09-20 — honest diagnosis

- Establish host reachability before anything is said about credentials. A dropped VPN is
  reported once, as one line naming the unreachable hosts, with `unknown / owner: factory`
  on every capability that depends on them: access neither verified nor denied, and no
  mention of keys, tokens or SSH. Split the single `glab` catch-all failure into
  `host_unreachable`, `network_transient` and `cli_config_error`, and retry only what is
  transient by nature.
- Give every non-ok capability a machine-readable `remedy`: what is missing in plain words,
  where to obtain what the person does not hold and with which rights, ordered steps with
  routes the factory can take itself placed first, the cost of doing nothing together with
  what still works, and who verifies the result.
- Let Doctor run the read-only probes that settle a question instead of printing an
  instruction to run them, and report the outcome rather than the diagnosis. A probe is
  diagnosis, not repair: no config, pipeline or artifact is ever written.
- Detect the host from hook receipts instead of assuming Codex, record receipts on every
  host, and run the live allow/deny probe wherever the active manifest declares the hook
  events. Include every shipped manifest in the probe fingerprint.
- Block a story only on a capability the story requires that was actually refused. An
  unfinished question no longer refuses to start work that does not depend on it.
- Stop presenting the factory's own defects as the project's: exempt the orchestrator's
  control plane from the artifact seal, add the event `exit_gate.py` already wrote to the
  journal vocabulary, name the backlog file the audit actually read, and print an owner on
  every audit finding.
- Keep stage completion monotonic: ordinary later work never un-completes an accepted
  stage. Retire a checkpoint that later accepted work on the same stage replaced.
- Carry gate waivers into the delivery ledger as `waived:<observed state>` — closed by a
  recorded decision, never disguised as executed.
- Assemble `env_preflight` and `witness` in the reducer from the blocks, so the output
  contract is reachable without hand-editing an artifact; emit no witness when no block
  names a summary.
- Refuse an untyped `--label` run inside an active story dispatch, naming the block that
  would not appear and the stage that could not then report.
- Record `format_changed` and `format_all` separately so a role formats only what the story
  touched, add `records_policy` for where shared factory records are committed, pin the
  final case scope with `revise_plan` before Gate A, and move `git config` from an
  instruction into the guard.

Also shipping in this build, accumulated since 0.7.2:

- Permit equivalent complete MR evidence through an authorized browser or connector when
  the API route fails; preserve separate Git, API and source-completeness results.
- Reject malformed controller `known_paths` before journaling. Recover older unnamed
  lists without rewriting events or guessing path identities; prepare resolves current roots.
- Correlate literal Codex probe calls independently of optional shell-tool arguments;
  explicit PowerShell selection no longer makes successful allow/deny probes unverified.
- Accept genuine Jira HTML attachments with `X-Seraph-LoginReason: OK` while rejecting
  denied authentication and login redirects. Recheck historical technical blockers after
  an explicit restart or relevant repair; `--ungrounded` never waives required sources.
- Preserve pending shell sessions and durable smoke reports in Doctor; empty polls no
  longer imply a broken installation. Recognize exact stdout-only live probe echoes.
- Let the ticketless Doctor context probe pass stage checks when stories already exist,
  after current same-session allow/deny verification. Keep normal story guards intact;
  exercise both PreToolUse hooks and SubagentStart with one and multiple existing stories.
- Add project-scoped Codex Full access setup to installation and upgrade procedures,
  including Desktop activation, persistent defaults, CLI launch and active-mode checks.
  Onboarding distinguishes sandbox restrictions from plugin failures.
- Recognize literal result-variable shell calls in live hook probes, and map the desktop
  context diagnostic to qa-scout without requiring an unsupported agent_type argument.
  Report guard verification and pending context delivery separately.
- Probe Git remote reads (including SSH) independently of provider APIs. Scope API gaps
  to operations that need them; do not label network failures as authentication failures
  or treat an unused case library as a global Doctor blocker.
- Require typed, source-bound observation contracts and independent oracles before Gate A;
  strengthen accepted tests without silently expanding the approved case/instance scope.
- Reject case ID collisions before writing; join results, triage and sensitivity proofs by
  exact instance and attempt identity. Preserve product failures when proof is missing.
- Validate producer artifacts before handoff and prepare manual evidence requests in code.
  Reports and dashboards share the same recorded verification projection.
- Preserve semantic Gate A approval across validated technical normalization; semantic
  changes explicitly reopen the gate before independent design review.
- Save durable continuation packets and fence session ownership with leases. Normal
  rollover waits for all work to finish. Hosts without verified fresh-session support
  receive manual continuation instructions; agent usage is never called orchestrator usage.

- Add Codex hooks, native event/patch adaptation, multi-file policy and validation checks,

## 0.6.0 — 2026-09-17 — sequential execution and durable evidence

This release changes active-task contracts. Follow [UPGRADE.md](UPGRADE.md) before
resuming old tasks; completed historical tasks remain unchanged.

- Collect a canonical inventory of relevant task/parent/mentioned sources, paginated
  comments and original attachments through a direct Jira API connection. Track fetching,
  inspection, unavailable materials and local evidence integrity separately.
- Build lifecycle packets and content hashes in code; keep discovery limits advisory,
  preserve all facts, and hand off changes without repeating completed discovery.
- Separate approved pre-deployment baseline capture from product verification and regression.
- Capture incremental usage during work, name unpriced external consumers, and measure
  owned hooks/commands without adding model calls. Windows process identity uses the native
  API rather than repeated PowerShell startup.

- Track behavior obligations and assertion-level sufficiency, including developer/CI tests,
  before Gate A; pin the approved plan and oracle hashes through execution.
- Bind current coverage to independent accepted reviews, behavior-specific sensitivity
  proofs and immutable execution receipts; reuse trusted imported results without rerunning.
- Publish validated manual before/after evidence with the report. Invalidate only affected
  obligations and reject stale, missing or altered evidence rather than reporting green.
- Require explicit reviewed lifecycle actions for obsolete tests and conditional, approved
  TMS archival; keep history and reconcile unknown transport outcomes without blind retries.
- Add explicit v1-to-v2 migration and code-generated coverage/evidence projections.
  See `UPGRADE.md` for installation and migration.

- Place Gate A after case design and required independent review; validate sourced risk,
  pin case versions and deduplicate both manual and automated cases before publication.
- Persist lifecycle events, scoped approvals, checkpoints, cumulative budgets and immutable
  instance outcomes. Recover interrupted work without restarting accepted work.
- Use typed, targeted execution; reuse author green evidence and isolate critic red proof.
  Regression remains a recommendation for the user, never a factory execution.
- Add extensible capability/profile readiness, source/deployment provenance, managed
  external dependencies, guarded mutations and a one-block hook retry fuse.
- Project cases, jobs, gaps and actual/provisional costs onto the dashboard in code;

- Preserve legacy evidence through explicit migration and compact delivery records.

## 0.5.0 — 2026-09-17

Eleven defects reported from a third project — green-lantern (ai-runway), stories
TP2-2104, -2381 and -2386, run on 0.3.x — and the halves of them 0.4.0 had already
closed. The shape is the one this factory keeps finding: a rule that held everywhere except
the one place nothing checked it.

### What you must do after updating

`claude plugin uninstall qa-factory@qafactory` → `claude plugin marketplace update
qafactory` → `claude plugin install qa-factory@qafactory`, then `/qa-factory:qa-doctor`
once.

**No re-onboarding.** `cases_root` is new and optional (`readiness.OPTIONAL_TOP_KEYS`), so
`config_schema` stays `ok`, and an unset key means today's behaviour exactly: cases stay with
the story. Two keys are worth adding by hand on a project whose tests are not pytest —
`run.reporter` and `run.report_path`; without them a green `dotnet test` or `ng test` is still
recorded as `not_executed`.

Habits that change, all visible on the first story: a stash names its paths, the case store is
the project's own when it has one, the manifest is merged rather than rewritten, an artifact is
repaired by the role that owns it, and a gap accepted at gate A is not raised again at gate B.

### The factory follows the project's filing, not its own

Onboarding always looked for the project's case store — `p1-discovery.md` names the signals: a
`test-cases/` directory, files named `TC-*`, a TMS link in the docs — and the finding went into
no config key. So it was found correctly and then dropped, and every case the factory wrote
landed in `qa-factory/artifacts/<TICKET>/work/test-cases/`, a second library beside the
project's real one. For test **code** the same discipline already worked — `app_root` and
`tests_root` are detected separately, the automator is handed the tests root, and on the first
pilot the factory found the existing class and extended it. The case documents were the missing
half.

`config.cases_root` carries it now. Discovery records the candidate with its evidence, interview
topic 1b confirms it (or asks, when nothing was found), and phase 4 writes it.
`contract.cases_root` resolves it for the story scripts and `check_coverage` reads the same key
for the project-wide map; in a shared store a story's own cases are selected by the `task` field
every case carries. The new `case_store` readiness capability refuses a store that does not
exist or points inside `protected_app_paths`, and the pre-tool guard refuses a case written
anywhere else.

### Results the factory can actually read

`run_suite.py` equipped pytest with `--junitxml` and understood nothing else. A `dotnet test`
whose log said `Passed: 10, Failed: 0, Total: 10` was recorded as `execution_status:
not_executed`; a Karma run of `TOTAL: 18 SUCCESS` the same; and a genuine .NET failure was
indistinguishable from a broken MSBuild — both `broken_run`. Roles then read the raw logs and
rebuilt the results by hand into the manifest and the run report.

A reporter is resolved per run — `pytest | junit-xml | trx | none`, from `--reporter`, then
`config.run.reporter`, then the shape of the command — JUnit XML and .NET TRX are parsed into
the same summary, and the report is copied into `evidence/`. Where there is none, the summary
carries `parse_gap` naming the flag to add, because a run nobody can read is recorded as
`not_executed` however green its log looks.

### The manifest is merged into, never replaced

"Windows run one after another — they write the same file" was a sentence in a phase file. On
TP2-2104 window 2's `Write` replaced window 1, whose accepted work was then rebuilt by
hand from the journal, the surviving evidence logs and `git diff`. `manifest_put.py` merges by
case; `runs[]` and `self_fixes[]` are append-only; a whole-file `Write` over a manifest that
already holds entries is refused. This also removes the reason parallel S5 windows were deferred
in 0.4.0 — they stay off, because nothing in that release has run live yet.

### An artifact is repaired by its owner

Manifest entries rebuilt (2104), report and manifest structures corrected after the roles had
finished (2381), a runner's omission patched instead of returned (2386): the orchestrator fixed
what came back wrong, so the artifact had no reviewer and the correction was paid out of the one
context that lives the whole story. The guard refuses a `Write`/`Edit` of a role-owned artifact
when **no stage is running** and the call is not from a subagent — a role writing inside its own
dispatch fails both conditions — and names the way back: `SendMessage` to the agent id
`pipeline.json` recorded.

### A decision survives to the next gate

At gate A on TP2-2381 the R-9 coverage gap was reviewed and accepted: the approved scope
was sufficient. The acceptance was prose, so gate B recomputed the gap from the same artifacts,
`delivery_ready` came back no, and the story went round plan, cases, review, automation, review,
run and report to ask the same person the same question. `waiver.py` writes `gate_waivers[]` into
`pipeline.json`; `check_traceability`, `ledger` and `check_delivery` read it as a terminal
`deferred_by_decision` carrying the human's own words, with the gap still named beside them. Gate
A asks the question in a form that produces an answer; gate B shows what was already decided.

### A stand that cannot be cleaned is known before the data is designed

An early E2E case created fifty COMPLETED records on a persistent stand with no delete endpoint;
a later test expecting exactly one found twenty of fifty-one, and about eight runs and 267
seconds went on proving the data was at fault rather than the product. `env_probe.py --env
<name>` prints `data_cleanup: available | absent | unknown` from `test_data.cleanup_owner` and
the stand's `safe_to_break`, at S0 — so it reaches gate A as a design constraint: bulk data
becomes a decision, every Then stays inside the case's own records, and the automator tags its
data per run and filters by the tag.

### Cases stop saying Draft, reports stop being incomplete, markers stop being late

- **`Draft` → `Automated`** is part of the critic's verdict now. The contract gave it that
  transition, its own charter never mentioned the case file, and `artifact-contract-plan.md` —
  the document that names it the owner — is not injected to it. On TP2-2386 fifteen of
  sixteen cases were automated, approved and green while every file still read `Draft`, so the
  coverage map, which counts that frontmatter, reported zero. `check_delivery` refuses
  `delivery_ready` while the contradiction stands.
- **The run report accounts for every case** S5 automated and every manual-agent row of the plan
  — in results, manual checks, skipped, impossible, env_blocked or manual_human. The hole used to
  surface two stages later, after the runner's dispatch had closed, and cost a corrective
  re-dispatch.
- **The TC marker is checked in the test file**, not only in the manifest entry, at the moment
  the automator writes the manifest — before the critic and before any run.
- **The dirty-tree guard no longer stashes the factory's own artifacts**: the tree check excludes
  `qa-factory/`, the stash names its paths, and stage-guard rule 7 refuses one that does not.

### Injection weight, measured and capped

Every injected byte is read on the first turn of a dispatch and re-billed on every turn after it;
on TP1-14336's 26 dispatches each opened with 28–47 KB of rules before its first useful
action. `artifact-contract-json.md` (12 KB) was injected whole to six roles that each write one
of its six artifacts. It is split by reader — grounding, automation, run, ledger — with the
story's state files left behind: the scout drops 40.9 KB → 30.9, the automator 44.0 → 35.4, the
runner and the failure analyst 35.5 → 26.9, the retro 39.5 → 28.9. Audit rule **A22** caps a
role's injection at 42,000 bytes and the common list at 18,000, because no single addition ever
looks expensive on its own.

### Deliberately not done

**A detector for global-count assertions in test code.** The same line is correct on a stand that
resets and wrong on one that does not, and these detector families are hard rejects — a rule that
cannot tell the two apart would reject good tests. The fact reaches gate A instead, where a
person decides.

**Parallel S5 windows**, still. The manifest is coherent by construction now, so the blocker is
gone; what remains is that nothing in 0.4.0 has run live yet, and this release adds more to try
first.

## 0.4.0 — 2026-09-16

The cost release, and the fixes from two more live stories. Two runs were measured request
by request (TP1-14501 → MR !666, TP1-14336 → MR !667): 1,238 and 2,271 requests,
138.8M and 236.4M billed tokens, $81 and $142 at Sonnet list prices. **95% of those tokens
are cache reads** — context charged again on the next turn — and the split is the same in
both runs: the orchestrator 40%, S5 (automator + code critic) 23–36%, rework up to 10%.
Almost everything below follows from that one arithmetic: a token placed in a context at
turn *i* of *N* is paid for *(N − i)* times.

### What you must do after updating

`claude plugin uninstall qa-factory@qafactory` → `claude plugin marketplace update
qafactory` → `claude plugin install qa-factory@qafactory`, then run
`/qa-factory:qa-doctor` once.

**No re-onboarding.** Two config keys are new (`factory_may_edit_strategy`, `turns`) and
neither is treated as missing: `readiness.OPTIONAL_TOP_KEYS` names keys that post-date the
current `schema_version`, so `config_schema` stays `ok`. Nothing on disk breaks.

Two habits change, both visible on the first story:

- **The orchestrator ends its window at a gate.** After a gate decision it stops and hands
  you one line: `continue with /qa-factory:qa-story <TICKET>`. Resuming was always
  supported (`pipeline.json` and the journal hold the state); now it is the normal path.
- **Some calls are refused with an explanation** — a `Read` of a file over 30 KB without a
  line range, a `git commit` that names no paths, a tracker write from a shell. Each message
  names what to use instead.

Optional, and worth it: add `code_repos[]` for every application repository (a cross-repo
story now grounds on all of them), and paste the `permissions.allow` block `qa-doctor`
prints if every `grep` asks you for a keystroke.

### The project is where its config is, not where git says

`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is set by the harness for hook calls only, so every script a role runs
through `Bash` fell through to `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. With the project nested in a
monorepo (`testproject1-sdk/test-harness/qa-factory/`) that is a different repository's root: on
TP1-14336 every `log_append.py` call from gate A to gate B wrote into a **sibling
journal created at the monorepo root**, evidence files landed there too, and
`check_witness.py` reported a real file as missing — so gate B carried a false
`delivery_ready: no` and cost a re-dispatch to disprove.

The project root is now the nearest directory carrying `qa-factory/config.json`, and a
writer that cannot find one **refuses** instead of creating it. `mkdir(parents=True)` is
what made the misresolution silent.

### The orchestrator stops paying for its own history

Its context grew from 73K tokens at the first request to 405K at the last, over 472
requests — 40% of that story's bill, spent re-reading itself. Six times a pause outlived the
cache and the next turn rewrote the whole context at 1.25×: 2.65M tokens, about $10, for
waiting.

- **The window ends at a gate** (S0–S3, then S4–S8 with delivery, then the retro).
- **`stage_done.py` closes a stage in one call** — `pipeline.json` and the journal together.
  It was an `Edit`, a `log_append.py` and usually a `Read`: about 72 of those 472 requests
  produced nothing but state. It also removes a real defect — two hands wrote one
  transition, so a stage could be `done` in the state and absent from the journal.

### Somebody counts the turns

Turn economy was the one rule in `common-rules.md` that nothing enforced — the section said
so itself — and five dispatches ran 140, 126, 117, 109 and 105 turns. No role could have
done better: nothing told it how many turns it had spent. `turn_budget.py` counts every
session's tool calls and interrupts at 60, then every 30, with the number and what to do
about it. A notice, not a refusal: repeating the call proceeds.

### Read the slice, not the file

3.12M characters of file content entered contexts over one story.
`automation-manifest.json` alone was read 32 times for 806,531 characters — 63 KB by the
fifth window, read whole by both the automator and the critic to work on two cases. One diff
was read whole at turn 10 of 140 for 102,214 characters and re-billed on all 130 turns after
it.

- **`manifest_view.py`** returns a window, a case, the unresolved set or a summary.
- **`diff_pass.py`** prints a diff's changed files and changed lines, numbered in the new
  file — one call instead of a dozen greps.
- **The big-read guard** blocks a `Read` over 30 KB without `offset`/`limit` and names the
  alternative. Templates, references and the small state files are exempt;
  `config.read.max_bytes: 0` turns it off.

### A comment does not cost a second code review

`critic_verdict` had two values, so a missing ticket marker could only be said as
`rejected` — and `rejected` means the automator fixes it and a **fresh** critic dispatch
re-runs the rubric, the detectors, the arch-check and the suite. `approved_with_fixes`
carries `fix_notes[]`: the automator applies them, then the orchestrator returns to the
**same** critic, which confirms from the review it already holds. `diff_scope.py` decides
whether a change was cosmetic by looking at it — every changed line a comment, a docstring
or blank, or not — instead of leaving it to judgement. A re-run after a fix covers the
changed tests only.

`SendMessage` reopens a dispatch and is not `Agent`, so the stage guard never saw it. It is
matched now: the target must be an agent id this story recorded.

### A story can live in two repositories

QA-EXAMPLE's change was a backend MR and a frontend MR. `code_repos[]` — which
onboarding asks for, `readiness.py` checks and the audit validates — was read by **no role
at all**, and 0.3.0's anti-marathon rule ("first hit wins, no sweep of the other
repositories") taken literally ends the cascade at the backend. So the UI repository was
found by guesswork. The cascade now runs once per **declared** repository, first hit wins
inside each, nothing undeclared is searched; `context-manifest.json` gains
`implementations[]`, one entry per repository.

### S1 knows when it is done, and S2 says when S1 was not enough

- **A stop rule for the scout**: grounding is complete when every acceptance criterion
  carries an observable with a `path:line` or is recorded as having none. It had only a list
  of things not to do, so it kept reading — theme tokens, eleven component files one at a
  time — after both diffs were in hand.
- **The ticket is fetched once.** S1 re-derived it through the adapter although S0 had
  written the snapshot: the ticket half of `adapters-read.md` was injected to the scout,
  which then had both a file and a manual and used the manual.
- **A register observable citing a path the manifest never recorded** is refused unless the
  register carries a `manifest_gap` line naming it. S2 may read code; it may not read it
  silently — on QA-EXAMPLE it re-read the implementation beside a manifest holding 24
  grounded observables, and nothing recorded the gap, so S1 handed over the same hole again.

### Smaller, and each one a live defect

- **One case per result row.** Three cases chained into one test arrived as
  `"TC-001/TC-002/TC-003"`; `ledger.py` matches by equality, so all three reached the ledger
  as `not_executed` beside a green run. The validator refuses a compound cell;
  `contract.case_ids()` reads one already on disk.
- **A commit names its files.** `git add <file>` was the rule and was followed — the index it
  inherited was not, and the delivery commit swept in two scripts a teammate had staged
  before the session. Stage-guard rule 5 refuses a bare `git commit -m` and `-a`/`--all`.
- **`factory_may_edit_strategy` is written by somebody.** It was read in four places and
  written in none, so every project silently took the "propose, do not edit" branch and no
  knowledge fold ever reached a strategy document. Onboarding asks it beside external
  writes: both are permissions, not facts about the repository.
- **Time to the first test** is stamped (`pipeline.json.first_test_run_at`) and reported.
  "Four hours for a small task" is a claim about the hour before anything runs, and nothing
  measured it.
- **The stand is probed at S0**, not first at S6 — a dead stand used to surface after the
  plan, the cases and the automation had been written against it.
- **The retro reports the money**: the orchestrator's share, the three most expensive
  dispatches, the cost of rework. Without those figures none of the above can be shown to
  have worked.
- **Onboarding stops asking what it already read** — assertion style, fixture placement,
  mocking library and the rest are inferred from the real test files and shown at the
  summary gate for correction in place. One question is added in exchange: are there other
  repositories for this product?
- **`qa-doctor` prints a `permissions.allow` block** on request, for the human to paste.

### Deliberately not done

**Parallel S5 windows.** They would cut wall-clock time by an hour or more on a five-window
story, and they collide with the rule that keeps `automation-manifest.json` coherent —
windows run one after another because they write the same file. Splitting the manifest per
window and merging it is a real change to the artifact every S5 guard depends on, and
nothing in this release has run live yet. It stays on the roadmap with its measurement.

## 0.3.0 — 2026-09-16

Siblings and the handoff leave the factory; archiving becomes a person's decision, offered
by `qa-doctor`; a test result must carry a name, a status and — for a skip — a reason.
Every item was measured before it was changed; the evidence lives in the change plan the
owner keeps outside this repository.

### The factory no longer has a concept of a sibling

A role was told to collect "sibling stories with status" and given no way to get them: the
tracker field is populated only by the file adapter, and the normalization hook for a live
Jira is a stub. Handed that instruction, a parent epic key and nothing else, a role did the
only thing left — it **built ticket keys by incrementing a number** and queried each one,
across an epic several teams share (reported 2026-09-16: a sweep of 2281–2295, then
2296–2305, one search per key).

The whole reason that list was wanted was to decide whether to write `work/handoff.md` —
**a file no phase, no role and no inject map ever opened.**

- `qa-scout` now records the parent key as the tracker returned it, plus `related[]`: the
  tickets this ticket **names**, in its description, AC, comments, links field or MR
  threads, each with a `kind` (`implementation | blocker | bug | mention`) and the `source`
  where it was read. Expanding a parent into its other children, and constructing keys by
  incrementing a number, are now forbidden in the charter and checked in the artifact — an
  entry without a `source` is a ticket somebody went looking for, and the validator says so.
- `work/handoff.md` is gone. What outlives a story goes where it always should have: the S9
  knowledge fold into `strategy/*`, and `obligations.md` for what stays open — which **S0 of
  the next story reads**, showing the rows whose trigger arrived or whose area matches that
  ticket. That is the only carrier between stories, and it selects by area rather than by a
  relationship somebody had to declare in advance.
- `siblings` is out of the ticket adapter's schema, the snapshot template, the manifest
  contract and the freshness diff. An old snapshot that still has the key parses fine.

### Archiving is a decision, not an inference

`archived: true` used to be set by S9 when it concluded that "the feature's last sibling
story closed" — the inference that sent the factory walking the epic in the first place.

- New `scripts/archive_task.py` is the only writer of the flag: `--candidates [--days N]`
  lists stories that have stood still (14 days by default), `--task <T> --note "<words>"`
  archives one, `--undo` reverses it. A story with an unresolved halt or an unanswered gate
  is **refused** (exit 4) with its open items listed; `--force` is the human answering that
  those questions no longer matter, and then the halts are closed carrying that sentence as
  their recorded resolution.
- `qa-doctor` offers it, as its last step, after the report and the one next action — the
  only question the skill asks. Clean candidates in one message; a candidate with open items
  gets a message of its own naming the problem and three answers. It asks in plain text: the
  same skill runs under four manifests.
- `stage_guard --stories` still hides archived stories, but now **names** any archived one
  that still carries an open item. Hiding a story from the board must not also mean it stops
  being checked.

### A test result that says nothing is no longer accepted

A story written ahead of its implementation is all skips, so the skip rows **are** the
report. On TP2-2290 nine of them reached the board with no case name, a `?` status,
no reason — and an `origin` of `regression` that nobody had recorded.

Four faults in a row, each silent: `run_suite.py` returned skip reasons as a counter keyed
by reason text, so a skipped test had no name anywhere; `artifact-contract-json.md` said
`{test, result}` while the dashboard read `{test_id, status}`; the validator checked
`execution_status` and nothing about the rows; and the dashboard filled the gaps with `?`
and `regression`.

- `run_suite.py` emits `results[]`: one row per `<testcase>` — `test_id`, `status`, and for
  a skip the `<skipped message>`. Passed rows are capped at 500 with a note; failed, errored
  and skipped rows are always listed in full.
- `contract.py` gains `RESULT_STATUS` (`passed · failed · error · skipped · not_run`) — one
  **test's** status, as distinct from the run's `execution_status` — and tolerant accessors
  that read both field spellings. The contract now documents `test_id`/`status`.
- The validator requires a name and a status on every row, a reason on every skip, and that
  the non-passed row count matches `totals`.
- The dashboard prints `status not recorded` instead of `?`, `origin not recorded` instead
  of `regression`, and joins `automation-manifest.json`'s `unresolved[]` so a case awaiting
  implementation says **awaiting implementation** — before it has ever been run.
- `qa-runner` pastes those rows rather than typing them, and halts if the run produced none.

### A test is placed in the pyramid by the level the plan recorded

Nine skipped tests on TP2-2290 — six backend, three frontend component tests — all
showed under "Level 1 · API autotests". The dashboard decided API vs UI with
`"ui" in test_name.lower()`, so anything without those two letters was API.

The level was never missing: `test-plan.md` has a `level` column, the automation manifest
carries each test's `plan_row`, and the chain **case → manifest → plan row → level** was
complete. Nothing read it.

- `contract.PLAN_LEVELS` — `unit · component · api · integration · e2e-ui`. `component` is
  new: a frontend component test and a service test with its collaborators stubbed are
  neither `unit` nor `api`.
- The validator rejects a level outside the list and **requires one on every `automate`
  row**. An in-flight plan with empty levels will report one error per such row — the fix is
  one word per row.
- The dashboard groups by the recorded level, renders the tiers from the vocabulary instead
  of three hardcoded headings, leaves empty tiers out of the pyramid widget, and shows a row
  whose level is unknown under **`level not recorded`** rather than folding it into API.
- `run.levels` in the project config maps a level to path patterns, for the tests the
  factory did not write (`{"component": ["frontend/**/*.test.tsx"]}`); onboarding fills it
  from the layers it already discovers. It lives inside the existing `run` block, so no
  install is asked to re-onboard. What matches nothing stays `level not recorded` — the
  board never guesses a level from a test's name.

### The reference documents are split by reader, and one rule stopped being a wish

Three injected reference documents were over their 12,000-byte cap, and they were over
because every reader received every section. Splitting them by reader keeps every rule and
cuts what each dispatch carries: `adapters.md` became `adapters-read.md` (the scout) and
`external-writes.md` (the bug reporter) — halves that never had a common reader — and
`artifact-contract.md` became a shared part plus `artifact-contract-plan.md` (S2–S4),
`artifact-contract-results.md` (S8–S9) and `vocabularies.md`.

`vocabularies.md` closes a delivery gap, not just a size one: the closed lists lived in
`artifact-contract.md`, which `qa-runner`, `qa-automator`, `qa-failure-analyst` and
`qa-retro-analyst` never receive — while `execution_status`, the `unresolved[]` reasons, the
triage verdicts and the FLAKY mechanisms are exactly what those four must obey. And
`qa-retro-analyst`, which writes `retro.md`, had never been given that document's contract.

`common-rules.md` (injected into all twelve roles, so a byte costs twelve) went from 12,637
to 11,195 bytes by cutting justification where a guard already enforces the rule and its
block message names the fix. Nothing a guard does **not** enforce was shortened: the
turn-economy section keeps every rule and now says plainly that no guard counts your turns.

**"No role writes to an external system" is now enforced.** It was absolute in prose and
backed by nothing: a role holding `Bash` could run `glab issue create` and the factory would
never know. The PreToolUse guard now refuses a tracker or TMS write verb — including a
command the project itself declared as a write channel, and a `-X POST` through `glab api` —
and its message names the proposal path. Reading is untouched: `list`, `view`, `search` and
a ticket read through `ticket_adapter.py` all pass, and creating the merge request remains
the stage-gated delivery path.

With that, `scripts/selftest.py` is **23/23** for the first time.

### Repairs found while doing the above

- **`parent_feature` was never written.** The dashboard groups a feature's stories by
  `pipeline.json`'s `parent_feature`, the validator lists it among the required keys — and
  S0 created the file without it, so every story sat in "No feature". S0 writes it now, as
  the parent's **key alone**; the dashboard normalizes `{id, title}` and `KEY "Title"` to the
  same group, and looks in `artifacts/<task>/` rather than the pre-0.3.0 `state/<task>/`.
- **`obligations.md` had no declared writer.** `stages.json` named it an S9 output and the
  template said "written by qa-doc-scribe at S8/S9", but neither charter listed it, so the
  one carrier between stories depended on nobody's instruction. It is now an output of
  `qa-doc-scribe` (S8) and `qa-retro-analyst` (S9).
- **The ledgers were read at a path nothing writes.** The dashboard banner and audit A16
  looked for `qa-factory/state/obligations.md` and `.../factory-backlog.md`; canon is
  `qa-factory/<name>`. Both now read canon first and the old path as a fallback.
- **`parse_frontmatter` ate a closing quote** from a value that merely ends in one
  (`parent: QA-EPIC-1 "Inventory tagging"`). Cosmetic while nothing read `parent`; a
  dashboard heading now.
- `precompact_guard.py` stopped naming a handoff path from the previous factory.

### What you must do after updating

**Required: update the plugin, then run `/qa-factory:qa-doctor` once.** Nothing else is
mandatory. No re-onboarding: there are no new top-level config keys (the archive threshold
is a `--days` flag and `run.levels` lives inside the existing `run` block), so
`config_schema` stays valid.

Nothing on disk breaks. `work/handoff.md` files were never read by anything; an
`archived: true` set by the old rule means a closed feature and stays true; a `siblings:`
line in an old ticket snapshot is ignored; a `pipeline.json` without `parent_feature` is
valid (the story just groups under "No feature" until its next run).

**A story already in flight** is not re-validated against the new rules: the exit gate
checks required keys, not the new row rules, so nothing is blocked retroactively. The new
rules apply the next time a role **writes** the file — which is where two of them will
show up:

- the strategist rewriting `test-plan.md` (a gate-A edit) must now put a `level` on every
  `automate` row, one of `unit · component · api · integration · e2e-ui`;
- the runner rewriting `run-report.json` must give every `results[]` row a name and a
  status, and a reason on every skip. Both come straight out of `run_suite.py` now.

**Optional, and worth ten minutes:** add `run.levels` to `qa-factory/config.json` so the
project's own tests — the ones the factory did not write — land on the right pyramid tier
instead of `level not recorded`:

```json
"run": {"parallel": false,
        "levels": {"unit": ["tests/unit/**"],
                   "component": ["frontend/**/*.test.tsx"],
                   "api": ["tests/api/**"],
                   "e2e-ui": ["tests/e2e/**"]}}
```

**One change in habit: features stop archiving themselves.** When the board gets crowded,
run `/qa-factory:qa-doctor` and answer the archive offer at the end of its report.

## 0.2.0 — 2026-09-15

Fixes from the first live story (TP1-13958). Evidence for every item:
the change plan the owner keeps outside this repository. **Breaking: artifact names and
locations changed.**

### The one that mattered most

The harness addresses a plugin's agents as `qa-factory:<role>`, while `inject-map.json`,
`stages.json` and the witness/detector maps are keyed by the bare role. The lookup found
nothing, silently, so for the whole pilot:

- **context injection delivered zero bytes to all twelve roles** (measured: 39,111 bytes
  for `qa-scout`, 0 for `qa-factory:qa-scout`) — roles worked without the manifesto, the
  common rules, the artifact contract, the adapters and the project's own strategy;
- **the stage guard never ran** — order, gate A, manifest completeness and the delivery
  gate all returned ALLOW without printing a word;
- the exit gate's witness and detector checks were no-ops, and its artifact scoping
  degraded to "check everything".

One owner for the normalization now: `hooklib.role_name()`. `install_smoke.py` gained a
probe that fails when injection delivers nothing — a hook exiting 0 looks exactly like a
hook that silently did nothing, which is why nothing caught this for a whole story.

### Also fixed

- **Raw run logs are unreadable to a role**, by guard, not by convention: 50–64 KB (~15K
  tokens) that is re-billed on every later turn of the dispatch. Use the runner's JSON
  summary or `--detail <test>`. `run_suite.py` also stopped capturing live INFO output
  (`--log-cli-level=WARNING` unless `--verbose`), shrinking the log at the source.
- **The factory no longer runs regression.** A witness run is scoped to the node ids in
  `tests[]`; whole-file and neighbouring-suite commands go to the human in the report.
  Five whole-file runs cost the pilot 30 of its 43 minutes of test time, re-running eight
  untouched tests each time.
- **`runs[]` in the automation manifest** — every launch, by any role, with a
  `code_fingerprint`. It blocks nothing: a run after any code change is always warranted.
  It exists so the retro can count the runs that proved nothing new.
- **FLAKY needs three executions, not five** — counted across every role through `runs[]`
  instead of restarted per role, with `--reruns N` counted as N+1.
- **One ticket snapshot**, taken at S0. Re-read only when the story stood still: a resumed
  pipeline, or a gate answered more than 6 hours after it was posted.
- **Feature closure is a flag**, `pipeline.json` `"archived": true`, not a folder move.
  The move separated `requirements-register.md` from the cases citing it and blocked the
  pilot's own handoff.
- **`work/handoff.md` only when an open sibling exists** — it is a file for the factory's
  next dispatch, not for the human, and no longer a required output.
- **Per-dispatch tool histograms** in `cost_capture.py` (and a separate one for the
  orchestrator), so a marathon can be diagnosed rather than merely counted. The config
  template ships list prices for the current Claude families: the pilot burned 111M tokens
  and reported `total_cost_usd: null` because that block was empty.
- **`install_smoke.py` names the build it is running**, first line, and `qa-doctor`
  reports it: `PLUGIN: qa-factory <version> — <path>`. Nothing printed the installed
  version anywhere before. The doctor's verdict table gained a row above every other:
  no `PLUGIN:` line, a version below 0.2.0, or no `injection delivers` lines means the
  plugin must be updated before anything else in the report is worth reading — a check
  that does not exist in an older build is simply absent from its output, and absence
  reads as a pass.
- **`qa-doctor` step 4 is one script call**, `stage_guard.py --stories`, instead of a
  `Glob` plus a `Read` of every story's `pipeline.json` (~850 tokens each, for a
  twenty-token line). Measured: seven calls and ~5K tokens for six stories became one
  call and ~60 tokens. Archived stories are filtered inside the script, so a
  "N archived, not listed" line can no longer be forgotten.
- **qa-scout stopped exploring**: the cascade halts at the first hit, self-verifying
  searches are gone, and `framework-rules.md` is injected so the test-path map is read
  rather than re-derived by walking the repository.

### Breaking — artifacts

Four documents are written for a person, and they sit at the top of the story's folder:

| was | is |
|---|---|
| `scope-card.md` | `understanding.md` |
| `plan-brief.md` | merged into `test-plan.md` (which gained a `what we verify` column and lost its 15-row cap) |
| `ptr.md` | `test-report.md` |
| `results-brief.md` | merged into `test-report.md` |
| `ledger.md` | `work/ledger.md` — the generated table the report quotes |

Everything roles exchange moved to `artifacts/<TICKET>/work/`: the manifests, the register,
the cases, the run report, triage, the ledger, the handoff, `evidence/`, `proposals/`,
`bug-drafts/`. `pipeline.json` stays at the top.

`test-report.md` has six sections and the validator enforces their **order**: verdict, what
to run, product problems, then coverage, readiness, and only then anything about our own
tests. A flaky test of ours never appears above a problem of the product.

A closed story commits the four documents, the test code and the project-level files.
`work/` is not committed — **except** for a story stopped mid-way, which commits it
deliberately so the run can be resumed days later.

### What you must do after updating

A plain re-install does not pick up plugin changes; run the full cycle from `INSTALL.md`:

```
claude plugin uninstall qa-factory@qafactory
claude plugin marketplace update qafactory
claude plugin install qa-factory@qafactory
```

Then, per project:

1. **Check the install took.** `/qa-factory:qa-doctor` — its smoke step now asserts that
   injection actually delivers bytes. A `FAIL injection delivers to 'qa-factory:qa-scout'`
   line means the update did not land; repeat the uninstall/update/install cycle.
2. **Finish or park in-flight stories.** Nothing breaks if you do not: reads resolve
   `work/` first and fall back to the flat path, and the exit gate accepts either spelling,
   so a story started on 0.1.0 still hands off and still validates. But its folder will end
   up half flat and half under `work/`. A story past gate A is cleanest finished on the old
   layout; one at S0–S1 is cleanest restarted.
3. **Add model prices** to `qa-factory/config.json` if you want money rather than tokens in
   the retro — copy the `cost.model_prices` block from
   `references/templates/config.json` and confirm the numbers against your own contract.
   Without it the retro now says so explicitly instead of printing a silent `null`.
4. **Ignore the run logs**: add `qa-factory/artifacts/*/work/evidence/` to the project's
   `.gitignore`. New onboardings do this themselves. Nothing else under `work/` is ignored
   — an interrupted story commits it on purpose.
5. **Old artifacts keep their old names.** Closed stories are not migrated and do not need
   to be; nothing reads a finished story's `ptr.md`. Leave them.

Re-running `/qa-factory:qa-onboarding` is **not** required for any of this. Do it only if
the repository's tests, environments or conventions have themselves changed.

## 0.1.0 — 2026-09-12

First package skeleton. Ticket-driven functional testing, one repository, two human gates.

**Ships:**

- Three skills — `qa-onboarding` (discovery + interview + generate, gated on an explicit
  "yes"), `qa-story` (the S0–S9 pipeline for one ticket), `qa-doctor` (read-only diagnosis,
  one next action).
- Twelve `qa-*` roles dispatched by `qa-story`: `qa-scout`, `qa-requirements-tester`,
  `qa-test-strategist`, `qa-case-designer`, `qa-case-critic`, `qa-automator`,
  `qa-code-critic`, `qa-runner`, `qa-failure-analyst`, `qa-doc-scribe`, `qa-bug-reporter`,
  `qa-retro-analyst`.
- Hooks (`hooks/hooks.json`): P-00 (protected application paths) and secrets scanning on
  every write and shell command; the stage guard's four rules on every role dispatch and
  every git/MR/TMS command; artifact validators and the detector set after every write;
  the exit gate's required-output/witness check on every handoff; cost capture on
  session stop; a PreCompact guard and a post-compact reload.
- Scripts (`scripts/`): the deterministic layer behind every hook and every stage —
  guards, validators, the ledger, the delivery check, traceability, coverage, the quiet
  test runner, the ticket adapter, external-write proposals and execution, the readiness
  and audit checks, the dashboard, and `selftest.py`/`make_fixture_repo.py` for local
  verification.
- References (`references/`): the stage model and its machine-readable `stages.json`,
  the artifact contract (markdown and JSON), adapters, environments, the automation
  embedding ladder, the code-review rubric, common rules, the tester manifesto, and the
  per-artifact templates onboarding and the roles write from.
- One golden fixture (`evals/fixtures/sample-pytest-repo` + ticket `QA-1`) and one eval
  entry per skill (`skills/*/evals/evals.json`).

**Deferred to v1** (named, not silently dropped):

- Full regression runs — v0 lists the regression to run yourself in the gate-B brief; it
  does not run one.
- Non-functional testing: performance, security, accessibility, localization,
  compatibility, privacy.
- Bug-fix verification (`qa-verify-bug`) and release-readiness (`qa-release`) workflows.
- Two-way test-management sync — v0 proposes writes for a human to approve; it does not
  read back TMS state.
- A golden set beyond the one fixture repository and its one ticket.
- Parallel story runs and any cadence/maintenance concept (quarantine SLAs, scheduled
  audits, multi-user calibration).
